The Combined Commentary on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s New Flower Ornament Scripture, Scroll Seventeen.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a Śramaṇa from Khotan during the Tang Dynasty;
the commentary composed by Li Tongxuan, the Elder of Fangshan, Taiyuan, during the Tang Dynasty.

Compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhining of Kaiyuan Temple in Fuzhou during the Tang Dynasty, this is the tenth fascicle of the combined commentary on the *Lokadhātu-vyūha-rāja-samantavyūha-parivarta*, Chapter One.
[Sūtra] At that time, the lion throne of the Tathāgata was adorned with various precious, exquisite flowers; its circular dais, its foundations, its steps, and its doors were likewise so.
From each and every one of all such ornaments as these windows, there emerged bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field;

their names were: the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva Ocean-like Wisdom Sovereign of Sovereign Spiritual Powers, the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva Thunderous Sound Universally Resounding, the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva Crest of Universal Radiance of All Jewels, and the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva Great Wisdom Sun.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Courageous Wisdom, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Jewel-Seal of Inconceivable Merit and Knowledge,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Hundred-Eyed Lotus Topknot, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Perfect Golden Flame Light,
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Sound of the Dharma Realm, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Pure Moon of Cloud-Sound, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Virtue...

With the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Valorous Radiant Banner as their leader, there were as many such beings as there are atoms in numerous Buddha-fields who simultaneously appeared; each of these bodhisattvas raised various clouds of offerings, namely:
clouds of all kinds of mani-jewel flowers, clouds of the exquisite fragrance of all lotuses, and clouds of all precious spheres.
Clouds of boundless radiant light; clouds of fragrant flames from infinite realms; clouds of radiance from sun-treasury maṇi wheels;
clouds of all-enchanting musical sounds; clouds of flames from lamps of all jewels with infinite colors and forms;
clouds of flowers and fruits from the branches of various jewel trees; clouds of inexhaustible, pure, radiant maṇi-kings; and clouds of all kinds of ornaments.
The Cloud of Offerings of the Bhikṣuṇī King and others such as these were as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-world;
each of those bodhisattvas produced such clouds of offerings and rained them down upon the oceans of assemblies at all places of enlightenment, continuing without interruption.
Having manifested these clouds, they circumambulated the World-Honored One to the right for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of times, following him in every direction.
Not far from the Buddha, they manifested immeasurable and various kinds of precious lotus lion-thrones, upon each of which they sat cross-legged.
These bodhisattvas practiced purity as vast as the ocean; they attained the illumination of wisdom that shines upon the Universal Gate Dharma;
they accorded with the conduct of all Buddhas without obstruction; and they were able to enter into all modes of eloquence.
Having attained the inconceivable Dharma-gate of liberation, Samudrareṇu dwells in the stage of the Tathāgata’s Universal Gate;
he has fully acquired all *dhāraṇī* gates and is able to contain the entire ocean of all dharmas; he is well-established in the ground of the wisdom of equality throughout the three periods of time;
and he has attained profound faith, vast joy, and boundless merit, which are utterly pure like the dharma of space.
There is no realm that he does not observe; in all lands throughout the worlds of the ten directions where Buddhas have arisen, he diligently makes offerings to them all.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-vaśavarti-abhijñārāja, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the entire ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment and spoke these verses:

[Treatise] In various sutras within the Tathāgata’s seat, it is said that from every single one of the ornaments—such as the Tathāgata’s lion throne, the pedestals of exquisite jewel-flowers, the tiers of the base, and all the windows and doors—there emerge Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field.
Within this section, the meaning is divided into two parts: first, [the description of the emergence of the Bodhisattvas]; second, [the description of their activities].
II. Stating the Purpose of the Assembly’s Arrival. This section consists of two long divisions of the sutra text. First, stating the purpose of the assembly’s arrival: herein, there are three points:
first, to clarify that the various bodhisattvas are the ancient practices of former Buddhas; second, to clarify that the present Buddha accords with them;
third, to clarify that the ancient and the present are non-dual as the gateway. The seats upon which they sit correspond to the bodhisattva practices performed in antiquity. They rely...
The ancient precedents are as follows: that which all Buddhas have realized, I have already known.
I constantly take the Dharma-body as the seat itself, adorn it with the myriad practices of Samantabhadra, and take the wisdom of non-active great compassion as the Buddha seated upon the throne.
Whether before or after the Buddhas, they are all identical in this regard. This clarifies that the present Buddha accords with the traces of antiquity, thereby certifying sentient beings.
Because there is doubt, it is necessary to come; this is called the Tathāgata. His own practice is identical to that of the ancients.
The assembly constitutes the substance of the seat, and the substance is the Dharma-realm; his conduct is likewise the Dharma-realm.

Because he is thus unimpeded and sovereign, the seat and body are the primary retribution (*vipāka*), while the adornments upon the seat are the secondary retribution (*niṣyanda*) summoned by his practice. Now, returning from...
Within the fruits obtained as the retribution for original practices, there further emerge the assemblies of Bodhisattvas who were themselves the causes of those original practices;
this also clarifies that cause and effect are non-dual in essence, as in the "Dharmadhātu-parivarta," where the Tathāgata’s lion throne has the entire Dharmadhātu as its substance.
Second, regarding the long-term structural analysis of the sutra text: from "At that time, the Tathāgata’s lion... [and so forth].
Below the section on "Seated" there are twenty-nine lines of scripture (four hundred and ninety words; now twenty-five lines). Within this, there are seven points of meaning:
first, the manifestation of the assembly from the adornments upon the seat; second, the listing of the names of the manifested assembly; third, the arrival of the assembly and their offerings;
fourth, the assembly circumambulating the Buddha and paying homage; fifth, having paid homage, ascending the seat and sitting; sixth, praising those who have arrived.

The assembly’s virtue is proclaimed through the sevenfold majestic verses. From this point forward, ten bodhisattvas each speak twenty lines of verse to praise the Tathāgata’s merit and wisdom regarding his realization of the Way, as well as the primary and secondary [recompenses] and the causes cultivated in the past.
As subsequent scholars may follow the text and its meaning to offer their own praises, there is no need for further commentary on this section, which clarifies the present.

The Buddha accords with the ancient practice, and the ancient practice accords with the present Buddha. Those in the assembly of Samantabhadra outside the seat of enlightenment represent the Buddha’s conduct for the benefit of others;
those within the seat represent the Buddha’s own practice that accords with Samantabhadra.
This great assembly is the same path shared by all Buddhas of the past and present; there is no other way. Sentient beings who mount it [attain liberation].
It is called the inconceivable vehicle, the Tathāgata vehicle, the most supreme vehicle, and the unsurpassed vehicle that reaches the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
This is because all dharmas constitute the site of enlightenment. Taking the dharma-realm as the ground, the various *pāramitās* serve as the human effort of cultivation;
since all defilements are fundamentally pure by nature, one cultivates the treatment of ignorance to achieve fundamental wisdom (*mūla-jñāna*).
Therefore, although the scriptural text is vast and extensive, I have briefly set forth its essential meaning; as for the eulogies following the text, they are left to the discernment of later sages.

Within these ten verses, one should understand that there are twenty lines of verse below praising the Buddha’s ten *pāramitās* and the ten stages (*bhūmis*), while all the remaining sections likewise consist of twenty lines each.
[The Sūtra] That which all Buddhas have realized, he has fully known; Like space, unimpeded, he shines with universal illumination.
His light pervades immeasurable lands throughout the ten directions; Amidst the great assemblies, he is everywhere majestic and pure.
The merit of the Tathāgata is unfathomable; It completely fills the Dharma-realm of the ten directions.
Universally seated beneath all the kings of trees, the great lords have gathered together like clouds;
the Buddha possesses such supernatural power that in a single thought-moment he manifests infinite marks.
The realm of the Tathāgata is without limit, and each may perceive it according to their own liberation.

In the past, throughout oceans of kalpas, the Tathāgata diligently practiced various skillful means within all realms of existence to transform sentient beings, causing them to receive and practice the teachings of all Buddhas;
Vairocana, endowed with sublime marks and signs, sits upon the Lotus Treasury Lion Throne.
The entire assembly is pure and dwells in tranquility, gazing together in reverence.
A treasury of mani-jewels emits radiant light, universally producing boundless clouds of fragrant flames.
Infinite garlands of flowers hang down and spread about; upon such a seat sits the Tathāgata.
The auspicious gates are adorned with various ornaments; they constantly emit clouds of lamp-light and jewel-flames, vast and blazing, illuminating everything without exception.
Upon the Buddha’s seat, the excellence of the adornments increases, with windows made of various exquisite mani-jewels, draped with decorations of wondrous jewel-lotuses.
Constantly emitting sublime sounds that delight all who hear them, The Buddha sits upon it, exceptionally radiant;
a jeweled wheel supports his seat in the shape of a crescent moon.
With a pedestal of vajra, its color and flames brilliant, the Bodhisattva Jaṭāmukuṭadhara constantly surrounds him. The Buddha is most luminous in their midst.
Various transformations fill the ten directions, Proclaiming the vast vows of the Tathāgata;
All reflected images appear therein, And upon such a seat, the Buddha sits serenely.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Thunder-Sound-Resounding (Ghoṣasvararāja), empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, universally surveyed all paths.
The assembly in that ocean-like gathering then spoke these verses:
"The World-Honored One has gone forth to accumulate the practices for enlightenment, Making offerings to the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions.
Sustained by the majestic power of the Sugatas, Within the seat of the Tathāgata, there is nothing not seen."
The wish-fulfilling king of fragrant-flame maṇi-jewels adorns the lion throne with exquisite flowers;

all manner of ornaments appear therein as reflections. All those in the assembly clearly behold them, for the Buddha’s seat universally manifests these marks of adornment, with each form and category distinct in every thought-moment.
According to the differing understandings of sentient beings, each sees the Buddha seated upon it;
Precious branches hang down and spread, with nets of lotus flowers.
The flowers open to reveal Bodhisattvas emerging from within, Each producing subtle and pleasing sounds, praising the Tathāgata as he sits upon his seat.
The measure of the Buddha’s merit is like space; All adornments arise from this.
The various ornaments within each stage Cannot be comprehended by any sentient being.
The ground is made of diamond, indestructible, Vast, pure, and utterly level.
A net of mani-jewels hangs suspended in the air, pervading the space beneath the Bodhi tree;
its ground displays boundless colors and exquisite forms,
strewn with powdered pure gold and scattered with famous flowers and various jewels, all of which brilliantly illuminate the Tathāgata’s seat.
The earth deities rejoice and leap for joy, manifesting ceaselessly in every instant;
they universally provide clouds of all manner of adornments, remaining forever before the Buddha in reverent gazing.
Vast jewel lamps blaze with intense radiance, their fragrant flames and flowing light never ceasing.
Manifesting various distinctions according to the occasion, the earth deities offer this as an act of worship.
Within all the lands of the ten directions, every kind of adornment found upon those grounds now appears here in this place of enlightenment;
such is possible through the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Jewel-Light-Crest, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty,
surveyed the entire ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment and spoke in verse:
"When the World-Honored One practiced his path in the past, He beheld all Buddha-lands as perfectly complete."
Thus the inexhaustible earth is seen, all manifest within this site of enlightenment;
the World-Honored One’s vast and great supernormal powers radiate light everywhere, raining down mani-jewels,
and such treasuries of jewels are scattered across the site of enlightenment, its surrounding ground entirely adorned and magnificent.
Through the power of the Tathāgata’s merit and supernormal faculties,
the ground and the Bodhi tree are universally adorned with exquisite mani-jewels; they emit light and sound in succession, proclaiming the Dharma,
while immeasurable jewel-lamps rain down from the sky, interspersed with various precious kings as ornamental embellishments.
They all emit subtle sounds, proclaiming the Dharma;
thus the earth-spirits manifest this jeweled ground, which universally displays clouds of exquisite light.
Jeweled torches blaze with brilliance like flashing lightning, and jeweled nets are spread far and wide to cover it above; jeweled branches are scattered about as an adornment of beauty.
You all should universally observe this ground, adorned with various kinds of wondrous jewels,
which reveals the ocean of the karmas of sentient beings and causes them to understand the true nature of phenomena;
it encompasses all the perfect Bodhi trees of the Buddhas throughout the ten directions.
There is none who does not appear within the site of enlightenment,
expounding the Tathāgata’s pure Dharma according to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings. From throughout that ground, wondrous sounds universally emerge,
exactly as they should be expounded from the Buddha’s seat, with every single gateway of the Dharma fully explained.
That land constantly emits wondrous fragrant light; Within that light, pure sounds are universally proclaimed.
If there are sentient beings capable of receiving the Dharma, They all cause them to hear it so that their afflictions are extinguished.
Every single adornment is perfectly complete; Even in hundreds of millions of eons, none could describe it fully.
The Tathāgata’s spiritual power reaches everywhere; therefore, this ground is entirely adorned and pure.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Great Wisdom Sun of Valiant Intelligence, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, surveyed the ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment and spoke these verses:
The World-Honored One sits with serene composure in the Dharma Hall, Radiantly illuminating the midst of the palace.
According to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, His body appears universally throughout the lands of the ten directions.
The Tathāgata’s palace is inconceivable, Adorned with a treasury of mani jewels.
All the ornaments radiate brilliant light, and the Buddha seated therein is exceptionally resplendent.
Jeweled mani-pillars of various colors stand firm, with bells of pure gold hanging like clouds.
Precious staircases are arranged in rows on all four sides, and the gates open wide toward every direction.
Adorned with canopies of exquisite flowers and silken brocades, And beautified by the branches of jewel-trees;
With mani-garlands hanging down on all four sides, The Ocean of Wisdom sits serenely therein.
A net of mani-jewels and banners of wondrous fragrance, With lamps of blazing light spread out like clouds.
Covered with various kinds of ornaments, the World-Transcending One of Right Knowledge sits here;
clouds of transformations manifest everywhere throughout the ten directions, and those clouds proclaim the Dharma throughout the world,
taming all sentient beings— all of which appear from the Buddha’s palace.
Jewels form trees that blossom with wondrous flowers; Nothing possessed by all the ten directions can rival them.
The adornments of the lands throughout the three periods of time All manifest their reflections therein.
In every place there are clusters of jewels, Their radiant flames blazing in infinite varieties.
Doors and windows open in alternating patterns according to the cardinal directions; the architecture is magnificent and exceedingly beautiful.
The Tathāgata’s palace is inconceivable, pure and radiant, endowed with all marks;
all palaces appear within it, and in each one, a Tathāgata sits.
The palace of the Tathāgata is boundless, and the Self-Awakened One dwells within it;
all the assemblies from the ten directions gather here, none failing to come toward the Buddha.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Inconceivable Merit Jewel Wisdom Seal, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, universally...
Contemplating the ocean-like assemblies at all sites of enlightenment, he spoke these verses: "In the past,
the Buddha cultivated an ocean of manifold merits, Arising from the power of his supernormal knowledges,
vows, and aspirations, as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields— The site of enlightenment is thus adorned and pure, free from all defilement."
The king of wish-fulfilling jewels forms its roots; Vajra-maṇi gems constitute its trunk.
A vast net of jewels is spread above to cover it, While wondrous fragrances swirl and circulate around it.
Its branches are adorned with every kind of treasure, And maṇi pillars rise up in competition for height.
Branches and twigs are densely spread like heavy clouds; beneath them, the Buddha sits at the site of enlightenment.
This site of enlightenment is vast and inconceivable; the tree completely covers it on all sides.
Dense leaves and profuse blossoms shelter one another, reflecting each other’s light; within the flowers, *maṇi* fruits are fully formed.
From every branch, wondrous light emanates; that light shines everywhere throughout the site of enlightenment, pure, blazing, and inexhaustible.
Through the power of the Buddha’s vows, it appears in this way:
a treasury of maṇi jewels serves as flowers, casting shadows and radiating brilliance like variegated clouds.
Fragrance hangs from every tree, reaching everywhere; the site of enlightenment is universally adorned.
Behold the site of enlightenment of the Sugata: lotuses and jeweled nets are both pure, and wheels of light-flames manifest from them;
the sound of bells and chimes issues forth like clouds from the sky.
Within all the lands of the ten directions, All trees of wondrous form and adornment appear within the Bodhi tree;
Beneath it, the Buddha dwells, free from all defilements,
A site of enlightenment formed by vast merit, Where the branches rain down jewels eternally without end.
From within the jewels emerge all the bodhisattvas, who travel throughout the ten directions to serve the Buddhas.
The realms of the Buddhas are inconceivable; they cause the trees everywhere to produce the sound of music.
Just as the path to enlightenment was previously accumulated, the assembly hears the sounds and all are able to behold it.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Hundred-Eyed Lotus-Crest, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty,
surveyed the entire ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment and spoke these verses:
“From every mani-jewel, wondrous sounds emerge, Proclaiming the names of all Buddhas of the three periods of time.”
The immeasurable deeds of supernatural power of that Buddha are all manifested for viewing within this site of enlightenment;
various flowers bloom in competition like spread-out garlands, and clouds of light flow forth throughout the ten directions.
The deity of the Bodhi tree holds these toward the Buddha, gazing with single-minded devotion as an offering.
The flames of mani-jewels form banners everywhere; from within these banners, a blazing, wondrous fragrance issues forth.
This fragrance universally perfumes all beings, and thus that place is entirely adorned and pure.
Lotus flowers hang down, radiating golden light; from that light, clouds of the Buddha’s sublime voice emanate.
Universally shading all lands throughout the ten directions, The King of Bodhi Trees, by its sovereign power,
Eternally extinguishes the fever of afflictions for sentient beings; Constantly emitting light that is utterly pure,
The boundless assemblies of the ten directions All appear as reflections within the site of enlightenment.
The light-flames of the jewel branches are like bright lamps;
their radiance emits sounds proclaiming great vows, fully recounting all that the Buddha practiced throughout his former existences.
The tree-deities, as numerous as the atoms within all lands, all together rely upon this site of enlightenment.
Before the Bodhi trees of each Tathāgata, In every thought-moment, they proclaim the gates of liberation.
The various practices cultivated by the World-Honored One in the past, And his offerings to all the Tathāgatas—
Both those original practices and his renown Are all fully manifested within the mani jewels.
From the entire site of enlightenment, wondrous sounds emerge; Those sounds are vast and pervade the ten directions.
If there are sentient beings capable of receiving the Dharma, There are none who are not tamed and brought to purity.
The Tathāgata, in the past, universally cultivated and refined All manner of infinite adornments.
The Bodhi trees of all ten directions, each adorned with infinite varieties—
then the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Golden Flame Perfect Radiance, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty,
surveyed the entire ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment and spoke these verses:

In the past, when the Buddha cultivated the practices for awakening, he attained clear understanding regarding all objects of experience, distinguishing between what is possible and what is impossible with pure freedom from doubt; this is the Tathāgata’s first power of knowledge.
Just as in the past he contemplated the nature of all phenomena, he now clearly penetrates the entire ocean of karma.
Thus, within this net of light, you can universally expound throughout the ten directions the great skillful means cultivated over past kalpas;
according to the faculties of sentient beings, you transform and guide them, causing the minds of the entire assembly to be purified.
Therefore, the Buddha is able to achieve the power of knowledge regarding the faculties.
Just as the understandings of all sentient beings differ, And their desires, inclinations, and modes of conduct each vary,
The Buddha preaches the Dharma to them according to what is appropriate for each; By the power of his wisdom,
he is thus able to pervade the entire ocean of lands throughout the ten directions, Reaching every single realm of sentient beings.
The Buddha’s wisdom is equal to space, Capable of manifesting entirely within a single pore;
He fully knows the conduct of Buddhas in all places, Exhaustively and without remainder throughout the three periods of time in a single thought-moment.
Regarding the lands, eons, sentient beings, and times of the ten directions— He is able to reveal them all, causing them to be clearly perceived.
The power of meditative concentration and liberation is boundless, And the skillful means of samādhi are likewise so.
The Buddha manifests these to bring joy, Universally cleansing away the darkness of afflictions.
Buddha-wisdom is unimpeded, encompassing the three periods of time; In a single instant, it is entirely manifested within a single pore.
The Buddha-lands and their sentient beings— All that appears arises through the power of recollection.
The Buddha-eye is as vast as space, Universally perceiving the entire dharma-realm without exception.
Within the stage of non-obstruction lies peerless function; That eye is immeasurable, as the Buddha can proclaim.
All sentient beings are possessed of various fetters, Along with all their latent tendencies and habitual propensities;
The Tathāgata appears throughout the world And causes them all to be extinguished through skillful means.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Universal Sound of the Dharma Realm, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, universally surveyed all paths.
Having surveyed the ocean-like assembly, he then spoke these verses:
"By the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, throughout the ten directions,
The vast manifestations of the non-conceptual perfections of great awakening— All those fulfilled in the past are now made visible."
In the past, you gave rise to great compassion for sentient beings;
By practicing the perfection of generosity, your body became most sublime, Able to inspire joy in all who behold it.
In the past, throughout an ocean of boundless great kalpas, You cultivated the perfection of pure ethical discipline.
Thus you have attained a pure body pervading the ten directions, universally extinguishing all the heavy sufferings of the world.
Because your past cultivation of patience was pure, and because you understood reality with faith and without discrimination,
your physical marks are perfectly complete, universally emitting light that illuminates the ten directions.
In the past, through diligent cultivation over an ocean of many kalpas, you were able to turn away the deep and heavy obstacles of sentient beings;
thus, you could manifest emanation bodies throughout the ten directions, appearing beneath the King of Bodhi Trees.
Having practiced for immeasurable kalpas, the great ocean of your meditative concentration is universally pure.
Thus, those who behold him find their hearts filled with joy, And the defilements of the afflictive hindrances are entirely extinguished.
The Tathāgata, having cultivated an ocean of various practices in the past, Is fully endowed with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā).
Therefore, he radiates light that illuminates everywhere, Completely destroying all the darkness of ignorance.
Using various skillful means to transform sentient beings, Causing all that they cultivate and refine to be fully accomplished;
Traveling everywhere throughout the ten directions, Without ceasing for boundless eons—
The Buddha formerly practiced through oceans of great kalpas, Thoroughly purifying his vows and the perfections.
Therefore, he appears throughout all worlds, saving sentient beings until the end of the future;
having extensively cultivated and refined all powers and the *pāramitās* over immeasurable eons,
he is thus able to accomplish spontaneous power and manifest universally in all lands of the ten directions.
In the past, the Buddha cultivated the wisdom of the universal gate; The nature of all-knowledge is like empty space.
Therefore, he attained unimpeded power, Radiating light that universally illumines the lands of the ten directions.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Cloud-Sound Pure Moon, empowered by the Buddha’s majesty, universally observed all paths.
Having surveyed the ocean-like assembly, he immediately spoke these verses:
"The realm of spiritual powers is equal to space; No sentient being in the ten directions fails to see it.
The ground accomplished through practice in the past Is fully explained within the fruit of the mani-jewel."
Having purely and diligently practiced for immeasurable eons, one enters the First Ground, the Utterly Joyful,
giving birth to the vast wisdom of the Dharma-realm. Universally beholding the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions,
one attains the Stainless Ground within all phenomena, maintaining pure precepts equal in number to all sentient beings.
Having extensively practiced cultivation throughout many eons, Making offerings to oceans of boundless Buddhas, One accumulates merit on the Ground of Radiance (*Prabhākārī*);
The treasury of *śamatha*, the firm patience, and the vast clouds of Dharma have all been heard; Thus it is explained regarding the fruit of maturation.
The Ground of Immeasurable Wisdom, Radiant as a Sea of Flames, Thoroughly understanding all realms,
it gives rise to great compassion; With a body equal across all lands, it eloquently expounds The gates of the Universal Treasury,
as taught by the Buddhas— The Ground Difficult to Conquer, where movement and stillness accord without contradiction.
The realm of the Buddha-dharma is entirely equal; Just as the Buddhas have purified it, they can all explain it.
This ground of the ocean of wisdom through vast cultivation— All dharma-gates are fully understood therein.
Manifesting lands everywhere like space, From within the trees, this sound of Dharma is proclaimed.
The body of empty space pervading the entire Dharma-realm, A lamp of wisdom that universally illumines all sentient beings;
All skillful means are utterly pure, And what was formerly traversed through distant journeys is now fully expounded.
Adorned by all vows and practices, The infinite oceans of lands are all purified.
All conceptual constructions are unable to move it; this groundless state is proclaimed as the power of infinite spheres and supernormal knowledges.
It is the power of light that skillfully enters the teachings—this is the Ground of Pure Good Intelligence, wherein the practices of oceans of eons are fully elucidated.
The tenth stage, Vast Cloud of Dharma, contains all things and pervades the void;
it is proclaimed through the sounds of the realm of all Buddhas. These sounds are the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Banner of Light of Good Valor, receiving the Buddha’s majestic power, universally surveyed all.
Having seen the ocean-like assembly at the site of enlightenment, he then spoke these verses:
"Countless sentient beings within this assembly, With various inclinations and pure minds,
Are all able to awaken to and enter the Tathāgata’s wisdom, Thoroughly comprehending all realms of adornment."
Each having given rise to pure vows and cultivated all practices, they have all made offerings to immeasurable Buddhas;
they are able to see the true body of the Tathāgata, as well as all his divine transformations.
Some are able to see the Dharma-body of the Buddha, which is peerless, unimpeded, and universally pervasive.
All the infinite natures of phenomena enter his body without exception;
some behold the Buddha’s wondrous form-body, with boundless marks and signs blazing with light.
According to the differing understandings of sentient beings, he manifests various transformations throughout the ten directions.
Some see the body of unimpeded wisdom, equal throughout the three periods of time like space,
universally turning according to the inclinations of sentient beings' minds, so that all may behold its various distinctions;
some are able to comprehend the Buddha’s voice, which pervades all lands throughout the ten directions.
According to what sentient beings should understand, he utters speech and sounds without obstruction;
or they may see the various lights of the Tathāgata, shining in manifold ways throughout the world;
or within the Buddha’s radiance, they may further behold all Buddhas manifesting spiritual powers.
Some see the Buddha’s ocean-like cloud of light, emitting blazing radiance from every pore to manifest the path of his past cultivation,
inspiring deep faith and entry into the Buddha’s wisdom;
others see the marks of the Buddha adorned with merit, as well as the source from which this merit arises.
In the past, you practiced the ocean of all perfections; Within the marks of a Buddha, I clearly see them all.
The Tathāgata’s merits are immeasurable, Pervading the Dharma-realm without limit.
As for his supernormal powers and various spheres of activity, It is by the power of the Buddha that they can be proclaimed.
At that time, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, the entire ground of the Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean shook in six ways and eighteen manners:
namely, it moved, moved everywhere, and moved universally; it rose, rose everywhere, and rose universally; it leaped, leaped everywhere, and leaped universally;
it quaked, quaked everywhere, and quaked universally; it roared, roared everywhere, and roared universally; it crashed, crashed everywhere, and crashed universally.
Striking everywhere, each of these World-Leaders manifested inconceivable clouds of offerings that rained down upon the ocean-like assembly at the Tathāgata’s site of enlightenment, namely:
clouds of all kinds of fragrant flowers and ornaments; clouds of all exquisite adornments of mani-jewels;
clouds of nets of jewel-flames; and clouds of infinite varieties of circular halos of mani-gems. All of these...
Clouds of various colored precious pearls, clouds of all kinds of precious sandalwood incense, clouds of all kinds of precious parasols,
clouds of *maṇi* kings with pure and wondrous sounds, clouds of *maṇi* necklaces and wheels with the radiance of sunlight,
clouds of treasuries of all precious light, and clouds of all distinct types of ornaments— such clouds of offerings as these were beyond measure in number.

The measure of these lords of worlds is inconceivable; each one manifests such clouds of offerings, raining them down upon the ocean-like assembly at the Tathāgata’s site of enlightenment, pervading everywhere without exception.
Just as the mind of each lord of worlds in this world rejoices and makes such offerings, so too do they do so in every single world within the Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean.
All the lords of the worlds likewise made such offerings; in every world-system there was a Tathāgata seated at the site of enlightenment,
and each lord of the world had his own faith and understanding, his own objects of focus, his own gates of samādhi and skillful means,
his own cultivation of the factors conducive to enlightenment, his own attainment, and his own joy.
Each enters individually into various dharma-gates; each awakens to and understands them individually;
each enters the realm of the Tathāgata’s spiritual powers; each enters the realm of the Tathāgata’s strengths;

each enters the gates of the Tathāgata’s liberation—just as it is in this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, so it is likewise throughout all world-oceans in the ten directions, pervading the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space.
Thus it is. [Treatise]:
From the passage beginning "At that time, in the Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean" below, there are twenty-one lines of scripture (362 characters;
here, eighteen and a half lines) clarifying the shaking of the earth and the offering of worship. Regarding this section of the sutra, its meaning is as follows:
1. First, it clarifies the names of the worlds; 2. second, it deduces the Buddha’s spiritual power as the earth shakes in six ways;

3. third, it shows how the world rulers present offerings with joy; 4. fourth, it clarifies that this serves as an analogy for many lands; 5. fifth, it clarifies that the Buddha appears universally throughout the worlds; 6.
sixth, it clarifies that the world rulers each offer according to their own understanding; 7. seventh, it clarifies that the offerings presented at the Dharma assembly are universally identical.
He then asked, "Why does the earth tremble? He replied, "In general, there are five reasons for the earth to tremble: first, when the great assembly at this gathering attains the Way;
second, when a person of wisdom appears; third, when a person of wisdom passes away; fourth, during worldly calamities and transformations; and fifth, upon the joy of those who have attained the Way.
This [trembling] clarifies that the great assembly has obtained benefit and rejoices; thus the earth trembles to manifest the Buddha's spiritual power."

"Power" refers to clarifying the reverence between teacher and disciple by attributing virtue to those above. He asked: "For what reason does the earth tremble and offerings arise within this section?

He replied: "It is because this section clarifies that within the sphere of the assembly of beings who constantly followed the Buddha during the first assembly—the divine and celestial hosts—and within the seat of the Tathāgata, there are all Buddhas of the past and present who share the same causal conditions."
Within the multitude of Bodhi trees, there were multitudes of flowing light, as well as multitudes of Great Compassion within the palaces of the Tathāgatas.
Thus, when the assembly of the Buddha’s own retinue gathered, they further obtained benefit;

because their hearts rejoiced at the appearance of the Buddha and their minds were moved with joy, the earth also shook in accordance with those minds. This clarifies the great [manifestation] within the sphere of the first assembly.
Once the assembly has concluded, light emanates from the face-gate, universally gathering those from other lands so that they also come to this assembly.

This is because within the absence of self and other, there is "other" [in the sense of manifestation]. Thus, the ritual of transformation and the principal and attendant figures are clearly revealed;

this is the natural accord of the Dharma-work, serving as a model for the training of sentient beings. In this way, through the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), it universally pervades all lands throughout the dust-motes of the universe.

Within a single kṣaṇa, the three periods of time share the same limit; by means of the "Gate of the Interpenetration of the One and Many," this [text] encompasses such matters as the emission of light and the gathering of the assembly, intending to let it be known that the characteristics of the Buddha’s realm are mutually inclusive and non-dual.
The above constitutes the first section: the manifestation of the five stages of practice, which is the ultimate fruit of the cause of this entire treatise.

The sutra contains six levels of cause and effect in total: First, from the "Chapter on the Sublime Adornment of the World-Ruler" through to the "Chapter on the Flower Treasury World-Ages," these five chapters clarify the initial attainment of perfect enlightenment, manifesting the practice gates of the five stages, the retributive attainments, and the demonstrations of entering the Dharma—this constitutes one level of cause and effect.

the light of the universally adorned site of enlightenment where the assembly of bodhisattvas gathers; and the light of wondrous sounds extolling all buddhas.
The names, the radiances, and so forth, were as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field;

each of these, in turn, had as many rays of light as there are atoms in a buddha-field as its retinue. These rays all possessed the colors of various wonderful jewels and universally illuminated ten directions, reaching world-oceans as numerous as the atoms in one hundred million buddha-fields. Within those world-oceans, the assemblies of bodhisattvas [perceived] the light.
Within that clarity, each beheld this Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean;
by the Buddha’s spiritual power, its light spoke these verses before all the assemblies of bodhisattvas:
Through oceans of practice over immeasurable eons, Making offerings to oceans of Buddhas throughout the ten directions,
And transforming and delivering oceans of all sentient beings, You have now attained the state of Wondrous Enlightenment as the All-Illuminating Honored One;
From within each pore you emit clouds of emanations, Whose radiance shines universally throughout the ten directions.
All those ready for transformation are fully awakened, Led toward Bodhi with purity and unimpededness.
In the past, the Buddha traversed all realms of existence, Teaching and ripening all living beings;
His supernormal powers are sovereign and boundless, Causing all to attain liberation in a single thought.
The Bodhi tree of exquisite mani jewels is adorned with every kind of extraordinary ornament;
beneath it, the Buddha attained perfect enlightenment, emitting great rays of light that shine everywhere with majestic brilliance.
With a thunderous voice that resounds throughout the ten directions, he universally proclaims the Dharma of tranquil extinction.
According to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, you employ various skillful means to bring them to awakening.

You have fully perfected all the perfections practiced in the past, and all the powers are entirely accomplished, as numerous as the atoms within a thousand lands. You all should go together to behold and pay homage to him.
Buddha-sons from lands as numerous as the atoms of the ten directions have all gathered together in joyful accord;
having rained down various clouds as offerings, they now stand before the Buddha, gazing up with single-minded devotion.
The Tathāgata’s single voice is immeasurable, able to expound the profound and vast ocean of the sūtras.
The Sublime Dharma rains down universally, responding to the minds of all; you should go to see that Honored One Among Two-Legged Beings.
All the vows of the Buddhas of the three times were proclaimed beneath the Bodhi tree;
they all appear manifest within a single instant. You should quickly proceed to the presence of the Tathāgata.
The Great Ocean of Vairocana’s Wisdom Radiates light from his countenance so that none fail to see it;
Now, awaiting the assembly, he is about to manifest his voice. You should go to behold and hear what is being taught.
[Commentary] The second section, beginning from "At that time, the World-Honored One, having known the thoughts in the minds of the bodhisattvas," and so forth, continues as follows:

A section of prose followed by a verse constitutes the "Tathāgata Emits Light from His Teeth and Announces to the Multitudes in the Ten Directions, Causing Them All to Assemble, and Manifesting the Dharma to Answer the Previous Question. Within this section, there are eleven main points:
(1) the Tathāgata knows that the minds of the assembly harbor doubts; (2) the light from his two teeth shines everywhere; (3) that light has ten names.

1. The fourth clarifies that the light is complete with its retinue. 2. The fifth sets forth the characteristics of the light’s color and form. 3. The sixth clarifies the distance to which the light shines. 4.
The seventh clarifies how the great assembly, having received the light, can see one another. 5. The eighth clarifies that the light pervades the assemblies in other directions. 6.

The ninth clarifies that the light is able to produce sounds to address the assembly. 7. The tenth clarifies that the assemblies from the ten directions, having heard the address, all come forward and ask: "For what reason [is this]?"
Light issued from the gaps between the teeth of the Tathāgata’s face, and he addressed the assembly, saying:

"The light issues from within my face and teeth because the sound of my speech emerges from therein. Now, wishing to answer the doubts of the assembly, I shall summon the great multitudes from the Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions to assemble here to reveal the Dharma. This answers the previous thirty-seventh question: "What are the Buddhas?"
Because the Buddha’s realm, the Buddha’s empowerment, the Buddha’s conduct, and the Buddha’s power are equal to those of the [Bodhisattva] stages, he emits light from his mouth and between his teeth.

"Light" has the meaning of removing darkness. Furthermore, it answers the previous question: "What is the Buddha’s radiance? It removes the darkness of doubt in the minds of sentient beings in the present and the future.
As for the "mouth and teeth," they are the locus of exhaling and inhaling speech and sound—the means by which he teaches the Dharma and communicates his message.
Because of this, light issued forth from within it; regarding this radiance, twenty verses were spoken.
Their general purport is to praise the Tathāgata’s fulfillment of the Path and his illumination of sentient beings, as he emits sounds to inform the assembly to gather and hear the Dharma.
[Sūtra] At that time, all the assemblies in the oceans of worlds throughout the ten directions, having been awakened by the Buddha’s radiance,
each came together to approach and make offerings to the Tathāgata Vairocana.
That is to say, to the east of this Flower Bank Array Ocean of Worlds, there is another ocean of worlds named Pure Light Lotus Array.
Within the world-system known as Maṇi-Necklace, there is a land named Vajragarbha; its Buddha is named Dharma-water Awakened Boundless Space King.

Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Lotus Banner Observing Supreme Dharmas, who, together with as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, has come to this place.
Each Buddha manifested ten kinds of clouds of bodhisattva physical forms that filled the void without dispersing or ceasing;

furthermore, they manifested ten kinds of clouds of light from all-jeweled lotuses raining down, ten kinds of clouds of Sumeru jewel peaks, ten kinds of clouds of solar disc radiance, and ten kinds of clouds of precious flower garlands. They further manifested...
Ten kinds of clouds of all manner of music appeared; ten kinds of clouds of powdered incense trees appeared;
ten kinds of clouds of various forms of ointment incense and burning incense appeared; ten kinds of clouds of all manner of fragrant trees appeared.
Such clouds of offerings, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely filled the void without dispersing or perishing, manifesting these clouds.
Having already paid homage to the Buddha as an act of worship, they each manifested in the eastern direction various lion-thrones of the Flower-Light Treasury (*kusumaprabhāgarbha-siṃhāsana*).

Upon these thrones, they sat cross-legged. To the south of this Flower Treasury World-Ocean (*kusumagarbhalokadhātusamudra*), there is a world-ocean named All-Jeweled Moon Light Adornment Treasury (*sarvaratnacandraprabhāvyūhagarbha*). This is the world-system of that [world-ocean].
Within it is a land named Boundless Light Perfectly Adorned, where the Buddha is named Universal Wisdom Radiant Virtue Sumeru King.
Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Wisdom Universally Illumining the Ocean of Dharma,
who, together with as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came to the presence of the Buddha, each manifesting ten [transformations].
Clouds of mani-kings, treasuries of light that adorn all things, filled the void of space without dispersing;
furthermore, ten kinds of clouds of mani-kings appeared, raining down all manner of precious ornaments and universally illuminating;
furthermore, ten kinds of clouds of mani-kings appeared, with blazing jewel-flames proclaiming the names of the Buddhas; furthermore, ten kinds of [clouds] appeared that expound...
Clouds of mani-kings of all Buddha-dharmas further manifest ten kinds of clouds of mani-kings adorned with various wonderful trees at the site of enlightenment;
clouds of mani-kings further manifest ten kinds of universally illuminating jewel-lights that appear as multitudes of manifested Buddhas;
clouds of mani-kings further manifest ten kinds of images that universally manifest the adornments of all sites of enlightenment; clouds of mani-kings further manifest ten kinds...
Clouds of mani-kings of the *Guhyajvālā-pradīpa* (Secret Flame Lamp) proclaiming the realm of all Buddhas appeared;

furthermore, clouds of mani-kings manifesting ten kinds of inconceivable images of Buddha-lands and palaces appeared; furthermore, clouds of mani-kings manifesting ten kinds of universal images of the bodies of Buddhas of the three periods of time appeared;
such clouds of mani-kings, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely pervaded the void.
Without dispersing or ceasing, these clouds manifested and paid homage to the Buddha as an offering;
they then each miraculously created, in the southern direction, lion thrones with cores of Jāmbūnada gold and Indranīla gems, and sat upon those thrones in the full lotus posture.
To the west of this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, there is another world-ocean named Lovely.
In that world-system called Jewel Radiance of Joy, there is a land named Source of Exquisite Requisites for Sustaining the Body;

the Buddha there is named Fragrant Flame Merit Jewel Adornment. Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Moonlight Fragrant Flame Universal Adornment, together with as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds.

They all came together to the place where the Buddha was, each manifesting ten kinds of clouds of pavilions made of all manner of precious incense and exquisite flowers, which filled the void without dispersing or perishing; they further manifested ten kinds of clouds of pavilions of various jewel-kings with infinite colors and forms;
they further manifested ten kinds of clouds of pavilions of precious lamps and fragrant flames; they further manifested ten kinds of [clouds of pavilions] of all true...
Clouds of jewel pavilions appeared once more; clouds of pavilions of all kinds of jewel flowers appeared in ten ways;

clouds of pavilions adorned with jewel necklaces appeared in ten ways; clouds of pavilions that are treasuries of light universally manifesting all adornments of the ten directions appeared in ten ways;
and clouds of pavilions adorned with an interlacing of various powdered jewels appeared in ten ways.
They manifested ten kinds of clouds of pavilions adorned with all manner of jewels pervading the ten directions;
they further manifested ten kinds of clouds of pavilions with flower-gateways and networks of bells.

Such clouds of pavilions, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely filled the void without dispersing or perishing. Having manifested these clouds, they prostrated before the Buddha as an act of worship.
In the western direction, he manifested for each of them a lion throne made of great jewel-treasuries with leaves of pure gold, and sat upon those thrones in the full lotus posture.
To the north of this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, there is another world-ocean named Vaidūrya Lotus Light Perfect Treasury.
Within that lineage of worlds, there is a land named Utpala Flower Adornment.
The Buddha’s name was King of the Sound of the Banner of Universal Wisdom.

Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there was a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Lion-Leaping Radiance, who, together with as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came to the place where the Buddha was.
Each manifested ten kinds of clouds of various exquisite trees made of all-fragrant maṇi jewels, which completely filled the void.
While remaining empty and without dispersal, there further appeared ten kinds of clouds of trees adorned with secret leaves and sublime fragrances;
further appeared ten kinds of clouds of trees adorned by the manifestation of all infinite forms and appearances;
further appeared ten kinds of clouds of trees adorned by the pervasive distribution of all flowers; and further appeared ten kinds of clouds adorned by the perfect radiance of all jewel-flames.
Furthermore, ten kinds of tree-clouds manifesting the bodily adornments of all Bodhisattvas of Sandalwood Fragrance appeared;
furthermore, ten kinds of tree-clouds manifesting the inconceivable adornments of former sites of enlightenment appeared;

furthermore, ten kinds of tree-clouds appearing as treasuries of various precious garments, like the radiance of the sun, appeared; furthermore, ten kinds of tree-clouds universally emitting all that brings joy appeared.
Clouds of trees of the sounds of intention, and other such clouds as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely pervaded the void without dispersing or ceasing.
Having manifested these clouds, they prostrated before the Buddha as an offering;
then, in the northern direction, each miraculously created a lion throne of a lotus-treasury mani-lamp, upon which they sat cross-legged.
To the northeast of this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, there is another world-ocean named Jāmbūnada-vaidūrya-varṇa-dhvaja.
Within its world-system, there is a land named Sarva-ratna-vyūha, where the Buddha is named Sarva-dharma-abhaya-pradīpa.
Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva named...
The Bodhisattva Anantaguṇakośa-uttamaprabhāsa-dīpa, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came to where the Buddha was.

Each manifested ten kinds of clouds of lion thrones from the treasury of jewel lotuses of boundless colored forms, which filled the void without dispersing or ceasing; they further manifested ten kinds of lion thrones from the treasury of light of the king of maṇi jewels.
Furthermore, clouds of lion thrones adorned with ten kinds of all manner of ornamental implements appeared;
furthermore, clouds of lion thrones appearing as treasuries of flaming jewel garlands appeared; furthermore, clouds of lion thrones that universally rained down precious necklaces appeared;
furthermore, clouds of lion thrones appearing as treasuries of all fragrant flowers and precious necklaces appeared.
Clouds of lion thrones manifesting ten kinds of displays of the adornments of the seats of all Buddhas, which are treasuries of mani-jewel kings, further appeared;
clouds of lion thrones adorned with ten kinds of windows, doorways, staircases, and various necklaces further appeared;
and clouds of lion thrones that are treasuries of the branches and trunks of all mani-trees further appeared.
Furthermore, ten kinds of clouds of lion thrones, adorned with various precious incenses and named "Treasury of Sunlight," appeared;
such clouds of lion thrones, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely filled the void without dispersing.
Having manifested these clouds, they paid homage to the Buddha as an offering, and then, from each direction in the northeast, they each magically transformed into jeweled lotus flowers.
Upon a lion throne of mani-jewel light banners, he sat cross-legged;
to the southeast of this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, there is another world-ocean named Gold Adorned Lapis Lazuli Light Universally Shining.
Within that world-system, there is a land named Pure Fragrance Radiance, where the Buddha is named King of Universal Joy and Profound Faith.

Within that ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Wisdom Lamp Universal Radiance (*Prajñāpradīpa-samantaprabhā*), who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came to the place where the Buddha was.

Each manifested ten kinds of clouds of all-fulfilling wish-fulfilling jewel canopies (*sarva-cintāmaṇi-rāja-vitāna*) that pervaded the entirety of space without dispersing or vanishing; they further manifested ten kinds of celestial...
Furthermore, clouds of canopies adorned with all kinds of blue jewel flowers appeared; ten kinds of clouds of canopies made of all-fragrant mani-jewels appeared;
ten kinds of clouds of canopies of jewel-flame lamps appeared; ten kinds of clouds of canopies of mani-kings that manifest the supernatural powers and preaching of the Buddhas appeared;
and ten kinds of clouds of mani-jewels manifesting the colors and forms of all clothing and ornaments appeared.
Clouds of canopies reappeared, manifesting ten kinds of radiant clouds of all-jeweled flower clusters; clouds of canopies reappeared, manifesting ten kinds of sounds from jewel nets and bells;
clouds of canopies reappeared, manifesting ten kinds of mani-jewel pedestals with lotus flowers as their nets;
clouds of canopies reappeared, manifesting ten kinds of images of inconceivable ornaments appearing in all their forms—such were these clouds of canopies.
Clouds of various precious canopies, as numerous as the atoms within oceans of worlds, completely filled the void without dispersing or ceasing;
manifesting these clouds, they prostrated before the Buddha as an offering, and immediately to the southeast,
each miraculously created a lion throne of jewel lotus-treasury and sat upon it cross-legged within this Flower Treasury World-Ocean.
To the southwest, there is a world-ocean named Sunlight Pervasively Illuminating.
Within that world-system, there is a land named Lion Sun Radiance, where the Buddha is named Universal Wisdom Radiant Sound.
Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Universal Flower Radiant Flame Topknot, who is equal in number to the atoms within an ocean of worlds.

A multitude of bodhisattvas came together to the place where the Buddha was, each manifesting ten kinds of clouds of various wondrously adorned jewel parasols that filled the void without dispersing; they further manifested ten kinds of clouds of flower parasols adorned with light;
they further manifested ten kinds of clouds of pearl-treasury parasols of boundless colors; and they further manifested ten kinds [of clouds] from which all bodhisattvas emerged.
Again, clouds of mani-kings’ canopies with sounds of compassion appeared; again, clouds of canopies of garlands of flames of ten kinds of various exquisite jewels appeared;
again, clouds of canopies of hanging nets and bells adorned with ten kinds of exquisite jewels appeared; again, clouds of canopies adorned with branches of mani-trees appeared;
again, clouds of mani-kings’ canopies with sunlight shining everywhere appeared; again, ten [such clouds] appeared.
Clouds of all kinds of ointment-incense and burning-incense canopies appeared; furthermore, ten kinds of sandalwood-treasury canopies appeared;
furthermore, ten kinds of vast Buddha-realms universally radiant and adorned canopies appeared.

Such clouds of various precious canopies, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely filled the void without dispersing or perishing. Having manifested these clouds, they turned toward [the Buddha].

The Buddha paid homage as an act of worship and immediately, to the southwest, manifested lion thrones adorned with the light-flames of sapphire-blue jewels, each within its own treasury; upon these thrones he sat cross-legged.
To the northwest of this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, there is another world-ocean named Jewel Radiance; within that world-system, there is...
The land is named Adorned with Various Fragrances, and the Buddha’s name is Light of the Ocean of Immeasurable Merits.
Within that ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva named King of Inexhaustible Radiance Maṇi,
who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came to the place where the Buddha was, each manifesting ten kinds of all-jeweled spheres.
The clouds of full radiance pervaded all of space without dispersing or ceasing;

furthermore, there appeared ten kinds of clouds of perfect light-flames of all jewels, ten kinds of clouds of perfect light of all exquisite flowers, ten kinds of clouds of perfect light of all emanation-buddhas, and ten kinds of clouds of perfect light of the buddha-lands of the ten directions. Furthermore—
There further appeared ten kinds of clouds of perfect light from jewel trees with the thunderous sound of the Buddha’s realm;

there further appeared ten kinds of clouds of perfect light from all kinds of lapis lazuli jewel-mani kings; there further appeared ten kinds of clouds of perfect light manifesting the forms of infinite sentient beings within a single thought-moment;
and there further appeared ten kinds of clouds of perfect light proclaiming the sounds of the great vows of all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, ten kinds of clouds of full radiance that manifest the voices of all sentient beings through their transformations—
namely, clouds of the perfect radiance of the *maṇi* king— and clouds of full radiance as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, all pervaded the void without dispersing or ceasing.
Having manifested these clouds, they paid homage to the Buddha as an offering, and then, from each of the northwestern directions...
He manifested a lion throne of inexhaustible radiance and majestic power, and sat upon it in the full lotus posture.
Beneath this Flower Treasury Ocean of Worlds, there is another ocean of worlds named Lotus Fragrance Sublime Virtue Treasury.
Within that world-system, there is a land named Radiant Illumination of Jewel Lions, where the Buddha’s name is Dharma.

Within that ocean-like assembly of the Tathāgata, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Dharmadhātu-jvālā-prabhā-mati, who, together with as many bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, came to where the Buddha was.
Each manifested ten kinds of clouds of light from all the treasuries of maṇi jewels, which filled the void without dispersing or ceasing; furthermore, they manifested—
Ten kinds of clouds of light from all fragrances appeared; ten kinds of clouds of light from all jewel flames appeared;
ten kinds of clouds of light emitting the sounds of all Buddhas preaching the Dharma appeared;
ten kinds of clouds of light manifesting the adornments of all Buddha-lands appeared; and ten kinds of clouds of light from all exquisite flowered pavilions appeared.
Furthermore, ten kinds of light-clouds manifesting the deeds of all Buddhas teaching and transforming sentient beings throughout all kalpas appeared;
ten kinds of light-clouds of the filaments of all inexhaustible jewel-flowers appeared; and ten kinds of light-clouds of all adorned seats appeared.
Such light-clouds, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, completely pervaded the void.
Though empty and without dispersal or extinction, these clouds appeared and paid homage to the Buddha as an offering;
they then each miraculously manifested at the nadir a lion throne of precious flaming lamps within a lotus treasury, upon which they sat cross-legged.
Above this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, there is another world-ocean named Mani-Jewel Illumination.
Within that world-system called Resplendent Adornment, there is a land named Subtle Light of Signlessness;

therein resides a Tathāgata named King of Unobstructed Merit Radiance. Within the ocean-like assembly of that Tathāgata, there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Unobstructed Power and Vigorous Wisdom, who, together with as many Bodhisattvas as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, has come to this place.
Each Buddha manifested ten kinds of clouds of radiant flames of jewel-light with infinite forms and colors, which filled all of space without dispersing or extinguishing;
furthermore, they manifested ten kinds of clouds of radiant flames of mani-jewel nets,
ten kinds of clouds of radiant flames adorning all vast buddha-fields, and ten kinds of clouds of radiant flames of all sublime fragrances.
He manifested ten kinds of clouds of light-flames of all-encompassing adornments; he further manifested ten kinds of clouds of light-flames of the various transformations of all Buddhas;
he further manifested ten kinds of clouds of light-flames of exquisite trees and flowers; he further manifested ten kinds of clouds of light-flames of all vajras;
he further manifested ten kinds of clouds of light-flames of mani-jewels proclaiming the boundless practices of Bodhisattvas; he further manifested...
Ten kinds of clouds of light-flames from all pearl-lamp radiance, and so forth— clouds of light-flames as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds—
pervaded the entirety of space without dispersing or extinguishing. Having manifested these clouds, they prostrated before the Buddha as an offering,
and immediately above each of them, they magically transformed into lion thrones of the Lotus Treasury, which emanated the light of the Buddha’s voice.
Upon those seats, they sat cross-legged; in this manner, within as many oceans of world-systems as there are atoms in ten billion buddha-fields,
there were as many bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as there are atoms in ten billion buddha-fields,
each surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds, who came together to assemble there.
Each of the bodhisattvas manifested clouds of various offerings, as numerous as the atoms within an ocean of worlds, adorned with every kind of ornament;
these filled the entirety of space without dispersing or vanishing. Having manifested these clouds, they prostrated before the Buddha as an act of worship.
Then, according to the power of their respective arrivals, each magically created a lion throne adorned with various jewels, and upon those thrones—
Having sat down thus in the full lotus posture, from every single pore of the bodies of those bodhisattvas,
there appeared ten world-ocean-microdust numbers of multicolored radiances composed of all kinds of jewels. Within each and every radiance,
there were manifested ten world-ocean-microdust numbers of bodhisattvas, all seated upon lion thrones within lotus treasuries.
Seated here, these bodhisattvas are all able to enter universally into every atom within the ocean of all established realms throughout the entire dharma-realm.
Within each and every atom, there are vast lands as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-worlds;
within each of these lands, there are the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, of the three periods of time. These bodhisattvas are all able to go everywhere to personally attend them.
In every thought-moment, through the dharma-gate of manifesting mastery over dreams as an act of near-offering, they awaken world-ocean-microdust numbers of sentient beings;
in every thought-moment, through the dharma-gate of manifesting the death and rebirth of all devas, they awaken world-ocean-microdust numbers of sentient beings;
and in every thought-moment, through the teaching of all bodhisattva practices, they awaken world-ocean-microdust numbers of sentient beings.
The Dharma-door of Awakening World-Ocean-Dust-Numbered Sentient Beings in Every Thought-Moment through Universally Shaking All Lands and Praising the Buddha’s Merits and Spiritual Transformations;
and the Dharma-door of Awakening World-Ocean-Dust-Numbered Sentient Beings in Every Thought-Moment through Adorning and Purifying All Buddha-Lands and Manifesting the Ocean of All Great Vows.
He awakens world-ocean-microdust-numbered sentient beings in every thought-moment through the Dharma-door of the Buddha’s voice using speech that universally encompasses all sentient beings;

he awakens world-ocean-microdust-numbered sentient beings in every thought-moment through the Dharma-door of being able to rain down clouds of all Buddha-dharmas; he awakens world-ocean-microdust-numbered sentient beings in every thought-moment...
In every thought-moment, by means of the dharma-gate of manifesting spiritual transformations that universally illumines the lands of the ten directions and pervades the entire dharma-realm,
he awakens sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within oceans of worlds. In every thought-moment, by means of the dharma-gate of the power of liberation of all Tathāgatas,
which universally manifests Buddha-bodies filling the entire dharma-realm, he awakens sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within oceans of worlds.
In every thought-moment, through the Dharma-gate of establishing all assemblies and ocean-like sites of enlightenment by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
he awakens world-oceans as numerous as the atoms within them; thus pervading the entire Dharma-realm,
he causes all sentient beings to awaken according to their minds, and in every thought-moment, in each and every land, he causes [the manifestations] to be like Mount Sumeru.
May as many sentient beings as there are atoms in a mote of dust who have fallen into the evil realms be forever freed from their suffering;
may as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru who abide in false certainty be led into the assembly of those with right certainty;

and may as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru be born in the heavens according to their respective inclinations. May [as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru] likewise be so transformed.
He causes as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru to dwell securely in the stages of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas;
he causes as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru to serve spiritual friends and fulfill various meritorious practices;

he causes as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru to resolve upon unexcelled Bodhicitta; and he causes as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru to advance toward [the goal].

At each stage of the Bodhisattva’s non-retrogressive ground, they cause sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru to attain the pure eye of wisdom and perceive all the equal dharmas seen by the Tathāgata;
they cause sentient beings as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru to dwell securely in the ocean of various powers and vows, taking inexhaustible wisdom as their method.

They then purified the Buddha-lands, causing as many sentient beings as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru to all dwell securely within the vast ocean of Vairocana’s vows and be born into the family of the Tathāgata. At that time, from within the radiance of those bodhisattvas,
voices simultaneously sounded forth, speaking these verses:
From within all the radiances, wondrous sounds emerge, Pervading all lands throughout the ten directions,
proclaiming the virtues of the sons of the Buddha. They are able to enter the sublime path to enlightenment,
Practicing through oceans of eons without weariness or fatigue, Causing suffering sentient beings to attain liberation.
With a mind free from inferiority or weariness, the Son of the Buddha skillfully enters these expedient means;
practicing them throughout oceans of kalpas, they enter every single dharma-gate—
immeasurable, boundless, and without exception— while constantly proclaiming that their nature is quiescent extinction.
All vows held by the Buddhas of the three times, I shall cultivate and fulfill them all;
Using these to benefit all sentient beings, I shall perform the pure deeds of my own practice.
Within the assemblies of all Buddhas, I shall go everywhere throughout the ten directions, leaving none unvisited.
All, by means of the ocean of profound wisdom, enter that Tathāgata’s dharma of quiescent extinction;
each and every light is boundless, all entering inconceivable lands,
which the pure eye of wisdom can see everywhere— this is the sphere of activity of these bodhisattvas.

The Bodhisattva is able to abide upon the tip of a single hair, Causing all lands throughout the ten directions to tremble universally, Yet without causing sentient beings to have any thought of fear; This is the stage of pure skillful means.
Within each and every atom, infinite bodies appear, Furthermore manifesting various kinds of adorned buddha-fields.
May all who die and are reborn in a single thought-moment Attain the adornment of unimpeded wisdom;
May they be able to manifest within a single instant All kalpas of the three periods of time.
Knowing that the body is like an illusion, devoid of essence or form, They realize and testify to the unimpeded nature of reality (dharmatā).

Within this, bodhisattvas practice together to benefit sentient beings. The section on "The Realm" answers the thirty-seven doubts previously raised by the great assembly, so as to bring about an awakening in future ages identical to that of the present, wherein the realms of body and mind are sovereign and unimpeded, like the realm of Indra’s net.
