Chapter Two: The Remainder of the "Appearance of the Tathāgata’s Signs.
[Sūtra] At that time, the World-Honored One, wishing to cause the entire assembly of bodhisattvas to attain the boundless realm of the Tathāgata, [spoke as follows].
By the power of his mastery over the realms, he emitted a ray of light from between his eyebrows;
this light was named "The Universal Illumination of the Wisdom-Light of All Bodhisattvas, the Treasury of the Ten Directions.

Its form was like a cloud of jewel-colored lamps that shone everywhere throughout all Buddha-fields in the ten directions, causing all those lands and their sentient beings to appear clearly. Furthermore, it caused all worlds to tremble universally.

Within each and every pore of the net, countless Buddhas appear, universally raining down clouds of the wondrous Dharma wheels of all Buddhas of the three periods of time according to the differing inclinations and desires of sentient beings; they manifest the ocean of the Tathāgatas’ perfections (*pāramitā*).
Furthermore, they rain down immeasurable clouds of renunciation, causing all sentient beings to forever cross over birth and death; they also rain down the great vows of all Buddhas.

Having manifested the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva throughout the worlds of the ten directions, Cloud Display circumambulated the Buddha to the right and entered through the soles of his feet. At that time, a great lotus flower suddenly appeared before the Buddha;
this flower possessed ten kinds of adornments that no other lotus could equal, namely: [the assembly of... (as per the provided fragment).
Its stalk was composed of various interspersed jewels, its core of the sovereign maṇi-jewel king, its leaves formed from all the jewels of the dharma-realm, and its filaments from fragrant maṇis.
Its pedestal was adorned with Jāmbūnada gold and covered by a wondrous net of pure, radiant colors.
Within a single thought-moment, it manifested the infinite spiritual transformations of all Buddhas.
This king of mani-jewels capable of producing all sounds manifests the bodies of Buddhas within those sounds,
universally proclaiming all the practices and vows cultivated by Bodhisattvas. Once this flower has arisen, in a single thought-moment,
there is a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Sarvadharma-jaya-ghoṣa within the *ūrṇā-kośa* (white tuft) of the Tathāgata, who [appears] together with the world.
A multitude of bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms within oceans of world-systems, emerged simultaneously and circumambulated the Tathāgata to the right for immeasurable circuits.

Having prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, the Bodhisattva Supreme Sound sat upon the lotus pedestal, while the assembly of bodhisattvas sat upon the lotus filaments, each taking their place in succession. Then, the Bodhisattva Supreme Sound of All Dharmas realized the profound.
Giving rise to great joy within the Dharma-realm, they enter the wisdom of the Buddhas' sphere of action without doubt or obstruction;
they enter the unfathomable ocean of the Buddhas' Dharma-body and travel to the abodes of all Tathāgatas in all lands, manifesting spiritual powers from every pore of their bodies.

Moment by moment, they universally contemplate the entire Dharma-realm, and the Buddhas of the ten directions collectively bestow their power upon them, causing them to dwell securely in universal peace.
Remaining in samādhi throughout all future kalpas, constantly beholding the Buddhas and the bodies of the ocean of merit within the boundless Dharma-realm,
and even all samādhis, liberations, supernormal powers, and transformations, he then, by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power,
surveyed the ten directions amidst the assembly and spoke in verse:
The Buddha’s body fills the entire Dharma-realm, Appearing universally before all sentient beings;
Responding to conditions and meeting needs without exception, Yet he ever remains upon this seat of Bodhi.
Within each and every pore of the Tathāgata, All Buddhas sit amidst the atoms of every world-system.
Surrounded by the assembly of Bodhisattvas, he expounds the sublime conduct of Samantabhadra.
The Tathāgata, seated upon the seat of enlightenment, manifests oceans of many lands within a single pore;
it is likewise in every single pore, pervading the entire Dharma-realm in this manner.
Sitting serenely within each and every land, they pervade all buddha-fields throughout the ten directions;
bodhisattvas gather like clouds, none failing to come to the site of enlightenment.
In number equal to the atoms of all buddha-fields, there is an ocean of bodhisattvas with the radiance of merit.
Universally present within the assemblies of the Tathāgatas, Pervading everywhere throughout the entire realm of phenomena,
even within the lands as numerous as atoms; Manifesting thus within all such multitudes—
this sphere of wisdom of the emanated bodies— Can be established through the practices of Samantabhadra.
Within the assemblies of all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas of supreme wisdom sit together;

each listens to the Dharma and gives rise to joy. Having practiced in every place for immeasurable eons, they have entered the vast vows of Samantabhadra; each brings forth the manifold teachings of the Buddha.
Within the ocean of Vairocana’s Dharma, Through cultivation, one realizes the stage of the Tathāgata.
Awakened by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, All Tathāgatas join in praise and joy.
Having attained the great supernormal powers of all Buddhas, One flows throughout the Dharma-realm, reaching everywhere.
In numbers equal to the atoms of all buddha-fields, they constantly manifest clouds of bodies that completely fill [the world],
universally emitting great rays of light for the sake of sentient beings, each raining down the rain of Dharma according to their inclinations.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another bodhisattva mahāsattva named Avalokiteśvara-padma-sarva-dharmābhyudgata.
King Prabhāmati, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
The Tathāgata’s profoundly deep wisdom universally enters the Dharma-realm; Able to revolve through the three periods of time, he serves as the guiding light for the world.
All Buddhas share the same Dharma-body; It is without dependence and without distinction.
In accordance with the inclinations of all sentient beings, They cause them to see the physical form of the Buddha;
Endowed with all-knowledge and universally cognizant of all phenomena, Throughout all lands, there is nowhere the Buddha’s body and radiance do not appear.
Their physical marks and characteristics are inconceivable for those sentient beings who have faith and joy.
According to their needs, he causes all to see, within the body of a single Buddha, manifested as infinite Buddhas;
with a thunderous voice that pervades all lands, he expounds the Dharma as deep as the ocean.
From every single pore, webs of light pervade the ten directions, proclaiming the wondrous sounds of the Buddha’s voice to subdue those who are difficult to tame.
From within the Tathāgata’s radiance, there constantly issues forth a profound and wondrous sound,
praising the ocean of the Buddha’s merits and the practices of the Bodhisattvas. As the Buddha turns the wheel of the True Dharma,
the teachings he proclaims are immeasurable and boundless, peerless and unfathomable to those of shallow wisdom throughout all worlds.
Manifesting their bodies as they attain perfect enlightenment, each displays miraculous transformations that completely fill the entire Dharma-realm.

From each and every body of the Tathāgata, there appear Buddhas equal in number to all sentient beings; throughout all lands as numerous as atoms, they universally manifest their powers of spiritual penetration.
At that time, there was another bodhisattva mahāsattva in the assembly named Dharmaprītiprajñāprabha, who, empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority,
surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
The Buddha’s body is eternally manifest, filling the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).

He constantly utters a vast sound that universally resounds throughout the lands of the ten directions. The Tathāgata manifests his body everywhere, entering all worlds according to the inclinations and desires of sentient beings, displaying his supernormal powers; the Buddha accords with the minds of sentient beings.
He manifests universally before them; whatever sentient beings behold, All is the Buddha’s spiritual power, boundless light, And his preaching of the Dharma is likewise immeasurable.
Sons of the Buddha, according to their capacities for wisdom, can enter and observe it: The Buddha-body has no birth, yet it can manifest birth.
The nature of phenomena is like space; All Buddhas dwell within it. Neither dwelling nor departing, they are seen everywhere;
Their radiance is all-pervading, And their renown is heard afar.
They have no substance and no place of abode, Nor can any birth be found; They are without marks and without form.
All that appears is like a shadow; according to the minds of sentient beings, the Buddha raises great clouds of Dharma through various gates of skillful means to instruct, awaken, and subdue them.
In all worlds, one sees the Buddha sitting at the site of enlightenment, surrounded by a great assembly, illuminating the lands of the ten directions.
The bodies of all Buddhas possess inexhaustible marks; though they manifest immeasurable forms and appearances, they are ultimately never exhausted.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another bodhisattva-mahāsattva named Fragrant Flame Light Universal Radiance Wisdom, who, having received the Buddha’s...
Observing the ten directions with majestic spiritual power, he spoke these verses:
"The bodhisattvas in this assembly have entered the inconceivable stages of the Buddha. Each and every one is able to perceive the spiritual powers of all Buddhas;
their bodies of wisdom can universally enter into all the atoms within every land."
Seeing one's own body therein, one sees all Buddhas everywhere; like reflections appearing in all lands where the Tathāgatas dwell, within all of those, one manifests miraculous deeds.

In all Buddha-lands, they manifest their supernatural powers, Displaying various bodies and various names;
Within a single moment, they universally manifest All manner of miraculous transformations,
Attaining perfect enlightenment at the site of awakening And turning the sublime wheel of Dharma Throughout all vast realms.
Within the inconceivable samādhis of bodhisattvas throughout billions of eons,
they are able to manifest all buddha-lands in a single thought-moment; each and every bodhisattva universally enters the body of the Buddha,
which is boundless and inexhaustible.
At that time, there was another bodhisattva mahāsattva in the assembly named Siṃhavikrāntamatividyūtaprabha, who,
receiving the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
Vairocana Buddha is able to turn the true wheel of Dharma; throughout all lands of the dharma-realm, he pervades them all like clouds.
Within all the great oceans of worlds throughout the ten directions, by the power of his buddha-activities and vows, he turns the wheel of Dharma everywhere in all buddha-fields.
Within vast assemblies, names differ according to each; He expounds the wondrous Dharma as is appropriate.
The Tathāgata’s great majestic power is accomplished through the vows of Samantabhadra; Throughout all lands, his sublime voice reaches everywhere.
The Buddha’s body is equal in extent to the dust motes of all realms, Universally raining down the rain of Dharma.
Unborn and without distinction, yet manifesting throughout all worlds;
Throughout countless billions of eons, within every atom and every land, The deeds performed in the past are all fully proclaimed by wondrous voices.
In lands as numerous as atoms in the ten directions, networks of light pervade everywhere; Within every ray of light, there is a Buddha.
Universally transforming all classes of beings, the Buddha-body is without distinction;
it fills the entire dharma-realm and enables them to behold the form-body. According to their capacities, he skillfully tames them.

all of this is heard by those in this assembly.

They proclaim the sphere of the Buddha’s conduct, heard throughout the lands of the ten directions; within each and every thought-moment, they universally contemplate all phenomena.

The vast voices of all Buddhas, throughout the entire Dharma-realm, are heard by none; Bodhisattvas are able to understand them and skillfully enter the ocean of sounds.

Those whose wisdom pervades the three periods of time enter that stage of vocal resonance; so too do they comprehend every sound of all sentient beings.

With the light of wisdom universally clear and bright, he is able to know all Buddhas and the sovereign nature of their essence.
Seeing the true body of the Buddha, one awakens to the most profound Dharma; Universally observing the entire dharma-realm, they assume bodies according to their vows.
Born from an ocean of merit, dwelling upon the ground of wisdom,
Observing all phenomena and practicing the supreme path, Within all Buddha-fields, wherever Tathāgatas reside,
Thus pervading the entire Dharma-realm, they perceive the true essence Throughout the vast lands of the ten directions.
Having diligently practiced for billions of eons, you are able to roam through the knowledge of the Truly All-Knowing One.
The ocean of all dharmas is the single, firm, and secret body; it is seen within every atom.
Unborn and without marks, you appear universally in all lands, manifesting before all sentient beings in accordance with their minds.

Through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, bodhisattvas appear; sustained by the Buddha’s might, they universally behold all Tathāgatas, the Teachers of the Multitude, and through their immeasurable majestic spiritual power, they awaken all bodhisattvas.

Through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, they observe all phenomena.

One accomplishes all-knowledge, enters the deep ocean of Dharma, and dwells securely in the Buddha-lands. Arising everywhere, one neither goes nor comes.
Such is the nature of all Buddhas; the ocean of all sentient beings likewise appears as reflections within the Buddha-body according to their various understandings. Thus do they behold the Guide:
from every single pore, he manifests supernatural powers. Those who have purified themselves through the practice of Samantabhadra’s vows are able to see this.
With each and every body, the Buddha turns the wheel of Dharma in every place; it pervades the entire dharma-realm, beyond the reach of thought.

The Buddha’s body is inconceivable; all lands are contained within it. In every such place, he guides the world and proclaims the true Dharma.

The wondrous wheel of Dharma that he turns is based on the undifferentiated nature of phenomena (dharmatā) and the single principle of ultimate reality. He expounds the characteristics of all dharmas with a perfectly complete voice.

there one sees the Buddha seated at the site of enlightenment, his body appearing like a reflection,
where neither arising nor ceasing can be apprehended.
At that time, there was another bodhisattva mahāsattva in the assembly named Dharmadhātu-samantāloka-mati, who, empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority,
surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse:
The Tathāgata’s subtle and wondrous body, Its form and characteristics are inconceivable; Those who see it give rise to joy, reverence, and faith, and delight in the Dharma.
Every single mark upon the Buddha’s body Manifests infinite Buddhas, Universally entering the realms of the ten directions;
Within each and every atom, Are oceans of lands throughout the ten directions.
The infinite and boundless Buddhas, in every single thought-moment, each manifesting spiritual powers;
The Bodhisattvas of Great Wisdom, who have deeply entered the ocean of Dharma; Sustained by the power of the Buddhas, they are able to know this skillful means.
If there are those who already abide securely in all the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, [they shall likewise attain this].
Beholding all those world-systems through the spiritual power of all Buddhas,
if a person possesses faith and understanding as well as great vows, and is endowed with profound wisdom,
they will penetrate all phenomena and be able to examine each and every body of the Buddhas, unimpeded by form or sound.

Universally encompassing the entire Dharma-realm, they are able to manifest within a single thought-moment all such lands—as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field—within every single atom.

such is the power of the Bodhisattva.
At that time, within the assembly, there was another Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Unobstructed Wisdom of Diligent Power who, having received the Buddha’s...
Observing the ten directions with majestic spiritual power, he spoke in verse:
The Buddha utters a single wondrous sound, Which is heard throughout the lands of the ten directions. All voices are fully contained within it;

In all Buddha-fields, they turn the pure wheel of Dharma; In all lands, they behold the Buddha’s miraculous transformations And hear the sound of the Buddha preaching the Dharma.
Having heard it, they proceed toward Bodhi throughout the lands of the Dharma-realm; Within every single atom, there is the power of the Tathāgata’s liberation.
Manifesting bodies everywhere therein, the Dharma-body is equal to space;
Unobstructed and without distinction, its forms and colors are like reflections, Appearing with all manner of diverse marks.
These reflections have no location, and like space, they lack intrinsic nature; The person of vast wisdom thoroughly realizes their equality.
The Buddha-body is ungraspable; It is without birth and without arising. Appearing universally before all things, it is equal like space.
All Buddhas throughout the ten directions Are entirely contained within a single pore, Each manifesting their own spiritual powers;
Only those with the eye of wisdom can perceive this— The Buddha Vairocana.
The power of his vows pervades the entire Dharma-realm; throughout all lands, he constantly turns the unsurpassed wheel.
Within a single hair-pore he manifests spiritual transformations, which all Buddhas proclaim together; even after passing through immeasurable eons, one cannot reach their limit.
Thus, within the site of enlightenment in this world-system of four continents, one should know that by the Buddha’s spiritual power,
assemblies of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten million world-oceans have gathered from each of the ten directions;
and it should be understood that this is likewise the case in every single site of enlightenment within every world-system of four continents throughout all world-oceans.

[Treatise] Fourth: From the passage beginning "At that time, the World-Honored One, desiring to cause the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas to attain the boundless realm of the Tathāgata" (484 characters), there is a long prose section consisting of twenty-eight and a half lines of scripture.
This is divided into two parts: first, from the beginning, ten lines of scripture clarify the virtue of light; second...

The eight-and-a-half-fascicle sutra clarifies the first [chapter], "The Manifestation of the Lotus. Regarding the general meaning of the first section, which elucidates the virtue of light, there are eleven points:
(1) causing the assembly to eliminate doubts and obtain benefit; (2) revealing the source from which the light emerges; (3) revealing the name of the light; (4) revealing the color of the light;
(5) clarifying the distance to which the light shines; and (6) clarifying the majestic movement produced by the light's illumination.

The seven lights illuminate the world, appearing within the dust motes as countless Buddhas who bestow benefit according to the faculties [of beings]. The eighth light rains down clouds of the ten kinds of Dharma wheels.
The ninth light circles the Buddha. The tenth light enters the wheel-marks on the soles of the Buddha’s feet, thereby perfecting the faith of the great assembly;
for it is clear that the soles of the feet are where initial faith enters, and thus the ten kinds of wisdom-Buddhas are taught as being one's own self.

Faith takes the wisdom of immovability as its primary characteristic. Second, at that time, the eighteen and a half lines of scripture following "In front of the Buddha" clarify the appearance of the lotus flower.
Within this section, there are eleven main points: first, clarifying the cause for the manifestation of the flower;
second, clarifying that the flower is endowed with ten kinds of adornments; third, clarifying the emergence of the light from the *ūrṇā* (hair-treasure) and the arrival of the assembly.
1. Seated with the Bodhisattva Supreme Sound as the principal figure and others as his retinue;
2. The supreme qualities of the Bodhisattva Supreme Sound’s mastery of the five sciences; 3. All Buddhas bestowing power upon Supreme Sound;
4. Supreme Sound constantly beholding all Buddhas; 5. Supreme Sound’s sovereign mastery of spiritual transformations; 6. Supreme Sound observing the assemblies and speaking in verse.

This section of the sūtra clarifies the meaning of the verse: "The light emerging from the ūrṇā between the Tathāgata’s eyebrows, named 'The Universal Radiance of All Bodhisattvas Pervasively Illuminating the Treasuries of the Ten Directions,' clarifies that this is the light of the path of practice and realization within the wisdom-perfection of the tenth-stage bodhisattva;
furthermore, from within the ūrṇā-mark emerge various bodhisattvas who possess worldly..."
The leader among those as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of realms, named Sarvadharmavijayasvara (All-Dharmas-Supreme-Sound),

is the one who has fulfilled the fruit and practice of the Middle Way across the ten stages; he shall, by means of this dharma-gate of the Middle Way— wherein awakening-practice, compassion, wisdom, and the activities of the Dharma-realm are perfected—
respond to the thirty-seven questions of the great assembly through the unobstructed dharma of the oceans of lands within a single hair-pore.

In the present and the future, those who believe in this Dharma-gate of the causes and effects of the ten stages within the *dharmadhātu* shall fulfill their practices throughout the ten directions and cause all to obtain benefit.

Therefore, the Sūtra says: "Desiring to enable the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas to attain the power of the Tathāgata’s boundless realm and supernormal knowledges (*abhijñā*), he emits light from between his eyebrows. Furthermore, the essence of this light is the Dharma itself.
The ocean-like assembly of the Supreme Sound (Ghoṣadatta) is the functional application of the practice of the Dharma-realm;
thus, it clarifies that from the initial mind of the ten abodes (*daśabhūmi*), the essence and function of the myriad practices of principle and wisdom are inseparable.

Therefore, from the stage of the ten faiths (*daśa-śraddhā*), one immediately accords with the conduct of fruition, causing the cultivation of the essence and function of principle and wisdom to be unified. Consequently, one proceeds from the conduct of fruition toward faith and advancement.

Furthermore, while the Bodhisattva Supreme Sound (*Jin-yin*) sits upon the lotus pedestal and the assembly of all other bodhisattvas sit upon the lotus filaments, this clarifies the relationship between the principal and the retinue.
It demonstrates that the myriad practices of all bodhisattvas are encompassed within the single practice of the Bodhisattva Supreme Sound;

for all those myriad practices are the single practice of Supreme Sound, which is the unimpeded and sovereign practice fully perfected within the wisdom and principle of the Dharma-realm. Thus, it is as explained previously.
The light rays flowing from the pores of a Bodhisattva manifest the essential nature of Bodhisattva practices as being identical yet diverse, mutually inclusive, and infinitely sovereign.
They are without substance and cannot be obstructed, for within each single *pāramitā* all ten are fully present, extending even to infinity.

Because they arise through dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda*), they function as mutual causes and effects, with the primary and the attendant in sovereign harmony. This general meaning can be perceived by illuminating them with the wisdom of principle (*li-zhi*).

The *Dharmadhātu-caryā-mukha-prakāśana* (Illumination of the Gate of Practice in the Dharma-realm): Because a single practice pervades all practices, there is mastery over both the identical and the distinct.
This section correctly explains the intent of the verses. Within it, the Bodhisattva Samantaghoṣa has ten bodhisattvas, each presenting a segment of verse.
The first twenty lines of verse praise the Buddha’s body for its pervasive omnipresence, manifesting before all sentient beings and within every pore, land, and world-system.
The assembly’s inexhaustible characteristics and their mutual entry are clarified in detail by the two lines of one verse as presented in the text; there is no need for further explanation.
Once the general principle and the main outline are grasped, the meaning of the sūtra text will naturally become clear. These ten sections of verses comprise nine segments totaling ten lines;

this final segment collectively answers the questions posed by the World-Ruling Lord in the previous life and further clarifies that the bodhisattvas of this assembly are capable [of such realization].
Entering the realm of the Tathāgata, there are three lines of scripture (fifty-one characters) at the very end that clarify the collective conclusion:

that the worlds of the ten directions likewise gather together simultaneously. Above this, the manifestation of supernatural powers and the verbal responses have concluded the answers to the doubts of the great assembly.
As for the demonstration of karma and the teaching of the Dharma, it is as follows: in the "World-Formation" chapter (*Lokadhātunirdeśa*), within the *Lotus Treasury* (*Padmagarbha*).
In the *World Chapter*, the *Vairocana Chapter*, and the *Chapter on the Manifestation of Supernatural Powers and Dharma-Activities*,

these are presented collectively as the answer concerning the dharma-activities inherent to each respective category of supernormal power. Thus, the first assembly consists of six chapters— the *Samādhi of Samantabhadra*, the *Accomplishment of Worlds*,
the *Flower Treasury World*, and the *Vairocana*— which exhort the cultivation of the Buddha-fruit.
Chapter Three:

The Samādhi of Samantabhadra [Śāstra] To explain this chapter, it shall be briefly analyzed through three sections: first, the explanation of the title of the chapter; second, the explanation of the chapter’s content.
The intention for [this section] is threefold. First, the explanation of the title of the chapter: "Universal Wisdom" (*prajñā*) refers to the boundlessness of principle and wisdom;
"Worthy One" (*bhadra*) refers to benefiting others according to their faculties. "Samādhi" is called "right absorption" (*samyaksamādhi*);
it is "right" because it is undisturbed, and it is "absorption" (*samāpatti*) because it can receive, retain, and discern all phenomena. Thus, it is named "right absorption."
It is also called *samādhi* (equipoise), because it is the correct concentration that can give rise to correct wisdom;

since it is the basis for all dharmas of equipoise, it is thus named *samādhi*. It is Samantabhadra, the heir to the Buddha’s house of great wisdom within the *dharmadhātu*, and the eldest son of the Buddhas whose myriad practices are universally pervasive.
This answers the first of the thirty-seven questions previously asked: "What is one?"

Because one must enter meditative concentration (*samādhi*) to thoroughly discern all phenomena— such as the ocean of all bodhisattva practices, the ocean of renunciations, the ocean of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), the ocean of perfections (*pāramitā*), and the ocean of worlds—
in order to answer the questions previously posed and cause the delusions of the assembly to be resolved, it is necessary to enter concentration. However,
because Samantabhadra Bodhisattva is eternally free from both concentration and distraction in order to demonstrate the Dharma-principle, he must act in this manner.
Furthermore, the initial section exhorts practice by citing the fruit; the middle section takes entry into meditative concentration as its principle;
and the subsequent "Ten Concentrations" chapter clarifies that when the ten stages are perfected and various conceptions arise, one truly enters the second stage.

The intent behind the "Two Explanations" chapter is to clarify that Samantabhadra Bodhisattva constantly abides in samādhi, wherein stillness and distraction are universally true, and thus he accomplishes the Dharma by teaching and transforming sentient beings.

He answered the questions and doubts that had arisen; he skillfully discerned the characteristics of the entry into and emergence from, as well as the similarities and differences between, the various samādhis;
and he skillfully chose [to explain] the ocean of karmic results of sentient beings and the ocean of karmic results of the Buddha’s own deeds.
Having thus entered meditative concentration and emerged from it, he spoke the "Chapter on the Formation of Worlds" and the "Chapter on the Flower Treasury World," concerning Vairocana.

This chapter answers the questions posed previously; thus, the reason this chapter must appear is to clarify that when first entering the Dharma, one must apply meditative concentration (*samādhi*) and karmic action to manifest the gateway of reality.
In the subsequent ten chapters on *Samādhi*, the true wisdom of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) has already been fully explained.

Now, it is shown that wisdom must accord with the thoughts and perceptions of all sentient beings, responding to their faculties to engage them—this is precisely how a practitioner of the Path should understand it. (3)
Regarding the explanation of the meaning according to the text, within this chapter of the sutra, the meaning is divided into two sections: first, the intent of the sutra;
second, the explanation of the name of the samādhi. As for the first section, the intent of the sutra:
[Sūtra] At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra sat upon a lion throne within the Lotus Treasury before the Tathāgata.

Empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, he entered into a samādhi called "The Universal Entry into the Equality of All Buddhas and the Body-Treasury of Vairocana Tathāgata," which is able to manifest to all within the Dharma-realm.
These images are vast and unimpeded, equal to space; they enter without exception into the whirlpools of the ocean of the Dharma-realm.

They give rise to all dharmas of samādhi and are universally able to encompass the ocean of the light of wisdom of the Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time, all of which arise from them.
All the oceans of established realms existing throughout the ten directions can be manifested and contained within them.
The power of all Buddhas, the liberation of the wisdom of all Bodhisattvas, which enables all atoms within every land to universally contain the infinite Dharma-realm;
which accomplishes the ocean of all Buddha-merits; which manifests the great ocean of the Tathāgatas' vows;
and which ensures that all wheels of Dharma of all Buddhas circulate and are upheld without interruption—such as this.
In this world, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva entered this samādhi before the World-Honored One; likewise, throughout the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space,
in all ten directions and the three periods of time, there were subtle, unimpeded, and vast luminous lands seen by the Buddha-eye,
reached by the Buddha’s power, and manifested by the Buddha’s body— including every single atom within all those lands and within this very land.
Within a single atom, there are Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds; within each of these lands, there are Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds;

and before each of these Buddhas, there are Samantabhadra Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds—all of whom likewise enter this Samādhi of the Tathāgata Vairocana’s Body-Treasury of All Buddhas. At that time...
Before each and every Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, all the Buddhas of the ten directions appeared;
those Tathāgatas spoke in unison, praising him: "Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You are able to enter this Bodhisattva samādhi of the Body-Treasury of Vairocana Tathāgata, which encompasses all Buddhas. Son of the Buddha, this is the one [samādhi] of the ten directions..."
All Buddhas together empower you through the power of the original vows of Vairocana Tathāgata,
and also through the power of your own cultivation of the practices and vows of all Buddhas— namely, because you are able to turn the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas,
reveal the ocean of wisdom of all Tathāgatas, and universally illumine all oceans of established worlds throughout the ten directions, leaving none unmanifested.
Furthermore, it causes all sentient beings to purify their various defilements and attain purity; it universally encompasses all great lands without attachment;
it penetrates deeply into the realms of all Buddhas without obstruction; it universally manifests all the merits of the Buddhas;
and it enables the entry into the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena, increasing wisdom—thus one contemplates.
Because he examines all dharma-gates, understands the faculties of all sentient beings, and is able to uphold the ocean-like collection of teachings and texts of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas,

at that time all the Buddhas of the ten directions immediately bestowed upon the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra the power of wisdom to enter the nature of omniscience and the wisdom to enter the boundless measure of the Dharma-realm.
The wisdom that accomplishes the realm of all Buddhas; the wisdom that knows the formation and destruction of all oceans of worlds;
the wisdom that knows the vastness of all realms of sentient beings; the wisdom of the various samādhis that abide in the profound liberation of all Buddhas without distinction;
the wisdom that enters the ocean of the faculties of all Bodhisattvas; and the wisdom that knows all sentient beings.
The wisdom of eloquence for turning the wheel of Dharma within oceans of speech; the wisdom of the body that universally enters all oceans of worlds within the dharma-realm;

and the wisdom of attaining the vocal sounds of all Buddhas—just as the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra received such wisdom from all the Buddhas before the Tathāgata in this world-system, so too did he receive it in all such oceans of world-systems and throughout those oceans of world-systems.
Within every single atom, all Samantabhadras are likewise so. Why is this? Because the Dharma of that samādhi is realized as such.
At that time, the Buddhas of the ten directions each extended their right hands and stroked the crown of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva’s head.
Those hands were all adorned with the marks and signs of excellence; they emitted wonderful nets of light, flowing fragrances, and blazing flames, and further produced the seeds of all Buddhas.
Within it appear all the matters of the various sublime sounds and sovereign spiritual powers of the past, present, and future;
the ocean of Samantabhadra’s vows of all bodhisattvas; the pure wheels of Dharma of all Tathāgatas; and the images of all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Just as in this world, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra is touched on the crown of his head by all the Buddhas of the ten directions, so too do they appear therein.

In this way, within every single atom of all these oceans of worlds and those individual atoms of each ocean of worlds, Samantabhadra likewise had his head stroked by the Buddhas of the ten directions.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra arose from this samādhi; as he arose from this samādhi, he emerged from the atoms of all oceans of worlds.
They arise from oceans of samādhi gates, namely: they arise from the samādhi gate of skillful wisdom that knows the non-differentiation of every thought-moment throughout the three periods of time;
they arise from the samādhi gate of knowing all atoms within the entire dharma-realm of the three periods of time;
they arise from the samādhi gate of manifesting all buddha-lands of the three periods of time; and they arise from the samādhi gate of manifesting the dwellings of all sentient beings.
They arise from the samādhi-door of knowing the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings; they arise from the samādhi-door of knowing the individual names of all sentient beings;
they arise from the samādhi-door of knowing the distinct locations and positions of the dharma-realms of the ten directions;
they arise from the samādhi-door of knowing that within every single atom there are infinitely vast Buddha-bodies.
When the Samādhi Door of Clouds arose from the Samādhi Door of Expounding the Ocean of Principles of All Dharmas,

and when Samantabhadra Bodhisattva arose from such samādhi doors as these, each of those bodhisattvas individually attained oceans of clouds of samādhis numbering as many as the atoms in an ocean of worlds,
and oceans of clouds of dhāraṇīs numbering as many as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.
Clouds of oceans of skillful means of all dharmas, as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds;
clouds of oceans of gateways of eloquence, as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds; clouds of oceans of practices, as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds;
clouds of oceans of the light of wisdom from the treasuries of merit of all Tathāgatas who universally illumine the dharma-realm, as numerous as the atoms in an ocean of worlds.

Within each and every pore of all Tathāgatas— numbering as many as the atoms in oceans of worlds within clouds of oceans of worlds, which are themselves as numerous as the atoms in the ocean of worlds of the "Cloud of Non-differentiated Expedient Means of the Wisdom and Powers of All Tathāgatas"—
each manifests a multitude of clouds of oceans of lands. Within each of these, bodhisattvas appear, numbering as many as the atoms in oceans of worlds within clouds of oceans of worlds,
manifesting their descent from the Tuṣita heaven, their birth, their attainment of Buddhahood, and their turning of the wheel of Dharma.

In this world-system, such as the ocean-cloud of the turning of the true Dharma wheel and the parinirvāṇa, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra arose from samādhi, and the assembly of bodhisattvas obtained such benefits.
In all such oceans of world-systems, and within every single atom of those oceans of world-systems, it was likewise in each and every atom. At that time, throughout all the ten directions...
By the power of the majestic spiritual authority of all Buddhas and the power of the samādhi of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, the oceans of worlds all tremble slightly;
each and every world is adorned with various jewels and emits sublime sounds that expound all dharmas.
Furthermore, within the ocean-like assemblies of all Tathāgatas at their sites of enlightenment, ten kinds of clouds of great *maṇi* kings rain down everywhere. What are they?
These constitute the ten, namely: clouds of mani-kings of exquisite golden star-pennants; clouds of mani-kings of radiant illumination;
clouds of mani-kings with jeweled wheels hanging down; clouds of mani-kings manifesting bodhisattva images from various jewel treasuries;
clouds of mani-kings proclaiming the names of Buddhas; and clouds of mani-kings whose blazing light universally illuminates the sites of enlightenment in all buddha-fields.
There were clouds of mani-kings illuminating the ten directions; clouds of mani-kings manifesting various transformations;
clouds of mani-kings praising the merits of all bodhisattvas; clouds of mani-kings as blazing and intense as the light of the sun;
clouds of mani-kings with delightful and pleasing sounds heard throughout the ten directions; and clouds of these ten kinds of great mani-kings raining everywhere.
Then, from every pore of all the Tathāgatas, rays of light were emitted, and within those rays, they spoke these verses:
Samantabhadra goes everywhere to all lands, Seated upon a precious lotus flower, beheld by all.
There are no supernatural powers that he does not manifest, And he is able to enter all immeasurable samādhis.
Samantabhadra constantly uses various bodies To circulate throughout the entire dharma-realm, filling it completely.
Through the power of his samādhis, supernatural faculties, and skillful means, He expounds the universal sound extensively and without obstruction.
In all buddha-fields, wherever the Buddhas dwell, they manifest various samādhis and supernatural powers;
each and every power pervades everywhere throughout the lands of the ten directions without exception.
Just as it is in the presence of the Tathāgatas in all fields, so too is it within every atom of those fields.
The manifestations of samādhi and supernormal powers are the power of Vairocana’s vows;
The body of Samantabhadra is like space, abiding in reality and not in a land.
According to the desires of the minds of all sentient beings, He manifests his universal body, equal to all.
Samantabhadra dwells securely in all great vows, Having attained these immeasurable powers of spiritual penetration;
Into every land belonging to all Buddha-bodies, He manifests his form and proceeds there.
The oceans of all assemblies are without limit, And his emanated bodies dwelling therein are likewise immeasurable.
The lands he manifests are all pure and adorned; In a single kṣaṇa, he perceives many kalpas.

Samantabhadra dwells peacefully in all lands; The spiritual powers he displays are supreme and peerless, Shaking the ten directions so that none are left untouched, Causing all who behold them to see clearly.
Through the power of the wisdom and merit of all Buddhas, All various great Dharmas are fully perfected;
By means of the gates of various samādhis and skillful methods, They manifest their own past practices for enlightenment.
Such sovereign and inconceivable [powers] Are manifested throughout the lands of the ten directions.
To manifest the universal entry into all samādhis, the Buddha’s clouds of light praised his virtues.

At that time, the entire assembly of bodhisattvas turned toward Samantabhadra, joined their palms, and gazed up at him; empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, they praised him with one voice, saying:
Born from the dharmas of all Buddhas, And arisen through the power of the Tathāgata’s vows,
The treasury of space, equal to true suchness (tathatā), You have already purified this Dharma-body;
Within the assemblies of all Buddha-fields, Samantabhadra dwells everywhere therein.
The radiance of the ocean of merit and wisdom shines equally throughout the ten directions,

such that there is nowhere it does not reach; Samantabhadra’s vast ocean of merit pervades all lands within every atom of the ten directions, Able to travel to each of them and manifest clearly therein.
O Son of the Buddha, we have always seen you; you have personally approached and dwelt in the samādhi of the true realm within all the Tathāgatas.
O Son of the Buddha, throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of all lands, you are able to manifest your universal body and travel to every land throughout the ten directions.
They ferry across the great ocean of sentient beings; There is not a single atom of the Dharma-realm that they do not enter.
Entering into every atom of the Dharma-realm, Their bodies are inexhaustible and without distinction, Pervading everywhere like empty space, As they proclaim the vast Dharma of the Tathāgata.
The Radiance of All Merit, you go forth to the ocean of sentient beings— vast, powerful, and most excellent—
as if unto clouds; you expound the peerless Dharma of the Buddha’s conduct throughout oceans of eons to deliver all beings, cultivating all the supreme practices of Samantabhadra.
You manifest all dharmas like a great cloud; your voice is so vast that there is nowhere it is not heard.
How are the lands established? How do the Buddhas appear, as well as the ocean of all sentient beings?
We pray that you will explain these matters according to their true meaning.
[Verse: Within this immeasurable ocean-like assembly, All stand before the Honored One with reverence;
To turn the pure and wondrous Wheel of Dharma, All Buddhas rejoice in unison.
[Treatise: This section of the sutra (consisting of eighty-two lines and one thousand three hundred fifty-six words) contains eleven points in its intent. First:
At that time, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra first clarifies entering meditative absorption by relying on the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power through one and a half lines of scripture;
second, from "Having entered this samādhi" onwards, eight and a half lines of scripture clarify the naming of the samādhi and the praise of its virtues;
third, from "In this world" onwards, approximately seven lines of scripture clarify the general presentation of Samantabhadra’s entry [into the state].
5. Establishing this realm as such, it is likewise throughout the ten directions;

at that time, each and every Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and those below him are described in eleven and a half lines of scripture, clarifying that Samantabhadra enters meditative absorption, all Buddhas appear before him, he is empowered by the Buddhas' power, and the Buddhas speak words of praise for Samantabhadra’s virtues. 5. At that time, all Buddhas of the ten directions... [already...]
1. The seven lines of sūtra below clarify the ten kinds of wisdom of Samantabhadra bestowed by all Buddhas;

2. the three lines of sūtra following "In this world" and so forth clarify how, throughout the worlds of the ten directions, all Buddhas simultaneously bestow their wisdom and Dharma upon Samantabhadra;
3. the six lines of sūtra beginning with "At that time" and so forth [clarify the conclusion].
The passage from "The Sutra on Practice clarifies that all Buddhas, with their hands, empower and stroke the crown of Samantabhadra’s head" through "in this way,
throughout all such oceans of worlds" (lines 8–9) summarizes that all worlds in the ten directions are likewise.
From "At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva" onwards (nine and a half lines), the text clarifies that Samantabhadra arises from samādhi and sets forth [his realization].

10. The name of the samādhi; from "When the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra arose from this gate of samādhi" onwards, twelve and a half lines of scripture clarify the benefits obtained by the great assembly and conclude that this is likewise the case throughout the ten directions. 11.
From "At that time, in all the oceans of worlds in the ten directions" down to the end of the verses, there are ten [sections].
Two and a half lines of the sūtra clarify that through the power of the Buddha and the power of samādhi, the earth slightly trembled and offerings were presented;
at the end, the light from the pores of all Buddhas spoke verses in praise of Samantabhadra’s virtues. Question:

For what reason did the earth shake in six ways with eighteen signs at the end of the "Chapter on the Array of the World-Ruler's Subtle Adornments" in the previous section, while in this chapter, why [is it different]?

Regarding the slight movement of the earth, the answer is as follows: Previously, it was explained that when the Tathāgata first attained perfect enlightenment, the great assembly offered congratulations to the Buddha and themselves all attained the benefit of the fruit of Buddhahood;
because this benefit is vast and its position supreme, and because his practice has reached its consummation, the earth shook greatly.
This present chapter answers the doubts raised by the World Rulers (*Lokendra*) so as to establish the first stage of faith; therefore, the earth shakes only slightly.
When the Bodhisattvas within the assembly manifest doubts, it is a skillful means to provide benefit by appearing to share their uncertainty;
this is all intended to establish the initial faith of ordinary beings. Therefore, this section is titled "The Section on Exhorting Practice by Pointing to the Fruit and Generating Faith.

It still involves faith in other Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who have attained such realization, yet it is not yet faith in one's own mind attaining that same state. In the second assembly, [the Buddha] appeared in golden... [text truncated].
Only after the World-Honored One, Akṣobhyajñāna Buddha, has departed does one clearly believe that one’s own mind is likewise so;

this is further clarified in the twelfth fascicle, where the various lords of the world pose twenty-eight questions before one finally believes that one’s own mind is the Buddha, the Immovable Wisdom (*akṣobhyajñāna*), and so forth.
It is only upon reaching the text of the "Dharmadhātu Chapter" that it is clarified that this sutra extends all the way to the City of Enlightenment (*bodhimanda*).

The Bodhisattvas who have come from the East and the entire great assembly are all those who rely upon phenomena; they are alike in their delusion, yet they manifest the practice and realization of cultivation.
Only the five hundred youths, the young women, the laymen (*upāsaka*), and the laywomen (*upāsikā*) in the city of Jeta possess [the capacity for] the five hundred and ten thousand dragons;
these represent the various stations of ordinary beings, signifying that among ordinary people there are those who can enter [the path].
Therefore, if there were no actual attainment, how could the Buddha’s teaching be a mere empty practice? The Noble Ones established these models so that ordinary beings might attain them in reality;
they are never applied in vain. One should know it thus, one should believe it thus, and not deceive oneself.
If someone were to say, "This sutra is not within the realm of ordinary beings, but is the domain of Bodhisattvas," such a person...

You should know that those who destroy the Buddha’s knowledge and vision, who cause the True Dharma to perish so that its correct teaching does not circulate in the world, and who prevent right view from arising in the world, thereby severing the seed of the Buddhas—wise people should not act in such a way.
Even if they do not exhort others to practice, if they themselves practice, they will not lose the seeds of goodness; they will still achieve the accumulation of superior merit in future lives.
For this reason, within the verses spoken regarding the light from the pores of the Buddha’s body, there follow two sections of verses.
In the first twenty lines of verse, the light from the Buddha’s pores is used to praise the virtues of Samantabhadra as clearly set forth in the text;
that is, the light from the pores is the light of the myriad practices (*sāhasra-caryā*), and thus it further extols the myriad practices of Samantabhadra. At that time, all [the bodhisattvas]...
Below the section on the Bodhisattvas, there are twenty verses that clarify the great assembly’s praise of Samantabhadra and their request for the teaching of the final three chapters;
these are also explained in detail as presented in the text. Second, regarding the explanation of the name of the samādhi, the meaning within this name is divided into two parts:
first, explaining the name of the samādhi; second, explaining the essence and function of the samādhi.
Third, praising the virtue of samādhi. First, explaining the name of the samādhi: it is called the *Vairocana-tathāgatagarbha-kāya*.
*Vairocana* means "light," and *citra* (here rendered as *che-na*) means "variously illuminating. Thus, the Tathāgata is the essence of the *dharmatā*.
*Garbha-kāya* refers to the wisdom that encompasses all phenomena. This clearly demonstrates the various teachings and practices through the integration of principle and wisdom.

This light illuminates the vessels of sentient beings, bestowing benefit according to their faculties, as clearly explained in the two interpretations within the section praising the virtues in the sutra.

Regarding the essence and function of this samādhi: the essence of this samādhi takes the fundamental wisdom of the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*) as its essence, while its great function takes the wisdom of differentiation as its function.
Furthermore, taking the fundamental wisdom of the dharma-realm as its essence, it follows...
The wisdom of sentient beings is its function, while entering samādhi is its essence and emerging from concentration is its function;
furthermore, neither entering nor emerging is its essence, while both entering and emerging are its function; moreover, both entering and emerging are its essence.
By inferring through these principles, the essential points can be seen. To speak briefly, this is intended as a method for transforming sentient beings.
Having entered the essence of the Samādhi of Illumination, one subsequently arises from that concentration and manifests ten names of samādhis.
This application of the ten names of samādhis takes as its essence the nature of the wisdom of non-abiding within the Dharma-realm;
this essence is also called the Śūraṅgama Samādhi, and it serves as the essence for all unspeakable samādhis and gateways of wisdom.
As it is fully elucidated within the "Praise of Virtues," as the Sūtra says: "There is no whirlpool in the ocean of worlds that he does not enter.
This refers to the function of this samādhi, which penetrates and pervades the names of all phenomena. Thus, "ocean" signifies vastness, and "whirlpool" signifies profound depth;
it clarifies that the essence and function of this samādhi are vast, profound, and inexhaustible—the enlightenment of all Buddhas.

Because the practice of Samantabhadra and all sentient beings of the six realms throughout the ten directions is universally pervasive, this single samādhi completely answers the previous thirty-seven questions in their entirety. Previously, by the Buddha’s spiritual power, it was asked among those thirty-seven questions:
"What are the Buddha-ground, the Buddha-ocean, the Buddha-eye, the Buddha-ear, the Buddha-nose, and so forth? Now, [it is answered] through the Samantabhadra...

In the response to the first thirty-seven questions, regarding the inquiry as to how a bodhisattva practices the ocean of samādhis and so forth, it is intended to clarify that the essence and function of the Buddha’s practice and the bodhisattva’s practice are thoroughly penetrating.

Taking the Buddha as the essence and the ocean of Samantabhadra’s practices as the function, this essence and function encompass all phenomena such that there is no phenomenon that is not exhausted; therefore, [the text speaks of] the Buddha’s eyes and ears.
With the nose, tongue, body, and mind as its essence, it has the capacity to universally know the activities of sentient beings as its function.

Below this, the Tathāgata’s Wisdom of Universal Goodness and the Wisdom of Universal Goodness [of the practitioner] are brought into accord with the Buddha’s Fundamental Wisdom; these two wisdoms are not distinct.
This is so that future believers may have no doubt that their own wisdom and the Buddha’s Fundamental Wisdom are of one substance and non-dual. Therefore, throughout the ten directions...
The Buddhas stroking his crown with their hands clarifies the reception [of beings] through patience (*kṣānti*).

The statement that Samantabhadra arises from samādhi clarifies that the essence of concentration follows the functional application according to the faculties of beings. That he further attains benefit based on those faculties is called the arising of its function;

it is inexhaustible. Briefly citing ten instances serves to represent its inexhaustibility; the remaining meanings are fully explained within the sutra text itself, as the intent is to clarify them extensively.
It clarifies that the fundamental wisdom of the Buddha is the essence of meditative concentration (*samādhi*), while Samantabhadra is its function.
