[Sūtra] If one constantly places faith in and reveres all Buddhas, then one will be able to uphold the precepts and cultivate the points of training.
If one constantly maintains the precepts and trains in the points of study, Then one can fully possess all meritorious qualities.
The precepts can bring forth the root of bodhi; Training is the ground for diligently cultivating merit.
Always acting in accordance with the precepts and training, One is praised by all Tathāgatas.
If one constantly has faith in and honors all Buddhas, Then one can assemble great offerings;
If one can assemble great offerings, That person’s faith in the Buddha is inconceivable.
If one constantly has faith in and honors the Honored Dharma, Then one will never tire of hearing the Buddha’s teachings.
If one hears the Buddha’s Dharma without weariness, that person’s faith in the Dharma is inconceivable;
if they constantly revere and take refuge in the pure Saṅgha, they will attain a faith that does not regress.
Once they have attained this non-regressive faith, no power can shake their strength of conviction.
If one attains the power of faith that cannot be shaken, Then one attains the purity, clarity, and sharpness of the faculties.
If one attains the purity, clarity, and sharpness of the faculties, Then one is able to distance oneself from evil associates.
If one is able to distance oneself from evil associates, Then one attains the opportunity to draw near to virtuous friends.
If one succeeds in drawing near to a spiritual friend, Then one can cultivate vast and sublime goodness.
If one can cultivate vast and sublime goodness, That person will achieve the power of great causal conditions.
If a person achieves the power of great causal conditions, Then they will attain a supreme and resolute understanding.
If one attains this supreme and definitive understanding, One will be protected and remembered by all Buddhas;
If one is protected and remembered by all Buddhas, One will be able to give rise to the bodhicitta;
If one is able to give rise to the bodhicitta, One will be able to diligently cultivate the qualities of a Buddha.
If one can diligently cultivate the virtues of the Buddha, Then one will be born into the family of the Tathāgata.
If one is born into the family of the Tathāgata, Then one will skillfully practice expedient means.
If one skillfully practices expedient means, Then one will attain a mind of pure faith and joy.
If one attains a mind of faith and joy that is pure, then one attains the superior and most excellent mind;
if one attains the superior and most excellent mind, then one constantly practices the pāramitās;
if one constantly practices the pāramitās, then one is able to fulfill the Mahāyāna.
If one can be fully endowed with the Mahāyāna, Then one can make offerings to the Buddha according to the Dharma;
If one can make offerings to the Buddha according to the Dharma, Then one can recollect the Buddha with an unmoving mind;
If one can recollect the Buddha with an unmoving mind, Then one will constantly behold immeasurable Buddhas.
If one constantly beholds immeasurable Buddhas, Then one sees that the Tathāgata’s body is eternally abiding.
If one sees that the Tathāgata’s body is eternally abiding, Then one can know that the Dharma never perishes.
If one can know that the Dharma never perishes, Then one attains unimpeded eloquence.
If one possesses unimpeded eloquence, Then one can expound the boundless Dharma;
If one can expound the boundless Dharma, Then one can compassionately deliver sentient beings;
If one can compassionately deliver sentient beings, Then one attains a firm and steadfast heart of great compassion.
If one can make the mind of great compassion firm, Then one will be able to delight in the profound Dharma;
If one can delight in the profound Dharma, Then one will be able to abandon the faults of the conditioned;
If one can abandon the faults of the conditioned, Then one will be free from arrogance and heedlessness.
If one is free from pride and negligence, Then one can benefit all beings;
If one can benefit all beings, Then one will not grow weary amidst birth and death.
If one does not grow weary amidst birth and death, Then one will be courageous and invincible.
If one is courageous and invincible, Then one can give rise to great supernormal powers;
If one can give rise to great supernormal powers, Then one knows the conduct of all sentient beings;
If one knows the conduct of all sentient beings, Then one can bring all multitudes of beings to fulfillment.
If one can bring all sentient beings to fulfillment, Then one attains the wisdom that skillfully gathers sentient beings;
If one attains the wisdom that skillfully gathers sentient beings, Then one is able to accomplish the four methods of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*);
If one can accomplish the four methods of attraction, Then one brings infinite benefit to sentient beings.
If one brings infinite benefit to sentient beings, Then one possesses the most supreme wisdom and skillful means.
If one possesses the most supreme wisdom and skillful means, Then one abides in the courageous, unsurpassed path.
If one abides in the courageous, unsurpassed path, Then one is able to crush and eliminate all demonic powers.
If one can utterly destroy all demonic powers, Then one can transcend the realms of the four māras.
If one can transcend the realms of the four māras, Then one attains the stage of non-retrogression.
If one attains the stage of non-retrogression, Then one attains the profound dharma-patience of non-arising.
If one attains the profound dharma-patience of non-arising, Then one receives the prediction of Buddhahood from all Buddhas;
If one receives the prediction of Buddhahood from all Buddhas, Then all Buddhas manifest before one;
If all Buddhas manifest before one, Then one realizes the profound and secret functions of supernormal powers.
If one realizes the profound and secret application of supernormal powers, Then one will be remembered by all Buddhas;
If one is remembered by all Buddhas, Then one will adorn oneself with the virtues of a Buddha;
If one adorns oneself with the virtues of a Buddha, Then one will obtain a body of sublime merit and dignified beauty.
If one attains a sublime and majestic body of wondrous merit, then that body will shine radiantly like a mountain of gold;
if the body shines radiantly like a mountain of gold, then it will be adorned with the thirty-two marks;
if it is adorned with the thirty-two marks, then it will be further embellished by the secondary characteristics.
If one is adorned with the secondary marks (anuvyañjana), then the radiance of the body is limitless;
If the radiance of the body is limitless, then there is the adornment of inconceivable light;
If there is the adornment of inconceivable light, then from that light emerge various lotus flowers.

When that light issues forth from the various lotus flowers, immeasurable Buddhas sit upon the flowers, manifesting throughout the ten directions without exception; they are all able to subdue all sentient beings.
If one can thus subdue sentient beings, then one manifests immeasurable supernormal powers.
If one manifests immeasurable supernormal powers, One abides in inconceivable lands and expounds inconceivable teachings,
Causing inconceivable multitudes to rejoice. If one expounds inconceivable teachings, One causes inconceivable multitudes to rejoice.
Then, by the power of wisdom and eloquence, one transforms and guides according to the minds of sentient beings;
if, by the power of wisdom and eloquence, one transforms and guides according to the minds of sentient beings,
then with wisdom as the precursor, the actions of body, speech, and mind are forever without fault.
If one takes wisdom as the precursor, so that the actions of body, speech, and mind are ever without fault,
then the power of one's vows will attain mastery, manifesting forms throughout all realms of existence according to their needs.
If the power of one's vows attains mastery, one manifests forms throughout all realms of existence according to their needs.
When he is able to preach the Dharma for the multitude, his voice adapts to each type in ways that are inconceivable;
when he is able to preach the Dharma for the multitude, his voice adapts to each type in ways that are inconceivable.
Then, regarding the minds of all sentient beings, he knows them all in a single thought-moment without exception.
If one knows, in a single thought-moment, the minds of all sentient beings without exception,
Then one knows that afflictions do not arise, And will never again be submerged in birth and death.
If one knows that afflictions do not arise, One will never again be submerged in birth and death.
Then one attains the body of the dharma-nature of merit, manifesting in the world through the power of the Dharma;
If one attains the body of the dharma-nature of merit, manifesting in the world through the power of the Dharma,
Then one attains the ten stages and the ten masteries, practicing the perfections and supreme liberations.
If one attains the ten stages and the ten masteries, And practices the supreme liberations of the perfections,
Then one obtains the great supernormal powers of consecration And abides in the most excellent samādhis.
If one obtains the great supernormal powers of consecration, One abides in the most excellent samādhis.
Then, in the presence of all Buddhas of the ten directions, one shall receive empowerment and ascend to the rank; if,
in the presence of all Buddhas of the ten directions, one shall receive empowerment and ascend to the rank,
then one will be graced by all Buddhas of the ten directions, who with their own hands shall pour the nectar upon one’s crown.
If one is graced by all the Buddhas of the ten directions, Who pour the nectar upon the crown of one’s head,
Then the body becomes pervasive like space, Abiding immovably and filling the ten directions.
If the body becomes pervasive like space, Abiding immovably and filling the ten directions.
Then his conduct will be peerless, such that neither gods nor men can know it.
[Treatise] 6: From "If one constantly places faith in the Buddhas" onwards, ninety-five stanzas clarify the section on advancing in practice and attaining the fruit.
[Sūtra] The Bodhisattva diligently cultivates the practice of great compassion; his vow to deliver all beings is never without fruit.
Whether they see, hear, listen to, or receive [the teaching], or even make offerings [to him], there are none who do not attain peace and happiness.
Through the majestic spiritual power of these Great Beings, the Dharma-eye is ever complete, without deficiency or diminution.
The ten wholesome paths of action and all other supreme, excellent jewels are made to appear;
just as a mass of vajras in the great ocean produces various jewels through its power—
neither decreasing, nor increasing, nor ever exhausted— so too is the mass of a bodhisattva’s merit.
In some lands where there is no Buddha, he manifests the attainment of perfect enlightenment;
in realms where the Dharma is unknown, he proclaims the treasury of the sublime Dharma.
Without discrimination and without effort, in a single thought-moment, he pervades the ten directions.
Like the moon’s light and shadow, reaching everywhere, Through immeasurable skillful means, he transforms all living beings.
Throughout those worlds of the ten directions, In every thought-moment, he manifests the attainment of the Buddha-way,
Turns the wheel of the sublime Dharma, and enters nirvana, Even until his relics are widely distributed.
Sometimes manifesting the paths of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, Or manifesting the attainment of Buddhahood with universal adornment;
Thus expounding the teachings of the three vehicles, He extensively delivers sentient beings throughout immeasurable kalpas.
Sometimes manifesting the forms of boys and girls, Or as devas, nāgas, and asuras.
Even unto the mahoragas and others, according to their inclinations, they cause all to see;
the forms and characteristics of sentient beings are each different, and their karmic actions and voices are likewise immeasurable—
all such things they are able to manifest through the majestic spiritual power of the Ocean-Seal Samādhi.
They purify inconceivable buddha-fields and make offerings to all Tathāgatas;
they emit boundless great radiance and deliver sentient beings without limit.
Their wisdom is sovereign and inconceivable, and their speech in expounding the Dharma is unimpeded.
Generosity, morality, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration, Wisdom, skillful means,
and the supernormal powers— In all such matters, he is sovereign through the power of the Buddha-Flower Adornment Samādhi;
Entering samādhi within a single atom, He accomplishes the meditative concentrations of all atoms.
Yet those atoms do not increase; within a single atom, inconceivable lands appear everywhere.
Within that one atom are many lands—some with Buddhas, some without Buddhas;
some defiled, some pure; some vast, some narrow.
Some are forming, some are disintegrating; some abide upright, some abide horizontally.
Some are like mirages in a vast wilderness, and some are like Indra’s net in the heavens.
As it is manifested within a single atom, so it is in all atoms without exception.
These sages of great renown, through the power of their samādhi, liberation, and supernormal faculties,
if they wish to make offerings to all Buddhas, enter into samādhi and manifest miraculous transformations;
with a single hand, they pervade the three thousandfold world-system, universally making offerings to all Tathāgatas.
All the supreme and wondrous flowers, unguents, powdered incense, and priceless jewels throughout the ten directions—
all these emerge from his hands, offered to the Most Victorious Ones at the tree of enlightenment.
Priceless jewel robes and various exquisite fragrances, as well as precious banners, pennants, and canopies, all magnificently adorned.
Pure gold for flowers and jewels for canopies— there was nothing that did not rain down from his palms.
All the exquisite things existing throughout the ten directions, worthy of being offered to the Unsurpassed Honored One,
were all rained down from his palms without exception as he made offerings to the Buddha before the Bodhi tree.
All the various musical instruments of the ten directions— bells, drums, lutes, and harps of every kind—
all play together in harmony with exquisite and subtle sounds, none of which fail to emerge from the palms of the hands.
All the hymns of praise existing throughout the ten directions extol the true merits of the Tathāgata.
Such various and wondrous words and phrases are all expounded from within his palms.
The Bodhisattva’s right hand emits pure light, and from within that light, fragrant water rains down from the sky,
sprinkling universally throughout the Buddha-lands of the ten directions to make offerings to all the Lamps that Illuminate the World.
Again, he emits a light called "Exquisite Adornment," Which produces immeasurable precious lotuses;
The colors and forms of these flowers are all most wonderful, And with them he makes offerings to all Buddhas.
Again, he emits a light called "Flower Adornment," In which various exquisite flowers gather to form canopies.
They are scattered everywhere throughout the lands of the ten directions, making offerings to all the Greatly Virtuous Honored Ones.
Again, they emit light adorned with fragrance, with various exquisite incenses gathering together to form canopies;
these are scattered everywhere throughout the lands of the ten directions, making offerings to all the Greatly Virtuous Honored Ones.
Again, he emits a light called "Arrayed with Powdered Incense," Wherein various powders of incense gather to form canopies,
Which are scattered throughout the lands of the ten directions As an offering to all the Great Virtuous Honored Ones.
Again, he emits a light called "Adorned with Robes," Wherein various famous garments gather to form canopies.
They scatter [offerings] throughout all lands in the ten directions, making offerings to all the Greatly Virtuous Honored Ones;
they further emit light adorned with jewels, with various exquisite gems gathered into canopies,
scattering them throughout all lands in the ten directions as offerings to all the Greatly Virtuous Honored Ones.
Again, he emits a light called "Lotus Adornment," With various lotuses gathered into canopies,
Which are scattered throughout all lands in the ten directions, As an offering to all the Honored Ones of Great Virtue.
Again, he emits a light called "Necklace Adornment," With various exquisite necklaces gathered into canopies.
They are scattered everywhere throughout the lands of the ten directions as offerings to all the Great Virtuous Honored Ones.
Again, they emit the light of the "Pinnacle of Adornment," banners that are brilliantly radiant and complete with every color;
diverse and immeasurable, all exquisitely beautiful, these adorn the buddha-fields.
Canopies adorned with various kinds of miscellaneous jewels, And exquisite silk banners hanging together as ornaments;
Maṇi-jewel bells proclaiming the voice of the Buddha— Holding these up in offering to all the Tathāgatas, The hands produce inconceivable offerings; With such offerings, one worships a single Guide.
It is thus at all the abodes of the Buddhas: By the power of samādhi and supernormal knowledges, the Great Being dwells within samādhi;
Through various sovereign means, he gathers in sentient beings, Using the dharmas of his practiced merits and immeasurable skillful expedients to guide and inspire them.
Either through the gate of making offerings to the Tathāgata, or through the gate of inconceivable generosity,
or through the gate of asceticism and upholding the precepts, or through the gate of unwavering patience,
or through the gate of arduous effort and diligence, or through the gate of tranquil meditative concentration.
Either by means of the gate of decisive wisdom, or by means of the gate of practiced skillful means,
or by means of the gate of Brahma-abodes and supernormal powers, or by means of the gate of benefiting through the four methods of attraction,
or by means of the gate of the adornments of merit and wisdom, or by means of the gate of liberation through causes and conditions.
Either by means of the gateway of the faculties, powers, and the noble path; or by means of the gateway of the Śrāvaka’s liberation;
or by means of the gateway of the Pratyekabuddha’s purity; or by means of the gateway of mastery in the Mahāyāna;
or by means of the gateway of impermanence and manifold suffering; or by means of the gateway of non-self and the absence of a life-principle.
Whether by means of the gate of detachment through impurity, or by means of the gate of the samādhi of cessation,
according to the differing illnesses of sentient beings, they treat them all with the medicine of the Dharma;
according to what the minds of sentient beings delight in, they satisfy them all through skillful means.
In accordance with the diverse conduct of all sentient beings, They bring them all to fulfillment through skillful means.
Such are the characteristics of the samādhis and supernormal powers; No gods or humans can fathom them.
There is a wondrous samādhi called "Accordance with Joy"; When Bodhisattvas abide therein, they observe everywhere.
Manifesting in accordance with what is appropriate to deliver sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice and follow the transformation of the Dharma;
during times of famine and calamity within the kalpa, providing all the worldly requisites for happiness to the world,
fulfilling all their desires, and universally bringing benefit to all sentient beings.
Whether it be food and drink of exquisite flavor, precious garments, ornaments, and various wonderful objects,
or even the throne of kingship— they are able to renounce all these to cause those who delight in giving to be fully transformed.
Or they may adorn their bodies with the marks and signs of excellence, wearing the most sublime robes and precious necklaces.
Adorned with flower garlands and bodies anointed with fragrant unguents, they possess perfect deportment as they deliver sentient beings.
Whatever the world prizes— whether physical form, countenance, or attire—
they manifest universally according to need to satisfy the hearts of others, so that those who delight in form may all follow the Path.
With the exquisite voice of the kalaviṅka bird and the wondrous sounds of the cuckoo and others,
they are fully endowed with all varieties of Brahma-sounds; according to the inclinations of beings' minds,
they preach eighty-four thousand Dharma-gates— by these means, the Buddhas deliver sentient beings.
He likewise, according to the distinctions of the Dharma, converts sentient beings as is appropriate for the world.

Regarding suffering and joy, gain and loss, and all such phenomena enacted within the world, he is able to manifest in accordance with them and participate in those affairs; by this means, he universally delivers all sentient beings.
All the various sufferings and afflictions of the world are as deep, vast, and boundless as the great ocean;
yet one can endure all these while acting for the sake of others, causing them to obtain benefit and peace.
If there are those who do not recognize the Dharma of renunciation and do not seek liberation from worldly clamor and distraction, [one should act for their sake].
The Bodhisattva manifests the renunciation of kingdom and wealth, always delighting in the mind of renunciation and tranquil stillness.

Since the home is a place bound by craving and attachment, he manifests leaving the home to attain liberation, so that all sentient beings may be completely freed from it; he has no love for any sensual pleasures.
The Bodhisattva manifests the practice of ten kinds of conduct, And also practices all the dharmas of great beings,
Including the practices of the various sages, without exception, For the sake of benefiting sentient beings.
If there are sentient beings with immeasurable lifespans, Whose afflictions are subtle and who are fully endowed with happiness,

The Bodhisattva attains mastery therein; he manifests the various afflictions of old age, sickness, and death, or displays the presence of desire, hatred, and delusion, with the fierce fires of the afflictions constantly blazing.
The Bodhisattva manifests old age, sickness, and death for the sake of bringing all those sentient beings to complete subdual.
The Tathāgata’s ten powers and fearlessnesses, as well as the eighteen unique qualities— all these immeasurable merits—
are manifested to deliver sentient beings; through the knowledge of others' minds,
exhortations, and supernormal powers, all are the sovereign applications of the Tathāgata.
All those Great Beings manifest various skillful means of the Bodhisattvas capable of bringing all sentient beings to complete subdual; following worldly conventions to deliver sentient beings,
they are like a lotus flower unsullied by water, thus remaining in the world to inspire deep faith.
With profound learning and vast talent, a king among those skilled in composition; in song, dance, and discourse, he is the delight of all.
Among all the various arts and crafts of the world, there is nothing he does not manifest, like a master illusionist.
Sometimes he acts as a head of a clan or a lord of a town; sometimes he serves as a guide for merchants and traders.
Sometimes they become kings or great ministers; sometimes they act as skilled physicians well-versed in all treatises.
Sometimes they become great trees in the wilderness, or they become excellent medicines and treasuries of jewels.
Or they become precious garments according to what is sought, or they show the right path to sentient beings.
When he sees the world first coming into being, and sentient beings have not yet acquired the means for sustaining their bodies,
at that time the Bodhisattva acts as a craftsman; for their sake, he manifests various types of work,
never performing any act that would distress living beings, but speaking only of matters that benefit the world.
He is able to expound all such treatises as those on incantations and medicinal herbs;

he can fully perform all the extraordinary practices of the sages, as well as the laws of difficult austerities that are equally revered by humans, devas, and other beings, according to their respective needs.
Some appear as renunciants of non-Buddhist paths, or dwell in mountain forests practicing self-mortification;
some go naked without clothing, acting as teachers and elders among those groups;
or they manifest various modes of wrong livelihood, practicing what is contrary to the Dharma and regarding it as supreme.
Sometimes he manifests the various dignified demeanors of a brahmin and serves as the leader among that assembly;
sometimes he undergoes the five heats while turning with the sun; sometimes he observes the vows of a cow, a dog, or a deer;
sometimes he wears tattered rags and worships fire—to transform such beings, he acts as their guide.

Some manifest visiting the temples of various devas; others manifest entering the waters of the Ganges, eating roots, fruits, and so forth, displaying all such practices. Toward these, they constantly contemplate their own superior Dharma;
some manifest squatting or standing on one foot; others lie upon grass, thorns, or ashes.
Or again, lying upon a pestle to seek liberation, acting as the leader among such hosts of various non-Buddhists;
observing their inclinations and engaging in their activities,
he displayed ascetic practices that the world could not endure, causing them all to be tamed upon seeing him.
Sentient beings, deluded and following false teachings, dwell in evil views and undergo manifold sufferings;
for their sake, he preaches the sublime Dharma as a skillful means, causing them all to realize the truth of ultimate reality.
Whether through border dialects he speaks the Four Truths, or through skillful secret language he speaks the Four Truths.
Some speak the Four Truths in direct human speech; some speak the Four Truths in secret celestial language;
some speak the Four Truths by analyzing written characters; some speak the Four Truths by definitively establishing their principles;
some speak the Four Truths skillfully refuting the assertions of others; and some speak the Four Truths as being unshakable by external influences.
Sometimes the Four Truths are taught in the languages of the eight classes of beings;
sometimes they are taught in all languages according to the speech and sounds by which those beings understand.
For the sake of liberation, the Four Truths are taught through every single Buddha-dharma; all are thus spoken without exception.
Knowing that the realm of speech is inconceivable— this is called the power of the *dharmadeśanā-samādhi*.

[Treatise] From the verse beginning with "The seven bodhisattvas having diligently practiced the conduct of great compassion" onwards, one hundred and fifty-one stanzas clarify the section on the Bodhisattva’s attainment of the fruit,
practicing compassion to transform sentient beings, and exercising mastery in making offerings.
[Sūtra] There is a supreme samādhi named "Peace and Bliss," Which can universally rescue and deliver all living beings.
It emits inconceivable great radiance, Causing all who see it to be fully tamed.
The emitted light is named "Excellent Manifestation"; If any sentient beings encounter this light...
They ensure that all obtain benefit so it is not in vain; By this, they shall attain unsurpassed wisdom.
In the past, they manifested before the Buddhas, Showing the Dharma, showing the Sangha, and showing the True Path;
They also showed Buddha-stūpas and images. For this reason, they have attained this radiance.
Again, he emits a light named "Illumination," which eclipses all the radiance of the devas;
there is no darkness or obstruction that it does not dispel. It universally brings benefit to all sentient beings, awakening them all and causing them to hold up lamps as offerings to the Buddha.
Because one makes offerings of lamps to the Buddhas, One attains the state of the unsurpassed lamp in the world.
Whether it be oil lamps or ghee lamps, Or likewise various kinds of bright torches,
Exquisite incense, wondrous medicinal herbs, and supreme jewel-candles— By making these offerings to the Buddha, one obtains this light.
Again, he emits a light named "Deliverance," This light can awaken all beings,
causing them universally to give rise to the great vow-mind To deliver and liberate the multitudes of sentient beings from the ocean of desire;
If they can universally give rise to the great vow-mind To deliver and liberate the multitudes of sentient beings from the ocean of desire.
Thus one is able to cross over the four torrents; Showing the path to the city of liberation, free from sorrow.
Upon the great waters along the paths of conditioned phenomena, One constructs bridges and rafts;
Censuring the conditioned and praising tranquility— Therefore, this radiance is accomplished.

Again, he emits a light named "Extinction of Craving. This light awakens all sentient beings, causing them to abandon the five desires and focus their thoughts exclusively on the wondrous flavor of the Dharma of liberation.
If one can abandon the five desires and focus their thoughts exclusively on the wondrous flavor of the Dharma of liberation...
Thus, one is able to rain down the Buddha’s nectar to universally extinguish all thirst and craving in the world;

by providing pools, wells, springs, and flowing streams as acts of giving, and by single-mindedly seeking the path of unsurpassed bodhi while disparaging the five desires and praising meditative concentration, one therefore attains this radiance.
Again, he emits a light named "Joy"; this light awakens all beings, causing them to cherish and long for the Buddha’s Bodhi.
They resolve their minds to realize the Teacherless Way and fashion images of the Tathāgata’s great compassion, adorned with all the marks and seated upon lotus thrones.
Constantly praising the most supreme virtues, Therefore, this radiance is accomplished.
Furthermore, it emits a light named "Beloved," This light can awaken all beings,
Causing their minds to delight in the Buddhas, And to take joy in the Dharma and the Sangha.
If one always delights the mind in the Buddhas, And delights in the Dharma and the Sangha,
Then one will dwell within the assemblies of the Tathāgatas, Attaining the supreme and profound *dharmakṣānti*,
Awakening immeasurable sentient beings, Universally causing them to recollect the Triple Gem of Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha.
And by demonstrating the meritorious conduct of generating the bodhicitta, one thus attains this radiance.
Furthermore, a light named "Accumulation of Merit" is emitted;
this light awakens all beings, causing them to practice various kinds of immeasurable giving, through which they seek the unsurpassed path.
He established great assemblies of giving without restriction; all who came to seek were fully satisfied, so that their hearts felt no lack. For this reason, he attained this radiance.
Furthermore, he emits a light named "Endowed with Wisdom," which is able to awaken all sentient beings.
Causing one to fully understand all immeasurable dharma-gates within a single dharma and a single thought-moment;
to analyze the dharmas for the sake of all sentient beings and to decisively realize their true meaning;
and to skillfully explain the meaning of the teachings without deficiency—it is for these reasons that this light is accomplished.
Again, he emits a light named "Wisdom Lamp"; this light awakens all beings, causing them to know that the nature of sentient beings is empty and quiescent.
It proclaims that all phenomena are non-existent, that all phenomena are empty and without a master, being like an illusion, a flame, or the moon reflected in water.
Even as it is like a dream or a reflection, therefore this radiance is accomplished.
Furthermore, he emits a light named "Sovereignty over Dharma";
this light awakens all beings, causing them to attain inexhaustible dhāraṇīs, and enabling them to uphold all the teachings of the Buddhas.

By reverently making offerings to those who uphold the Dharma, serving and protecting all the worthy sages, and bestowing various forms of the gift of Dharma upon sentient beings, one thus attains this radiance.
Furthermore, a light is emitted named "Able to Renounce"; this light awakens stingy sentient beings.
Causing them to know that all wealth and treasures are impermanent, Always delighting in giving with a mind free from attachment;
The difficult-to-tame stingy mind is thus tamed, Understanding that wealth is like a dream or floating clouds,
Increasing the pure mind of wisdom and generosity— For this reason, this radiance is attained.
Again, he emits a light named "Dispelling Heat. This light awakens those who have violated the precepts, causing them all to receive and uphold the pure precepts;
it inspires the aspiration to realize the teacherless path and exhorts sentient beings to receive and uphold the precepts, so that the ten paths of wholesome action are entirely purified.
Furthermore, it causes them to resolve toward the mind of enlightenment; therefore, this radiance is accomplished.

Again, he emits a radiance named "Adorned with Patience"; this light awakens those who harbor anger, causing them to eliminate hatred and abandon pride, so that they may always delight in the dharma of patience and gentleness.
Sentient beings are violent and evil, difficult to endure; yet for the sake of Bodhi, his mind remains unshakable.
He always delights in praising the merit of patience, and thus he has attained this radiance.
Furthermore, he emits a light named "Valiant," which awakens those who are indolent.
May they always, within the Triple Gem, Reverently make offerings without weariness;
If they always, within the Triple Gem, Reverently make offerings without weariness,
Then they shall be able to transcend the realms of the four Māras And swiftly attain the unsurpassed Bodhi of a Buddha.
Exhorting and transforming sentient beings to advance toward the path, Constantly and diligently making offerings to the Triple Gem,
And single-mindedly protecting the Dharma when it is about to perish— For these reasons, he attained this radiance. Furthermore,
he emits a light named "Tranquility," A dharma capable of awakening those with distracted minds.
Causing them to distance themselves from greed, anger, and delusion, With minds unshakable and established in right concentration,
they abandon all evil associates, Idle chatter, and defiled conduct;
by praising meditative absorption and forest hermitages, They therefore achieve this radiance.
Again, he emits a light named "Wisdom Adornment. This light awakens those who are deluded and confused, causing them to realize the Truths and understand dependent origination;
it enables all their faculties and wisdom to be fully penetrating.
If one can realize the Truths and understand dependent origination, all their faculties and wisdom will be fully penetrating.
Thus one attains the *Dīpa-pradīpa* Samādhi; with the light of wisdom, one attains the fruit of Buddhahood.
One is able to relinquish both national wealth and one’s own possessions;

for the sake of Bodhi, one seeks the True Dharma, and having heard it, applies oneself with diligence to explain it for the sake of the multitude. Therefore, one succeeds in accomplishing this radiance.
Again, he emits a light named "Buddha-Wisdom. This light awakens all sentient beings,
causing them to see immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, each seated upon a precious lotus flower,
praising the Buddha’s majestic virtue and liberation, and proclaiming the Buddha’s immeasurable sovereignty.
To manifest the Buddha’s power and supernormal faculties, he thus brings this radiance to fulfillment.
Furthermore, he emits a light named Fearlessness; when this light touches those who are terrified, all poisons and harms inflicted by non-human beings are swiftly extinguished.
Able to bestow fearlessness upon sentient beings, Whenever encountering harm or affliction, they urge others to cease it;
Rescuing those in distress and aiding the orphaned and destitute— By these means, this radiance is attained.
Furthermore, a radiance named "Peaceful Security" is emitted; This light can illuminate those who are sick.
Causing all sufferings and pains to be removed, And enabling all to attain the bliss of right concentration and samādhi;
Bestowing excellent medicines to rescue the multitude from their ailments, Applying the fragrance of wondrous jewels to prolong life,
And providing ghee, oil, milk, and honey as food and drink— By these means, this radiance was achieved.

Again, he emits a light named "Beholding the Buddha. This light awakens those who are about to die, causing them to recollect and behold the Tathāgata as they pass away, so that they may be reborn in his Pure Land.
Seeing those at the point of death, he exhorts them to mindfulness of the Buddha, and further displays sacred images for them to gaze upon with reverence.
Causing them to take deep refuge and仰 (revere) toward the Buddha, Therefore, this radiance is accomplished;
furthermore, it emits a light named "Delight in the Dharma.
This light can awaken all beings, causing them to always rejoice in the True Dharma, Through hearing its exposition, as well as through transcribing it.
When the Dharma is about to perish, one is able to expound it, so that those who seek the Dharma have their minds fulfilled;
through delighting in the Dharma and practicing with diligence, one thus attains this radiance.
Furthermore, one emits a radiance named "Exquisite Sound," and this light awakens all bodhisattvas.
It can cause all sounds within the three realms to be heard by listeners as the voice of the Tathāgata;
by praising the Buddha with a great voice and offering bells, chimes, and various musical instruments,
it causes the sound of the Buddha to be heard throughout the world— therefore, this radiance is attained.
Again, he emits a light named "Bestowing Ambrosia. This light awakens all sentient beings, causing them to abandon all heedless conduct;
it causes them to fully cultivate all meritorious virtues and to proclaim that conditioned phenomena are not secure, being entirely filled with immeasurable suffering and affliction.
Constantly delighting in praising the bliss of quiescence, Therefore, he has attained this radiance.
Furthermore, he emits a light named "Supreme," Which awakens all sentient beings,
Causing them to universally hear from the Buddha The sublime Dharma of ethical discipline, meditative concentration, and wisdom.
Constantly delighting in praising all Buddhas— Their supreme precepts, supreme concentration, and sublime wisdom— Thus seeking the unsurpassed path, He therefore attained this radiance.
Furthermore, he emits a light named Jewel Adornment; This light can awaken all sentient beings.
Causing them to obtain inexhaustible treasuries of jewels, With which they make offerings to all Tathāgatas;
By offering various kinds of supreme and wondrous jewels To the Buddhas and their stūpas,
And likewise bestowing the gift of wisdom upon the impoverished, For this reason, they have accomplished this radiance.
Again, he emits a light named "Fragrant Adornment. This light awakens all beings, causing those who hear it to find delight;

they will certainly become persons of merit destined for Buddhahood, anointing the ground with the exquisite incense of devas and humans, making offerings to the Sovereign of All Most Victorious Ones.
Furthermore, by constructing stupas and images of the Buddha, one thus attains this radiance; moreover,
a light named "Various Adornments" is emitted, with countless jeweled banners, pennants, and canopies,
burning incense, scattering flowers, and playing various music, filling the interior and exterior of cities and towns.

Originally, by means of subtle and exquisite music, various fragrances, wonderful flowers, banners, canopies, and other such diverse adornments, they made offerings to the Buddha; therefore, they have attained this radiance.
Furthermore, they emit a light named "Pure Adornment," which makes the earth level and smooth like the palm of a hand.
Because he adorned the Buddha-stūpas and their sites, he has attained this radiance;
furthermore, he emits a light named "Great Cloud," which can raise clouds of fragrance and rain down perfumed water,
sprinkling it upon the stūpas and their courtyards— therefore, he has attained this radiance.

Again, he emits a light named "Ornament," which causes those who are naked to obtain excellent garments and exquisite objects for adorning their bodies as gifts; therefore, this light is accomplished.
Again, he emits a light named "Supreme Flavor," which enables the hungry to obtain delicious food.
By bestowing various kinds of rare delicacies as gifts, one thus achieves this radiance.
Furthermore, a light is emitted named Great Wealth, which causes those who are destitute to obtain treasuries of jewels;
by giving inexhaustible things to the Triple Gem, one thus achieves this radiance.
Again, he emits a light named "Purity of the Eye," Which enables the blind to see all forms;
Because he offered lamps to the Buddha and the Buddha-stūpas, He has therefore accomplished this radiance.
Again, he emits a light named "Purity of the Ear," Which enables the deaf to hear everything clearly.
By providing music to entertain the Buddha and his stūpas, one attains this radiance;
furthermore, by emitting light, one’s sense of smell becomes purified, so that all fragrances never before heard are now perceived.
This is because one offered incense to the Buddha and his stūpas; therefore, one attains this radiance.

Again, he emits a light named "Purity of the Tongue," Which, through its beautiful voice, praises the Buddha And forever eliminates coarse, evil, and unwholesome speech; Therefore, this radiance is accomplished.
Again, he emits a light named "Purity of the Body," Which causes those with deficient sense organs to become complete.
By prostrating with the body before the Buddha and his stūpas, one thus achieves this radiance.

Furthermore, there is a light named "Purity of Mind," which causes those who have lost their minds to attain right mindfulness and to practice samādhi with complete mastery; it is for this reason that this radiance is achieved.
Again, he emits a light named "Purity of Form," Causing one to behold the inconceivable forms of all Buddhas;
Because he adorns stupas with various wondrous colors, He therefore accomplishes this radiance.
Again, he emits a light named "Purity of Sound," Causing one to know that the nature of sound is fundamentally empty and quiescent.
Observing that sounds arise through conditions like an echo, one thus attains this radiance.
Furthermore, emitting a light named "Pure Fragrance," it causes all foul odors to become fragrant and clean;
by washing stupas and Bodhi trees with scented water, one thus attains this radiance.
Again, he emits a light named "Purity of Taste," Which can eliminate all poisons within flavors;
Constantly making offerings to the Buddha, the Sangha, and one's parents, Therefore, he is able to accomplish this radiance.
Again, he emits a light named "Purity of Touch," Which can cause all harsh touches to become soft and supple.
Spears, shafts, swords, and halberds rain down from the sky, All of which are transformed into exquisite flower garlands.
Because in the past, while on the road, You welcomed and saw off the Tathāgata with ointments,
scattered flowers, and spread out garments for him to tread upon, Therefore you have now obtained such radiance as this.
Again, he emits a light named "Dharma Purity," Which causes every single pore to proclaim the inconceivable, wondrous Dharma.
All sentient beings who hear it joyfully awaken to the realization that what arises from causes and conditions has no inherent birth; The Dharma-body of all Buddhas is not a body.
The nature of phenomena is eternally abiding like space; The light of its explained meaning is thus.

[Treatise] From the eighth verse, "From the Samādhi of Supreme Existence named 'Peaceful Bliss'," and below, there are one hundred and sixty lines of verse clarifying the section on the causes and effects of emitting light.
[Sūtra] Such gateways of light as these, infinite in number like the sands of the Ganges, all issue forth from the pores of the Great Sage. Each performs its own distinct function;
just as the light emitted from a single pore is immeasurable and countless, like the sands of the Ganges.
All pores are likewise so; this is the power of the Great Sage’s samādhi.
The light obtained through his original practices is now emitted as such, following those who shared his past conditions and practices;
this is the sovereign mastery of the Great Sage’s wisdom.
Those who in the past practiced meritorious deeds together, And those who, with joyful devotion,
were able to rejoice in what was done— They all likewise behold this light.
If one personally cultivates various meritorious deeds, Making offerings to countless Buddhas, [they too shall see it].
One should always aspire to seek the Buddha’s virtues; this is what is awakened by this light.

It is like one born blind who does not see the sun—not because the sun has not risen in the world, but because those with eyes all see it clearly, each pursuing their own tasks and cultivating their own work.
The light of the Great Being is likewise: those possessed of wisdom all behold it, yet ordinary people of false faith and inferior understanding cannot perceive this radiance.
The palace of mani-jewels and the celestial chariots are polished and adorned with exquisite gems and sacred incense.
Those with merit naturally possess it; it is not something those without merit can attain.

The radiance of the Great Being is likewise: it illuminates and touches all those of profound wisdom, yet no one who possesses false faith, inferior understanding, or is an ordinary fool can perceive this light.
If there are those who hear of these distinctions of light, They can give rise to pure, profound faith and understanding;
Forever severing all nets of doubt, They will swiftly accomplish the banner of unsurpassed merit.
[Commentary] Ninth: The twenty verses beginning from "Such as these gates of light" clarify the source from which the light emerges.
And the section on the distinctions of light.
[Sūtra] There is a supreme samādhi capable of manifesting retinues and adornments with total mastery throughout all the lands of the ten directions;
the assembly of the Buddha’s sons therein is without peer.
There are exquisite lotus flowers adorned with light, equal in measure to the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world-system;
their bodies sit upright, completely filling them all—this is the supernatural power of this samādhi.
Furthermore, there are as many exquisite and beautiful lotus flowers as there are atoms in ten buddha-fields surrounding [the central one].

The assemblies of all Buddha-sons sit therein; abiding in the majestic spiritual power of this samādhi and having accomplished virtuous causes and conditions in past lives, they are fully endowed with the practice of the Buddha’s merits.
These beings surround the Bodhisattva, all joining their palms together, gazing upon him without weariness.
Just as the bright moon stands among the stars, so too does the Bodhisattva dwell amidst the assembly;
such is the practice of the Great Being. Through the majestic power of entering this samādhi, he manifests himself in one direction while surrounded by the multitude of all the Buddha-sons.
It is thus in all directions; by the majestic power of this samādhi, there is a superior samādhi named "Network of Directions.

When a bodhisattva dwells in this, they extensively reveal themselves, manifesting their bodies everywhere throughout all directions—sometimes appearing to enter meditative absorption, and sometimes emerging from it.
Sometimes entering right concentration in the east and emerging from concentration in the west;
sometimes entering right concentration in the west and emerging from concentration in the east;
or entering right concentration in another direction and emerging from concentration in yet another direction.
Thus entering and emerging throughout the ten directions— this is called the power of the bodhisattva’s samādhi.
Exhausting all the lands in the eastern quarter, he manifests before all the countless Tathāgatas therein,
approaching them all universally while remaining unmoving in the stillness of samādhi.
And throughout all the worlds in the western direction,
he manifests arising from samādhi before all the Tathāgatas; he extensively performs immeasurable offerings,
reaching to the end of all the lands in the west where the Tathāgatas are beyond measure.
Manifesting before them all, they draw near universally; abiding in samādhi, tranquil and unmoving,
they appear before all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, in all the worlds of the eastern direction,
and arising from that samādhi, they extensively perform immeasurable offerings.
Thus, in all worlds throughout the ten directions, Bodhisattvas enter them all without exception;
some manifest the stillness and immobility of samādhi, while others manifest reverent worship and offerings to the Buddhas.
They enter right concentration within the faculty of the eye, and emerge from that concentration within the objects of form.
He manifests the inconceivable nature of form, which no humans or devas can know.
Entering right concentration within the sensory object of form, he emerges from concentration regarding the eye with an undisturbed mind.
He declares that the eye is unborn and without arising; its nature is empty, quiescent, and unconditioned.
Entering right concentration within the faculty of the ear, Emerging from concentration within the object of sound,
He discerns all sounds of speech and language, Which neither gods nor worldlings can comprehend.
Entering right concentration within the object of sound, He emerges from concentration within the ear with an undisturbed mind.
He teaches that the ear is unborn and has no arising; its nature is empty, quiescent, and unconditioned.

Entering right concentration within the faculty of the nose, he emerges from that concentration amidst the objects of fragrance, universally perceiving all sublime and wondrous scents, such that neither gods nor worldly people can know it.
Entering right concentration amidst the object of fragrance, he emerges from concentration amidst the nose-sense-field with an undisturbed mind;
he teaches that the nose is unborn and without arising, its nature being empty, quiescent, and unconditioned.
Entering right concentration amidst the faculty of the tongue, he emerges from concentration amidst the object of flavor.
Universally obtaining all supreme flavors, which neither gods nor worldlings can comprehend;
Entering right concentration amidst the objects of taste, arising from samādhi through the tongue with an undisturbed mind;
He speaks that the tongue is unborn and without arising, its nature being empty, quiescent, and unconditioned.
Entering right concentration within the body-faculty, he emerges from concentration within the object of touch;
he is skillfully able to discern all touches, such that neither gods nor worldlings can know him.
Entering right concentration within the object of touch, he arises from concentration in the body with a mind undisturbed.
He speaks of the body as being without birth and without arising, its nature empty, quiescent, and unconditioned.
Entering right concentration within the faculty of mind, he emerges from that concentration amidst mental objects;
he discerns the characteristics of all phenomena, such that neither gods nor men can comprehend him.
Entering right concentration amidst the objects of the mind, he emerges from that mental concentration with an undisturbed mind;
he teaches that the mind is unborn and without arising, its nature being empty, quiescent, and unconditioned.
Entering right concentration within the body of a youth, he emerges from concentration within the body of middle age.
Entering right concentration within a body in the prime of life, emerging from concentration within a body in old age;
entering right concentration within a body in old age, emerging from concentration within a body of a virtuous woman;
entering right concentration within a body of a virtuous woman, emerging from concentration within a body of a virtuous man.
Entering right concentration within the body of a virtuous man, emerging from concentration within the body of a bhikṣuṇī;
entering right concentration within the body of a bhikṣuṇī, emerging from concentration within the body of a bhikṣu;
entering right concentration within the body of a bhikṣu, emerging from concentration within the bodies of those in training (śaikṣa) and those beyond training (aśaikṣa).
Entering right concentration with the body of one beyond training, emerging from concentration with the body of a pratyekabuddha;
entering right concentration with the body of a pratyekabuddha, emerging from concentration manifesting as the body of a Tathāgata;
entering right concentration with the body of a Tathāgata, emerging from concentration within the bodies of the various devas.
Entering right concentration within the bodies of various devas, he emerges from concentration within the bodies of great nāgas;
entering right concentration within the bodies of great nāgas, he emerges from concentration within the bodies of yakṣas;
entering right concentration within the bodies of yakṣas, he emerges from concentration within the bodies of ghosts and spirits.
Entering right concentration within the body of a spirit or deity;
emerging from concentration within a single pore and entering right concentration within a single pore;
emerging from concentration within all pores and entering right concentration within all pores; emerging from concentration at the tip of a single hair.
Entering right concentration at the tip of a single hair; emerging from concentration within a single atom and entering right concentration within a single atom;
emerging from concentration within all atoms and entering right concentration within all atoms; emerging from concentration within the vajra-ground.
Entering right concentration within the vajra-ground, emerging from concentration atop a mani-tree;
Entering right concentration atop a mani-tree, emerging from concentration within the Buddha’s radiance;
Emerging from concentration within the rivers and oceans.
Entering right concentration within the rivers and oceans, he emerges from concentration within the element of fire;
entering right concentration within the element of fire, he emerges from concentration within the element of wind;
entering right concentration within the element of wind, his mind remains undisturbed as he emerges from concentration within the element of earth.
Entering right concentration within the great element of earth, Emerging from concentration within the celestial palaces,
Entering right concentration within the celestial palaces, Rising from concentration in space with an undisturbed mind—
This is called one of immeasurable merit, Whose mastery over samādhi is inconceivable.
All Tathāgatas of the ten directions could not exhaustively describe them even in immeasurable kalpas.
[Treatise: From "Having emerged from the Samādhi of Supreme Existence" onwards, eighty-one verses clarify the section on the mastery of samādhi;
such unimpeded mastery over similarities and differences is the entrance into the Great Square Net Samādhi gate.

Regarding the mastery over appearing and disappearing simultaneously: because the Buddhas possess mastery over the attainment of the Way, they manifest according to the differences in what is seen by sentient beings based on their respective karma;
and because they possess mastery over the karma of sentient beings, the Tathāgata’s mind is of a non-active nature.
Thus, wisdom responds to conditions like a reflection, being devoid of coming or going, yet capable of being grasped or relinquished—just as an echo corresponds to a sound. This is the analogy.
Water flows secretly beneath the surface, causing various plants and trees to grow; it is like the spring sun bringing forth grasses and wood,
like water nourishing fish and dragons, like the earth producing all vegetation, like fire preparing food,
and like the wind arising to benefit living beings by determining their longevity and lifespan— contemplate these through analogy and illuminate them with wisdom.
When conceptual clinging ceases and one acts in accordance with true reality, such wisdom is fundamentally as it should be;
however, because of the persistence of conceptual clinging, even if one attains a portion of the fruits of the supramundane path, one cannot achieve great mastery.
