Clouds of rain showered from hundreds of billions of heavens; clouds of agalloch incense rose up; hundreds of billions of precious banners were erected; hundreds of billions of precious streamers were suspended;
hundreds of billions of precious silk ribbons hung down; hundreds of billions of incense burners were lit; hundreds of billions of precious garlands were spread out;
hundreds of billions of precious fans were held; hundreds of billions of precious fly-whisks were grasped; and nets of hundreds of billions of precious bells were hung.
A gentle breeze stirred them, producing wondrous sounds; a hundred trillion jeweled railings encircled it on all sides;
a hundred trillion jeweled *tāla* trees were arranged in successive rows; a hundred trillion windows of exquisite jewels were magnificently adorned;
a hundred trillion jeweled trees surrounded it, casting down shade; and a hundred trillion jeweled pavilions extended far and wide with elegant ornamentation.
Ten trillion jeweled gates were draped with hanging necklaces; ten trillion golden bells emitted wondrous sounds;
ten trillion auspiciously marked necklaces hung down in pure adornment; ten trillion *siddhika* jewels could eliminate all evils;
ten trillion golden treasuries were woven from gold threads; and ten trillion jeweled canopies, with poles made of various gems, were held aloft.
There were rows of hundreds of billions of nets of all kinds of jewel ornaments interspersed with various decorations;
hundreds of billions of radiant jewels emitting manifold rays of light; hundreds of billions of rays of light shining everywhere;
hundreds of billions of solar treasuries and hundreds of billions of lunar treasuries, all composed of jewels of immeasurable colors; and hundreds of billions of fragrances.
The radiance of their flames shines through and illuminates a hundred trillion blooming lotus treasuries, which are fresh and flourishing;
it covers a hundred trillion jewel nets, a hundred trillion flower nets, and a hundred trillion incense nets;
and there are a hundred trillion celestial precious robes, a hundred trillion celestial blue garments, a hundred trillion celestial yellow garments, and a hundred trillion celestial red garments.
There were a hundred trillion celestial garments of wondrous colors, a hundred trillion celestial garments of various precious jewels,
a hundred trillion garments perfumed with diverse fragrances, a hundred trillion garments made of every kind of jewel, and a hundred trillion pure white garments,
all beautifully spread out so that those who saw them rejoiced; there were also a hundred trillion celestial bells and banners, and a hundred trillion golden [ornaments].
The net-banner emitted subtle and wondrous sounds; ten trillion celestial silk banners were complete with every color;
ten trillion incense banners draped down nets of fragrance; ten trillion flower banners rained down all manner of flowers;
ten trillion celestial robe banners hung and spread exquisite garments; ten trillion celestial maṇi-jewel banners were adorned with various jewels; ten trillion celestial... [celestial banners].
There were banners of ornamental jewels adorned with hundreds of billions of celestial garlands, various flower garlands arrayed on all four sides,

and hundreds of billions of celestial parasol-banners with precious bells chiming in harmony, which all who heard brought joy; there were hundreds of billions of celestial conchs emitting wondrous sounds,
hundreds of billions of celestial drums producing great sounds, and hundreds of billions of celestial *vīṇā* lutes.

A hundred trillion celestial *mudrā* deities produced subtle and wondrous sounds; a hundred trillion celestial deities simultaneously played various musical instruments, producing great and sublime tones;
a hundred trillion celestial deities of sovereign joy produced exquisite vocal sounds, the resonance of which pervaded all buddha-fields;
a hundred trillion celestial deities of transformative joy produced sounds like echoes, universally responding to all.

A hundred trillion celestial drums produced wondrous sounds upon being struck; a hundred trillion celestial wish-fulfilling instruments spontaneously emitted sounds with harmonious rhythms and melodies;
a hundred trillion various celestial musical ensembles produced wondrous sounds that extinguish all afflictions;
a hundred trillion pleasing sounds offered praise and worship; and a hundred trillion vast sounds offered eulogies.
They praised the service of a hundred trillion profound sounds; they praised the cultivation of practice with a hundred trillion myriad wonderful sounds;
they praised the karmic fruits of the Buddha’s deeds with a hundred trillion subtle sounds; they praised the principle of suchness with a hundred trillion unobstructed true sounds;
they praised the Buddha’s past conduct with a hundred trillion pure sounds; and they praised his offerings to the Buddhas of the past.
A hundred trillion sounds of Dharma-gates praise the supreme fearlessness of all Buddhas;

a hundred trillion immeasurable sounds praise the inexhaustible merits of all Bodhisattvas; a hundred trillion sounds of the Bodhisattva stages praise and reveal the practices corresponding to all Bodhisattva stages;
and a hundred trillion uninterrupted sounds praise the Buddha’s merits as being without end.
They sever hundreds of billions of sounds of conformity, praising and extolling the conduct of beholding the Buddha;
they proclaim hundreds of billions of billions of profound sounds of Dharma, extolling the principle corresponding to unimpeded wisdom regarding all phenomena;

they possess hundreds of billions of vast sounds, whose resonance fills all buddha-fields; they possess hundreds of billions of unimpeded, pure sounds, which accord with the inclinations of beings' minds.
There were a hundred trillion sounds that cause all to rejoice and do not abide within the three realms, causing those who hear them to penetrate deeply into the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*);
a hundred trillion sounds of joy, causing those who hear them to have no mental obstructions and to possess deep faith and reverence;
and a hundred trillion sounds of the Buddha’s sphere, such that every sound produced is able to reveal the meaning of all dharmas. There were a hundred trillion... [and so forth].
The sound of the dhāraṇī skillfully proclaims the distinctions among all dharma-words, decisively elucidating the secret treasury of the Tathāgata;
its hundreds of thousands of millions of sounds of all dharmas are harmonious and flow smoothly, perfectly blending with all music.

[Treatise] Regarding the fourth [section], from the one hundred million *koṭis* of tiers below down to the passage "harmonizing all music," there are one hundred and eleven and a half lines of scripture.
This contains one hundred eighty-four sets of one hundred million *koṭis* of jewel thrones adorned with various types of colors and categories, as well as the space-division.
The commentary explains that these one hundred million *koṭis* of tiers surround [the assembly] on all sides.
Regarding "circumambulating": the ten abodes (*bhūmi*) are said to be one hundred thousand; the ten practices (*caryā*) are said to be one million;

the ten dedications (*pariṇāmanā*) are said to be one hundred billion, signifying the ascending stages of clarity. Regarding the "one hundred billion golden nets": this is because the net of the well-expounded Dharma is luminously pure.

Regarding the "one hundred billion flower canopies": this is because the myriad practices (*sahasra-caryā*) encompass and integrate all meanings. Regarding the "one hundred billion jewel canopies": [this signifies the adornment of the ultimate reality].
Because one contemplates that the wisdom of all sentient beings is noble and can be encompassed;
because the hundred million billion canopies of garlands represent the great compassion descending into the mundane world to benefit sentient beings;

and because the hundred million billion canopies of incense are spread and displayed above them to clarify the spreading of the karmic retribution of the perfumes of morality, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation, with flower garlands hanging down and emitting fragrance.
The phrase "the fragrance pervades everywhere" clarifies that patience is adorned with ornaments.

The "hundred trillion flower canopies" signify the meaning of the myriad practices (pāramitās) covering and nurturing all sentient beings. The "hundred trillion garland canopies" signify the meaning of compassionate shelter.

The "hundred trillion jewel canopies" signify the meaning of using the Dharma-jewel to shelter the mundane world. The "various devas standing in attendance" clarify those who are able to practice the Way.
The rows on the four sides collectively refer to the four means of integration (*saṃgrahavastu*) and the four immeasurables (*apramāṇa*).

The fact that a hundred trillion precious robes are spread upon them clarifies that through the wisdom and principle of great kindness and great compassion, one constantly dwells within birth and death, clothing sentient beings with robes so as not to cease the karmic retribution [of service].
Thus, the hundred trillion pavilions are exquisitely radiant and magnificently adorned.
The "variegated and radiant adornment" refers to the differentiation of the wisdom of the Bright Observation Tower and the Wisdom Pavilion.
The "hundred million *koṭis* of mani-jewel nets" signifies the teaching-net that filters out the defilements of various delusions.
The "hundred million *koṭis* of jewel nets" signifies that the teaching is able to protect and nurture sentient beings. On the four sides are the "hundred million *koṭis* of jewel garland nets."

The hanging [ornaments] signify that the myriad practices serve as necklaces; because the four means of integration (*saṃgrahavastu*) gather sentient beings, they are named as decorations hanging down from the four sides.

To state the essential point: in general, all resultant environments correspond to their causes and conditions, whether they follow wisdom, practice, compassion, pity, the *pāramitās*, contemplative observation, the factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*), or great vows.
Now, this karmic fruit is represented by the net; principle and wisdom by the pavilion; practice and teaching by the multi-storied tower; contemplative wisdom by the palace;

correct wisdom and the benefit of living beings by the hall; infinite nurturing by the throne; the universal seal of the emptiness of phenomena and the myriad practices of compassion and wisdom by the canopy;
the harmonious and joyful sound of the Dharma by the bells; and the flowers by the gathering of sentient beings according to their faculties.

This symbolizes the blossoming of the eye of the Way and also represents the flowers of practice supporting the fruit. Although the numbers ten, hundred, thousand, ten-thousand, hundred-million, and billion encompass all vast quantities, they are infinite;
one should understand them according to the principles of the Dharma, as it is evident and need not be further explained.
As for what is called *bimba-vastra* in Sanskrit, this is translated here as "shadow-image" (*ying-xing*); it means that the radiance of this canopy is able to manifest all shadows.
Because images appear within it, *bimbara* incense is so named; this fragrant light is pure and bright, capable of manifesting all reflections.
Furthermore, its red-colored radiance is as clear as a *bimbara* fruit. *Arūṇa* incense is like the brilliant, blazing light of the sun.
*Kusuma* flowers—this term has both general and specific meanings; generally, it refers to all grasses.
The "wood-flower" (mùhuā) is another variety; its flowers are white, about the size of a coin, resembling this white chrysanthemum.
"Lánguò yánmào" (lofty pavilions extending far) refers to precious towers connected in long succession.
"Bǎoxīdǐjiā" is translated here as "the mark on the Buddha’s chest consisting of a hundred million virtues. In full, it is called "Qié'āsīdǐjiā"; "qié" means "joy."
*Asitika* means "existence" (*asti*) in this [language]. It clarifies that because one who possesses these marks has great bliss, they are used as an ornament upon the seat.
This mark is a specific name for the *mudrā* (seal) of the devas of joy and the heavenly drum;
it is only through being struck that it can produce sound.
[Sūtra] There were ten trillion bodhisattvas who had first resolved their minds [on enlightenment], who, upon merely seeing this seat, further increased their resolve for omniscience;
ten trillion bodhisattvas who had cultivated the ground, whose minds were pure and filled with joy; ten trillion bodhisattvas who were practicing, whose realization was purified;
ten trillion bodhisattvas of noble birth, who dwelt in superior aspiration and delight; and ten trillion [bodhisattvas] of skillful means.
There were one hundred trillion bodhisattvas who had perfected the arousal of the Mahāyāna practice;

one hundred trillion bodhisattvas dwelling in right-mindedness who diligently cultivated all bodhisattva paths; one hundred trillion non-retrogressive bodhisattvas who purely cultivated all bodhisattva stages;
one hundred trillion youthful bodhisattvas who attained the light of all bodhisattva samādhis; and one hundred trillion crown princes of the Dharma...
When the Bodhisattva entered the inconceivable realm of all Buddhas, one hundred trillion consecrated bodhisattvas were able to manifest the ten powers of immeasurable Tathāgatas;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas attained sovereign supernatural powers; one hundred trillion bodhisattvas gave rise to pure understanding;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas felt love and joy in their hearts; and one hundred trillion bodhisattvas developed profound faith.
It destroys the power of a hundred trillion bodhisattvas; it expands the vast renown of a hundred trillion bodhisattvas;

it increases the exposition of the meaning of the Dharma by a hundred trillion bodhisattvas, causing their wisdom to become definitive; it causes the right mindfulness of a hundred trillion bodhisattvas to remain undisturbed;
it causes a hundred trillion bodhisattvas to give rise to definitive knowledge; and it causes a hundred trillion bodhisattvas to attain the power of hearing and retaining the teachings.
All Buddha-dharmas: one hundred trillion bodhisattvas give birth to immeasurable and vast awakening and understanding;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas abide securely in the faculty of faith; one hundred trillion bodhisattvas attain the dāna-pāramitā and are able to practice universal giving;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas attain the śīla-pāramitā and fully maintain all precepts; one hundred trillion bodhisattvas attain...
With minds unmoved by the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), they are able to endure all Buddha-dharmas;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas have attained the perfection of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*) and are able to practice immeasurable diligence for transcendence;

one hundred trillion bodhisattvas have attained the perfection of meditation (*dhyāna-pāramitā*) and are fully endowed with the immeasurable radiance of meditative concentration (*samādhi*); one hundred trillion bodhisattvas have attained *prajñā*...
If the light of wisdom of the *pāramitās* can universally illuminate ten million billion bodhisattvas so that their great vows are all completely purified;
if ten million billion bodhisattvas attain the dharma-gate of the lamp of wisdom-light that illuminates all phenomena;
if ten million billion bodhisattvas are illuminated by the dharma-light of the Buddhas of the ten directions; and if ten million billion bodhisattvas pervade the ten [directions]...
As he was expounding the Dharma for the abandonment of delusion, one hundred trillion bodhisattvas universally entered all buddha-fields;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas attained the dharma-body that reaches all buddha-lands; one hundred trillion bodhisattvas obtained the voice of the Buddha, capable of widely awakening others;
one hundred trillion bodhisattvas attained the skillful means for generating all-knowledge; and one hundred trillion...

The Bodhisattva has attained the accomplishment of all dharma-gates; through the bodhisattvas’ accomplishment of the wisdom of dharmas, which is like a precious banner, he is able to universally manifest all Buddha-dharmas. One hundred trillion bodhisattvas are able to fully manifest the realm of the Tathāgata.
One hundred trillion celestial kings pay him respectful homage and prostrate themselves before him. One hundred trillion dragon kings gaze upon him with profound attention.
One hundred trillion Yakṣa kings joined their palms above their heads; one hundred trillion Gandharva kings gave rise to pure faith;
one hundred trillion Asura kings severed their prideful intentions;
one hundred trillion Garuḍa kings held silk ribbons in their mouths; one hundred trillion Kiṃnara kings leaped for joy; one hundred trillion [Mahoraga] kings...
The King of the Hūlagas gazed upon him with joy; one hundred trillion lords of the world bowed their heads in prostration;
one hundred trillion kings of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven gazed upon him without blinking; one hundred trillion kings of the Yāma Heaven rejoiced and offered praise;
one hundred trillion kings of the Tuṣita Heaven prostrated themselves with their bodies; and one hundred trillion kings of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven paid homage by touching their heads to the ground.
One hundred trillion kings of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven paid homage with palms joined; one hundred trillion Brahmā kings observed with single-minded attention;
one hundred trillion Maheśvara kings made reverent offerings; one hundred trillion bodhisattvas raised their voices in praise;
one hundred trillion celestial maidens made offerings with focused devotion; and one hundred trillion deities of shared aspiration leaped forth.
Leaping with joy, he was praised by a hundred trillion gods of the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations;
a hundred trillion gods of the Brahma-body realm prostrated themselves with their bodies; a hundred trillion gods of the Ministers of Brahmā joined their palms at their crowns;
a hundred trillion gods of the Retinue of Brahmā surrounded him as his attendants; and a hundred trillion Great Brahmās extolled and proclaimed his immeasurable merits.
Ten trillion Abhasvara devas prostrated themselves with their five limbs touching the ground;
ten trillion Parittabha devas proclaimed and praised that a Buddha’s appearance in the world is difficult to encounter; ten trillion Apramanabha devas paid homage to the Buddha from afar;
ten trillion Abhāsvarābha devas praised how exceedingly difficult it is to behold a Tathāgata; and ten trillion Śuddhāvāsa devas, together with their celestial palaces, came to this place.
One hundred trillion Śuddhāvāsa-devas bowed their heads in salutation with pure minds;
one hundred trillion Apramāṇaśubha-devas threw themselves down, desiring to see the Buddha; one hundred trillion Śubhakṛtsna-devas approached with reverence, respect, and offerings;
one hundred trillion Vṛhatphala-devas recollected their past roots of goodness; and one hundred trillion Parittaśubha-devas [reflected] upon the Tathāgata...
Upon his arrival, a hundred trillion immeasurable and vast gods of the Heaven of Rare Occurrence conceived thoughts of wonder and resolutely honored him, giving rise to various roots of goodness;

a hundred trillion gods of the Vast Fruit Heaven bowed their bodies in reverence; a hundred trillion gods of the Untroubled Heaven, their faculties of faith firm and steadfast, paid him homage with prostrations;
and a hundred trillion gods of the Heatless Heaven joined their palms in mindfulness of the Buddha, never wearying of their devotion.
Ten trillion gods of the Sudarśana Heaven prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet;
ten trillion gods of the Sudṛśa Heaven maintained a mind of offering to the Buddha without weariness; ten trillion gods of the Akaniṣṭha Heaven paid reverent homage;
ten trillion various gods were all filled with great joy and raised their voices in praise; and ten trillion devas each engaged in profound reflection.
A hundred trillion Bodhisattvas adorned the Buddha’s seat with celestial protections in an uninterrupted display of splendor;
a hundred trillion Flower-Handed Bodhisattvas rained down all manner of flowers; a hundred trillion Incense-Handed Bodhisattvas rained down all manner of incenses;
a hundred trillion Garland-Handed Bodhisattvas rained down all manner of garlands; and a hundred trillion Powdered-Incense-Handed Bodhisattvas rained down all manner of powdered incenses.
A hundred trillion Bodhisattvas with Hands of Incense Powder rained down all kinds of incense powder; a hundred trillion Bodhisattvas with Hands of Ointment rained down all kinds of ointments;
a hundred trillion Bodhisattvas with Hands of Robes rained down all kinds of robes; a hundred trillion Bodhisattvas with Hands of Canopies rained down all kinds of canopies;
a hundred trillion Bodhisattvas with Hands of Banners rained down all kinds of banners; a hundred trillion Bodhisattvas with Hands of Pennants rained down all kinds of pennants.
The Bodhisattva *Vajra-koṭi-ratna-hasta* rained down all manner of jewels; the Bodhisattva *Śata-koṭi-vyūha-hasta* rained down all manner of ornaments.
One hundred trillion sons of gods emerged from their celestial palaces and arrived at the place of the seat.
One hundred trillion sons of gods, together with their palaces, did so out of pure faith. One hundred trillion *Jāti-prabhava* sons of gods...
A hundred trillion crown princes (*abhiṣeka-devaputra*) held up their entire bodies to support the seat;

a hundred trillion Bodhisattvas of Contemplation (*cintā-maṇi-bodhisattva*) respectfully contemplated it; a hundred trillion Bodhisattvas of Noble Birth (*jāti-śreṣṭha-bodhisattva*) gave rise to pure minds;

a hundred trillion Bodhisattvas experienced joy in their sense faculties; a hundred trillion Bodhisattvas attained purity of their profound resolve (*gambhīra-citta*); and a hundred trillion Bodhisattvas were filled with faith.
They understand the purification of the myriad billions of karmas of bodhisattvas; they possess the mastery over birth of the myriad billions of bodhisattvas;
they illuminate with the light of the Dharma of the myriad billions of bodhisattvas; they achieve the stages of the myriad billions of bodhisattvas;
and they are skillfully able to teach and transform all sentient beings.

[Treatise] Fifth: There are one hundred trillion Bodhisattvas who have first resolved their minds [upon enlightenment], down to one hundred trillion Bodhisattvas who are well-able to teach and transform all sentient beings;
seventy-six fascicles of sutra explain the Bodhisattvas’ entry into the Dharma.
The assembly of the various devas and the eight classes of supernatural beings totals one hundred and eight times one hundred trillion, forming a vast ocean of the great assembly.
Having clearly distinguished the arrayed jewel-ground and the space above, the forty assemblies of bodhisattvas clearly perceive the adornment of their seats;
through the method of contemplation, they enter the Dharma with double-folded intensity, ascending and progressing as the realm of adornment.

These "forty assemblies" clarify the ten abodes (*bhūmi*), the ten practices (*caryā*), the ten transferences (*pariṇāmanā*), and the ten stages (*bhūmi*). This clarifies that these celestial aggregates cultivate these four.
Because the stages and dharmas of Samantabhadra’s conduct are spontaneously perfected,
from the hundred trillion celestial kings below down to the hundred trillion Mahesvara celestial kings above— totaling sixteen kings—
one comprehensively clarifies that these ten dharma-gates of dedication pervade the three realms, using wisdom to encompass both the lords of the desire realm and the form realm.
Because they follow compassion to universally benefit sentient beings throughout the six realms with sovereignty like that of a king,

the names of sixteen kinds of kings are cited in total to clearly manifest this stage as comprehensively encompassing the human and celestial realms of the six paths; because they teach and transform sentient beings with wisdom like a king,
exercising unimpeded sovereignty, first, one hundred trillion celestial kings are mentioned in total, clarifying that the celestial kings possess the greatest sovereignty.
Thus, separately mentioning the Dragon King who clearly observes and understands, the Yakṣa King Root-Rain-Dharma-Sovereign who joins his palms above the crown of the head to provide protection,
and the Gandharva King Sovereignty-Arising-Pure-Faith who delights sentient beings with the joy of the Dharma,
as well as the hundred trillion Asura Kings who have severed arrogance, clarifies [the following].
Entering the ocean of birth and death through great compassion, they humbly engage in the same activities as others;

this signifies the mastery of guiding and receiving sentient beings by descending into the mundane world. One hundred trillion *garuḍa* kings with silk ribbons held in their beaks represent this mastery.
One hundred trillion *kiṃnara* kings leaping for joy signify that they are able to delight sentient beings with the music and songs of the Dharma.
"Because they are joyful and sovereign, the hundred trillion mahoraga kings gaze upon him with joy" clarifies that those who crawl on their bellies express the meaning of reverence.

"Because they are sovereign, the hundred trillion lords of the world bow their heads in prostration" clarifies the meaning of the Four Heavenly Kings leading sentient beings according to the rules of conduct. Thus, these are the masters and the deities.
From the nāgas and spirits down to those in the hells, all are gathered under his authority;
ten million billion kings of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven gaze upon him with unblinking eyes as he dwells in the stage of the Ten Abodes, cultivating skillful means and seeking the definitive meaning.
Ten million billion kings of the Yāma Heaven joyfully praise him, for his dharma-music of hymns and verses is like the pleasures of the world.
The praise clarifies that because this deva delights in the ten dharmas of practice, one hundred trillion kings of the Tuṣita Heaven prostrate by stretching out their bodies;
this clarifies that this deva possesses great compassion, stretching his body like the earth to bear all burdens without weariness.
That one hundred trillion kings of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven pay homage with their heads at his feet clarifies his humble disposition.

"Penetrating to the Great Compassion that bends wisdom to the ultimate limit of compassion" means that the hundred million *koṭi* of kings of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven join their palms in reverence to clarify that wisdom and compassion, as well as saṃsāra and nirvāṇa, are not one bit different.
"The hundred million *koṭi* of Brahmā kings observe with a single mind" clarifies the meaning of eliminating subtle habitual tendencies. The hundred million... [text ends]
A hundred million Mahesvara Heavenly Kings reverently make offerings; because the Dharma-body of clear wisdom and great compassion is perfect and worthy of reverence and offering,
these aforementioned sixteen heavenly kings, dragon kings, and others— whose wisdom, clarity,
and compassion are perfected and who exercise sovereignty over the three realms and six paths like kings— are all [numbered] one hundred million each, which signifies this meaning.
"Endowed with great vows, wisdom, compassion, and conduct" clarifies that the aforementioned sixteen kings collectively encompass the bodhisattva practices,

such that they are all universally worthy of praise. "A hundred trillion goddesses made offerings with single-minded devotion" clarifies that the practices of the preceding sixteen kings and others were untainted by defilement and characterized by great loving-kindness and compassion.
Because it pervades the three realms, one hundred trillion devas who shared the same vows leap for joy;
this clarifies that within this stage of the desire realm, there were likewise those who shared the same vows in the past.
Furthermore, one hundred trillion devas who dwelt together in the past clarify that the bodhisattvas in these ten stages of dedication all share the same vows and practices as the Buddhas.

After all the Buddhas had established themselves in the great compassionate vows and practices, they manifested their bodies to pay homage to the hundred trillion Brahmakāyika devas below, down as far as the Akaniṣṭha heaven.
Above the luminous realm of the first dhyāna, there are twenty assemblies of devas in total; these collectively comprise all the various hosts of the form realm, beginning with the sixteen kings.
This section, comprising approximately sixteen lines of scripture, simultaneously encompasses the aforementioned sequence of distinct listings of the heavens of the Formless Realm (*ārūpyadhātu*).

Because these realms are characterized by meditative absorption (*samādhi*), they are submerged in stillness and are not yet capable of generating the aspiration for awakening (*bodhicitta*) in the present world; thus, the ritual of transformation does not reach their domain.
From the Brahmakāyika heaven downward to the Akaniṣṭha heaven, there are twenty assemblies of devas. Akaniṣṭha...
The *Tathāgata* Heaven is the Akaniṣṭha Heaven; this heaven is the pinnacle of the Form Realm (*rūpadhātu*).
Above this, the twenty assemblies of devas represent the practice of great compassion within these ten dedications (*pariṇāmanā*). "Heaven" signifies purity.

It clarifies that through great compassion and great wisdom, one constantly dwells in birth-and-death (*saṃsāra*) to teach and transform sentient beings; like Maheśvara, one remains free from defilement.
Regarding the Brahmakāyika devas prostrating with their bodies, there are two meanings: first, to pay respectful homage to the Tathāgata;

second, to manifest the Dharma of great compassion that is as humble as the earth. Regarding the hundred trillion Brahmapurohita devas joining their palms at their crowns, there are also two meanings:
first, to revere the Buddha; second, to manifest the Dharma of joyful progress. The hundred trillion Brahmakāyika devas surround and attend them as an escort.
There are also two meanings: first, to show reverence and compliance toward the Buddha; second, to manifest that by following right mindfulness, one delivers sentient beings.
Furthermore, there are two meanings to the fact that a hundred trillion Great Brahmā deities praise and extol his immeasurable merits: first, to reverently praise the Buddha;
second, to manifest through the Dharma that sentient beings possess the merits of the Buddha. There are also five [meanings] regarding the hundred trillion Ābhāsvara deities...
Prostrating oneself by casting the body to the ground also has two meanings: first, to show reverence for the Buddha; second, to manifest the Dharma.

In relation to this stage, taking great compassion as the "ground" clarifies that one casts the precepts, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation onto the ground of the compassion within birth-and-death.
Furthermore, the hundred trillion *parītta-ābhā* (Lesser Light) devas proclaiming and praising how difficult it is to encounter a Buddha in the world also has two [meanings].

The first meaning is to revere the World-Honored One, who is difficult to encounter; the second is to express the Dharma and praise sentient beings regarding the difficulty of generating the bodhicitta.
Regarding the passage on the immeasurable light-devas of hundreds of millions of billions who from afar pay homage to the Buddha, there are also two meanings: first, to revere the Buddha;

second, to express the Dharma, clarifying that he teaches and transforms all sentient beings so that they may attain faith and understanding; therefore, it is called "seeing from afar" hundreds of millions of billions.
The praise by the Ābhāsvara devas that the Tathāgata is extremely difficult to encounter also has two meanings: first, that he is difficult to meet and difficult to see;
second, it expresses the Dharma by showing that one's own mind is difficult to know.

That hundreds of millions of billions of pure devas, together with their palaces, come to visit the Buddha also has two meanings as before: first, to pay respect to the Buddha; second, to express the Dharma by clarifying compassion.
In the Palace of Perfect Wisdom, one hundred trillion Śuddhāvāsakāyika gods of the Minor Purity Heaven prostrated themselves with pure minds.
There are two meanings as before: first, to pay homage to the Buddha; second, to manifest reverence for the principle and phenomena of the Light of Dharma.
One hundred trillion gods of the Immeasurable Purity Heaven, desiring to see the Buddha, cast their bodies downward. There are two meanings as before.

First, revering the Buddha; second, manifesting the Dharma and bestowing compassion to save the mundane world—hereafter, one should understand these according to their meaning and practice them accordingly.

As for the phrase "ten million billion various heavens all rejoice," these heavenly hosts consist of various classes of gods from both the Form Realm and the Desire Realm; therefore, they are called "various. This collectively expresses the multitude of practices.
Because they are fully endowed with various practices for the benefit of sentient beings, one hundred trillion devas each engage in skillful reflection;

this collectively refers to all the devas within the Form Realm and the Desire Realm heavens, who are all called the "one hundred trillion Bodhisattva devas" who protect and uphold the Buddha’s seat with uninterrupted adornment.
This refers specifically to the Tuṣita Heaven, yet it also serves to symbolize the Dharma.
The Dharma-realm constitutes the body of the seat, and the myriad practices serve as its adornments. These aforementioned three assemblies, together with the preceding twenty-three assemblies—
from the Bodhisattva Flower-Hand of a hundred trillion down to the hundred trillion consecrated sons of heaven—
constitute eleven assemblies of bodhisattvas who support the seat with their entire bodies, along with four assemblies of sons of heaven, all of whom collectively [support it].

Regarding the first of the fifteen assemblies, the hundred trillion Puṣpahasta Bodhisattvas rained down all manner of flowers; this has three meanings: first, raining flowers from the void as an offering to the Buddha;
second, initiating practice through emptiness; and third, clarifying that in past lives they created flowers as the cause [for their present state].
Furthermore, the hundred trillion Gandhahasta Bodhisattvas rained down all manner of incense; this also has three meanings: first, raining down incense...
Making offerings to the Buddha through the two types of clarity (vidyā) and the fragrance of the fivefold Dharma-body; making offerings with incense through the three types of past causal practices.

Regarding the offering of garlands by the hundred million *koṭi* of Mālāhasta Bodhisattvas, there are also three meanings: first, raining down garlands as an offering to the Buddha; second, taking patience (*kṣānti*) as a garland;
and third, clarifying the past causes of creating garlands to offer to the Buddha. The subsequent sections should be understood according to this principle, as in the *Bai* [Sūtra].
The myriad billions of devaputras emerge from their celestial palaces and arrive at the assembly; this has two meanings: first, they leave their palaces to make offerings to the Buddha;
second, it clarifies that wisdom unites with compassion. The myriad billions of devaputras, together with their palaces, do so with pure faith;
this also has two meanings: first, they present their palaces as offerings to the Buddha; second, it symbolizes the perfect integration of compassion and wisdom.
The hundred trillion *Janmaja* (Born-Noble) devaputras supporting the seat with their bodies also has two meanings: first, to support the seat as an offering to the Buddha;
second, to symbolize that this "Born-Noble Abode" is governed by the fourth *pāramitā*, for diligence (*vīrya*) is the meaning of supporting the seat.
The hundred trillion *Abhiṣikta* (Consecrated) devas supporting the seat with their entire bodies also has two meanings: first, to lift the entire body...
Holding the seat and making offerings to the Buddha—these two represent the empowerment, wisdom, compassion, and power of the tenth stage (*daśabhūmi*), which have been further strengthened.
These four kinds of devaputras are precisely the various devaputras within the Tuṣita Heaven of the desire realm.

As the sutra states, by calculating them in succession, they are combined with the tenth stage; furthermore, it clarifies that "son" refers to the name of "loving-kindness" (*maitrī*), because one cultivates loving-kindness. Thus, it is complete.

He was titled "Compassionate. Following this, from the hundred million *koṭi* of Bodhisattvas who have attained contemplation down to those who are well-able to teach and transform all sentient beings—this section contains ten Bodhisattvas who, by purifying the three karmas or entering and abiding in the stages (*bhūmi*), adorn the Dharma assembly;
their names and meanings are all readily understandable.
[Sūtra] Born from hundreds of thousands of millions of roots of goodness; sustained by hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddhas; perfected by hundreds of thousands of millions of merits;
purified by hundreds of thousands of millions of sublime minds; adorned and cleansed by hundreds of thousands of millions of great vows;

brought forth by hundreds of thousands of millions of virtuous deeds; made firm by hundreds of thousands of millions of wholesome dharmas; [empowered by] hundreds of thousands of millions of spirits...
He praises with a hundred trillion methods of praise accomplished through the hundred trillion merits manifested by his power.
[Treatise] From "born from the sixth hundred trillion roots of goodness" down to "hundred trillion methods of praise."
Regarding the praise, the *Pañcākāra-sūtra* clarifies the ten kinds of roots of goodness that adorn the palace and the jeweled throne;

the commentary on its meaning states: "From 'born from hundreds of thousands of millions of roots of goodness' down to 'adorned by ten million times ten million myriad virtuous practices,' it is fully explained as in the sūtra."
[Sūtra] Just as the King of Tuṣita in this world has respectfully prepared a high seat for the Tathāgata,
so too do the Kings of Tuṣita in all worlds prepare seats for the Buddha in such a manner, with such adornments,
such rituals, such faith and joy, such purity of mind, such delight, such gladness, and such reverence.
They conceived such thoughts of rarity, such exultation, and such yearning— all of which were entirely equal.
[Treatise] The seventh section, from "In this world" down to "all are entirely equal," clarifies this through five lines of scripture.
Having collectively bound the ten directions into uniform divisions, there were one hundred eighteen kinds of assemblies of more than a hundred billion followers;
there were one hundred eighty-four kinds of adornments of more than a hundred billion adornments.
These constitute the total number for this section; the aforementioned adornments, as well as the bodhisattvas, devas, and classes of celestial maidens, were interspersed among one another.
The phrase "either sequential or non-sequential" indicates that these ten stages of dedication (*pariṇāmanā*) constitute a great ocean of compassion achieved through wisdom arising from pity.
Within the six realms of existence—humans and devas—one simultaneously and equally transforms beings throughout the infinite, all-pervading Dharmadhātu.
According to their faculties, one bestows the Dharma, whether sequentially, by leaping over stages, by remaining stationary, through faith, or through the successive ranks of the ten stages.
Whether among the realms of the earth, humans, or devas, there is no single instance where roots of goodness are established in a fixed, sequential order.
This is because they are interspersed with these adornments and the symbolic manifestations of bodhisattvas and devas, which do not follow a sequential arrangement.

For example, within a gathering of bodhisattvas there may be devas, or within a gathering of devas there may be nāgas and spirits. One should reflect upon this principle to discern the intended meaning of the sūtra. Thus it was asked.

It is said that in the Ten Abodes (*daśabhūmi*), there are only the assemblies of devas who come to welcome the World-Honored One; in the Ten Practices (*daśacaryā*), there are assemblies of devas as well as bodhisattvas.
Why is it that in this assembly, the great multitude of the eight classes of beings is so vast, magnificent, and diverse in their forms?
Furthermore, why is it that in the Ten Grounds (*daśabhūmi*), there is no mention of celestial kings and their retinues coming to welcome him into the palace hall?
Regarding the purpose of preparing the high seat and other such matters: why is it that while his position is elevated, no extensive offerings are presented? The answer is:

for those in the Ten Abodes (*daśabhūmi*), there is no welcoming by Bodhisattvas from the heavens as there is for the Tathāgata; the offerings provided here are intended for the stage of the Ten Abodes.

Furthermore, this clarifies that although one has been born into the family of Buddha-wisdom, one has not yet previously seen the Way. Thus, only the various devas are enumerated, and not [the Bodhisattvas].

There are bodhisattvas who, being at the very beginning as ordinary persons (*pṛthagjana*) on the stage of faith (*śraddhā-bhūmi*) and not yet having entered the stage of the noble ones (*ārya*), are represented by this "Chapter on First Ascending the Summit of Mount Sumeru.
Because there is no assembly of bodhisattvas listed here, but only various devas welcoming the Tathāgata, it clarifies that from this stage one enters the stream of the noble ones.
This is why, in the "Chapter on Entering the Yāma Heaven Palace," [the assembly of bodhisattvas] is indeed present.

The fact that the assembly of devas and bodhisattvas offers praise and eulogy clarifies that those in the stage of the Ten Abodes have already attained the Path of Vision (*darśana-mārga*) and entered the [bodhisattva] stages.
Within the progression of the Ten Practices (*daśa-caryā*), there is an assembly of bodhisattvas who welcome the Buddha into the assembly to enter the Dharma-gate of the Ten Practices;
for while the Ten Abodes and Ten Practices establish various practices, the supramundane mind is predominant.
Because Great Compassion while dwelling in the world has not yet attained mastery, the assembly is not yet complete.

Thus, the abundance of devas, bodhisattvas, and varieties of adornments in this Tuṣita Heaven Palace illustrates that through this gate of dedication, compassion and wisdom are harmoniously integrated;
transcending the world and yet being one with it, one accomplishes great compassion to universally nurture all sentient beings.
Consciousness pervades everywhere, benefiting all beings without abandoning even the smallest life form.

Therefore, the celestial kings, dragon kings, the eight classes of spirits, the various kings, and the Bodhisattvas—the Dharma Kings—possess immeasurable assemblies and boundless manifestations of adorned realms and physical forms.

They clearly manifest the stage of compassion, embracing and expanding it to save living beings without limit. Their benefit of beings is vast and the gain obtained is inexhaustible; such is this heaven.

Its adornment is as vast as the stage of the ten bhūmis; yet, regarding this period of the ten dedications (*pariṇāmanā*) within Great Compassion, it is the gateway through which wisdom nurtures the far-reaching [scope] of Great Compassion, causing it to grow and become firm and thick.
There is no other dharma apart from this for further pursuit. Even if there were extraordinary paths of wisdom, they would merely be subtle refinements within this very stage. Therefore—

When the Buddha ascended to the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations (*paranirmita-vaśavartin*), there was no separate retinue to welcome him, nor was there any need to discuss the addition of further tiers to the seat for his cultivation; this can be understood.
[Sūtra] At that time, the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, having prepared a seat for the Tathāgata, gave rise to a mind of deep respect and, together with ten...
Ten billion *asaṃkhyeya* sons of the Tuṣita heaven welcomed the Tathāgata, raining down clouds of *asaṃkhyeya* colored flowers with pure minds;
raining down clouds of inconceivable colors and fragrances; raining down clouds of various colored garlands;
raining down clouds of vast and pure sandalwood; raining down clouds of immeasurable and diverse canopies; and raining down clouds of exquisite celestial garments.

Clouds of various exquisite jewels rained down, clouds of celestial ornaments rained down, clouds of immeasurable varieties of burning incense rained down, and clouds of all kinds of sandalwood, aloeswood, and solid powdered incense rained down.
At that time, from the bodies of each of the hosts of devaputras, these various clouds issued forth;
then hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* Tuṣita devaputras and other devas present in the assembly [did likewise].
The assembly of sons [of the Buddha] was filled with great joy; they paid homage with reverence and prostrated themselves.
Countless celestial maidens leaped for joy and, with longing admiration, gazed intently upon the Tathāgata.

In the Tuṣita palace, unspeakably many bodhisattvas remained suspended in mid-air, diligently and single-mindedly offering to the Buddha all manner of celestial offerings that surpassed those of the gods, while paying him respectful obeisance.
The *Saṃghāṭa* music was performed all at once.

[Treatise] Second: This section of the sūtra, from "At that time, the King of Tuṣita Heaven" down to "the music was performed all at once," clarifies how the King of Tuṣita Heaven, having already prepared a seat for the Buddha, together with the assembly of devas, [proceeded] with a pure mind.

Regarding the passage "raising clouds of offerings and various bodhisattvas to welcome the Tathāgata," the *Fen shi yi* (Explanation of the Divided Meaning) states that there are two meanings to welcoming the Tathāgata with ten trillion *asaṃkhyeya* devaputras from Tuṣita: first, to invite the Buddha to enter the palace;
second, to manifest the Dharma by using the great wisdom that abides nowhere through liberation to dwell amidst all of birth and death.
Benefiting sentient beings is the meaning of "welcoming the Buddha. Another interpretation is as follows:

just as one who has newly entered the stage of sainthood (*ārya-bhūmi*) enters the gate of reality through the samādhi of skillful means (*upāya-samādhi*), so too does this stage of the Ten Dedications (*daśa-pariṇāmanā*)—by means of the stainless, correct wisdom found within the Ten Abidings (*daśa-vihāra*) and the Ten Practices (*daśa-caryā*)—enter great compassion and skillful means. This is like "welcoming the Buddha into the palace," analogous to the stages (*bhūmi*) within the Three Vehicles.
The first thirty minds constitute the preparatory stage (*prayoga*) for the ten stages (*bhūmi*). The path of seeing (*darśana-mārga*) is as described in this sutra:

the ten minds of faith (*śraddhā-citta*) serve as the preparatory provisions (*sambhāra*), while the initial mind of the ten abidings (*vihāra*) constitutes the path of seeing. The attainment of Buddhahood proceeds through the ten practices (*caryā*), the ten transferences (*pariṇāmana*), the ten stages, and the eleventh stage, which serve as the provisions.
Through these provisions, the initial mind of right view (*samyag-dṛṣṭi*) in the first abiding is perfected, thereby causing one to become habituated to it.
This is because, according to the teachings of the three vehicles, one only attains Buddhahood after three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas*.

Thus, it is established that while Bodhisattvas of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) attain the three kinds of mind-made bodies (*manomaya-kāya*), this does not mean they have attained the wisdom of a Buddha’s birth-body (*jāti-kāya*).

Therefore, the Bodhisattvas of the three stages of worthiness (*tri-puṇya-kṣetra*) prior to the ten stages constitute the stage of equipment (*sambhāra-avasthā*), while the ten stages of seeing the path (*darśana-mārga*) constitute the stage of application (*prayoga-avasthā*).

Within the stage of Equal Enlightenment (Samyaksambodhi) of the first bhūmi, the practices of Samantabhadra finally reach their consummation; the twelve bhūmis constitute the fruit of the Buddha of Sublime Enlightenment (Miaojue).
This is the "Flower of the Buddha" (*Buddhapuṣpa*); its meaning is that the fruit of Buddhahood comes first, followed by practice.

Only after the fruit of Buddhahood is first realized does one employ the practice of compassionate vows to support the essence of enlightenment, so that compassion and wisdom may be equally balanced. For this reason, it is called the "Flower of the Buddha."

Therefore, this present King of Tuṣita Heaven employs the skillful means of great compassion (*mahākaruṇopāya*) to support the great wisdom and the fruit of Buddhahood within the ten abodes (*daśavihāra*) and ten practices (*daśacaryā*). For the purpose of welcoming the Buddha,
the teaching of this stage manifests the great essence of the Dharma by employing the ocean of great compassion to support the Buddha [nature] within the ten abodes and ten practices.
Because of the perfect awakening of wisdom, he is titled the "Welcoming Buddha. For the Dharma has no beginning or end;
in a single thought-moment, all practices—compassion and wisdom—are equal and complete in their essence. When the teachings are established through names and words, these cannot stand together;

yet while names and explanations seem to imply a sequence of before and after, one who realizes the essence of names finds that names have no beginning or end. One who penetrates the teaching [realizes] the realm.
The intent of this teaching is that wisdom does not shift; it clarifies that the present and the past are one single limit (*ekānta*), and that emotional defilements are shattered in the very moment.
Ultimately, one must not interpret this in terms of extension or contraction. From beginning to end, the vision as a whole does not transcend the principle of "timelessness" (*akāla*).

It is through this that the gates of reconciling the one and the many, and their various distinctions, are opened. Generally, to regard a prior stage as distant from a subsequent stage constitutes "vision from afar."
The true meaning of the Buddha’s arrival at the palace to rain down clouds of incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) colored flowers with a pure mind has two significances:
first, to make offerings to the Buddha; second, to symbolize that the light of the Dharma and great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) pervade all through the myriad practices (*sādhana*).

That these clouds possess ten kinds of luminous qualities signifies the perfection of the practice of the Dharma. That they all issue from celestial bodies signifies that the body of wisdom (*jñānakāya*) gives rise to the myriad practices.

The *Mahāsattva-devaputra-sūtra* (The Scripture of the Great Assembly of Deva-sons) states that those who joyfully prostrate themselves [to the Buddha] do so because the light of the Dharma’s rules and regulations benefits sentient beings and causes them to attain happiness.

It clarifies that the great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) of the Bodhisattvas causes sentient beings to attain happiness, for this is the happiness of the Bodhisattvas themselves—just as when a worldly mother’s child is happy, the mother is happy. This cannot be fully described even within the Tuṣita Palace.
The various bodhisattvas dwell in the midst of space, diligently and single-mindedly making offerings that surpass those of the devas;

through the clarity of the emptiness of phenomena (*dharma-śūnyatā*), they perfect their practice, thereby excelling the conditioned practices of the world. This section contains thirteen kinds of assemblies.
