[Sūtra] When the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, O Son of the Buddha, dedicate in this manner, they do not discriminate between "self" and "mine."
They do not conceptually differentiate the Buddha nor the Buddha-dharma; they do not differentiate the buddha-fields nor their adornment and purification;
they do not differentiate sentient beings nor their discipline; they do not differentiate karma nor the retribution of karma.

They do not cling to volition nor that which arises from volition; they do not destroy causes nor destroy results; they do not grasp at phenomena nor grasp at dharmas; they do not claim that saṃsāra has divisions.
"Separation" does not mean that *nirvāṇa* is eternally quiescent; it does not mean that the Tathāgata, having realized the Buddha-realm, has even the slightest dharma coexisting with other dharmas.
[Śāstra]: From "The six Buddha-sons" down to "there is not even the slightest dharma coexisting with dharmas," there are six lines of sūtra.
The section on clarity, non-discrimination, non-attachment, and non-appropriation.
[Sūtra] When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, they universally bestow all roots of goodness upon sentient beings,
bringing them to certain maturity and teaching them with equanimity— being signless, objectless, immeasurable, and free from falsehood, far removed [from conceptualization].

Having thus dedicated [merit], the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, free from all conceptualization and attachment, attains inexhaustible roots of goodness by recollecting all Buddhas of the three periods of time; he attains inexhaustible roots of goodness by recollecting all Bodhisattvas;
and he attains inexhaustible roots of goodness by purifying all Buddha-fields. He attains inexhaustible roots of goodness by purifying one...
Because they encompass the entire realm of sentient beings, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness; because they enter deeply into the dharma-realm, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness;
because they cultivate immeasurable minds equal to the realm of empty space, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness;

because they profoundly understand the sphere of all Buddhas, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness; and because they diligently practice and train in the deeds of Bodhisattvas, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness.
"Because they thoroughly comprehend the three periods of time, they attain inexhaustible roots of goodness.
[Treatise] From "The disciples of the seven Buddhas" down to "attaining inexhaustible roots of goodness," there are ten lines of scripture;
this constitutes the section on the Bodhisattva attaining inexhaustible roots of goodness.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this manner, they realize that the realm of sentient beings contains no sentient beings;
they understand that all phenomena contain no life-span; they know that all phenomena contain no agent;
they awaken to the fact that all phenomena contain no *pudgala*; and they realize that all phenomena contain no anger.
He contemplates that all phenomena arise from conditions and have no place of abiding; he knows that all things have nothing upon which they rely;
he understands that all lands are entirely without a fixed location; he contemplates that all bodhisattva practices likewise have no locus;
and he sees that all objective realms are utterly non-existent.

[Treatise] From "The eight sons of the Buddha" down to "all objective spheres are non-existent," these six lines of sūtra clarify that the Bodhisattva realizes that within the realm of sentient beings there are no sentient beings, and regarding phenomena there is nothing to be attained or realized.
*Pudgala* means "one who repeatedly takes up existence."
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates in this manner, his eye ultimately never sees impure buddha-fields, nor does he see sentient beings with diverse characteristics.
There is not the slightest dharma that enters into wisdom, nor is there the slightest wisdom that enters into dharmas.
He understands that the body of the Tathāgata is not like empty space; it is comprised of immeasurable and wondrous merits.
Because it is perfected by the Dharma, it causes all sentient beings in all places to fully accumulate roots of goodness so that they are completely satisfied.
[Treatise] From "The nine sons of the Buddha" down to "completely satisfied," there are five lines of scripture clarifying the bodhisattva’s absence of...
The section on the entry of wisdom into phenomena and the entry of phenomena into wisdom.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, in every thought-moment, attains the unspeakably unspeakable stages of the Ten Powers;
he is fully endowed with all merit, has perfected pure roots of goodness, and acts for the sake of all sentient beings.
Kṣetra-guṇa: This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has accomplished the treasury of merit of the wish-fulfilling maṇi;
thus, whatever articles of enjoyment he requires, he obtains them all. In whatever direction he travels, he is able to adorn and purify all lands.
In whatever place he goes, he causes unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings to become entirely pure and brings them into his embrace.
"Because of cultivating and purifying all practices through merit.
[Treatise]: From "O sons of the Buddha" down to "because of cultivating and purifying all practices," there are six and a half lines of scripture;
this constitutes the section on how the Bodhisattva accomplishes the treasury of merit and is worthy of being a field of merit for sentient beings.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva thus dedicates [merit], they cultivate all Bodhisattva practices;
their meritorious and sublime physical marks are peerless, and their majestic power and radiance transcend all worlds. Neither Māra nor his followers can gaze upon them.
They are fully endowed with roots of goodness, have accomplished their great vows, and their minds are so vastly expanded that they are equal to omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
In a single thought-moment, they are able to pervade all immeasurable Buddha-fields with the power of wisdom;
they possess immeasurable knowledge that thoroughly penetrates the realms of all Buddhas; they attain profound faith and understanding in all Buddhas; they abide in boundless wisdom;
their bodhicitta-power is as vast as the Dharma-realm and ultimately equal to space. O Son of the Buddha, this is called the fifth [stage] of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
The Dedication to the Inexhaustible Treasury of Merit.

[Commentary]: From "O sons of the Buddha" down to the fifth dedication, the Inexhaustible Treasury of Merit—spanning approximately seven and a half lines of scripture—constitutes the section on the Bodhisattva’s marks of merit, which are peerless in the world.
[Sūtra] When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this dedication, they attain ten kinds of inexhaustible treasuries. What are these ten? They are:
attaining the inexhaustible treasury of seeing Buddhas, because within a single pore they see incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) Buddhas appearing in the world;
attaining the inexhaustible treasury of entering the Dharma, because by the power of the Buddha’s wisdom they perceive that all phenomena (*dharma*) entirely enter into a single phenomenon.
Thus, they attain the inexhaustible treasury of recollection and retention, because they uphold all the teachings spoken by all Buddhas without forgetfulness;
they attain the inexhaustible treasury of definitive wisdom, because they skillfully know the secret expedient means of all the teachings spoken by all Buddhas;

they attain the inexhaustible treasury of understanding meaning and intent, because they skillfully know the principles, patterns, and limits of all phenomena; and they attain boundless realization and comprehension.

Because they have penetrated all phenomena of the three periods of time through wisdom that is like space, they obtain the inexhaustible treasury of merit, which fills the minds of all sentient beings and is itself inexhaustible;

because they are able to completely eliminate the cataracts of ignorance and folly of all sentient beings, they obtain the inexhaustible treasury of courageous wisdom-awakening; because they obtain definitive eloquence—
The inexhaustible treasury of expounding the equality of all Buddhas, so that all sentient beings may fully understand it;

the attainment of the ten powers and fearlessnesses through the inexhaustible treasury; the fulfillment of all bodhisattva practices by binding the crown of the head with a stainless silk ribbon until reaching unobstructed omniscience—these, O sons of the Buddha, are the ten [qualities] of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
When dedicating all roots of goodness, one attains these ten kinds of inexhaustible treasuries.
[Treatise] From "the bodhisattva-mahāsattva" downwards to the ten kinds of inexhaustible treasuries, there are fourteen and a half lines of scripture;
this is the section of the scripture concerning the bodhisattva’s attainment of the ten inexhaustible treasuries. It says: "In a single pore..."

Seeing the appearance of countless Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, arising in the world and attaining entry into the inexhaustible treasury of the Dharma, one clarifies that the nature of the mind is fundamentally without distinctions of large or small.
Taking the entire body as the limit of wisdom’s reflection, the Buddha-lands are likewise so;

the purity of wisdom’s reflections and their mutual interpenetration of large and small forms are illustrated by the analogy of the realm of Indra’s net. As the Sūtra says: "By means of the Buddha-wisdom..."
To forcefully contemplate that all phenomena enter into a single phenomenon means to clarify that although the myriad objects are many, they all arise from the one mind;
when the mind perishes, the objects perish, and the myriad objects are all empty, like various reflections in clear water.

When the water vanishes, the reflections vanish—this is explained in terms of destroying existence to establish non-existence. Furthermore, regarding objects in relation to wisdom: wisdom arises [from] objects, yet wisdom is empty and objects are illusory and manifold.
The illusory appearance enters into and is not separate from the one; the void does not differ from the illusory, and the illusory does not differ from the void.

Illusion and the void are non-dual; whether as one or as different, they are entirely void. This is explained by way of the gate of the sovereign and unimpeded mastery of the voidness of illusion through wisdom.

All of this is spoken by borrowing phenomena as metaphors for what is known in accordance with reality; it can only be realized when thought is extinguished, and only when one’s wisdom accords with that [reality] can it be attained.

Functioning while remaining eternally true, one is not deluded regarding the mind and its objects; through the power of great vows, bodies manifest as illusory transformations according to wisdom, equal in number to all sentient beings, gathering and transforming them as appropriate.
Therefore, it is called the "Inexhaustible Treasury of Merit. The remainder is fully contained within the text itself and need not be further explained here.
[Sūtra] At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse.
[Śāstra] Section Thirteen: From "At that time" onwards, this single line of sūtra clarifies the section on the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja’s delivery of verses.
[Sūtra] The Bodhisattva accomplishes the power of profound resolve, attaining mastery over all dharmas.
Through the merit of exhorting [the Buddhas] and rejoicing [in their deeds],
he skillfully dedicates it with unimpeded expedient means to all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, purifying Buddha-fields throughout the world.
There are no merits that are not fully possessed; the dedication to pure lands is likewise.
All the Buddha-dharmas of the three periods of time, the Bodhisattva contemplates them all with clear mindfulness.
Gathering them into the mind without exception, he thus adorns the buddha-fields.
Even if one were to exhaust all eons throughout the three periods of time To praise the various merits of a single Buddha-field,
The eons of the three periods of time might yet come to an end, But the merits of a Buddha-field are inexhaustible.
In this way, the Bodhisattva perceives all such Buddha-fields Without exception or remainder.
In total, they adorn a single Buddha-field; all Buddha-fields are likewise so.
Those sons of the Buddha whose minds are pure are all born through transformation from the Tathāgata’s Dharma.
With minds adorned by every merit, they fill all Buddha-lands.
Those bodhisattvas are all fully endowed with bodies adorned by immeasurable marks and signs;
their eloquence in preaching pervades the world, like the great ocean which is inexhaustible.
These bodhisattvas dwell securely in various samādhis, and all their practices are completely perfected.
Their minds are pure and peerless, their radiance universally illuminating the worlds of the ten directions;
thus, throughout all Buddha-fields without exception, these bodhisattvas completely fill them.
They have never even thought of the vehicle of the śrāvakas, nor do they seek the path of the pratyekabuddhas.
With such a pure mind, the Bodhisattva dedicates their roots of goodness to all living beings,
universally desiring that they all attain the Perfect Path. Possessing complete knowledge of all the Buddha-dharmas,
the Bodhisattva’s majestic power utterly crushes all the māras and enemies throughout the ten directions.
With courageous wisdom that none can surpass, The Bodhisattva resolutely practices the ultimate Dharma.
By the power of these great vows, All dedications are performed without obstruction;
They enter the inexhaustible treasury of merit, Ever undiminished throughout the past, future, and present.
The Bodhisattva skillfully contemplates all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*) and thoroughly understands that their nature is not independent.
Having realized that the nature of all phenomena is thus, they do not falsely grasp at karma or its retribution.
There is neither form nor the formless, and neither perception nor non-perception.
Both existent phenomena and non-existent phenomena are entirely absent; One thoroughly understands that all things are unattainable.
All phenomena arise through causes and conditions; Their essential nature is neither existent nor non-existent.
Regarding these causes, conditions, and that which arises from them, Ultimately, there is no grasping or attachment therein.
In the realm of the speech of all sentient beings, there is ultimately nothing to be found;

one realizes that names and forms are all mere conceptual constructions. Clearly understanding that all phenomena are entirely without self, and that the nature of sentient beings is fundamentally quiescent—thus one understands all dharmas.
Encompassing all that is included within the three periods of time without exception, may lands and all karmic actions be equal;
dedicating with such wisdom, may merit arise according to one’s realization,
and these signs of merit likewise accord with that realization— how could there be anything further to be attained therein?
Thus, with a mind of dedication free from defilement, one never attempts to measure the nature of all phenomena,
for one realizes that their very nature is non-nature; neither abiding in the world nor departing from it,
one dedicates all the various wholesome deeds performed to all living beings.
There is nothing whose true nature they do not fully realize; all conceptual discriminations are dispelled.
All false views whatsoever are completely abandoned without remainder;
forever free from the fever of affliction and ever-cool, they abide on the unimpeded ground of liberation.
The Bodhisattva does not destroy any phenomena, nor does he annihilate the nature of dharmas;

he understands all phenomena to be like echoes. He is entirely unattached to anything, and knows that all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time arise solely from the conjunction of causes and conditions.
They also know the inclinations and habitual tendencies of the mind; they have never destroyed or ruined any phenomena.

They thoroughly understand that the nature of karma is not karma itself, yet they do not contradict the characteristics of all phenomena, nor do they subvert the retribution of karmic results. Thus they teach that the nature of all phenomena arises from conditions.
[Verse]: Knowing that sentient beings have no birth, And that there are no sentient beings who transmigrate, There are no real sentient beings to be spoken of;
They are merely provisionally designated according to worldly convention. [Treatise]:
The fifty verses above consist of two lines per verse, as they appear in the text; they are explained exactly as stated.
Regarding the second stage of practice, the explanation of the meaning according to the text: what is meant by "the dedication of inexhaustible treasuries of merit"?
This stage clarifies that meditative concentration (*dhyāna*) and wisdom (*prajñā*) are in profound union, and wisdom and compassion (*karuṇā*) meet.

Taking the inexhaustible void as a single site of practice (*maṇḍala*), one takes the manifestations of the ignorance and conduct of inexhaustible sentient beings as the Buddha-work. One constantly serves [the Buddhas] with the body...
Exhausting all Buddhas to pervade the entire Dharma-realm, transforming inexhaustible sentient beings so that they all collectively attain the Buddha-body;

with internal and external forms mutually vanishing and beginning and end utterly exhausted; universally knowing all dharmas without destroying the mindless state—it is therefore called the Treasury of Inexhaustible Merit.
The sixth is the dedication that accords with all firm roots of goodness. This clarifies that its essence is the *prajñāpāramitā*.

It is represented by the spiritual friend Sudhana, who dwells in the city of Supratiṣṭhita and constantly makes offerings to the *caitya* of the Buddha seated upon a sandalwood throne; his name, *Vaiśravaṇa*, means "encompassing" (*saṃgraha*).

"Containing Buddha-fields within his body" is a name based on his dwelling in the Land of Good Deliverance (*Sukhāvatī*); this is named according to his transformative conduct, for he presides over wisdom and skillfully delivers sentient beings.

"Making offerings to the *candana* throne stūpa" clarifies that the essence of the throne is the Dharma-body of precepts, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation. "Attaining the state of Buddhahood without entering final nirvāṇa" clarifies...
The essence of precepts, concentration, and wisdom is without extinction or disappearance, as explained extensively in the sutras.

That the seat does not take on a fixed form illustrates the principle of signlessness (*animitta*), for this is the meaning of Buddhahood. Seeing the seat is thus entry into the Dharma. Therefore, the city is named "Good Crossing" (*Sudhāra*).
When the body merges with emptiness, it is called the Buddha-land; it is also termed "Encompassing," because it clarifies that signless wisdom is such.
The Dharma-gate of the Buddha’s Non-extinction is so called because wisdom is without arising or ceasing.
Regarding the long-form structural analysis (*dīrgha-vibhāga*) of the meaning of this scripture, this section is divided into sixty-four segments as follows.
Within the prose section of this dedication, there are sixty-one segments; these scriptures collectively clarify the practice of giving, and within each segment, there are three meanings.
First, it clarifies the accomplishment of the mind that practices giving; second, it clarifies the dedication of the gift toward Bodhi;
third, it clarifies the formulation of ten kinds of vows for each, all vowing for both self and others to attain Buddhahood.
The following three sections summarize the merit of the gifts bestowed and present the verses spoken by the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja upon observing the assembly.
First, they practice giving by relinquishing their own body, flesh, hands, feet, kingdom, cities, wives, and children.
[Sūtra] "O Son of the Buddha, what is the dedication of all roots of goodness that accords with firmness for a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva?
O Son of the Buddha, this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva may become a sovereign emperor ruling over a great nation, his majestic virtue far-reaching.
His fame shook the world, and among all his enemies, there were none who did not submit. His proclamations and commands were entirely in accordance with the True Dharma (*saddharma*).
Holding a single parasol, he provided universal shade over the ten thousand regions; as he traveled throughout the realm, there was no obstruction wherever he turned.

With a *vimala* silk cloth bound upon his crown, he attained mastery over the Dharma; all who saw him bowed in submission. Without resorting to execution or punishment, they were moved by his virtue and followed him.
Transforming through the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), he gathers all sentient beings as a universal monarch (*cakravartin*) who provides for all;
this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells in such sovereign merit, possessing a great retinue that cannot be broken,
free from all faults, never tiring for those who behold him, adorned with the marks and signs of merit, and with limbs and body parts perfectly proportioned.
They shall be endowed with a body as firm as that of Nārāyaṇa, achieve great strength that cannot be overcome,
and attain pure karma free from all karmic obstructions. They shall be fully accomplished in the practice of all forms of giving—
whether giving food and drink or various superior flavors, or giving vehicles, or giving clothing, or giving flower garlands, mixed incenses, ointments, seats, and couches.
He joyfully gave away dwellings and residences, exquisite lamps and candles, medicinal decoctions for the sick, precious vessels, and precious chariots;

he gave well-trained elephants and horses, all magnificently adorned. Furthermore, to those who came to beg, he gave the throne upon which the king sat, as well as canopies, umbrellas, banners, flags, precious objects, various ornaments, the jeweled crown upon his head, and the bright pearl from his topknot, and so forth.

He has no attachment whatsoever to his royal throne; if he sees sentient beings within prisons, he relinquishes all wealth, treasures, wife, children, and kinsmen, even his own body, to rescue them and bring them liberation.
If he sees a prisoner about to be executed, he immediately offers his own body to take their life in its place.
Or, if he sees someone come to beg for his skin, head, or topknot, he joyfully bestows them as well, without any regret.
With a heart of joy, he gave away everything he cherished— his eyes, ears, nose, tongue, teeth, head, crown, hands, feet, flesh, blood, marrow, bones, heart, kidneys,
liver, lungs, large intestine, small intestine, thick skin, thin skin, all the fingers of his hands and feet along with their flesh, and his nails—
and even cast himself down into deep and vast [waters] when requested for the sake of the unprecedented Dharma.
Whether entering a pit of fire to protect and uphold the True Dharma of the Tathāgata by enduring all manner of suffering and poison,
or seeking the Dharma even for the sake of a single word and being able to relinquish everything within the four seas,

he constantly transforms and guides all sentient beings through the True Dharma, causing them to cultivate wholesome deeds and abandon all evils; should he see sentient beings being harmed or ruined...
With a mind of loving-kindness toward others, he rescues them and causes them to abandon their sinful karma.

If he sees the Tathāgata achieve supreme perfect enlightenment, he extols and praises him so that all may hear and know. Or he gives land to construct monasteries, lodgings, and halls as dwelling places;
or he gives servants to perform service and labor; or he gives his own body to those who come to beg; or he gives...
For the sake of seeking the Dharma from the Buddha, they leaped for joy; for the sake of sentient beings, they served and made offerings to him.
Whether it was relinquishing their royal thrones, cities, towns, villages, palaces, gardens, wives, children, or retinues, they fulfilled every request made to them.
Or, they relinquished all their necessities of life and universally established great, unrestricted assemblies of giving (*pūjā-mahā-dāna*). Within these, [they gave everything].
Sentient beings are various fields of merit; they may come from afar or from near, they may be wise or foolish, handsome or ugly, male or female, human or non-human.
Their mental activities differ and their aspirations vary, yet the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives to all of them equally, causing them all to be fully satisfied.
O Son of the Buddha, when the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva practices such giving, he generates wholesome gathering.
They dedicate their minds entirely as follows: they skillfully gather and conform to all roots of goodness through form, which is firm;

they skillfully gather and conform to all roots of goodness through perception, volition, and consciousness, which are firm; they skillfully gather and conform to all roots of goodness through royal sovereignty, which is firm;
they skillfully gather and conform to all roots of goodness through retinues, which are firm; and they skillfully gather [all roots of goodness] through requisites.
In accordance with the need for firmness, they skillfully gather and bestow all roots of goodness, thereby conforming to the firmness of all roots of goodness.
[Treatise] Second, the giving of food.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, whatever objects a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives are immeasurable and boundless; by means of those roots of goodness...
Such is the dedication: when giving sublime food to sentient beings, one’s mind is pure;

regarding the gift, one is without greed, without attachment, and without any sense of regret or stinginess. One practices giving fully and vows that all sentient beings may obtain the food of wisdom, their minds free from hindrance, understanding the nature of food so as to have no craving or attachment, but finding joy only in the delight of the Dharma.
Dwelling apart from [craving], their wisdom is filled and they remain steadfast in the Dharma;

they gather roots of goodness, and with pure bodies of Dharma and wisdom, they travel about out of compassion for sentient beings, acting as a field of merit while manifesting the acceptance of solid food.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give food.
[Treatise] Third is the gift of drink.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives the gift of drink, he dedicates these roots of goodness in this way, namely:
"May all sentient beings drink the water of the flavor of the Dharma, diligently practice and cultivate it, fulfill the Bodhisattva path, and sever..."

The world is parched with craving and constantly seeks the Buddha’s wisdom; having left the realm of desire, one attains the joy and bliss of the Dharma, and from these pure dharmas, one’s body is born.
Always using samādhi to discipline and gather the mind, one enters the ocean of wisdom, raises great clouds of the Dharma, and pours down the great rain of the Dharma.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives drink.
[Treatise] The fourth is the gift of flavors.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give various kinds of pure, superior flavors— namely, sour, bitter, salty, bland, sweet, and pungent—
and all such diverse tastes that are moistening and complete, they are able to bring peace and stability to the four great elements.
The physical body is harmonious and full, with vigor and strength; the mind is pure and constantly experiences joy. When swallowing and chewing, there is no coughing or obstruction;
the sense faculties are clear and sharp, and the internal organs are filled and robust. Poisons cannot invade, and diseases cannot harm.
From beginning to end, there is no affliction, and one attains eternal peace and happiness. By means of these roots of goodness, one dedicates them as follows:
May all sentient beings obtain the supreme flavor of ambrosia and be filled with it;
may all sentient beings obtain the flavor of Dharma-wisdom and fully understand the functions of all flavors;

may all sentient beings obtain the immeasurable flavor of Dharma and, having thoroughly realized the Dharma-realm, dwell securely within the great city of the ultimate reality; may all sentient beings become the Great Dharma.
May clouds pervading the entire Dharma-realm rain down the rain of Dharma everywhere to teach and transform all sentient beings.
May all sentient beings obtain the flavor of supreme wisdom and be filled with unsurpassed Dharma-joy throughout their bodies and minds.
May all sentient beings attain freedom from greed for all superior flavors, remain unstained by any worldly tastes, and constantly and diligently cultivate the One Vehicle.
May all sentient beings obtain the flavor of the single Dharma of all Buddha-dharmas and realize that all Buddha-dharmas are entirely without distinction.
May all sentient beings obtain the most supreme flavor and, mounting the vehicle of omniscience, never again regress.
May all sentient beings attain entry into the non-differentiated flavor of the Buddhas' Dharma and be able to discern all faculties. May they...
The Dharma-flavor of all sentient beings increases and they are constantly satisfied with the unimpeded Buddha-dharma;

this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives the flavor of food, in order to cause all sentient beings to diligently cultivate merit and virtue so that they may all be fully endowed with an unimpeded body of wisdom.
[Treatise] Fifth, the gift of vehicles.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives vehicles, he dedicates his roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, may all sentient beings fully attain the vehicle of omniscience and ride upon the Great Vehicle.
The destructible vehicle, the most excellent vehicle, the supreme vehicle, the swift vehicle, the vehicle of great power,

the vehicle endowed with merit, the supramundane vehicle, and the vehicle that gives birth to the infinite bodhisattvas— this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives vehicles.
[Treatise] The sixth is the gift of clothing.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives clothing, he dedicates his roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, may all sentient beings obtain the clothing of shame and modesty to cover their bodies, thereby abandoning the nakedness of false paths.
With an excellent form, a radiant complexion, and delicate, soft skin, they achieve the foremost bliss of all Buddhas and attain the most pure knowledge of all modes;
this is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give clothing.
[Treatise] The seventh is the gift of flowers.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva constantly practices the giving of various kinds of named flowers—
namely, exquisite fragrant flowers, flowers of various colors, immeasurable and wondrous flowers, *sudarśana* flowers, and delightful flowers— all of them.
At that time, with flowers as rare and cherished by gods, humans, and the world, with flowers of exquisite fragrance and pleasing appearance—
using such immeasurable and wondrous flowers— he made offerings to all Buddhas currently present, as well as to all stūpas and shrines after the Buddhas had passed into extinction;
he offered them to those who preach the Dharma, or to the Sangha of Bhikṣus, and to all Bodhisattvas.
When giving to all spiritual friends, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, parents, kinsmen, down to one's own self and all others who are poor,
destitute, and without shelter, one dedicates the roots of goodness in this way: that is to say,
may all sentient beings attain the flowers of the samādhis of all Buddhas, and may they be able to cause all dharmas to fully blossom.
May all sentient beings attain a joyful heart, like those who behold the Buddha, never wearying of it;
may all sentient beings find everything they see to be harmonious and pleasing, their minds free from agitation or confusion; may all sentient beings fully practice vast and pure deeds;
may all sentient beings constantly mind their virtuous friends, their hearts never wavering. May all sentient beings...
May all sentient beings be born like the agada medicine, capable of eliminating the manifold poisons of all afflictions;
may all sentient beings fulfill their great vows and all become kings of supreme wisdom;
may the sun of wisdom of all sentient beings shatter the darkness of ignorance; may the pure moon of bodhi of all sentient beings increase and reach fulfillment; may all...
When sentient beings enter the great jewel island and see spiritual friends who are fully endowed with all roots of goodness,
this is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give flowers, performed so that all sentient beings may attain pure and unobstructed wisdom.
[Treatise] The eighth is the gift of garlands.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives a garland as a gift, they dedicate the roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, may all sentient beings be pleasing for others to behold; may those who see them admire them; and may those who see them regard them with affection.

Those who behold it with love and joy, those who gaze upon it with thirsty longing, those whose sorrows are dispelled by seeing it, those who give rise to gladness upon seeing it, those who abandon evil through seeing it,
those who always attain proximity to the Buddha through seeing it, and those who become pure and obtain all-knowledge—
this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives away flower garlands.
[Treatise] Ninth: The Gift of Fragrance.
[Sūtra] When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, O Son of the Buddha, gives the gift of fragrance, he dedicates his roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the fragrance of ethical discipline; may they attain ethical discipline that is unimpaired, unmixed, and untainted."
The precept of repentance, the precept of detachment from entanglements, the precept of freedom from feverish affliction, the precept of non-transgression,
the boundless precept, the supramundane precept, and the bodhisattva pāramitā precept— may all sentient beings, by virtue of these precepts, fully accomplish the precept-body of all Buddhas.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives incense, in order to cause all sentient beings to...
Because they have attained the perfect and unimpeded aggregate of ethical discipline (*śīlaskandha*).
[Treatise] Tenth: The Gift of Perfumes.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives perfumes, he dedicates his roots of goodness in this manner:
That is to say: may all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the fragrance of giving, so that they are able to relinquish all that they possess;
may all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the fragrance of precepts, so that they attain the ultimate pure precepts of the Tathāgata;

may all sentient beings be universally perfumed by the fragrance of patience, so that they are free from all treacherous and harmful intentions; may all sentient beings [be universally perfumed by the fragrance of] diligence...
May the fragrance universally permeate them as they constantly don the armor of diligence for the Mahāyāna;

may all sentient beings be universally permeated by the fragrance of meditative concentration, dwelling securely in the samādhi of the presence of all Buddhas; may all sentient beings be universally permeated by the fragrance of wisdom, attaining the unexcelled King of Knowledge in a single thought-moment;
may all sentient beings be universally permeated by the fragrance of the Dharma, attaining non-attachment toward the unexcelled Dharma.
I vow that the fragrance of the virtues of all sentient beings shall universally permeate, so that they may accomplish all great merits and wisdom;
I vow that the fragrance of the bodhi of all sentient beings shall universally permeate, so that they may attain the ten powers of a Buddha and reach the other shore;
I vow that the wondrous fragrance of the pure white dharmas of all sentient beings shall universally permeate, so that all unwholesome dharmas may be forever extinguished. This is...
When a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives powdered incense, they dedicate their roots of goodness.
[Treatise] Eleventh: Giving Beds and Seats.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives beds and seats, they dedicate their various roots of goodness in this manner.
That is to say: may all sentient beings obtain the couches and seats of the devas and realize great wisdom;
may all sentient beings obtain the couches and seats of the noble ones, abandon the mind of ordinary worldlings, and abide in the bodhicitta;

may all sentient beings obtain the couches and seats of peace and happiness, forever leaving behind all the sufferings and afflictions of birth and death; may all sentient beings attain ultimate [enlightenment].
May all sentient beings obtain seats upon which they may behold the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings obtain seats of equanimity, constantly and universally cultivating all wholesome dharmas;
may all sentient beings obtain the most excellent seats, possessing pure karma peerless in the world; may all sentient beings obtain seats of peace and security, realizing the true Dharma.
To fulfill the ultimate aspiration that all sentient beings obtain pure seats and cultivate the realm of the Tathāgata’s pure wisdom;
to aspire that all sentient beings obtain seats of secure abiding and be constantly followed, protected, and sheltered by virtuous friends;
and to aspire that all sentient beings obtain lion-thrones and always lie on their right sides as the Tathāgata does—this is [the practice].
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give beds and seats, they dedicate their roots of goodness so that sentient beings may cultivate right mindfulness and properly guard their sense faculties.
[Treatise] Twelfth: Giving Lodgings.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives dwellings, he dedicates his roots of goodness in this way: that is to say,
may all sentient beings attain secure residence in pure Buddha-fields, diligently cultivate all meritorious qualities,
abide in the sphere of profound samādhi, and be completely free from attachment to any place of dwelling.
All dwelling places are non-existent; they dwell apart from all worldly realms, having embraced the abode of omniscience and the abodes where all Buddhas reside.
They dwell in the ultimate path, the abode of peace and bliss, constantly abiding in the foremost pure roots of goodness, never forsaking the unsurpassed abode of the Buddhas.
This is the excellence of a bodhisattva mahāsattva when giving houses and dwellings.
The dedication of the faculties is for the purpose of benefiting all sentient beings by contemplating their protection according to their respective needs.
[Treatise] Thirteenth: The Abiding in Giving of Dwelling Places.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives dwellings, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, they vow that all sentient beings shall always obtain wholesome benefit and that their minds be peaceful and happy;

they vow that all sentient beings shall abide by means of the Tathāgata, abide by means of great wisdom, abide by means of spiritual friends, abide by means of the most honored and supreme, and abide by means of virtuous conduct.
Abiding in great loving-kindness, abiding in great compassion, abiding in the six perfections,
abiding in the great bodhicitta, and abiding in the path of all bodhisattvas— this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives a dwelling place,
for the sake of purifying all merit, for ultimate purity, and for the purification of wisdom.
Therefore, because the Path is pure, the Dharma is pure, the precepts are pure, the aspiration and delight are pure,
the faith and understanding are pure, the vows are pure, and all supernatural powers and merits are pure.
[Treatise] Fourteen: The Offering of Lamps.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva offers various lamps, namely:
ghee lamps, oil lamps, jewel lamps, maṇi lamps, lacquer lamps, fire lamps, aloeswood lamps, sandalwood lamps, and all manner of incense lamps in immeasurable colors.
When offering lamps such as these—immeasurable lamps—in order to benefit all sentient beings and to gather in all sentient beings, one dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, may all sentient beings attain immeasurable light that universally illumines the true Dharma of all Buddhas; may all sentient beings attain purity...
May all sentient beings obtain the light of purity that illuminates even the most subtle forms in the world;

may they be freed from cataracts and realize that the realm of sentient beings is empty and devoid of inherent existence; may all sentient beings obtain a body of boundless light that emits wondrous radiance universally illuminating all;
and may all sentient beings obtain the light of universal illumination, so that their minds never regress from the teachings of all Buddhas.
I vow that all sentient beings may attain the pure light of the Buddhas, appearing clearly within all lands;
may every single sentient being attain unimpeded light, with each ray of light universally illuminating the entire Dharma-realm;
may all sentient beings attain uninterrupted light, shining upon the lands of all Buddhas so that their radiance never ceases; may all sentient beings attain the Banner of Wisdom.
"May light universally illuminate the world; may all sentient beings attain immeasurable colored lights that illuminate all lands, manifesting spiritual powers.
When a bodhisattva thus offers lamps, it is for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings and bringing peace and happiness to all sentient beings;
by means of these roots of goodness, they follow after sentient beings and embrace them with these roots of goodness.
By means of these roots of goodness, they distribute [them] among sentient beings; by means of these roots of goodness, they feel compassion for sentient beings;

by means of these roots of goodness, they nurture and protect sentient beings; by means of these roots of goodness, they rescue and guard sentient beings; by means of these roots of goodness, they fulfill sentient beings;
by means of these roots of goodness, they attend to sentient beings with mindfulness; by means of these roots of goodness, they benefit sentient beings equally.
To observe sentient beings with roots of goodness is for a bodhisattva mahāsattva, when giving lamps,
to dedicate those roots of goodness in such a way that there is no obstruction, universally causing all sentient beings to abide within roots of goodness.
[Treatise] Fifteenth: The Gift of Medicinal Decoctions.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives medicinal decoctions, he dedicates his roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, he makes the vow that all sentient beings may ultimately emerge from all hindrances and entanglements; he vows that all sentient beings...
May they forever leave behind the body of illness and attain the body of a Tathāgata; may all sentient beings become great efficacious medicines to eliminate all diseases of unwholesome karma;
may all sentient beings become agada medicines and abide in the stage of non-retrogression of Bodhisattvas;
may all sentient beings become the medicine of the Tathāgata, capable of extracting the poisoned arrows of all afflictions.
May all sentient beings draw near to the noble and holy ones, extinguish all afflictions, and cultivate pure conduct.
May all sentient beings become great kings of medicine who forever eliminate all illnesses so that they do not recur.
May all sentient beings become indestructible trees of medicine, capable of healing and saving all sentient beings. May all sentient beings attain everything...

Jñānaprabha, may you extract the arrows of all diseases from the assembly; may all sentient beings skillfully understand the methods of worldly medicine so that all their illnesses may be healed for them.

When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas bestow medicinal decoctions, it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to forever leave behind all diseases, for the sake of ultimate peace and security, and for the sake of ultimate purity, just as with the Buddha.
Because they have eradicated all arrows of illness, they attain an inexhaustible and solid body;
because they have attained a body indestructible by the Vajra-perimeter mountains, they attain firm and perfect strength;
because they have attained the perfect and irremovable bliss of a Buddha, they attain the firm body of mastery of all Buddhas—thus do they dedicate their roots of goodness.
[Treatise] The sixteenth is the gift of utensils.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is able to bestow all kinds of utensils, namely:
golden vessels filled with various jewels; silver vessels filled with many wonderful gems; lapis lazuli vessels filled with diverse treasures; and...
Pearl vessels were filled with immeasurable ornaments of precious jewels; mother-of-pearl vessels were filled with red pearls; agate vessels were filled with coral and mani-jewels;
white jade vessels were filled with various kinds of fine food; sandalwood vessels were filled with celestial garments;
diamond vessels were filled with various exquisite fragrances; and countless, innumerable vessels made of various jewels were filled with immeasurable [substances].
They give various kinds of countless jewels to the Buddhas because they believe in the inconceivable field of merit of the Buddhas;
they give to the Bodhisattvas because they know that spiritual friends are difficult to encounter; they give to the noble Saṃgha so that the Buddha-dharma may long abide in the world;
they give to the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas so as to generate pure faith toward all the Noble Ones; or they give...
Because they respect their parents; because they give to teachers and elders so as to constantly encourage and instruct them to cultivate merit in accordance with the holy teachings;
because they look upon all sentient beings with eyes of great loving-kindness and great compassion, viewing even the lowly, the poor, and the destitute;
and because they single-mindedly fulfill the *dāna-pāramitā* of all bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present.
Because they universally bestow all things upon all beings and never grow weary of relinquishing them for the sake of all sentient beings,
when practicing such giving, they are entirely without attachment to either the objects given or the recipients.
When Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas give by filling various precious vessels with immeasurable treasures, they dedicate these roots of goodness in this manner.

That is to say: may all sentient beings become equal to space, possessing boundless treasuries and vast power of mindfulness, able to receive and uphold all mundane and supramundane scriptures without ever forgetting them;
may all sentient beings become pure vessels, able to awaken to the profound, true Dharma of all Buddhas; may all sentient beings become unsurpassed...
May all beings be able to receive and uphold the Buddha-dharma of the three periods of time; may they accomplish the vast Dharma-vessels of the Tathāgatas.
Through indestructible faith, may they embrace the Bodhi-dharma of the Buddhas of the three periods of time;
may all beings accomplish the most supreme jewel-adorned vessel and abide in the Bodhicitta of great majestic power. May all beings...

May all sentient beings become vessels that serve as the basis for accomplishing the merit of birth; may they give rise to pure faith and understanding toward the immeasurable wisdom of all Tathāgatas;
may they vow to accomplish the vessel for entering into all-knowledge; may they vow to ultimately attain the unimpeded liberation of the Tathāgatas;
and may they cause all sentient beings to obtain the vessel of bodhisattva practice throughout all future kalpas.
May all universally abide in the power of the knowledge of all modes; may all sentient beings achieve the supreme vessel of merit for the lineage of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
may they be able to receive and uphold all that is spoken by the wondrous voices of all Buddhas;
and may all sentient beings achieve the capacity to contain all Tathāgatas of all worlds throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space.
The vessel for the assembly and the site of enlightenment is the foremost for praising and teaching the Great Beings,
and it is the exhortation to all Buddhas to turn the wheel of the True Dharma; this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives a vessel,
done so that all sentient beings may universally attain the vessel of the complete vows and practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
[Treatise] Seventeenth: The Gift of Various Kinds of Jeweled Ornamented Chariots.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva offers various chariots adorned with many jewels as gifts to the Buddhas, the Bodhisattvas, teachers, virtuous friends, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas—thus to immeasurable and diverse fields of merit.
Even those who are impoverished and destitute— this multitude of people, some coming from afar and some from nearby,
some having come because they heard the renown of the Bodhisattva’s name, some having come due to their connection with the Bodhisattva,

some having come because they heard of the vows of generosity the Bodhisattva made in the past, and some having come because of the Bodhisattva’s own heart-felt aspirations— at that time, the Bodhisattva...
Some gave jeweled chariots or golden chariots, all exquisitely adorned with nets of bells covering them above and precious ribbons hanging down;
some gave superior lapis lazuli chariots decorated with immeasurable rare treasures;
others gave silver chariots covered with golden nets and drawn by spirited horses; and others gave chariots made of countless varieties of miscellaneous jewels.
He gave away chariots adorned with precious nets and drawn by fragrant elephants, or else he gave away sandalwood chariots with wheels of exquisite jewels and canopies of various gems;

these were furnished with magnificent jeweled lion-thrones upon which hundreds of thousands of court ladies sat in rows, while a hundred thousand men pulled and guided them as they traveled. Or else he gave away chariots made of *vaidūrya* gemstone.
Adorned with various exquisite jewels, it was filled with beautiful women; precious canopies covered it above, while banners and streamers stood by its side.
Furthermore, there were agate chariots decorated with many jewels and perfumed with various incenses, strewn and adorned with diverse wonderful flowers.
Hundreds of thousands of maidens held jeweled necklaces, driving the vehicles with balanced and harmonious control.
When traversing dangerous terrain, he remains at ease; furthermore, he provides a firm and solid fragrant chariot, magnificently adorned with wheels made of various jewels.
A precious canopy covers it from above, and jeweled nets hang down from it, while various precious garments are spread within.

Pure and exquisite incense wafts its fragrance outward until it permeates all; this fragrance is so sublime and pleasing that it delights the hearts of men, as immeasurable devas follow and attend him on his journey.
They are carried upon vehicles made of various jewels, provided with whatever is needed at any time;
or else they are given radiant jewel-chariots, wherein all manner of precious gems reflect one another in brilliant colors, and exquisite nets of various jewels cover them from above.

Garlands of diverse jewels hang down all around, and powdered incense is scattered about, making both the interior and exterior fragrant and pure. Beloved sons and daughters are all seated within these vehicles—such are the Buddha-sons, the Bodhisattvas.
When the Mahāsattva offered such various and wondrous jeweled chariots to the Buddha, he dedicated these roots of goodness as follows:
"May all sentient beings fully understand how to make offerings to the supreme field of merit;

may they develop deep faith in making offerings to the Buddha and obtain immeasurable rewards. May all sentient beings turn their minds single-mindedly toward the Buddha and constantly encounter immeasurable purity."
May all sentient beings, regarding the pure field of merit, be without stinginess toward the Tathāgatas and fully accomplish the mind of great relinquishment (*mahātyāga*).

May all sentient beings, while practicing acts of giving before the Buddhas, remain free from the aspirations of the two vehicles (*dviyāna*) and attain the unimpeded liberation and the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*) of the Tathāgata. May all sentient beings, regarding all...
May all sentient beings enter the Buddha’s inexhaustible giving and attain the Buddha’s immeasurable merit, wisdom, and vows;
may they enter the Buddha’s supreme wisdom and achieve the pure, unsurpassed King of Wisdom.

May all sentient beings attain the Buddha’s omnipresent and unimpeded supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), so that wherever they wish to go, they are never without mastery. May all sentient beings deeply enter the Great...

May all sentient beings, mounting the vehicle of immeasurable wisdom and abiding in unwavering vows, be able to give birth to the dharmas of omniscience and become the supreme field of merit for all devas and humans.

May all sentient beings harbor no feelings of resentment toward the Buddhas, diligently plant roots of goodness, and joyfully seek the wisdom of the Buddha. May all sentient beings be able to proceed spontaneously and effortlessly.
May all Buddha-fields, within a single kṣaṇa, universally pervade the entire Dharma-realm without weariness;
may all sentient beings attain the sovereign supernormal powers of Bodhisattvas, manifesting bodies that fill the entirety of space, drawing near to and making offerings to all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings obtain incomparable bodies that travel everywhere throughout the ten directions without [exhaustion].
May all sentient beings grow weary of [suffering] and attain vast bodies that travel with swift flight wherever they desire, never tiring or retreating;

may all sentient beings attain the ultimate sovereign power of the Buddhas, manifesting within a single kṣaṇa all the supernatural transformations of the Buddhas throughout the entirety of space; may all sentient beings cultivate peace and happiness.
May they practice in accordance with all bodhisattva paths; may all sentient beings swiftly attain the ultimate ten powers, wisdom, and supernormal knowledges;
may all sentient beings universally enter the dharma-realm, reaching the very limits of the lands of the ten directions without distinction;
and may all sentient beings practice the conduct of Samantabhadra without ever turning back.
Having reached the other shore and attained all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), may all sentient beings ascend the vehicle of incomparable wisdom,
accord with the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), and perceive reality as it truly is.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva offers precious chariots to all Buddhas currently present and to all stupas and temples after their parinirvāṇa.
In order to cause sentient beings to attain the Tathāgata’s ultimate liberation through the unimpeded vehicle, O Son of the Buddha,
when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives various precious chariots to spiritual friends such as other Bodhisattvas, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way: that is to say,
"May all sentient beings always remember and uphold the teachings of spiritual friends, and apply themselves with single-minded diligence."

May they be protected so as not to forget or lose [the Dharma]. May all sentient beings share the same purpose and benefit as spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), universally gathering all together with their roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*).

May all sentient beings draw near to spiritual friends, honoring and making offerings to them, relinquishing everything to accord with their hearts' desires. May all sentient beings attain virtuous aspirations and follow after the good.
May all sentient beings never be separated from their spiritual friends, always encountering them and serving them with single-minded devotion, never disobeying their instructions.
May all sentient beings delight in spiritual friends, never abandoning them, remaining constant and pure in their association without error.
May all sentient beings be able to offer their very bodies as a gift to spiritual friends.
May all sentient beings follow their instructions and commands without any contravention, and may they be embraced by spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).

May all sentient beings cultivate great loving-kindness (*maitrī*) and remain far removed from all evils. May all sentient beings, following spiritual friends, hear the True Dharma (*saddharma*) preached by all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings share the same roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*) as their spiritual friends.
May the fruits of pure karma be shared with all Bodhisattvas in the same practice and vows;
may all sentient beings ultimately attain the ten powers, be able to receive and uphold the teachings of spiritual friends, and reach the state of all samādhis, wisdoms, and supernormal powers.
May all sentient beings be able to receive and uphold all true dharmas, cultivate all practices, and arrive at that [state].
May all sentient beings ride upon the Mahāyāna without obstruction, ultimately accomplishing the path to all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*).
May all sentient beings fully attain rest within the vehicle of all-knowledge, reaching the place of peace and security without ever regressing.
May all sentient beings know the practice of suchness and, according to what they have heard, [realize] all Buddha-dharmas.

May all attain ultimate realization and never again forget or lose it; may all sentient beings be universally embraced by all Buddhas and attain unimpeded wisdom that thoroughly penetrates all phenomena.

May all sentient beings attain non-retrogressive and sovereign supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), reaching wherever they wish to go in a single thought-moment. May all sentient beings attain mastery over coming and going.

"May I act as a guide to transform and lead others, causing them to abide in the Mahāyāna; may the practices of all sentient beings not be in vain, but carry them upon the vehicle of wisdom to the ultimate stage.
May all sentient beings attain the unimpeded vehicle and reach all places through unimpeded wisdom.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva bestows various chariots upon spiritual friends.
In order to cause sentient beings to become fully endowed with merit, equal and no different from that of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,

the sons of the Buddha— the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas— when giving precious chariots as a gift to the Saṅgha, give rise to the mind that learns all forms of giving, the mind of skillful understanding, the mind of pure merit, the mind of compliant relinquishment,
the mind that the Jewel of the Saṅgha is difficult to encounter, the mind of deep faith in the Jewel of the Saṅgha, and the mind of gathering [the Saṅgha].

Maintaining the mind that upholds the true teaching, abiding in superior aspiration and joy, attaining what has never been attained before, and performing great assemblies of giving that give rise to immeasurable and vast merit;
with deep faith in the Buddha’s teachings that cannot be thwarted, they dedicate all roots of goodness in this way:
namely, wishing that all sentient beings may universally enter the Buddha-dharma and remember it without forgetting; wishing that all sentient beings...

May all sentient beings leave behind the dharmas of the foolish and ordinary and enter the station of the noble ones; may they swiftly enter the ranks of the sages and be able to guide and inspire others through the successive stages of the Buddha-dharma.
May all sentient beings be honored and revered by the world, their words always trusted and relied upon.
May all sentient beings skillfully enter the equality of all dharmas and fully realize that the self-nature of the dharma-realm is non-dual.
May all sentient beings be born from the realm of the Tathāgata’s wisdom and be surrounded by those who are well-disciplined;
may all sentient beings abide in the dharma free from defilement and eliminate all the dust and grime of afflictions;
may all sentient beings fully accomplish the unsurpassed Saṅgha Jewel, leave the stage of ordinary beings, and enter the assembly of the noble ones. May it be so!
May all sentient beings diligently cultivate wholesome dharmas and attain unimpeded wisdom, endowed with noble merit;
may all sentient beings attain the mind of wisdom, remaining unattached to the three periods of time and possessing sovereign mastery among all beings like a king;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of wisdom and turn the wheel of the true Dharma; may all sentient beings be fully endowed with supernormal powers in a single thought-moment.
May they be able to travel to unspeakably unspeakable worlds; may all sentient beings ride upon bodies of empty space, possessing unimpeded wisdom regarding all worlds;

may all sentient beings universally enter all dharma-realms of empty space within the assemblies of all Buddhas, accomplishing the supreme practice of the *pāramitās*; and may all sentient beings attain the power of levitation.
May all sentient beings attain the supreme wisdom of the body that is able to enter all Buddha-fields;
may all sentient beings obtain boundless and skillful supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*), universally manifesting their bodies in all fields;
may all sentient beings obtain a body that is entirely non-reliant, universally appearing like a reflection through the power of spiritual penetrations (*abhijñā*); may all sentient beings...
May they attain inconceivable sovereign spiritual powers to appear before those who can be transformed according to their needs, thereby teaching and subduing them;
may all sentient beings enter the Dharma-realm through unimpeded skillful means and, in a single thought-moment, travel throughout the lands of the ten directions—
this is the dedication of roots of goodness from the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s gift of a precious chariot to the Saṅgha, for the sake of sentient beings.
Because the Universal Vehicle of Pure, Unsurpassed Wisdom turns the wheel of unimpeded Dharma-wisdom throughout all worlds,
O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives precious chariots as a gift to Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas,
they give rise to such thoughts: namely, the mind of a field of merit, the mind of reverence, and the mind of an ocean of merit capable of producing [virtue].
A mind of virtue and wisdom born from the power of the Tathāgata’s merits; a mind cultivated for hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of kalpas;
a mind capable of practicing the bodhisattva path for unspeakable kalpas; a mind liberated from all fetters of Māra;
a mind that crushes and destroys all hosts of Māra’s armies; and a mind whose light of wisdom clearly illuminates the unsurpassed Dharma. By means of this...
One dedicates all the roots of goodness from this gift of a vehicle in this way:
that is to say, may all sentient beings become the foremost field of merit trusted by the world, and be fully endowed with the unsurpassed *dānapāramitā*;
may all sentient beings be free from useless speech, always delight in dwelling alone, and have no dualistic thoughts in their minds; and may all sentient beings become the most supreme.
May the pure field of merit gather all sentient beings and cause them to cultivate meritorious deeds;
may all sentient beings become deep pools of wisdom, able to bestow upon sentient beings immeasurable and innumerable fruits of the roots of goodness.
May all sentient beings abide in unimpeded conduct and fulfill the foremost pure field of merit. May all sentient beings abide in the dharma of non-contention and attain realization.
May all phenomena be without activity, having non-substantiality as their nature;
may all sentient beings always be able to draw near to the supreme field of merit and fully cultivate and perfect immeasurable virtue.
May all sentient beings be able to manifest immeasurable sovereign supernormal powers, gathering all conscious beings through the pure field of merit. May all sentient beings be fully endowed with...
May all sentient beings become true fields of merit capable of producing the fruit, and may they achieve the inexhaustible accumulation of merit for omniscience;
may all sentient beings attain the dharma for extinguishing transgressions and be able to receive and uphold the meanings and phrases of the Buddha-dharma never heard before.
May all sentient beings always diligently listen to and receive all Buddha-dharmas, hearing them and fully understanding them without letting any go to waste;
may all sentient beings, upon hearing the Buddha-dharmas, attain ultimate penetration and expound them in accordance with what they have heard;
may all sentient beings, within the teachings of the Tathāgata, believe, understand, and practice them, abandoning all nine [afflictions].
May all sentient beings always see the worthy and noble ones and increase all their most supreme roots of goodness;
may all sentient beings’ minds always have faith and delight in those who practice wisdom, dwelling together with and rejoicing alongside the various sages and philosophers;
may all sentient beings hear the names of the Buddhas so that none is in vain, according to their [capacities].

May all that is heard be seen with one's own eyes; may all sentient beings skillfully discern and know the true teachings of all Buddhas, and may those who uphold the Buddha-dharma be able to protect them in their entirety.
May all sentient beings always delight in hearing all Buddha-dharmas, receiving, upholding, reading, reciting, revealing, and illuminating them.
May all sentient beings have faith and understanding in the true efficacy of the Buddha’s teachings.
Virtuously relinquishing all that one possesses to respectfully honor and make offerings to them—

this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives various chariots to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas. It is for the purpose of causing all sentient beings to fully achieve pure,
supreme wisdom and supernormal powers, to practice with diligence free from indolence, and to obtain the power of all-knowledge and fearlessness.

Therefore, when a son of the Buddha, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, gives various precious chariots as gifts to fields of merit, including the poor, the destitute, and the solitary, he relinquishes everything requested according to their needs.
With a heart full of joy and free from weariness, he further addresses those people, saying: "I should have gone to you myself to provide offerings and support; I ought not to trouble you."
Having traveled from afar and being weary and exhausted, he spoke and then prostrated himself, inquiring after his health and well-being.

Whatever was required was granted to him in its entirety; at times he was given a *maṇi* jewel chariot filled with the foremost woman-treasure (*strī-ratna*) of Jambudvīpa, or again he was given a gold-adorned chariot filled with a human woman-treasure, or again he was given...
He gave exquisite lapis lazuli chariots filled with palace maidens; or he gave various kinds of wondrous jeweled chariots filled with young girls like celestial nymphs;
or he gave countless chariots adorned with jewels, filled with precious women who were gentle, bright, eloquent, and wise;
or he gave excellent sandalwood chariots for riding; or again, he gave crystal chariots.
They were all filled with precious women whose countenances were upright and whose physical features were peerless;
adorned in magnificent garments, those who saw them were filled with joy. Furthermore, he bestowed agate chariots upon the consecrated crown princes, who sat within them;
at other times, he bestowed chariots of solid fragrance, with all the men and women seated therein; or he bestowed everything.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, the sons of the Buddha, place their cherished and beloved kin and retinues upon jewel-adorned chariots;
with such immeasurable jeweled chariots as these, they respectfully bestow them according to the requests of others, causing all to fulfill their wishes and be joyfully satisfied.
They dedicate these roots of goodness in this way, namely: "May all sentient beings ride upon the..."
May all sentient beings mount the vast vehicle of the irreversible wheel of non-obstruction and proceed beneath the inconceivable Bodhi tree;
may they, by means of the great dharma-vehicle of pure causes, cultivate the bodhisattva practices throughout all future kalpas, never to regress.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of the non-existence of all phenomena and forever be free from [dualistic grasping].
May all beings constantly cultivate the path of omniscience by severing all conceptual discrimination and attachment;
may all beings ride the vehicle of straightforwardness, free from flattery and deceit, traveling to the buddha-fields with sovereign unimpededness;
and may all beings, in accordance with the vehicle of omniscience, dwell in peace and find mutual delight through the teachings of all Buddhas. May all sentient beings...
May they all mount the vehicle of the bodhisattva’s pure conduct, fully possessing the ten paths of renunciation of a bodhisattva and the bliss of samādhi;
and may they cause all sentient beings to mount the four-wheeled vehicle— namely, dwelling in a favorable land, relying upon virtuous persons,
accumulating supreme merit, and making great vows— thereby fulfilling all the pure brahmacarya of a bodhisattva.
May all sentient beings attain the vehicle of the light that universally illumines the ten directions and cultivate the power of the wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
May all sentient beings ride upon the vehicle of the Buddha-dharma and reach the ultimate further shore of all phenomena.
May all sentient beings be borne by the inconceivable vehicle of manifold blessings, virtues, and dharmas, universally demonstrating the secure and correct path throughout the ten directions.
May all sentient beings mount the vehicle of great giving and abandon the defilement of stinginess;

may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of pure precepts and uphold pure precepts as boundless as the dharma-realm; may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of patience and always remain free from the turbid mind of anger toward sentient beings;
may all sentient beings mount the vehicle of great vigor, the vehicle of non-retrogression, and be firm.

May all sentient beings, practicing supreme conduct on the path leading to enlightenment, ride the vehicle of meditative concentration and swiftly reach the site of awakening to realize the wisdom of bodhi.

May all sentient beings ride the vehicle of wisdom and skillful means, manifesting transformation bodies that fill the entire dharma-realm and the spheres of all Buddhas. May all sentient beings ride the vehicle of the Dharma King and achieve perfection.
May they fearlessly and constantly bestow the Dharma of omniscience upon all;
may all sentient beings ride the vehicle of unattached wisdom and be able to enter everywhere throughout the ten directions, remaining unmoved within the true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*).
May all sentient beings ride the Buddha-vehicle of all Buddhas, manifesting births throughout the lands of the ten directions.

Without losing or destroying the path of the Mahāyāna, may all sentient beings mount the supreme jewel-vehicle of omniscience and fulfill the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva without weariness;
this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives various precious chariots as offerings to fields of merit, including even the poor, the destitute, and the solitary.
In order to cause sentient beings to possess immeasurable wisdom, to leap with joy, and ultimately to all attain the vehicle of omniscience (sarvajñatā-yāna),
[this concludes] the forty-fifth fascicle of the *Great Vaipulya Buddha’s New Avataṃsaka Sūtra Commentary* (*Dafangguang fo xin huayan jing helun*).
