Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a Śramaṇa from the Kingdom of Khotan during the Tang Dynasty.
The Treatise composed by Li Tongxuan, the Elder of Fangshan in Taiyuan, Tang China;
the Sūtra-collation and Treatise-compilation by the Śramaṇa Zhining of Kaiyuan Monastery in Fuzhou, Tang China.
Chapter Twenty-five, Part Five: The Ten Dedications.
[Treatise] Eighteenth: The Gift of the Elephant Treasure.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives away the elephant treasure, it is by nature well-tamed, endowed with its seven limbs, in the prime of its youth, possessing six pure tusks, its mouth red as a lotus flower, and its body brilliant white.
For example, it is like a golden pillar adorned with ornaments from the Snowy Mountains, covered by a net of jewels and embellished with various exquisite treasures;
those who see its trunk find delight in gazing upon it without ever growing weary. It can stride ten thousand *li* without ever becoming fatigued.

Furthermore, it may be bestowed as a gift—a well-trained and excellent horse-precious jewel, complete with all auspicious marks like a celestial steed, its radiance adorned by a wheel of exquisite, moon-like jewels.
A net of genuine golden bells covers its back; its gait is level and upright, providing security and comfort to the rider.
It travels as swiftly as the wind wherever it pleases, roaming through the four continents with sovereign ease and without obstruction.

With these precious elephants and precious horses, the Bodhisattva either provides for his parents and spiritual friends, or bestows them upon poor, destitute, and suffering sentient beings, his mind [remaining pure].
With a vast and open mind, free from regret or stinginess, they redouble their joy and celebration while increasing their compassion;
thus they cultivate the virtues of a bodhisattva and purify the bodhisattva-mind, dedicating these roots of goodness as follows:
"May all sentient beings abide in the vehicle of harmony and increase all the merits of bodhisattvas; may all sentient beings obtain the skillful vehicle and be able..."
May all sentient beings, following the birth of all Buddha-dharmas, attain the vehicle of faith and understanding;

may they attain the unimpeded power of wisdom of the Tathāgata Universal Radiance; may all sentient beings attain the vehicle of setting forth, which can universally give rise to and sustain all great vows;
and may all sentient beings be fully endowed with the vehicle of the equal pāramitās, bringing all equality to fulfillment.
By these roots of goodness, may all sentient beings accomplish the jewel-vehicle and give birth to the supreme wisdom-jewel of the Buddha-dharmas;
may all sentient beings accomplish the adorned vehicle of bodhisattva practices and cause the flowers of all bodhisattva samādhis to bloom;
may all sentient beings obtain the boundless and swift vehicle and purify their bodhisattva minds throughout incalculable eons.
Diligently contemplating and thoroughly comprehending all phenomena, may all sentient beings achieve the most supreme and well-tamed Great Vehicle;

through skillful means, may they be fully endowed with the stages of a bodhisattva. May all sentient beings achieve the highest, most vast, and firm Great Vehicle, capable of universally transporting all beings so that they all reach the state of omniscience—this is called bodhi.
When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives elephants and horses, he dedicates that root of goodness so that all sentient beings may mount the vehicle of unimpeded wisdom,
reaching the ultimate perfection of the Buddha-vehicle.
[Treatise] Nineteenth: Giving the Lion Throne.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives a seat, he may give a lion throne as his dwelling place—a throne that is high, broad, extraordinary, and exquisite, with legs made of lapis lazuli and a soft garment woven of golden threads.
Spreading [a canopy] over it, they erected jeweled banners and burned various sublime incenses;
it was adorned with countless varieties of precious ornaments, covered above by a golden net, and with jeweled bells that emitted exquisite sounds when stirred by the wind.
Adorned all around with tens of thousands of rare treasures, it was gazed upon by all the ministers and subjects, while the consecrated Great King sat alone upon its summit.
He proclaimed the transformation of the Dharma so that the myriad kingdoms followed and honored his kingship.

Furthermore, he adorned his body with wondrous jewels—namely, the Jewel of Universal Radiance, the Great Sapphire, the Supreme Sapphire, and the Victorious Treasury Maṇi-jewel—which was as bright and pure as the sun and as cool as the moon.
These were spread all around like the multitude of stars; this supreme and exquisite adornment was foremost, peerless, and ocean-like in its excellence.
Adorned with various ornaments of wondrous jewel-seas, firm banners, and extraordinary inscriptions, he was the most honored and supreme among the great assembly.
With a crown of Jāmbūnada gold and stainless precious silk upon his head, he received the position of consecration and ruled over Jambudvīpa.
Possessing immeasurable power of great majesty and virtue, he took compassion as his primary guide to subdue all enemies and provide instruction.
He caused all his actions to be performed in accordance with [the Dharma], and at that time,

the Wheel-Turning King offered such hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of immeasurable and innumerable jewel-adorned seats to the Tathāgata— the foremost field of merit— as well as to the Bodhisattvas,
true spiritual friends, the Sangha of noble sages, the teachers who expound the Dharma, his parents and kinsmen, and the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.

Those who have set out upon the bodhisattva vehicle give everything that is required—ranging from a stūpa of the Tathāgata to all things needed by the poor, the destitute, and the homeless—and dedicate these roots of goodness as follows:
"May all sentient beings sit upon the seat of enlightenment and be able to awaken to the true Dharma of all Buddhas; may all sentient beings abide..."
May all sentient beings attain the lion-throne of the Buddha’s sovereignty, which grants mastery over all dharmas, cannot be destroyed by any adamantine mountains,
and is capable of utterly subduing all demonic armies; may all sentient beings be gazed upon with reverence by all beings,
and may all sentient beings attain unspeakably, unspeakably many kinds of various sublime [qualities].
May all sentient beings attain the two kinds of most excellent seats in the world,
adorned by vast roots of goodness, through the adornment of the Jewel-Adorned Seat that guides beings with mastery over the Dharma;
may all sentient beings attain seats that pervade unspeakably unspeakable worlds, which could not be exhausted even if praised for incalculable eons.
May all sentient beings attain the seat of great, profound, and secret merit, their bodies filling the entire dharma-realm.
May all sentient beings attain inconceivable seats of various jewels, and according to their original vows, may they extensively open the gift of Dharma for all sentient beings they contemplate.
May all sentient beings attain the excellent and wondrous seat, manifesting unspeakable numbers of Buddhas.
Through supernatural power, may all sentient beings obtain all kinds of inconceivable jewel thrones—
thrones of all jewels, all incense, all flowers, all garments, all garlands, all *maṇi* gems, all lapis lazuli, and so forth;
thrones as numerous as immeasurable and unspeakable worlds, adorned with the splendors of all worlds.
The manifestation of all vajra seats as pure, wherein the Tathāgatas display sovereign power and majesty to achieve supreme perfect enlightenment—
this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva bestows precious seats,
for the purpose of causing sentient beings to attain the supramundane seat of great bodhi and to spontaneously awaken to all Buddha-dharmas.
[Treatise] Twenty: The Gift of Precious Canopies.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives precious canopies—canopies that are extraordinary and noble, adorned with various great jewels, and which are the most supreme among hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of exquisite canopies—this is [the twenty-first perfection].
The first assembly of beings features poles made of the finest jewels, covered above by exquisite nets, with precious cords and golden bells hanging down all around.
Strings of *maṇi* jewels are suspended in succession, which, when stirred by a gentle breeze, produce harmonious and wondrous sounds.
Various treasuries of pearls and jade are filled with all manner of rare treasures, all of which serve as adornments. Sandalwood and aloeswood incense of sublime fragrance pervade Jambudvīpa.

With a pure mind, they offer gold, radiance, and such infinite hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asankhyeyas of various exquisite jewels to adorn and perfect them, presenting them to the Buddha and to all stupas and temples after his parinirvāṇa;
or, for the sake of the Dharma, they give them to bodhisattvas, spiritual friends, renowned Dharma masters, or others.
Whether giving to one's parents, or to the Sangha Jewel, or offering to all the Buddhas and their teachings,
or giving to various fields of merit among sentient beings, or giving to teachers, monks, and venerable elders, or giving to those who have first resolved upon Bodhicitta,
and even to all who are poor, destitute, and exposed— giving to whoever comes seeking, whatever they may require— and by means of these roots of goodness, just as...
This dedication means: may all sentient beings diligently cultivate roots of goodness to cover their bodies, so that they are always sheltered by the protection of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings take merit and wisdom as their canopy, forever remaining free from all worldly afflictions;
and may all sentient beings be covered by wholesome dharmas to eliminate the world.
May all sentient beings attain the treasury of wisdom free from the heat of defilements and afflictions, and may they find such joy in beholding it that their hearts never tire of it.
May all sentient beings cover themselves with the white dharmas of tranquility, so that they all attain the ultimate, indestructible Buddha-dharma.
May all sentient beings well-veil their bodies, ultimately attaining the Tathāgata’s pure Dharma-body.
May all sentient beings become universal canopies of the wisdom of the ten powers, pervading and covering the world.
May all sentient beings attain sublime wisdom that transcends the three periods of time, remaining unstained by anything.
May all sentient beings attain the canopy of those worthy of offerings, becoming supreme fields of merit that receive all offerings. May all sentient beings attain the most supreme canopy.
Attaining unsurpassed wisdom and spontaneous awakening—this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva practices the canopy of giving.
It is for the sake of enabling all sentient beings to attain the canopy of mastery, so that they may uphold all wholesome dharmas;
it is for the sake of enabling all sentient beings to use a single canopy to universally cover the entirety of space and the dharma-realm.
To manifest the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas in every buddha-field without regression;
to enable all sentient beings to adorn all worlds in the ten directions with a single canopy as an offering to the Buddhas;
and to cause all sentient beings to offer exquisite banners, pennants, and various jeweled canopies to all Tathāgatas.
To cause all sentient beings to obtain universally adorned canopies that pervasively cover all Buddha-lands without exception;
to cause all sentient beings to obtain vast canopies that universally shelter all beings, leading them all to give rise to faith and understanding in the Buddhas;
and to cause all sentient beings to offer unspeakably many canopies of exquisite jewels as offerings.
Because each and every Buddha among those unspeakably many Buddhas is likewise so;
in order to cause all sentient beings to attain the vast and expansive canopy of a Buddha’s bodhi that universally covers all Tathāgatas;
and in order to cause all sentient beings to attain canopies adorned with all kinds of maṇi jewels and canopies adorned with all kinds of precious necklaces.
Canopies adorned with all kinds of firm and solid fragrances; canopies adorned with various pure jewels; canopies adorned with immeasurable pure jewels;

canopies adorned with vast pure jewels; and jeweled nets covering everything, from which jeweled bells hang down, swaying in the wind to produce subtle and wondrous sounds that universally pervade the Dharma-realm, the realm of empty space, and all worlds where the Buddhas dwell.
Furthermore, it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to obtain the canopy of the adornment of unobstructed and unhindered wisdom that universally covers all Tathāgatas;
again, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to obtain the foremost wisdom;
again, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to obtain the adornments of the Buddha's merits; and again, because he wishes to cause all sentient beings, regarding...

Because he gives rise to a mind of pure aspiration for the qualities of the Buddha; because he desires to cause all sentient beings to obtain the jewel of a mind of immeasurable and boundless sovereignty;
because he desires to cause all sentient beings to fulfill the sovereign wisdom regarding all dharmas;
because he desires to cause all sentient beings to universally cover all things with their roots of goodness; and because he desires—

To cause all sentient beings to achieve the most supreme canopy of wisdom; furthermore, desiring to cause all sentient beings to achieve a canopy that is universally pervasive throughout the ten directions;
furthermore, desiring to cause all sentient beings to be able to cover all Buddha-fields within the Dharma-realm with a single canopy;
and furthermore, desiring to cause all sentient beings to be masters of the Dharma and to act for the sake of the Dharma.
The King further desires that all sentient beings attain a mind of great majesty and sovereign power;
he further desires that all sentient beings attain vast wisdom that is ever-continuous and never-ending;
he further desires that all sentient beings attain immeasurable merit that universally covers all things and reaches ultimate perfection; he further desires that all sentient beings, by means of...
Because he wishes to cover his own mind with all merits; because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to cover all beings with a mind of equanimity;
because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to attain the great wisdom of the covering of equanimity;
because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to possess the skillful means of great dedication; and because he wishes to cause all sentient beings to obtain...
Because he desires to purify his own mind through supreme aspiration and joy; because he desires to cause all sentient beings to attain wholesome aspiration and a purified intention;
and because he desires to cause all sentient beings to attain the great dedication that universally covers all beings.
[Treatise] Twenty-first: The Gift of the Jewel Banner.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva may give various kinds of sublime banners and pennants, with poles made of many jewels and pennants made of precious silk;
these banners are adorned with various multicolored fabrics, covered with jeweled nets, and filled with radiant light.
Precious bells sway gently, their rhythms harmonizing; these extraordinary and wondrous jewels are shaped like half-moons, their Jāmbūnada gold outshining the bright sun.
All are placed atop the banners, adorned with various marvelous objects manifested according to the karmic fruits of the worlds.
Thus, countless thousands of myriads of koṭis of nayutas of such exquisite banners and streamers join their shadows together.
Their radiance shines forth in successive brilliance, pure and majestic, pervading the great earth and filling the ten directions,
the void, the dharma-realm, and all buddha-fields. With such immeasurable banners and streamers, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas— with minds of pure faith and resolve—
either offer them to all present Buddhas or to all stūpas and temples existing after the Buddhas have entered parinirvāṇa.
Whether giving the Dharma-jewel, or the Sangha-jewel, or to Bodhisattvas and spiritual friends,
or to Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, or to the great assembly, or to individuals who come as supplicants— giving universally to all with these roots of goodness,
one dedicates them in this way: namely, "May all sentient beings be able to establish all [virtuous qualities]."
May the banners and streamers of roots of goodness and merit be indestructible;
may all sentient beings erect the banners and streamers of sovereign mastery over all dharmas, honoring and delighting in them while diligently guarding and protecting them;

may all sentient beings constantly transcribe the True Dharma with precious silk and uphold the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; may all sentient beings erect lofty and eminent [banners].
May the lamp of wisdom blaze like a banner, universally illuminating the world; may all sentient beings establish firm banners and be able to utterly destroy all demonic activities.
May all sentient beings erect the banner of the power of wisdom, which no demons can ever destroy.
May all sentient beings attain the great wisdom of Nārāyaṇa’s banner and annihilate all [obstacles].
May all sentient beings obtain the great light-banner of the sun of wisdom, the banner of the world;

may they universally illumine the dharma-realm with the sunlight of wisdom. May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the banner of immeasurable jewel-adornments, filling all worlds throughout the ten directions to make offerings to all Buddhas. May all sentient beings obtain the banner of the Tathāgata to destroy [all obstacles].
To extinguish all ninety-six kinds of heterodox views of external paths is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives banners and streamers;
it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to attain the banner of the profound, lofty, and vast bodhisattva practices,
as well as the pure path of the banner of the supernormal powers of all bodhisattvas.
[Treatise] The twenty-second: Bestowing the Treasury of Jewels.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva opens the treasuries of various jewels and bestows hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of exquisite and rare treasures upon countless all sentient beings, giving them according to their wishes with a heart free from stinginess.
These roots of goodness are dedicated in this way: that is to say, may all sentient beings always behold the Buddha-jewel and abandon ignorance to practice right mindfulness;
may all sentient beings fully attain the radiance of the Dharma-jewel and uphold the treasury of the teachings of all Buddhas; and may all sentient beings be able to fully embrace the Sangha-jewel.
May they provide constant offerings without ever becoming weary; may all sentient beings attain the jewel of the supreme mind of omniscience and the pure bodhicitta, never regressing;
may all sentient beings attain the jewel of wisdom that universally enters into all phenomena with a mind free from doubt;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with the jewels of the various merits of a bodhisattva and open [the treasury of the Dharma].
May they demonstrate and expound immeasurable wisdom; may all sentient beings attain the jewels of immeasurable sublime merit and cultivate the realization of the ten powers of perfect enlightenment;

may all sentient beings attain the jewels of sublime samādhi and the sixteen kinds of knowledge, ultimately fulfilling vast and great wisdom; may all sentient beings achieve the foremost field of merit.
May all sentient beings awaken to and enter the unsurpassed wisdom of the Tathāgata, and may they all attain the status of the foremost, unsurpassed King of Jewels;
by means of inexhaustible eloquence, may they expound and manifest all dharmas.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva bestows various jewels, performed in order to cause all sentient beings to fully accomplish the foremost treasure of wisdom.
Because the Tathāgata possesses the jewel of the unimpeded pure eye.
[Treatise] Twenty-third: The Gift of Various Exquisite Ornaments.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva may practice giving by means of various exquisite ornaments.
This refers to all ornaments that adorn the body, making it pure, exquisite, and beyond reproach.
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas regard all sentient beings in the world as their only child, desiring that they all attain the pure adornment of the body and achieve the supreme worldly peace and happiness,
the bliss of Buddha-wisdom, and abide securely in the Dharma to benefit all beings.

When Jāti practices the perfection of giving by diligently bestowing hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of various exquisite and wonderful jewel ornaments, he dedicates those roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings achieve unsurpassed and sublime ornaments, adorned with all pure merits and wisdom."
May all sentient beings among humans and devas attain the mark of pure adornment, adorning their bodies with pure merit;
may all sentient beings attain the mark of supreme and wondrous adornment, adorning their bodies with the marks of a hundred merits;
may all sentient beings attain the mark of non-confused adornment, adorning their bodies with all marks.
May all sentient beings attain the mark of adornment through pure and excellent speech, endowed with various inexhaustible eloquences.
May all sentient beings attain the mark of adornment through the sound of all merits, their voices being so pure that all who hear them are filled with joy.
May all sentient beings attain the mark of adornment through the delightful speech of all Buddhas, causing...
May all sentient beings, upon hearing the Dharma, rejoice and cultivate pure conduct;
may they attain the mark of the adornment of the mind for all sentient beings, enter profound meditative concentration, and universally behold all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings attain the mark of the adornment of dhāraṇī, illuminating the true Dharma of all Buddhas. May all sentient beings attain the mark of the adornment of wisdom by means of...
The Buddha’s wisdom adorns their minds; this is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas bestow all manner of ornaments,
so that sentient beings may be fully endowed with all the immeasurable merits and wisdom of the Buddha-dharma,
achieving perfect adornment and forever leaving behind all pride and negligence.
[Treatise] Twenty-four: Bestowing the Jewel Crown and the Pearl from the Topknot.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, having received the position of the Sovereign King through consecration, bestows upon all sentient beings the maṇi-jewel crown and the pearl from his topknot;
with a heart free of stinginess, he constantly and diligently practices this, acting as a great donor.
Training in generosity and wisdom, increasing the faculty of relinquishment, and becoming skillful in wisdom, his mind becomes vast as he bestows gifts upon all.
With those roots of goodness, he dedicates them in this way: "May all sentient beings receive the consecration of the Buddha-dharmas and achieve omniscience;
may all sentient beings be endowed with the uṣṇīṣa and attain the supreme wisdom."
May all sentient beings reach the other shore; may they universally gather in all beings with the jewel of wondrous wisdom, causing them all to ultimately reach the pinnacle of merit.
May all sentient beings achieve the crest-jewel of wisdom, becoming worthy of the veneration of the world. May all sentient beings adorn their heads with the crown of wisdom.
May all sentient beings have the luminous pearl of wisdom bound upon their crowns as sovereign kings with mastery over all phenomena, such that none in any world can behold them;
may all sentient beings be fully capable of receiving the prostrations of the world, achieving the summit of wisdom that illuminates the Buddha-dharma;
and may all sentient beings wear upon their heads the crown adorned with the Ten Powers.
May all sentient beings reach the crown of the great earth and attain omniscience;
may they perfect the ten ultimate powers and shatter the hosts of Māras at the summit of the desire realm.
May all sentient beings become the foremost, unsurpassed Crown Kings, attaining the crown of the light of omniscience that can never be eclipsed or stolen away.

When giving jeweled crowns as a bodhisattva mahāsattva, one dedicates the roots of goodness for the sake of causing all sentient beings to obtain the crown of the wondrous maṇi-jewel of wisdom— the foremost knowledge and most pure state.
[Treatise] Twenty-fifth: Giving Wealth, Treasures, Wife, and Children to Rescue Sentient Beings from Prison.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees sentient beings situated within prisons and dark places, their bodies bound by handcuffs, fetters, and shackles, unable to rest in sitting or rising, with various sufferings converging upon them and having no relatives or acquaintances—
Seeing those who were without refuge or protection, naked, famished, emaciated, and suffering from unbearable, acute agony,
the Bodhisattva relinquished all his wealth, treasures, wife, children, and kinsmen, as well as his own person, to rescue those sentient beings from within the prison. Having thus delivered them,
like the Great Compassionate Bodhisattva and the Bodhisattva King Wondrous Eye, he provided for them everything they required according to their needs.
Having bestowed gifts to eliminate their suffering and afflictions and cause them to attain peace and security, he then bestows the unsurpassed jewel of the Dharma,
causing them to abandon negligence and abide in roots of goodness, so that within the Buddha’s teaching their minds never regress. O Son of the Buddha,
when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva rescues sentient beings from within a prison, he dedicates his various roots of goodness in this way, making the following vow:
May all sentient beings attain ultimate liberation from the fetters of craving and greed;

may all sentient beings sever the stream of birth and death and ascend to the shore of wisdom; may all sentient beings eliminate ignorance, cultivate wisdom, and be liberated from the entanglements of all afflictions;
may all sentient beings extinguish the bonds of the three realms and attain omniscience.
May all sentient beings ultimately attain liberation, forever severing all fetters of affliction and reaching the shore of wisdom—a state free from affliction and free from obstruction.

May all sentient beings be detached from all stirring thoughts, reflections, and discriminations, entering the ground of impartial, immovable wisdom. May all sentient beings be released from the bonds of desire and forever be free from them.
May all worldly desires leave them unstained within the three realms;
may all sentient beings attain superior aspiration and joy, constantly receiving the teaching of the Dharma-gates from all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings attain a mind of liberation—unattached and unbound—vast as the *dharmadhātu* and ultimate as space; may all sentient beings attain...
The bodhisattva’s supernormal powers subdue sentient beings in all worlds, causing them to leave the mundane world behind and abide in the Mahāyāna;
this is the dedication of roots of goodness by the bodhisattva-mahāsattva when rescuing sentient beings suffering in prison,
performed so that sentient beings may universally enter the ground of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.
[Treatise] Twenty-six: Sacrificing One’s Body to Spare Another’s Life.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva sees a prisoner bound at five points, undergoing various agonizing torments, being guarded and driven toward the place of execution where his life is about to be cut short, he renounces all the pleasures and possessions of Jambudvīpa.
When relatives and friends have all bid them eternal farewell, they place them upon high wooden blocks and butcher them with knives,
or impale their bodies on wooden stakes, wrap them in cloth, drench them in oil, and burn them with fire. Having seen such various forms of suffering and oppression,
the Bodhisattva relinquishes his own body to undergo it in their stead, as was the case with the Bodhisattva Ajita’s supreme excellence.

The Bodhisattva Cāritramati and countless other great bodhisattvas, for the sake of sentient beings, voluntarily relinquished their own bodies and lives and underwent various forms of suffering and poison.
At that time, the bodhisattva spoke to the official, saying: "I vow to sacrifice my body to take his life in its place;
such sufferings as these may be given to me. Whether you treat this person or act according to your will, even if it exceeds those sufferings, let it be done."
"Even if I must undergo [suffering] for an incalculable number of times my own measure, I shall cause them to be liberated.
If I were to see them being led to execution and yet did not sacrifice my own body and life to redeem them from their suffering, I would not be said to abide in the Bodhisattva mind.
Why is this? It is because I have generated the Bodhicitta of omniscience for the sake of protecting and rescuing all sentient beings. O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva..."
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva sacrifices their own body and life to save sentient beings, they dedicate all roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, they vow that all sentient beings shall attain an inexhaustible and ultimate body and life, forever free from all calamities, misfortunes, and afflictions;
and that all sentient beings shall abide in the presence of all Buddhas, receive all-knowledge, and be fully endowed with the ten powers of enlightenment.
I vow that all sentient beings may universally rescue all conscious beings, causing them to be free from fear and forever emerge from the evil realms;
I vow that all sentient beings may attain all life and enter the realm of deathless wisdom;

I vow that all sentient beings may forever be parted from enemies and adversaries, be free from all calamities and hardships, and always be sustained by the Buddhas as their virtuous friends. May all...
May all sentient beings abandon all swords, blades, weapons, and instruments of evil suffering, and practice various kinds of pure and wholesome deeds.
May all sentient beings be free from all fears; beneath the Bodhi tree, may they subdue the armies of Māra.
May all sentient beings be free from the fear of the great assembly; regarding the unsurpassed Dharma, may their minds be pure and fearless, and may they be able to act as supreme leaders.
With a great lion’s roar, he vows that all sentient beings may attain the unobstructed wisdom of a lion;

that they may practice right action within all worlds; and that they may reach the state of fearlessness, constantly mindful of rescuing and protecting all suffering beings—this is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva relinquishing his own body and life to save those prisoners facing execution.
At that time, he dedicated his roots of goodness so that sentient beings might leave behind the suffering of birth and death and attain the supreme, wondrous bliss of the Tathāgata.
[Treatise] Twenty-seventh: Giving away the crown of the head with its skin intact.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas— such as the Bodhisattva Ratnaśikhin, the Bodhisattva Śikhi, the Bodhisattva Uttama-kāya, and other immeasurable Bodhisattvas—
saw a beggar approaching, their hearts were filled with joy, and they spoke to him, saying: "If you now require my topknot together with its skin, you may take it."
"Regarding my taking of this *uṣṇīṣa*, it is the foremost in Jambudvīpa. When he spoke these words, his mind was undisturbed;
he did not dwell on other activities, but abandoned the world, aspiring for tranquility and ultimate purity.
With diligent and upright resolve toward omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), he then took a sharp blade and cut from his head the *uṣṇīṣa* together with its skin, starting from the right.
Kneeling on the ground with palms joined, they single-mindedly offer their devotion;

with right mindfulness toward all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time, they give rise to great joy and superior aspiration. Their minds are well-illuminated and liberated regarding all phenomena;
they do not grasp at suffering, but thoroughly understand that the sensation of suffering is signless and unarisen, and that all sensations arise in mutual succession without any permanence.

Therefore, I should, together with all Bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present, practice great relinquishment (*mahātyāga*), generate deep faith and joy, and seek omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) without ever turning back;

through the power of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) and not by means of instruction from others, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva performs such giving, he dedicates these roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*) in this way: namely, may all sentient beings attain...

May all sentient beings attain hair as dark blue as a sapphire, hair like a vajra, and hair that is fine and soft, which can extinguish all the afflictions of sentient beings—just as the Bodhisattva Anavalokitamūrdha possesses a crown-protrusion like a stupa;
may all sentient beings attain lustrous hair, dense hair, and hair that does not encroach upon the temples or the forehead; may all sentient beings attain hair that is supple and soft.
May all sentient beings obtain hair that grows from the temples and forehead; may all sentient beings obtain hair with the *svastika* mark and curls spiraling to the right like a conch shell;
may all sentient beings obtain hair with the marks of a Buddha, forever free from the fetters and habitual tendencies of all afflictions;
may all sentient beings obtain radiant hair, its light universally illuminating the worlds of the ten directions. May all sentient beings...
May all sentient beings obtain hair that is naturally free from disorder, as pure, wondrous, and unadulterated as the hair of a Tathāgata;

may those who see it perceive it as the hair of a Buddha. May all sentient beings obtain the unstained hair of a Tathāgata, forever free from all darkness, obscurations, dust, and defilements. This is the bodhisattva’s... [aspiration].
When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gave away his skin and topknot, he dedicated those roots of goodness for the sake of causing the minds of all sentient beings to be tranquil,
so that they might all attain the perfection of all dhāraṇīs and the ultimate, tenfold power of the Tathāgata’s knowledge of all modes.
[Treatise] Twenty-eighth: The Gift of the Eyes.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his eyes as a gift to those who come to beg, just as the Bodhisattva Pramudita-caryā, the Bodhisattva Candraprabha-rāja, and countless other Bodhisattvas practiced such acts of giving.

When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his eyes, he gives rise to a mind of pure giving of eyes; he gives rise to a mind of pure wisdom-eye; he gives rise to a mind that relies upon the light of the Dharma;
he gives rise to a mind that realizes the unsurpassed Buddha-way; he gives rise to a mind of dedication toward vast wisdom;
he gives rise to a mind of impartial renunciation equal to that of the bodhisattvas of the three periods of time; and he gives rise to a mind directed toward the unobstructed eye.
With unshakable pure faith, they give rise toward beggars to a mind of joyful acceptance, for the sake of perfecting all supernatural powers,
for the sake of producing the Buddha-eye, for the sake of increasing the vast bodhicitta, for the sake of cultivating great compassion,
and for the sake of subduing the six sense faculties; it is toward such dharmas that the sons of the Buddha direct their minds.
When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his eyes as a gift, he conceives a heart of love and joy toward the beggar;
he establishes assemblies for the Dharma, increases the power of the teachings, abandons worldly attachment, views, and negligence, severs the bonds of desire, and cultivates bodhi.
In accordance with whatever is sought, his mind remains unshakable; he does not oppose their wishes but satisfies them all, always acting in conformity with them.
With this practice of non-dual equanimity, they dedicate these roots of goodness in this way:
namely, they vow that all sentient beings may obtain the most supreme eye to guide all; they vow that all sentient beings may obtain the unimpeded eye to open wide the treasury of wisdom;
they vow that all sentient beings may obtain the pure physical eye, its radiance penetrating so clearly that nothing can obscure it. All...
May all sentient beings obtain the pure celestial eye and see the karmic fruits of birth and death for all beings;
may all sentient beings obtain the pure Dharma-eye and be able to enter the realm of the Tathāgata in accordance with it;

may all sentient beings obtain the wisdom-eye and abandon all conceptual discrimination and attachment; may all sentient beings be fully endowed with the Buddha-eye and be able to awaken to all things.
May all phenomena be realized; may all sentient beings achieve the Universal Eye, exhausting all realms without obstruction.
May all sentient beings achieve the pure eye free from the cataracts of ignorance, seeing that the realm of sentient beings is empty and non-existent.
May all sentient beings be endowed with the pure, unobstructed eye and attain ultimate perfection.
The ten powers of the Tathāgata constitute the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives his eyes,
for the purpose of causing sentient beings to attain the pure eye of omniscience.
[Treatise] The twenty-ninth is the gift of the ears.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are able to give their ears and noses to those who beg for them—
just as when King Śreṇika, the Bodhisattva Aśoka, the Bodhisattva Vijitāvin, and other immeasurable Bodhisattvas gave them away— they personally...
I further entreat you: may those who practice with single-minded devotion the various bodhisattva deeds, possess the lineage of the Buddhas, and be born into the family of the Tathāgatas;
may they constantly and diligently give rise to the awakening of all Buddhas by recollecting the practices performed by the bodhisattvas;

may they purify their faculties through merit and wisdom, and observe the three realms of existence as lacking even a single thing of substance; and may they always behold all Buddhas and bodhisattvas according to their vows.
Mindfully recollecting all Buddha-dharmas, he knows that the body is illusory, empty, non-existent, and devoid of anything to be craved or cherished.

When the Bodhisattva thus gives his ears and nose, his mind remains constantly tranquil, he subdues his sense faculties, and he strives to rescue sentient beings from their perilous and evil hardships.
He brings forth all wisdom and merit, enters the great ocean of giving, and fully realizes the meaning of the Dharma.
Cultivating all paths by relying on the practice of wisdom, one attains mastery over the Dharma and exchanges this non-solid body for a solid body.
Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives away their ears, they dedicate these roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, they vow that all sentient beings may attain unimpeded ears and universally hear the sounds of all teachings being expounded; they vow that all...
May all sentient beings attain unobstructed ears, capable of fully understanding and comprehending all sounds.
May all sentient beings attain the ears of a Tathāgata, being universally discerning and free from any impediment.

May all sentient beings attain pure ears, such that they do not give rise to discriminatory thoughts based on the sense-base of the ear. May all sentient beings attain ears free from deafness, so that they may receive [all teachings].
May obscured consciousness never arise; may all sentient beings attain ears that pervade the entire Dharma-realm and fully know the sounds of the teachings of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings attain unimpeded ears and awaken to all unhindered dharmas.
May all sentient beings attain indestructible ears, such that they skillfully understand all treatises and none can defeat them. May one...
May all sentient beings attain the vast and pure universal-hearing ear that serves as the sovereign of all ears;

may all sentient beings be fully endowed with the divine ear and the Buddha-ear. This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives their ears, performed so that all sentient beings may obtain pure ears.
[Treatise] The thirtieth: Giving the Nose.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his nose, he dedicates the merit in this way:

that is to say, he makes the vow that all sentient beings may obtain a prominent and straight nose, a nose of the secondary marks (anuvyañjana), a nose of excellent characteristics, and a nose that is lovely and delightful.
May they obtain a pure and wondrous nose, a compliant nose, a prominent and distinguished nose,
a nose that subdues enemies, a well-seeing nose, and a nose like that of a Tathāgata. May all sentient beings obtain a face free from anger,
a face of all dharmas, an unobstructed face, a well-seeing face, a compliant face, a pure face, and a face free from faults.

May they obtain a face like that of the Tathāgata; may they obtain a face that pervades all places; may they obtain a face of immeasurable beauty. This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives their nose, in order to cause sentient beings to ultimately enter into all Buddha-dharmas, in order to cause sentient beings to ultimately embrace all Buddha-dharmas, and in order to... In order that sentient beings may ultimately and fully comprehend all Buddha-dharmas;
in order that sentient beings may ultimately uphold and maintain all Buddha-dharmas; in order that sentient beings may ultimately and constantly behold all Tathāgatas;
in order that sentient beings may all realize and attain the gateways of the Buddha-dharmas; and in order that sentient beings may ultimately achieve an indestructible mind.

It is for the sake of enabling all sentient beings to clearly perceive and understand the true Dharma of all Buddhas; it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to universally adorn and purify all Buddha-lands;

it is for the sake of causing all sentient beings to attain the body of great majestic power of the Tathāgata—this is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas give their ears and noses.
[Treatise] Thirty-first: Giving Teeth.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells securely in the stage of the firm and sovereign ground (*dṛḍha-svabhūmi*), they are able to give their teeth to all sentient beings, just as in the past the Bodhisattva King Puṣpadanta and the Bodhisattva Six-Tusked Elephant King did.
When other immeasurable bodhisattvas, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, gave their teeth as a gift, their minds were pure, rare, and difficult to find—like the udumbara flower.
That is to say: they gave with an inexhaustible mind; they gave with a mind of great faith; they gave with a mind that accomplishes the immeasurable at every step;
they gave with a mind that subdues all the sense faculties; they gave with a mind that relinquishes everything entirely; they gave with a single-minded resolve.
With a mind of all-knowing aspiration, a mind that bestows peace and happiness upon sentient beings, a mind that practices great giving, supreme giving, most excellent giving, and peerless giving—
giving even the essential requirements of one’s own body without any resentment— the Bodhisattva at that time dedicates these roots of goodness as follows:
namely, may all sentient beings obtain sharp, white teeth, become most excellent stupas, and receive the offerings of the heavens.
May all sentient beings be provided for and attain teeth that are even and level, like the marks and signs of a Buddha, without gaps or deficiencies.
May all sentient beings attain a tamed mind and skillfully enter the bodhisattva practices of the pāramitās.
May all sentient beings have mouths that are perfectly pure, with teeth that are bright white and clearly manifest. May all sentient beings attain...
May they be mindful of adorning their teeth so that their mouths are pure and free from any loathsome appearance;
may all sentient beings achieve fully developed teeth numbering forty, constantly emitting various rare and wondrous fragrances;
and may the minds of all sentient beings be well-tamed, their teeth as fresh and white as lotus flowers, with patterns swirling in the form of the *svastika*.
I vow that all sentient beings shall have fresh and pure lips and white teeth, emitting immeasurable light that shines everywhere;
I vow that all sentient beings shall have firm and sharp teeth, eating grains without leaving a single whole particle, remaining free from attachment to flavors, and becoming supreme fields of merit;
I vow that all sentient beings shall constantly emit radiance from between their teeth to empower all bodhisattvas.
The first prediction is that when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives his teeth as a gift,
he dedicates these roots of goodness so that sentient beings may possess all-knowledge and attain purity of wisdom regarding all phenomena.
[Treatise] Thirty-second: The Gift of the Tongue.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, if there should come a person who begs for the tongue of a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, that Bodhisattva, out of a mind of compassion toward the beggar, speaks with gentle and affectionate words, just as in the past the Bodhisattva Prasenajit did not retreat.
When the Bodhisattva Vajra-āvarta and other immeasurable sons of the Buddha— bodhisattvas, mahāsattvas—
take birth within the various realms of existence, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sentient beings come to beg for their tongues.
At that time, the bodhisattva seats those people upon lion thrones with a mind free from anger and a mind free from malice.
With a mind free from resentment, a mind of great majestic power, a mind born from the lineage of the Buddha, a mind abiding in the dwelling of a bodhisattva,
a mind that is never turbid or confused, a mind abiding in great strength, a mind unattached to the body, and a mind unattached to speech; with both knees touching the ground,
he extends his tongue from his open mouth to show it to the beggar, and addresses him with a compassionate heart and gentle words.
He said, "I now offer this body of mine entirely to you; you may take my tongue and use it as you please, so that all your aspirations may be fulfilled.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicated his roots of goodness in this way, namely:
"May all sentient beings obtain a universal tongue, capable of proclaiming and teaching all languages and dharmas; may all sentient beings..."
May all sentient beings obtain tongues that naturally cover their faces, such that what they say is non-dual and entirely true;
may they obtain tongues that manifest the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas, covering all Buddha-lands;
may all sentient beings obtain soft and thin tongues, always experiencing exquisite, pure, and supreme flavors; and may all sentient beings obtain eloquence.
May their tongues be able to sever all the nets of doubt in the world;

may all sentient beings obtain tongues of radiance capable of emitting countless tens of billions of rays of light; may all sentient beings obtain tongues of definitive eloquence, explaining all dharmas without end;
may all sentient beings obtain universally subduing tongues, skillfully able to reveal and teach all secrets.
May all speech be accepted with faith; may all sentient beings attain a universally pervasive tongue that skillfully enters the great ocean of all languages;

may all sentient beings attain a tongue that skillfully expounds all dharma-gates and reaches the further shore of wisdom regarding all speech. This is the bodhisattva mahāsattva’s giving of the tongue.
He dedicates his roots of goodness so that all sentient beings may attain perfect and unimpeded wisdom.
[Treatise] Thirty-third: Giving the Head.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his head to those who come to beg, it is like the most supreme wisdom.

The practice of giving by Bodhisattvas and great beings such as the King of Kāśī and other great Bodhisattvas is for the sake of accomplishing the entry into the supreme wisdom that heads all dharmas;
it is for the sake of accomplishing the realization of great bodhi and becoming the head who rescues sentient beings;
it is for the sake of fulfilling the vision of the most foremost among all dharmas; and it is for the sake of attaining right view and purity.
Vimalamati [Pure Wisdom Head] for the sake of accomplishing the unobstructed head; Jyeṣṭhabhūmiprāptiśīrṣa [Head of Attaining the First Stage] for the sake of realizing the foremost stage;

Lokottarajñānaśīrṣa [Head of Supramundane Supreme Wisdom] for the sake of seeking the most excellent wisdom of the world; Trailokyānavalokitamūrdha [Head Unseen by the Three Realms] for the sake of perfecting pure wisdom;

Sarvadiṅniḥsaraṇajñānarājaśīrṣa [Head of the King of Wisdom Manifesting Universal Reach to the Ten Directions] for the sake of attaining the manifestation of universal reach to the ten directions; and Sarvadharmaparipūrṇaśīrṣa [Head Perfecting All Dharmas] for the sake of fulfilling all dharmas.
The sons of the Buddha, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who are capable of destroying the heads of the Māras, abide in this Dharma and practice it with diligent application;
they have thus entered the lineage of all Buddhas, training in the conduct of a Buddha and practicing generosity.
In the presence of all Buddhas, they give rise to pure faith, increase their roots of goodness, and cause all beggars to attain satisfaction; their minds are pure, joyful, and delighted.

With immeasurable minds, pure faith, understanding, and illumination of the Buddha-dharma, they give rise to the aspiration for enlightenment (*bodhicitta*), abide in equanimity, and experience joy in their faculties.
Their merits increase, and they generate a wholesome desire for the Dharma, always delighting in the practice of vast and extensive deeds.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates all these roots of goodness in this way: "May all sentient beings attain the state of a Tathāgata."
His head possesses the mark of the invisible crown; nowhere can it be eclipsed, and among all Buddha-fields it is the most preeminent.
His hair curls to the right, luminous, pure, and glossy, adorned with the *svastika*—rare in the world.
He is endowed with the head of a Buddha, the head of wisdom, the foremost head in all worlds; he is the complete head, the pure head.
The head is the perfection of wisdom for sitting at the site of enlightenment;
this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva gives their head, so that sentient beings may attain the most supreme dharma and achieve unsurpassed, great wisdom.
[Treatise] Thirty-fourth: Giving Hands and Feet.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas give their hands and feet to all sentient beings, just as the Bodhisattva Constant Diligence, the Bodhisattva King Without Sorrow, and other immeasurable Bodhisattvas have planted [roots of merit] throughout the various realms of existence.

In whatever place of birth one may be reborn, may one have hands for giving; with faith as one's hand, may one undertake deeds of benefit, moving back and forth to diligently cultivate the True Dharma.
May one obtain precious hands and practice giving with those hands so that all actions are not in vain, fulfilling the Bodhisattva path.
May one always extend one’s hand to provide vast kindness, walking with steady steps, courageous and fearless, endowed with the power of pure faith.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, Son of the Buddha, who practices with diligence to eliminate the evil realms and achieve awakening,
when giving in this manner, employs an immeasurable, boundless, and vast mind to open the gateways of the pure Dharma,

enter the ocean of all Buddhas, and perfect the hand of generosity. Providing for all throughout the ten directions, they sustain the path of omniscience through the power of their vows and abide in the ultimate state of liberation.
With a mind free from defilement, their dharma-body and wisdom-body are uninterrupted and indestructible; no demonic activities can shake them.
Relying upon spiritual friends, they stabilize their minds and practice the perfection of generosity together with all bodhisattvas.
O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva seeks omniscience for the sake of all sentient beings and gives away his hands and feet, he dedicates his roots of goodness in this manner:
Dedication refers to the vow that all sentient beings shall possess supernatural powers and each obtain a "jewel-hand";
having obtained these jewel-hands, they shall respect one another and regard each other as fields of merit, mutually making offerings with various kinds of jewels.
Furthermore, they shall offer various jewels to all Buddhas, raising clouds of exquisite jewels that pervade all Buddha-lands, causing all sentient beings to give rise to mutual compassion.
With minds free from mutual affliction or harm, they travel through all Buddha-fields, dwelling in fearlessness and naturally possessing ultimate supernatural powers (*abhijñā*).

Furthermore, they cause all beings to obtain the jewel-hand, flower-hand, incense-hand, robe-hand, parasol-hand, garland-hand, powdered-incense-hand, ornament-hand, boundless-hand, immeasurable-hand, and universal-hand; having obtained these hands, they employ their supernatural powers.
With constant vigor, he frequents all Buddha-lands; he is able to touch all Buddha-worlds with a single hand;
with hands of mastery, he receives all sentient beings; his hands are exquisite, emitting immeasurable light;
he can cover all sentient beings with a single hand; he has perfected the Tathāgata’s marks of webbed fingers and copper-colored nails—such is the Bodhisattva.
At that time, with the hand of great vows, he universally covers all sentient beings, vowing that all sentient beings shall always joyfully seek supreme enlightenment,
give birth to the great ocean of all merits, feel no weariness or satiety upon seeing those who come to beg,
enter the ocean of the Buddha-dharma, and share in the same roots of goodness as the Buddha. This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his hands and feet.
[Commentary] Thirty-fifth: Giving Blood.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva breaks his own body to draw blood and gives it to sentient beings, this is the karma of one who practices according to the Dharma.
When the Bodhisattva King Sādhucarita and the other immeasurable bodhisattvas gave their own bodies and blood within the various realms of existence,
they gave rise to the mind that accomplishes all-knowledge, the mind that yearns for great enlightenment, the mind that delights in practicing the bodhisattva path,
the mind that does not grasp at painful sensations, the mind that joyfully beholds beggars, and the mind that never feels resentment toward those who come to ask for alms.
He gives rise to a mind that inclines toward all bodhisattva paths; he gives rise to a mind that protects the renunciation of all bodhisattvas;
he gives rise to a mind that increases and expands the virtuous giving of bodhisattvas; he gives rise to a mind of non-retrogression, a tireless mind, and a mind free from attachment to self.
He dedicates these roots of goodness in this manner, namely: "May all sentient beings fully accomplish the Dharma."
May all sentient beings attain a body of wisdom; may they attain a body like adamant, free from weariness and fatigue;

may they attain an indestructible body that cannot be harmed; may they attain a body like a transformation-body (*nirmāṇakāya*), appearing throughout the world without end; and may all sentient beings attain a pure and delightful body.
May all sentient beings attain a body born of the Dharma-realm through wondrous and firm vows, identical to that of the Tathāgata and free from any dependence;
may all sentient beings attain a body of wondrous jewel-like radiance that no person in the world can eclipse;
may all sentient beings attain a body that is a treasury of wisdom and achieve mastery within the deathless realm.
May all sentient beings obtain a body like a jewel-ocean, seeing which they all receive benefit without it being in vain;
may all sentient beings obtain a body like space, such that worldly afflictions and sufferings cannot defile them.
This is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s state of mind when giving his own blood: a Mahāyāna mind, a pure mind, a vast mind, a joyful mind, and a mind of celebration.
With a mind of joy, a mind of superior peace, a mind of bliss, and a mind free from turbidity, he dedicates his roots of goodness.
[Treatise] The thirty-sixth: Giving the Marrow.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva sees someone begging for the marrow and flesh of his body, he speaks with joyful and gentle words.
It means saying to the beggar: "Take my marrow and flesh as you please;

like the Bodhisattva Sarvasattvapriyadarśana, the Bodhisattva King of All-Givers, and other immeasurable bodhisattvas, when I give my marrow and flesh to beggars throughout various realms of existence and diverse places of birth, may my joy be vast and my mind of giving increase, so that I may practice in common with all bodhisattvas."
Cultivating roots of goodness, they leave behind the dust and defilements of the world and attain deep resolve and joy.

They universally offer their bodies with an inexhaustible mind, fully possessing immeasurable and vast roots of goodness. They embrace all treasures of sublime merit and, in accordance with the Dharma of Bodhisattvas, practice without weariness.
Their minds always delight in the merit of giving, providing for all completely without regret. Thus they examine themselves with precision.

Contemplating that all phenomena arise from conditions and lack intrinsic substance, one does not crave the act of giving nor its karmic rewards; rather, one practices impartial giving according to whatever circumstances may arise.
When a son of the Buddha, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, gives in this manner, all Buddhas appear before them, and by perceiving them as a father, they receive their protective mindfulness.
Consequently, all sentient beings appear before them, and they cause them all to be universally benefited.
Because they abide in the pure Dharma, all worlds appear before them; because they adorn and purify all Buddha-lands, all sentient beings appear before them;
because they universally rescue and protect with great compassion, all paths of the Buddhas appear before them;
because they joyfully contemplate the ten powers of the Tathāgata, [all things of] the past, future, and present appear before them.
Because all Bodhisattvas manifest before them to collectively perfect all roots of goodness, all fearlessnesses manifest before them as they are able to utter the supreme lion’s roar;
because all three periods of time manifest before them as they attain equalizing wisdom and universally observe;
and because all worlds manifest before them as they give forth vast vows to exhaust the future...
Because they cultivate bodhi throughout future kalpas, all the tireless practices of all bodhisattvas manifest before them;
because they give rise to immeasurable and vast resolve, O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his marrow and flesh, he dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
namely, may all sentient beings attain a vajra-body that cannot be destroyed.
May all sentient beings attain a firm and dense body that is forever without deficiency or diminution;
may all sentient beings attain a mind-born body, adorned and pure like the body of a Buddha;

may all sentient beings attain a body with the marks of a hundred merits, adorned by themselves with the thirty-two major marks; may all sentient beings attain the eighty minor marks of exquisite adornment.
May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the ornaments of the body and possess the ten powers that cannot be severed or destroyed;
may all sentient beings attain the body of a Tathāgata, which is ultimately pure and immeasurable; may all sentient beings attain a firm and solid body that cannot be harmed by any Māras or enemies;
may all sentient beings attain the body of one mark, being of one and the same body as the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
May all sentient beings attain an unobstructed body, pervading the realm of empty space with the pure Dharma-body;
may all sentient beings attain the body of the treasury of Bodhi, capable of universally containing all worlds.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when seeking all-knowledge through the giving of marrow and flesh, in order to cause all sentient beings to [attain this].
Because of attaining the Tathāgata’s ultimately pure and immeasurable body.
