[Treatise] Thirty-seventh: The Mind of Giving.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas give their own hearts to those who come to beg, they do so like the Bodhisattva Arhatapratigha (No-Regret) and the Bodhisattva Asaṅgarāja (Unobstructed King),
as well as other immeasurable great Bodhisattvas. At the time of giving their own hearts to beggars,
they train in the mind of sovereign giving, cultivate the mind of universal giving, and practice the mind of the *dānapāramitā*.
The mind that accomplishes the *dāna-pāramitā*; the mind of training in the generosity of all bodhisattvas;
the inexhaustible mind that relinquishes everything; the mind habituated to giving all things; the mind that bears the burden of the practice of all bodhisattvas;
the mind of right mindfulness with all Buddhas appearing before one; and the uninterrupted mind that makes offerings to all who come as supplicants.
When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives in this manner, his mind is pure because he seeks to deliver all sentient beings,
because he seeks to attain the state of enlightenment endowed with the ten powers, because he practices in reliance upon his great vows,
because he desires to abide securely in the bodhisattva path, because he desires to accomplish all-knowledge, and because he does not abandon his original vow.

One dedicates all roots of goodness in this way: namely, the vow that all sentient beings may attain the adamantine treasury heart (*vajragarbha-citta*), which cannot be destroyed by any adamantine perimeter mountains or the like;
that all sentient beings may attain the *svastika*-adorned adamantine realm heart (*vajradhātu-citta*), the unshakable heart, the fearless heart, and the heart that brings benefit.
A mind that is eternally inexhaustible in the world; a mind that is a treasury of wisdom with great heroic valor;
a mind as firm and solid as Nārāyaṇa’s banner; a mind as inexhaustible as the ocean of sentient beings; a mind that is a treasury of Nārāyaṇa, indestructible by any;
a mind that extinguishes all demonic activities and the hosts of Māra’s armies; a mind free from fear; and a mind of great majestic power.
The mind attains constant diligence; the mind attains great valor; the mind attains freedom from fear and dread; the mind attains the donning of the adamantine armor;
the mind attains the supreme state of all Bodhisattvas; the mind attains the accomplishment of the light of the Buddha-dharma and Bodhi;
the mind attains the sitting beneath the Bodhi tree, abiding securely in the true Dharma of all Buddhas, free from all delusions, and becoming one.

The mind of all-knowledge attains accomplishment; this mind of the ten powers is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the mind of giving, in order to cause sentient beings to remain unstained by the world and to become fully endowed with the mind of the Tathāgata’s ten powers.
[Treatise] Thirty-eighth: The Gift of the Liver and Lungs.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, if a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is requested for his intestines, kidneys, liver, or lungs, he gives them all away, just as the Bodhisattva Sudatta, the Bodhisattva Mārajit Viśeṣarāja, and countless other great Bodhisattvas did.

When practicing this giving, upon seeing a beggar approach, his heart rejoices; he gazes upon them with eyes of affection and, for the sake of seeking enlightenment, bestows everything they require without any regret in his mind.
He contemplates that this body is devoid of solidity and thinks, "I should give it to them in order to obtain a solid body.
Furthermore, he reflects that this body will soon perish and that those who see it will feel revulsion.
This body is impermanent and will inevitably be cast aside to be devoured by foxes, wolves, and hungry dogs; it is food for others, devoid of self-awareness.
When a son of the Buddha, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, contemplates in this way, he realizes that the body is impermanent and the ultimate in impurity.
He attains great joy through his understanding of the Dharma and, with a heart of reverence, gazes intently upon the beggar who approaches him.
When spiritual friends come to protect them, they grant whatever is requested without exception, exchanging this non-substantial body for a solid and enduring body.
O Son of the Buddha, when Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas give in this manner, they dedicate all their roots of goodness,
vowing that all sentient beings may attain a body that is a treasury of wisdom, pure both internally and externally, and that all sentient beings [may likewise attain it].
May they obtain a body that is a treasury of merit, capable of universally sustaining all vows for omniscience.
May all sentient beings attain a most sublime body, with wondrous fragrance within and radiant light emanating from without.

May all sentient beings attain a body where the abdomen does not protrude, with the upper and lower parts straight and the limbs and joints in perfect proportion. May all sentient beings attain a body of wisdom through the flavor of the Buddha-dharma.
May all sentient beings be filled with joy and flourish; may they attain an inexhaustible body and practice abiding in the profound nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*).
May all sentient beings attain the *dhāraṇī* treasury of a pure body and manifest all dharmas through wondrous eloquence.
May all sentient beings attain a pure body, such that both body and mind are pure within and without. May they be so.
May all sentient beings attain the body of profound contemplative practice of the Tathāgata’s wisdom, be filled with wisdom, and rain down the great rain of Dharma.
May all sentient beings attain a body of inner tranquility, act as a king of the banner of wisdom for the sake of sentient beings externally, and emit great light that universally illumines all.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when giving their intestines, kidneys, livers, and lungs.
This was done in order to cause sentient beings to become pure both internally and externally, so that they may all dwell securely in unimpeded wisdom.
[Treatise] Thirty-ninth: Giving of Limbs, Joints, and Bones.
[Sūtra] O Sons of the Buddha, when Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas give their limbs, joints, and bones to beggars— such as Dharmagarbha Bodhisattva, Prabhāsarāja Bodhisattva,
and countless other great bodhisattvas— at the time they give these parts of their bodies, limbs, and bones,
they see the beggar coming and give rise to a heart of affection and delight, a heart of joy, a heart of pure faith, a heart of peace and happiness, and a heart of courage.
With a fierce mind, a compassionate mind, an unimpeded mind, and a pure mind, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives with a heart that grants whatever is requested.
When giving his own body and bones, he dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings attain a body like a transformation-body (nirmāṇakāya) and no longer receive a body of bone, flesh, and blood; may all sentient beings attain..."

May all sentient beings attain the indestructible and invincible Vajra-body, and may they be born within the realm that is unbound, unattached, and unconditioned, attaining the perfect Dharma-body of omniscience.

May all sentient beings attain the body of the power of wisdom, with all faculties perfected, uninterrupted and indestructible. May all sentient beings attain the body of the power of Dharma and wisdom.
May all sentient beings reach the further shore through mastery of power; may they obtain a firm and solid body that is constant and indestructible;
may all sentient beings obtain a body that manifests in accordance with needs to teach and transform all beings;
and may all sentient beings obtain a body perfumed by wisdom, possessing the great strength of Nārāyaṇa in every limb and joint.
May all sentient beings attain a firm, continuous, and uninterrupted body, forever free from all exhaustion and fatigue.
May all sentient beings attain a body of great power and stability, fully endowed with the great strength of diligence.
May all sentient beings attain a universal Dharma-body throughout the world, abiding in the realm of immeasurable, supreme wisdom.
May all sentient beings attain the body of the power of merit, so that those who behold it may receive benefit and remain far removed from all evils.
May all sentient beings attain the body of the place of non-reliance, so that they may all be fully endowed with the wisdom of non-attachment.
May all sentient beings attain the body of being gathered by the Buddhas, so that they are always protected by the empowerment of all Buddhas. May all sentient beings attain...
May all sentient beings universally benefit others; may their bodies be able to enter all paths;
may all sentient beings attain a body that manifests everywhere and universally illuminate and manifest all Buddha-dharmas;
may all sentient beings attain a body of perfected diligence, single-mindedly and assiduously cultivating the wisdom-practices of the Mahāyāna; and may all sentient beings be free from pride.
I dedicate this offering so that all sentient beings may attain a body of supreme purity and wisdom, forever dwelling in unshakable composure;
I pray that all sentient beings may achieve firm conduct and accomplish the Mahāyāna karma of omniscience;

I pray that all sentient beings may attain the body of the Buddha’s family and be eternally free from all birth and death in the mundane world. This is the excellence of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva when giving his own body and bones.
The dedication of the faculties is for the sake of causing sentient beings to attain all-knowledge and achieve ultimate purity.
[Treatise] Forty: Giving the Skin.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees someone come with a sharp knife in hand, begging for the skin of his body...
A joy arises in his heart and all his faculties are gladdened, just as if someone were to bestow a great favor upon him.
He welcomes and receives them, prepares a seat for them to sit upon, and bows with reverence, thinking: "This beggar is most rare to encounter;
he has come to seek alms because he wishes to fulfill my vow for omniscience. He seeks to benefit me; therefore, I shall greet him with a joyful and serene countenance."
And he said to him: "I now relinquish this body of mine entirely; whoever requires my skin may take it as they please.

This is no different from the Bodhisattva Viśuddhagarbha, the Bodhisattva Suvarṇapārśvamṛgarāja, and other immeasurable great bodhisattvas of the past. Thus did the Bodhisattva at that time dedicate his roots of goodness.
That is to say: may all sentient beings obtain skin so subtle that it is like the physical marks of a Tathāgata, pure and clear, such that those who behold it never tire;
may all sentient beings obtain indestructible skin, like a vajra, which nothing can destroy;
may all sentient beings obtain golden skin, like the supreme and wondrous Jāmbūnada gold, pure, bright, and clean.
May all sentient beings obtain skin of immeasurable colors, manifesting pure hues according to their mental inclinations;
may all sentient beings obtain pure and wondrous skin, fully endowed with the excellent, soft, and pure physical marks of a Tathāgata;
may all sentient beings obtain the foremost skin, its self-nature being a pure physical mark beyond compare.
May all sentient beings achieve the pure skin-color of a Tathāgata, adorned with all the marks and signs;
may all sentient beings obtain exquisite skin that emits great light, universally illuminating all;
may all sentient beings obtain a skin like a net of light, emitting unspeakably many perfect radiances like a lofty banner in the world. May all [sentient beings]...
Sentient beings obtain a moistened complexion and skin, and all their physical marks become entirely pure;

this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his own skin, for the purpose of causing all sentient beings to attain all adorned and pure Buddha-fields and to be fully endowed with the great merits of a Tathāgata.
[Treatise] Forty-first: Giving the Fingers of the Hands and Feet.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives his fingers of the hands and feet to those who beg for them, just as the Bodhisattva Firm Diligence (Dṛḍhavīrya), the Bodhisattva Sovereign King of Jambudvīpa (Jambudvīpeśvararāja), and other immeasurable great Bodhisattvas did.
At that time, his countenance was serene and joyful, his mind peaceful and virtuous, free from all inversion. Riding upon the Mahāyāna, he sought neither sensual desires nor fame;
he gave rise solely to the vast intention of a bodhisattva, remaining far removed from all stains of stinginess and envy.
With single-minded devotion toward the unsurpassed, wondrous Dharma of the Tathāgata, the Buddha-son, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva thus practiced giving.
At that time, he gathered all roots of goodness and dedicated them all with this vow: "May all sentient beings obtain fingers that are slender and long, no different from those of a Buddha;
may all sentient beings obtain fingers that are straight and round, with the upper and lower joints in perfect proportion;
may all sentient beings obtain fingernails of red copper, their nails raised high, pure and translucent. May all sentient beings obtain one... [further vow].
May all sentient beings obtain fingers like those of the Supreme Man of All-Knowledge, capable of grasping and upholding all dharmas;
may all sentient beings obtain the mark of well-proportioned fingers, fully endowed with the ten powers;
may all sentient beings obtain the mark of fingers like a wheel, with joints perfectly rounded and lines spiraling to the right.
May all sentient beings obtain fingers marked with the thousand-spoked wheel and the svastika, like a lotus, adorned with the marks and signs resulting from the karma of the ten powers;
may all sentient beings obtain fingers that are a treasury of light, emitting great radiance that illuminates unspeakably many Buddha-worlds;
may all sentient beings obtain well-arranged fingers, skillfully distributed and complete with webbed membranes—this is called Bodhi.
When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gave his finger as a gift, he dedicated the roots of goodness for the purpose of causing all sentient beings to attain purity of mind.
[Treatise] Forty-second: Giving the fingernails along with the flesh.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva requests the Dharma, if someone should say, "If you can give me your fingernails along with the flesh, I shall give you the Dharma," the Bodhisattva should reply, "Simply give me the Dharma;
as for the fingernails with the flesh, take them as you please. This is as in the case of the Bodhisattva Sovereign King Seeking the Dharma, the Bodhisattva Inexhaustible, and countless others.

For the sake of seeking the Dharma, these great bodhisattvas—desiring to reveal, expound, and benefit all sentient beings with the True Dharma so that they may all attain fulfillment—give their flesh-and-nail-clad fingernails to those who beg for them.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way: "May all sentient beings attain the [qualities] of all Buddhas."
May all sentient beings obtain copper-colored nails; may they be adorned with the secondary mark of moist and lustrous nails;
may all sentient beings obtain light-pure nails that are most penetrating;
may all sentient beings obtain all-knowing nails, endowed with the marks of a Great Man; may all sentient beings obtain incomparable nails that are unstained by any world.
May all sentient beings attain the light of wonderfully adorned nails that universally illumines all worlds;
may all sentient beings attain indestructible nails that are pure and without flaw;
may all sentient beings attain the nails of the skillful means and marks of entry into all Buddha-dharmas, with vast wisdom that is entirely pure; may all sentient beings...
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Attaining the Pure and Wondrous Nails of Good Birth, whose karmic fruits are entirely pure and wondrous,
vows that all sentient beings may obtain the nails of the Great Guide of All-Knowledge and emit a treasury of immeasurable colors of sublime light.

This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his fingernails together with the flesh for the sake of seeking the Dharma, so as to cause sentient beings to be fully endowed [with these qualities].
Because of the unimpeded power of the fingernails of the all-knowing wisdom of all Buddhas.
[Treatise] Forty-third: Casting oneself into a fire pit for the sake of seeking the Dharma.
[Sūtra] Sons of the Buddha, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, seeking the treasury of the Buddha-Dharma, honor and respect it, conceiving the thought that it is difficult to encounter.
There was a teacher who came and said to him, "If you can cast yourself into a fire-pit seven fathoms deep, I shall bestow the Dharma upon you.
Upon hearing this, the Bodhisattva was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; he reflected:

"For the sake of the Dharma, I should endure immeasurable suffering even while dwelling for a long time in all the evil realms such as the Avīci hell; how much more so when it is merely entering a fire-pit in the human world?"
He immediately heard the Dharma. "How marvelous! This True Dharma is so very easy to obtain. One shall not undergo the immeasurable agonies of the hells;
merely by entering a fire pit, one can hear it. For my sake alone, enter the fire pit!
Thus did King Bodhisattva and Vajracitta Bodhisattva enter the fire pit for the sake of seeking the Dharma. It was thus, O Bodhisattva, that he entered.

At that time, he dedicated these roots of goodness in this way: namely, may all sentient beings abide in the dwelling of the Buddhas, the dharma of omniscience, and never regress from unsurpassed bodhi;

may all sentient beings be free from all perils and hardships and receive the peace and bliss of the Buddhas; may all sentient beings attain a fearless mind and be liberated from all terrors. May one...
May all sentient beings always joyfully seek the Dharma and be fully endowed with the joy and delight of the adornments of all dharmas.
May all sentient beings be free from all evil destinies and extinguish the blazing fires of the three poisons.

May all sentient beings constantly attain peace and happiness, being fully endowed with the supreme and wondrous bliss of the Tathāgata. May all sentient beings attain the bodhicitta and forever be free from...

May all beings be completely extinguished from the fires of greed, anger, and delusion; may they all attain the bliss of the various bodhisattva samādhis and universally behold all Buddhas with great joy in their hearts.
May all beings skillfully expound the True Dharma, reaching its ultimate depths and never forgetting it.
May all beings be fully endowed with the wondrous bliss of bodhisattva supernormal powers and abide in ultimate peace.
Abiding in all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*) is the dedication of roots of goodness when a bodhisattva mahāsattva throws himself into a pit of fire in search of the true Dharma,
for the purpose of causing sentient beings to leave behind obstructive karma and to fully attain the fire of wisdom.
[Treatise] Forty-fourth: For the sake of seeking the True Dharma, one undergoes immeasurable suffering and affliction with one’s own body.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, for the sake of seeking the True Dharma, analytically expounds and elucidates the Bodhisattva path, reveals the way to Bodhi, and proceeds toward supreme wisdom;
he diligently cultivates the mind of omniscience throughout the ten directions, extensively demonstrates it to all, and attains the unimpeded...
When obstructing the dharmas of wisdom so that sentient beings may dwell in purity within the bodhisattva realm,
diligently cultivating great wisdom and protecting the Buddha-bodhi, he experienced immeasurable suffering and affliction with his own body—
just as the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vīradhvaja and other immeasurable great bodhisattvas underwent immeasurable suffering for the sake of seeking the Dharma, even unto its total gathering.

Whatever sufferings such extremely wicked persons—who are shrouded by the evil karma of slandering the True Dharma and possessed by the deeds of Māra—ought to undergo, he undergoes them all for the sake of seeking the Dharma; and with these roots of goodness, he dedicates them in this way:
namely, "May all sentient beings forever be free from the oppression of all suffering and afflictions, and may they achieve peace and happiness."
May all sentient beings, through their sovereign spiritual powers and vows, forever leave behind all suffering and attain all happiness;
may all sentient beings forever extinguish the aggregates of suffering and illuminate their present bodies so that they constantly experience peace and joy;
may all sentient beings transcend the prison of suffering and accomplish wise conduct; and may all sentient beings behold the path of tranquility and depart from all evil realms.
May all sentient beings attain the joy of the Dharma and forever sever all suffering;

may all sentient beings eternally uproot all suffering and cherish one another with compassion, free from any intent to harm; may all sentient beings attain the bliss of all Buddhas and depart from the suffering of birth and death;
may all sentient beings achieve pure, incomparable peace and happiness, free from all afflictions and distress.
May no one be able to cause harm; may all sentient beings attain all supreme happiness, ultimately becoming fully endowed with the unimpeded bliss of the Buddhas—
this is the dedication of roots of goodness by Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas when undergoing various sufferings for the sake of seeking the Dharma,
desiring to rescue and protect all sentient beings so that they may leave behind perilous difficulties and abide in omniscience without obstruction.
Because it obstructs the state of liberation.

[Treatise] The forty-fifth: for the sake of seeking the Dharma—even for as little as a single word or a single phrase—one renounces their royal throne, kingdom, city, wife, children, and all possessions.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva occupies the throne of a king and seeks the True Dharma,

even if it be for the sake of a single word, a single letter, a single phrase, or a single meaning, they conceive the thought that such [Dharma] is difficult to obtain; they are able to completely relinquish everything within the seas—
whether near or far— including kingdoms, cities, towns, the populace, treasuries, gardens, ponds, houses, dwellings, groves, and flowers and fruits.
He was able to renounce everything— precious deposits, exquisite objects, palaces, towers, wives, children, kinsmen, and even his royal throne—
and sought the firm Dharma within that which is not firm. Desiring to benefit all sentient beings,
he diligently pursued the path of the Buddhas’ unimpeded liberation and ultimate purity of omniscience, like Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
The Bodhisattva King of Supreme Virtue and countless other great bodhisattvas diligently sought the true Dharma,
even to the extent of prostrating with their five limbs upon the ground for the sake of a single word; they mindfully contemplated all the Buddha-dharmas of the three periods of time,
joyfully practiced them, never craving fame or gain, and sought [the Dharma] by renouncing their sovereign royal positions in the world.
The Buddha, the Sovereign Dharma-King, has no attachment to the mind of worldly pleasure;
he nurtures his mind with supramundane dharmas, forever departing from all worldly conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), and abides in the non-proliferated dharma of all Buddhas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates all roots of goodness in this way, namely: "May all sentient beings always delight in [the supramundane]."
May all practice giving and relinquish everything; may all sentient beings be able to renounce all they possess without regret in their hearts;
may all sentient beings always seek the True Dharma, not begrudging their bodies, lives, or the necessities of life;
may all sentient beings fully obtain the benefits of the Dharma and be able to sever all doubts and delusions; may all sentient beings attain goodness.
May the mind that desires the Dharma always rejoice in the True Dharma of all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings, seeking the Buddha-Dharma, be able to relinquish body, life, and royal throne to practice the unsurpassed Bodhi with a great resolve;
may all sentient beings honor the True Dharma, always deeply loving and delighting in it without begrudging body or life; may all sentient beings protect and uphold all...
The Buddha is extremely difficult to encounter; one should always diligently cultivate the Dharma.
May all sentient beings attain the light of the Bodhi of all Buddhas and accomplish the practices for enlightenment, awakening through their own realization rather than by depending on others.

May all sentient beings be able to constantly contemplate all Buddha-dharmas, uproot the arrows of doubt, and attain peace and stability of mind. This is the practice of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva seeking [enlightenment].

When relinquishing his kingdom and city for the sake of the True Dharma, he dedicates his roots of goodness so that sentient beings may attain the perfection of knowledge and vision, and always abide upon the path of peace and security.
[Treatise] Forty-sixth: A Bodhisattva personally abandons the occupation of slaughter.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva acts as a great king with sovereign mastery over the Dharma, he universally carries out his commands to eliminate the karma of killing.
Within Jambudvīpa, in all cities, towns, and villages, he causes all slaughter to be strictly prohibited.
Toward all classes of living beings—whether footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed—he universally bestows fearlessness, possessing a heart free from deceit or plunder.

Extensively cultivating all the practices of a bodhisattva, he treats all beings with benevolence and does not inflict harm or affliction upon them; he establishes a wondrous jewel-like mind to bring peace and security to sentient beings.

In the presence of all Buddhas, he forms a profound aspiration and delight, constantly dwelling himself in the three kinds of pure precepts, and causes other sentient beings to likewise dwell therein.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva causes all sentient beings to abide in the five [precepts].
Through the precept of forever severing the karma of killing, one dedicates these roots of goodness as follows:
that is to say, may all sentient beings resolve upon the bodhicitta, be fully endowed with wisdom, and eternally preserve their life-span so that it has no end;
may all sentient beings abide for immeasurable kalpas, making offerings to all Buddhas, reverently and diligently practicing, and further increasing their life-span; may all...
May all sentient beings be fully endowed with the practice of the dharma that transcends old age and death, so that no calamities or poisons may harm their lives.
May all sentient beings be fully accomplished in a body free from illness and affliction, possessing mastery over their lifespan and able to abide therein at will.
May all sentient beings attain inexhaustible life, remaining throughout future kalpas to perform the bodhisattva practices of teaching, transforming, and subduing others.
May all sentient beings take all sentient beings as the gateway to longevity, so that the roots of goodness of the ten powers may increase therein;
may all sentient beings be fully endowed with roots of goodness, attain inexhaustible life, and fulfill their great vows;
may all sentient beings behold all Buddhas, make offerings to them, serve them, abide in inexhaustible life, and cultivate roots of goodness.
May all sentient beings, having well trained in what is to be learned under the Tathāgata, attain the joy of the noble Dharma and inexhaustible life;
may all sentient beings attain the life-faculty that is free from aging and illness, remaining eternally present, and enter the wisdom of the Buddha through courageous diligence—
this is the root of goodness of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva who, abiding in the three clusters of pure precepts, forever severs the karma of killing.
This dedication is for the purpose of causing sentient beings to attain the perfect wisdom of the ten powers of a Buddha.
[Treatise] The forty-seventh [case]: seeing those who are cruel and harming humans and animals, one rescues them with a compassionate heart—this refers to removing their male organs.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva sees sentient beings harboring cruelty, who damage the male organs of humans and animals,
causing their bodies to become deficient and making them undergo various forms of torment,
and having seen this, gives rise to great compassion and piteously rescues them, causing all the people of Jambudvīpa to abandon such karma— at that time, the Bodhisattva...
He said to that person: "What have you done to commit such evil karma? My storehouses are filled with hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of all manner of articles of enjoyment;
whatever you require, I shall provide it all to you. As for the various sins you have committed, they arose from yourself;
I now exhort you not to do such things again, for the actions you have performed are contrary to reason."
"Even if there were something gained, what use would it be? To harm others for one's own benefit—such a thing can never be.
Such evil conduct and all unwholesome dharmas are not praised by any Tathāgata.
Having spoken these words, he immediately gave away all his articles of pleasure as gifts, and further, with kind speech, he expounded the sublime Dharma to bring them joy.
That is to say, they demonstrate the teachings of tranquility so that others may believe and accept them, thereby eliminating unwholesome conduct and practicing pure deeds;
they give rise to mutual compassion and refrain from harming one another. When those people hear this, they forever abandon evil.
At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way: "May all sentient beings be endowed with the physical form of a great man and attain perfect accomplishment."
I pray that all sentient beings may possess the mark of the male organ concealed within the sheath, give rise to a courageous mind, and cultivate all pure conduct (*brahmacarya*).
I pray that all sentient beings may possess courageous power, always act as leaders, abide in unimpeded wisdom, and never regress.
I pray that all sentient beings may fully attain the body of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa*) and forever be free from the mind of desire.
May all sentient beings be free from attachment and fully achieve the Dharma-wisdom of a true son of noble family, praised by all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings universally possess the power of a Great Being and always be able to cultivate the roots of goodness of the Ten Powers;
and may all sentient beings never lose or destroy the physical form of a man.

Through the cultivation of merit and wisdom, by means of these unprecedented dharmas, may all sentient beings be without attachment or bondage amidst the five desires, and may their minds attain liberation;
may they grow weary of and renounce the three realms of existence, abiding in the bodhisattva practices.

May all sentient beings achieve the foremost wisdom of a great man (mahāpuruṣa), such that all honor, trust, and submit to their transformative influence. May all sentient beings be fully endowed with [these qualities].
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, a man of wisdom, shall before long achieve the state of the Unsurpassed Great Hero;
this is the dedication of roots of goodness for severing all causes that destroy the male form, so as to cause sentient beings to possess the male form,
to be able to protect all virtuous men, to be born into the families of sages and saints, and to be fully endowed with wisdom, constantly and diligently practicing.
Practicing the supreme conduct of a great man and possessing the utility of a great man, he is skillfully able to manifest the seven attributes of a great man:

he is fully endowed with the lineage of all Buddhas as a virtuous great man, the correct teaching of a great man, the valor of a great man, the diligence of a great man, and the wisdom of a great man;
being pure, he causes all sentient beings everywhere to ultimately attain them all.
[Treatise] Forty-eighth: When a Bodhisattva sees a Tathāgata appear in the world, they universally announce to sentient beings that they should abandon the play of pride and conceptual proliferation.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees a Tathāgata appear in the world and expound the True Dharma...
With a great voice, he universally proclaims to all that a Tathāgata has appeared in the world, that a Tathāgata has appeared in the world,
so that all sentient beings may hear the name of the Buddha, abandon all pride and conceptual proliferation, and further be exhorted to quickly see the Buddha,
to bring the Buddha to mind, to turn toward the Buddha, to take the Buddha as their object of focus, to contemplate the Buddha, and to praise the Buddha.
Furthermore, he extensively explained that a Buddha is difficult to encounter, appearing only once in ten million billion kalpas;
that sentient beings, by virtue of this, come to see the Buddha and give rise to pure faith, leaping for joy with exultation, and respectfully making offerings;
and that, having heard the names of various Buddhas at the Buddha’s place, they further encounter countless other Buddhas, planting roots of goodness and cultivating them until they increase.
At that time, because they had seen the Buddha, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of sentient beings all attained purity and ultimate subduing.
Those sentient beings all conceived the thought of the Bodhisattva as their supreme spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*);
by means of the Bodhisattva, they accomplished the Buddha-dharma, universally throughout the world, through the roots of goodness planted over countless eons.

While performing these Buddha-activities, the Buddha-sons, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, reveal them to sentient beings so that when they behold the Buddhas, they may dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:

"May all sentient beings, without waiting for exhortation or inducement, go of their own accord to see the Buddhas, serve and make offerings to them, and cause them all to rejoice; may all sentient beings always delight in seeing the Buddhas."
May their minds never abandon [their resolve], and may all sentient beings constantly and diligently cultivate vast wisdom, upholding the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas.
May all sentient beings awaken to the Buddha-dharma upon hearing any sound;
may they practice the bodhisattva path for immeasurable eons; and may all sentient beings abide in right mindfulness, always seeing with the eye of wisdom.
May all sentient beings, upon the appearance of a Buddha, not think of other activities but constantly remember and behold the Buddha, diligently cultivating the ten powers;
may all sentient beings everywhere always see all Buddhas and fully comprehend that the Tathāgata pervades the realm of empty space;
may all sentient beings attain the sovereign body of a Buddha and universally achieve enlightenment throughout the ten directions.
When preaching the Dharma, they vow that all sentient beings may encounter spiritual friends and constantly hear the Buddha-dharma, attaining indestructible faith in all Tathāgatas;
they vow that all sentient beings may be able to praise the appearance of the Buddhas in the world, causing all who see them to attain universal purity.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas praise the appearance of the Buddhas in the world.
To cause sentient beings to see all Buddhas and to make offerings to and serve them, so that they may ultimately attain purity in the unsurpassed Dharma.
[Treatise] The forty-ninth: Abandoning the Great Earth.
[Sūtra] O Sons of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas relinquish the great earth and give it as a gift to the Buddhas to construct vihāras;
or they give it for the use of Bodhisattvas and spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) according to their wishes; or they give it to the Saṃgha to serve as a dwelling place;
or they give it to their parents; or they give it to individuals, Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and various fields of merit (puṇyakṣetra), even unto all beings.
To the poor, the orphaned, the destitute, and the other four assemblies, he gives according to their wishes so that they lack for nothing;
or he may construct stūpas and temples for the Tathāgata, providing in all such places the necessary provisions and utensils so that they may use them as they please without fear.
In whichever direction the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva bestows land, [he acts in this manner].

At that time, one dedicates all roots of goodness in this way: namely, the vow that all sentient beings may be fully endowed with the ground of pure omniscience and reach the further shore of all practices of Samantabhadra;

that all sentient beings may attain the ground of dhāraṇī and correctly maintain all Buddha-dharmas through right mindfulness; and that all sentient beings may abide in the power of upholding [the Dharma] and always be able to...
May they protect all the Buddha-teachings; may all sentient beings attain a mind like the earth, always pure in their intentions toward all beings and free from evil thoughts.

May all sentient beings uphold the seeds of all Buddhas and accomplish the successive stages of the bodhisattva grounds without interruption. May all sentient beings universally bring peace and security to all.

May all beings be tamed in every situation and abide in the path of purity; may they share with all Tathāgatas in benefiting the world, universally and diligently cultivating themselves to dwell securely in the power of the Buddhas.
May all beings be universally beloved by the world, and may they all be established in the unsurpassed bliss of the Buddhas. May all beings attain skillful means.
Abiding within the dharmas of the Buddha’s powers and fearlessnesses, he vows that all sentient beings may attain earth-like wisdom and sovereign mastery in the practice of all Buddha-dharmas.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives the great earth,
for the purpose of causing all sentient beings to fully attain the pure stages of all Tathāgatas.
[Treatise] The fiftieth: Giving away servants.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives servants as offerings to all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and true spiritual friends;
or he gives them to the Sangha Jewel; or he presents them to his parents and other supreme fields of merit; or else he bestows them upon others.
They cause suffering beings to have no lack so that their lives may be sustained;
or they give to the poor, the orphaned, the destitute, and all others who have no one to care for them; or they act as guardians of the Tathāgata’s stūpas and temples;
or they transcribe and uphold the True Dharma of the Buddhas, providing at all times hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of servants, giving those servants whatever is required.
May they all be wise and skillful, naturally disciplined and compliant, always diligent and energetic without indolence;
may they possess a mind of integrity, a mind of peace and happiness, a mind of benefit, a mind of benevolence, a mind of reverence, a mind free from resentment, and a mind free from enmity;
and may they be able to act for the benefit of others in whatever ways are appropriate to the customs and conditions of those various places. Furthermore, may they all...
Through the power of the pure karma of the Bodhisattva, they attain mastery in all capacities, skills, arts, and mathematics;
they are highly proficient in serving others and gladdening their hearts. At that time, the Bodhisattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings attain a mind of harmony and discipline; may they cultivate roots of goodness in the presence of all Buddhas. May one... [dedicate them] thus.
May all sentient beings, in accordance with their inclinations, make offerings to all Buddhas; may they be able to hear and receive all that is taught by the Buddhas.
May all sentient beings obtain the Buddhas' acceptance and constantly contemplate the Tathāgata without any other thoughts.
May all sentient beings never allow the lineage of the Buddhas to perish, diligently cultivating all roots of goodness that accord with the Buddhas. May all sentient beings always be diligent...
May the offerings made to all Buddhas never be in vain; may all sentient beings uphold the sublime meanings and words of all Buddhas, traveling with pure conduct and fearlessness;

may all sentient beings always delight in seeing the Buddhas, their hearts never weary of it, and at the abodes of the Buddhas, they do not begrudge even their own bodies or lives; may all sentient beings attain the vision of all [the Buddhas].

The Buddha-mind is free from defilement and attachment, transcending all worldly dependencies; may all sentient beings take refuge solely in the Buddha and forever leave behind all false objects of refuge.
May all sentient beings follow the path of the Buddha, their minds always joyfully contemplating the unsurpassed Buddha-dharma.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives servants and attendants, in order to—
Because sentient beings distance themselves from dust and defilement, purify the Buddha-ground, and are able to manifest the sovereign body of a Tathāgata.
[Treatise] The fifty-first: relinquishing one's own body to give it to all sentient beings, being humble and free from pride.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his own body to those who come to beg, at the time of giving he generates a mind of humility;
he generates a mind like the earth; he generates a mind that endures all sufferings without fluctuation; he generates a mind of service toward sentient beings without weariness;
and he generates a mind toward all sentient beings like that of a compassionate mother, such that all his roots of goodness—

They dedicate these roots of goodness by generating a mind that universally forgives all manner of injuries inflicted by foolish, treacherous, and extremely wicked sentient beings, remaining settled in roots of goodness and diligently attending to Bodhisattvas. At that time, they dedicate their roots of goodness in this way:
"May all sentient beings never lack anything according to their needs as they constantly cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva."
Without interruption or abandonment, they fulfill all the aims and benefits of a bodhisattva;
they dwell securely on the path practiced by bodhisattvas, thoroughly comprehend the equal dharma-nature of bodhisattvas, and attain inclusion within the lineage of the Tathāgatas.

Abiding in truthful speech and maintaining the conduct of a bodhisattva, they cause all worlds to purify the Buddha-dharma through profound faith and understanding, and lead them to realize the ultimate perfection of the Dharma.
May all sentient beings give birth to pure and superior roots of goodness, abide in great merit, and possess all-knowledge.

Furthermore, by means of these roots of goodness, may they always provide offerings to all Buddhas, understand all dharmas, receive, uphold, read, and recite them without forgetting, losing, destroying, or dispersing them; and with minds well-tamed, may they tame those who are untamed.
They discipline them by means of the dharma of tranquility, causing those sentient beings to abide in such matters before the Buddhas.
Furthermore, by means of these roots of goodness, they cause all sentient beings to become the foremost reliquaries (stūpas), worthy of receiving various offerings from the world;
they cause all sentient beings to become the supreme field of merit and to attain the wisdom of a Buddha, achieving awakening.
May I cause all sentient beings to become supreme recipients, universally able to benefit all sentient beings;
may I cause all sentient beings to achieve the most excellent welfare and benefit; may I cause all sentient beings to be fully endowed with all roots of goodness;
may I cause all sentient beings to become the foremost field of merit for giving; may I cause them to obtain immeasurable rewards of merit; may I cause all sentient beings...
Born within the three realms, they all attain liberation; they act as the supreme guides for all sentient beings, able to show the world the path of reality as it is;
they cause all sentient beings to obtain sublime *dhāraṇī*, fully upholding the true Dharma of all Buddhas;
and they cause all sentient beings to realize the immeasurable, foremost *dharmadhātu*, being fully endowed with emptiness.

The unimpeded right path of emptiness is the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s dedication of his own roots of goodness by means of a "turning of the body," in order to cause all sentient beings to attain the immeasurable wisdom-body of one worthy of offerings. Therefore, O Son of the Buddha,
when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva hears the Dharma with joy and gives rise to pure faith, he is able to offer his very body to all Buddhas, delighting in and faithfully understanding it.
Regarding the unsurpassed Dharma-treasure, they conceive of all Buddhas as their parents; they read, recite, receive, and uphold the Dharma of the unobstructed path;
they universally enter the great treasure of wisdom—the countless *nayuta* gates of Dharma and all doors of roots of goodness; their minds constantly remember immeasurable Buddhas;
they enter the realm of the Buddhas and profoundly penetrate its principles and meanings; and they are able to [employ] the subtle and secret Brahma-voice of the Tathāgata.

Raising the clouds of the Buddha-dharma and raining down the rain of the Buddha-dharma, they are valiant and sovereign, able to analytically expound the foremost stage of those who possess all-knowledge (*sarvajña*).
Fully accomplishing the vehicle of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-yāna*), their faculties are brought to perfection through immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayutas* of great dharmas.
O Son of the Buddha, these Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas hear [the teachings] from the presence of the Buddhas as follows...
Rejoicing in this Dharma immeasurably, they dwell securely in the True Dharma; they sever their own doubts and cause others to sever theirs as well.

Their minds are perpetually serene and joyful, their merits are perfected, and their roots of goodness are complete. Their intention is constant and continuous, benefiting sentient beings with a mind that never falters.
They attain supreme wisdom, become Vajragarbhas, draw near to all Buddhas, purify all Buddha-fields, and are ever diligent.
Making offerings to all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas, one then dedicates these roots of goodness in this way:
namely, may all sentient beings attain the most supreme body, perfected and embraced by all Buddhas;
may all sentient beings always remain near the Buddhas, dwell in reliance upon the Buddhas, and constantly behold them with reverence, never ceasing.
May all sentient beings be far removed from [defilements] and attain a pure, indestructible body, fully endowed with all merits and wisdom;
may all sentient beings constantly and diligently make offerings to all Buddhas and practice the ultimate Brahma-conduct of non-apprehension;
may all sentient beings attain a selfless body and be free from the notions of "I" and "mine. May all...
May all sentient beings be able to manifest bodies throughout the lands of the ten directions like reflections appearing, yet without coming or going;
may all sentient beings attain bodies of mastery, traveling everywhere throughout the ten directions, free from self and free from grasping;
may all sentient beings be born from the body of the Buddha, dwelling within the supreme, non-abiding household of the Tathāgata; may all sentient beings attain the power of the Dharma.
May all sentient beings attain an incomparable body, a body of great power of patience that cannot be destroyed by any;
may they achieve the Tathāgata’s pure Dharma-body and give birth to a body of supramundane merit within the pure Dharma-realm of non-apprehension.
This is the root of goodness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva who offers their own body to the Buddha.
They dedicate [their merit] so that sentient beings may dwell forever in the family of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.

O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives their own body as a gift to all sentient beings, desiring to cause them universally to accomplish roots of goodness and to bring to mind those roots of goodness.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva vows that their own body shall become a great bright lamp, capable of illuminating everything.

Sentient beings are like various articles of pleasure, for they are universally able to provide for all sentient beings; sentient beings are like a treasury of the sublime Dharma, for they are universally able to sustain all sentient beings;
sentient beings are like pure radiance, for they are universally able to enlighten all sentient beings;

sentient beings are like the light and shadow of the world, for they cause all sentient beings to always behold them; sentient beings are the causes and conditions for roots of goodness, for they cause all sentient beings to always...
May they encounter true spiritual friends who guide and instruct all sentient beings; may they become level paths for all sentient beings to tread upon;
may they possess unsurpassed, perfect peace and happiness for all sentient beings to be free from suffering and purified;
and may they be like bright, pure suns, universally bringing impartial benefit to the world.
At all times, he dedicates his roots of goodness in this way: that is to say, he vows that all sentient beings may always draw near to the Buddhas and enter the ground of Buddha-wisdom;
that all sentient beings may attain conforming wisdom and abide in unsurpassed enlightenment;
that all sentient beings may always dwell within the assemblies of Buddhas with minds well-tamed; and that all sentient beings may have their conduct...
May they possess the majestic deportment of a Buddha; may all sentient beings fully attain nirvana; may all sentient beings deeply understand the meaning of the Dharma;

may all sentient beings be endowed with the practice of contentment and be born into the family of the Tathāgata; may all sentient beings abandon ignorance and desire, and abide in the aspiration and joy of the Buddha;
may all sentient beings give birth to supreme roots of goodness and sit beneath the Bodhi tree. May all...
To slay the thieves of affliction within sentient beings, to abandon thoughts of enmity and harm, and to vow that all sentient beings shall fully possess and maintain all Buddha-dharmas—
this is the dedication of roots of goodness when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives his own body as a gift to all sentient beings;
it is for the purpose of benefiting all sentient beings and causing them to attain the state of unsurpassed peace and security.
[Treatise] The fifty-second [practice]: Offering one’s own body to serve all Buddhas.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva personally serves all Buddhas with his own body;

in the presence of all Buddhas, he reflects upon their profound kindness and seeks to repay it, regarding the Tathāgatas as his parents, giving rise to deep faith and joy toward them with a pure mind.
Protecting the Buddha’s bodhi, abiding in all Buddha-dharmas, being free from worldly conceptions, being born into the family of the Tathāgatas,
following in the footsteps of all Buddhas, departing from the realm of Māra, thoroughly understanding all that is practiced by the Buddhas, and becoming a vessel for accomplishing all Buddha-dharmas—
the Bodhisattva at that time dedicates these roots of goodness in this way, namely: "May all sentient beings obtain..."
May they adorn themselves with the jewel of the pure mind of omniscience; may all sentient beings abide in excellent self-mastery and remain far removed from all unwholesome karma;

may all sentient beings obtain indestructible and steadfast retinues and be universally able to uphold the true Dharma of all Buddhas; may all sentient beings become disciples of the Buddha and reach [the goal].
May all sentient beings, at the stage of the Bodhisattva’s consecration, be constantly sustained by all Buddhas and forever leave behind all unwholesome dharmas;
may all sentient beings follow the Buddhas and practice the most supreme dharma of a bodhisattva;
may all sentient beings enter the realm of the Buddhas and all attain the bestowal of omniscience.
I vow that all sentient beings shall be entirely equal to all Tathāgatas, and that there be no Buddha-dharma in which they do not attain mastery.
I vow that all sentient beings shall be gathered and sustained by all Buddhas, and that they may always practice deeds free from attachment.
I vow that all sentient beings shall always serve as the foremost attendants of all Buddhas in all their assemblies.
Cultivating the practice of wisdom is the dedication of roots of goodness by which a bodhisattva mahāsattva serves all Buddhas;
it is for the sake of realizing the bodhi of all Buddhas, for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings, for the sake of transcending all three realms,
for the sake of accomplishing a mind free from affliction, and for the sake of attaining immeasurable and vast bodhi.
It is because they wish to achieve the wisdom that illuminates the Buddha-dharma; because they wish to be constantly sustained by the protection of all Buddhas;
because they wish to obtain the guardianship and support of all Buddhas; because they wish to have faith and understanding in all Buddha-dharmas;

because they wish to accomplish roots of goodness equal to those of the Buddhas of the three periods of time; and because they wish to fulfill a mind free from regret and realize all the qualities of a Buddha.
[Treatise] The fifty-third [topic]: The giving of land, all manner of goods, and the relinquishing of worldly affairs.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is able to give away kingdoms, all manner of goods, and even royal thrones;
he completely relinquishes all worldly affairs, attaining mastery of mind, free from attachment, unbound, and without any lingering craving.

They remain far removed from evil karma and bring great benefit to sentient beings; they do not cling to the fruits of karma, take no pleasure in worldly dharmas, and no longer crave or become defiled by any place of birth.
Although they dwell in the world, their minds do not arise from this place, nor do they harbor attachment to the phenomena of the aggregates, elements, or sense bases.
Their minds have no point of reliance upon internal or external phenomena, and they never forget or depart from the practices of all bodhisattvas.
All spiritual friends uphold the vast practices and vows of bodhisattvas and always delight in serving all virtuous friends.
At that time, a bodhisattva dedicates these roots of goodness in this way, namely:
"May all sentient beings become great Dharma Kings, attaining mastery over the Dharma and reaching the further shore; may all sentient beings become Buddhas, the Kings of Dharma."
May all afflictions and hostile thieves be utterly destroyed; may all sentient beings abide in the sovereign rank of the Buddha and attain the wisdom of the Tathāgata to expound the Buddha-dharma;
may all sentient beings abide in the realm of the Buddha and be able to turn the unsurpassed, sovereign wheel of Dharma;
may all sentient beings be born into the family of the Tathāgata, attaining mastery over the Dharma and eternally protecting and upholding the lineage of the Buddhas.

May they ensure that [the lineage] is never severed; may all sentient beings be revealed and taught the immeasurable True Dharma of the Dharma King, and may they accomplish the state of boundless great Bodhisattvas.
May all sentient beings dwell in the pure Dharma-realm as Great Dharma Kings, manifesting the appearance of Buddhas appearing in the world in continuous succession.
May all sentient beings become Kings of Wisdom in all worlds to transform and guide [beings].

May I never for a moment abandon all living beings; may all sentient beings universally become donors of the Dharma for all beings throughout the worlds of the Dharma-realm and the space-realm, causing them all to dwell securely in the Mahāyāna.
May all sentient beings attain the status of sovereigns of all perfected virtues, equal to the roots of goodness of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
This is the dedication of roots of goodness from a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s gift of his royal throne,
intended to cause all sentient beings to ultimately abide in a state of peace and security.
[Treatise] Fifty-four: Relinquishing the capital city, the frontier passes, and the collected taxes.

[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva sees someone come to beg for the king’s magnificent and grand capital city, as well as all the taxes collected at the frontier passes, he gives them all away without any stinginess in his heart, directing himself solely toward Bodhi.
They give rise to great vows, abide in great loving-kindness, and practice great compassion; their minds are joyful as they benefit sentient beings.
Through vast wisdom, they understand profound dharmas and dwell securely in the equal dharma-nature of all Buddhas.
They resolve their minds for the sake of seeking omniscience, because they give rise to deep delight in the dharma of mastery and seek to realize sovereign wisdom.
Because they have purified all merits, because they abide in firm and vast wisdom, because they have extensively gathered all roots of goodness,
because they practice the vows for all Buddha-dharmas, because they have spontaneously awakened to the dharma of great wisdom,
because they dwell securely in the bodhicitta without regression, and because they cultivate all bodhisattva practices and vows for the sake of the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).
They practice giving for the sake of ultimate perfection, and dedicate these roots of goodness in this way:
that is to say, they vow that all sentient beings may fully adorn and purify immeasurable buddha-fields to offer as dwelling places for all Buddhas;
they vow that all sentient beings may always joyfully dwell in forest hermitages (āraṇya), remaining in tranquility and immovability; they vow that all sentient beings...
May they be born never relying on royal capitals or villages, but delighting in tranquility and forever attaining the ultimate.
May all sentient beings never take pleasure in or be attached to any worldly realm, and always delight in remaining far removed from worldly speech.
May all sentient beings attain freedom from a greedy mind, giving away all that they possess without any regret in their hearts. May all sentient beings...
May they develop a mind of renunciation and abandon all household affairs; may all sentient beings attain a mind free from stinginess and constantly practice generous giving;
may all sentient beings attain a mind free from attachment and leave behind the ways of household life;
may all sentient beings be freed from all suffering and eliminate all calamities, misfortunes, and fears; may all sentient beings adorn and purify the ten directions.
To offer all worlds to the Buddhas is the dedication of the roots of goodness of a bodhisattva mahāsattva’s gift of a royal capital,
for the sake of enabling all sentient beings to completely adorn and purify all Buddha-fields.
Combined Commentary on the New Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, Fascicle Forty-seven.
