Chapter Twenty-five, Part Ten: The Ten Dedications.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva generates respect for those roots of goodness, complies with them, and accepts them with patience, he attains ultimate joy and firm resolve.

He himself abides securely and causes others to abide securely; through diligent cultivation of non-attachment and mastery, he accumulates and perfects the superior aspiration for dwelling in the sphere of the Tathāgata. His power increases until he fully knows all.
One should see that all roots of goodness are dedicated in this way: namely, by means of a mind of non-attachment, non-binding, and liberation, one accomplishes the physical karma of Samantabhadra;
by means of a mind of non-attachment, non-binding, and liberation, one purifies the verbal karma of Samantabhadra;
and by means of a mind of non-attachment, non-binding, and liberation, one fulfills the mental karma of Samantabhadra. Through this mind of non-attachment, non-binding, and liberation...

With a mind that gives rise to the vast and great diligence of Samantabhadra, they are endowed with the *dhāraṇī* gate of Samantabhadra’s unimpeded voice through a mind of non-attachment, non-binding, and liberation; its sound is vast and universally pervades the ten directions.
With a mind of non-attachment, non-binding, and liberation, they are endowed with the *dhāraṇī* gate of Samantabhadra’s vision of all Buddhas, constantly beholding the ten [directions].

Just as all Buddhas, with a mind of liberation that is unattached and unbound, have accomplished the *dhāraṇī* gate of understanding all sounds and preach immeasurable teachings in all voices; and just as they, with a mind of liberation that is unattached and unbound,
have accomplished the *dhāraṇī* gate of Samantabhadra’s dwelling through all eons and cultivate the bodhisattva path throughout the ten directions— so too [should one do].
By means of a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, one accomplishes the sovereign power of Samantabhadra;
within the body of a single sentient being, one manifests the cultivation of all bodhisattva practices throughout all future eons without interruption.
As it is with the body of one sentient being, so it is with the bodies of all sentient beings; thus, by means of a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, one achieves [this].
By means of the sovereign power of Samantabhadra, universally entering all assemblies of bodhimandas and appearing before all Buddhas to cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva,
one achieves the sovereign power of the Buddha Samantabhadra through a mind of liberation that is unattached and unbound;
within a single gateway, one manifests for unspeakably unspeakable eons without end, causing each—
May all sentient beings attain entry through the mind of liberation— unattached and unbound— and achieve the sovereign power of Samantabhadra Buddha;
may they manifest within various gateways throughout unspeakably unspeakable eons without end,
causing all sentient beings to attain entry, and may their bodies appear universally before all Buddhas.
With a mind of non-attachment, non-bondage, and liberation, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra;
in every thought-moment, they cause unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings to abide in the wisdom of the ten powers with minds free from weariness.
With a mind of non-attachment, non-bondage, and liberation, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra and manifest all Buddhas within the bodies of all sentient beings.
Through sovereign supernormal powers, they cause all sentient beings to abide in the conduct of Samantabhadra; with a mind of liberation that is unattached and unbound,
they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra, producing the speech of all sentient beings within the speech of each individual sentient being,
causing every single sentient being to abide upon the ground of omniscience through non-attachment.
With a mind liberated from bondage, they achieve the sovereign power of Samantabhadra;
within the body of each and every sentient being, they universally accommodate the bodies of all sentient beings, causing them all to perceive themselves as having achieved the Buddha-body.
With a mind liberated from attachment and bondage, they achieve the sovereign power of Samantabhadra, such that they can adorn all worlds throughout the ten directions with a single flower.
With a mind of non-attachment, non-binding, and liberation, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra and emit great sounds that pervade the entire Dharma-realm,
reaching all Buddha-lands to gather in and subdue all sentient beings;
with a mind of non-attachment, non-binding, and liberation, they accomplish the sovereign power of Samantabhadra throughout the limits of the future.
One can say that throughout expressible and inexpressible eons, within every single thought-moment, they are able to universally enter all worlds;
by the Buddha’s spiritual power, they adorn them according to their thoughts, and with a mind of liberation— unattached and unbound— they achieve the sovereign power of Samantabhadra,
constantly able to universally enter all worlds throughout all eons remaining until the end of the future, manifesting their attainment of enlightenment.
The Buddha appears in the world and, with a mind of liberation free from attachment and bondage, accomplishes the practices of Samantabhadra;

with a single light he universally illumines all worlds throughout the entirety of space, and with a mind of liberation free from attachment and bondage, he accomplishes the practices of Samantabhadra,
attains immeasurable wisdom, possesses all supernatural powers, and expounds various teachings through a mind free from attachment and bondage.
With a mind of liberation, they accomplish the conduct of Samantabhadra and enter the Tathāgata’s immeasurable supernatural wisdom that exhausts all kalpas;
with a mind of liberation, unattached and unbound, they accomplish the conduct of Samantabhadra and abide as the source of all Tathāgatas throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
Thus, through the Buddha’s spiritual power, they cultivate all bodhisattva practices, and their physical, verbal, and mental karma—never...
Without weariness, with a mind of non-attachment, non-binding, and liberation, one accomplishes the conduct of Samantabhadra;
not contradicting the meaning and not destroying the Dharma, with pure speech and inexhaustible eloquence,
one teaches and tames all sentient beings so that they may attain the unexcelled Bodhi of all Buddhas, practicing with a mind of non-attachment, non-binding, and liberation.
When Samantabhadra’s practice enters a single dharma-gate, it emits immeasurable light that illumines inconceivable dharma-gates;
as it is with one dharma-gate, so it is with all dharma-gates. Thus penetrating them all without obstruction, one shall ultimately attain the stage of omniscience.
With a mind liberated from attachment and bondage, one abides in the bodhisattva practices and attains mastery over all dharmas.
Having reached the other shore of Samantabhadra’s adornments, one observes and enters into every single realm with all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*),
yet all-knowledge remains inexhaustible. With a mind liberated from attachment and bondage, beginning from this very life until the end of the future,
one dwells in the conduct of Samantabhadra without ever ceasing, attaining all-knowledge and awakening to it.
One may speak of, or not speak of, the true Dharma; yet regarding all phenomena, one is ultimately free from delusion.
With a mind liberated through non-attachment and non-binding, one cultivates the practices of Samantabhadra with mastery in skillful means, attaining the radiance of the Dharma.
One clearly and unimpededly illuminates all the deeds performed by Bodhisattvas, cultivating the conduct of Samantabhadra with a mind liberated through non-attachment and non-binding.
They attain the wisdom of all skillful means, knowing all skillful means— namely, immeasurable skillful means, inconceivable skillful means,
the skillful means of bodhisattvas, the skillful means of omniscience, the skillful means for the discipline of all bodhisattvas,
the skillful means for turning the immeasurable wheel of Dharma, the skillful means of unspeakable timing, and the boundless skillful means of teaching various dharmas.
The Treasury of Fearlessness at the Limit explains all dharmas through skillful means without exception; by means of a mind liberated from attachment and bondage,
one abides in the conduct of Samantabhadra, accomplishing the body-karma so that all sentient beings who see it rejoice,
do not give rise to slander, and resolve their minds on Bodhi, never regressing, ultimately pure, through non-attachment and non-bondage.
With a mind of liberation, they cultivate the conduct of Samantabhadra and attain the pure wisdom of the speech of all sentient beings;
their every utterance is fully adorned, universally responding to all beings to bring them joy.

With a mind of liberation that is unattached and unbound, they abide in the conduct of Samantabhadra, establish a superior resolve, possess a pure mind, and extensively manifest great spiritual powers.
With great wisdom, he universally approaches all vast worlds, vast lands, and vast sentient beings;
he expounds the unspeakably vast Dharma of all Tathāgatas and the treasury of the perfection of vast adornments;
through a mind of liberation, unattached and unbound, he fulfills the practices and vows of Samantabhadra’s dedication and attains the purity of all Buddhas.
With body purified and mind purified, they grasp the Buddha’s merits and abide in the realm of the Buddhas.

With the seal of wisdom universally illuminating, they manifest the pure deeds of Bodhisattvas; they skillfully enter all distinct phrases and meanings, and demonstrate the vast sovereignty of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
For the sake of all sentient beings, they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment through liberation that is unattached and unbound.
Through diligent mental cultivation of the practices and vows of Samantabhadra, one attains the faculties of keen intelligence, the faculties of pliancy and compliance,

the faculties of mastery over all phenomena, the inexhaustible faculties, the faculties of diligently cultivating all roots of goodness, the faculties of equality regarding the spheres of all Buddhas,
the faculties of receiving the prediction of non-retrogression for all Bodhisattvas, and the faculties of thoroughly understanding the gold of all Buddha-dharmas.
The Root of the Vajra Realm, the Wisdom-Light-Illuminating Vajra-Flame Root of all Tathāgatas,
the Distinguishing Root of all faculties, the Sovereign Root of all faculties, the Root that establishes immeasurable sentient beings in omniscience,
the Boundlessly Vast Root, the Perfectly Complete Root, and the Pure Unobstructed Root— cultivate the universal [path] with a mind liberated from attachment and bondage.
The noble conduct attains all the spiritual powers of Bodhisattvas, namely: the spiritual power of immeasurable and vast strength; the spiritual power of immeasurable sovereign wisdom;
the spiritual power of manifesting universally in all Buddha-fields without moving the body; the spiritual power of unimpeded and uninterrupted sovereignty;
the spiritual power of gathering all Buddha-fields and placing them in a single location; and the spiritual power of a single body pervading everywhere.
The power of fulfilling all Buddha-fields; the power of unimpeded liberation through the play of spiritual powers; the power of non-action; the power of sovereign mastery in a single thought-moment;
the power of abiding in the natureless and the supportless; the power of sequentially establishing unspeakable numbers of worlds within a single pore;
and the power of traveling throughout the entire Dharma-realm to the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas, manifesting to all sentient beings so that they may all enter therein.
By the spiritual power of the gate of great wisdom, with a mind liberated from attachment and bondage, one enters the gateway of Samantabhadra and gives rise to the practices of a bodhisattva.
Through sovereign wisdom, in a single thought-moment, one universally enters immeasurable Buddha-lands;

with a single body, one accommodates and contains immeasurable Buddha-fields, attaining the wisdom that is able to adorn and purify Buddha-lands, and constantly observing and beholding them with wisdom.
In all boundless Buddha-lands, they never again give rise to the mind of the two vehicles;
with a mind of liberation that is unattached and unbound, they cultivate the skillful practices of Samantabhadra, enter the realm of wisdom, and take birth in the dwelling of the Tathāgatas.
Abiding as Bodhisattvas, they are fully endowed with unspeakably unspeakable, immeasurable, inconceivable, and supreme mental activities and practices, which are infinite.
May I, without ever resting, thoroughly know all dharma-realms of the three periods of time; with a mind liberated through non-attachment and non-binding,
may I accomplish the pure Dharma-gate of Samantabhadra, such that within the space of a single hair-tip,
I may fully contain and clearly perceive as if they were one all the unspeakably unspeakable lands throughout the entirety of empty space and the pervasive dharma-realm.
In every space the size of a single hair-tip throughout the entirety of the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, it is likewise in each and every such space.
With a mind of liberation, unattached and unbound, one accomplishes the profound mind and skillful means of Samantabhadra;
within a single thought-moment, one manifests the mental reflections of an unspeakably unspeakable number of kalpas for a single sentient being, and so on until one manifests [the same] for all.

With a mind that has been cultivated for as many eons as there are sentient beings—a mind of non-attachment, non-binding, and liberation—they enter the stage of skillful means of Samantabhadra’s dedication practices.
Within a single body, they are able to encompass all the unspeakably unspeakable bodies throughout the entire dharma-realm;
yet the realm of sentient beings neither increases nor decreases, remaining as it was from a single body until pervading the entirety of the dharma-realm.
All bodies are likewise thus; with a mind of liberation that is neither attached nor bound, one accomplishes the skillful means of the great vows of Samantabhadra.

Having abandoned all inversions of perception, inversions of mind, and inversions of view, one universally enters the realm of all Buddhas, constantly beholding the Buddhas’ pure Dharma-body—equal to the realm of empty space—and adorned with the marks and signs of excellence and sovereign spiritual powers.
Constantly using wondrous sounds to reveal and expound the Dharma without obstruction or interruption, causing those who hear it to receive and uphold it as taught;

regarding the body of the Tathāgata as utterly unattainable; with a mind of non-attachment and non-binding liberation, practicing the conduct of Samantabhadra and dwelling in the stages of a Bodhisattva;
entering all worlds within a single thought-moment—namely, entering worlds that are inverted.
They cover unspeakably unspeakable worlds throughout all places in the ten directions via the net of Indra;
through the skillful means of differentiation, they universally distinguish the entire dharma-realm,
causing various worlds to enter into a single world, and unspeakably unspeakable, immeasurable worlds to enter into a single world.
One should practice the vows and conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva with a mind of liberation— unattached and unbound—

so as to cause all the infinite worlds established within the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) to enter into a single world, and all the infinite worlds established within the entire realm of empty space (*ākāśadhātu*) to enter into a single world,
yet without destroying their established characteristics, making them all clearly visible.
Having received the Buddha’s consecration, they enter the stage of skillful means within a single thought-moment and dwell in the fulfillment of all practices.

They are able to fully comprehend all conceptualizations, namely: the conceptualization of sentient beings, the conceptualization of phenomena, the conceptualization of lands, the conceptualization of directions, the conceptualization of Buddhas, the conceptualization of worlds, the conceptualization of karma, the conceptualization of conduct, the conceptualization of realms, the conceptualization of understanding, the conceptualization of faculties, the conceptualization of time, the conceptualization of upholding, and the conceptualization of afflictions.

The perception of purity; the perception of maturation; the perception of seeing the Buddha; the perception of turning the wheel of Dharma; the perception of hearing and understanding the Dharma; the perception of subduing; the perception of the immeasurable;
the perception of renunciation; the perception of various stages; the perception of immeasurable stages; the perception of the Bodhisattva’s thorough knowledge;

the perception of the Bodhisattva’s cultivation; the perception of the Bodhisattva’s samādhi; the perception of the Bodhisattva’s emergence from samādhi; and the perception of the Bodhisattva’s accomplishment.

The Bodhisattva’s perception of destruction, the Bodhisattva’s perception of death, the Bodhisattva’s perception of birth, the Bodhisattva’s perception of liberation, the Bodhisattva’s perception of mastery,

the Bodhisattva’s perception of sustaining power, the Bodhisattva’s perception of the spheres of experience, the perception of the formation and dissolution of kalpas, the perception of light, the perception of darkness,

the perception of day, the perception of night, the perception of half-months, months, seasons, years, and the perception of change; as well as the perception of going, the perception of coming, and the perception of abiding.
Whether they conceive thoughts of sitting, sleeping, waking, or any such perceptions, they are able to fully comprehend them within a single thought-moment;

yet they remain free from all conceptualization and without discrimination. Having severed all hindrances and being without attachment, the wisdom of all Buddhas fills their minds, and all Buddha-dharmas cause their roots of goodness to grow. They become one and the same body as all Tathāgatas.
They are embraced by all Buddhas; they study and practice all stainless and pure Buddha-dharmas until reaching the other shore;
with a mind liberated from attachment and bondage, they cultivate the conduct of Samantabhadra for the sake of all sentient beings, giving rise to the jewel of great wisdom;
within each and every thought-moment, they know immeasurable minds according to their respective bases and according to their...
He discerns and clearly perceives all things according to their lineages, their activities, their functions, their characteristics, and their various modes of thought, without exception.
With a mind of liberation, unattached and unbound, he accomplishes the jewel-like wisdom of Samantabhadra’s great vows;
within a single location, he knows infinite and ineffable locations as if they were one.
In this manner, throughout all places and in all respects, one cultivates the ground of wisdom for the practices of Samantabhadra with a mind that is unattached,
unbound, and liberated; within a single action, one is able to know immeasurable, unspeakably unspeakable actions,
clearly perceiving and seeing how each of those actions is produced by various conditions, just as one does for a single action, so too for all.
All karma is likewise so. With a mind free from attachment and bondage, one cultivates the wisdom of Samantabhadra that knows all phenomena;
within a single phenomenon, one knows unspeakably unspeakable phenomena, and within all phenomena, one knows a single phenomenon.
Thus, these various phenomena are each distinct, yet there is no obstruction, no contradiction, and no attachment. By means of this—
Abiding in the bodhisattva practice with a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, one attains the unhindered ear-faculty of Samantabhadra;
within a single utterance, one knows the unspeakably unspeakable varieties of speech-sounds,
infinite and boundless, yet remains without attachment— just as with one utterance, so it is with all utterances, through this [unhindered faculty].
With a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated, they cultivate the wisdom of Samantabhadra, initiate the practices of Samantabhadra, and abide in the stage of Samantabhadra.
Within each and every dharma, they expound unspeakably unspeakable dharmas;
these dharmas are vast and manifoldly differentiated, teaching and gathering in beings through inconceivable skillful means, at immeasurable times and at all times.
In accordance with the various desires and understandings of sentient beings, and according to their faculties and the time, he preaches the Dharma using the voice of a Buddha;
with a single sublime sound, he causes immeasurable sentient beings within the assemblies at the site of enlightenment to rejoice, beyond what can be described.
All Tathāgatas are filled by immeasurable Bodhisattvas who pervade the Dharma-realm, establishing supreme resolve and generating vastness.
Having seen and thoroughly understood all conditioned phenomena (*saṃskāra*), they abide in the stage of Samantabhadra;

according to the teachings they expound, they are able to realize and enter them in every thought-moment. Within a single instant, they increase an immeasurable, unspeakably unspeakable mass of great wisdom, continuing thus until the end of all future eons. In all buddha-fields, they practice and cultivate the vast void.
Having perfected the practice of the equality of emptiness and the like, one cultivates the gateway of the conduct of the faculties of Samantabhadra with a mind free from attachment and bondage,
thereby becoming a king of great conduct who, within each and every faculty, is able to fully comprehend the immeasurable faculties, the immeasurable mental inclinations,
and the wondrous practices arising from inconceivable realms, all through a mind free from attachment and bondage.
The mind abides in the great dedication of the practices of Samantabhadra, attaining the extremely subtle wisdom of form, the extremely subtle wisdom of the body,
the extremely subtle wisdom of lands, the extremely subtle wisdom of eons, the extremely subtle wisdom of worlds, the extremely subtle wisdom of directions,
the extremely subtle wisdom of time, the extremely subtle wisdom of numbers, the extremely subtle wisdom of karmic retribution, and the extremely subtle wisdom of purity.
With such subtle wisdom, they are able to fully comprehend all things, even those most minute, within a single thought-moment;
yet their minds are neither terrified nor deluded, neither distracted nor scattered, neither turbid nor inferior.
Their minds are focused on a single object, well-settled in tranquility, well-discriminating, and well-established, abiding in a mind that is liberated through non-attachment and non-binding.
The Bodhisattva’s wisdom cultivates the conduct of Samantabhadra without weariness; they are able to know the extremely subtle destinies of all sentient beings,
the extreme subtlety of the death of sentient beings, the extreme subtlety of the birth of sentient beings, the extreme subtlety of the abiding of sentient beings,
the extreme subtlety of the dwelling places of sentient beings, the extreme subtlety of the categories of sentient beings, and the extreme subtlety of the realms of sentient beings.
The arising of formations is extremely subtle; sentient beings are extremely subtle; the grasping of sentient beings is extremely subtle;
and the objects of focus for sentient beings are extremely subtle. All such things, being extremely subtle, he is able to fully comprehend within a single thought-moment.

With a mind liberated from attachment and bondage, he establishes a profound aspiration and delight in cultivating the practices of Samantabhadra, and is thus able to know all bodhisattvas from their first production of the thought of enlightenment.
For the sake of all sentient beings, they cultivate the bodhisattva practice; they possess the most subtle dwelling place of a bodhisattva,
the most subtle supernormal powers of a bodhisattva, the most subtle wandering through immeasurable buddha-fields of a bodhisattva,
the most subtle light of the Dharma of a bodhisattva, the most subtle pure eye of a bodhisattva, and the most subtle accomplishment of the sublime mind of a bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Subtlety of the Extremely Subtle proceeds to the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas;

the Bodhisattva Subtlety of the Extremely Subtle’s Dharma-door of Dhāraṇīs and Wisdom; the Bodhisattva Subtlety of the Extremely Subtle’s Exposition of the Treasury of All Eloquence and the Grounds of Immeasurable Fearlessness;
the Bodhisattva Subtlety of the Extremely Subtle’s Characteristics of Immeasurable Samādhis; and the Bodhisattva Subtlety of the Extremely Subtle’s Vision of All.
The Buddha’s samādhi-wisdom is extremely subtle; the bodhisattva’s profound samādhi-wisdom is extremely subtle;
the bodhisattva’s great adornment samādhi-wisdom is extremely subtle; the bodhisattva’s dharma-realm samādhi-wisdom is extremely subtle;
the bodhisattva’s samādhi-wisdom of great sovereign supernormal powers is extremely subtle; and the bodhisattva’s vast practice extending to the end of the future is [extremely subtle].
The Bodhisattva who dwells in the extremely subtle wisdom of samādhi; the Bodhisattva who gives birth to the extremely subtle wisdom of immeasurable varieties of samādhi;
the Bodhisattva who gives birth to the extremely subtle wisdom of samādhi that constantly practices offerings before all Buddhas without ever abandoning them;
and the Bodhisattva who cultivates all extremely profound, vast, unobstructed, and unimpeded [wisdom].
The extremely subtle wisdom of the bodhisattvas who abide in the ultimate stage of omniscience,
the stage of sustaining practice, the stage of great spiritual powers, and the stage of definitive meaning— the extremely subtle wisdom of the *vimala-samādhi* (stainless samādhi)—
all such extremely subtle things they are able to fully comprehend. With a mind liberated from attachment and bondage, they cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra and know them all.
The wisdom established by all bodhisattvas is extremely subtle; the bodhisattva stages are extremely subtle; the immeasurable practices of bodhisattvas are extremely subtle;
the generation and dedication of bodhisattvas are extremely subtle; the attainment of the treasury of all buddhas by bodhisattvas is extremely subtle;
the wisdom of observation of bodhisattvas is extremely subtle; and the power of the vows of the supernormal knowledges of bodhisattvas is extremely subtle.
The Bodhisattva’s exposition of samādhi is extremely subtle; the Bodhisattva’s mastery of skillful means is extremely subtle; the Bodhisattva’s seal is extremely subtle;
the Bodhisattva’s state of being in his final birth before enlightenment is extremely subtle; the Bodhisattva’s birth in the Tuṣita Heaven is extremely subtle;
the Bodhisattva’s dwelling in the celestial palace is extremely subtle; and the Bodhisattva’s adornment and purification of the Buddha-land is extremely subtle.
The Bodhisattva’s observation of the human realm is extremely subtle; the Bodhisattva’s emission of great light is extremely subtle;
the Bodhisattva’s excellence of lineage is extremely subtle; the Bodhisattva’s assembly at the site of enlightenment is extremely subtle;

the Bodhisattva’s taking birth throughout all worlds is extremely subtle; and the Bodhisattva’s manifestation of all bodies within a single body and the passing away of their life-span is extremely subtle.
The extremely subtle Bodhisattva entering the mother’s womb; the extremely subtle Bodhisattva abiding in the mother’s womb;
the extremely subtle Bodhisattva manifesting within the mother’s womb all the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment throughout the entire Dharma-realm;
the extremely subtle Bodhisattva manifesting within the mother’s womb all the spiritual powers of all Buddhas; the extremely subtle Bodhisattva manifesting.
The birth of the Bodhisattva is extremely subtle; the lion-like stride of the Bodhisattva as he takes seven steps is extremely subtle;

the Bodhisattva’s manifestation of dwelling in a royal palace through skillful means is extremely subtle; the Bodhisattva’s renunciation of the world and cultivation of the practice of self-discipline is extremely subtle;
the Bodhisattva’s sitting beneath the Bodhi tree at the site of enlightenment is extremely subtle; and the Bodhisattva’s destruction of Māra’s hosts is extremely subtle.
The Tathāgata who has attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* is exceedingly subtle;

the Tathāgata seated upon the bodhi-maṇḍala emitting great radiance that illuminates the worlds of the ten directions is exceedingly subtle; the Tathāgata manifesting immeasurable supernatural transformations is exceedingly subtle;
the Tathāgata’s lion’s roar of the Great Parinirvāṇa is exceedingly subtle; the Tathāgata who tames all sentient beings is exceedingly subtle.
Yet it is unimpeded and exceedingly subtle; the inconceivable power of the Tathāgata’s mastery is like a vajra;
the bodhicitta is exceedingly subtle; the Tathāgata’s universal protective mindfulness of the realms of all worlds is exceedingly subtle;
and the Tathāgata’s universal performance of buddha-activities in all worlds throughout all future kalpas without rest is exceedingly subtle.
The Subtly Minute Tathāgata’s unimpeded spiritual power pervades the entire Dharma-realm;
the Subtly Minute Tathāgata universally manifests the attainment of Buddhahood throughout all worlds within the entirety of empty space to subdue sentient beings;

the Subtly Minute Tathāgata manifests immeasurable Buddha-bodies from within a single Buddha-body; and the Subtly Minute Tathāgata [is present] throughout the three periods of time—past, future, and present.
Abiding in the site of enlightenment with sovereign wisdom that is exceedingly subtle, they are able to fully comprehend all such subtle aspects and achieve purity.
They are able to manifest throughout all worlds, increasing their wisdom in every thought-moment;
they fulfill the non-retrogressive skillful means of practicing the bodhisattva path without rest, thereby accomplishing the conduct of Samantabhadra.
The ground of dedication is fully endowed with all the merits of the Tathāgatas; it never tires of nor abandons the conduct of Bodhisattvas;
it gives rise to the manifest realm of Bodhisattvas; its immeasurable skillful means are entirely pure; it universally desires to bring peace and security to all sentient beings;
it cultivates the practices of a Bodhisattva and accomplishes the stage of great majestic power of a Bodhisattva, thereby attaining the state of all Bodhisattvas.
With a mind that desires to attain the gate of dedication known as the Vajradhvaja, one gives birth to the treasury of all merits within the Dharma-realm;
one is constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas; one enters the profound and wondrous Dharma-gates of all Bodhisattvas;
one expounds the meaning of all that is true; one is skillful in the Dharma without error or loss; and one gives rise to great vows never to abandon sentient beings.

Within a single thought-moment, they fully know all minds; they reveal the treasury of the non-mind-ground within the state that is not mind, manifesting birth within the mind while remaining far removed from language.

Abiding in wisdom, they practice the same conduct as all bodhisattvas, manifesting the attainment of the Buddha-way through their power of mastery, never ceasing throughout the bounds of the future for all worlds.
The conceptual constructions and verbal designations regarding the kalpas of sentient beings are all manifested through the power of supernormal knowledges and vows;
by cultivating the conduct of Samantabhadra with a mind of non-attachment and non-binding liberation, one attains the most subtle wisdom regarding the realms of all sentient beings—
namely, the extremely subtle wisdom that discriminates the realms of sentient beings and the extremely subtle [wisdom regarding] the verbal designations of the realms of sentient beings.
The extremely subtle attachment of sentient beings to the realm of wisdom; the extremely subtle diversity of the realm of wisdom of sentient beings;
the extremely subtle homogeneity of the realm of wisdom of sentient beings; the extremely subtle infinite destinies of the realm of wisdom of sentient beings;
the extremely subtle various conceptualizations and activities of the inconceivable realm of wisdom of sentient beings; and the immeasurable realm of wisdom of sentient beings.
The extremely subtle wisdom regarding the realm of sentient beings that is thoroughly afflicted, and the extremely subtle wisdom regarding the immeasurable realm of sentient beings that is purified—
thus, all such realms of sentient beings are extremely subtle; within a single thought-moment, one is able to know them all as they truly are through wisdom,
extensively gathering in sentient beings and preaching the Dharma for them, revealing various gates of pure Dharma so that they may practice.
The Bodhisattva’s vast wisdom manifests infinite transformation bodies that bring joy to all who behold them;
with the light of the sun of wisdom, they illumine the Bodhisattva’s mind, causing it to awaken.

Possessing mastery over wisdom and a mind liberated from attachment and bondage, they cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra for the sake of all sentient beings in all worlds, until they reach the ultimate limit of the realm of empty space and the Dharma-realm.
The extremely subtle wisdom regarding all worlds, namely: extremely subtle wisdom regarding small worlds; extremely subtle wisdom regarding large worlds;
extremely subtle wisdom regarding defiled worlds; extremely subtle wisdom regarding pure worlds; extremely subtle wisdom regarding incomparable worlds;
extremely subtle wisdom regarding diverse worlds; and extremely subtle wisdom regarding vast worlds.
The subtle wisdom of the extremely minute worlds; the subtle wisdom of the unimpeded adornments of worlds;
the subtle wisdom of the appearance of Buddhas throughout all worlds; the subtle wisdom of the preaching of the True Dharma throughout all worlds;
and the subtle wisdom of the universal manifestation of bodies throughout all worlds.
The extremely subtle wisdom that radiates great light; the extremely subtle wisdom that manifests the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas throughout all worlds;
the extremely subtle wisdom that, with a single voice, manifests all sounds throughout all worlds;
and the extremely subtle wisdom that enters the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment in all Buddha-fields throughout all worlds.
The extremely subtle wisdom that makes all dharma-realms and buddha-fields into a single buddha-field;
the extremely subtle wisdom that makes a single buddha-field into all dharma-realms and buddha-fields; the extremely subtle wisdom that knows all worlds to be like dreams;
the extremely subtle wisdom that knows all worlds to be like reflections; and the extremely subtle wisdom that knows all worlds to be like illusions.
With subtle wisdom, one thus understands and gives rise to the path of all bodhisattvas;
entering the conduct of Samantabhadra, endowed with wisdom and supernormal powers, and possessing the contemplation of Samantabhadra, one cultivates the bodhisattva practices constantly without rest.

Attaining the sovereign spiritual transformations of all Buddhas and possessing an unimpeded body, one dwells in non-reliant wisdom, remaining without attachment to any wholesome dharmas within the mind.

In all that they practice, they find nothing to be grasped; in all places, they give rise to the perception of detachment; in the conduct of a bodhisattva, they give rise to the perception of pure cultivation;
regarding omniscience, they maintain the perception of non-attachment. Adorned by various samādhis, their wisdom accords with the entire dharma-realm.
With a mind of liberation—unattached and unbound—they enter the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Entering the gate of the infinitely subtle wisdom of the dharma-realm; expounding the infinitely subtle wisdom of all dharma-realms;
entering the infinitely subtle wisdom of the vast dharma-realm; discerning the inconceivable infinitely subtle wisdom of the dharma-realm;
discerning the infinitely subtle wisdom of all dharma-realms; and the infinitely subtle wisdom that pervades all dharma-realms in a single thought-moment.
The wisdom that universally enters all dharma-realms; the extremely subtle wisdom that knows all dharma-realms are unattainable;
the extremely subtle wisdom that contemplates all dharma-realms as being without obstruction; the extremely subtle wisdom that knows all dharma-realms are without arising;
and the extremely subtle wisdom that manifests spiritual transformations within all dharma-realms—just so.
All these phenomena within the dharma-realm are extremely subtle; with vast wisdom, he knows them all as they truly are.
Having attained mastery over the Dharma, he demonstrates the conduct of Samantabhadra, causing all sentient beings to be fully satisfied.

Without abandoning the ultimate meaning nor becoming attached to phenomena, he gives rise to the wisdom of equality and non-obstruction. Knowing the root of non-obstruction, he does not abide in any phenomena and remains indestructible.

The nature of all phenomena is, in accordance with reality, undefiled like space; yet, in conformity with the world, it gives rise to verbal expression to reveal the true meaning and demonstrate the nature of cessation.
In all objects, it is without dependence or abiding, free from conceptual differentiation, clearly perceiving the vast establishment of the *dharmadhātu*.
It understands that all worlds and all phenomena are equal and non-dual, transcending [all extremes].
With a mind free from attachment, unbound, and liberated, one cultivates the practices of Samantabhadra and gives rise to the most subtle wisdom regarding all kalpas—
namely, the subtle wisdom that takes unspeakable kalpas as a single thought-moment, the subtle wisdom that takes a single thought-moment as unspeakable kalpas,
and the subtle wisdom that enters unspeakably many kalpas into a single kalpa.
The extremely subtle wisdom that enters one eon into incalculable eons; the extremely subtle wisdom that enters long eons into short eons;
the extremely subtle wisdom that enters short eons into long eons; the extremely subtle wisdom that enters eons with Buddhas and eons without Buddhas;
the extremely subtle wisdom that knows the number of all eons; and the extremely subtle wisdom that knows all eons as non-eons.
With subtle wisdom, one perceives within a single thought-moment all kalpas of the three periods of time;
with such extremely subtle wisdom, one knows all these kalpas exactly as they are through the Tathāgata’s wisdom in a single thought-moment.

One attains the mind of the sovereign of the perfect practices of all Bodhisattvas, enters the mind of Samantabhadra’s conduct, and becomes free from all conceptualization, divergent paths, and frivolous proliferation.
A mind that gives rise to great vows without weariness; a mind that universally perceives the infinite network of worlds filled with immeasurable Buddhas;
a mind capable of hearing and retaining the roots of goodness of all Buddhas and the practices of all Bodhisattvas;
a mind that, having heard the vast conduct for comforting all sentient beings, never forgets it; and a mind capable of manifesting the appearance of Buddhas in the world throughout all eons.
In each and every world, until the end of the future, they practice the immovable conduct with an untiring mind;
throughout all worlds, they fill the bodies and minds of bodhisattvas with the physical actions of the Tathāgata;
with a mind of liberation that is unattached and unbound, they cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra, attain non-retrogression, and achieve the most subtle wisdom regarding all phenomena, namely:
The extremely subtle wisdom regarding the profound Dharma; the extremely subtle wisdom regarding the vast Dharma; the extremely subtle wisdom regarding various dharmas;
the extremely subtle wisdom regarding the adorned Dharma; the extremely subtle wisdom regarding the immeasurability of all dharmas;
the extremely subtle wisdom regarding all dharmas entering into one dharma; the extremely subtle wisdom regarding one dharma entering into all dharmas; all...
The extremely subtle wisdom that [discerns] the dharma-base as non-dharma; the extremely subtle wisdom that establishes all dharmas within the absence of dharmas without contradiction;

the extremely subtle wisdom that enters the skillful means of all Buddha-dharmas without exception—such extremely subtle wisdoms regarding all conventions established by all speech throughout all worlds are identical to those [of the Buddhas].
Equalizing their unimpeded wisdom, they know all things as they truly are and enter the mind of the boundless Dharma-realm.
Within each and every Dharma-realm, they dwell with firm resolve in their profound mind, accomplishing unimpeded conduct.

Filling all their faculties with omniscience, they enter the wisdom of all Buddhas through the skillful means of right mindfulness, perfecting the vast merits of all Buddhas so that they pervade the entire Dharma-realm and universally enter into the One.
The bodies of all Tathāgatas manifest the various bodily actions (*kāyakarman*) of all Bodhisattvas; they expound the Dharma in accordance with the languages of all worlds;

they obtain the empowerment of the spiritual power (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all Buddhas; their mental actions (*manaskarman*) give rise to immeasurable skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) and the discernment of all phenomena through the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), by means of liberation that is unattached and unbound.
One cultivates the practices of Samantabhadra with the mind to give birth to all most subtle wisdoms— namely, the most subtle wisdom that knows all lands,
the most subtle wisdom that knows all sentient beings, the most subtle wisdom that knows the retributions of all phenomena,
the most subtle wisdom that knows the minds of all sentient beings, and the most subtle wisdom that knows all times of preaching the Dharma.
Subtle wisdom knows that all dharma-realms are extremely subtle; wisdom knows that all throughout the realm of empty space across the three periods of time are extremely subtle;
wisdom knows that all paths of speech are extremely subtle; wisdom knows that all worldly activities are extremely subtle;
wisdom knows that all world-transcending activities are extremely subtle; and so on, until it knows all such things as they truly are.

They come to know, according to reality, both the letter and the meaning of all bodhisattva paths and all paths of sentient beings; they possess the extremely subtle wisdom that cultivates the bodhisattva practices and dwells in the path of Samantabhadra.

They give rise to the wisdom that perceives things as reflections, the wisdom that perceives them as dreams, the wisdom that perceives them as illusions, the wisdom that perceives them as echoes, the wisdom that perceives them as transformations, the wisdom that perceives them as empty space, and the wisdom of ultimate quiescence.
[The arising of] the wisdom that gives birth to all dharma-realms; the arising of the wisdom that has no basis; the arising of the wisdom of all Buddha-dharmas.

[Treatise: From "the second son of the Buddha" down to "the arising of the wisdom that has no basis and the arising of the wisdom of all Buddha-dharmas," the preceding twelve pages of scripture clarify the cultivation of the first ten kinds of roots of goodness and the cultivation of the ten kinds of respectful practices.
The Section on the Dedication of Liberation Without Attachment or Bondage for Entering the Subtle Sphere of Samantabhadra’s Wisdom:
This section generally clarifies the accomplishment of the fruit-virtues of all Buddhas of the three periods of time and the subtle dharmas of Samantabhadra’s fruit-practice;
regarding these subtle dharma-gates, ten kinds of subtleties are established as a brief illustration, while the remainder are [omitted].

Following this principle, within the subtle body of a single Buddha—just as within the *saṃbhogakāya* of a Buddha—and within the body of a single sentient being, there are unspeakably and immeasurably many Buddha-bodies; this applies universally to all Buddha-bodies and all sentient beings' bodies.
Second, the subtle wisdom of the Buddhas pervades the entire realm of empty space within a single instance of wisdom.
They know with distinct clarity all the dharmas according to the inclinations of sentient beings; they know in detail the births of the three Buddhas;

and they reduce all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions to dust, wherein within each single mote of dust, they simultaneously undergo conception, simultaneously take birth, simultaneously proceed to the site of enlightenment, and simultaneously turn the wheel of Dharma, yet without destroying the arising of their manifestations.
Because they manifest in forms corresponding to [the capacities of] beings, they gather and transform all sentient beings of the three periods of time;

they are subtle within the atoms of all Buddha-fields, possessing the practices of Samantabhadra; before each and every sentient being, they manifest forms according to their kind to preach the Dharma and teach them, each distinct yet layered and unimpeded; they are subtle within the five lands, even within each and every atom.
Within each [of these], there are immeasurable and vast world-systems equal in extent to space;
each world-system interpenetrates one another in infinite layers without obstruction, like the Flower Treasury Ocean (*Kusuma-garbha-sāgara*).

These six assemblies of bodhisattvas are more subtle than the aforementioned atoms within the Buddha-fields; within each atom, there are all the Buddhas’ great *bodhimaṇḍas*, equal in extent to space.
The oceans of the assembly of bodhisattvas completely fill [all realms]; within the dust-motes of all such lands, it is entirely like this.
Thus, these sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) and these oceans of assemblies interpenetrate one another in layers without obstruction, like light and like shadows.
The seven bodhisattvas behold the Buddha’s subtle manifestations according to their ten abodes (*vihāra*), ten practices (*caryā*), ten dedications (*pariṇāmanā*), and ten stages (*bhūmi*).
All see the Tathāgata as if facing him before their eyes, as he teaches the Dharma according to each individual's station and reveals the body according to each individual's station.

The voices of the eight Buddhas are subtle; the voice of the Tathāgata does not issue from the mind nor from the body, yet it is ever-present, constantly pervading the ten directions, so that all may hear it according to their capacity. It is subtle even throughout the nine periods of kalpas.
The unspeakable eons of the three periods of time are such that all Buddhas do not emerge from a single thought-moment, yet they are universally present right now;
the Buddhas manifesting before us now likewise abide in the future and the past, with the three periods of time interpenetrating one another at once.

Eon after eon, layer upon layer, they are unimpeded. This is because the subtle power of the ten supernatural faculties and the path of wisdom-body pervades all through the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*).

It is likewise: with the wisdom that is without abiding or support, the physical bodies manifest throughout the ten directions in resonance, yet there is no coming or going, nor any mind of transformation or contrivance. Through wisdom, one accords with the Dharma of original vows;
it should be thus, and so too are all realms within every atom, layered upon layer without end. Thus is the aforementioned establishment.
These ten dharma-gates explain the method of dedication within this stage;

the general significance is such that it clarifies how a bodhisattva is capable of entering this stage of non-attachment and non-binding dedication. The remaining text should be understood accordingly.
By means of the dharma-body of non-action and the wisdom of non-abiding, one harmonizes and integrates them through the great vows of the ten dedications.
May they achieve the ocean-like conduct of great compassion that benefits sentient beings;
may all conceptualization and discrimination function as the activity of wisdom; may all knowledge and vision collectively become the gate of dhyāna;

and may the originally unmoving nature of reality, through the gate of fundamental quiescence and concentration, give rise to the bodies of differentiated wisdom, the bodies of insight, and the bodies of transformation.

They dedicate [their merit] in this way: so that within a single pore they may establish all Buddha-fields and sentient-being fields without any obstruction, and because they have attained mastery over the conditioned and unconditioned as a single Dharma-realm.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, with a mind that is unattached, unbound, and liberated,
dedicates [merit] without discriminating between the world and worldly phenomena, without discriminating between awakening and the bodhisattva,
without discriminating between the bodhisattva’s practice and the path of transcendence, and without discriminating between the Buddha and all the Buddha-dharmas.
One does not discriminate between those who have been tamed and those who have not been tamed; one does not discriminate between roots of goodness and dedication;
one does not discriminate between self and other; one does not discriminate between the object given and the recipient;
one does not discriminate between the bodhisattva practice and perfect enlightenment; and one does not discriminate between phenomena and wisdom.

[Treatise] From the third "Son of the Buddha" downward, up to the passage "not discriminating whether it be dharmas or wisdom," there are seven lines of sūtra that clarify the attainment of the stage of non-discrimination.
[Sūtra] Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dedicates those roots of goodness in this manner, namely: with a mind that is without...
Unattached, unbound, and liberated in body; unattached, unbound, and liberated in speech; unattached, unbound, and liberated in action;
unattached, unbound, and liberated in retribution; unattached, unbound, and liberated in the world;
unattached, unbound, and liberated in Buddha-fields; unattached, unbound, and liberated in sentient beings; unattached to phenomena.

With the wisdom of liberation from non-binding and non-fettering, when the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, free from attachment and non-binding, thus dedicates [merit], he practices dedication as all Buddhas of the three periods practiced dedication when they were Bodhisattvas;
he learns the dedication of past Buddhas, accomplishes the dedication of future Buddhas, and abides in the dedication of present Buddhas. He is established therein.
Abiding in the path of dedication of all Buddhas of the past, not abandoning the path of dedication of all Buddhas of the future, and following the path of dedication of all Buddhas of the present;
diligently cultivating the teachings of all Buddhas of the past, accomplishing the teachings of all Buddhas of the future, and thoroughly understanding the teachings of all Buddhas of the present;
fulfilling the equality of all Buddhas of the past and accomplishing [the equality] of all Buddhas of the future.
The Buddha abides in equality with all present Buddhas, practices the equal conduct of all past Buddhas, dwells in the realm of all future Buddhas,
and is equal to the realm of all present Buddhas. He attains the roots of goodness of all Buddhas of the three periods of time,
possesses the lineage of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, and dwells in accordance with the conduct of all Buddhas of the three periods of time.
The realm of all Buddhas of the three periods of time— this, O Son of the Buddha, is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s ninth dedication of the mind of liberation,
unattached and unbound. [Treatise] From the fourth "Son of the Buddha" down to the ninth dedication of the mind of liberation, unattached and unbound.
There are sixteen lines and a half of sūtra text clarifying that by practicing this dedication, one attains the state where the three karmas are without attachment or bondage,
equal to the dedication-liberation of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
[Sūtra] When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells in this dedication, they are not obstructed by any of the Vajra-circumferential mountain ranges.
He is foremost among all sentient beings in the excellence of his physical form, with none able to equal him; he is capable of utterly destroying all the demonic and heterodox activities of others;
he universally manifests throughout all worlds in the ten directions to practice the bodhisattva path;
desiring to awaken all sentient beings, he expounds the Buddha-dharma through skillful means and attains great wisdom regarding all the teachings of the Buddhas.
With a mind free from delusion, in whatever place of birth one may be—whether walking or staying—one shall always encounter an indestructible retinue.
Through pure mindfulness, one shall be able to receive and uphold the True Dharma taught by the Buddhas of the three periods of time.

Cultivating the practices of a Bodhisattva throughout all future kalpas without ever ceasing, one shall be free from all attachment, causing the practices and vows of Samantabhadra to increase and reach full perfection.
[They] attain all-knowledge, perform the work of a Buddha, and accomplish the sovereign supernormal powers of a Bodhisattva.

[Treatise: From the fifth Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva down to "accomplishing the sovereign supernormal powers of a Bodhisattva," there are nine lines of scripture that clarify how this cultivation of dedication results in indestructible roots of goodness, such that wherever one is born, one encounters a Buddha.
Section on the Sovereign Supernatural Powers.
[Sūtra] At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, surveyed the ten directions and spoke in verse.
[Commentary] Sixth, the single line of sūtra beginning with "At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajradhvaja" clarifies the surveying of the assembly and the subsequent discourse.
Section on Verses.
[Sūtra] Toward the Peerless Honored Ones throughout the ten directions, I have never once given rise to a thought of contempt;
In accordance with the meritorious deeds they have cultivated, I likewise pay them homage and give rise to reverence.
All the merits one cultivates, neither for oneself nor for others,
are constantly dedicated with the mind of supreme faith and understanding for the sake of benefiting sentient beings;
never does one give rise to a heart of pride, nor does one ever harbor an inferior thought.
All the physical and other actions of the Tathāgata, as well as the various roots of goodness he has cultivated through diligent practice—
all these he asks about, for the benefit of all sentient beings who dwell in profound resolve and vast understanding,
so that they may dedicate themselves to the state of merit of the Honored One among Men.
All the infinite varieties in the world— The diverse, skillful, and marvelous things, whether coarse,
subtle, vast, or profound— There is none that he does not practice or fail to fully comprehend.
Regarding all the various bodies in the world, He enters into them all through the equality of his own body.
Having attained realization through practice herein, they achieve the gateway of wisdom and never regress.
Regarding the infinite varieties of worldly realms— whether subtle or vast, upright or inverted— the Bodhisattva,
by means of the gateway of wisdom, perceives them all within a single pore.
The mental activities of sentient beings are immeasurable; They can cause them all to enter equally into a single mind.
Through the gateway of wisdom, they awaken them all, So that they do not regress from their practice.
The faculties, inclinations, and desires of sentient beings— Whether superior, middling, or inferior—are each different.

All things are profoundly deep and difficult to know; yet, according to their inherent nature, they can fully comprehend all the various karmas of sentient beings. Whether superior, middling, or inferior, each is distinct;
the Bodhisattva enters deeply into the power of the Tathāgata and perceives everything clearly through the gateway of wisdom.
Inconceivable and immeasurable eons can be made to enter equally into a single thought-moment;
having seen this, they pervade the ten directions and cultivate all pure deeds.
Regarding the past, future, and present, they understand that their characteristics are each different.
Yet they do not contradict the principle of equality; this is the practice of great-minded, clear realization.

Though the practices of sentient beings in the world differ—whether manifest or hidden in infinite ways—the Bodhisattvas fully know their distinct characteristics, and they also know that all such characteristics are ultimately signless.
The sovereign power of supernatural transformations manifested by all Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions is vast and inconceivable;
Bodhisattvas are able to discern and know it all.
Within the Tuṣita heavens of every world, they fully understand those lions among men who have attained spontaneous awakening.
His merit is vast, pure, and peerless; he perceives all things exactly as they are in their essence and form.

Sometimes he manifests his descent into a mother’s womb; through immeasurable, sovereign, and great spiritual transformations, he becomes a Buddha, preaches the Dharma, and demonstrates parinirvāṇa, pervading the entire world without a moment’s rest.
When the Lion among Men was first born, all those of supreme wisdom— Śakra, Brahmā,
and the other lords of the devas— honored and attended him with reverence; throughout the ten directions, without exception,
across the infinite and boundless reaches of the Dharma-realm, there was none who did not do so.
Without beginning or end, without distance near or far, the Tathāgata manifests his sovereign power;
having appeared as the Honored Guide among men, he walks seven paces in each direction.
Desiring to awaken all sentient beings through the sublime Dharma, the Tathāgata gazes upon them everywhere.
Seeing all sentient beings submerged in the ocean of desire, Enveloped by blindness, darkness, and ignorance, The Sovereign among Men manifests a smile;
Reflecting that he shall rescue them from the suffering of the three realms of existence, The Great Master utters this wondrous sound of a lion’s roar: “I am the foremost honored one in the world.”
One should kindle the bright lamp of pure wisdom To extinguish the darkness of ignorance within birth and death.
When the Lion-King among Men appears in the world, He universally radiates immeasurable great light,
Causing all evil realms to come to rest, And forever extinguishing the manifold sufferings and hardships of the world.
At times he manifests dwelling in royal palaces, and at times he manifests leaving home to practice the path;
for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, he displays such sovereign power.
When the Tathāgata first sat upon the site of enlightenment, the entire great earth shook and trembled.
The worlds of the ten directions are all bathed in light, And sentient beings of the six realms are all freed from suffering.
All the palaces of the māras are shaken, And the minds of sentient beings throughout the ten directions are awakened.
Those who were previously transformed by the Buddha and those who have practiced the path— May they all come to realize the true meaning.
All the lands throughout the ten directions enter entirely into a single pore without exception;
within those infinite lands of every pore, he universally manifests his supernormal powers.
Whatever has been expounded by all the Buddhas, he awakens to it all through immeasurable skillful means.
Even that which has not been taught by all the Tathāgatas, they can understand and diligently practice until it pervades the trichiliocosm;
and as for all the various immeasurable evils wrought by the hosts of Māras who incite strife and contention,
the gateway of unimpeded wisdom can utterly extinguish them all.
Whether the Tathāgata is in various Buddha-fields, or manifests in the palaces of the devas,
or appears in the Brahma-heavens, the Bodhisattvas see all these without obstruction;
the Buddha manifests infinite and diverse bodies, turning the pure and wondrous Wheel of Dharma.
Even throughout all kalpas of the three periods of time, one cannot find their limit.
The precious throne is high, vast, and peerless, Pervading the immeasurable realms of the ten directions, adorned with various wondrous marks. The Buddha sits upon it, inconceivable.
Surrounded by the assembly of all Buddha-sons, who pervade the entire realm of phenomena,
you reveal the immeasurable practices of enlightenment— the path by which all the Most Victorious Ones proceed,
the deeds performed by the Buddhas according to their suitability, as infinite and boundless as the realm of phenomena itself.
The wise one, through a single skillful means, fully understands everything without exception;
by the sovereign power of the Buddhas' spiritual penetrations, they manifest all manner of diverse bodies—
appearing as infinite births within the various realms of existence, or appearing surrounded by a host of celestial maidens.
In immeasurable worlds, he manifests leaving the household life, attaining the path of Buddhahood,
and even reaching final parinirvāṇa; he distributes his body to establish stupas and temples—
such are the various boundless practices that the Guide expounds as the dwelling place of the Buddha.
May all the great virtues of the World-Honored One be fully realized through the practice of my vows;
when dedicating those roots of goodness, may I abide in such skillful means.
Thus cultivating the conduct of enlightenment, may my mind never experience weariness or indolence.

All the great supernormal powers possessed by the Tathāgata, as well as his boundless and supreme merits, and even all the various modes of worldly knowledge—He knows them all completely, without exception.
Such is the Lord among Men; according to all his respective spheres of experience, [he acts].
In a single thought-moment, they fully awaken to all things, yet never abandon the practices of enlightenment.
They are able to know and accord with all the subtle deeds of the Buddhas and the various phenomena of all lands;
ultimately dedicating these merits, they reach the further shore.
All kalpas, whether numbered or unnumbered, the Bodhisattva understands as being but a single thought-moment;
thus skillfully entering the practice of enlightenment, they constantly and diligently cultivate it without ever regressing.
Throughout all the infinite realms of the ten directions—whether they be defiled or pure—[they enter them all].
And all those Tathāgatas, as well as the Bodhisattvas, he is able to discern and know;
in every single thought-moment, he clearly perceives inconceivable and immeasurable eons.
Thus, throughout the three periods of time without exception, he fully cultivates and purifies the Bodhisattva practices.
Entering with equanimity into all minds, And entering with equal thoroughness into all phenomena until they are empty;
The Buddha-fields are likewise so. He fully understands those supreme practices, The arising of sentient beings and all dharmas, And all the various kinds of wisdom.
The spiritual power of the Bodhisattva is likewise so; thus all things are inexhaustible.

Each of the subtle wisdoms is distinct, yet the Bodhisattva encompasses them all without exception, thoroughly knowing both their common and their differing characteristics. Thus they practice these vast and expansive deeds.

The infinite Buddha-fields of the ten directions, and the various and diverse classes of beings within them who take birth through immeasurable destinies— having established themselves in the power of abiding,
they fully know all the Teachers of the past, future, and present worlds.
If a person knows this and dedicates [their merit], they will be equal in practice to those Buddhas;
if a person can cultivate this dedication, they will be training in the path traveled by the Buddhas,
and shall attain all the virtues of all Buddhas, as well as all the wisdom of all Buddhas.
Nothing in all the worlds can destroy them; All that they have studied is fully accomplished.
They are always able to recollect all Buddhas, And constantly behold all the Lamps of the World.
The sublime conduct of these Bodhisattvas is immeasurable, And their qualities and dharmas are likewise so.
Having already abided in the supreme conduct of the Tathāgatas, they fully know the sovereign power of all Buddhas.
[Treatise] From the seventh verse downward, there are one hundred and two lines of verse; the meaning of the text is complete within these two lines per stanza.
Second, as for the word-by-word commentary: what is meant by "the dedication of liberation that is unattached and unbound"?
The wisdom of the absence of intrinsic nature is without dependence; it is entirely unattached and entirely unbound. Therefore, a sutra says:
"With profound and subtle wisdom, one cultivates the bodhisattva practices and dwells in the path of Samantabhadra.

One knows both the words and their meanings as they truly are, giving rise to the wisdom that [all things] are like shadows, like dreams, like illusions, like echoes, like transformations, and like space," and so forth.
The wisdom of non-reliance and so forth arises.
