Chapter Twenty-seven, Part Three: The Ten Determinations.
[Sūtra] "O Son of the Buddha, what is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’s Samādhi of the Treasury of the Radiance of Wisdom?
"O Son of the Buddha, when that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva abides in this samādhi, he is able to know all Buddhas throughout all kalpas in all future worlds—
whether they have already spoken or have not yet spoken, whether they have already received a prediction [of enlightenment] or have not yet received a prediction."

The names and titles by which they are known are each different, namely: the name "Innumerable," the name "Immeasurable," the name "Boundless," the name "Unequaled," the name "Uncountable," the name "Ineffable," the name "Inconceivable," the name "Unfathomable," and the name "Inexpressible.
They shall appear in the world, they shall benefit sentient beings, they shall act as Dharma-kings, and they shall perform the Buddha-work.
One should proclaim the benefits, praise the meaning of the wholesome, explain the meaning of the bright portion, purify all evils, abide in merit,
reveal the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), enter the stage of empowerment (*abhiṣeka*), and accomplish all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*).
Those Tathāgatas have cultivated perfect conduct, made perfect vows, entered perfect wisdom, and are endowed with a perfect assembly.
This Bodhisattva thoroughly understands all such things as the perfect adornment, the accumulation of perfected merit, the realization of the perfected Dharma,
the attainment of the perfected fruit, the possession of perfected marks, the achievement of perfected awakening, the names, clans, and lineages of those Tathāgatas,
their skillful means, their supernormal powers and transformations, their maturing of sentient beings, and their entry into parinirvāṇa.
In a single thought-moment, they are able to enter one kalpa, a hundred kalpas, a thousand kalpas, a hundred thousand kalpas,

a hundred thousand *koṭi-nayuta* kalpas; they enter as many kalpas as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa, as many kalpas as there are atoms in the four continents, as many kalpas as there are atoms in a small chiliocosm,
as many kalpas as there are atoms in a medium chiliocosm, and as many kalpas as there are atoms in a great trichiliocosm.

Entering eons as numerous as the atoms in a world-system, entering eons as numerous as the atoms in a hundred buddha-fields, entering eons as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand buddha-fields,
entering eons as numerous as the atoms in a hundred thousand *koṭi-nayuta* buddha-fields, entering eons as numerous as the atoms in countless buddha-fields,
entering eons as numerous as the atoms in immeasurable buddha-fields, and entering eons as numerous as the atoms in boundless buddha-fields.
For kalpas numbering as the atoms in an incomparable buddha-field; for kalpas numbering as the atoms in incalculable buddha-fields;
for kalpas numbering as the atoms in ineffable buddha-fields; for kalpas numbering as the atoms in inconceivable buddha-fields;
for kalpas numbering as the atoms in immeasurable buddha-fields; for kalpas numbering as the atoms in inexpressible buddha-fields.
One enters eons as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;
thus, one is able to fully comprehend with wisdom all the eons contained within all future worlds.

Because of this comprehension, the mind further enters ten kinds of sustaining gates (*dhāraṇī-mukha*). What are these ten? They are: because of entering the sustaining power of the Buddhas, one attains the unspeakable...

Because they enter the sustaining power of the Dharma through being protected and remembered by Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, they attain ten kinds of light from dhāraṇīs and inexhaustible eloquence;
because they enter the sustaining power of practice through giving rise to the force of perfectly fulfilled and supreme vows, they cannot be eclipsed or overcome;
and because they enter the sustaining power of wisdom, there are no obstructions in the Buddha-dharmas they practice.
By entering the sustaining power of great compassion, one turns the pure wheel of Dharma that never regresses;
by entering the sustaining power of skillful mastery in the distinctions of words, one turns the wheel of all syllables and purifies the stages of all dharma-gates;

by entering the sustaining power of the lion’s birth-method, one opens the locks of the Dharma and emerges from the mire of desire; by entering the sustaining power of the treasury of wisdom, one constantly cultivates the practices of a bodhisattva.
Entering without rest through the sustaining power of spiritual friends; causing boundless sentient beings everywhere to attain purity through the sustaining power of non-abiding;
entering unspeakably unspeakable vast eons through the sustaining power of the Dharma;
and, O Sons of the Buddha, Mahāsattva Bodhisattvas, knowing through unimpeded skillful means that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is pure.
Having dwelt in this samādhi, they are skillfully established for unspeakably unspeakable kalpas;
they are skillfully established in unspeakably unspeakable buddha-fields; they are skillfully cognizant of unspeakably unspeakable varieties of sentient beings;
they are skillfully cognizant of the diverse characteristics of unspeakably unspeakable sentient beings; and they are skillfully cognizant of unspeakably unspeakable [phenomena].

Skillfully knowing the distinctions in the continuities of the habitual tendencies of the faculties and the various actions of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of beings through their common and differing karmic retributions; skillfully knowing the unspeakably unspeakable varieties of immeasurable defiled and pure reflections;
and skillfully knowing the manifestation of unspeakably unspeakable meanings of the Dharma through immeasurable syllables.
They skillfully know the various lineages, times, signs, teachings, and activities of the appearance of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddhas, as well as their entry into parinirvāṇa;
they skillfully know the unspeakably unspeakable gateways of infinite wisdom; and they skillfully know all unspeakably unspeakable supernormal powers.

O Son of the Buddha, it is like the rising of the sun in the world: all things such as villages, camps, cities, towns, palaces, houses, mountains, marshes, birds, beasts, forests, flowers, and fruits—all such various objects—are clearly seen by those who possess eyes.
O Son of the Buddha, the sunlight is impartial and without discrimination, yet it enables the eyes [to see].

Just as one perceives various signs, so too is this great samādhi: its essential nature is equal and free from discrimination, enabling the bodhisattva to know incalculably, incalculably many hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of distinct characteristics.
Son of the Buddha, when the bodhisattva-mahāsattva understands in this way, he causes all sentient beings to attain the ten [powers].
What are the eleven kinds of non-emptiness? First, the non-emptiness of seeing, which causes all sentient beings to give rise to roots of goodness.
Second, the non-emptiness of hearing, which causes all sentient beings to attain maturity. Third, the non-emptiness of co-residence, which causes the minds of all sentient beings to be tamed.
Fourth, the non-emptiness of initiation, which causes all sentient beings to act according to their words.
Fifth, because it brings about the thorough penetration of the meaning of all phenomena; sixth, because its practice is not in vain, purifying boundless worlds;

seventh, because its proximity is not in vain, severing the doubts of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of sentient beings in the presence of Tathāgatas in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields; eighth, because its vow is not in vain, in accordance with...
Eighth, by mindful of sentient beings so that they may perform supreme offerings and fulfill all their vows, one skillfully ensures that the Dharma is not in vain,
causing them all to abide in unimpeded liberation and pure wisdom. Ninth, by raining down the rain of Dharma not in vain,
one uses skillful means to reveal the practices of omniscience among sentient beings with unspeakably unspeakable faculties.
Tenth, because they abide in the Buddha-way, they manifest non-empty appearances, displaying boundless marks so that all sentient beings may receive their illumination.
Son of the Buddha, when Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this samādhi and attain these ten kinds of non-emptiness, the hosts of celestial kings all come to prostrate at their feet;
the hosts of dragon kings raise great clouds of incense; and the yakṣa kings...
The Asura Kings prostrate at his feet; the Garuḍa Kings respectfully make offerings while surrounding him before and behind;
all the Brahmā Kings come to entreat him; the Kiṃnara Kings and Mahoraga Kings all join in praising him;
the Gandharva Kings constantly come to attend upon him; and the hosts of human kings serve and make offerings to this Son of the Buddha.
This is the skillful wisdom of the sixth *samādhi*, the Great Treasury of Wisdom-Light, for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
[Treatise] Regarding the sixth *samādhi*, the Treasury of Wisdom-Light, it clarifies that this Bodhisattva is able to know all Buddhas throughout all future eons—
whether they have already preached the Dharma or have not yet preached it— and can fully comprehend them all.
One who knows the treasury of the light of wisdom (*jñānāloka-garbha*) does not depart from a single thought-moment yet encompasses the kalpas of the three periods of time;

thus, this wisdom is called a "treasury" (*garbha*). Other meanings are fully contained within the text itself. Among them, the names of the eight classes of kings and others were already explained based on the first assembly.
These names do not symbolize dharmas here, but rather they approach the Tathāgata for the sake of making offerings and paying respect to the Dharma.
[Sūtra] "O Son of the Buddha, what is the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva’s Samādhi of Knowing the Buddha-Adornments of All Worlds?
O Son of the Buddha, for what reason is this samādhi called 'Knowing the Buddha-Adornments of All Worlds'?
O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva abides in this samādhi, they are able to enter the worlds of the eastern direction in succession, and likewise [the other directions]."
Entering the worlds of the south, the west, the north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir—
all such worlds likewise he is able to enter in succession; in all of them he beholds the appearance of Buddhas in the world,
he beholds all the spiritual powers of those Buddhas, he beholds all the playful manifestations of the Buddhas, he beholds the vast majesty and virtue of the Buddhas, and he beholds them.
They see the supreme sovereignty of all Buddhas; they also see the Great Lion’s Roar of all Buddhas; they also see the various practices cultivated by all Buddhas;
they also see the manifold adornments of all Buddhas; they also see the miraculous transformations of the spiritual powers of all Buddhas;
and they also see the assemblies of all Buddhas—whether these assemblies are gathered like clouds, pure, vast, or of a single characteristic.
He clearly perceives all such things as assemblies of many forms, the locations where assemblies reside, assemblies that are being matured,
assemblies that are being disciplined, and the majestic power [of these assemblies]; he also sees assemblies equal in size to Jambudvīpa,
assemblies equal to the four continents, and assemblies equal to a small thousandfold world system.
Within the assemblies, they also see [the world] equal in measure to a thousandfold world system; within the assemblies, they also see it filled with a trichiliocosm;

within the assemblies, they also see it filled with hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields; within the assemblies, they also see it filled with incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) Buddha-fields;
and within the assemblies, they also see it filled with as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in a hundred Buddha-fields. They also see the assembly.
He also sees assemblies filling as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in a thousand Buddha-fields;
he also sees assemblies filling as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields;

he also sees assemblies filling as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in countless Buddha-fields; and he also sees assemblies filling as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in immeasurable Buddha-fields.
He also saw assemblies filling Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in boundless Buddha-fields;

he also saw assemblies filling Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in incomparable Buddha-fields; he also saw assemblies filling Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in incalculable Buddha-fields;
and he also saw assemblies filling Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms in inexpressible Buddha-fields.
In some Buddha-fields, they also saw assemblies filling as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in an inconceivable number of Buddha-fields;

in some Buddha-fields, they also saw assemblies filling as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in an immeasurable number of Buddha-fields; in some Buddha-fields, they also saw assemblies filling as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in an unspeakable number of Buddha-fields;
and in some Buddha-fields, they also saw assemblies filling as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in an unspeakably unspeakable number of Buddha-fields.
One may say that within as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in a Buddha-field, one also sees various Buddhas appearing in their respective assemblies and places of enlightenment,
manifesting various signs, at various times, in various lands, with various transformations, various supernormal powers,
various adornments, various masteries, various forms and dimensions, and various activities, O Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
He also saw his own body going to that assembly; he also saw his own body there preaching the Dharma;
he also saw his own body receiving and upholding the Buddha’s words; he also saw his own body thoroughly understanding dependent origination;
he also saw his own body dwelling in empty space; he also saw his own body abiding in the Dharma-body; he also saw his own body remaining free from defiled attachment; and he also saw his own body...

He perceives his own body as not abiding in conceptual discrimination; he perceives his own body as being free from weariness; he perceives his own body as universally entering into all forms of knowledge;

he perceives his own body as universally understanding all meanings; he perceives his own body as universally entering all stages (*bhūmi*); he perceives his own body as universally entering all realms of existence (*gati*);
he perceives his own body as universally knowing all skillful means (*upāya*); and he perceives his own body as universally abiding in the Buddha-state.
Previously, he also personally saw his own body universally entering all powers; he also personally saw his own body universally entering True Suchness (*tathatā*);
he also personally saw his own body universally entering the absence of contention (*araṇa*); and he also personally saw his own body universally entering all phenomena (*dharmas*).
When seeing in this way, he did not discriminate lands, did not discriminate sentient beings, did not discriminate Buddhas, and did not discriminate dharmas; nor did he cling to a self-body.
He clings neither to bodily action nor to mind nor to intellect; just as all phenomena do not discriminate their own nature nor discriminate sounds,
yet their nature does not abandon names nor cease them, so too the bodhisattva mahāsattva does not abandon practice,
acts in accordance with worldly affairs, and remains unattached to these two.
O Son of the Buddha, when Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas behold the Buddhas’ immeasurable light and color, their immeasurable forms and marks, perfectly accomplished, equal, and pure—
each appearing before them clearly and realized through direct perception; or when they see the various radiances of the Buddha’s body,
or the halo extending one fathom around the Buddha’s body, or the Buddha’s body possessing the color of the blazing sun, or they see the Buddha...
The body’s subtle light and color may appear as the Buddha’s body manifesting in a pure color; or the Buddha’s body manifesting in a golden-yellow color;
or the Buddha’s body manifesting in a vajra color; or the Buddha’s body manifesting in a deep blue color; or the Buddha’s body manifesting in a boundless color;
or the Buddha’s body manifesting in the color of a great blue maṇi jewel; or the Buddha’s body manifesting in [other colors].
Its measure may be seven cubits; or one may see the Buddha’s body at eight cubits, or nine cubits, or ten cubits;
or one may see the Buddha’s body at twenty cubits, or thirty cubits, and so on, up to a hundred cubits, a thousand cubits, or even seeing the Buddha’s body [at such measures].
They may see the Buddha’s body as one *krośa* in measure; or they may see the Buddha’s body as half a *yojana* in measure;
or they may see the Buddha’s body as one *yojana* in measure; or they may see the Buddha’s body as ten *yojanas* in measure; or they may see the Buddha’s body as a hundred *yojanas* in measure;

or they may see the Buddha’s body as a thousand *yojanas* in measure; or they may see the Buddha’s body as a hundred thousand *yojanas* in measure; or they may see the Buddha’s body as [the size of] Jambudvīpa.
Some see the Buddha’s body as the size of four continents; some see the Buddha’s body as the size of a small thousand-world system;

some see the Buddha’s body as the size of a medium thousand-world system; some see the Buddha’s body as the size of a great thousand-world system; some see the Buddha’s body as the size of a hundred great thousand-world systems;
some see the Buddha’s body as the size of a thousand great thousand-world systems; or some see the Buddha’s body as the size of a hundred thousand [great thousand-world systems].
They may see the Buddha’s body as the size of a great trichiliocosm; or they may see the Buddha’s body as the size of hundreds of thousands of billions of *nayutas* of great trichiliocosms;
or they may see the Buddha’s body as the size of countless great trichiliocosms; or they may see the Buddha’s body as the size of immeasurable great trichiliocosms;
or they may see the Buddha’s body as the size of boundless great trichiliocosms; or they may see the Buddha’s body as the size of incomparable [great trichiliocosms].
They may see the body of the Buddha as the measure of a thousand-world system; or they may see the body of the Buddha as the measure of incalculable great trichiliocosms;
or they may see the body of the Buddha as the measure of inexpressible great trichiliocosms; or they may see the body of the Buddha as the measure of inconceivable great trichiliocosms;
or they may see the body of the Buddha as the measure of immeasurable great trichiliocosms; or they may see the body of the Buddha as the measure of unspeakable great trichiliocosms.

Whether measuring a thousandfold world system or seeing the body of a Buddha as immeasurably vast as unspeakably unspeakable numbers of great trichiliocosms—O Son of the Buddha, a Bodhisattva thus perceives the Tathāgatas with immeasurable physical marks, immeasurable forms, immeasurable manifestations, immeasurable radiances, and immeasurable networks of light;
the extent of that light is equal to the Dharma-realm. In the Dharma...
Within the realms, there is nothing they do not illuminate, universally causing [beings] to give rise to unsurpassed wisdom.
Furthermore, they see the Buddha-body as being without defilement or attachment and without obstruction, supremely wondrous and pure.

O Son of the Buddha, when Bodhisattvas see the Buddha-body in this way, the Tathāgata’s body neither increases nor decreases, just as space remains unchanged within the hole of a mustard seed gnawed by an insect.
Nor does it diminish within countless worlds, nor does it expand; the bodies of those Buddhas are likewise thus.
When seen as large, they do not increase; when seen as small, they do not diminish. Son of the Buddha, it is like the lunar disc:
although the people of Jambudvīpa see its form as small, it does not thereby diminish for those who dwell within the moon.
Seeing their forms as large, yet they do not increase; so too it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who dwell in this samādhi.
According to the inclinations of their minds, they behold the various transformed manifestations of the Buddhas' bodies as they preach the Dharma through their speech;

they receive and uphold these teachings without forgetting them, yet the body of the Tathāgata neither increases nor decreases. O Son of the Buddha, it is like when sentient beings, after the end of their lives, are about to...
Just as at the time of birth one does not depart from what is seen by the mind, so too it is for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva who sees purity;
this son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, dwelling in this profound samādhi, accomplishes ten kinds of swift dharmas. What are these ten? They are: the swift increase of all practices.
May you swiftly fulfill your great vows and illuminate the world with the light of the Dharma; may you swiftly turn the wheel of Dharma through skillful means to deliver sentient beings;
may you swiftly manifest the pure buddha-fields of all Buddhas in accordance with the karma of sentient beings;
may you swiftly enter the ten powers through impartial wisdom; may you swiftly dwell together with all Tathāgatas; and may you swiftly destroy [all afflictions] through the power of great compassion.
They swiftly defeat the armies of Māra, quickly sever the doubts of sentient beings, and cause them to give rise to joy;
they swiftly manifest miraculous transformations according to [beings'] inclinations and purify all worlds through various sublime dharmas and modes of expression.
O Son of the Buddha, these Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas further attain ten kinds of Dharma-seals that seal all phenomena. What are the ten? First, they are identical with the past, future, and present.
First, they share with all Buddhas the equality of roots of goodness; second, they share with all Tathāgatas the attainment of the boundless wisdom-dharmakāya;
third, they share with all Tathāgatas the dwelling in the non-dual dharma;

fourth, they share with all Tathāgatas the observation of the infinite realms of the three periods of time as entirely equal; fifth, they share with all Tathāgatas the attainment of thorough penetration of the Dharma.
Sixth, they share with all Tathāgatas the unimpeded sphere of activity through the accomplishment of the ten powers;
seventh, they share with all Tathāgatas the permanent severance of dualistic conduct and abiding in the dharma of non-contention;

eighth, they share with all Tathāgatas the constant and uninterrupted teaching and transformation of sentient beings; ninth, they share with all Tathāgatas skillfulness in wisdom and skillfulness in meaning.
Tenth, they are able to skillfully observe that they are identical to all Tathāgatas, equal and non-dual with all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha, if a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva accomplishes this skillful means of the great samādhi of "knowing the Buddha-adornments of all worlds," they are one who has no teacher;
without relying on the instruction of another, they spontaneously enter into all Buddhas.
Because it is the Dharma, he is a Great Being (*mahāpuruṣa*), for he is able to awaken all sentient beings;
because he is pure, he knows that the nature of the mind is fundamentally pure; because he is supreme, he is able to deliver all the world;

because he is a source of consolation, he is able to enlighten all sentient beings; and because he is firmly established, he causes those who have not yet entered the lineage of the Buddhas to attain it.
Because they abide [in this], they are true knowers; because they enter the gateway to all-knowledge, they are free from divergent thoughts;

because their speech is non-dual, they are those who dwell in the treasury of the Dharma; because they vow to fully comprehend all Buddha-teachings, they are those who can rain down the rain of Dharma;
because they satisfy all according to the inclinations of the minds of sentient beings, O Son of the Buddha, it is like Śakra, the Lord of Devas, in regard to...
Within his topknot he placed a maṇi-jewel; by the power of that jewel, his majestic radiance became even more intense.
When the Śakra-devendra first obtained this jewel, he attained ten qualities that surpassed all those of the Trāyastriṃśa devas.
What are these ten? First, physical appearance; second, bodily form; third, manifestation; fourth, retinue; fifth, requisites; sixth...

First is voice; second is eloquence; third is the power of transformation; fourth is the power of birth; fifth is the power of vows; sixth is the sound of the voice; seventh is supernormal power; eighth is mastery;
ninth is wisdom and liberation; tenth is the application of knowledge. These ten kinds [of qualities] all surpass those of the Trāyastriṃśa devas. The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is likewise:
when first attaining this samādhi, they obtain ten kinds of vast treasuries of wisdom. What are these ten?
First, the wisdom that illuminates all Buddha-fields; second, the wisdom that knows the births of all sentient beings;

third, the wisdom that universally manifests transformations throughout the three periods of time; fourth, the wisdom that universally enters the bodies of all Buddhas; fifth, the wisdom that thoroughly penetrates all Buddha-dharmas;
sixth, the wisdom that universally gathers all pure dharmas; seventh, the wisdom that universally causes [all things] to be one...
Eighth is the wisdom of the pure universal eye that directly perceives all phenomena;
ninth is the wisdom of reaching the further shore through all sovereign powers; tenth is the wisdom that dwells securely in all vast dharmas, exhausting them all without exception.
Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva abides in this samādhi, they further attain ten kinds of supreme [wisdom].
What are the eleven aspects of the body of pure majestic power? First, in order to illuminate unspeakably unspeakable worlds, he emits unspeakably unspeakable wheels of light.
Second, in order to cause all worlds to become completely pure, he emits unspeakably unspeakable wheels of light of immeasurable colors and forms. Third, in order to...
First, they emit unspeakably unspeakable wheels of light in order to subdue sentient beings;
second, they manifest unspeakably unspeakable bodies in order to draw near to all Buddhas;
third, they rain down unspeakably unspeakable clouds of various exquisite fragrances and flowers in order to serve and make offerings to all Buddhas.

Sixth, in order to serve, honor, and make offerings to all Buddhas and to subdue all sentient beings, they manifest within each and every pore unspeakably unspeakable varieties of musical instruments.
Seventh, in order to bring sentient beings to maturity, they manifest unspeakably unspeakable varieties of immeasurable and sovereign spiritual transformations. Eighth.
This is for the purpose of inquiring about the Dharma at the abodes of all Buddhas throughout the ten directions who possess various names;
and this is for the purpose of ensuring that all sentient beings who see or hear [this] do so not in vain,
by manifesting unspeakably unspeakable varieties of immeasurable, pure forms and marks.

Tenth, their bodies are such that no one can see the crown of their heads, because they have produced unspeakably unspeakable sounds and speech in order to reveal and teach immeasurable secret dharmas to sentient beings.

Son of the Buddha, once Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas have attained these ten kinds of most pure and majestic bodies, they are able to cause sentient beings to attain ten kinds of perfection. What are these ten?
Eleventh, it enables sentient beings to behold the Buddha; second, it enables sentient beings to have deep faith in the Buddha;
third, it enables sentient beings to hear the Dharma; fourth, it enables sentient beings to know that there are Buddha-worlds;
fifth, it enables sentient beings to witness the Buddha’s supernatural transformations; sixth, it enables sentient beings to maintain mindfulness of him.
Seventh, it can cause the concentrated mind of sentient beings to reach perfection; eighth, it can cause sentient beings to enter the purity of the Buddha;
ninth, it can cause sentient beings to give rise to the bodhicitta; tenth, it can cause sentient beings to perfect the wisdom of a Buddha.
Son of the Buddha, after the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has caused sentient beings to attain these ten kinds of perfection, he further [acts for them]...
Sentient beings perform ten kinds of Buddha-activities. What are these ten? They are: performing Buddha-activities through sound in order to bring sentient beings to maturity;
performing Buddha-activities through physical form in order to discipline sentient beings; performing Buddha-activities through mindfulness in order to purify sentient beings;
and performing Buddha-activities by shaking the world-systems in order to cause sentient beings... [to attain awakening].
They perform the Buddha-work by awakening through skillful means so as to bring about birth apart from the evil realms;
they perform the Buddha-work by manifesting signs in dreams so as to prevent sentient beings from losing mindfulness;
they perform the Buddha-work by emitting great radiance so as to universally gather in all sentient beings; and they perform the Buddha-work by cultivating the practices of a bodhisattva.

He performs the Buddha-work by means of deeds in order to cause sentient beings to abide in supreme vows; he performs the Buddha-work by means of attaining perfect enlightenment in order to cause sentient beings to know that all phenomena are illusory;
he performs the Buddha-work by means of turning the sublime wheel of Dharma in order to preach the Dharma for the masses without missing the proper time;
he performs the Buddha-work by means of manifesting a long life in order to discipline all sentient beings; and he manifests parinirvāṇa...
Nirvāṇa performs the work of a Buddha because it knows that sentient beings become weary and exhausted;
O Son of the Buddha, this is the seventh skillful wisdom of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the great samādhi of thoroughly knowing the Buddha-adornments of all worlds.
[Treatise] Regarding the seventh samādhi, "Thoroughly Knowing the Buddha-Adornments of All Worlds":
this clarifies that this bodhisattva is able to universally enter all worlds throughout the ten directions; they see all the teachings and adornments of all Buddhas, perceiving them completely;
they serve and make offerings [to the Buddhas], and the Dharma they hear allows them to universally enter all realms of existence (*gati*).
The name is established because it exhaustively encompasses all things; the meaning of the text within this passage is already fully elucidated by the Sūtra itself.
[Sūtra] "O Son of the Buddha, what is the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s Samādhi of the Differentiated Bodies of All Sentient Beings?
O Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, they attain ten kinds of non-attachment. What are these?"
The ten are: non-attachment to all lands, non-attachment to all directions, non-attachment to all eons,
non-attachment to all assemblies, non-attachment to all phenomena, non-attachment to all bodhisattvas,
non-attachment to all bodhisattva vows, and non-attachment to all samādhis.
There is no attachment to any Buddhas, no attachment to any stages, and no attachment;
this is the tenth [stage], O Son of the Buddha. How does a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva enter this samādhi? How does he emerge from it?
O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva enters with his internal body and emerges with his external body; he enters with his external body and emerges with his internal body.
Entering one’s own body and arising in another’s body; entering another’s body and arising in one’s own body;
entering a human body and arising as a yakṣa; entering a yakṣa body and arising as a nāga; entering a nāga body and arising as an asura; entering an asura body and arising as a deva;
entering a deva body and arising as a Brahmā-king; entering a Brahmā-king body and arising in a body within the desire realm. Furthermore, entering among the devas...
Arising from hell, one enters among humans; arising from among humans, one enters other realms of existence;
arising as a thousand bodies, one enters a single body; arising as a single body, one enters a thousand bodies; arising as ten billion (*nayuta*) bodies, one enters a single body;
and arising as a single body, one enters among the multitude of beings in Jambudvīpa and arises among the multitude of beings in Aparagoyānī.
From among the multitude of beings in Aparagoyānī, he enters the multitude of beings in Uttarakuru and emerges from among the multitude of beings in Uttarakuru;
from among the multitude of beings in Pūrvavideha, he enters the multitude of beings in the three continents and emerges from among the multitude of beings in the three continents;
[from among the multitude of beings in the three continents,] he enters the four...
From among the multitudes of sentient beings in the four continents, they emerge; from among the multitudes of sentient beings in the four continents, they enter;
from among the multitudes of sentient beings distinguished by all oceans, they emerge; from among the multitudes of sentient beings distinguished by all oceans, they enter;

from among the multitudes of ocean deities, they emerge; from among the multitudes of ocean deities, they enter; from among the great waters of all oceans, they emerge; [they enter] all the waters of all oceans.
Entering all oceans of the great element of earth, they arise from all oceans of the great element of earth;
entering all oceans of the great element of fire, they arise from all oceans of the great element of fire;

entering all oceans of the great element of wind, they arise from all oceans of the great element of wind; entering all four great elements, they arise from all four great elements; entering the unconditioned...
Arising within the phenomena of birth, they enter the phenomena of non-arising; arising within Mount Sumeru, they enter the mountains of the seven treasures;
arising within the mountains of the seven treasures, they enter all lands with their various crops, forests, and Black Mountains;
arising within all lands with their various crops, forests, and Black Mountains, they enter all exquisite fragrances and flowers.

From within the manifestation of the jewel-adorned array of all wonderful fragrant flowers, they enter into the births of all sentient beings throughout the four continents of the lower and upper directions;

from within the manifestation of the births of all sentient beings throughout the four continents of the lower and upper directions, they arise within the assemblies of sentient beings in a small thousand-world system. From within the small thousand-world system, they arise... [and so on].

From among the multitudes of sentient beings in a world-system, they enter into the multitudes of sentient beings in a medium chiliocosm and emerge from among the multitudes of sentient beings in a medium chiliocosm;

from among the multitudes of sentient beings in a medium chiliocosm, they enter into the multitudes of sentient beings in a great trichiliocosm and emerge from among the multitudes of sentient beings in a great trichiliocosm;

from among the multitudes of sentient beings in a great trichiliocosm, they enter into the multitudes of sentient beings in hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of great trichiliocosms and emerge from among them.

From among the multitudes of sentient beings in hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of trichiliocosms, they enter the multitudes of sentient beings in countless worlds and emerge from the multitudes of sentient beings in countless worlds;

they enter the multitudes of sentient beings in immeasurable worlds and emerge from the multitudes of sentient beings in immeasurable worlds; they enter the multitudes of sentient beings in boundless Buddha-fields.
From within the assembly of sentient beings in boundless Buddha-fields, they emerge; from within the assembly of sentient beings in incomparable Buddha-fields, they enter;
from within the assembly of sentient beings in incomparable Buddha-fields, they emerge; from within the assembly of sentient beings in incalculable worlds, they enter;
from within the assembly of sentient beings in incalculable worlds, they emerge; from within the assembly of sentient beings in immeasurable worlds, they emerge... [and so forth].
One may enter from among the multitudes of sentient beings in conceivable worlds and emerge among the multitudes of sentient beings in inconceivable worlds;
one may enter from among the multitudes of sentient beings in inconceivable worlds and emerge among the multitudes of sentient beings in immeasurable worlds;
one may enter from among the multitudes of sentient beings in immeasurable worlds and emerge among the multitudes of sentient beings in ineffable worlds.

One may enter from among the assemblies of sentient beings of unspeakably unspeakable worlds into the assemblies of sentient beings of unspeakably unspeakable worlds, and emerge from among the assemblies of sentient beings of unspeakably unspeakable worlds; one may enter from among the assemblies of defiled sentient beings into the assemblies of defiled sentient beings, and emerge from among the assemblies of defiled sentient beings;
one may enter from among the assemblies of pure sentient beings into the assemblies of pure sentient beings.
Within the assembly, among the multitude of sentient beings subject to defilement, the sense-base of the eye arises from the sense-base of the ear;

the sense-base of the ear arises from the sense-base of the eye; the sense-base of the nose arises from the sense-base of the tongue; the sense-base of the tongue arises from the sense-base of the nose; the sense-base of the body arises from the sense-base of the mind;
the sense-base of the mind arises from the sense-base of the body; one’s own locus arises from another’s locus; another’s locus arises from one’s own locus; and a single atom arises [from these].

Entering countless world-microdusts within a single mote of dust, arising from countless world-microdusts; entering a single microdust within countless world-microdusts, arising from a single microdust;
entering the state of a śrāvaka and arising as a pratyekabuddha, entering the state of a pratyekabuddha and arising as a śrāvaka;

entering one's own body and arising as the body of a Buddha, entering the body of a Buddha and arising as one's own body; entering a single thought-moment and arising for a hundred million kalpas, entering a hundred million kalpas and arising in a single thought-moment.

Entering sameness while arising at a distinct time; entering a distinct time while arising in sameness; entering the past limit while arising in the future limit; entering the future limit while arising in the past limit;
entering the past limit while arising in the middle limit; entering the middle limit while arising in the past limit; entering the three periods of time while arising in a single moment;

entering a single moment while arising in the three periods of time; entering true suchness (*tathatā*) while arising in verbal expression; and entering verbal expression while arising in true suchness.

"O Son of the Buddha, it is as if there were a person possessed by a spirit, whose body trembles and cannot find rest, yet the spirit does not manifest its own form while causing the other's body to act.
In the same way, when a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, his own body enters meditative concentration while another's body arises from it;
or another's body enters meditative concentration while his own body arises from it. O Son of the Buddha, it is like a corpse..."
By the power of mantras, one is able to initiate activities, and whatever is undertaken is accomplished.

Although the corpse and the mantra are distinct from one another, they can harmonize to accomplish that task. O Son of the Buddha, it is the same for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwelling in this samādhi:
entering meditative absorption in one realm, they arise in a different realm; entering meditative absorption in a different realm, they arise in the same realm.
For example, just as a bhikṣu who has attained mastery over the mind can transform one body into many bodies or many bodies into one body—
wherein one body does not vanish while many bodies arise, nor do many bodies vanish while one body arises— in the same way,
when a bodhisattva mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, one body enters meditative absorption while many bodies emerge, or many bodies enter meditative absorption [while one emerges].
O Son of the Buddha, it is like the great earth: its essence is of one kind, yet the various crops that grow from it have diverse flavors.
Although the earth itself makes no distinction, the flavors differ. In the same way, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, there is no discrimination;
yet, while entering concentration with a single mode, they emerge in many modes, and enter concentration in many modes.

There is one kind of concentration that arises for the sons of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas; dwelling in this samādhi, they obtain ten kinds of dharmas of praise by which they are extolled.
What are these ten? They are as follows: because they have entered into suchness (*tathatā*), they are called Tathāgatas;
because they have awakened to all dharmas, they are called Buddhas; and because they are praised by all the worlds, they are called Dharmas.
Because the Teacher knows all phenomena (*dharma*), he is called the All-Knowing One (*sarvajña*). Because he is the refuge for all the world, he is called the Place of Reliance (*āśraya*).
Because he has thoroughly mastered the skillful means (*upāya*) regarding all phenomena, he is called the Guide (*nāyaka*).

Because he leads all sentient beings onto the path to omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), he is called the Great Guide (*mahānāyaka*). Because he is the lamp for all the world, he is called the Light (*prabhā*).
Having clarified the mind and perfected the purpose, having accomplished all that was to be done and abiding in unimpeded wisdom, he discerns and understands all phenomena;
therefore, he is called "One Endowed with the Ten Powers. Because he thoroughly penetrates all wheels of Dharma, he is called "The All-Seeing One.
O Sons of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, he further attains—
What are the ten kinds of radiant light that shine forth? They are as follows: the light of attaining equality with all Buddhas;
the light of attaining all worlds, being able to universally adorn and purify them;
the light of reaching all sentient beings to tame and subdue them; and the light of immeasurable fearlessness, manifesting the Dharma-realm as the field for its exposition.
By teaching, one attains the light of non-differentiation, because one knows that all phenomena lack any manifold nature;

by teaching, one attains the light of skillful means, because one enters into the limit of detachment from all phenomena; by teaching, one attains the light of reality, because the mind is equanimous within the limit of detachment from all phenomena;
by teaching, one attains the light of spiritual transformations throughout all worlds. Thus it is said.
Because the empowerment bestowed by the Buddhas never ceases, he attains the light of excellent contemplation;

because he reaches the shore of mastery over all Buddhas, he attains the light of the *tathatā* (suchness) of all phenomena; and because he skillfully expounds everything within a single pore—these are the ten.
Son of the Buddha, when a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi, he further attains ten kinds of non-action.
What are these ten? They are: the non-action of bodily karma; the non-action of verbal karma; the non-action of mental karma; the non-action of supernormal powers;
the non-action of the realization that all phenomena lack intrinsic nature; the non-action of knowing that karma is indestructible;
the non-action of non-discriminative wisdom; the non-action of the wisdom of non-arising; and the non-action of knowing that phenomena are without cessation.
To act in accordance with the letter without violating the meaning, and to perform no action—this is the tenth, O Son of the Buddha.
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells in this samādhi of immeasurable realms and various distinctions, it is as follows: entering one and arising many; entering many and arising one;
entering together and arising differently; entering differently and arising together; entering the subtle and arising the coarse; and entering the coarse and arising the subtle.

Entering the great and arising from the small; entering the small and arising from the great; entering in forward order and arising in reverse order; entering in reverse order and arising in forward order;
entering the bodiless and arising with a body; entering that which has a body and arising bodiless; entering the signless and arising with signs; entering that which has signs and arising signless;
and entering arising within arising—such as these are all the sovereign spheres of this samādhi, O Son of the Buddha.

For example, it is like a magician who, having mastered a mantra, is able to manifest various distinct forms and appearances. Although the mantra and the illusion are distinct, the mantra is able to produce the illusion;

the mantra is merely sound, yet it can magically create all manner of visible forms known by the eye-consciousness, all manner of sounds known by the ear-consciousness, all manner of fragrances known by the nose-consciousness, and all manner of tastes known by the tongue-consciousness.
Just as various tastes are known by body-consciousness and various tactile objects are known by mind-consciousness, so too it is for the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwelling in this samādhi:
he enters meditative absorption within sameness and emerges from it within difference; he enters meditative absorption within difference and emerges from it within sameness.
Son of the Buddha, it is like the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven and the Asuras hearing [the same sound].
At the time of battle, the devas were victorious and the asuras were defeated and retreated.

The body of the Asura King was seven hundred yojanas tall, and surrounded by fourfold armies numbering in the tens of millions, he used the power of *māyā* (illusory arts) to lead his host simultaneously into the pores of a lotus fiber.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this, having already fully accomplished [this feat].
The ground of illusory wisdom and illusory wisdom itself are the Bodhisattva; the Bodhisattva is himself illusory wisdom.

Therefore, one can enter meditative absorption within non-differentiated phenomena and emerge from it within differentiated phenomena; enter meditative absorption within differentiated phenomena and emerge from it within non-differentiated phenomena.
O Son of the Buddha, it is like a farmer who sows various seeds in a field; once they are sown, the fruits arise.
It is likewise for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who abide in this samādhi: they enter meditative absorption within one [atom] and emerge from it within many;

they enter meditative absorption within many and emerge from it within one. O Son of the Buddha, it is like when the red and white elements of a man and woman unite, and a sentient being takes birth therein;
at that time, it is called the stage of the kalala. From this point on, it develops in successive stages.
Due to the power of wholesome karma, throughout the ten months in the mother’s womb, all limbs and members are fully developed,
the sense faculties are unimpaired, and the mind and intellect are clear. Although the *kalala* stage and those six sense faculties have distinct physical forms,
through the power of karma they are able to be successively perfected, experiencing various fruits of both similar and dissimilar types.

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva is also like this: from the stage of the *kalala* of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), through the power of faith, understanding, and aspiration, his mind gradually increases, becoming vast, spontaneous, and sovereign;
he enters meditative absorption within non-existence and arises within existence, and enters meditative absorption within existence and arises within non-existence.
Son of the Buddha, it is as if a dragon palace stands supported by the earth and does not depend upon empty space.
The dragons dwell within their palaces, yet they do not reside in the void, and yet they are able to raise clouds that fill the sky.
When people look up, what they see as palaces should be known as all being *gandharva* cities and not the actual dragon palaces.
O Son of the Buddha, although the dragons dwell below, the clouds spread above; likewise, it is with the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who abide in this samādhi. Regarding this:
Entering the signless from the signful, arising from the signful to enter the signless, O Son of the Buddha:
it is like the palace where the Great Brahma King Mahāprabha dwells, named the Most Victorious Pure Treasury of All Worlds.
Within this great palace, one universally beholds all the four continents, celestial palaces, dragon palaces, and yakṣa palaces throughout the trichiliocosm.
The palaces of the gandharvas, the palaces of the asuras, the palaces of the garuḍas, the palaces of the kiṃnaras, and the palaces of the mahoragas;
the human dwellings and the three evil realms; Mount Sumeru and various other mountains;
the great oceans, rivers, streams, marshes, springs, cities, towns, villages, forests, and all manner of precious things—all such diverse adornments.
From the farthest reaches of the Great Cakravāḍa mountains to the finest motes of dust suspended in the air,
all are manifested within the Brahma palaces as clearly as one sees the reflection of one's face in a bright mirror.
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas abide in this Samādhi of the Great Body of the Differentiations of All Sentient Beings, they know various lands, see various Buddhas, and deliver various beings.

Planting various roots of merit, realizing various dharmas, accomplishing various practices, fulfilling various understandings, entering various samādhis, manifesting various supernormal powers, attaining various wisdoms, and abiding in various moments of time—O Son of the Buddha, these are the ten kinds of supernormal powers to the further shore of which this Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva has arrived.
What are the ten? They are: arriving at the exhaustion of all Buddhas...
Reaching the perfection of spiritual powers that pervade the dharma-realm like space; reaching the perfection of the ultimate, undifferentiated, and sovereign spiritual powers of Bodhisattvas;
reaching the perfection of spiritual powers for initiating the vast vows and practices of Bodhisattvas, entering the gates of the Tathāgatas, and performing Buddha-works;
and reaching the perfection of spiritual powers that can shake all worlds and all realms, causing them all to become completely pure.
Having reached the shore beyond, they attain mastery in knowing that the inconceivable karma and its fruits of all sentient beings are all like illusions and transformations;
having reached the shore beyond, they attain mastery in knowing the distinctions of the entry and exit of the coarse and subtle aspects of all samādhis;
having reached the shore beyond, they are able to courageously enter the realm of the Tathāgatas and therein generate the Great [Vow].
May they reach the other shore of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), being able to manifest as Buddhas, turn the wheel of Dharma, and subdue sentient beings,
causing them to produce the seed of Buddhahood, enter the Buddha-vehicle, and swiftly achieve the perfection of supernormal powers;
may they reach the other shore of knowing all unspeakable secret phrases and syllables, thereby turning the wheel of Dharma for hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of [beings]...
By expounding the dharma-gate of the ineffable, they all attain the purity of supernormal powers and reach the other shore;
without depending on days, nights, years, months, or kalpas, they are able to manifest supernormal powers throughout the three periods of time in a single thought-moment. This is the tenth [quality].
O sons of the Buddha, this is called the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva’s eighth excellence: the Great Samādhi of the Differentiated Bodies of All Sentient Beings.
Skillful Wisdom.

[Treatise]: The eighth is the Samādhi of the Differentiated Bodies of All Sentient Beings. This clarifies that by entering this samādhi, one is able to manifest the bodies of Buddhas and other differentiated bodies of sentient beings, appearing according to each type; hence its name is established.
Furthermore, because he is able to enter the samādhis of sameness and difference, and of direct and reverse order, his name is established accordingly;
the remaining meanings are fully contained within the text itself. *The Combined Commentary on the New Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha*, Fascicle Sixty-nine.
