A Concordance of the Sutras and Treatises, Chapter Thirty-Three, Part One: “The Inconceivable Dharma of the Buddha.
[Treatise] In order to explain this chapter, four sections are established: first, an explanation of the title of the chapter; second, an explanation of the purpose for its inclusion.
Third, the explanation of the master who preaches the Dharma; fourth, the word-by-word commentary on the meaning. First, regarding the explanation of the title of this chapter:

this chapter derives its name from the three karmas of the Tathāgata—body, speech, and mind. Why is it called "inconceivable" (*acintya*)? Because it cannot be reached by thought (*citta*), it is called "inconceivable.
Because it cannot be reached by consciousness (*vijñāna*), names, or words, it is called "inexpressible" (*avācya*). Thus, by means of thought, it is termed "inconceivable."
The mind is called "thinking" because it is a mind that grasps at objects; thus, one speaks of "meaning" and "names" as being "consciousness.

These are worldly conventions and linguistic measures, which are false estimations beyond the reach of the ordinary mind. Because the ordinary emotions have ceased and consciousness has been extinguished, one relies on the functioning of wisdom (*jñāna*).

Therefore, it is clarified that the functioning of the Tathāgata’s wisdom is not something known by the false sentiments and deliberations of the conscious mind; for when emotions cease and conceptualization is stilled, this is wisdom.

The manifestation must now occur through the power of the samādhi of cultivated skillful means; when the deluded consciousness is cleared away and correct wisdom manifests before one, it is called "inconceivable.
Regarding the purpose of this second chapter, "The Explanation of the Names":

since the preceding chapter explained the suitability of the Bodhisattvas' abodes for gathering and sustaining sentient beings, this chapter clarifies the wisdom capable of transforming them; therefore, it is titled "The Buddha."

This chapter has come forth because this inconceivable state is not something produced by the deliberations of non-sentient beings or the consciousnesses of sentient beings; rather, it functions through the self-nature of wisdom that is all-pervasive, and thus does not act merely in response to external objects.
Third, regarding the explanation of the Dharma-preacher: the name of the Bodhisattva who preaches the Dharma is Blue Lotus Treasury (*Nīlotpala-garbha*).
This clarifies that the Bodhisattvas of the preceding chapter have attained the Dharma, perfected patience, and achieved mastery over the mind, and are therefore so named.
O Mind-King, this clarifies that fundamental wisdom (mūla-jñāna) is perfectly luminous, pure, and unstained;
it is named the "Blue Lotus" because this fundamental wisdom, through its perfect luminosity, can give rise to the wisdom of differentiation (pratyavekṣaṇā-jñāna), which is called the "Treasury.

Thus, addressing the Bodhisattva Padmagarbha (Lotus-Treasury) clarifies the fundamental wisdom while addressing the wisdom of differentiation, so as to manifest their mutual accomplishment. Therefore, the names of the Three Vehicles are first attained.

The wisdom that takes the ultimate as its object follows the wisdom that takes the conventional as its object; this attainment of the One Vehicle is identical and undivided, for there is no sequence of before or after throughout the three periods of time.

Thus, the Bodhisattva Blue Lotus Treasury spoke to the Bodhisattva Lotus Treasury, explaining this inconceivable Dharma of the sovereign power of wisdom regarding the body, eyes, ears, nose, and so forth within the Tathāgata’s inconceivable buddha-field.
Therefore, the intent of this chapter is to clarify that by means of the fundamental wisdom of the sovereign mind-king (*cittarāja*),
one employs the wisdom of differentiation (*prabheda-jñāna*) to teach and transform sentient beings; because this constitutes the great sovereign function of the Buddha’s own enlightened activities,

eight chapters of the sutra— from the "Asaṃkhyeya" chapter to the "Manifestation" chapter— are presented here as a general discourse on the mental practices and dharmic rules within the stage of Buddhahood.
Because the first five stages share the same ultimate destination, they do not deviate from the essence of the thirteen samādhis—the universal radiance of wisdom (*samantaprabhā-jñāna*).
Since these eight chapters of the Dharma-gate and this entire scripture exist [within that essence], the names of the Bodhisattvas are all established based on the virtues of their own Buddha-wisdom;
thus, the teachings are explained in this way so that they may be easily understood. Fourth, the explanation of the meaning according to the text:

In this single chapter of the sutra, the text is divided into thirty-five sections: the first three sections consist of the questions, the Buddha’s empowerment, and the benefits obtained by the blue lotus; the final thirty-two sections constitute the answers.
[Sūtra] At that time, there were bodhisattvas within the great assembly who had this thought: "How inconceivable are the buddha-fields!
How inconceivable are the original vows of the Buddhas! How inconceivable is the lineage of the Buddhas!
How inconceivable is the appearance of the Buddhas! How inconceivable is the body of the Buddhas! How inconceivable is the voice of the Buddhas!"
Why is the voice inconceivable? Why is the wisdom of the Buddhas inconceivable? Why is the sovereignty of the Buddhas inconceivable?
Why is the unimpededness of the Buddhas inconceivable? Why is the liberation of the Buddhas inconceivable?
Why is it inconceivable?

[Treatise] First, from "At that time" onwards, up to "How is it inconceivable?", there are six lines of scripture clarifying the section on how the great assembly of bodhisattvas conceived the thought of questioning the Buddha regarding ten kinds of inconceivabilities.
[Sūtra] At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of the bodhisattvas, empowered them through his spiritual power,
sustained them with wisdom, illumined them with radiance, and filled them with majestic authority, causing the Bodhisattva Blue Lotus Treasury to abide in the fearlessness of the Buddhas,
enter the Dharma-realm of the Buddhas, attain the sovereign supernormal powers of the Buddhas' majestic virtue, and obtain the vast and unimpeded [wisdom] of the Buddhas.
Observing and knowing the sequence of the lineage of all Buddhas, they dwell in the ineffable skillful means of the Buddha-dharma.

[Treatise] Second: From "At that time, the World-Honored One" down to "the skillful means of the Buddha-dharma," four and a half lines of scripture clarify the section on how the Tathāgata empowers the Bodhisattva Blue Lotus Treasury with ten dharmas.
[Sūtra] At that time, the Bodhisattva Blue Lotus Treasury was able to penetrate the unimpeded Dharma-realm;
he was able to dwell securely in profound practices free from obstructions; he was able to fulfill the great vows of Samantabhadra; and he was able to know and see all Buddha-dharmas.
With a heart of great compassion, he observed sentient beings, desiring to purify them, and he practiced with diligent application without ever becoming weary.
Diligently receiving and practicing all the dharmas of the bodhisattvas, giving birth to the Buddha-wisdom within a single thought-moment,
fully understanding all inexhaustible gates of knowledge, and being completely endowed with dharanis and eloquence, he addressed the Bodhisattva Padmagarbha by the Buddha’s spiritual power,
saying: "O Son of the Buddha!"
[Treatise] Third: From the passage beginning "At that time, the Bodhisattva Blue Lotus Treasury" down to the Buddha’s address to the Bodhisattva Lotus Treasury,
"O Son of the Buddha, there are six practices," this section of the sūtra clarifies how the Bodhisattva Blue Lotus Treasury, having received the Buddha’s empowerment,
intends to answer the ten questions posed by the assembly of bodhisattvas through ten kinds of sovereign wisdom regarding the ten dharmas.
[Sūtra] The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have immeasurable abodes: namely, they abide in great compassion; they abide in manifesting various bodies to perform the Buddha-work;
they abide in the impartial mind that turns the pure wheel of Dharma; they abide in the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*) to preach immeasurable teachings;
they abide in all inconceivable Buddha-dharmas; they abide in a pure voice that pervades immeasurable lands; and they abide in the ineffable...
Abiding in the profound *dharmadhātu*, he manifests all supreme supernatural powers (*abhijñā*) and is able to reveal the ultimate Dharma that is free from all obstructions.
[Treatise] From "the fourth, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones" down to "the ultimate Dharma free from all obstructions," there is...
The *Wuxing jing* (Sūtra on the Five Elements) clarifies that the Bodhisattva Blue Lotus Treasury universally enumerates ten kinds of immeasurable abodes of all Buddhas.

Having provided a general response to the ten kinds of questions posed by the great assembly above, the following section concerning the ten kinds of immeasurable abodes comprises, in total, thirty-two kinds of immeasurables.
These are universally pervasive and unimpeded, encompassing both the general and the specific, as well as identity and difference, and formation and disintegration.
The "Gate of the Sovereign Indra’s Net" answers the ten previous questions by means of the Buddha’s inconceivable Dharma;

thus, within these thirty-two types of gates that mutually interpenetrate and universally pervade like Indra’s net, there are three hundred and twenty types of responses regarding their numerical count to answer the ten previous questions. These three hundred and twenty types of Indra’s nets...
Within this Dharma-gate of interpenetrating nets, the Buddha’s inconceivable nature is elucidated as inexhaustible within the inexhaustible, layer upon layer and limitlessly upon limitlessly.
As in each successive section, ten dharmas are inherently complete; these are clarified by the sutra itself, so there is no need for further detailed analysis.
[Sūtra] O Sons of the Buddha, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of dharmas that universally pervade the infinite and boundless Dharma-realm.
What are these ten? They are as follows: First, all Buddhas possess boundless bodies whose physical marks are pure;
they enter universally into all realms of existence without being stained or attached. Second, all Buddhas possess boundless, unobstructed eyes; within a single...
They are able to clearly perceive all phenomena; they possess the boundless, unobstructed ears of all Buddhas, capable of understanding all sounds;
they possess the boundless noses of all Buddhas, which can reach the shore of the sovereign mastery of all Buddhas;
and they possess the broad and long tongues of all Buddhas, which produce wondrous sounds that pervade the entire Dharma-realm.
All Buddhas possess boundless bodies that accord with the minds of sentient beings, causing all to behold them;
all Buddhas possess boundless intentions, abiding in the unimpeded and equal Dharma-body;
all Buddhas possess boundless, unimpeded liberation, manifesting inexhaustible great supernormal powers; all Buddhas possess boundlessness... [and so forth].
In the world-realm of Ultimate Purity, he manifests various Buddha-lands according to the inclinations of sentient beings, fully endowed with immeasurable and diverse adornments;

yet within them, he gives rise to no defiled attachment. All Buddhas possess boundless Bodhisattva practices and vows, having attained the perfection of wisdom and mastery in spiritual play, being able to thoroughly penetrate all Buddha-dharmas. Such is this Son of the Buddha.
Regarding the ten kinds of Buddha-dharma of the Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas, which pervade the boundless reaches of the Dharma-realm:
O Sons of the Buddha, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of wisdom that arise in every thought-moment. What are these ten?
They are as follows: In a single thought-moment, all Buddhas are able to manifest the descent from the heavens into immeasurable worlds. All...
All Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, are able to manifest the taking of birth by Bodhisattvas in immeasurable worlds;
all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, are able to manifest the renunciation of household life and the pursuit of the Way in immeasurable worlds;
all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, are able to manifest the attainment of equal enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree in immeasurable worlds.
All perfectly awakened Buddhas, in a single thought-moment, are able to manifest throughout immeasurable worlds the turning of the sublime wheel of Dharma;

all Buddhas, in a single thought-moment, are able to manifest throughout immeasurable worlds the teaching and transforming of sentient beings and the making of offerings to all Buddhas; all Buddhas, in a single thought-moment, are able to manifest throughout immeasurable...
In an inconceivable variety of worlds, all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment,
are able to manifest infinite worlds with their various adornments; all Tathāgatas, through their sovereign power, are the treasury of omniscience,
and all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, are able to manifest infinite worlds and infinities [of further manifestations].
In a single thought-moment, all Buddhas are able to manifest within countless pure realms the various faculties,
various degrees of diligence, and various modes of practice and understanding of the Buddhas of the three periods of time throughout immeasurable worlds,
as they attain equal and perfect enlightenment within those three periods. These, O sons of the Buddha, are the ten ways in which the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, do not fail.
At that time, what are the ten? They are: all Buddhas do not miss the proper time for attaining equal and perfect enlightenment;

all Buddhas do not miss the proper time for bringing those with whom they have a karmic connection to maturity; all Buddhas do not miss the proper time for bestowing predictions of enlightenment upon bodhisattvas;

all Buddhas do not miss the proper time for manifesting spiritual powers in accordance with the minds of sentient beings; all Buddhas, in accordance with... [the text continues]... [all Buddhas do not miss the proper time for... [and so forth].
All Buddhas manifest bodies for the sake of sentient beings without missing the proper time; all Buddhas abide in great equanimity without missing the proper time;
all Buddhas enter villages without missing the proper time; all Buddhas gather those of pure faith without missing the proper time;
all Buddhas discipline wicked sentient beings without missing the proper time; all Buddhas manifest... [the remainder of the sentence is incomplete in the source].
To contemplate the spiritual powers of all Buddhas without missing the proper time—this is the tenth.
Sons of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of incomparable and inconceivable realms of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. What are these ten? They are as follows:

First, all Buddhas, by sitting in a single cross-legged posture, pervade the infinite worlds of the ten directions. Second, all Buddhas, when speaking a single phrase of meaning, are able to... [all] completely... [understand].
He reveals all Buddha-dharmas: how all Buddhas, by emitting a single ray of light, are able to universally illumine all worlds;
how all Buddhas, within a single body, are able to manifest all bodies;
and how all Buddhas, within a single location, are able to manifest all worlds. All Buddhas, within a single...
Within their wisdom, they are able to decisively discern all phenomena without any obstruction;

all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, are able to travel everywhere throughout the worlds of the ten directions; all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, fully manifest the immeasurable majesty and virtue of the Tathāgatas;
and all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, universally take as their object of focus the Buddhas of the three periods of time and...

The minds of sentient beings are free from confusion; all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, are identical in essence and non-dual with all Buddhas of the past, future, and present—this is the tenth.
O sons of the Buddha, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, are able to give rise to ten kinds of wisdom. What are these ten?
They are as follows: all Buddhas know that all phenomena have no destination toward which they tend, and yet...
All Buddhas know that all phenomena are without body, yet they are able to produce the wisdom of pure bodies;
all Buddhas know that all phenomena are originally non-dual, yet they are able to produce the wisdom of awakening;
all Buddhas know that all phenomena are without self and without sentient beings.

Yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom that disciplines sentient beings; all Buddhas know that all phenomena are originally without marks, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom that thoroughly understands all marks;

all Buddhas know that no world-systems undergo arising or ceasing, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom that thoroughly understands arising and ceasing; all Buddhas know that all phenomena have no creator...
By performing [these deeds], they are able to give rise to the wisdom that knows the fruits of karma;
all Buddhas know that all phenomena are beyond verbal expression, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom that thoroughly understands verbal expression;

all Buddhas know that all phenomena are neither defiled nor pure, yet they are able to give rise to the wisdom that knows defilement and purity; all Buddhas know that all phenomena are without birth...
To be able to give rise to the wisdom that understands arising and ceasing while remaining in cessation is the tenth [attribute], O sons of the Buddha.

There are ten kinds of universal entry into the Dharma of all Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. What are these ten? They are as follows: All Buddhas possess pure and wondrous bodies that universally enter the three periods of time;
all Buddhas are fully endowed with the three kinds of mastery to universally transform sentient beings. All...
All Buddhas are fully endowed with all dhāraṇīs, enabling them to universally receive and uphold all Buddha-dharmas.
All Buddhas are fully endowed with the four kinds of eloquence, universally turning the pure wheel of Dharma.
All Buddhas are fully endowed with impartial great compassion, never abandoning or forsaking any sentient being.
All Buddhas are fully endowed with profound meditative concentration and constantly and universally observe all sentient beings.
All Buddhas are fully endowed with the roots of goodness for benefiting others, taming sentient beings without ceasing.
All Buddhas are fully endowed with an unimpeded mind, universally able to abide peacefully within the entire Dharma-realm.
All Buddhas are fully endowed with unimpeded spiritual power, universally manifesting all Buddhas of the three periods of time in a single thought-moment.
All Buddhas are fully endowed with unimpeded wisdom, universally establishing the kalpas of the three periods of time in a single thought-moment.
These are the ten [qualities], O Sons of the Buddha. There are ten kinds of vast dharmas that are difficult for the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, to be believed and accepted. What are these ten?
That is to say, all Buddhas are able to utterly destroy all Māras; all Buddhas are able to subdue all non-Buddhists;
all Buddhas are able to discipline all sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice;
and all Buddhas are able to travel to all worlds to transform and guide all classes of beings.
All Buddhas are fully able to know and realize the profound realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*).
All Buddhas are fully able, by means of their non-dual body, to manifest various bodies that fill all worlds.

All Buddhas are fully able, by means of pure sounds, to give rise to the four analytical eloquences (*pratisaṃvid*) and preach the Dharma without interruption; for all who have faith and receive it, the merit shall never be in vain.
All Buddhas are able to manifest within a single pore as many Buddhas as there are atoms in all worlds,
appearing without interruption; all Buddhas are able to display within a single atom as many lands as there are atoms in all worlds, complete with every kind of sublime and wondrous adornment.
Constantly turning the sublime wheel of Dharma within them to teach and transform sentient beings, the atoms do not become large and the worlds do not become small;

they always abide in the dharma-realm through realized wisdom. All Buddhas have fully penetrated the pure dharma-realm, using the light of wisdom to shatter the darkness of worldly delusion, causing all to attain clear understanding of the Buddha-dharma, following along as it is.
To come and abide within the ten powers is the mark of the ten sons of the Buddha. The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of great merit that are pure and free from fault.
What are these ten? They are: first, all Buddhas possess great majestic virtue and are pure and free from fault;
second, all Buddhas are born into the family of the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time, and their lineage is well-disciplined and pure, free from fault.
All Buddhas are pure in their abiding nowhere throughout the future, being free from faults and pure;
all Buddhas are pure in their non-attachment to all phenomena of the three periods of time, being free from faults and pure;
all Buddhas know that various natures are but a single nature, coming from nowhere, being free from faults and pure; all Buddhas [are pure] regarding the prior limit.
Their future merit shall be inexhaustible, equal to the Dharma-realm, and pure, free from fault;
they shall possess the boundless physical forms of all Buddhas, pervading the lands of the ten directions to discipline all sentient beings according to the time, being pure and free from fault;
they shall attain the four fearlessnesses of all Buddhas, free from all terrors, and roar the great lion’s roar with clarity amidst the assemblies.
All Buddhas, who have distinguished all phenomena and are pure by being free from faults, enter parinirvāṇa throughout unspeakably unspeakable eons;
yet when sentient beings hear their names, they obtain immeasurable merit, no different from the merit of the Buddhas being present in person.
All Buddhas, who are pure by being free from faults, dwell afar in worlds that are unspeakably unspeakable in number.
If there are sentient beings therein who maintain single-minded right mindfulness, they shall all behold that which is free from fault and utterly pure; this is the tenth.
O Sons of the Buddha, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of ultimate purity. What are these ten? They are:
the ultimate purity of the great vows of all Buddhas in the past; the ultimate purity of the Brahma-conduct maintained by all Buddhas...
Ultimately purifying all Buddhas' freedom from worldly delusions; ultimately purifying the adorned lands of all Buddhas;
ultimately purifying all retinues of all Buddhas; ultimately purifying all lineages of all Buddhas;
ultimately purifying the physical bodies, marks, and signs of all Buddhas...
They are ultimately pure in the dharma-body of all Buddhas, which is unstained and ultimately pure;
they are ultimately pure in the omniscient wisdom of all Buddhas, which is without obstruction and ultimately pure;

they are ultimately pure in the liberation, mastery, and fulfillment of what was to be done by all Buddhas, having reached the further shore and being ultimately pure—these, O Son of the Buddha, are the ten qualities of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
In all worlds and at all times, there are ten kinds of Buddha-activities. What are these ten?

First, if there are sentient beings who mindfully recollect [the Buddha] with single-minded devotion, he manifests himself before them. Second, if there are sentient beings whose minds are not disciplined or compliant, he preaches the Dharma for them.
Third, if there are sentient beings who are able to give rise to pure faith, he ensures that they will certainly attain... [the state of non-arising].

The four roots of merit of measure are: first, if there are sentient beings who can enter the stage of the Dharma (dharmatā), they shall all manifest realization and there will be nothing they do not understand;
second, teaching and transforming sentient beings without weariness or fatigue; third, traveling to and fro through all Buddha-fields without obstruction;
fourth, never abandoning any sentient being through great compassion; and fifth, constantly manifesting transformation bodies (nirmāṇakāya) without interruption.
Ninth is the mastery of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) that never ceases; tenth is abiding in the *dharmadhātu* while being able to observe it universally.
These are the ten, O Son of the Buddha. The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of inexhaustible oceans of wisdom regarding the Dharma.
What are these ten? They are: the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom regarding the boundless *dharmakāya* of all Buddhas; the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom regarding all... [the text continues].
The Dharma of the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of the infinite Buddha-activities of all Buddhas; the Dharma of the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom within the realm of the Buddha-eye of all Buddhas;
the Dharma of the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom of the immeasurable, countless, and inconceivable roots of goodness of all Buddhas;
the Dharma of the inexhaustible ocean of wisdom through which all Buddhas universally rain down the nectar of all sublime Dharmas. All Buddhas...

The Dharma of the Buddha’s Praise of the Inexhaustible Ocean of Wisdom of the Buddha’s Merits; the Dharma of the Inexhaustible Ocean of Wisdom of the Various Vows and Practices Cultivated by All Buddhas in the Past;
the Dharma of the Inexhaustible Ocean of Wisdom through which All Buddhas Constantly Perform Buddha-Works Throughout the Limits of the Future;
and the Inexhaustible Ocean of Wisdom through which All Buddhas Fully Know the Mental Activities of All Sentient Beings.
The Dharma is the adornment of the merit and wisdom of all Buddhas, unsurpassed by any and an inexhaustible ocean of wisdom;
such is the Dharma. These, O Son of the Buddha, are the ten [qualities]. Furthermore, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have ten kinds of eternal laws. What are these ten? They are as follows:
first, all Buddhas constantly practice all the *pāramitās*; second, all Buddhas are eternally detached from all phenomena.
All Buddhas are ever-deluded by the world, yet they are always endowed with great compassion; all Buddhas always possess the ten powers;
all Buddhas always turn the wheel of Dharma; all Buddhas always manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment for the sake of sentient beings;
all Buddhas always delight in taming all sentient beings; and the minds of all Buddhas are always in right mindfulness, non-dual.
Regarding this Dharma, after all Buddhas have transformed sentient beings, they constantly manifest entry into *nirupadhiśeṣa-nirvāṇa*;

for the realm of each and every Buddha is boundless. This is the tenth. O Sons of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of ways in which the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, expound the immeasurable Dharma-gates of the Buddhas. What are these ten? They are as follows: all Buddhas expound...
All Buddhas expound the gateways of the immeasurable realms of sentient beings; all Buddhas expound the gateways of the immeasurable practices of sentient beings;
all Buddhas expound the gateways of the immeasurable karmic fruits of sentient beings; all Buddhas expound the gateways of the immeasurable means of transforming sentient beings;
all Buddhas expound the gateways of the immeasurable purification of sentient beings. All Buddhas...
All Buddhas proclaim immeasurable gateways of bodhisattva practices; all Buddhas proclaim immeasurable gateways of bodhisattva vows;
all Buddhas proclaim immeasurable gateways regarding the eons of formation and destruction of all worlds;
all Buddhas proclaim immeasurable gateways of purifying Buddha-lands through the profound resolve of bodhisattvas; all Buddhas proclaim immeasurable [gateways of] one...
The gate of the successive appearance of all Buddhas of the three periods of time in all worlds throughout various kalpas;

the gate of all Buddhas expounding the wisdom of all Buddhas—these, O sons of the Buddha, are the ten ways in which the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, perform the work of a Buddha for the sake of sentient beings. What are these ten? They are as follows: all Buddhas manifest physical bodies.
All Buddhas perform the Buddha-work for sentient beings by emitting sublime sounds;
all Buddhas perform the Buddha-work for sentient beings through that which they receive; all Buddhas perform the Buddha-work for sentient beings through that which they do not receive;
all Buddhas perform the Buddha-work for sentient beings by means of earth, water, fire, and wind.
All Buddhas perform buddha-work for sentient beings by manifesting all objects of perception through the sovereign power of their spiritual faculties;
all Buddhas perform buddha-work for sentient beings through their various names and titles;
all Buddhas perform buddha-work for sentient beings by means of the realms of their buddha-fields; and all Buddhas purify and adorn their buddha-fields.
To perform the work of a Buddha for the sake of sentient beings while remaining silent and without speech—this is how all Buddhas perform the work of a Buddha for sentient beings.
These, O sons of the Buddha, are the ten [qualities]. Furthermore, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of most supreme dharmas. What are these ten? They are as follows:
the great vows of all Buddhas are firm and solid, incapable of being thwarted or destroyed; whatever they say must be done, and their words are never in vain.

First, all Buddhas, desiring to fulfill all merits, cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva throughout all kalpas until the end of the future without ever giving rise to weariness; second, all Buddhas, desiring to subdue all sentient beings,
travel to unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds and act thus for the sake of all sentient beings without interruption.
All Buddhas universally observe with great compassion the two kinds of sentient beings—those who have faith and those who are hostile—with impartiality and without distinction.
From their initial aspiration until their attainment of Buddhahood, all Buddhas never retreat or lose the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*).
All Buddhas accumulate immeasurable meritorious virtues and dedicate them all toward the nature of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).

All worlds are ultimately free from defilement and attachment; all Buddhas, having trained in the three types of action under various Buddhas, practice only the conduct of a Buddha and not that of the two vehicles, dedicating it all toward the nature of omniscience to achieve unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
All Buddhas emit great rays of light, which shine equally upon all places and...
They illuminate the teachings of all Buddhas, causing the minds of all bodhisattvas to become pure and fulfill all-encompassing wisdom.

All Buddhas abandon worldly pleasures, remaining neither greedy nor stained, while universally wishing that the world may be free from suffering and attain happiness, devoid of all frivolous proliferation.
All Buddhas take pity on sentient beings who undergo various sufferings, and they protect the lineage of the Buddhas.
Practicing the realm of the Buddhas, they transcend birth and death and attain the stage of the Ten Powers; this is the tenth, O sons of the Buddha.
There are ten kinds of unobstructed abidings of the Honored Ones from whom all Buddhas emerge. What are these ten? They are as follows:
first, all Buddhas are able to go to all worlds with unobstructed abiding; second, all Buddhas are able to abide in all worlds... [and so forth].
The unobstructed dwelling: all Buddhas are able to move, stand, sit, and lie down in all worlds without obstruction;
the unobstructed dwelling: all Buddhas are able to expound the True Dharma in all worlds without obstruction;
the unobstructed dwelling: all Buddhas are able to abide in the Tuṣita Heaven palace in all worlds without obstruction.
All Buddhas are able to abide without obstruction within the entire Dharma-realm;
all Buddhas are able to abide without obstruction at all sites of enlightenment throughout the three periods of time;
all Buddhas are able, in every thought-moment, to observe the mental activities of all sentient beings, teaching and subduing them through the three kinds of mastery.
The unobstructed dwelling wherein all Buddhas are able, with a single body, to abide in the presence of immeasurable and inconceivable Buddhas and in all places to benefit sentient beings;

the unobstructed dwelling wherein all Buddhas are able to reveal and teach the true Dharma spoken by immeasurable Buddhas; and the unobstructed dwelling—these, O Son of the Buddha, are the ten [unobstructed dwellings] of the Buddhas.
The Blessed One possesses ten kinds of supreme, unsurpassed adornments. What are these ten? They are as follows:
all Buddhas are fully endowed with the primary marks and secondary signs; this is the first supreme, unsurpassed bodily adornment of the Buddhas.
All Buddhas are fully endowed with sixty kinds of vocal qualities, and each of these vocal qualities possesses five hundred [sub-varieties].
Each individual part is adorned with immeasurable hundreds of thousands of pure sounds;
amidst all assemblies throughout the Dharma-realm, they utter the great lion’s roar without any fear, expounding the profound meaning of the Tathāgata’s Dharma.
All sentient beings who hear it are filled with joy, and according to their faculties and inclinations, they are all brought to subdual. This is the characteristic of all Buddhas.
The second is the supreme, unsurpassed adornment of speech: all Buddhas are endowed with the ten powers, the great samādhis, and the eighteen unique qualities;
their mental activities and spheres of action are unimpeded in their thorough penetration; they have attained all Buddha-dharmas without exception;
and they take as their adornment the adornment of the dharma-realm, which is the object of the minds of sentient beings within the dharma-realm.
To clearly perceive within a single thought-moment the distinct differences of all actions in the past, future, and present—
this is the third supreme and unsurpassed mental adornment of all Buddhas. All Buddhas are able to emit countless rays of light,
each ray having an unspeakable number of light-nets as its retinue, universally illuminating the entire world.
They extinguish all darkness in every buddha-field, manifesting the appearance of immeasurable buddhas whose bodies are equal and entirely pure; the buddha-deeds they perform are never in vain,
enabling sentient beings to reach the stage of non-retrogression— this is the fourth supreme, unsurpassed adornment of light of all buddhas.
Whenever all Buddhas manifest a smile, they emit from their mouths hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asamkhyeyas of light rays;
each individual ray possesses infinite, inconceivable, and manifold colors that universally illuminate all worlds throughout the ten directions.
Within the great assembly, they utter words of truth and bestow immeasurable, innumerable, and inconceivable [blessings].

To deliberate upon bestowing the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* upon sentient beings constitutes the fifth supreme and unsurpassed adornment of the smile manifested by all Buddhas, which is free from worldly delusion. All Buddhas possess the Dharma-body, which is pure and unimpeded;
they have attained ultimate penetration into all phenomena and abide within the Dharma-realm, which is without limit or boundary.
Although they dwell in the world, they are not mixed with worldly things; they realize the true nature of the world and practice supramundane dharmas.
Their path of speech is cut off, and they transcend the aggregates, elements, and sense bases. This is the sixth most supreme and unsurpassed adornment of the Dharma-body of all Buddhas.
All Buddhas possess immeasurable, eternal, and wondrous radiance, with unspeakably unspeakable varieties of color and form.
They consider it to be majestic and beautiful, a treasury of radiance that gives birth to immeasurable, perfect light which shines universally throughout the ten directions without obstruction;
this is the seventh supreme, unsurpassed, and eternally wondrous light-adornment of all Buddhas.
All Buddhas possess boundless exquisite colors, lovely exquisite colors, and pure exquisite colors that accord with the mind.
The manifested exquisite forms outshine all exquisite forms within the three realms; these unsurpassed exquisite forms have reached the further shore.
This constitutes the eighth most supreme and unsurpassed excellence of exquisite form among all Buddhas.

All Buddhas are born from the lineage of the Buddhas of the three periods of time; they have accumulated a multitude of jewels of various virtues, reaching ultimate purity, being free from all faults, and transcending the world.

Adorned with the most supreme, pure, and wondrous conduct among all dharmas that are subject to censure and slander, they have fully accomplished the lineage of the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*), which is pure and incapable of being reviled;
this is the ninth most supreme and unsurpassed lineage-adornment of all Buddhas. All Buddhas adorn their bodies with the power of great compassion (*mahāmaitrī*).
Ultimately pure, free from all craving, with bodily formations forever stilled and minds well-liberated, they never weary those who behold them;
through great compassion, they rescue and protect all worlds as the foremost field of merit and supreme recipients.
Out of pity, they benefit all sentient beings, causing them all to increase their immeasurable accumulations of merit and wisdom—these are the Buddhas.
The tenth is the adornment of the merit of supreme, unsurpassed great loving-kindness and great compassion; these are the ten, O Son of the Buddha.
What are the ten kinds of sovereign dharmas possessed by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones? They are as follows:
first, all Buddhas have attained mastery over all phenomena, clearly penetrating various bodies of phrases and bodies of flavor, and they possess the eloquence to expound all dharmas.

Unimpeded eloquence is the first sovereign dharma of all Buddhas; in teaching and transforming sentient beings, they never miss the proper time, preaching the True Dharma according to their aspirations and inclinations to bring them all to subdual without interruption—this is the second sovereign dharma of all Buddhas.
All Buddhas are able to cause [the light of wisdom] to pervade the entirety of the realm of empty space...
They cause all worlds, adorned with immeasurable varieties of ornaments, to quake in six ways, causing those worlds to either rise or fall,
expand or contract, or join together or disperse, yet without ever harming a single sentient being;
the beings therein do not perceive, know, doubt, or wonder at this— this is the third sovereign power of the Buddhas.
All Buddhas, by means of their supernormal powers, are able to completely adorn and purify all worlds;
in a single thought-moment, they universally manifest the adornments of all worlds. These various adornments could not be fully described even if one were to speak for incalculable eons;
they are all free from defilement, pure, and incomparable. All matters concerning the adornment and purification of every Buddha-field are made equal.
Entering into a single buddha-field is the fourth sovereign dharma of all Buddhas: seeing a single sentient being who should be transformed,
all Buddhas remain for that being’s sake for unspeakably unspeakable eons, even until the end of the future limit,
sitting cross-legged with body and mind free from weariness, focusing their minds on mindfulness without ever neglecting it.
They thus bring beings to subdual without missing the opportune moment; as they do for a single sentient being, so it is for all sentient beings.

This is the fifth sovereign dharma of all Buddhas: all Buddhas are able to go everywhere throughout all worlds, to all places where Tathāgatas travel, never for a moment abandoning any part of the ten directions of the entire Dharma-realm.
In each of the ten directions, there are immeasurable oceans of worlds; in each ocean of worlds, there are immeasurable species of worlds.
By means of his spiritual power, a Buddha reaches them all in a single thought-moment and turns the unimpeded, pure wheel of Dharma.
This is the sixth sovereign dharma of all Buddhas. All Buddhas, desiring to discipline and subdue all sentient beings, maintain this mindfulness.
While realizing *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* within a single thought-moment, he has neither already awakened to nor will he yet awaken to all Buddha-dharmas;
furthermore, he does not abide in the stage of one still in training (*śaikṣa*), but possesses all-knowing vision, unimpeded and infinite wisdom,
and infinite mastery in teaching and taming all sentient beings— this is [the state of a Bodhisattva].
The seventh sovereign dharma of all Buddhas: all Buddhas are able to perform the Buddha-work of the ear-sphere through the eye-sphere;
they are able to perform the Buddha-work of the nose-sphere through the ear-sphere; they are able to perform the Buddha-work of the tongue-sphere through the nose-sphere;

they are able to perform the Buddha-work of the body-sphere through the tongue-sphere; they are able to perform the Buddha-work of the mind-sphere through the body-sphere; and they are able [to perform the Buddha-work] through the mind-sphere.
In all worlds, within each and every mundane and supramundane realm, they are able to perform immeasurable and vast Buddha-activities; this is the eighth sovereign dharma of all Buddhas.
Within each and every pore of their bodies, all sentient beings can be accommodated, and the bodies of each and every sentient being [are likewise contained].
Equal in extent to unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, yet without any crowding, each and every sentient being is able to traverse countless worlds with every step;
thus proceeding in succession throughout the end of countless eons, they see all Buddhas appearing in the world to teach and transform sentient beings,
turning the pure wheel of Dharma and revealing the ineffable teachings of the past, future, and present.

Throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space, all sentient beings in every realm of existence—whether receiving bodies, maintaining postures, coming and going, or possessing various articles of enjoyment—are fully provided for, yet without any obstruction therein; this is the ninth sovereign dharma of all Buddhas.
In a single moment of thought, all Buddhas manifest as many [bodies] as there are atoms in all worlds.

As for each of these Buddhas, they all attain equal and perfect enlightenment upon lion thrones within the Lotus Treasury in the World of Vast Adornments of Various Exquisite Lotuses throughout the entire Dharma-realm; they manifest the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas,
just as they do in the World of Vast Adornments of Various Exquisite Lotuses, so too throughout the entire Dharma-realm.
Inexpressibly, inexpressibly many worlds— adorned with various ornaments, possessing various realms, various forms, various manifestations, and spanning various numbers of eons— are purified;
as they appear in a single thought-moment, so too do they appear within every single thought-moment throughout immeasurable,
boundless, incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, such that in one thought-moment all things manifest, and in one thought-moment they abide for the immeasurable.
Having never employed even the slightest power of skillful means—this is the tenth sovereign dharma of all Buddhas.
O Sons of the Buddha, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of immeasurable, inconceivable, and perfected Buddha-dharmas. What are these ten?
They are as follows: every single pure mark of all Buddhas is endowed with a hundred merits; all Buddhas have fully accomplished them.
All Buddhas have fully accomplished all Buddha-dharmas; all Buddhas have fully accomplished all roots of goodness;
all Buddhas have fully accomplished all merits; all Buddhas are able to teach and transform all sentient beings;
all Buddhas are able to act as the lords for all sentient beings; all Buddhas have fully accomplished [all these qualities].
In all pure Buddha-fields, all Buddhas have fully accomplished the wisdom of all-knowledge;
all Buddhas have fully accomplished the physical body with its marks and signs, such that those who see them obtain benefit and their merit is never in vain;
all Buddhas possess the equal and true Dharma of all Buddhas; and once all Buddhas have performed the work of a Buddha, there are none who do not manifest themselves.
Entering into nirvāṇa—this is the tenth [topic], O sons of the Buddha. There are ten kinds of skillful means belonging to the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.

What are these ten? They are as follows: First, all Buddhas thoroughly understand that all phenomena are free from conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*), yet they are able to reveal the roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*) of the Buddhas; this is the first skillful means. All Buddhas know the one...
All phenomena are entirely unobservable; they do not know one another, and there is neither bondage nor liberation, neither sensation nor accumulation, and no attainment.
Having attained mastery and reached the ultimate further shore, one knows the reality of all phenomena as it is—neither different nor distinct—and thus attains sovereignty.
Being without self and without sensation, one does not destroy the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), having already attained great mastery.
The earth constantly observes the entire dharma-realm; this is the second skillful means.
All Buddhas are forever detached from all signs and their minds dwell nowhere, yet they are able to know all things without confusion or error.
Although they know that all signs lack intrinsic nature, they are able to skillfully enter into them according to their true essence, while also manifesting non-existence.

To measure the form-body (*rūpakāya*) and all the various, inexhaustible signs of adornment of the pure Buddha-lands, to gather the lamp of wisdom, and to extinguish the delusions of sentient beings—this is the third skillful means.
All Buddhas abide in the *dharmadhātu*, not abiding in the past, future, or present; within the nature of suchness (*tathatā*), there is no coming, going, or being present.

By means of the nature of worldly phenomena, one is able to expound upon the appearance in the world of immeasurable Buddhas of the past, future, and present, causing those who hear it to universally perceive the realm of all Buddhas; this is the fourth skillful means:
that the body, speech, and mental actions of all Buddhas are without fabrication, without coming, without going, and without abiding, being utterly detached.
All numerical dharmas reach the further shore of all phenomena and constitute the treasury of all teachings; they possess immeasurable wisdom,
thoroughly comprehend various mundane and supramundane dharmas, and with unimpeded wisdom,
manifest immeasurable sovereign spiritual powers to subdue all sentient beings throughout the dharma realm— this is the fifth skillful means of all Buddhas.
He knows that all phenomena are invisible, neither one nor different, neither measurable nor immeasurable, neither coming nor going, and that they all lack intrinsic nature;

yet he does not contradict the various phenomena of the world. Within the non-sovereignty of the All-Knowing One, he perceives all phenomena, and while exercising mastery over phenomena by extensively expounding them, he always dwells peacefully in the true nature of *tathatā*.
This is the sixth skillful means: all Buddhas, at a single moment, empower all times such that beings possessing pure roots of goodness enter the stage of certainty without attachment;

regarding time—such as days, months, years, eons, and the formation and destruction of worlds—they neither abide in nor abandon it, yet they are able to manifest day and night, as well as the initial, middle, and final periods.
For one day, seven days, half a month, one month, one year, a hundred years, one kalpa, many kalpas, inconceivable kalpas, unspeakable kalpas,
and even until the end of all future kalpas, they constantly turn the sublime wheel of Dharma for the sake of sentient beings,
without interruption, without retreating, and without rest; this is the seventh skillful means of all Buddhas.
Constantly abiding in the *dharmadhātu*, they achieve the infinite fearlessnesses of all Buddhas, as well as incalculable eloquence, immeasurable eloquence, inexhaustible eloquence,
uninterrupted eloquence, boundless eloquence, unique eloquence, endless eloquence, true eloquence,
and the eloquence that skillfully reveals all phrases and all phenomena according to their respective faculties, natures, inclinations, and understandings.

The teaching of various dharma-gates—inexpressible, inexpressible hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of sūtras—each excellent in the beginning, middle, and end, and entirely consummate; this is the eighth skillful means:
that all Buddhas, abiding in the pure dharma-realm, know that all dharmas are fundamentally without names, having no name of the past and no name of the present.
There is no future; there is no name for sentient beings, no name for non-sentient beings, no name for lands, no name for non-lands,
no name for dharmas, no name for non-dharmas, no name for merit, no name for non-merit, no name for bodhisattvas,
no name for buddhas, no name for number, no name for non-number, no name for arising, no name for cessation, and no name for existence.
There is no name, nor is there a non-name; there is no single name, nor are there various names. Why is this? Because the intrinsic nature (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena (*dharma*) is inexpressible.
All phenomena have no direction and no location; they cannot be spoken of as gathered, nor can they be spoken of as dispersed;
they cannot be spoken of as one, nor can they be spoken of as many. Sound cannot reach them, and speech is entirely cut off, even though it follows the various conventions of the world.

To speak of speech as having no object of attachment and no volitional construction, being far removed from all false conceptual clinging, and thus ultimately reaching the other shore—this is the ninth skillful means. All Buddhas know that the intrinsic nature of all phenomena is quiescent and unarisen;
therefore, it is not form, because it is free from discursive proliferation; it is not sensation, because it has no names or numbers.
Therefore, it is not perception because there is no mental formation; it is not volitional formations because there is no grasping; it is not consciousness because there is no place of entry;

it is not the sense bases because there is nothing to be apprehended; and it is not the elements. Nevertheless, it does not destroy the original nature of all phenomena, for they are unarisen like space.
Thus, all phenomena are entirely empty and quiescent: there is no karma or its fruit, no cultivation, and no realization.
Because it is without birth, it is neither numbered nor unnumbered; neither existent nor non-existent; neither arising nor ceasing; neither defiled nor pure;
neither entering nor exiting; neither abiding nor non-abiding; neither disciplined nor undisciplined;
neither sentient beings nor non-sentient beings; neither life-span nor non-life-span; neither with causes and conditions nor without causes and conditions—and yet it is able to...

To thoroughly understand all sentient beings of the categories of those fixed in rightness, those fixed in error, and those who are undetermined, and to preach the sublime Dharma for them so that they may reach the other shore,
achieve the ten powers and the four fearlessnesses, roar the lion’s roar, possess all-knowledge, and abide in the realm of the Buddhas—
this, O Son of the Buddha, is the tenth skillful means; this is how the Buddhas accomplish these ten [qualities].
O Sons of the Buddha skilled in expedient means, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of vast buddha-activities that are immeasurable,
boundless, and inconceivable; none among the gods or humans of all worlds can know them,
nor can any of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas of the past, future, or present know them, except by the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata.
What are these ten powers? They are as follows: all Buddhas manifest birth in the Tuṣita heavens across all worlds throughout the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm;

they cultivate the bodhisattva practices and perform great Buddha-works through immeasurable physical forms, immeasurable majestic virtues, immeasurable radiance, immeasurable voices, immeasurable speech, and immeasurable...
The sphere of activity of immeasurable wisdom within samādhi encompasses all beings— humans, gods, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, asuras, and so forth—
through great compassion that is unimpeded and great pity that is ultimately equal,
benefiting all sentient beings by causing some to be born in the heavens, others to be born as humans, purifying their faculties, or harmonizing their minds, or...
At times he teaches the distinctions of the three vehicles, and at times he teaches the perfect single vehicle, universally delivering all beings so that they may transcend birth and death;

this is the first vast buddha-work. O Son of the Buddha, all Buddhas descend from Tuṣita Heaven into their mothers' wombs, observing the dharma of taking birth through ultimate samādhi as being like an illusion, like a transformation, and like a shadow.

Like space and like a mirage in the heat, they experience according to their inclination; they enter the immeasurable and unobstructed Dharma of non-contention (*araṇā*), give rise to non-attached wisdom, and, being pure through freedom from desire, they accomplish a vast and wondrous treasury of adornments.
Taking their final birth, they dwell in great jewel-adorned pavilions and perform the Buddha-work, whether by means of supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*) or by means of the Right [Dharma].
They perform Buddha-works by means of mindfulness; or they perform Buddha-works by manifesting supernatural powers; or they perform Buddha-works by manifesting the sun of wisdom;
or they perform Buddha-works by manifesting the vast realms of all Buddhas; or they perform Buddha-works by manifesting the immeasurable radiance of all Buddhas;
or they perform Buddha-works by entering countless, vast samādhis; or they manifest... from... [the text continues].

Those various samādhis arise and perform the work of a Buddha. O Son of the Buddha, at that time the Tathāgata, while within the mother’s womb, manifests various appearances for the sake of benefiting all the world and performs the work of a Buddha;
that is to say, he may manifest his initial birth, or manifest as a youth, or manifest in the palace, or manifest leaving home, or again manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment.
Whether awakening, or manifesting the turning of the sublime wheel of Dharma, or manifesting entry into parinirvāṇa—
in this way, through various skillful means, they perform Buddha-works in all directions, all networks, all revolutions, and in all kinds of worlds.
This is the second vast Buddha-work, O Son of the Buddha, of all [Buddhas].
The Buddha’s all wholesome karmas are already purified, and his knowledge of all births is already luminously clear;
yet, by means of the dharma of birth, he guides the deluded multitudes to awaken them. For the sake of sentient beings, he manifests birth in a royal palace while practicing all manner of goodness.
All Buddhas have already abandoned all forms of desire, palaces, and the music of courtesans, having no attachment whatsoever.
He constantly contemplates that all conditioned things are empty and devoid of intrinsic nature, and that all objects of pleasure are entirely unreal.
Upholding the pure precepts of the Buddha to ultimate perfection, he contemplates his inner palace, consorts, and attendants with great compassion.

Contemplating all sentient beings as illusory and unsubstantial, he gives rise to great loving-kindness. Contemplating the entire world as having not a single thing worth desiring, he generates the Great [Resolve].
Rejoicing in all dharmas, having attained mastery over the mind, they give rise to great equanimity (*mahopekṣā*) and are endowed with the qualities of a Buddha.
They manifest bodies whose physical marks are perfected within the *dharmadhātu*, and their retinues are pure; yet they remain unattached to anything whatsoever.

Using voices that accord with the various types of beings, they expound the Dharma for the masses, causing them to develop a profound sense of weary detachment from worldly phenomena, and they demonstrate the fruits of attainment according to their respective practices.
Furthermore, by means of skillful expedients, he teaches and transforms those who have not yet matured according to their needs, bringing them to maturity;
he brings those already matured to liberation, performing the work of a Buddha so that they do not regress.
Moreover, with a vast heart of compassion, he constantly expounds various dharmas for the sake of sentient beings and manifests three kinds of mastery to cause them to open [to the truth].
Having realized the mind, one attains purity; though dwelling within the inner palace and being beheld by all, one performs Buddha-works throughout all worlds.

With great wisdom and great diligence, one manifests various supernatural powers of the Buddhas—unimpeded and inexhaustible—constantly abiding in the three types of skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*), namely, the ultimate purity of physical action (*kāya-karma*).
Their verbal karma is pure and always proceeds in accordance with wisdom; their mental karma is profoundly deep and free from obstruction.
By these skillful means, they benefit sentient beings; this is the third vast buddha-activity.

O Son of the Buddha, all Buddhas manifest various adorned palaces, yet they observe them with detachment, renounce them, and go forth into homelessness, desiring to cause sentient beings to understand.
Knowing that all worldly dharmas are merely false imaginings, impermanent, and subject to decay and ruin, he gives rise to profound wearying detachment and does not produce defiled attachment;
forever severing the afflictions of worldly craving and love, he cultivates pure conduct to benefit sentient beings.

At the time of his renunciation, he discards secular decorum and abides in the dharma of non-contention, fulfilling his original vows and immeasurable merits, extinguishing [all obscurations] with the light of great wisdom.
In this world of delusion and darkness, he is the unsurpassed field of merit for all the world;

he constantly praises the Buddha’s virtues for the sake of sentient beings, causing them to plant roots of goodness within the Buddha’s presence. With the eye of wisdom, he perceives the true meaning.

Furthermore, for the sake of sentient beings, he praises and explains the purity and faultlessness of the renunciant life, leading them forever to transcendence. He is the lofty banner of wisdom for the world.
This is the fourth vast buddha-work: all the sons of the Buddha, all Buddhas endowed with omniscience, have fully known and seen immeasurable dharmas;
they have attained supreme perfect enlightenment beneath the bodhi tree, subdued all māras, and possess preeminent majesty and virtue;
their bodies fill all worlds, and the deeds performed through their spiritual powers are boundless and inexhaustible regarding all things.
Having attained mastery over all meanings practiced by wisdom, they have fully perfected the cultivation of all merits;
their seats of enlightenment are complete with adornments that pervade all worlds throughout the ten directions.
Seated upon them, the Buddhas turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma, proclaiming all the practices and vows of Bodhisattvas, revealing the infinite realms of all Buddhas, and causing all Bodhisattvas...
They all attain awakening and enter into the practice of various kinds of pure and wondrous conduct; furthermore, they are able to instruct and guide all sentient beings,
causing them to plant roots of goodness and be born within the ground of the Tathāgata’s equality, to abide in the boundless wondrous practices of all Bodhisattvas,
and to accomplish all supreme dharmas of merit— [this applies to] all worlds, all sentient beings, and all Buddhas.
To thoroughly understand all phenomena in every buddha-field, all bodhisattvas, all methods of instruction,
all taming throughout the three periods of time, all spiritual transformations, and the inclinations and desires of the minds of all sentient beings,
and thereby perform the work of a Buddha— this is the fifth vast buddha-work. O Son of the Buddha, it is the turning of the irreversible wheel of Dharma by all Buddhas.
He turns the wheel of Dharma that is immeasurable, so as to cause all bodhisattvas not to regress; he turns the wheel of Dharma that awakens all, so that all worlds may fully understand;
he turns the wheel of Dharma of the treasury of wisdom regarding all phenomena, so as to let out the great lion’s roar with fearlessness;
he turns the wheel of unimpeded Dharma, which opens the door to the treasury of Dharma and removes the veil of darkness, being equal to space.

Because it is empty, he turns the wheel of the Dharma that is free from attachment; because he contemplates all phenomena as being neither existent nor non-existent, he turns the wheel of the Dharma that illuminates the world;
because he causes all sentient beings to purify their Dharma-eye, he turns the wheel of the Dharma that reveals all-knowledge;
because it pervades all phenomena of the three periods of time, he turns the single wheel of the Dharma common to all Buddhas, for all Buddha-dharmas are not mutually contradictory.

Therefore, all Buddhas perform inconceivable Buddha-works by means of such immeasurable, innumerable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Dharma-wheels, according to the differences in the mental activities of sentient beings;
this is the sixth vast Buddha-work. O Son of the Buddha, all Buddhas enter into all royal capitals and cities for...
They perform the work of a Buddha for all sentient beings within the capitals of human kings, the capitals of deva kings,
nāga kings, yakṣa kings, gandharva kings, asura kings, garuḍa kings, kiṃnara kings, mahoraga kings,
rākṣasa kings, and piśāca kings— in short, within the cities and capitals of all such kings.

At that time, the great earth shook, and a brilliant light shone everywhere. The blind regained their sight, the deaf regained their hearing, the insane regained their minds, and the naked obtained clothing.
All those who were afflicted by sorrow and suffering attained peace and happiness.

All musical instruments sounded spontaneously without being struck, and all ornaments—whether worn or not—emitted wondrous sounds. Among all sentient beings who heard them, there was none who did not [experience joy].
They take delight in the pure marks and signs of the physical bodies of all Buddhas, which are so perfect that those who behold them never tire;
these bodies perform the work of a Buddha for sentient beings— whether by looking around, observing, moving, stretching,
walking, standing, sitting, lying down, remaining silent, speaking, manifesting supernatural powers, or preaching the Dharma.
If there are any such instructions, all of them are performed as Buddha-works for the sake of sentient beings; that is, all Buddhas,
throughout all the various oceans of the minds and inclinations of countless sentient beings in all worlds, universally exhort them to mindfully recollect the Buddha,
constantly and diligently observe him, plant various roots of goodness, and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva, while praising the Buddha’s physical marks as being most subtle and supreme.

All sentient beings find it difficult to encounter [a Buddha]; yet if there are those who, upon seeing him, give rise to faith, then all immeasurable wholesome dharmas will arise within them, and they will gather the merits of a Buddha, becoming universally pure.
Having thus praised the merits of the Buddha, his emanations go everywhere throughout the worlds of the ten directions, causing all sentient beings to behold, revere, contemplate, and observe him.
By serving and making offerings, planting various roots of goodness, and gaining the Buddha’s joy, they increase the seed of Buddhahood and shall all attain enlightenment.

Through such practices, they perform the work of a Buddha: either manifesting physical forms for the sake of sentient beings, or emitting sublime sounds, or simply smiling to inspire faith and delight;
they pay homage with their heads at his feet, bowing with palms joined, extolling and praising him.
They perform the work of a Buddha by inquiring after one's well-being and daily life; all Buddhas, through such immeasurable, innumerable, ineffable,
and inconceivable varieties of Buddha-works, throughout all worlds,
act according to the inclinations of the minds of sentient beings by means of the power of their original vows, the power of great compassion, the power of all-knowledge, and skillful means.
To teach and transform all beings so that they are fully subdued is the seventh vast buddha-work. Sons of the Buddha,
all Buddhas may perform buddha-works while dwelling in forest hermitages (āraṇya), or while dwelling in places of tranquility,
or while dwelling in secluded retreats, or while dwelling in the abodes of Buddhas, or while dwelling in the three...

They perform buddha-works while remaining obscure; or they perform buddha-works while dwelling alone in gardens and groves; or they perform buddha-works while concealing their bodies so as not to appear;
or they perform buddha-works while abiding in profound wisdom; or they perform buddha-works while abiding in the incomparable realm of all Buddhas;
or they perform buddha-works while abiding in various invisible bodily activities that accord with the inclinations and desires of sentient beings.
They perform the Buddha-work through skillful means and edification without ceasing;
they may perform the Buddha-work by seeking all-knowledge in the form of a celestial being, or in the form of a nāga,
yakṣa, gandharva, asura, garuḍa, kiṃnara, mahoraga, human, non-human, or other such bodies, seeking all-knowledge.
They perform Buddha-works through wisdom; or they perform Buddha-works by seeking all-knowledge through the bodies of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or bodhisattvas;
or they perform Buddha-works sometimes by preaching the Dharma and sometimes by remaining silent;
or they perform Buddha-works by speaking of a single Buddha or of many Buddhas; or they perform Buddha-works by explaining all the practices and all the vows of the bodhisattvas.

Performing Buddha-works through a single practice and vow; or teaching that the single practice and single vow of all Bodhisattvas constitute immeasurable practices and vows while performing Buddha-works;
or teaching that the realm of the Buddha is itself the realm of the world while performing Buddha-works;
or teaching that the realm of the world is itself the realm of the Buddha while performing Buddha-works; or teaching that the realm of the Buddha is itself non-existent...

They perform Buddha-works within their spheres of activity, whether abiding for a single day, a single night, half a month, a month, a year, or even for unspeakable eons, performing Buddha-works for the sake of all sentient beings;
this is the eighth vast Buddha-work. Sons of the Buddha, all Buddhas are born from pure goodness.

The treasury of the faculties causes all sentient beings to give rise to pure faith and understanding within the Buddha-dharma; it tames the faculties so that they are forever detached from the world;
it enables all bodhisattvas to possess the eye of wisdom regarding the requisites of enlightenment, attaining realization not through others;
and it performs the work of a Buddha by manifesting either parinirvāṇa, or by manifesting within the world that all things are impermanent.
They perform Buddha-works by speaking of the Buddha-body; or they perform Buddha-works by speaking of how all that was to be done has been fully accomplished;
or they perform Buddha-works by speaking of the perfection of merit without deficiency; or they perform Buddha-works by speaking of the eternal severance of the root of all existence (*bhava*);
or they perform Buddha-works by causing sentient beings to feel weary of and detached from the world, thereby conforming to the Buddha’s mind; or...
They perform Buddha-work by teaching that the end of life inevitably comes to exhaustion; or they perform Buddha-work by teaching that there is nothing in the world worth delighting in;
or they perform Buddha-work by proclaiming the making of offerings to all Buddhas throughout the limits of the future;
or they perform Buddha-work by teaching the turning of the pure Dharma-wheel of all Buddhas, causing those who hear it to give rise to great joy.
They perform Buddha-work by proclaiming the realm of all Buddhas to cause beings to resolve their minds and cultivate various practices;
or they perform Buddha-work by proclaiming the *buddhānusmṛti-samādhi* (samādhi of mindfulness of the Buddha) to cause beings to resolve their minds and constantly delight in seeing the Buddha;
or they perform Buddha-work by proclaiming the purification of the faculties so that beings diligently seek the Buddha-way with minds free from indolence or regression; or...
To travel to all Buddha-lands, observe various realms and their manifold causes and conditions, and perform the work of a Buddha;
or to encompass the bodies of all sentient beings and transform them into the body of a Buddha,
causing all indolent and heedless beings to abide in the pure prohibitions and precepts of the Tathāgata— this is the ninth vast Buddha-work of a Buddha.
Sons, when all the Buddhas enter parinirvāṇa, immeasurable sentient beings wail and weep with great anguish, looking at one another and saying:
"The Tathāgata, the World-Honored One, possesses great compassion;
out of pity, he benefits the entire world and serves as a savior and a refuge for all sentient beings. The appearance of a Tathāgata is difficult to encounter."
Having encountered this unsurpassed field of merit which now perishes forever, he performs the work of a Buddha by causing all sentient beings to wail with grief and yearn for him;
furthermore, for the sake of transforming and delivering all devas, humans, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras,
mahoragas, humans, and non-humans, he acts in accordance with their [capacities].
They would joyfully desire to shatter their own bodies into countless, innumerable, and inconceivable relics, so that all sentient beings might give rise to pure faith,
reverence, respect, and joyful offerings; thereby they would cultivate and bring to full perfection all meritorious virtues,
and further erect stupas adorned with various ornaments within the palaces of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, and gandharvas.
Within the palaces of the gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans,
he established stupas with their teeth, nails, and hair as offerings; causing all who saw them to mindfully recollect the Buddha,
the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, to develop irreversible faith and joy, and to revere them with sincerity and respect, these were distributed everywhere.
By practicing various meritorious deeds through giving and making offerings, by virtue of this merit, they will either be born in the heavens or dwell among humans with noble lineage and honor,
possessing abundant wealth and property; their retinues will all be pure, they will not enter the evil realms but will always be born in the good paths,
constantly obtaining the sight of the Buddhas, and being endowed with all pure dharmas, they shall swiftly attain liberation from within the three realms of existence.

According to their aspirations, they shall attain the fruits of their respective vehicles; having repaid the kindness of what the Tathāgatas have known for them, they shall forever serve as a refuge for the world.

O Sons of the Buddha, although the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have entered parinirvāṇa, they still act as inconceivable, pure fields of merit for sentient beings—fields of merit of inexhaustible virtue and supreme excellence—causing all sentient beings to be fully endowed with roots of goodness.
The perfection of the accumulation of merit is the tenth vast buddha-activity. O Son of the Buddha, these buddha-activities are immeasurable, vast, and inconceivable;

they cannot be known by any gods or humans in all worlds, nor by any śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas of the past, future, or present, except through the empowerment of the Tathāgata’s majestic spiritual power.

The Treatise composed by Li Tongxuan, Elder of Fangshan in Taiyuan, Tang Dynasty;

The Remainder of the Thirty-third Chapter, "The Inconceivable Dharma of the Buddha."
[Sūtra] O Sons of the Buddha, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of sovereign dharmas of non-dual conduct. What are these ten?
They are as follows: first, all Buddhas are able to skillfully explain the words of prophecy with certainty and non-duality;
second, all Buddhas are able to accord with the mental inclinations of sentient beings to fulfill their intentions with certainty and non-duality. All... [and so forth].
All Buddhas are able to manifest and awaken to all phenomena and expound their meaning with definitive non-duality;
all Buddhas are able to fully possess the wisdom of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present with definitive non-duality;
all Buddhas know that all moments (*kṣaṇa*) of the three periods of time are a single moment with definitive non-duality. All.
All Buddhas know that all Buddha-fields of the three periods of time enter into a single Buddha-field, being definitively non-dual;
all Buddhas know that all Buddha-speech of the three periods of time is the speech of a single Buddha, being definitively non-dual;
and all Buddhas know the essential nature of all Buddhas of the three periods of time and all sentient beings whom they transform.
Equal, definitive, and non-dual—thus all Buddhas know that the nature of worldly phenomena and the nature of the Buddha-dharma are without distinction, definitive, and non-dual.

All Buddhas know that all roots of goodness possessed by the Buddhas of the three periods of time are a single root of goodness, definitive and non-dual. These, O Son of the Buddha, are the ten [powers] possessed by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
There are ten kinds of abodes in which all phenomena abide. What are these ten? They are: first, all Buddhas abide in the awakening to the entire realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*);
second, all Buddhas abide in the speech of great compassion; third, all Buddhas abide in their fundamental great vows;
fourth, all Buddhas abide in never abandoning the discipline and conversion of sentient beings; fifth, all Buddhas abide in the dharma of selflessness.
All Buddhas abide in impartiality; all Buddhas abide in the quality of non-forgetfulness;
all Buddhas abide in an unobstructed mind; all Buddhas abide in a mind of constant right concentration;

all Buddhas abide in the equal entry into all phenomena without contradicting the characteristic of the limit of reality—these, O Son of the Buddha, are the ten qualities of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
There are ten kinds of knowledge of all phenomena without exception. What are the ten? They are: knowing all past phenomena without exception;
knowing all future phenomena without exception; knowing all present phenomena without exception;
knowing all phenomena of speech without exception; knowing all... [phenomena] without exception.
He knows the paths of the world exhaustively without remainder; he knows the minds of all sentient beings exhaustively without remainder;
he knows the various levels of the roots of goodness of all bodhisattvas—superior, middling, and inferior—exhaustively without remainder;
he knows the perfect wisdom and all roots of goodness of all Buddhas, neither increasing nor decreasing, exhaustively without remainder; and he knows that all phenomena arise from...
To know exhaustively and without remainder the exhaustion of dependent origination; to know exhaustively and without remainder all the various types of worlds;

to know exhaustively and without remainder all the diverse phenomena within the entire dharma-realm, like the Indra’s net—these, O Son of the Buddha, are the ten powers of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
What are these ten? They are: the power of vastness and the supreme power.

The power of immeasurable strength, the power of great majesty, the power difficult to acquire, the power of non-retrogression, the power of firmness, the power of indestructibility, the power inconceivable to all worlds, and the power that no sentient being can move—these are the ten.
Sons of the Buddha, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of great Nārāyaṇa-bannered heroic dharmas. What are these ten?
That which is called the body of all Buddhas is indestructible and its life-force cannot be severed;
it cannot be affected by worldly poisons or toxins, nor can the calamities of water, fire, or wind in any world-system cause harm to the Buddha’s body.
Furthermore, none of the various Māras, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas... [can harm it].
The rākṣasas, asuras, humans, non-humans, piśācas, and rākṣasas, exhausting all their power, rained down great vajras as large as Mount Sumeru and the Iron Ring Mountains,
filling the trichiliocosm and falling all at once; yet they could not cause the Buddha’s mind to feel even a moment of alarm or fear,
nor did even a single hair on his body move, whether he was walking, standing, sitting, or lying down.
In the dwelling place of the Unchanging Buddha, whether it be far or near in the four directions, if he does not permit it, rain cannot fall;
even if he does not restrain it and rain falls, it ultimately causes no harm.
If sentient beings who are sustained by the Buddha or dispatched by the Buddha cannot be harmed, how much less so the body of the Tathāgata? This is the foremost *nara* among all Buddhas.
