The Dharma-sons of the Buddha, who extend the banner of valor and strength, place all the Sumeru Kings of Mountains,
the Iron Ring Mountains, the Great Iron Ring Mountains, the great oceans, forests, mountains, palaces,

and dwellings within a single pore of their bodies throughout all worlds in the entire Dharma-realm for as long as all future kalpas; yet all sentient beings neither perceive nor know this, except for the Tathāgata.
Empowered by the spiritual power of the Buddha-sons, at that time all Buddhas, within a single pore, sustain as many worlds as there are throughout the kalpas of the future;
whether walking, standing, sitting, or reclining, they do not give rise to even a single thought of weariness or fatigue.
Buddha-son, it is like space, which universally sustains all worlds throughout the entire dharma-realm.
And without any weariness, all Buddhas likewise maintain all worlds within a single pore;
this is the second Dharma of the great Nārāyaṇa-bannered valor of the Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha, all Buddhas are able, in a single thought-moment, to take steps numbering as many as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable worlds, with each step being one such atom.
Passing through lands as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, proceeding in this manner for as many eons as there are atoms in all those worlds—
O Son of the Buddha, suppose there were a great mountain of diamond equal in measure to all those Buddha-fields passed over,
and suppose there were as many such great mountains of diamond as there are atoms in all those fields... [the text continues with an enumeration of their number].
It is said that Buddhas, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, can place all such mountains within a single pore of their bodies;
and since the pores on a Buddha’s body are equal in number to the pores of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, each and every pore contains that many great vajra-mountains.
Carrying that many mountains, they travel through the ten directions, entering the entirety of space.
Throughout all worlds, from the beginningless past to the endless future, across all kalpas, they never cease;
their Buddha-bodies suffer no injury nor do they experience fatigue; their minds are always in meditative concentration without distraction.
This is the third great Nārāyaṇa-bannered, heroic dharma of the Buddhas: O Son of the Buddha, all Buddhas eat in a single sitting.
Having already sat in the full lotus posture for unspeakable eons spanning the past and future limits, they enter the inconceivable bliss received from the Buddhas;
their bodies abide in tranquility, unmoving, yet they do not abandon the work of transforming sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha, suppose there were someone who, throughout every single world pervading all of space, were to measure them one by one in succession with the tip of a hair.
The Buddha is able to sit cross-legged upon the tip of a single hair and remain there until the end of all future kalpas;

as it is with the tip of one hair, so it is with the tips of all hairs. O Son of the Buddha, suppose every sentient being in all the worlds of the ten directions were such that the size of each individual being’s body equaled the number of atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields.
The measure of the number of worlds and their corresponding weight are likewise so.
All Buddhas are able to place as many sentient beings as there are upon the tip of a single finger, continuing thus through all kalpas until the end of time;
all such tips of fingers are likewise capable of holding all those sentient beings, entering every world throughout the entirety of space and the whole dharma-realm, until none remain.
Yet the Buddha’s body and mind never experience fatigue; this is the fourth great Narayana-bannered, heroic dharma of all Buddhas.

O Son of the Buddha, all Buddhas are able, within a single body, to manifest as many heads as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, and from each head, they manifest as many [bodies] as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.

From each of tongues as numerous as atoms, there emanate sounds of distinct varieties as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields; there is no sentient being in the Dharma-realm who does not hear them.
Each of these sounds expounds collections of sūtras as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, and each collection of sūtras further expounds...
If one were to speak of as many dharmas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields—
each dharma having as many words, phrases, and meanings as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields—

and were to expound them in this manner for as many eons as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, even after the completion of those eons, one would still not have finished expounding them all.
One might be able to reach the end of kalpas as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field,
proceeding in such a sequence until all the atoms in every world and all the mental thoughts of every sentient being have been exhausted— even until the very limits of the future;
yet the turning of the wheel of Dharma by the emanation bodies of the Tathāgata has no end, namely, the wheel of Dharma expounded through wisdom.
The wheel that severs all doubts; the wheel that illuminates all phenomena; the wheel that opens the treasury of non-obstruction;
the wheel that brings joy and subdues immeasurable sentient beings; the wheel that reveals and demonstrates all bodhisattva practices;
the wheel that rises high as the sun of perfect great wisdom; the wheel that universally kindles the bright lamp of wisdom to illuminate the world; the wheel of eloquence.
The various adornments of the wheel of Dharma of the Fearless One are like a single Buddha-body;
by means of his supernormal powers, he turns such diverse wheels of Dharma that no worldly phenomena can serve as a metaphor for them.
Thus, throughout the entirety of the realm of empty space, in every location the size of a hair-tip, there are worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
In each and every world-system, in every moment of thought, there appear emanation bodies as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields;

each and every emanation body is likewise so. The sounds, words, phrases, and meanings they proclaim fill every dharma-realm, such that all sentient beings therein attain understanding, yet the Buddha’s voice remains without change.
Being uninterrupted and inexhaustible is the fifth great Nārāyaṇa-standard of valorous strength of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha, all Buddhas adorn their chests with marks of virtue, which are like vajra and cannot be destroyed.
Seated cross-legged beneath the Bodhi tree, the hosts of Māra’s army, though numbering boundlessly and possessing various [forms], [cannot harm them].
Their strange forms were most terrifying; among sentient beings, there was none who did not tremble with fear, all of whom fell into madness or even met their death.

When the Tathāgata beheld these hosts of Māras filling the void of space, his mind felt no terror, his countenance remained unchanged, not a single hair stood on end, and he was unmoved and undisturbed.
Free from discrimination, detached from all joy and anger, he remained in profound stillness.
Abiding in purity where the Buddhas abide, possessing the power of compassion, with the faculties subdued and the mind fearless, they cannot be shaken by any hosts of Māras;
rather, they are able to crush all Māra armies, causing them to turn their hearts, prostrate, and take refuge.
Thereafter, they further teach and transform them through the three wheels, causing them all to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The intention for the three types of enlightenment never regresses; this is the sixth great Nārāyaṇa-standard of valorous strength of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha, all Buddhas possess unimpeded sound, and that sound pervades the worlds of the ten directions;
sentient beings who hear it are naturally tamed. The sounds produced by those Tathāgatas surpass those of Mount Sumeru and the like.
All mountains cannot obstruct it; the palaces of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and all such dwellings cannot obstruct it;
even the loud sounds throughout all worlds cannot obstruct it, as it proceeds according to those who are to be transformed.
All sentient beings without exception hear the meaning of these words and phrases and fully comprehend them;

this is the seventh great Nārāyaṇa-banner of heroic vigor of all Buddhas. O Son of the Buddha, the minds of all Buddhas are without obstruction, having been perpetually and thoroughly purified throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of unspeakably unspeakable eons, regarding the past, future, and present.
All Buddhas are of one and the same essence: unstained and unobscured, without self or what belongs to a self;

neither internal nor external, they realize that objects are empty and quiescent, giving rise to no delusive thoughts. Having nothing to rely upon and nothing to do, they do not dwell in any signs, having forever severed conceptual discrimination.
Their original nature is pure; they have abandoned all攀缘 (pān-yuan—clinging/mental engagement) and recollection regarding all phenomena.
Always free from conflict, abiding in the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), pure through detachment, and having entered the true realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), they expound the inexhaustible.
Having severed all conceptual constructions (*vikalpa*) regarding the measurable and the immeasurable, they are beyond all verbal expression;
having fully penetrated the ineffable and boundless realm, they have perfected unimpeded and inexhaustible wisdom and skillful means, and have attained the ten powers (*daśabala*).
Adorned with all merits and pure, they expound various and immeasurable dharmas, none of which contradict the true mark (*bhūtalakṣaṇa*).
Regarding all phenomena within the dharma-realm across the three periods of time, they perceive them as entirely equal and without distinction.

Ultimately sovereign, they enter the most supreme treasury of all dharmas; through right mindfulness, they are unconfused regarding all dharma-gates and dwell peacefully throughout the ten directions.
Without moving or shifting from any buddha-field, they attain uninterrupted wisdom; they know all phenomena to be ultimately without remainder and exhaust all outflows.
Their minds are well-liberated and their wisdom is well-liberated; they abide in the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi) and penetrate it without obstruction.
Their minds are always in right concentration, and they comprehend in a single thought-moment the dharmas of the three periods of time as well as the mental activities of all sentient beings.
All are without obstruction; this is the eighth great Nārāyaṇa-banner of valorous strength of all Buddhas.

O Son of the Buddha, all Buddhas share the same realm of the Dharma-body: a body of immeasurable merit, a world without bounds, a body inexhaustible in the mundane world, a body unstained by the three realms, a body manifested according to thought, a body that is neither real nor unreal, and a body of equal purity.
The pure body, which neither comes nor goes; the unconditioned and indestructible body; the single-characteristic body that is signless; the body of the self-nature of phenomena;

the body without location or direction that pervades all; the body of sovereign spiritual transformations with boundless forms and marks; the body that manifests in various ways and universally enters all things;
the body of skillful means of the sublime Dharma; the body of the treasury of wisdom that shines everywhere; and the body that demonstrates the equality of all phenomena.
The body that pervades the entire dharma-realm is unmoving and non-conceptual; it is neither existent nor non-existent, a body of eternal purity.
It is neither expedient nor non-expedient, neither extinguished nor non-extinguished.
It manifests bodies according to the various faiths and understandings of all sentient beings who are to be transformed. This body is born from the jewels of all merits and embodies all Buddhas.
The body of the true suchness of phenomena; the inherently quiescent and unobstructed body; the body that accomplishes all unimpeded dharmas;
the body that universally abides throughout the entire pure realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*); the body whose form and shape pervade all worlds;
the body free from objective clinging and non-retrogressive, eternally liberated, and endowed with all-knowledge that universally comprehends everything—this is the first [of the Buddhas].
The sons of the Buddha possess the nine great Nārāyaṇa-banners of courageous strength;
they have equally awakened to the Dharma of all Buddhas, practiced all Bodhisattva deeds, and—whether in aspiration or wisdom—are pure and equal like the great ocean.
Having fully attained fulfillment, their power of practice is most exalted and never regresses or falters as they abide in various samādhis.
They possess the power of knowledge that measures the objective realm, demonstrates all paths, exhorts toward the good, and restrains from evil;

they are foremost in the wisdom that fearlessly expounds the Dharma and are able to provide skillful answers to whatever questions are asked. Their wisdom in preaching the Dharma is impartial and pure; their conduct of body, speech, and mind is entirely free from confusion.
They abide in the dwelling-place of the Buddhas, within the lineage of all Buddhas, performing the Buddha-work through the wisdom of a Buddha, and thus they dwell.
The Omniscient One expounds immeasurable dharmas that have no root and no limit;
his supernormal powers and wisdom are inconceivable, such that none in all the worlds can fully comprehend them.
His wisdom penetrates deeply, perceiving all dharmas as subtle, vast, immeasurable, and boundless; he has thoroughly mastered the dharma-gates of the three periods of time throughout all worlds.
Able to awaken others through supramundane wisdom, they perform unspeakably various Buddha-deeds throughout all worlds;

possessing non-retrogressive wisdom, they enter the ranks of all Buddhas. Although they have already realized the ineffable Dharma that transcends words and letters, they are able to manifest through various forms of speech, and by means of Samantabhadra’s wisdom, they gather all virtuous practices to achieve the mark of a single thought-moment.
With sublime wisdom, one should be able to fully awaken to and comprehend all phenomena just as they were previously contemplated:
that all sentient beings rely upon their respective vehicles, and thus bestow the Dharma accordingly;

and that all phenomena, all worlds, all sentient beings, and all three periods of time—within the realm of the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*)—are such that the measure of these objects is boundless, which one comprehends entirely through unimpeded knowledge.
The sons of the Buddha are able to know and see that all Buddhas, within a single thought-moment, appear in the world according to those who are to be transformed;

they abide in pure lands, attain perfect enlightenment, and manifest supernatural powers to awaken the minds, intentions, and consciousnesses of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time without missing the proper moment. Sons of the Buddha, the worlds of sentient beings are boundless, and the dharmas are boundless.
The realms are boundless and the three periods of time are boundless; the most supreme Buddhas are likewise without limit, all manifesting therein to attain equal and perfect enlightenment.
Through the Buddha’s wisdom and skillful means, they awaken beings without ceasing.

O Son of the Buddha, all Buddhas, by the power of their spiritual penetrations, manifest most wondrous bodies, dwelling in boundless places with a heart of great compassion and skillful means that is free from obstruction.
To unimpededly and constantly expound the sublime Dharma for the sake of sentient beings at all times is the tenth great Nārāyaṇa-bannered valiant dharma of the Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha, this great Nārāyaṇa-bannered valiant dharma of all Buddhas is immeasurable, boundless, and inconceivable; it extends to all sentient beings of the past, future, and present.
The followers of the two vehicles cannot understand this, except for those sons of the Buddha who are empowered by the spiritual authority of the Tathāgatas.
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of definitive laws. What are these ten? They are: first, all Buddhas definitively descend from Tuṣita Heaven at the end of their lifespan;
second, all Buddhas definitively manifest taking birth and remaining in the womb for ten months; third, all Buddhas... [and so forth].
All Buddhas are determined to weary themselves of worldly pleasures and seek to leave the household life;

all Buddhas are determined to sit beneath the Bodhi tree and attain perfect enlightenment, awakening to all Buddha-dharmas; all Buddhas are determined to awaken to all phenomena in a single thought-moment;
all Buddhas manifest spiritual powers throughout all worlds; and all Buddhas are determined to turn the wondrous Wheel of Dharma in accordance with the proper time.
All Buddhas are certainly able to preach the Dharma and bestow predictions of enlightenment upon beings according to the roots of goodness they have planted at the appropriate time;
all Buddhas are certainly able to perform the works of a Buddha at the appropriate time;

all Buddhas are certainly able to bestow predictions of enlightenment upon all bodhisattvas who have attained accomplishment; and all Buddhas are certainly able to universally answer all questions in a single thought-moment.
This which the sentient beings ask is as follows: Sons of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of swift dharmas possessed by the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
What are these ten? They are: first, if any see all Buddhas, they will swiftly become far removed from all evil destinies;
second, if any see all Buddhas, they will swiftly attain the fulfillment of supreme merits; third, all Buddhas... [and so forth].
If any see the Buddha, they will swiftly be able to accomplish vast roots of goodness;
if any see all the Buddhas, they will swiftly attain rebirth in the pure and wondrous heavens; if any see all the Buddhas, they will swiftly be able to sever and eliminate all doubts;
and if those who have already resolved upon Bodhicitta should behold them, they will swiftly [attain their goal].
They attain the accomplishment of vast faith and resolve, never regressing; they are able to teach and transform sentient beings according to their needs;
if they have not yet resolved their minds, they can swiftly generate the mind set on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
and if they have not yet entered the stage of certainty (*samyaktva-niyāma*) but encounter all Buddhas, they will swiftly enter that stage. If there are any Buddhas...
Those who behold them can swiftly purify all mundane and supramundane faculties.
All Buddhas, if seen by anyone, will swiftly cause all obstacles to be eliminated. All Buddhas, if seen by anyone, will swiftly enable them to attain fearless eloquence.
These are the ten [qualities] of the sons of the Buddha; the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have ten things that should always be [practiced].
Recollection of the Pure Dharmas: What are the ten? They are as follows: all Bodhisattvas should constantly recollect the past causes and conditions of all Buddhas;
all Bodhisattvas should constantly recollect the pure and supreme practices of all Buddhas;
all Bodhisattvas should constantly recollect how all Buddhas have fulfilled all the perfections (pāramitās); [all Bodhisattvas should constantly recollect... one...
All Bodhisattvas should constantly recollect that all Buddhas have accomplished their great vows;

all Bodhisattvas should constantly recollect that all Buddhas have accumulated roots of goodness; all Bodhisattvas should constantly recollect that all Buddhas have already perfected the holy life (*brahmacarya*);
all Bodhisattvas should [constantly recollect] that all Buddhas have manifested perfect enlightenment.
One should constantly recollect the immeasurable form-bodies of all Buddhas; all Bodhisattvas should constantly recollect the immeasurable supernormal powers of all Buddhas;
all Bodhisattvas should constantly recollect the ten powers and fearlessnesses of all Buddhas.
These, O sons of the Buddha, are the ten [recollections] of the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones.
There are ten kinds of abodes of omniscience. What are the ten? They are as follows:
all Buddhas, in a single moment of thought, fully know the mental activities and mental concomitants of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time;

all Buddhas, in a single moment of thought, fully know all the karma accumulated by all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time, as well as the karmic fruits and retributions thereof. All Buddhas... [and so forth].
In a single thought-moment, the Buddha fully knows what is appropriate for all sentient beings and teaches and tames them through the three wheels.
In a single thought-moment, all Buddhas completely know all mental characteristics of all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm;
they universally manifest the arising of a Buddha in all places so that these beings may see him, and they skillfully gather and sustain them all.

In a single thought-moment, the Buddhas universally accord with the inclinations, desires, and understandings of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, manifesting and preaching the Dharma to bring them to subdual.

In a single thought-moment, all Buddhas fully know the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm and manifest spiritual powers for their sake. In a single thought-moment, all Buddhas pervade all things.
In accordance with the needs of all sentient beings to be transformed, he manifests his appearance and teaches that the Buddha-body is not to be grasped or attached to.
All Buddhas, in a single thought-moment, universally reach every place within the Dharma-realm and all sentient beings upon their respective paths.
In a single thought-moment, all Buddhas respond to those among sentient beings who possess mindfulness.

There is nowhere they do not go to respond to them; in a single thought-moment, all Buddhas fully know the understandings and desires of all sentient beings and manifest immeasurable physical forms for their sake. These, O sons of the Buddha, are the ten [qualities].
Furthermore, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of immeasurable and inconceivable Buddha-samādhis. What are these ten? They are as follows: first—
All Buddhas constantly abide in right concentration; within a single thought-moment, they pervade all places and extensively expound the sublime Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.

All Buddhas constantly abide in right concentration; within a single thought-moment, they pervade all places and universally teach the limit of non-self for the sake of all sentient beings. All Buddhas constantly dwell in right concentration; within a single thought-moment, they pervade...
In all places, they universally enter the presence of all Buddhas of the three periods of time, who are always in right concentration;
in a single thought-moment, they pervade all places and universally enter the vast Buddha-lands of the ten directions. All Buddhas are always in right concentration;
in a single thought-moment, they pervade all places and universally manifest immeasurable and diverse Buddha-bodies. All Buddhas are always...
All Buddhas, remaining constantly in right concentration, manifest within a single thought-moment throughout all places according to the various mental dispositions of sentient beings;
all Buddhas, remaining constantly in right concentration, preach all dharmas throughout all places within a single thought-moment, [revealing] the true limit free from desire.
All Buddhas, constantly abiding in right concentration, [pervade] within a single thought-moment...

In all places, they proclaim the nature of all dependent origination; all Buddhas constantly abide in right concentration, and within a single thought-moment, they manifest throughout all places the infinite, vast adornments of both mundane and supramundane realms, causing all sentient beings to always behold the Buddha.
All Buddhas constantly abide in right concentration, and within a single thought-moment, throughout...
In all places, they cause all sentient beings to fully penetrate all Buddha-dharmas and immeasurable liberations, ultimately reaching the unsurpassed further shore;
this is the tenth. O Sons of the Buddha, the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, possess ten kinds of unimpeded liberation.
What are these ten? They are as follows: All Buddhas are able to manifest within a single atom that which is... [inexpressible].
It is said that all Buddhas appear in the world in ineffable numbers;
all Buddhas can manifest within a single atom ineffable upon ineffable numbers of Buddhas turning the pure wheel of Dharma;
all Buddhas can manifest within a single atom ineffable upon ineffable numbers of sentient beings receiving transformation and being tamed; all Buddhas can [manifest within] a single atom...

All Buddhas of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-lands are able to manifest within a single atom unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Bodhisattvas receiving their predictions; all Buddhas are able to manifest within a single atom all Buddhas of the past, future, and present;
and all Buddhas are able to manifest within a single atom all the worlds of the past, future, and present.
All Buddhas are able to manifest all supernatural powers of the past, future, and present within a single atom;
all Buddhas are able to manifest all sentient beings of the past, future, and present within a single atom;
all Buddhas are able to manifest all Buddha-activities of the past, future, and present within a single atom—these are the ten.

[Treatise] The general purport of this chapter clarifies that by advancing from the preceding stages to this point, one’s own three karmas—of body, speech, and mind—attain the vast activity of the Buddha’s three karmas.

Thus, within a single karma, one answers the immeasurable activities of ten, hundred, thousand, ten-thousand, and so forth, up to countless sets of the three karmas; and upon each of these three karmas, one answers thirty sets of hundreds.
Upon each of the ten kinds of immeasurable threefold karma—such as the "ten million" and so forth—one answers with thirty times ten million, etc., of unspeakably immeasurable karmic functions;

the remaining two sections each possess ten, hundred, thousand, ten thousand, and hundred thousand immeasurables, clarifying that the karmic functions elucidated by the threefold karma do not depart from the two gates of the two truths: the ultimate and the conventional, each consisting of ten dharmas.
Among these, body, speech, and mind constitute the essence, while the remaining seven are the functional applications of these three activities (*karmayoga*).
Thus, when the Bodhisattva Blue Lotus Treasury answers the ten preceding questions, there are thirty-two types of responses; within each response, there are ten inexhaustible dharmas.
This is intended to clarify that, upon reaching the fruit of Buddhahood, the conventional and ultimate dharmas are perfected within the functional application of the Buddha’s three activities.

Because he is complete in these respects, the Buddha is titled the "Unsurpassed Honored One Among Two-legged Beings. This clarifies that his three types of karmic activity and two wisdoms are all-pervasive and universally encompass all phenomena.
Thus, the blue lotus represents true wisdom (*tathatā-jñāna*), while the lotus treasury represents conventional wisdom (*saṃvṛti-jñāna*).
By means of these two wisdoms—true and conventional—he himself proclaims the vast and sovereign mastery of his own three types of karmic activity.

Regarding "the gate of inconceivability, the person, the royal capital, and the city": the royal capital is the city where the king resides; that which governs the whole world is the capital, while all other areas are cities.

Regarding "palaces" (*gongdian*): the chambers where one dwells, stays, and sleeps are the palaces (*gong*); the places where one lives according to the Dharma and where the True Dharma is arrayed are the halls (*dian*).
Regarding *piśāca*: these are beings of the realm of hungry ghosts (*preta*); here [in Chinese] they are called "flesh-eaters" (*channren*).
The vital essence belongs to the Eastern Quarter and is governed by the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
"Dhṛtarāṣṭra" is translated here as "Holder of the Nation," so named because he protects and sustains the land.

The Gandharvas—here called "Seekers of Fragrance"—are deities of music who are likewise governed by this king. This is as if [they were contained] within the pores of the body or within a single atom.
All worlds, lands, all Buddhas, and all sentient beings dwell therein, performing the Buddha-work of transformation;
this occurs when deluded sentiments are extinguished, and only within the realm of wisdom is it thus. It manifests through the power of samādhi and is not something sought by ordinary consciousness.
The Dharma is always like this, yet it is only because of one's own deluded sentiments that it is obstructed, just as [the true nature of] the world is obscured.

The "Chapter on the Ocean of Marks and Signs of the Tathāgata’s Ten Bodies," the thirty-fourth. [Treatise] In order to explain this chapter, it is divided into three sections: first, the purpose for which this chapter has come; second, the explanation of the one who preaches the Dharma. Regarding the "Chapter on the Treasury of Flowers" (*Puṣpa-garbha*) mentioned above, its meaning has already been interpreted;

all other matters are fully contained within the text itself. [The Treatise continues: Now, in explaining this chapter, we shall rely upon three gates: first, the explanation of the intent for the chapter's arrival; second, the explanation of the one capable of preaching the Dharma.
Part One: An Exegesis of the Text Following the Main Body. First, regarding the explanation of the purpose for the arrival of this chapter:

It clarifies that the preceding chapter explained the three karmas and two wisdoms of the Buddha’s own nature, which enter the inconceivable limit and pervade everywhere in vastness and infinity to benefit sentient beings.
This chapter, however, concerns the reward-body (*saṃbhogakāya*) within those same three karmas and two wisdoms as they enter into inconceivable wisdom; therefore, this chapter follows.
Second, the explanation of the master who is able to preach the Dharma clarifies that this ocean of marks is accomplished through the retribution of practice;
Samantabhadra, being such a practitioner, causes the practitioner himself to speak of the fruits of the merit resulting from his own practice.
Third, the word-by-word commentary on the meaning divides this chapter of the sutra into ninety-nine sections.
[Sūtra] At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"O Sons of the Buddha, I shall now expound for you the ocean of marks possessed by the Tathāgata."
[Treatise] First, from the passage beginning with "At that time, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva" down to "all the oceans of marks," spanning one and a half lines of scripture,
is the initial general presentation of the Tathāgata’s bodily marks as being as vast and numerous as the ocean. Second,
the brief explanation of the ninety-seven kinds of marks of a Great Man is divided into ninety-seven sections, as follows.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, upon the crown of the Tathāgata’s head is the mark of a great man adorned with thirty-two jewels.
Among these marks of a great man is one named "Illuminating All Directions," which universally emits immeasurable nets of great light.
It is adorned with all manner of exquisite jewels, and its hair is soft, dense, and pervasive, each strand emitting mani-jewels.
His light fills all boundless worlds, manifesting the physical forms and marks of a Buddha in their full perfection;
this is the first mark of a Great Being, called the Cloud of Light from the Buddha-Eye, adorned with various kinds of mani-jewel kings that emit golden light,
which is like the radiance emitted from the ūrṇā-kośa between his eyebrows, and which universally illumines all worlds.
This is the second mark of a great man, called "The Cloud Filling the Dharma Realm," adorned with sublime jewel wheels that emit the lamp-light of the Tathāgata’s merit and wisdom,
universally illuminating all world-oceans within the entire dharma realm of the ten directions,
wherein all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are universally manifested. This is the third great [mark].
The fourth mark of a great man is named Cloud of Universal Illumination Manifesting Various Adornments of True Gold and Maṇi Jewels;
all these exquisite jewels emit light that illuminates inconceivable Buddha-lands, and within them, all Buddhas appear.
The fifth mark of a great man is named Pure Maṇi Jewel King Emitting Clouds of Precious Radiance.

Adorned with *vaiḍūrya* jewels as its filaments, it illuminates all dharma-realms in the ten directions and universally manifests various spiritual transformations therein, praising the wisdom and merit of the Tathāgata’s past practices.
This is the fifth mark of a great being, called the "Tathāgata-Manifestation-Pervading-Dharma-Realm-Mahāvaśitā-Cloud" Bodhisattva.
He wears a crown made of divine transformation jewel-flame maṇis; he possesses the power of a Tathāgata and awakens all beings;
he wears a garland of jewel-flame light-circles whose radiance universally illumines the worlds of the ten directions, wherein all Tathāgatas are manifested sitting at their sites of enlightenment;
clouds of omniscience fill the void and the infinite Dharma-realm—this is [the mark].
The sixth mark of a great man is named Tathāgata Universal Lamp Cloud;

it adorns the great sovereign ocean of jewel-seas that shake the lands of the dharma-realm, emitting pure light that fills the dharma-realm and universally manifests within it the oceans of merit of the bodhisattvas of the ten directions, as well as the oceans of the wisdom-pennants of the Buddhas of the past, present, and future. This is it.
Seventh is the mark of a great man called Universal Illumination of All Buddhas’ Vast Cloud Indra-Jewel Wish-Fulfilling King Jewel Maṇi-Rāja,
which serves as its adornment; it constantly emits the radiant light of the bodhisattva’s flaming lamp,
universally illuminating all worlds in the ten directions, wherein appear the oceans of various physical marks and forms of all buddhas and their great voices.

The ocean of sound and the ocean of pure power constitute the eighth; next is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Perfect Radiance," adorned with exquisite *vaiḍūrya* and *maṇi* kings and various jewel flowers,
wherein all manner of jewels extend great nets of flames that fill all worlds throughout the ten directions, such that all sentient beings see the Tathāgata manifesting therein.
Sitting before them, they praise the merits of the *dharmakāya* of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, causing them to enter the pure realm of the Tathāgatas;

this is the ninth. Next, there is a mark of greatness called "The Cloud of Radiant Light from the Treasury of Universal Bodhisattva Practices," adorned with various exquisite jewel flowers that universally illuminate immeasurable worlds with precious light.
His flames universally cover all lands throughout the ten directions of the Dharma-realm; they penetrate without obstruction, vibrating with the Buddha’s voice as he proclaims the ocean of Dharma.

This is the tenth mark of a Great Man, called "Cloud of Universal Radiance," adorned with Vaiḍūrya, Indra-blue, and diamond *maṇi* jewels, its lapis lazuli jewel-light and color-form being utterly transparent and brilliant.
Universally illuminating all oceans of worlds, it emits wondrous sounds that fill the Dharma-realm;
all such manifestations arise from the great ocean of merit and wisdom of the Buddhas.
This is the eleventh mark of a Great Man, called Cloud of Perfect Enlightenment, adorned with various jewel flowers, each of which radiates light.

It is clearly manifest that there are Tathāgatas seated upon the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), filling all infinite worlds and causing all worlds to attain universal purity, forever severing all false conceptualizations and discriminations; this constitutes the twelfth [mark].
Next, there is a mark of a Great Being called Cloud of Radiant Illumination, adorned with the heart-king maṇi-jewel of the ocean-treasury of precious flames.

He emits a magnificent great radiance; within this light appear immeasurable bodhisattvas and all the practices performed by those bodhisattvas, as well as the oceans of all forms and marks of the wisdom-body and dharma-body of all Tathāgatas, filling the entire Dharma-realm.
This is the thirteenth. Next, there is a mark of greatness called "Cloud Adorned with Universal Illumination," which consists of vajra-flowers and *vaiḍūrya* jewels.

It was adorned with the radiance of great light; within that light were great precious lotus thrones, complete with every adornment, covering the entire Dharma-realm and spontaneously proclaiming the four practices of Bodhisattvas. Their voices pervaded the ocean of all Dharma-realms.
This was the fourteenth. Next, there appeared a mark of greatness called "The Clouds of Practice of the Ocean of Samādhis Manifesting Buddhas," which in a single thought-moment—
In the center, he manifests the Tathāgata’s immeasurable adornments that universally adorn the entire inconceivable ocean of worlds throughout the dharma-realm;

this is the fifteenth. Next, there is a mark of greatness called the Cloud of Universal Illumination from the Ocean of Transformations, adorned with exquisite jewel lotuses as vast as Mount Sumeru, wherein the radiance of all jewels appears, born from the vows of the Buddha.
The inexhaustibility of all emanations constitutes the sixteenth [mark].
Next is the mark of a great man called "The Pure and Wondrous Jewel Adorned with the Clouds of Liberation of All Tathāgatas," which emits great light to adorn the lion thrones of all Buddhas,
manifesting the physical forms of all Buddhas, as well as immeasurable Buddha-dharmas and Buddha-fields.
The ocean is the seventeenth mark of a great man, named Sovereign Skillful Means Universally Illuminating Cloud;
it is adorned with beryl lotuses, true-gold lotuses, and mani-king lamps of the wondrous Dharma-flame clouds,
emitting dense clouds of precious flames of all Buddhas and pure light that fills the dharma-realm, within which a single [Buddha] appears everywhere.
All manner of exquisite and magnificent ornaments constitute the eighteenth mark; furthermore,
there is a mark of a great man called "The Cloud of the Buddha-lineage Awakening," adorned with immeasurable jewel-lights, complete with a thousand-spoked wheel that is pure both inside and out,
born from roots of goodness in the past, its light pervading the worlds of the ten directions and radiating the sun of clear wisdom.
The Dharma-ocean is the nineteenth mark of a great man, named Cloud of Sovereignty Manifesting the Marks of All Tathāgatas;
it is adorned with clusters of various precious garlands and beryl jewel-flowers, and it extends great jewel-flames that fill the entire dharma-realm,
within which are universally manifested as many Buddhas of the past, future, and present as there are atoms in all Buddha-fields.
The Buddha is like a lion king, courageous and fearless, fully endowed with physical marks and wisdom;
this is the twentieth. Next is a mark of a great man called "Cloud that Universally Illuminates All Dharmadhātus.
His precious marks are pure and adorned, emitting great radiance that universally illuminates the dharmadhātu, manifesting all the infinite and boundless Buddhas.
The Bodhisattva’s treasury of sublime wisdom is the twenty-first mark of a great man, known as the Cloud of the Tathāgata Vairocana’s Marks.
It is adorned with exquisite jewel flowers and pure, wondrous moons of vaidūrya,
all emitting immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of light rays from mani-jewels that fill all space and phenomena.
Within the realms, he manifests immeasurable Buddha-fields, each with a Tathāgata sitting in the full lotus posture;

this is the twenty-second mark of a great man. It is named "Universal Illumination of All Buddhas’ Clouds of Light and Adornment of Exquisite Jewels and Lamps," which emits pure radiance that shines throughout all worlds in the ten directions, manifesting all Buddhas therein.
Turning the wheel of Dharma constitutes the twenty-third mark of a great man, called "The Universal Manifestation of Clouds of All Adornments.
It is adorned with various jewel-flames that emit pure light filling the entire dharma-realm.
In every thought-moment, it constantly manifests unspeakably unspeakable numbers of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas seated at their sites of enlightenment.
This is the twenty-fourth mark of a great man. Next, there is a mark named "The Mani Jewel Ocean of Clouds of Sounds Emanating from All Dharma Realms, Adorned with Supreme Sandalwood.

It spreads a vast network of flames that fills the dharma realm, universally proclaiming subtle and wondrous sounds to reveal to all sentient beings the ocean of all their karmas; this is the twenty-fifth.

Next, there is a mark of a great man called "The Pure Eye Adorned by the Clouds of the Transformation Wheels of All Buddhas Shining Universally," which illuminates all worlds in the ten directions and universally manifests all the various ornaments possessed by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present;
furthermore, it emits wondrous sounds that expound the inconceivable and vast ocean of the Dharma. This is [the thirty-third mark].

The twenty-sixth mark of a great man is named "Cloud of the Buddha-Sea Illumined by Light," wherein light universally illuminates all worlds throughout the entire dharma-realm without obstruction, such that in every place there is a Tathāgata sitting cross-legged;
this is the twenty-seventh [mark]. The next mark of a great man is named "Cloud of Jewel Lamps," which emits the vast radiance of a Tathāgata.
Universally illuminating all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions, therein universally manifesting all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
as well as the inconceivable oceans of sentient beings— this is the twenty-eighth mark of a great man,
called "The Cloud of Non-differentiation of the Dharma-realm," which emits the great wisdom-light of the Tathāgata, universally illuminating the Buddha-lands of the ten directions.

Within the infinite oceans of Dharma at the assemblies of the bodhisattva maṇḍalas throughout all lands, he universally manifests various supernatural powers and further emits sublime sounds that, according to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, proclaim the practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, causing them to dedicate their merit;
this is the twenty-ninth [mark]. Next, there is a mark of greatness called "Abiding Securely in All."
Clouds of light universally illuminating the oceans of worlds emit precious radiance that fills all space and the dharma-realm;
within it, pure and wondrous sites of enlightenment and the adorned physical forms of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas appear everywhere, such that those who see them attain the state of "seeing nothing.
This is the thirtieth mark of greatness, named "Pure Radiant Flame of All Jewels."
Clouds of immeasurable Buddhas and Bodhisattvas emit the pure light of mani-jewels that universally illumines all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions;

within them, oceans of Bodhisattvas appear everywhere, all fully endowed with the spiritual powers of the Tathāgatas, constantly traveling through the ten directions across the entire network of lands as far as the limits of space. This is the thirty-first [mark], followed by:
The mark of a great man called "Cloud of Adornments Universally Illuminating All Dharma Realms" is situated at the center,
gradually rising upward and adorned with a Jāmbūnada-gold Indra-net that emits clouds of pure light filling the dharma realms;
it constantly manifests in every thought-moment within the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in all worlds— this is the third.
O Sons of the Buddha, upon the crown of the Tathāgata’s head are thirty-two such marks of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa*) that serve as his adornment.

O Sons of the Buddha, between the Tathāgata’s eyebrows is a mark of a great man called the "Mani-jewel Flower of the Light-Cloud Pervading the Dharma-realm" (*dharmadhātu-vyāpi-prabhā-megha-maṇi-ratna-puṣpa*), which serves as his ornament.
It emits great light, possessing the colors of all jewels, and is as penetratingly bright as the sun and moon.
Its light is utterly pure, universally illuminating the lands of the ten directions;
therein appear the bodies of all Buddhas, which further emit wondrous sounds proclaiming the ocean of Dharma.
This is the thirty-third mark of a Great Man, called the Cloud of Sovereign Universal Vision, adorned with various exquisite jewels, its mani-jewel radiance pure and luminous.
Pervadingly seeing all things without obstruction— this is the thirty-fourth mark of a Great Man of the Tathāgata’s nose,
called “The Pure and Wondrous Jewel Adorned with the Clouds of All Superknowledges and Wisdom. The light of various jewel colors completely covers it,
and from within it appear immeasurable transformation Buddhas sitting upon precious lotus flowers, proceeding to all worlds.
The realm of this thirty-fifth Tathāgata’s tongue, which manifests a cloud-mass of images of sounds for all Bodhisattvas and all sentient beings,
proclaiming the inconceivable ocean of all Buddha-dharmas, is adorned with various colors of exquisite jewels;
it is accomplished through the roots of goodness from past lives, and his tongue is broad and long, completely covering [the world].
Whenever the Tathāgatas of all the oceans of worlds manifest a joyful smile, they invariably emit the light of all *maṇi* jewels.
This light shines universally throughout the dharma-realm of the ten directions, enabling the minds of all beings to attain refreshing clarity.
All Buddhas of the past, future, and present appear vividly within this light, each proclaiming the vast and sublime Dharma.
The sound of his voice pervades all lands and remains for immeasurable eons; this is the thirty-sixth mark of a Tathāgata’s tongue.

Furthermore, there is a mark of greatness called Dharma-realm Cloud: its palm is flat and even, adorned with various jewels, emitting wondrous jewel-light whose color and form are perfect, just like the light emitted from between his eyebrows. This light universally illumines all Buddha-lands. Only...
That which is composed of dust has no intrinsic nature; within that light, there further appear immeasurable Buddhas who all emit sublime voices to preach all dharmas.

This constitutes the thirty-seventh [mark]: upon the tongues of the Tathāgatas there is a mark of greatness called the "Light-Cloud of the Sovereign Jewel King Illuminating the Dharma Realm," which serves as an adornment and naturally and constantly emits golden jewel-flames.
Within it, reflections of all oceans of Buddhas appear, and they further emit wondrous sounds that fill all infinite worlds.

Within each sound, every possible sound is contained, all expounding the sublime Dharma so that listeners’ hearts rejoice; even after passing through immeasurable eons of contemplation and savoring, they do not forget it.
This is the thirty-eighth mark. Furthermore, upon the tip of the Tathāgata’s tongue, there is another mark of a Great Man called "Illumination."

Adorned with the sovereign maṇi-jewel of the clouds of the dharma-realm, it manifests various colors and forms with subtle, wondrous radiance that fills immeasurable lands throughout the ten directions;
throughout the entire dharma-realm, there is nothing that is not purified.
Within it, there are infinite Buddhas and bodhisattvas, each emitting sublime sounds to provide various explanations and reveal all aspects of the bodhisattva path.
The aforementioned listening and receiving [of the teaching] constitutes the thirty-ninth mark of a Great Man on the upper palate of the Tathāgata’s mouth,
named "Cloud of the Manifestation of the Inconceivable Dharma Realm. It is adorned with Indra-ratnas and Vaiḍūrya jewels,
emitting clouds of pure light from the flames of fragrant lamps that fill all dharma realms throughout the ten directions, manifesting various kinds of supernatural powers.
Skillfully expounding the profound and inconceivable Dharma throughout all oceans of worlds—this is the fortieth mark.
On the lower right molar of the Tathāgata’s mouth, there is a mark of a great man called "Buddha-tooth-cloud-multitude-jewels-maṇi-svastika-cakravartin," which serves as an adornment;
it emits great light that universally illuminates the entire dharma-realm, within which [the Dharma] is everywhere...
Manifesting the bodies of all Buddhas to circulate throughout the ten directions and awaken all sentient beings—this is the forty-first [mark].
On the upper right canine tooth of the Tathāgata’s mouth, there is a mark of a great man called the "Jewel Flame Meru Treasury Cloud Maṇi Jewel Treasury," which serves as an adornment.
It emits the pure radiance of vajra-fragrant flames; each ray of light fills the Dharma-realm.
He manifests the spiritual powers of all Buddhas throughout the realms and further manifests the pure and wondrous sites of enlightenment in all worlds of the ten directions;

this is the forty-second mark. On the lower left canine tooth of the Tathāgata’s mouth, there is a mark of greatness called Jewel Lamp Universally Illuminating Cloud, adorned with all manner of exquisite jewels that extend flowers and emit fragrances, emitting clouds of lamp-flames that are pure.
Pure light fills all oceans of worlds, within which all Buddhas appear seated upon lotus-treasury lion thrones,

surrounded by assemblies of bodhisattvas; this is the forty-third mark of a great man on the left upper tooth of the Tathāgata’s mouth, named Pure Light of the Tathāgata-Cloud Manifesting Illumination.
Adorned with nets of Jambūnada gold and precious flowers, they emit great wheels of flames that fill the Dharma-realm;

therein, all Buddhas appear universally, and by means of their supernormal powers, they distribute the milk of the Dharma, the lamp of the Dharma, and the treasure of the Dharma within the void to teach and transform the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas. These are the forty-four Tathāgatas.
The teeth possess the mark of a great man called "Universal Manifestation of Clouds of Radiance. The space between each tooth is adorned by an ocean of marks;
when he smiles, they all emit light of manifold jewel colors, with the flames of mani-jewels curling to the right and spreading throughout the Dharma-realm until it is completely filled.
They proclaim the voice of the Buddha’s words and expound the practices of Samantabhadra—this is the forty-fifth.

The Tathāgata’s lips possess a mark of a great man called "Manifesting All Jewel-Light Clouds Emitting the Radiance of Jāmbūnada Gold, Lotus Color, and All Jewel Colors," a vast light that illuminates the entire dharma-realm and causes it all to be purified;
this is the forty-sixth. The Tathāgata’s neck possesses a mark of a great man called "Universally Illuminating All Worlds."
Adorned with cloud-maṇi jewel-kings, it is formed of deep blue lotus fibers, soft, supple, and smooth,
emitting the pure light of Vairocana that fills all worlds throughout the ten directions, wherein all Buddhas appear universally;
this is the forty-seventh mark of a great man on the right shoulder of the Tathāgata, called "The Vastness of the Buddha."
From all the clouds of jewels, there emanate rays of light in the colors of all jewels, true gold, and lotus flowers, forming a net of jewel-flames that universally illumines the Dharma-realm;
within it, all Bodhisattvas are universally manifested. This is the forty-eighth mark on the right shoulder of the Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, upon the right shoulder, there is another mark of a great man called "Cloud of the Most Victorious Jewel Universal Illumination," whose color is pure like Jambūnada gold.
Golden light emanates from the *maṇi* jewels, filling the entire Dharma-realm; within it, all bodhisattvas are universally manifested. This is the forty-ninth [mark].
Upon the left shoulder of each Tathāgata is a mark of greatness called "Cloud of Supreme Light Illuminating the Dharma-realm.
Just as with the crown of the head and the space between the eyebrows, it is adorned with various ornaments, emitting the colors of Jāmbūnada gold and lotuses.
The Jewel Radiance forms a great web of flames that fills the Dharma-realm, within which all spiritual powers are manifested;
this is the fiftieth [mark]. *The Compendium of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Fascicle 75.

Phonetic Transcriptions: *xiōng* (thorax) *yù* (chest) *zhé* (to be terrified) *bì* (a prediction or decree) *zhì* (fine or dense) *yí* (cheerful) *è* (palate) *fù* (cheeks/jaw) *hù* (smooth/slippery) *wǎn* (deeply curved) *jǐng* (neck) *bǐng* (bright) *dàn* (to eat)
The Combined Commentary on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s New Flower Ornament, Scroll Seventy-Six.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a Śramaṇa from Khotan during the Tang Dynasty;
The Treatise composed by Li Tongxuan, a Layman of Fangshan, Taiyuan, during the Tang Dynasty.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhining of Kaiyuan Temple in Fuzhou during the Tang Dynasty, Collating the Sūtras and Composing the Treatise, Chapter Thirty-Four:
The Remainder of "The Ocean of the Marks of the Ten Bodies of the Tathāgata.
[Sūtra]: On the left shoulder of the Tathāgata there is another mark of a great man called Cloud of Universal Radiance; this mark spirals to the right.
Adorned with the sovereign mani-jewel of Jambūnada gold, it emits the radiance of various jewel flowers, fragrances,
and flames that pervades the entire Dharma-realm; therein are universally manifested all Buddhas and all pure, adorned lands—
this is the fifty-first mark on the left shoulder of the Tathāgata, called the Cloud of Universal Illumination.
Its mark is right-ward spiraling, subtly and densely adorned, emitting clouds of Buddha-lamp flames and pure radiance that pervade the entire Dharma-realm;
within it appear all the various adornments of all Bodhisattvas, each exquisitely beautiful.
This is the fifty-second Tathāgata’s mark upon the chest, shaped like the svastika and named Auspicious Ocean Cloud (Śrī-sāgara-megha).
She is adorned with jewel-lotuses that emit wheels of various light-flames in all precious colors, filling the Dharma-realm and universally purifying it;
furthermore, they produce wondrous sounds that proclaim the ocean of the Dharma—this is the fifty-third auspicious mark.
To her right is a mark of greatness called Cloud of Manifesting Radiant Light, adorned with Indra’s net.
He emits a great wheel of light that fills the Dharma-realm, within which he universally manifests immeasurable Buddhas;

this is the fifty-fourth auspicious mark. On his right side, there is again a mark of a Great Man called "Clouds of Tathāgatas Appearing Universally," adorned with the mani-jewel crowns of all Bodhisattvas, emitting great radiance that shines universally throughout the ten directions.

He causes all worlds to be completely purified, within which he manifests the Buddhas of the past, future, and present seated at their sites of enlightenment, universally displaying spiritual powers and extensively proclaiming the ocean of Dharma; this is the fifty-fifth auspicious mark.
To his right, there is another mark of a great man called "Cloud of Blooming Flower-Maṇi Jewels," adorned with flower-like maṇi jewels, emitting precious fragrant flames and lamps of pure light.
Pure light, appearing like lotus flowers, fills the world; this is the fifty-sixth auspicious mark.
To the right, there is another mark of a great being called "Delightful Golden Cloud," adorned with the *maṇi* kings of the treasury of all jewel-heart-kings.
It emits pure light that illuminates the dharma-realm, within which it appears everywhere, as if...
Like the Buddha-eye, vast and luminous, it is a treasury of mani jewels; this constitutes the fifty-seventh auspicious mark.
On the right side, there is another mark of a great man called Buddha-Ocean-Cloud, adorned with Vaiḍūrya jewel incense lamps and flower garlands.
It emits mani-jewel kings of incense lamps whose great flames and pure radiance fill and pervade all of space.
Within all lands of the ten directions, he universally manifests assemblies at sites of enlightenment; this constitutes the fifty-eighth auspicious mark.
On his left side is the mark of a great person called "Manifesting Clouds of Radiance," adorned by countless bodhisattvas seated upon precious lotuses.
They emit various intermingled jewel-flame radiances from *maṇi*-king gems, which universally purify all things.
Within the ocean of the dharmadhātu of all phenomena, there are manifested therein immeasurable Buddhas and the sublime voices of those Buddhas expounding the Dharma;

this constitutes the fifty-ninth auspicious mark. To its left, there is again a mark of a great person named "Cloud of Light Manifesting Throughout the Dharmadhātu," adorned with an ocean of maṇi jewels, which emits great light pervading the entire [universe].
Within all lands, he universally manifests the assemblies of all bodhisattvas; this is the sixtieth auspicious mark.
To his left, there is another mark of a great man called Universal Victorious Cloud, Sunlight Radiance Mani King Jewel Wheel Garland, which serves as an adornment.
It emits great flames of light that fill the oceans of worlds throughout the Dharma-realm, within which he manifests all worlds.
All the Tathāgatas of all realms and all sentient beings constitute the sixty-first auspicious mark.
On the left side, there is again a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Wondrous Sound Turning the Wheel of Dharma," adorned with the pure incense and medicinal herbs that are lamps of all dharmas.
It emits great radiance that fills the dharma-realm, within which the abodes of all Buddhas are universally manifested.
The ocean of marks and the ocean of mind constitute the sixty-second auspicious mark.
To the left, there is another mark of a great man called Cloud of Adornment, which uses the oceans of all Buddhas of the past, future, and present as its adornment;
it emits pure light that purifies and adorns all Buddha-lands, universally manifesting all Buddhas of the ten directions therein.
The practices performed by Bodhisattvas and Buddhas constitute the sixty-third [mark].

On the right hand of the Tathāgata is a mark of a great man called "Cloud Arrayed with All Jewels Illumined by the Ocean," which constantly emits the pure radiance of lunar flames that fills all worlds throughout space,
and issues forth a great sound praising all the practices of Bodhisattvas.
In the right hands of the sixty-four Tathāgatas, there is again a mark of a great man called Cloud Manifesting Radiant Illumination,
adorned with flowers of *vaiḍūrya* and *indranīla* maṇi jewels; it emits great light that universally illuminates all worlds,
such as the Lotus Treasury and Maṇi Treasury where Bodhisattvas dwell, appearing therein in their entirety.
Innumerable Buddhas, with their pure Dharma-bodies, sit beneath the Bodhi tree, shaking all the lands of the ten directions;

this is the sixty-fifth mark of a Tathāgata. Furthermore, on the right hand there is another mark of a great man called Lamp-Flame-Crest-Universal-Purity-Cloud, adorned with Vairocana-jewels, emitting great radiance that forms a net of transformations.
Within [this mark], there universally appear hosts of bodhisattvas, all wearing jeweled crowns and expounding the ocean of all practices; this is the sixty-sixth.
Furthermore, on the Tathāgata’s right hand, there is a mark of greatness called "Universal Manifestation of All Maṇi Clouds and Lotus Flame Lamps," which serves as an adornment.
It emits light from the ocean-treasury that pervades the entire dharma-realm, within which there universally appear immeasurable...
The Buddha sits upon a lotus throne; this constitutes the sixty-seventh Tathāgata.
Furthermore, his right hand possesses a mark of greatness called the Ocean of Maṇi Flames of Clouds of Radiance, which serves as an adornment.

It emits flames of various jewels, fragrant flames, and flower flames, along with pure light that fills all the networks of worlds, universally manifesting the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas therein.
The sixty-eighth Tathāgata has on his left hand a mark of a great man named Vaidūrya-Pariśuddha-Dīpa-Megha-Ratna-Bhūmi-Prabhāsa-varṇa-vyūha;
it emits the golden light of a Tathāgata, constantly manifesting all manner of supreme and wondrous ornaments in every thought-moment.
This is the sixty-ninth Tathāgata. Furthermore, on his left hand there is again a great...

The mark on the left hand of the Tathāgata is named Cloud of the Sound of the Lamp of Wisdom of All Lands, adorned with Indra’s net and diamond flowers, emitting the pure radiance of Jambūnada gold that universally illuminates all worlds in the ten directions;
this is the seventieth. Furthermore, the Tathāgata’s left hand has another mark of a great man named Abiding upon a Precious Lotus.

The multitude of clouds of light is adorned with exquisite flowers of various jewels, emitting great radiance like the Lamp of Mount Sumeru that universally illumines all worlds in the ten directions;

this is the seventy-first mark. Furthermore, on the Tathāgata’s left hand there is another mark of a great man called Cloud Illuminating the Dharma Realm, which consists of exquisite jewel garlands, jewel wheels, jewel vases, and Indra-nets.
Adorned with a multitude of wondrous marks, he emits great radiance that universally illuminates all lands throughout the ten directions;
therein he manifests all dharma-realms, all oceans of worlds, and all Tathāgatas seated upon lotus thrones—this constitutes the seventy-second [mark].
On the right hand of the Tathāgata is a mark of a great man called "Manifesting All Kalpas and Oceans of Lands."
It is adorned with swirling clouds, water-moons, flame-treasures, and *maṇi* kings of all kinds of precious flowers, emitting great radiance that fills the Dharma-realm;
from within it, subtle and wondrous sounds constantly emerge, filling the lands of the ten directions. This is the seventy-third [mark].
On the left hand of the Tathāgata is a mark of greatness called "Abiding in All Jewel Clouds," which is adorned with *indranīla* [gems]...
Adorned with blue vajra-jewels, it radiates the light of a multitude of maṇi-kings and various gems that fills the entire dharma-realm;
therein, all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are universally manifested. This is the seventy-fourth [mark].
On the palm of the Tathāgata’s right hand is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Radiance, which is adorned with a thousand-spoked jewel wheel of maṇi-kings.
Adorned with the emission of jewel radiance, that light spirals to the right and fills the Dharma-realm;
within it, the bodies of all Buddhas appear universally, their flames blazing as they preach the Dharma to deliver sentient beings and purify all worlds—this is the seventy-fifth [mark].
On the palms of the Tathāgatas' left hands is a mark of a great man called "Flame-Wheel Universal Increase," which manifests through transformation.
The Clouds of the Dharma-realm Bodhimanda are adorned with thousand-spoked wheels made of sun-light mani-kings,
emitting great radiance that fills all oceans of worlds. Within them, they manifest all bodhisattvas,
expounding the ocean of practices of Samantabhadra, entering all buddha-lands, and individually awakening immeasurable beings.

Sentient beings are the seventy-six Tathāgatas whose secret organ is concealed within a sheath (*kośagatavastiguhyatā*), a mark of a Great Man, named *Universal Emanation of Buddha-Sound-Clouds Adorned with All Sublime Jewels*. They radiate the brilliant light of *maṇi*-lamp flower-flames;
that light is intensely blazing, possessing the colors of all jewels, universally illuminating the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm, and therein universally manifests a single...
The fact that all Buddhas travel and come and go, pervading every place, constitutes the seventy-seventh mark of a Great Man on the right hip of the Tathāgatas,
called the "Cloud of Universally Illuminating Jewel Lamp Garlands. It is adorned with various *maṇi* jewels and emits inconceivable jewel-flame radiance,
which spreads throughout the entirety of the ten directions, the entire *dharmadhātu*, and the realm of empty space.
Being of one single mark, yet able to give birth to all marks, with every single mark manifesting the sovereign spiritual transformations of all Buddhas—

this is the seventy-eighth. On the left hip of the Tathāgata is a mark of greatness called "Cloud of Lotus-like Pure and Wondrous Jewels Manifesting the Light of the Ocean of All Dharma Realms Pervading Space."
Adorned with this, he emits a net of light that universally illumines all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions, wherein clouds of various manifestations appear everywhere;
this is the seventy-ninth mark of a Great Man on the right thigh of the Tathāgata, called "Universally Manifesting Clouds.
It is adorned with mani-jewels of myriad colors, its upper and lower portions being perfectly proportioned, and it radiates light.
The light of the sublime Dharma from the Niyama [mark] can, in a single thought-moment, universally manifest the ocean of marks of the walking-steps of all jewel-kings;
this is the eighty-first mark of a Great Man on the left thigh of the Tathāgata,
named "Manifesting the Ocean of Clouds of Infinite Marks of All Buddhas," which is adorned by abiding in accordance with all oceans of jewels, and through which he performs vast wanderings.
He emits pure light that universally illumines all sentient beings, causing them all to aspire to the unsurpassed Buddha-dharma;
this is the eighty-first mark of a Great Man on the right thigh of the Tathāgata,
called "Adorned with the Wondrous Jewel of Clouds of Light from the Dharma-realm of All Space," which is round and straight, enabling him to walk with grace as he emits [light].
The pure radiance of Jambūnada gold shines universally throughout all Buddha-worlds, emitting a great sound that causes them all to tremble;
furthermore, within all Buddha-lands, there appear beings dwelling in space adorned with jewel-flames,
from which immeasurable bodhisattvas are manifested— this is the eighty-second [mark], the *aineya* on the left side of the Tathāgata.
The calves of the Deer King possess a mark of a great man called Ocean-Cloud Adornment;
its color is like pure gold, it can travel throughout all buddha-fields, emitting pure light of all jewels that fills the dharma-realm and performs the work of a Buddha—this is the eighty-third.
The hair on the upper part of the Tathāgata’s precious calves possesses a mark of a great man called Universally Manifesting the Dharma-realm.
The clouds of reflected images upon his body have their hairs curling to the right;
from the tip of each hair, he emits jewel-like radiance that fills all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions, manifesting the spiritual powers of all Buddhas.
From all his pores, light is emitted, within which all Buddha-fields appear. This is the eighty-fourth mark of a Great Man: the soles of his feet are marked with the sign of the wheel.
The eighth is named "Clouds of the Abiding Ocean of All Bodhisattvas, with Colors Like Vajra-Jāmbūnada Gold,
Pure Lotus Flowers Emitting Precious Radiance Universally Illuminating the Oceans of Worlds in the Ten Directions, Clouds of Jewel-Fragrance Flames Pervading Everywhere,
and Fragrant Streams Flowing Upon Raising the Feet, Possessing the Colors of All Jewels and Filling the Dharma Realm."
Fifteenth, upon the right foot of the Tathāgata, there is a mark of a great man called "Universal Illumination Cloud of All Radiance," adorned with all kinds of precious jewels;
it emits great light that fills the Dharma-realm and manifests all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
This is the eighty-sixth [mark]. Sixteenth, upon the left foot of the Tathāgata, there is a mark of a great man called "Universal Manifestation."
The clouds of all Buddhas are adorned with jewel-treasury *maṇi*s, which emit precious light;

in every thought-moment, they manifest the supernatural transformations and the ocean of teachings of all Buddhas at their respective sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), continuing without interruption throughout all future kalpas.
This is the eighty-seventh [sign]. Between the right toes of the Tathāgata, there is a great man.
The mark named "Illuminating the Ocean-like Clouds of All Dharma Realms, Sumeru Lamp Mani King with Thousand-spoked Flaming Wheels," adorned with various ornaments,
radiates great light that fills all world-oceans throughout the ten directions of the entire dharma realm;
therein it universally manifests all the various jewel-adorned marks of all Buddhas— this is the eightieth.
Between the toes of the left feet of the eight Tathāgatas is a mark of a great man called "Manifesting the Ocean-Clouds of All Buddhas,
Maṇi-Jewel Flower Fragrance Flame Lamp Garlands Adorned with All Jewel Wheels.
It constantly emits a pure light from an ocean of jewels that fills the void and reaches all worlds throughout the ten directions, manifesting everything therein.
The perfect voices, the *śrīvatsa* mark, and other such signs of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas benefit immeasurable sentient beings;

this is the eighty-ninth [mark]. On the right heel of the Tathāgata is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Sovereign Radiance," adorned with powdered *indranīla* gems, which constantly emits the wondrous jewel-light of the Tathāgata; that light...
Excellently filling the Dharma-realm, all are of one single mark without distinction;
therein he manifests all Buddhas sitting at the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) expounding the sublime Dharma—this is the ninety-first [mark].

On the left heel of the Tathāgata is a mark of a great man called "Manifesting the Ocean-like Clouds of Sublime Sounds Expounding All Dharmas," which, by means of a maṇi-jewel of the ocean of transformations, [manifests these things].
The soles of the right feet of the ninety-first Tathāgata are adorned with oceans of jewel-incense flames, Sumeru-flowers, maṇi-jewels, and lapis lazuli,
emitting great radiance that fills the Dharma-realm; therein, the spiritual powers of all Buddhas are universally manifested—
this is the mark of a Great Man named "Cloud of Radiant Light Manifesting All Adornments from Myriad Jewels."

The left foot of the Tathāgata is adorned with a mark of greatness called "Cloud Manifesting All Colors," which produces exquisite adornments and emits pure light of Jambūnada gold that universally illuminates all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions;
the appearance of this light is like a great cloud that covers all the bodhimaṇḍas of all Buddhas. This is the ninety-second [mark].
Adorned with all moon-flame treasuries and Vairocana-jewel-indranīla gems, they traverse the oceans of all dharma-realms in every thought-moment,
emitting the light of mani-lamp incense-flames; this light pervades all dharma-realms—
this is the ninety-third mark of a great man on the circumference of the Tathāgata’s right foot.
It is adorned with the *Indranīla-vajra-ratna* clouds known as "Universal Treasury," which emit jewel-light that fills the void;
within this light, all Buddhas are manifested sitting upon lion-thrones made of the sovereign *maṇi*-jewel at their sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
This is the ninety-fourth mark of a Great Man located around the left foot of the Tathāgata. It is named:
The ninety-fifth is the Cloud of Universal Radiance Illuminating the Dharma Realm, adorned with mani-jewel flowers that emit great light filling the dharma realm in a single mark of equality;
therein they manifest the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
expounding through a wondrous and sublime voice the inexhaustible Dharma-gates of the dharma realm.
On the tip of the Tathāgata’s right toe is a mark of a great man called Cloud of Manifesting Adornments, which is most lovely and delightful.
It is adorned with pure Jambūnada gold and emits great light that fills all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions.
Within it, there are manifested the inexhaustible oceans of the seeds of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
The various meritorious supernatural transformations constitute the ninety-sixth [mark].

Upon the tip of each left toe of these Tathāgatas is a mark of a great man called "Cloud of Manifesting the Divine Transformations of All Buddhas," adorned with inconceivable Buddha-light moon-flames and universally fragrant maṇi-jewel flame-wheels.
It emits pure radiance of various jewel colors, filling the entire [universe].
Within all the oceans of worlds, he manifests all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, expounding the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas;

this is the ninety-seventh mark of a great man. O Son of the Buddha, the Tathāgata Vairocana possesses such marks as these, numbering as many as the atoms in ten Flower Treasury oceans of worlds, each part of his body adorned with various jewels.
[He] is adorned with sublime marks. [Treatise:

The final section summarizes the various marks, numbering as many as the atoms within ten Flower Treasury worlds, serving as a general conclusion that encompasses the entire text from the beginning, "At that time," down to this point;
thus, there are ninety-nine sections of scripture in total to encompass these ten flowers.
The Chapter on the Ocean of the Marks of the Ten Bodies Adorned with an Ocean of Marks as Numerous as the Dust-Motes of the Buddha-worlds:

The general purport of this chapter clarifies the three types of karmic activity—the vast and limitless benefits of body, speech, and wisdom—which bring forth the roots of goodness for all sentient beings.
It further describes the superior rewards and the marks of merit arising from these practices, beginning first with the thirty-two marks upon the crown of the head.

Within the mark of a great man called "Jeweled Adornment," there is a mark of a great man named "Illuminating All Directions and Universally Emitting Immeasurable Nets of Great Radiance, Adorned with All Mysterious Jewels.
First, the thirty kinds of jewels clarify the three types of karmic functions; these constitute the general characteristic of the ten thousand virtues. The two kinds of jewels are...
The two wisdoms of the Tathāgata’s three karmas are the foundation for cultivating all merits;
therefore, there is no ocean of myriad roots of goodness that does not take these three karmas and two wisdoms as its essence.
Thus, the fruit first attained is designated at the beginning as the foremost, and they are further used to adorn the head of the Tathāgata. As the sutra says: "Within it, there is a great..."
The human characteristic is named "Light Illuminating All Directions. "Directions" refers to the Dharma;
because it is the method by which fundamental wisdom (mūla-jñāna) becomes differentiated wisdom (pratyavekṣaṇā-jñāna), it universally emits immeasurable great nets of light.

This refers to the manifestation of the fruit resulting from the application of teachings according to the faculties of all sentient beings within differentiated wisdom to rescue and deliver them. In terms of its cause, it is called a "net of light."
"Adorned with all manner of exquisite jewels" means that all karmic fruits and the marks of merit obtained as retribution are adorned by these two types of wisdom.
"Jewel-hair pervading everywhere" clarifies that he governs and sustains beings through wisdom, circulating and universally covering them;
this is born of such retribution. "Jewel-hair that is soft and dense" signifies that his compassion is gentle and pervasive toward all beings.
Because the roots of universal salvation have been perfected, each and every jewel-hair emits the light of *maṇi* jewels that fills all infinite worlds,
manifesting the physical forms and marks of the Buddha in their full perfection; this clarifies that from the fundamental wisdom (*mūla-jñāna*), the various differentiated wisdoms arise,
and the performance of differentiated activities is entirely pure and stainless, such that one attains the *maṇi* jewels as a result of maturation (*vipākaja*).
The pure light of the Bhikṣuṇī transforms the Buddha-body; because these two wisdoms are purely immaculate and unimpeded, all their resultant objects collectively constitute the function of wisdom.
Therefore, they are identical to the body. Among these three types of karma, the first consists of one resultant [karma] and thirteen karmas;
the second consists of thirty karmas. Thus, regarding the two kinds of wisdom, there are thirty-two types of precious functions in total that adorn [the Buddha].
The mark of the protuberance on the crown (*uṣṇīṣa*) extends above this crown and throughout the body; briefly stated, there are ninety-seven kinds of marks of a Great Man (*mahāpuruṣa*).

This clarifies that, by relying on the two wisdoms of the ultimate and the conventional, purifying the three types of action (*trikarma*), practicing the seven factors of enlightenment (*bodhyaṅga*) and the ten perfections (*pāramitā*), and thereby being able to purify all nine grades of afflictions within the triple world, one takes wisdom as the means and employs that wisdom.
Because it is pure, all its resultant fruits are also pure; because wisdom is unimpeded and sovereign, all its resultant fruits are also sovereign.

Regarding the nine grades of afflictions: there is one grade in the desire realm, four grades in the form realm (the four dhyānas), and eight grades in the formless realm (the four dhyānas of the upper two realms).
Together with the one grade of the desire realm, these constitute the nine grades. There are those capable of awakening to them.
By means of the two wisdoms, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the ten pāramitās, through skillful means (*upāya*), one accomplishes self-benefit and the benefit of sentient beings;
by fulfilling the conduct of Samantabhadra, one brings these to completion and thereby manifests these ninety-seven marks.
