The Combined Commentary on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha, the Great Vaipulya, Scroll Eighty-Two.
The Sūtra translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a Śramaṇa from Khotan during the Tang Dynasty;
the Commentary composed by Li Tongxuan, a Lay Elder of Fangshan in Taiyuan during the Tang Dynasty.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhining of Kaiyuan Temple in Fuzhou during the Tang Dynasty, *The Combined Commentary on the Sūtra*, Chapter Thirty-Eight, Part Two: "The Transcendence of the World.
[Sūtra] O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of powers possessed by Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are these ten? They are as follows: namely, entering into one...
The power of entering all phenomena through their own intrinsic nature; the power of entering all phenomena as being like transformations; the power of entering all phenomena as being like illusions;
the power that all phenomena are the Buddha-dharma; the power of non-attachment toward all phenomena; the power of profound and clear understanding of all phenomena;
the power of never abandoning or failing to respect spiritual friends at any time; the power that causes [all beings] to become one...
The power of all roots of goodness that accord with and lead to the sovereignty of unsurpassed wisdom; the power of deep faith and non-slander toward all Buddha-dharmas;
the power of skillful means that prevents the mind of omniscience from ever regressing—these are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will possess the unsurpassed powers of the Tathāgata. O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of equanimity.
What are these ten? They are: equality toward all sentient beings; equality toward all phenomena; equality toward all buddha-fields;
equality toward all profound intentions; equality toward all roots of goodness; equality toward all bodhisattvas;
equality toward all vows; equality toward all perfections; and equality toward all practices.
The equality of all Buddhas constitutes the tenth. If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they shall attain the unsurpassed dharma of equality with all Buddhas.
Son of the Buddha, there are ten phrases of the true meaning of the Buddha-dharmas for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.
What are the ten? They are as follows: first, that all dharmas are merely names; second, that all dharmas are like illusions. First...
All phenomena are like reflections; all phenomena are merely dependent origination; all phenomena are pure through karma; all phenomena are produced by mere words;
all phenomena are the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); all phenomena are signless (*animitta*); all phenomena are the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*);
all phenomena are the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*). These are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will skillfully enter [into them].
The Buddha-son, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, speaks of ten kinds of dharmas concerning the supreme, true meaning of the knowledge of all-knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).
What are these ten? They are: speaking of the profound dharma; speaking of the vast dharma; speaking of various dharmas; speaking of the dharma of all-knowledge;
speaking of the dharmas that accord with the *pāramitās*; speaking of the dharmas that give rise to the powers of the Tathāgata; and speaking of the three periods of time.
The teaching on the dharmas of correspondence, the teaching on the dharmas that cause Bodhisattvas not to regress, the teaching on the praise of the Buddha’s merits,
the teaching on all the trainings of Bodhisattvas, the teaching on the equality of all Buddhas, and the teaching on the dharmas corresponding to the realm of all Tathāgatas—
these are the ten. If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed skill in preaching the Dharma, O Son of the Buddha.
A Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has ten kinds of upholding. What are these ten? They are: upholding all accumulated roots of merit and virtue;
upholding all teachings spoken by all Tathāgatas; upholding all parables; upholding all gateways to the principles of all dharmas;
upholding all gateways of *dhāraṇī* that bring forth [realization]; and upholding all dharmas that eliminate doubt and confusion.
They accomplish all bodhisattva dharmas; they uphold the gate of the samādhi of equality spoken by all Tathāgatas;
they uphold the gate of illumination of all dharmas; and they uphold the power of the miraculous play of the supernatural faculties of all Buddhas—these are the ten.
O Son of the Buddha, if bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will obtain the sustaining power of the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed great wisdom.
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas have ten kinds of eloquence (*pratibhāna*). What are the ten? They are: eloquence that is non-discriminative regarding all phenomena;
eloquence that is without activity regarding all phenomena; eloquence that is without attachment regarding all phenomena;
eloquence that thoroughly realizes emptiness regarding all phenomena; and eloquence that is free from the darkness of doubt regarding all phenomena.
The eloquence empowered by the Buddhas regarding all phenomena; the eloquence of self-awakening regarding all phenomena;
the eloquence of skill in the differentiation of words and phrases regarding all phenomena; the eloquence of speaking the truth regarding all phenomena;
and the eloquence that gladdens the minds of all sentient beings according to their inclinations—these are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide in them...
By this dharma, one attains the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed and skillful eloquence. Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of mastery for a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva.
What are these ten? They are: mastery in teaching and disciplining all sentient beings;
mastery in universally illuminating all dharmas; mastery in the practice of cultivating all roots of goodness; and mastery in vast wisdom.
Mastery over precepts that are without dependence; mastery in dedicating all roots of goodness toward enlightenment;
mastery in non-retrogressive diligence; mastery in wisdom that crushes and destroys all demons; mastery in causing [beings] to resolve upon bodhicitta according to their inclinations;
and mastery in manifesting the attainment of perfect awakening according to those who are to be transformed—these are the ten. If any bodhisattvas...
When a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, a son of the Buddha, dwells securely in this Dharma, they attain the Tathāgata’s supreme mastery of great wisdom.
There are ten kinds of non-attachment; what are these ten? They are:
non-attachment toward all worlds, non-attachment toward all sentient beings, non-attachment toward all phenomena, and non-attachment toward all activities.
To be unattached to all roots of goodness, unattached to all places of rebirth,
unattached to all vows, unattached to all practices, unattached to all bodhisattvas, and unattached to all buddhas— these are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will be able to swiftly transform all conceptual perceptions.
Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the sons of the Buddha, who possess unsurpassed, pure wisdom, have ten kinds of impartial mind.
What are these ten? They are: the impartial mind that accumulates all merits; the impartial mind that gives rise to all distinct vows;
the impartial mind regarding the bodies of all sentient beings; and the impartial mind regarding the karmic retributions of all sentient beings... [and so forth].
It is the mind of equanimity toward all phenomena; the mind of equanimity toward all pure and impure lands;
the mind of equanimity that understands all sentient beings as equal; the mind of equanimity that makes no distinctions among all practices;
the mind of equanimity regarding the powers and fearlessnesses of all Buddhas; and the mind of equanimity regarding the wisdom of all Tathāgatas. This is it.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these ten, they shall attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, great mind of equanimity.
O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of wisdom that give birth to the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas. What are the ten? They are:
the wisdom that knows how to give rise to the understanding of all sentient beings; the wisdom that gives rise to knowledge of the various distinctions among all Buddha-fields; [and so forth].
They give birth to the wisdom that knows the divisions and sections of the net of the ten directions; they give birth to the wisdom that knows all worlds, whether inverted or upright;
they give birth to the wisdom that knows the vast abiding in the single nature and manifold natures of all phenomena;
they give birth to the wisdom that knows all various bodies; and they give birth to the wisdom that knows the inverted delusions of all worlds.
The wisdom born from being entirely without attachment; the wisdom born from knowing that all phenomena ultimately transcend through a single path;
the wisdom born from knowing the Tathāgata’s spiritual power to enter all dharma-realms;
and the wisdom born from knowing that the Buddha-seed of all sentient beings throughout the three periods of time is never severed—these are the ten. If any bodhisattvas...
When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the Son of the Buddha, dwells securely in this Dharma, there is nothing among all phenomena that he does not fully comprehend.
There are ten kinds of transformations of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva; what are these ten? They are:
the transformation of all sentient beings, the transformation of all bodies, the transformation of all lands, the transformation of all offerings, and the transformation of all sounds. First...
The transformation of all practices and vows; the transformation of all teachings that discipline and subdue sentient beings; the transformation of all attainments of perfect enlightenment;
the transformation of all preaching of the Dharma; and the transformation of all empowerments—these are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will become fully endowed with all supreme dharmas of transformation, O Son of the Buddha! Bodhisattva!
Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of sustaining powers (*bala*). What are these ten? They are:

the sustaining power of the Buddha, the sustaining power of the Dharma, the sustaining power of sentient beings, the sustaining power of karma, the sustaining power of conduct, the sustaining power of vows, the sustaining power of the objective realm, the sustaining power of time, the sustaining power of goodness, and the sustaining power of wisdom. These are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, then regarding one...
All dharmas attain the supreme power of mastery. Sons of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of great consolation.
What are these ten? They are as follows: all Bodhisattvas give rise to this thought:
"Throughout all future ages, whenever any Buddhas appear in the world, I shall follow and serve them all, causing them to rejoice. As it is said: [and so forth].

With a mind of great joy and comfort from such reflection, he further thinks: "When those Tathāgatas appear in the world, I shall honor and make offerings to them all with unsurpassed requisites. With a mind of great joy and comfort from such reflection, he further thinks:
"When I present offerings to those Buddhas, those Tathāgatas will surely grant me instruction and guidance."
I have listened to and received this Dharma with a profound mind of reverence, and I shall practice it exactly as taught.

I will certainly attain birth in the bodhisattva stages—whether already born, currently being born, or yet to be born—and with such thoughts, my heart is filled with great joy and consolation. Furthermore, I resolve:
"Throughout unspeakably unspeakable eons, I shall practice the bodhisattva conduct, always in the company of all Buddhas and bodhisattvas."
Attaining such a state of shared realization, he reflects with great joy and further thinks:

"In the past, before I had resolved upon the unsurpassed, great Bodhicitta, I was possessed of various fears—namely, the fear of lacking a livelihood, the fear of ill repute, the fear of death, the fear of falling into the evil realms, and the fear of the majesty of the great assembly. Yet, from the moment I first resolved my mind [upon enlightenment], all these have been entirely abandoned."
Startled yet not terrified, not fearful, not cowed, and not afraid, they cannot be destroyed by any demons or externalists.
Reflecting thus, their hearts are filled with great solace and joy. They further think:
"I shall cause all sentient beings to attain unexcelled bodhi; once they have attained bodhi, I shall practice the bodhisattva path under those Buddhas."
Throughout the remainder of their lives, they shall generate great faith to offer all appropriate articles of worship to the Buddhas;
furthermore, after their parinirvāṇa, they shall each erect immeasurable stupas to honor the relics and uphold and protect all the remaining teachings.
Contemplating in this way, their hearts will be filled with great joy and satisfaction. They will further think: "All that exists throughout the ten directions..."
"I shall adorn all worlds with unsurpassed adornments, causing them all to be fully endowed with various wonders, equality, and purity.

Furthermore, by means of various great supernormal powers, I shall sustain, shake, and illuminate them, causing these qualities to pervade everywhere. Thinking thus, his heart was filled with great joy and he further reflected:
I shall sever the doubts and delusions of all sentient beings, purify the aspirations of all sentient beings, awaken the minds and intentions of all sentient beings,
extinguish the afflictions of all sentient beings, close the gates to the evil destinies for all sentient beings,
open the gates to the auspicious realms for all sentient beings, shatter the darkness of all sentient beings, and bestow light upon all sentient beings.
"May all sentient beings be freed from the deeds of Māra, and may all sentient beings reach the place of peace and security.
Thinking thus, his heart was filled with great joy and consolation. Furthermore, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva formed this thought:
"The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are as difficult to encounter as the Udumbara flower; in immeasurable kalpas, one may not see even a single one. In the future, I shall [encounter them]."
If those in the world wish to see the Tathāgata, they shall immediately behold all the Buddha-Tathāgatas.
May the Tathāgatas never abandon me, but dwell constantly within my presence, enabling me to see them and allowing them to preach the Dharma for me without interruption.
Having heard the Dharma, may my mind become pure, free from flattery and crookedness, upright and without guile. In every thought-moment, may I constantly see the Buddhas; may I contemplate thus.
With great joy in his mind, he further thought: "In the future, I shall attain Buddhahood;

by the spiritual power of a Buddha, I will manifest the attainment of equal and perfect enlightenment for all sentient beings in all worlds, each individually, as a Great Lion’s Roar that is pure and fearless.
By virtue of my original great vow, I shall pervade the entire Dharma-realm, beat the Great Dharma Drum, and rain down [the Dharma]."
Raining down the great Dharma rain, they constantly perform the great gift of Dharma throughout immeasurable eons, perpetually expounding the True Dharma.
Sustained by great compassion, their physical, verbal, and mental actions are never weary or exhausted. Contemplating in this way, their minds experience great consolation and joy.
O Son of the Buddha, these are the ten kinds of great consolation for Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas; if Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they shall attain [the state of] non-... [omitted].

The Buddhas, the Sons of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who have attained supreme perfect enlightenment and possess great joy in wisdom, have ten kinds of profound entry into the Buddha-dharma.
What are these ten? They are: entering all worlds of the past; entering all worlds of the future; entering all worlds of the present;
entering the enumeration of worlds; entering the activities of worlds; and entering the teachings concerning worlds.
Purified, they enter into the various natures of all worlds; they enter into the various karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
they enter into the various practices and knowledges of all bodhisattvas; they know the succession of all past buddhas;
they know the succession of all future buddhas; and they know all the buddha-lands of the present throughout the ten directions, equal to the void and the dharma-realm.

They skillfully teach the Dharma for the sake of taming beings, knowing the dharmas of the world, the dharmas of śrāvakas, the dharmas of pratyekabuddhas, the dharmas of bodhisattvas, and the dharmas of Tathāgatas.
Although they know that all dharmas are without discrimination, they expound various teachings, all of which enter the dharma-realm because there is nothing to enter.
Thus, they teach according to the nature of those dharmas without grasping or attachment; this is the tenth. If bodhisattvas abide in these...
By this principle, one enters the great wisdom and profound nature of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of bases upon which Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas rely to practice the conduct of a Bodhisattva. What are these ten? They are:
relying on the practice of making offerings to all Buddhas to practice the conduct of a Bodhisattva; relying on... [the rest of the text follows].
The practice of a bodhisattva that relies upon taming all sentient beings; the practice of a bodhisattva that relies upon approaching and attending upon all virtuous friends;
the practice of a bodhisattva that relies upon accumulating all roots of goodness;
the practice of a bodhisattva that relies upon purifying all buddha-fields; the practice of a bodhisattva that relies upon never abandoning any sentient being.
Entering deeply into all perfections is the bodhisattva practice; relying on the fulfillment of all bodhisattva vows is the bodhisattva practice;
relying on the immeasurable practices of the bodhicitta is the bodhisattva practice;
and relying on the bodhi of all Buddhas is the bodhisattva practice. These are the ten [bases] upon which a bodhisattva practices, O Son of the Buddha.
Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of resolve to give rise to a fearless mind. What are these ten? They are: the resolve to give rise to a fearless mind by extinguishing all obstructive karma;
the resolve to give rise to a fearless mind by protecting and upholding the True Dharma after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa; the resolve to give rise to a fearless mind by subduing all Māras;
the resolve to give rise to a fearless mind by not begrudging one’s own body or life; and the resolve to shatter and destroy all... [obstacles].
He gives rise to a fearless mind that refutes the heterodox and erroneous doctrines of outsiders; he gives rise to a fearless mind that causes all sentient beings to rejoice;
he gives rise to a fearless mind that causes all those in the assembly to rejoice;
and he gives rise to a fearless mind that subdues all devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.
To leave behind the stages of the two vehicles and enter the profound Dharma, giving rise to a fearless mind;
to practice the bodhisattva conduct for unspeakably unspeakable eons with a mind free from weariness or fatigue, giving rise to a fearless mind—this is the tenth.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed great wisdom and fearless mind. O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva...
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives rise to ten kinds of minds free from doubt regarding all Buddha-dharmas, with no uncertainty in his mind.
What are these ten? They are as follows: the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva gives rise to such a mind as this: "I shall gather in all sentient beings through giving;
I shall gather in all sentient beings through ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, wisdom, kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity."
When generating this mind, one must be resolute and free from doubt; for it is impossible that doubt should arise. This is the first [vow]:
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva generates the mind of being free from doubt. Furthermore, he reflects: "When all future Buddhas appear in the world, I shall serve and make offerings to them all.
When generating this mind, one must be resolute and free from doubt; for it is impossible that doubt should arise.
That his mind would harbor such a state is impossible; this is the second arising of the mind of a bodhisattva mahāsattva free from doubt.
Furthermore, he reflects: "I shall universally adorn all worlds with various wondrous nets of light.
When he gives rise to this thought, he is certain and without doubt; that he would give rise to a doubting mind is impossible—this is the third.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Free from Doubt further reflects: "I shall, throughout all kalpas until the end of the future, cultivate the bodhisattva practices—practices that are innumerable, immeasurable, boundless, incomparable, incalculable, ineffable, inconceivable, unfathomable, unspeakable, and beyond the reach of speech;
practices that transcend all calculation and reach the ultimate limit of the Dharma-realm."
"I shall bring all sentient beings throughout the realm of empty space to maturity by means of the unsurpassed methods of teaching and discipline.
When this thought is generated, it is certain and without doubt; for it is impossible that such doubt should arise.
This is the fourth generation of the mind of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva who is free from doubt. Furthermore, he reflects: "I shall cultivate the bodhisattva..."
When one fulfills great vows, possesses all-knowledge, and dwells therein, at the moment of generating this mind, one is certain and without doubt;
it is impossible for a mind of doubt to arise. This is the fifth generation of the mind of non-doubt by a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva.
Furthermore, he reflects: "I shall universally practice the conduct of a Bodhisattva for the sake of the entire world as if for a single being."
All phenomena are pure and luminous, illuminating all Buddha-dharmas. When this mind is generated, it is certain and free from doubt;
for it to give rise to doubt is impossible. This is the sixth generation of the mind of a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva:
the mind free from doubt. Furthermore, he reflects: "I shall know that all phenomena are indeed Buddha-dharmas, according to sentient beings..."
He expounds it for them with his mind so as to cause them all to attain awakening. When he gives rise to this mind, he is resolute and without doubt;
it is impossible for a mind of doubt to arise. This is the seventh [vow]: the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva gives rise to a mind free from doubt.
Furthermore, he reflects: "I shall attain the gate of non-obstruction regarding all phenomena, knowing that all obstructions are ungraspable."
Because they have attained this, their minds are thus free from doubt and abide in true reality, continuing until the attainment of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
When they give rise to this mind, they are certain and without doubt; it is impossible for a mind of doubt to arise. This is the eighth [perfection]:
the bodhisattva mahāsattva who gives rise to a mind free from doubt. Furthermore, he reflects as follows:
I shall know that all phenomena are none other than supramundane dharmas;
having distanced myself from all false conceptions and inversions, I shall adorn myself with a single adornment, yet remain without anything to adorn.
Having realized this for myself and not through the awakening of another, when I give rise to this mind, it is certain and without doubt; were a mind of doubt to arise, such a thing is impossible.
For the sake of the ninth stage, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who has given rise to a mind free from doubt further reflects:

"I shall attain supreme perfect enlightenment regarding all phenomena (*sarvadharma*) because I am free from all conceptual constructions (*vikalpa*) and inversions (*viparyāsa*); because I have attained the wisdom of single-moment correspondence (*ekakṣaṇa-samprayukta-jñāna*);

because neither identity nor difference can be apprehended; because I am free from all numerical reckonings; and because I have reached the ultimate unconditioned (*atyanta-asaṃskṛta*). Thus he is liberated.
Because all verbal expressions ultimately abide in the limit of the ineffable realm, when this mind is generated, it is certain and free from doubt;
for it is impossible that a mind of doubt would arise. This is the tenth generation of the mind of non-doubt.
If Bodhisattvas dwell securely in this Dharma, they will have no doubts whatsoever regarding any of the Buddha-dharmas. O Son of the Buddha, these are the Bodhisattva-mahasattvas...
Bodhisattvas have ten kinds of inconceivability. What are the ten? They are: the inconceivability of all roots of goodness;
the inconceivability of all vows; the inconceivability of knowing that all phenomena are like illusions;
the inconceivability of generating the bodhicitta and practicing the bodhisattva path without losing those roots of goodness and without any conceptual discrimination.
Although their deliberations penetrate deeply into all phenomena, they do not take parinirvāṇa because all their vows have not yet been fulfilled. Inconceivably practicing the bodhisattva path,
they manifest descending from heaven, entering the womb, being born, leaving home, practicing austerities, proceeding to the site of enlightenment,
subduing the hosts of Māra, attaining supreme perfect awakening, turning the wheel of the true Dharma, and entering parinirvāṇa.
The sovereign mastery of miraculous transformations is unceasing; never abandoning compassionate vows to rescue and protect sentient beings, it is inconceivable.

Although he can manifest the sovereign mastery of the Tathāgata’s ten powers and miraculous transformations, yet he does not abandon the mind that is equal to the Dharma-realm in teaching and transforming sentient beings—this is inconceivable.
He knows that all phenomena are signless, and that this very sign is itself non-existence.
The characteristic of non-discrimination is discrimination, and discrimination is non-discrimination; that which is not existent is existent, and that which is existent is non-existent;
non-action is action, and action is non-action; that which is not speech is speech, and that which is speech is non-speech.
This inconceivable state knows that the mind is equal to bodhi, knows that bodhi is equal to the mind, and [knows] that the mind, bodhi, and sentient beings are [equal].
They likewise do not give rise to mental distortions, conceptual distortions, or view-distortions; they are inconceivable.

In every moment of thought, they enter the meditative absorption of cessation (*nirodha-samāpatti*) and exhaust all outflows (*āsrava*), yet they do not realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). They do not exhaust their roots of goodness that are free from outflows;
though they know all phenomena are without outflows, they also know the exhaustion of outflows and the cessation of outflows. Though they know the Buddha-dharma...

That which is worldly phenomena is itself the Buddha-dharma; yet within the Buddha-dharma one does not differentiate worldly phenomena, nor within worldly phenomena does one differentiate the Buddha-dharma. All phenomena enter the Dharma-realm because there is nothing to enter.
Thus one knows that all phenomena are non-dual and immutable. This is the tenth inconceivable [quality].
"O Son of the Buddha, these are the ten kinds of inconceivability of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas;
if Bodhisattvas abide in them, they shall attain all the unsurpassed, inconceivable dharmas of all Buddhas.
O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of skillful esoteric speech. What are the ten? Namely, regarding all..."
The skillful and esoteric language of the Buddha’s sūtras regarding all places of rebirth;

the skillful and esoteric language regarding the manifestation of all bodhisattvas’ supernormal powers and their attainment of equal and perfect enlightenment; the skillful and esoteric language regarding the karmic retribution of all sentient beings;

the skillful and esoteric language regarding the defilement and purification arising in all sentient beings; and the skillful and esoteric language regarding the ultimate non-existence of all phenomena.

Regarding the skillful secret language of the gateway of obstacles: throughout every single location within all realms of empty space, there are worlds either forming or decaying, with no intervening empty space; this is the skillful secret language.

Throughout the entire dharma-realm and in all ten directions, even down to the most minute points, there are Tathāgatas manifesting from their initial birth through to their attainment of Buddhahood and entry into parinirvāṇa.
The skillful esoteric language sees the entire Dharma-realm filled and pervaded, yet it discerns and perceives all sentient beings as equal in unchanging nirvāṇa;
thus, it does not abandon the great vow so that the vow for omniscience may be brought to fulfillment.
Although the skillful esoteric language knows all phenomena and awakens to them without depending on others, it does not abandon or depart from the various...
To further increase one’s respect for spiritual friends toward the Tathāgata; to be in harmony with spiritual friends without duality;
to cultivate and plant all roots of goodness and dedicate them; to abide in the same activity, the same nature, the same renunciation, and the same accomplishment;
and to be skilled in esoteric speech—these are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide in these...
In this way, one attains the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed, skillful, and subtle secret speech. O Son of the Buddha, there are ten kinds of skillful discerning wisdom for Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas.
What are these ten? They are: the skillful discerning wisdom that enters all lands;
the skillful discerning wisdom that enters the abodes of all sentient beings; and the skillful discerning wisdom that enters the mental activities of all sentient beings.
The wisdom that enters into the skillful discernment of the faculties of all sentient beings; the wisdom that enters into the skillful discernment of the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
the wisdom that enters into the skillful discernment of the practices of all śrāvakas; the wisdom that enters into the skillful discernment of the practices of all pratyekabuddhas;
the wisdom that enters into the skillful discernment of the practices of all bodhisattvas; and the wisdom that enters into the skillful discernment of all worldly dharmas.
The wisdom that enters all Buddha-dharmas through skillful discernment is the tenth.
If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they attain the supreme, skillful wisdom of all Buddhas for discerning all phenomena.
Sons of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten ways of entering samādhi. What are these ten? They are: [entering] into all worlds...
Entering samādhi within the realms and sense-bases; entering samādhi within the bodies of all sentient beings;
entering samādhi within all phenomena; entering samādhi in beholding all Buddhas; entering samādhi in abiding through all kalpas;
entering samādhi in arising from samādhi to manifest inconceivable bodies; entering samādhi within the bodies of all Buddhas; and awakening all sentient beings.
Entering samādhi with equanimity; entering all bodhisattva samādhis and wisdoms within a single thought-moment;
entering samādhi with unimpeded wisdom to accomplish all the practices and vows of all bodhisattvas without rest—entering samādhi in this way constitutes the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide therein, they shall obtain the [Dharma-body] of all Buddhas.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, the sons of the Buddha, possess ten kinds of universal entry into the methods of supreme skillful samādhi.
What are these ten? They are: universal entry into sentient beings; universal entry into lands; universal entry into the various characteristics of worlds;

universal entry into the calamity of fire; universal entry into the calamity of water; universal entry into Buddhas; universal entry into adornments; and universal entry into the boundless merits of the Tathāgatas.
The body universally entering all various forms of preaching the Dharma; universally entering all various offerings to the Tathāgatas—these are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they will attain the Tathāgata’s supreme great wisdom that universally enters all phenomena.
O Sons of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten gates of liberation. What are these ten?
These are: the liberation door of a single body pervading all worlds;
the liberation door of manifesting infinite varieties of physical forms in all worlds; the liberation door of entering all worlds into a single Buddha-field;
the liberation door of universally sustaining all realms of sentient beings; and the liberation door of filling [all realms] with bodies adorned by all Buddhas.
The liberation door of filling all worlds; the liberation door of seeing all worlds within one's own body;
the liberation door of going to all worlds in a single thought-moment; the liberation door of manifesting the appearance of all Tathāgatas in a single world;
the liberation door of a single body filling the entire dharma-realm; and in a single thought-moment...
To manifest the liberation door of all Buddhas’ playful supernatural powers is the tenth.
If Bodhisattvas abide within these, they shall attain the Tathāgata’s unsurpassed liberation door. Sons of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of supernatural powers.
What are the ten? They are: the supernormal knowledge of the skillful means of remembering billions of past lives; the divine ear; and so forth.
The supernormal power of unimpeded knowledge of skillful means that understands the inconceivable mental activities of other sentient beings;

the supernormal power of knowledge of skillful means that observes with the divine eye without obstruction; the supernormal power of skillful means that manifests inconceivable great spiritual powers according to the minds of sentient beings;
and the supernormal power of skillful means that universally manifests a single body throughout immeasurable worlds.
The skillful wisdom-penetration of mindfulness that enters unspeakably unspeakable worlds;
the skillful wisdom-penetration that produces immeasurable ornaments to adorn inconceivable worlds; the skillful wisdom-penetration that manifests unspeakable transformation bodies;
and the skillful wisdom-penetration that appears in unspeakable worlds according to the minds of inconceivable sentient beings.
The skillful means of the wisdom of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* constitutes the tenth.

If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they attain the unsurpassed and great skillful supernatural powers (*abhijñā*) of the Tathāgata, manifesting in various ways for the sake of all sentient beings and causing them to practice and learn.
O Sons of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of clarity (*vidyā*). What are they?
These constitute the ten [knowledges], namely: the skillful knowledge of wisdom that knows the karmic retributions of all sentient beings;
the skillful knowledge of wisdom that knows the realm of all sentient beings to be quiescent, pure, and free from all conceptual proliferation (*prapañca*);

and the skillful knowledge of wisdom that knows the various objects of focus of all sentient beings to be of a single characteristic (*ekalakṣaṇa*), such that they are entirely unapprehendable, and that all phenomena are like adamant (*vajra*).
The light of skillful wisdom can universally cause immeasurable, subtle, and wondrous sounds to be heard throughout all worlds in the ten directions;
the light of skillful wisdom universally destroys all mental attachments and defilements;
the light of skillful wisdom is able to manifest through skillful means both taking birth and not taking birth; the light of skillful wisdom relinquishes all realms of perception and sensation.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Skillful Wisdom-Light, who knows that all dharmas are neither with marks nor without marks,
being of a single nature yet devoid of intrinsic nature and free from conceptual discrimination; who is yet able to comprehend the various kinds of dharmas and,
throughout immeasurable eons, analytically expound them while abiding in the dharma-realm and attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
They know that the birth of all sentient beings is fundamentally non-existent; because they have thoroughly realized that the process of taking birth cannot be apprehended,
they know causes, they know conditions, they know phenomena, they know objects, they know conduct, they know arising, they know cessation, they know verbal expression, they know delusion,
they know the departure from delusion, they know inversion, they know the departure from inversion, they know affliction, they know purification, and they know birth-and-death.
He knows nirvāṇa; he knows what is knowable and what is unknowable; he knows attachment and non-attachment;
he knows stability and movement; he knows departure and return; he knows arising and non-arising; he knows ruin and renunciation; he knows maturation; he knows the faculties;
and he knows how to discipline and teach them in various ways as appropriate, never forgetting the duties of a bodhisattva.
Regarding practice: for what reason does a bodhisattva resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* solely for the benefit of sentient beings and for no other purpose?
Therefore, a bodhisattva constantly transforms sentient beings without physical fatigue and does not contravene anything performed in the world;
this is called the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s clear wisdom of skill in dependent origination (*pratītyasamutpāda-kuśala-jñāna*).
He is unattached to the Buddha and does not give rise to a mind of attachment; he is unattached to the Dharma and does not give rise to a mind of attachment;
he is unattached to the lands and does not give rise to a mind of attachment; he is unattached to sentient beings and does not give rise to a mind of attachment.

While he teaches, disciplines, and preaches the Dharma without perceiving the existence of sentient beings, he nevertheless never abandons the various practices of a bodhisattva, nor his great compassion and great vows.
Having heard the Dharma from the Buddha, they practice in accordance with it, planting all roots of goodness based upon the Tathāgata, and honoring and making offerings to him without ceasing.
They are able to use their supernormal powers to shake immeasurable worlds throughout the ten directions, for their minds are vast and equal to the Dharma-realm.
Thus, they know the various ways of preaching the Dharma; they know the number of sentient beings, they know the distinctions among sentient beings, and they know the arising of suffering.
Knowing the cessation of suffering and knowing that all conditioned phenomena are like reflections, they practice the bodhisattva path to forever sever the root of all rebirth.
They practice the bodhisattva path solely for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings, yet they act without acting.
In accordance with the lineage of all Buddhas, they give rise to a mind like the king of great mountains, knowing all things to be false and inverted.
Entering the gateway of all-knowledge, their wisdom is vast and unshakable;
they shall attain perfect enlightenment and skillfully ferry all sentient beings across the ocean of birth and death with the light of their skillful wisdom—this is the tenth.
If Bodhisattvas abide therein, O Son of the Buddha, they shall attain the Tathāgata’s supreme and great skillful light of wisdom.
Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of liberation. What are these ten? They are: liberation from afflictions; liberation from false views;
liberation from all grasping; liberation from the aggregates, bases, and elements; liberation that transcends the two vehicles;
liberation through the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena; and liberation from attachment to all worlds, all lands, all sentient beings, and all dharmas.
The liberation of dwelling in the boundless; the liberation of initiating all bodhisattva practices; the liberation of entering the Tathāgata’s stage of non-conceptuality;
and the liberation of being able to fully comprehend all three periods of time within a single thought-moment—these are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they are then able to perform the unsurpassed work of a Buddha, teaching and bringing others to maturity.
O sons of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of groves. What are the ten? They are as follows:

Birth-and-death (*saṃsāra*) is the grove of Bodhisattvas because they never weary of renouncing it; teaching and transforming sentient beings is the grove of Bodhisattvas because they do not grow weary;
abiding through all kalpas is the grove of Bodhisattvas because they embrace all great practices; [purity]...
The pure world is a park and grove for the bodhisattva, as it is that upon which he relies; all the palaces of Māra are a park and grove for the bodhisattva, as they are to be subdued;
reflecting upon the teachings one has heard is a park and grove for the bodhisattva, as it involves investigation according to reality;
the six perfections, the four means of attraction, and the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment are the [park and grove] of the bodhisattva...
Because they inherit the realm of their compassionate fathers, the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, the eighteen unique qualities,
and even all Buddha-dharmas constitute the grove of the bodhisattva, for they do not dwell upon other dharmas. Manifesting all the majestic power, sovereign mastery,
and supernormal faculties of bodhisattvas constitutes the grove of the bodhisattva, by which they turn the wheel of the true Dharma through great spiritual power.
Because they tame sentient beings without rest, in a single thought-moment they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment in all places for the sake of all sentient beings;
because their Dharma-body pervades all worlds throughout the entirety of space—these are the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they shall attain the unsurpassed freedom from sorrow and affliction of the Tathāgata.
O sons of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who practice the Great Peaceful and Joyful Conduct have ten kinds of palaces. What are these ten?
They are as follows: the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*) is the palace of the Bodhisattva, because it is never forgotten;

the merit and wisdom of the ten paths of wholesome action are the palace of the Bodhisattva, because they transform sentient beings in the desire realm; and the four Brahma-abodes and meditative concentrations...
This bodhisattva’s palace arises in the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven in order to transform sentient beings of the form realm;
this bodhisattva’s palace arises in the formless realm because it is untainted by any afflictions;
this bodhisattva’s palace arises in defiled worlds in order to cause all sentient beings to leave behind places of hardship; this bodhisattva’s palace causes all sentient beings...
Because he has severed the afflictions, his dwelling within the inner palace with wife, children, and retinue is a bodhisattva’s palace;
because he manifests as a wheel-turning monarch, a world-protector, Śakra, or Brahmā to [gather] sentient beings who practiced together in the past, this is a bodhisattva’s palace;
and because he dwells in all bodhisattva practices to tame those sentient beings whose minds are autonomous, he attains mastery over the playful superknowledges.
Mastery is the palace of the bodhisattva, because they skillfully sport in all meditative absorptions (*dhyāna*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), samādhis, and wisdom;
it is the palace of the bodhisattva where they receive the consecration (*abhiṣeka*) and prediction of the supreme mastery of the King of All-Knowledge from all Buddhas;

it is the palace of the bodhisattva who dwells in the adornment of the ten powers (*daśabala*) to exercise sovereign authority over all dharmas as a Dharma King—this constitutes the ten. If there are any bodhisattvas...
When the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, a Son of the Buddha, dwells therein, they obtain the Dharma-consecration and attain sovereign power through spiritual might over all worlds.
There are ten kinds of delights for such a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva; what are these ten? They are: delighting in right mindfulness because the mind is not distracted;
delighting in wisdom because it discerns all phenomena; and delighting in approaching the presence of all Buddhas.
They delight in hearing the Dharma without weariness; they delight in the Buddhas filling the ten directions to their infinite limits;
they delight in the sovereign power of Bodhisattvas who manifest bodies for the sake of all sentient beings through immeasurable gateways;

they delight in the gateways of samādhi, wherein by entering a single gateway to samādhi one enters all gateways to samādhi; and they delight in dhāraṇīs, which maintain the Dharma without forgetting so that it may be transmitted to others.

For the sake of sentient beings, they delight in unimpeded eloquence, because they can analyze and expound upon a single word or a single phrase of the sutras for unspeakable eons without ever reaching exhaustion;
they delight in attaining perfect enlightenment, because they manifest the attainment of perfect enlightenment through immeasurable gateways for the sake of all sentient beings;
and they delight in turning the wheel of Dharma, because it crushes and destroys all heterodox paths. This is...
If Bodhisattvas abide in these ten dharmas, they shall attain the unsurpassed dharma-bliss of all Buddhas, Tathāgatas.
O Sons of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of adornments. What are the ten? They are:
the adornment of power, because it is indestructible; the adornment of fearlessness, because it cannot be overcome; the adornment of meaning, because its explanations are... [inexhaustible].
The adornment of Dharma, because the meaning that can be explained is inexhaustible;
the adornment of vows, because one observes and expounds the eighty-four thousand clusters of Dharma without forgetfulness;
the adornment of conduct, because one transcends through the cultivation of the practices of Samantabhadra; and the adornment of lands, because all lands are made into a single land.
Thus, there is the adornment of universal sound, which rains down the rain of Dharma throughout all Buddha-worlds;
the adornment of sustaining power, which maintains the practice of countless deeds throughout all kalpas without interruption;
and the adornment of transformation, which manifests from the body of a single sentient being as many bodies as there are sentient beings, so that all sentient beings may fully know and see them.
Because they seek omniscience without regressing—this is the tenth. If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they will attain all the unsurpassed dharma-ornaments of a Tathāgata, O Son of the Buddha.

What are the ten kinds of immovable minds that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas generate? They are as follows: being immovable in their ability to relinquish all possessions whatsoever; [The text continues with the remaining nine items: ...being immovable in their resolve for the Mahāyāna; being immovable in their cultivation of the roots of goodness; being immovable in their practice of the perfections; being immovable in their mastery of the stages; being immovable in their skillful means; being immovable in their wisdom; being immovable in their liberation; being immovable in their great compassion; and being immovable in their attainment of the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of a Tathāgata. These are the ten kinds of immovable minds. If bodhisattvas abide in these ten kinds of immovable minds, they will swiftly attain the unexcelled, perfect enlightenment of a Tathāgata. Thus it was said.
The immovable mind that contemplates and observes all Buddha-dharmas; the immovable mind that recollects and makes offerings to all Buddhas;
the immovable mind that vows never to harm any sentient being; the immovable mind that universally gathers in all beings without discriminating between enemies and kin;
the immovable mind that seeks all Buddha-dharmas without rest; [the immovable mind] toward all things.
For as many eons as there are sentient beings—unspeakably, unspeakably many—they practice the bodhisattva conduct without ever becoming weary or disheartened, nor do they ever regress.

They achieve an unshakable mind, a rooted faith, an untainted faith, a pure faith, an utterly pure faith, a stainless faith, a lucid faith, a faith that reverently makes offerings to all Buddhas, a non-regressive faith, and an... [faith].
The unshakeable mind that can fully trust and cannot be destroyed by anything; the unshakeable mind of great joy and exultation;

the unshakeable mind that accomplishes and gives birth to the path of skillful means for all-knowledge; the unshakeable mind that hears all the dharmas of the bodhisattva practices and accepts them with faith without slandering them—these are the ten.
If bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they shall attain the unsurpassed all-...
O sons of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas whose minds are immovable through wisdom have ten kinds of profound and great resolve that they do not forsake.
What are these ten? They are: the profound and great resolve to bring all the bodhi of the Buddhas to full completion;
the profound and great resolve to teach, transform, and subdue all sentient beings; and the profound and great resolve to never sever the lineage of all Buddhas.
The profound and great mind that does not abandon approaching all spiritual friends; the profound and great mind that does not abandon making offerings to all Buddhas;
the profound and great mind that does not abandon single-mindedly seeking all Mahāyāna meritorious dharmas;
the profound and great mind that does not abandon practicing the Brahma-faring and upholding pure precepts in the presence of all Buddhas; the profound and great mind that does not abandon.
The great and profound mind that draws near to all bodhisattvas without abandoning the seeking of all Buddha-dharmas;
the great and profound mind that protects and sustains through skillful means without abandoning the fulfillment of all bodhisattva practices and vows;
and the great and profound mind that gathers all the Buddha-dharmas—these are the ten. If bodhisattvas abide in these, they will be able to never abandon any of the Buddha-dharmas.
O Sons of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas possess ten kinds of wisdom-observation. What are these ten? They are:
the wisdom-observation that skillfully analyzes and explains all dharmas; the wisdom-observation that fully knows all roots of goodness throughout the three periods of time;
and the wisdom-observation that fully knows the sovereign transformations of all bodhisattva practices. The wisdom-observation... [and so forth].
The wisdom-observation that thoroughly understands the meanings and gateways of all phenomena; the wisdom-observation that thoroughly understands the majestic power of all Buddhas;
the wisdom-observation that thoroughly understands all dharani-gateways; the wisdom-observation that universally proclaims the True Dharma in all worlds;
the wisdom-observation that enters into all dharma-realms; and the wisdom-observation that knows the one.
To observe all the inconceivable wisdoms of the ten directions, to know all Buddha-dharmas through the light of wisdom, and to observe with unobstructed wisdom—these constitute the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they will attain the Tathāgata’s supreme great wisdom of observation. O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds [of such wisdom].
What are the ten ways of teaching the Dharma? They are: teaching that all phenomena arise from conditions;
teaching that all phenomena are entirely like illusions; teaching that all phenomena are free from conflict; teaching that all phenomena have no boundaries;
teaching that all phenomena have no basis of dependence; teaching that all phenomena are like vajras; and teaching that all phenomena...
They all speak of all phenomena as being suchness; they speak of all phenomena as being utterly tranquil;
they speak of all phenomena as being transcendence; they speak of all phenomena as abiding in a single meaning, perfected by their own nature.
These are the ten. If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they will be skillful in speaking of all phenomena. O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten [qualities].
What are the ten kinds of purity? They are: purity of the profound resolve; purity of severing doubt; purity of being free from views;
purity of the objective realm; purity of seeking all-knowledge; purity of eloquence; purity of fearlessness; purity of abiding in the wisdom of all bodhisattvas;
purity of receiving the vows of all bodhisattvas; and the perfection and accomplishment [of these].
The thirty-two marks of supreme enlightenment, the hundredfold auspicious signs, and the purity of all roots of goodness of the white and pure dharmas—these constitute the ten.
If Bodhisattvas abide therein, they shall attain all the unsurpassed, pure dharmas of the Tathāgatas.
O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas have ten kinds of seals. What are the ten? They are as follows: namely, bodhi...

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, knowing the suffering of suffering, the suffering of change, and the suffering of conditioned formations, single-mindedly seeks the Buddha-dharma without giving rise to indolence.
He practices the bodhisattva path without weariness or fatigue; he is not startled, not afraid, not terrified, and not frightened.
Without abandoning his great vow, he seeks all-knowledge (sarvajñā), remaining firm and non-retrogressive until he reaches ultimate *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. This is [the mark].
When the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Prathamamudrā sees sentient beings who are deluded and deranged, or who mutually insult and humiliate one another with coarse and wicked speech,
or who inflict harm with swords, staves, tiles, or stones, he never abandons the bodhicitta because of such circumstances;
rather, through patience and gentleness, he exclusively cultivates the Buddha-dharma, abides in the most supreme path, and enters [into it].

The state of being free from birth is the second seal. When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas hear the profound Buddha-dharma associated with omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), they are able, through their own wisdom, to deeply believe, accept, understand, and enter into it;
this is the third seal. Furthermore, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas form this thought: "I have resolved my deep mind to seek omniscience."

"When I attain Buddhahood and achieve Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, I shall also cause all sentient beings wandering through the five destinies and undergoing immeasurable suffering to likewise give rise to the bodhicitta, to have deep faith and joy, and to cultivate diligence with firm resolve without retreating.
This is the fourth seal. Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas know that the Tathāgata’s wisdom is thus.

The Tathāgata’s wisdom has no limit and cannot be measured by any boundary; because Bodhisattvas have heard of the Tathāgata’s wisdom as being limitless from the presence of immeasurable Buddhas, they are able not to measure it by boundaries.
All that is spoken through the words of the world has limits, yet none can fully know the Tathāgata’s wisdom. This is the fifth seal.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva, regarding unexcelled perfect enlightenment, attains the most excellent aspiration, the profound aspiration,
the vast aspiration, the great aspiration, the manifold aspiration, the unsurpassed aspiration, the unassailable aspiration, the firm aspiration—
an aspiration that cannot be destroyed by any māras, non-Buddhists, or their retinues— and the aspiration to seek omniscience without ever regressing.
When a bodhisattva dwells in such aspirations and never regresses from supreme enlightenment, this is the sixth seal.
Because the bodhisattva mahāsattva practices the bodhisattva path without regard for body or life, cannot be thwarted or destroyed, has resolved to advance toward all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*),
and because the nature of all-knowledge is ever-present before them, they attain the light of the wisdom of all Buddhas.
Therefore, they never abandon the Buddha’s bodhi and never abandon spiritual friends; this is the seventh seal.

When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas see sons or daughters of good family who are intent upon the Great Vehicle, they cause them to increase their aspiration for the Buddha-dharma, cause them to dwell securely in all roots of goodness, and cause them to embrace all-knowledge.
To cause the mind not to regress from unsurpassed bodhi is the eighth seal.
It is that which causes all sentient beings to attain a mind of equanimity, encourages them to diligently cultivate the path to omniscience,
and, through great compassion, preaches the Dharma for them so that they never again regress from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

To have the same roots of goodness as the Buddhas of the three periods of time and to ensure that the lineage of all Buddhas is never severed, thereby ultimately attaining the knowledge of all modes (sarvajñajñāna)—this is the ninth seal.
Son of the Buddha, this is the tenth seal. By means of these ten seals, a bodhisattva mahāsattva swiftly accomplishes unexcelled [enlightenment].
O Son of the Buddha, Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who are fully endowed with the Tathāgata’s seal of supreme wisdom regarding all dharmas possess ten kinds of light of knowledge.
What are these ten? They are: the light of knowledge that knows they shall certainly attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
the light of knowledge that perceives all Buddhas; and the light of knowledge that perceives... [and so forth].
The light of wisdom that knows all sentient beings as they die here and are born there; the light of wisdom that illuminates and understands all *sūtra* dharma-gates;
the light of wisdom that relies upon spiritual friends to resolve upon bodhicitta and accumulate all roots of goodness; the light of wisdom that manifests the appearance of all Buddhas;
and the light of wisdom that teaches and transforms all sentient beings, causing them all to dwell securely in the stage of the Tathāgata.
The light of wisdom that illuminates and expounds the inconceivable and vast Dharma-gates;

the light of wisdom that illuminates the skillful knowledge of the supernatural powers and majestic might of all Buddhas; the light of wisdom that illuminates the fulfillment of all perfections (*pāramitās*).
These are the ten. If Bodhisattvas abide in these dharmas, they shall attain the unsurpassed [state] of all Buddhas.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas who are sons of the Buddha, illuminated by the light of wisdom, have ten kinds of peerless abodes in which all sentient beings, śrāvakas, and pratyekabuddhas are entirely without equal. What are these ten? They are as follows:

although the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas contemplate the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), they do not realize it because their various vows have not yet been fully accomplished. This is the first peerless [abode].
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva who abides equally in all roots of goodness that are equal to the dharma-realm, yet has no slight attachment therein—
this is the second "Abiding in the Peerless" (asama-sthiti) bodhisattva-mahāsattva practicing the bodhisattva path.
Knowing all phenomena to be like illusions and because all phenomena are utterly quiescent, such a one gives rise to no doubt or confusion regarding the Buddha-dharma.
For the third peerless abiding, although a bodhisattva mahāsattva is free from all worldly conceptualizations,
they are able to apply their attention to practicing the bodhisattva path for unspeakable eons, fulfilling their great vows without ever giving rise to a mind of weariness or fatigue;
this is the fourth peerless abiding of a bodhisattva mahāsattva regarding all phenomena.
Because the nature of all dharmas is quiescent, they do not grasp at anything and yet do not realize nirvana.
Why is this? Because the path of omniscience has not yet been fully perfected. This is the fifth peerless dwelling.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva knows that all eons are themselves non-eons, yet he truly speaks of the enumeration of all eons; this is the sixth.
The seventh stage of the Peerless Abiding Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is knowing that all phenomena are entirely without activity,

yet not abandoning the practice of the path while seeking all Buddha-dharmas. The eighth stage of the Peerless Abiding Bodhisattva is knowing that the three realms are mind-only and the three periods of time are mind-only, and thereby realizing that this mind is immeasurable and boundless.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva in the ninth stage, the Stage of Equality (samatā-vihāra), for the sake of even a single sentient being, practices the bodhisattva conduct for unspeakable eons, desiring to establish them on the ground of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-bhūmi*);

and as he does for one sentient being, so he does for all sentient beings, yet he never gives rise to weariness or fatigue. This is the ninth stage of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, the Stage of Equality. Although...
How is it that their practice is perfected yet they do not realize bodhi? It is because the Bodhisattva forms this thought:

"My undertaking was originally for the sake of sentient beings; therefore, I should remain long in saṃsāra, employing skillful means to benefit them and cause them all to dwell securely in the unsurpassed Buddha-way.
This is the tenth Peerless Abode (*asama-vihāra*). O Son of the Buddha, this is the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s...
The Ten Peerless Abodes of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva: if bodhisattvas abide therein, they attain the peerless abode of supreme great wisdom and all Buddha-dharmas.

The Sūtra translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a Śramaṇa from Khotan during the Tang Dynasty;
