Within it dwells a wheel-turning king, his body exceedingly subtle and wondrous, adorned with the thirty-two marks and the secondary signs.
Born by transformation within a lotus, his body is of golden hue and radiant light.
Rising into the air, he illuminated near and far, pervading the entire Jambudvīpa. That king had a thousand sons, valiant and handsome in form;
his ministers numbered one hundred million, and his consorts ten billion, possessing wisdom and skillful means, with countenances like celestial maidens and minds that were beneficial and gentle.
With a heart of loving-kindness, he served the king; that king transformed the world through the Dharma.
His influence spread throughout the four continents and within the iron mountain ranges of the great earth, so that all things became abundant and prosperous.
At that time, I was a precious woman endowed with the Brahma-voice, my body emitting golden light that illuminated a thousand yojanas.
The sunlight having already set, all music fell silent; the Great King and his attendants all lay down in peaceful sleep.
At that time, the Buddha Sāgaradatta appeared in the world, manifesting the power of his supernatural faculties, filling the realms of the ten directions and emitting a great ocean of light.
Bodies of various sovereign powers, as numerous as the atoms in all lands, pervade the ten directions.
From the earth, a wondrous sound issues forth, universally proclaiming that a Buddha has appeared in the world. The hosts of devas, humans, nāgas, and spirits are all filled with joy.
From within each and every pore, oceans of the Buddha’s transformation bodies emerge.
Pervading all ten directions, he taught the sublime Dharma according to the needs of beings.
At that time, within my dream, I beheld the Buddha’s various miraculous transformations and also heard the profound and wondrous Dharma; my heart was filled with great joy.
Ten thousand night goddesses together dwelt in the air, praising the appearance of the Buddha in the world.
Simultaneously awakening me, O wise one, you should arise! A Buddha has appeared in your land, difficult to encounter even in an ocean of kalpas;
those who behold him attain purity. At that time, I was asleep, yet upon waking I beheld a pure light.
Observing from where it came, I saw the Buddha beneath the King of Trees.
The body adorned with all marks is like the king of jewel mountains;
from every pore it emits a great ocean of light. Having seen this, my heart rejoiced, and I immediately gave rise to this thought:
"May I attain such great supernormal powers as the Buddha. At that moment, I attained awakening.
The Great King, together with his retinue, was made to behold the Buddha’s radiance; all were filled with joy and celebration.

At that time, I, along with the Great King and a following of thousands of millions, as well as immeasurable sentient beings, proceeded together to the place where the Buddha was. For twenty thousand years, I made offerings to that Tathāgata.
The seven treasures and the four continents— I offer all of these as gifts.
At that time, that Tathāgata preached the *Sūtra of the Universal Cloud of Merit*, universally responding to the minds of all sentient beings.
The night goddess Adorned with the Ocean of Vows awakened me, causing me to obtain benefit; I vow to manifest such a body.
Awakening all those who are heedless, I have from this first moment Aroused the supreme vow for bodhi;
throughout my comings and goings within the various realms of existence, My mind shall never forget it.
From this point forward, I shall make offerings to ten billion nayutas of Buddhas, Constantly enjoying the bliss of gods and humans, And bringing benefit to all living beings.
The first was Buddha Guṇasāgara; the second, Guṇapradīpa; the third, Ratnaketu;
the fourth, Gaganajñāna; the fifth, Padmagarbha; the sixth, Asaṅgaprajña; the seventh, Dharmendrarāja; the eighth, Jñānapradīpacakra; and the ninth, Dvipadottama.
The Lamp-King of Jewel-Flame Mountain, The Tenth Teacher and Subduer;
The Flower-Light Sound of the Three Times— To all such Buddhas as these, I have made offerings in their entirety.
Yet I had not yet attained the eye of wisdom to enter the ocean of liberation. Following this in succession, there was the realm of Universal Jewel Light.
That kalpa was named Devavijaya, during which five hundred buddhas appeared in the world.
The first was Candramaṇḍala, the second Sūryapradīpa, the third Prabhāketu, the fourth Ratnasumeru,
the fifth Puṣpajvāla, the sixth named Dīpasamudra, and the seventh was the Buddha Jvalita.
The eighth was the Buddha Devasamudragarbha; The ninth, Prabhāsarājadhvaja;
The tenth, Samantaprajñāprabharāja— To all such Buddhas as these, I have made offerings in their entirety.
Yet, regarding all phenomena, I still reckoned what does not exist to be existent. After this, there was again an eon Named Brahmāprabhāsa.
In the world-realm Lotus Lamp, Adorned with supreme and exquisite splendor, There dwell immeasurable Buddhas, each with an immeasurable assembly;
I have made offerings to them all, Reverently hearing the Dharma.
First was the Buddha Jewel Sumeru, Second was the Buddha Ocean of Merit, Third was the Buddha Sound of the Dharma Realm.
The fourth was the Buddha Vajra-thunder; the fifth was named Dharma-dhvaja; the sixth was named Pṛthivī-prabha;
the seventh was named Dharma-bala-prabha; the eighth was named Gaganabuddhi;
the ninth was Sumeru-prabha; and the tenth was Guṇamegha. To all such Tathāgatas as these, I have made offerings in the past.
Unable to clearly understand the Dharma, I entered the ocean of all Buddhas.
Subsequently, there was an eon named Guṇacandra; at that time, there was a world named Guṇadhvaja.
Within it were eighty nayutas of Buddhas, all of whom I honored with exquisite offerings.
With a profound mind, I pay respectful homage to: First, the Gandharva King; Second, named Mahādruma-rāja;
Third, Guṇasumeru; Fourth, Ratnanetra Buddha; Fifth, Rocana; Sixth, Prabhālaṃkṛta; Seventh, Dharmasāgara Buddha; Eighth, Prabhājaya Buddha.
The ninth was named Bhadraśrī Buddha, and the tenth was Dharmarāja Buddha.
I have made offerings to all such Buddhas as these, yet I did not attain profound wisdom or enter the ocean of the Buddhas.
After this, there was another eon called Śāntamati, and the world-system was named Vajraratna.
The adornments are all exquisite and sublime; within them, a thousand Buddhas appear in succession.
Sentient beings have few afflictions, and the entire assembly is completely pure.
The first is Buddha Vajranābhi, the second is Buddha Anāvaraṇabala; the third is named Dharmadhātupratibimba, and the fourth is titled Daśabalapradīpa.
The fifth was named Compassionate Light; the sixth, Ocean of Precepts; the seventh, Lamp-Wheel of Forbearance;
the eighth, Wheel-Dharma Light; the ninth, Adorned with Light; and the tenth, Tranquil Light.
To all such Buddhas as these, I have made offerings in their entirety, yet I have still not attained profound awakening.
Like the pure dharma of space, he travels through all lands. Therein he cultivates the sequence of all practices;

furthermore, there was an eon named "Excellent Manifestation. The land was called "Clouds of Fragrant Lamps," composed of both purity and impurity, wherein billions of Buddhas appeared, adorning both the land and the eon.
The various teachings that were spoken, I am able to remember and uphold them all: The first was named Buddha Universal Renown;
the next was named Buddha Ocean of Dharma; The third was named Sovereign King; the fourth was named Cloud of Merit;
The fifth was Buddha Supreme Dharma; the sixth was Buddha Celestial Crown; The seventh was Buddha Flame of Wisdom.
The eighth was Ākāśapratisthita; the ninth was Dvipadottama; the tenth was named Viśvajanin Viśeṣa, the Unsurpassed One (Anuttara).
With the supreme light between his brows—having made offerings to all such Buddhas as these—I have still not been able to purify the path that is free from all obstacles.
Next there was another eon named Saṃcita-dṛḍharāja. The world-system was called Sarvakuśalavibhakta-ratnadhvajarāja, wherein five hundred Buddhas appeared.
I paid them homage and made offerings to them, seeking unimpeded liberation; this was the first wheel of merit.
The next was Śāntasvara; the next was named Guṇasāgara; the next was named Sūryaprabharāja;
the fifth was Guṇarāja; the sixth was Merudhvaja; the next was named Dharmeśvara;
the next was Buddha-guṇarāja; the ninth was Puṇyameru; and the tenth was Prabhāsarāja.
All such Buddhas as these, I have previously made offerings to all; The entire pure path enters universally into purity without remainder.
Yet regarding the gateways entered, I had not yet achieved the stages of patience (*kṣānti*).
Subsequently, there was another eon named *Suvikrāntādhipati* (Excellent Sovereign); The world-system was called *Śāntanirghoṣa* (Sound of Tranquility).
When the afflictions of sentient beings were thin, a Buddha appeared therein;
I have made offerings to all eighty nayutas of them as they practiced the most supreme path. The first Buddha was named Flower Cluster;
the next was named Ocean Treasury; The next was named Arising of Merit; the next was titled Heavenly King Topknot.
The fifth was Maṇigarbha; the sixth, Suvarṇaparvata; the seventh, Ratnarāśi;
the eighth, Dharmadhvaja Buddha; the ninth was named Jayasena; and the tenth was named Prajñā.
These ten were the leaders, making offerings to them all without exception. Following this, there was another eon.
Named Thousand Merits, there was at that time a world Called Banner-Lamp of Skillful Transformation;
sixty billion nayutas Of Buddhas arose in that world. The first was Śāntadhvaja, the second was Śamatha, The third was Śatadīparāja, and the fourth was Śāntaprabha.
The fifth was Meghasamghāta, the sixth Sūryaprabha; the seventh was named Dharmapradīpa, the eighth Viśiṣṭārci;
the ninth was named Devajaya-garbha, and the tenth Mahānādaniḥsvana—these and all other such Buddhas I have constantly made offerings to, yet I had not yet attained pure patience (*kṣānti*).
Deeply entering the ocean of all dharmas, there followed in succession another eon named Unattached Adornment.
At that time, there was a world named Boundless Light, wherein thirty-six nayutas of Buddhas appeared: the first was Guṇameru, and the second was Ākāśacitta.
The third was Adorned with All Ornaments; the fourth, Sound of the Dharma Thunder;
the fifth, Voice of the Dharma Realm; the sixth, Cloud of Wondrous Sounds; the seventh, Illumining the Ten Directions;
the eighth, Sound of the Ocean of Dharma; the ninth, Ocean of Merit; and the tenth, Banner of Merit. Such were these Buddhas.
I have made offerings to them all; subsequently, there appeared a Buddha named Guṇadhvaja.
At that time, I was the goddess Candrānanā, and I made offerings to that Lord of Men. Then the Buddha taught me the wondrous Dharma-gate of Non-reliance;
having heard it, I focused my mind upon it and maintained it, thereby giving birth to an ocean of various vows.
I have attained the pure eye, the samādhi of quiescence, and the dhāraṇī; In every thought-moment, I am able to see the oceans of all Buddhas.
I have attained the treasury of great compassion, the universally luminous eye of skillful means, and the increase of the bodhicitta;
Having accomplished the powers of the Tathāgata, I behold the delusions of sentient beings.
Grasping at permanence, bliss, self, and purity, shrouded by the darkness of ignorance,
they give rise to delusions, afflictions, and the proliferation of views; wandering through the ocean of craving,
they accumulate immeasurable and diverse karmas within the various evil realms, receiving bodies according to their karma throughout all states of existence.
Afflicted by the myriad sufferings of birth, old age, and death, And oppressed by immeasurable pain—for the sake of those sentient beings, I have resolved upon the Unsurpassed Mind.

Vowing to become like the Honored Ones of Ten Powers throughout the ten directions, I take the Buddhas and all beings as my object, Raising a great cloud of vows; from this point on, I shall cultivate merit.
Entering the path of skillful means, may the clouds of aspiration completely pervade all;
universally entering all bodhisattva practices, fulfilling the *pāramitās*, and filling the entire dharma-realm;
swiftly entering the oceans of skillful means across the three times and all the stages (*bhūmis*); in a single thought-moment, cultivating the Buddhas and all unimpeded conduct.
"O Son of the Buddha, at that time, I attained entry into the path of Samantabhadra and fully understood all the various gateways of the ten dharma-realms.
Good son, what do you think? Was he not the Universal Monarch named Daśadigpati (Lord of the Ten Directions) who was able to succeed [to the throne]?"
"Is the one who causes the lineage of the Buddhas to flourish anyone other than this youth Mañjuśrī?
That night goddess who awakened me at that time was but an emanation of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
At that time, as the queen-consort of King Ratna, I was awakened by that night goddess, who caused me to see the Buddha and resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
From that time forth, for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, this bodhicitta has never caused me to fall into the evil destinies;

I have always been born among humans and devas, and in every place I have constantly seen all the Buddhas, until I attained this liberation of the Bodhisattva Universal Joy Banner of Great Power from the Buddha Lamp of Wondrous Virtue Banner. By means of this liberation, I have benefited beings in this way.
"O sons of good family, all you sentient beings, I have attained only this liberation door of the Universal Joy Banner of Great Power.
As for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, in every thought-moment they go before all Tathāgatas and are able to swiftly enter the ocean of omniscience;
in every thought-moment, through the gate of setting forth, they enter into all..."
Within every thought-moment, through the gateway of the ocean of vows, he brings forth all practices throughout all future eons;
from each and every practice, he produces bodies as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-lands; with each body, he universally enters the gateways of all dharma-realms;
and within each gateway of the dharma-realms, in every buddha-field, he acts in accordance with the minds of sentient beings.
He speaks of all sublime practices; within every single atom of all lands, he perceives the infinite oceans of Tathāgatas;
at the site of each and every Tathāgata, he perceives the spiritual powers of the Buddhas pervading the entire Dharma-realm;

at the site of each and every Tathāgata, he perceives the cultivation of bodhisattva practices throughout past kalpas; and at the site of each and every Tathāgata, he receives and protects all the wheels of Dharma.
Just as a Tathāgata perceives the entire ocean of spiritual transformations of all Tathāgatas throughout the three periods of time, how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
Good son, within this assembly there is a night goddess named Samantabhadra-sattvatrāṇa-guṇaviśuddhā;
go to her and ask: "How does a bodhisattva enter the bodhisattva practice and purify the bodhisattva path?"

When he was on the path to the realization of the Bodhisattva way, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed upon him with deep reverence, took his leave, and departed.
[Treatise] From the passage beginning "At that time, the youth Sudhana" onwards, within the first section on the Dharma-gate of entering the specific stage (*dharmaparyāya*), it is as follows:
I have attained only this liberation door of the Universal Joy Banner; within this palace, it is divided into five sections:
first, reflecting on the instructions of the spiritual friend to advance further; second, Sudhana’s desire to go to the night goddess Priyadarśanā-sattva-avalokanī;
third, the night goddess’s empowerment through her supernormal power, which enables Sudhana to know how to draw near to the virtuous friend.

Knowledge brings great benefit; having received the empowerment of the four [goddesses], Sudhana quickly gave rise to this thought, knowing for himself that by associating with spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), he would be able to courageously and diligently cultivate the path to omniscience.

Fifth, Sudhana went to the presence of the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā and observed the sphere of her activity in gathering and transforming sentient beings for their benefit. From here—
The section concerning the Night Goddess whom he beheld, seated upon a lion throne within the Lotus Treasury in the assembly of the Tathāgata’s *bodhimaṇḍa*, is divided below into twelve parts:
first, at that time, after the youth Sudhana had formed this thought, [he proceeded] until "causing all to rejoice and obtain benefit";
this consists of five lines and a half of scripture clarifying his initial observation.
The section on the sphere of conversion through the guidance of the Night Goddess Priyadarśanā is divided into two parts.

Specifically, from the passage "having emitted clouds of immeasurable emanation bodies that fill all worlds throughout the ten directions" down to "thus proclaiming the various methods of practice for all Bodhisattvas for the sake of benefiting them," there are eighty-three lines of scripture that clarify the ten *pāramitās*.
The section on the *Pāramitā* of gathering and transforming sentient beings is divided into three parts. Furthermore, from the passage beginning with "From each and every pore,

there emerge immeasurable clouds of various bodies of sentient beings" down to "the clouds of similar bodies of the presiding deities of the directions (*dig-devatā*) pervading the ten directions and filling the *dharmadhātu*," seventeen and a half lines of scripture clarify the pores of the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā.

The section on manifesting emanations throughout the ten directions to gather sentient beings through their own kind is divided into four parts. From the passage beginning "In the presence of all those sentient beings,
he manifests various sounds" down to the eight lines of scripture concerning the merit accumulated from the first generation of the mind of enlightenment,
it clarifies the manifestation of the goddess Priyadarsana pervading the ten directions with her voice and describes Priyadarsana’s initial generation of the mind of enlightenment.
The merit of all that has come forth— approaching all Buddhas and the ocean of *pāramitās* they practice— is divided into five parts.

Specifically, from "having served all spiritual friends" down to "causing immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the stage of the Tathāgata," forty-six lines and a half of scripture clarify the joy described by the previously manifested sounds.
The section on the realm of the deity’s practice, offerings, and the Buddha’s transformation of sentient beings consists of six parts.

At that time, after the youth Sudhana had seen and heard all the aforementioned marvelous events, he proceeded to cultivate the practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; thus, for eight and a half lines of scripture, it describes Sudhana’s vision.

As described above, having attained entry into the sphere of instruction, this concludes the seventh section of the liberation gate called "The Sovereign Power of the Universal Joy Banner of Inconceivable Great Might," which is the dharma practiced by the Night Goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, as indicated by one and a half lines of scripture below, spoke verses to praise the merit of the goddess Pramuditanayanā.
Within the "Section on Virtue" (*Guṇavibhāga*) consisting of eight verses, there are ten lines of verse that clearly express the intent of the verses by praising the virtue of the Night Goddess.
Section Nine: At that time, the youth Sudhana... (the following three lines of scripture clarify how Sudhana asks the Night Goddess about the duration since she attained liberation).
Section Ten: "I recall the past... (from here until "...his mind does not forget").
The section on the loss [of the lifespan] consists of twenty-six verses clarifying the Night Goddess’s response regarding the duration of the eon in which Sudhana dwells;

this is divided into eleven parts. Following this, from "Having made offerings to ten billion nayutas of Buddhas" down to "thoroughly knowing that all ten dharma-realms are without differentiation," there are sixty-five verses answering Sudhana’s inquiry regarding the offerings made during his residence in the eon.
Regarding the number of Buddhas—whether long or short, many or few—in this section on making offerings, there are eleven segments.
Each segment contains ten Buddha names; thus, the Buddha names across all eleven segments correspond to the eleven stages (*bhūmi*).
As one advances through the positions, each stage is assigned ten Buddha names, such that the ten stages are assigned one hundred Buddha names, and the eleventh [stage] is assigned eleven.

The stages (*bhūmi*) correspond to the names of the Buddhas; this is clarified because the subsequent [stage] subsumes the many preceding ones, and it is clarified that a single stage possesses the practices of all ten stages, as they are formed through the mutual interpenetration of the ten *pāramitās*.

Regarding the first [stage], it is initially clarified that "from here, one makes offerings to ten *nayuta* of Buddhas," which corresponds to the first stage, the Joyful (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), because the beginning subsumes the end, and the beginning contains [the whole].
Because it is manifold and because the vows are vast, the first stage (*bhūmi*) clarifies the superior resolve of generating the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*).
"Manifold" at the very beginning signifies its general characteristic (*sāmānya-lakṣaṇa*). This first stage is the first stage within the third stage;
likewise, up to the tenth stage is the tenth stage within the third stage. Thus, "the ocean of the Buddha's qualities at the beginning" refers to the first stage within the third stage.
The gate of the *dānapāramitā* is the primary element, while the other nine serve as its companions;
since this stage constitutes the third bhūmi, the ten *pāramitās* of the preceding and succeeding stages are all subsumed within this stage.

Other stages are likewise to be understood according to this pattern of mutual inclusion, like a net of Indra (*indrājāla*), where one enters many. Thus, this clarifies that the essence of patience (*kṣānti*) universally subsumes both cause and fruit.
In each stage of the five stages, it is likewise so. In the second [stage], the realm is named *Sarvaratnaprabhā* (All-Jewel-Light), and its eon is named *Devajaya* (Victory of the Gods).
Because the perfection of morality (*śīla-pāramitā*) constitutes the essence of the second stage, the "God" (*deva*) signifies mastery over pure morality.
This mastery over pure morality is superior to the afflictions (*kleśa*), and is thus called "Victory of the Gods. Therefore, [the name is] fivefold.
Regarding the appearance of one hundred Buddhas in the world: the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*) is the primary factor among the five stages.
The five hundred perfections within these stages are all subsumed within the essence of pure ethical discipline; thus, they are termed the "appearance of five hundred Buddhas in the world.

If, within the very nature of one's own mental state, one perceives external Buddhas as being distinct from this stainless self-nature, such a person has not yet escaped the activities of Māra. This is the first Buddha.
The name "Moonlight Disk" (*Candramaṇḍala*) signifies the perfection of the light of ethical discipline (*śīla*).
The remaining nine Buddha names represent the primary and attendant *pāramitās* within that discipline, as well as their causes and effects, as follows: [the list of names].

Although I have made offerings to all such Buddhas, I still conceptualized non-existent phenomena as being existent because my *prajñā-pāramitā* (perfection of wisdom) had not yet become perfectly clear and luminous.
Regarding the advancement of those whose precepts are not yet matured, the clinging to rules and rituals (*śīlavrataparāmarśa*) still manifests;

however, when discussed in terms of the maturation of this advancement, one reaches the tenth stage where the perfection of wisdom (*jñānapāramitā*) is perfectly luminous. Within this, there are five hundred layers of advancement where the habits (*vāsanā*) of maturation differ.
This clarifies the distinctions within the general characteristic and the differences within the same state: once the bodhicitta has been generated, one has already received the [unconditioned]...
Regarding the measure of the bliss cultivated through the ten stages (*bhūmi*)—both in their raw and matured states—it remains until the eleventh stage is reached for them to be fully exhausted;

only upon reaching the state of Buddhahood are the two delusions (*moha*) and their habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) completely eliminated. To counteract these habitual tendencies, the various stages and levels are established as antidotes.

As for the principle of their wisdom, the distinctions between the ten stages are like the tracks of birds in the sky; yet, in terms of the specific characteristics of their shared and distinct habitual tendencies, they are not non-existent.
Third, following this, there is another eon named Brahmā-prabhāsa; this is the name of the third stage, the Radiant Ground (Prabhākari-bhūmi).
Because one cultivates the eight dhyānas on this Radiant Ground, all habitual obstacles of the three realms are thoroughly remedied:

the obstacles of sensual desire in the desire realm, and the obstacles of attachment to the bliss of dhyāna in the two higher realms. As the light of the ultimate truth (paramārtha) manifests, pure and unobstructed, the eon is thus named.
"Brahma-light" (*brahmāloka*)—the name "Brahma" signifies purity—refers to the purification of a portion of the defiled habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*) of the three realms;
thus it is called the "Pure Light World. The world is named "Lotus Lamp," which is the designation for the conduct of this stage being free from defilement.
Its adornments are exceedingly sublime; because it takes the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*) as its adornment, it is called "Exceedingly Sublime."
"Patience is the foremost of practices; those immeasurable Buddhas therein" means that because the essence of patience subsumes all practices, it is said:

"I shall make offerings to all those immeasurable Buddhas. This is because making offerings through the practice of patience—namely, honoring and respecting—is the way to make offerings to all Buddhas.
Regarding the first Buddha, Ratnasumeru: this refers to the patience of humility and respect cultivated in the third bhūmi.
Because it is preeminent within the practice, it is like Mount Sumeru in its loftiness; this Buddha acts as the sovereign while the other Buddhas act as his retinue within this patience.
Below this, each stage is sequentially assigned to the principal and attendant factors of the ten stages, the eleventh stage, the ten pāramitās, and the myriad practices.
All Buddhas rely upon the principle and wisdom within these five stages of practice.
Because one attains the fruit of Buddhahood through compassionate vows, it is impossible to see the Buddha apart from these dharmas.
That which is described as the magnitude of a kalpa in terms of the sphere and locus of wisdom has no time, days, months, or years at all; it is entirely a realm of great wisdom.
One must discuss this in terms of the true Buddha, true wisdom, and true dharma, and must not follow after the delusions of self or others.
If false views were to be eliminated, wisdom would be fulfilled and conduct perfected, encompassing all that is below the Buddha;

this constitutes the fourth stage, which is assigned to the *vīrya-pāramitā* (perfection of vigor). The "eighty *nayutas* of Buddhas" symbolizes the eightfold noble path as the essence of the practice of vigor.
As for the remaining eight types of conduct, they are not [the state of] Buddhahood. "Nayuta" represents the totality of the ten thousand practices.
In the fifth stage, the *dhyāna-pāramitā*, there is an intermediate kalpa named "Silent Sound" (*śānta-nirghoṣa*) and a world-realm (*kṣetra*) called "Vajra-Jewel.
This represents the Dharma-nature body (*dharmatā-kāya*) as the essence of meditative concentration; it signifies that both speech and silence are tranquil.

The Vajra Universal Illumination represents the indestructible nature of the essence of meditative concentration. Within this, the successive appearance of a thousand Buddhas symbolizes the essence of meditative concentration.
Subsuming the functions back into their source, within each of the ten stages (*bhūmi*) there are one hundred *pāramitās* acting as primary and secondary;
thus, within this stage of Dhyāna, the ten stages are subsumed as a thousandfold sequence. In the sixth stage, Prajñā is the primary [pāramitā].
There is an eon named "Excellent Manifestation," which symbolizes that wisdom is skillfully able to manifest all dharmas. The name of the buddha-field is "Fragrance."
The cloud of lamps symbolizes wisdom; the fragrance represents the destruction of darkness, and the lamp represents the teaching of the Dharma that universally covers all.
That billions of Buddhas appear therein signifies the application of *prajñā* (wisdom), as it is raised from the previous stage of "thousands" to this stage of "billions.
That five hundred Buddhas arise therein during the seventh stage symbolizes skillful means (*upāya*).
The *pāramitās* universally encompass the five stages; herein, supramundane wisdom is integrated with worldly activity to accomplish the practice of great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*).
Thus, five hundred Buddhas are cited as the number of practices, and the eon is named "Accumulation of Firmness" (*Saṃghāta-dṛḍha-rāja*).

One who remains untainted while dwelling amidst the entanglements is truly called a "King of Firmness. This signifies mastery (*vaśitā*), which exists in the eighth stage (*bhūmi*) in eighty *nayutas*.
"The Buddhas of other [realms]" signifies that the great function of effortlessness has already been perfected; "the eightfold right path" indicates that the practices are fully prepared.
"Ninety billion nayutas of Buddhas"—one nayuta being equivalent to a *gō* (koti)—represents the twentieth numerical position, signifying the rank of the Dharma Master.
It also signifies that the Dharma-cloud rains universally throughout the six realms of existence, such that transformation is complete. This also represents the [tenth]... [stage].

Generally speaking, because the rain of Dharma falls universally throughout the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) to bring them to fulfillment, the presence of thirty-six *nayuta* Buddhas within these ten stages signifies the perfection of wisdom;
it indicates that the three periods of time and the six positions are simultaneously illuminated, as cause and effect are thoroughly penetrated.

This is because through the increasing clarity of wisdom, the three periods of time and the six positions are seen to be without beginning or end, being a single, perfect wisdom. Thus, there is the eleventh stage.
"One Buddha" signifies the gathering of the three periods of time and the six positions into a single dharma-realm as a great, unimpeded function;

thus, it gathers the particular into the fundamental, relying on fundamental wisdom (*mūla-jñāna*). Because the fruit of Buddhahood is perfected as the gate of Samantabhadra, the one and the many penetrate each other.
As seen by carefully examining the words and meanings of the sutra, this intent is inherent within them; it is not a matter of human sentiment imposing it upon them.

In the twelfth section, from "Good son" onwards, up to "I only know this liberation door of the Banner of Universal Joy of Great Power," there are nine lines and a half of scripture that clearly provide a general conclusion.

Above this, the section on the beginning and end of the arousal of the mind, its causes and effects, and the duration of the kalpas, concludes within this segment; therein, that universal monarch was named Ten.
As for the one who presides over the quarters and is capable of perpetuating and exalting the lineage of the Buddhas—could this be anyone else? It was Mañjuśrī.
That night goddess who awakened me at that time was an emanation of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
As for the king’s precious daughter who was transformed by that night goddess, she is none other than this night goddess Priyanetra; she represents the Dharma and is the basis of the faculties.
The principle of the *dharmakāya* of fundamental wisdom gives rise to the activity of discriminative wisdom and great compassion that is not limited by time or eons;

even if one were to use the number of atoms in a buddha-field as a metaphor for such durations, through practicing for an amount of eons equal to these, one attains this liberation of the "Great Power Universal Joy Banner.
This clarifies the cultivation of the specific remedies for the three realms in the third stage.
Because he has attained mastery over the four dhyānas and eight samādhis, he dwells in the world practicing compassion and patience until one portion [of his vow] is completed;
because he always rejoices in all sentient beings, whether good or evil, and never grows weary of them,

he uses this practice throughout kalpas to answer the previous question of Sudhana regarding the duration since he first resolved his mind, thereby clarifying that the nature of patience is all-pervasive and omnipresent.

At that time, he answered in general: "Furthermore, because wisdom has no before or after, the Sūtra says that 'all requisites for the dhyāna-pāramitā' refers to generosity, morality, patience, diligence, the four foundations of mindfulness, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and so forth;
these are the requisites for the family of dhyāna. Moreover, the five methods of settling the mind (*pañca-vastuka*), the eighteen things, and secluded, tranquil places are also dhyāna."
The requisites for this dhyāna are also the correct teachings of the Master’s sequential Dharma-knowledge;

the requisites for this dhyāna are also the ten pāramitās, the four means of integration (saṃgrahavastu), and the four immeasurables (apramāṇa), which serve as aids to manifest the sovereign functioning of the essence of the Dharma-realm (dharmadhātu).
This is the third stage, the Radiant (Prabhākārī), where the spiritual friend [is characterized by] the perfection of patience (kṣānti-pāramitā).

With honey as the primary element and the other nine as its companions, it treats the two obstacles—defilement and purity—of those dwelling in the meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) within the three realms, causing them to practice great compassion so that they may become unimpeded.
Thus, when a portion of both the defiled and purified habitual tendencies becomes thin and subtle, one begins with a portion of sentient beings who are neither virtuous nor evil;
by no longer giving rise to aversion or indifference toward them, one attains great power and the liberation of the Universal Joy Banner (*Samantamukha-prīti-dhvaja*).
In the five ranks and ten stages preceding this gate, what is expressed through verbal discourse may not be fully comprehended;
yet upon reaching this stage, Sudhana seeks spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) by means of their names, locations, genders, titles— such as elders, bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs,
upāsakas, upāsikās, bodhisattvas, and night goddesses— as well as their names, modes of conduct, characteristics, and the phenomena upon which they rely.

Furthermore, these matters are presented so as to facilitate easy understanding. Second, within the section titled "The Gate of Inferring Virtue and Advancement," from the passage beginning with "Just as the various Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas" down to "took their leave and departed," there are fourteen lines of scripture which are divided approximately into five gates:
first, inferring virtue and advancement; second, indicating the location of spiritual friends; third, citing excellence... [text continues].
The name of the Knowledge-holder is Rātri-devī (Night Goddess), whose name is Samantabhadra-sattva-trāṇa-guṇa-vyūhā (Universal Protector of Beings with Wondrous Virtue).
She exhorts Sudhana four times to go visit her. Fifth, regarding the ritual of paying respects and departing, as for the interpretation of the meaning according to the text:
among those in this assembly, there is a night goddess who clarifies that Bodhi and wisdom-compassion are perfected; the name of this night goddess in this assembly is as previously described.

This explains the fourth stage among the ten stages, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom (*Arciṣmatī-bhūmi*), which is the position of being born into the family of all Buddhas, the station of abiding in enlightenment, and the gateway of the growth of great compassion.

It concerns the night goddess named Universal Virtue Pure Radiance (*Samantaguṇaviśuddhaprabhā*), who, within the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), first met with the light of the bodhicitta; this constitutes the second [point], the generation of the mind through supreme vows.

Because the local assemblies realize the Middle Way, from this point onward until the tenth stage (*bhūmi*), they nurture the mind of great compassion until the end of the eleventh stage, which is purely the realm of Samantabhadra’s sublime practices. Of these, the first three stages involve the purification of karma within the three realms;
their completion is called the Radiant Stage (*Prabhākarī-bhūmi*). On this stage, one is born into the family of the Tathāgata.
The manifestation of pure wisdom is called the Stage of Blazing Wisdom (Arciṣmatī-bhūmi); the remainder is fully detailed in the text itself.
Within the fourth assembly, the Night Goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā presides over the Stage of Blazing Wisdom.
[Sūtra] At that time, the youth Sudhana, having heard from the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā the liberation door of the Banner of Universal Joy,
believed, understood, entered into, comprehended, followed, reflected upon, and practiced it;

he contemplated the instructions of the spiritual friend without ever abandoning them for a moment, his faculties remained undistracted, and with a single mind he vowed to behold the spiritual friend.

Diligently seeking throughout the ten directions without weariness, may I always remain close to spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), give rise to all merits, and share the same roots of goodness as them;
may I attain the skillful means of spiritual friends and enter the ocean of vigor by relying upon them, never being separated from them for immeasurable eons.
Having made this vow, he proceeded to Samantabhadra, the One of Wondrous Virtue Who Universally Saves All Beings.
At that time, the Night Goddess manifested for the youth Sudhana the power of a bodhisattva’s liberation for taming sentient beings;

her body was adorned with all the marks and signs of excellence, and from between her two eyebrows she emitted a great light called "The Banner of Universal Illumination and Pure Wisdom-Lamp," which had immeasurable rays of light as its retinue, and this light shone everywhere.
Having illuminated all worlds, [the light] entered the crown of Sudhana’s head and filled his body.
At that moment, Sudhana attained the samādhi called "The Ultimate Pure Wheel. Having attained this samādhi, he saw everything within the space between the two goddesses:
all the particles of earth, water, and fire, as well as vajras, maṇi-jewels, and various precious gems.
Within every single atom of all such adornments as fine dust, flowers, incense, and necklaces,
one perceives the formation and destruction of world-systems as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field;
one also perceives the vast accumulations of the great elements— earth, water, fire, and wind— and sees all worlds joined together, all sustained by the earth-wheel.
They dwell in various mountains and seas, various rivers and ponds, various groves of trees, and various palaces— namely,
the palaces of devas, the palaces of nāgas, the palaces of yakṣas, and even the palaces and abodes of mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth; they are born,
revolving through all dwelling places in the various realms of existence, including the hells, the animal realm, and the world of Yama.
He saw, without exception, the various distinctions of how beings pass away and return according to their karma and receive their retributions.
Furthermore, he saw the differences among all worlds: namely, some worlds were defiled, some were pure;
some worlds tended toward defilement, some tended toward purity; and some worlds were both defiled and pure.
There are worlds that are pure and mixed with defilement, or worlds that are entirely pure; there are worlds whose forms are level and upright,
or those that dwell inverted, or those that dwell sideways— in all such worlds and within all realms of existence,
one sees this Night Goddess Who Universally Saves Sentient Beings at all times and in all places, according to [the needs of] all beings.
By the power of skillful means, he appears before all sentient beings— distinguished by their physical forms, speech, conduct, and understanding—
to transform and deliver them according to their needs: causing those in the hells to escape all bitter poisons, causing those among the animals not to devour one another,
causing those among the hungry ghosts to be free from hunger and thirst, and causing the nāgas and others to be liberated from all fears within the desire realm.
May sentient beings be freed from the suffering of the desire realm; may they be freed from the fear of darkness, the fear of being reviled, the fear of ill repute,
the fear of the great assembly, the fear of lacking a livelihood, the fear of death, the fear of the evil destinies, the fear of severing the roots of goodness,

the fear of regressing from the bodhicitta, the fear of encountering evil associates, the fear of being separated from virtuous friends, and the fear of falling into the stages of the two vehicles within the various cycles of birth and death.

They cause all such fears as the fear of dwelling together with beings of different kinds, the fear of taking birth in evil times, the fear of taking birth among evil lineages, the fear of committing evil karma,
the fear of the obstacles of karma and afflictions, and the fear of being bound by attachment to various perceptions—

to abandon them entirely. Furthermore, they see all sentient beings— those born from eggs, those born from wombs, those born from moisture, and those born by transformation, as well as those with form.
They appear before all beings in the formless realm, whether possessing perception, lacking perception, or neither possessing nor lacking perception;

they constantly and diligently provide protection and rescue for the sake of fulfilling the power of the Bodhisattva’s great vows, for the sake of deeply entering the power of the Bodhisattva’s samādhis, for the sake of strengthening the power of the Bodhisattva’s supernormal knowledges,
for the sake of giving birth to the power of Samantabhadra’s practices and vows, and for the sake of expanding the ocean of the Bodhisattva’s great compassion.
Thus, they attain unimpeded great compassion that universally covers all sentient beings; they attain the ability to universally bestow immeasurable joy and bliss upon all sentient beings;
they attain the wisdom and skillful means to universally gather in all sentient beings; they attain the vast liberation, mastery, and supernormal powers of a bodhisattva;
they purify all buddha-fields; they awaken to the understanding of all phenomena; and they make offerings...
Because they nourish all Buddhas; because they uphold all Buddha-teachings; because they accumulate all roots of goodness and cultivate all sublime practices;
because they enter the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings without obstruction;
because they know the faculties of all sentient beings to teach and mature them; and because they purify the faith and understanding of all sentient beings and remove their evil obstructions.
Therefore, because she destroys the dark ignorance of all sentient beings and causes them to attain the pure radiance of omniscience,
when the youth Sudhana beheld this night goddess’s inconceivable supernatural power and profound state—
the bodhisattva liberation that universally manifests to discipline all sentient beings— he was filled with immeasurable joy and bowed his head.
As he paid homage with his face turned toward her and gazed upon her with single-minded devotion,
that night goddess cast off her bodhisattva ornaments and restored herself to her original form, yet she did not relinquish her sovereign spiritual power. At that time,
the youth Sudhana stood to one side with palms joined in reverence and praised her in verse:
I, Sudhana, having beheld such great supernormal power, my heart was filled with joy, and I spoke these verses in praise:
"I behold your venerable and wondrous body, adorned with all the marks, like stars in the sky; every part is perfectly pure, emitting most excellent light."
As numerous as the atoms in immeasurable lands, Various and subtle colors shine everywhere throughout the ten directions.
From every single pore, light is emitted, Equal in number to the thoughts of sentient beings.
At the tip of each and every ray of light, Precious lotus flowers emerge; From within these flowers, transformation bodies appear, Able to extinguish the suffering of sentient beings.
From within the light, wondrous fragrances emerge, Pervasively perfuming all sentient beings. Furthermore, various flowers rain down as offerings to all Buddhas.

Between his two eyebrows, he emits wondrous light, Equal in measure to Mount Sumeru, Universally touching all conscious beings, Causing them to extinguish the darkness of ignorance. From his mouth, he emits pure light.
Just as immeasurable suns Universally illuminate the vast expanse, The eye of Vairocana emits pure light;
Just as immeasurable moons Universally illuminate the lands of the ten directions,
Completely extinguishing the cataracts of worldly ignorance, He manifests various transformed bodies, With features equal in number to all sentient beings.
Pervading the realms of the ten directions, you deliver beings from the ocean of the three existences.
Your wondrous body manifests everywhere throughout the ten directions before all living beings, extinguishing all fears such as those of water, fire, thieves, and kings.
Having received the instruction of you, the Joyful-Eyed One, I have now come to your presence and beheld the mark between your eyebrows.
Emitting great, pure light that universally illumines the oceans of the ten directions,
It completely extinguishes all darkness and manifests supernormal powers; Entering into my body, I encounter this perfect radiance,
And with a heart of great joy, I attain dhāraṇī and samādhi, Universally manifesting the Buddhas of the ten directions.
In every place where I travel, I see all the subtle atoms; within each and every atom, I see as many lands as there are atoms.
Some are infinite lands where all beings are turbid and defiled, undergoing various sufferings, constantly lamenting and weeping in sorrow; others are lands that are both defiled and pure.
With little joy and much sorrowful suffering, they manifest the forms of the three vehicles to go there and deliver beings.
Whether in defiled or pure lands, they are what sentient beings delight to behold; Bodhisattvas constantly fill them, upholding all Buddha-dharmas.
Within each and every atom, there are infinite oceans of pure lands.
Vairocana Buddha, purified through the adornments of past eons, sits beneath the Bodhi tree in every land;
having attained enlightenment and turned the wheel of Dharma, he delivers all living beings.
I see the Universal Savior, the Deva, in those immeasurable lands, in the presence of all Buddhas.
"Go everywhere to make offerings.
At that time, after the youth Sudhana had spoken these verses, he addressed the Night Goddess Sarvasattvaparitrāṇaśrī, saying:
"O Goddess, what is the name of this liberation which is so profound and rare? How did you attain this liberation?"
"For how long has she practiced what kind of conduct to attain such purity? The night goddess replied, "Noble son, this matter is difficult to know;
it cannot be fathomed by gods, humans, or any of those belonging to the two vehicles. Why is this? Because this is the domain of those who dwell in the practice of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
it is the domain of those who abide in the treasury of great compassion; it is for the sake of protecting and rescuing all sentient beings."
It is the realm of those who are born; it is the realm of those who can purify all three evil states and eight difficult conditions;

it is the realm of those who can ensure that the lineage of the Buddhas is perpetuated and never interrupted within all Buddha-fields; it is the realm of those who can maintain and uphold all Buddha-dharmas;
and it is the realm of those who can cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva throughout all kalpas to bring the ocean of great vows to fulfillment.
Because it is the sphere of activity wherein one can extinguish the darkness of ignorance with the light of pure wisdom throughout the ocean of all dharma-realms;
because it is the sphere of activity wherein one can universally illumine the ocean of skillful means of all three periods of time with the radiance of wisdom in a single thought-moment;
because it is the sphere of activity [of such realization], I now, by the power of the Buddha, shall explain it for you, O son of good family. Long ago, in a past age...
Past as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, there was an eon named Paripūrṇaviśuddha and a world named Vairocanamahātejas.
Within it, as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru appeared;
that buddha-world had as its substance all kinds of fragrant-king maṇi-jewels, was adorned with various treasures, and rested upon the stainless ground.
Upon the ocean of the Radiant Mani King, its shape is perfectly circular; it is covered by clouds of canopies of all manner of ornaments formed from a combination of pure and impure elements.
It is encircled a thousand times by mountains of mani-jewels of every adornment. Within it are hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of four-continent worlds, all exquisitely adorned;
yet among them, there are also four-continent worlds where sentient beings exist who have performed evil karma.
Within it dwell sentient beings with mixed karma from the four continents; within it dwell sentient beings with roots of goodness from the four continents;
and within it dwell the great bodhisattvas who are exclusively pure throughout the four continents.
On the side of the Cakravāḍa Mountains at the eastern limit of this world-system, there is a set of four continents named...
In this realm of the Pure Land of Jewel-Lamp Flower Banners, food and drink are abundant and do not depend on plowing or sowing; rice and grain grow spontaneously.

The palaces and towers are all wondrous and marvelous. Rows of various wish-fulfilling trees stand everywhere, while various incense trees constantly emit clouds of fragrance, various garland trees constantly produce clouds of garlands, and various flower trees perpetually rain down exquisite blossoms.
Various jewel trees produce all manner of rare treasures and immeasurable colored lights that shine radiantly all around;
music trees produce various musical sounds that, stirred by the wind, play exquisite melodies;

the sun, moon, and light-manifesting *maṇi* jewel-kings universally illuminate everything, such that one enjoys pleasure day and night without interruption. Within these four continents, there are hundreds of billions [of such worlds].
In those *nayuta* of royal realms, each individual kingdom was surrounded by a thousand great rivers.
Each river was covered with exquisite flowers that drifted and swayed with the current, emitting the sounds of celestial music.
Various jewel-trees were planted along their banks, adorned with all manner of rare and wonderful treasures. Boats came and went, and beings enjoyed themselves as they pleased.
Within a single river there are a hundred trillion cities; in each city there are a hundred trillion nayutas of villages.
All such cities and villages are respectively surrounded by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of palaces and gardens.
Within Jambudvīpa of these four continents, there is a land named Ratna.
Adorned with flower lamps, the realm was peaceful, prosperous, and joyful, and its population flourished. The sentient beings therein fully practiced the ten virtuous actions.
A wheel-turning king appeared within it, named Vairocana-Surabha-Padma-Keśa (Vairocana Wondrous Jewel Lotus-Hair).
He was suddenly born by transformation within a lotus flower, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, endowed with the seven treasures, and ruled over the four continents.
He constantly instructs all living beings with the True Dharma. The King has a thousand sons who are handsome, brave, and strong, capable of subduing enemies.
His hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of palace ladies and maidservants have all planted roots of goodness together with the King and practiced his words and deeds in concert.
They were born at the same time, being as upright and exquisite as celestial maidens, their bodies of true golden color, constantly emitting—
From all his pores, light constantly emanates a wondrous fragrance. The king is fully endowed with ten billion virtuous ministers and fierce generals.
He has a principal queen named Pūrṇamukhī; she is the King’s jewel of a woman (strī-ratna), exquisite and extraordinary in her beauty.

Her skin is golden, her eyes and hair are deep blue, and her speech is like the Brahma-voice. Her body possesses a celestial fragrance and constantly radiates light that illuminates a thousand *yojanas*. Whoever...
There was a woman named Samantaprajñārci-vicitraguṇanetra, whose physical form was upright and majestic, and whose appearance was exceptionally beautiful;
all sentient beings who beheld her could never tire of the sight. At that time, the lifespan of sentient beings was immeasurable, though some were indeterminate and met with untimely death.
They possessed various forms and colors, various voices, various names, and various clans and lineages—whether foolish or wise, brave or... [the text continues].
Fearing that the various classes of beings—whether poor or wealthy, suffering or happy—are all entirely different, someone might say to another, "My body is handsome, while your form is vulgar.
Having spoken these words, they mutually revile one another and accumulate unwholesome karma.
Because of this karma, their lifespan, physical appearance, strength, and all pleasant things are utterly diminished. At that time, in that city...
To the north is a Bodhi tree named Universal Radiance Dharma-Cloud Sound Banner.
Its roots are formed by indestructible *maṇi* kings that manifest the adornments of the *bodhimaṇḍa* of all Tathāgatas in every thought-moment; its trunk is composed of all kinds of *maṇi* jewels;
and its leaves are made of various exquisite gems, distributed in successive order and perfectly proportioned in the four directions.
From top to bottom, it was perfectly adorned and radiated precious light, emitting sublime sounds that proclaimed the profound realm of all Tathāgatas.

Before those trees stood a fragrant pond named Jewel Flower Radiance Proclaiming the Thunder of Dharma, with banks made of exquisite jewels, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *nayutas* of jewel trees; each tree was shaped like a *bodhi* tree.
Garlands of various jewels from *tīrtha* trees hung down all around, and immeasurable pavilions made entirely of jewels adorned the entire site of enlightenment.

From within that fragrant pond emerged a great lotus named "Cloud of Adornments Manifesting the Realms of All Tathāgatas of the Three Times," within which Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru appeared.
The first Buddha was named Samantaprajñāratnajvālā-suvimalaketu; upon this flower, he first attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
For immeasurable thousands of years, he expounded the True Dharma to bring sentient beings to maturity.
Ten thousand years before that Tathāgata attained Buddhahood, this great lotus emitted a pure radiance called...

He manifests various supernatural powers to bring sentient beings to maturity; if any sentient beings encounter this light, their minds awaken of themselves, and there is nothing they do not understand.

Ten thousand years later, a Buddha shall appear. Nine thousand years prior [to his appearance], he emits a pure radiance named "Stainless Lamp for All Sentient Beings"; if any sentient beings encounter this light, they attain purity.
With his eyes, he sees all forms and knows that after nine thousand years, a Buddha shall appear.
Eight thousand years before [his appearance], he emits a great light named "The Sound of the Karmic Results of All Sentient Beings.

If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, they all come to know for themselves the retribution of their various karmas and know that after eight thousand years, a Buddha shall appear. Seven thousand years before [his appearance], he emits...
There is a great light named "Sound Producing All Roots of Goodness.
If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, all their faculties shall become fully perfected. They will know that after seven thousand years, a Buddha shall appear.
Six thousand years prior [to that], he emits a great light named "Sound of the Inconceivable Realm of the Buddha. If there are sentient beings who encounter this light...
His mind was vast and he attained universal mastery; he knew that six thousand years hence a Buddha would appear.
Five thousand years prior to that, he emitted a great radiance named "Adorning and Purifying All Buddha-fields.

If there were sentient beings who encountered this light, they all beheld all the pure Buddha-lands and knew that five thousand years hence a Buddha would appear. Four thousand... [years hence... a Buddha would appear.
Four thousand years prior [to his appearance], he emitted a great light named "The Undifferentiated Lamp of the Realm of All Tathāgatas.
Any sentient beings who encountered this light were all able to go and behold all the Buddhas.
Three thousand years prior [to his appearance], he emitted a great light named "The Illuminating Lamp of the Three Times. Any sentient beings who encountered...
This light is able to manifest and reveal the ocean of all the past deeds of all Tathāgatas;
it knows that three thousand years hence a Buddha shall appear, and two thousand years prior to that, it emits a great radiance named "The Tathāgata’s Lamp of Wisdom Free from Obscuration.
If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, they will obtain the Universal Eye and see the spiritual transformations of all Tathāgatas.
In all Buddha-lands and throughout all worlds, sentient beings know that two thousand years hence a Buddha shall appear.
One thousand years prior to his appearance, he emits a great radiance called "Causing All Sentient Beings to See the Buddha and Gather All Roots of Goodness.
If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, they shall attain the Samādhi of Seeing the Buddha and know [the future] for one thousand years.
Seven days before the future Buddha is to appear, he will emit a great light named "Sound of Joy for All Sentient Beings.
Any sentient beings who encounter this light will be able to see all Buddhas universally and give rise to great joy, knowing that the Buddha will appear seven days hence.
When the seven days have fully elapsed, all worlds will tremble and become purely radiant.
With minds free from defilement, they universally behold all the pure Buddha-fields of the ten directions and manifest their various adornments;
if there are sentient beings whose faculties and natures are matured and who should see a Buddha, they all proceed to the site of enlightenment.
