[Sūtra] At that time, all the Cakravāḍa mountain ranges, all the Sumeru mountains, and all the various mountains within that world-system...
From all the great oceans, all the lands, all the cities, all the walls, all the palaces, all the music, and all the languages,
there issued forth sounds praising and expounding upon the realm of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas;
furthermore, there issued forth clouds of all kinds of incense, clouds of all kinds of burning incense, clouds of all kinds of powdered incense, and clouds of all fragrances.
Clouds of mani-jewel images; clouds of all jewel-flames; clouds of all flame-treasuries;
clouds of all mani-garments; clouds of all necklaces; clouds of all exquisite flowers; clouds of the radiance of all Tathāgatas;
clouds of the halo of all Tathāgatas; clouds of all music; clouds of the sound of the vows of all Tathāgatas; and all such [clouds].

The ocean-clouds of voices and sounds proclaim: "O Sons of Good Family, this Great Jewel Lotus King, which illuminates the adorned realms of all Tathāgatas throughout the three periods of time, is surrounded by as many lotuses as there are atoms in ten Buddha-fields; each of these lotuses..."
Within each flower was a lion throne made of a treasury of mani jewels, and upon every throne sat a bodhisattva in the full lotus posture.
Son of good family, when that Tathāgata King of the Banner of Wondrous Virtue of Universal Wisdom-Jewel Flame attained unexcelled,
perfect, and complete enlightenment here, he did so simultaneously in all worlds throughout the ten directions.
Having attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, he manifests before all sentient beings according to their inclinations to turn the wheel of Dharma;
in each and every world, he causes immeasurable sentient beings to leave behind the suffering of the evil realms,
causes immeasurable sentient beings to attain rebirth in the heavens, and causes immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the stages of *śrāvaka* and *pratyekabuddha*.
He causes immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhisattva practice of renunciation; he causes immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhisattva practice of the Banner of Valor;
he causes immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhisattva practice of the Light of Dharma;
he causes immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhisattva practice of the Pure Faculties; he causes immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish...
The practice of the path to enlightenment through the power of equanimity causes immeasurable sentient beings to achieve entry into the city of Dharma;

the practice of the path to enlightenment through the power of indestructible supernormal knowledge that reaches all places causes immeasurable sentient beings to enter the path of skillful means of the universal gate; the practice of the path to enlightenment... [causes immeasurable sentient beings to... achieve.
They cause immeasurable sentient beings to abide in the bodhi-practice of the gate of samādhi; they cause immeasurable sentient beings to accomplish the bodhi-practice of perceiving all pure objects;
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to resolve upon the mind of enlightenment (bodhicitta);
they cause immeasurable sentient beings to dwell upon the path of enlightenment; and they cause immeasurable sentient beings to abide securely in the pure pāramitās.

The Way causes immeasurable sentient beings to dwell in the first stage of bodhisattvas; it causes immeasurable sentient beings to dwell in the second stage of bodhisattvas, and so on up to the tenth stage;
it causes immeasurable sentient beings to enter the sublime practices and vows of bodhisattvas;
and it causes immeasurable sentient beings to abide securely in the pure practices and vows of Samantabhadra. Good son, that [Buddha] is named Universal Wisdom Jewel Flame Wondrous...
When the Tathāgata Guṇadhvaja manifested such inconceivable sovereign spiritual power to turn the wheel of Dharma,
he tamed immeasurable sentient beings in each and every one of those worlds, according to their needs, from moment to moment. At that time,
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva knew that the sentient beings within the city of Ratnapuṣpadīpa were relying on their own physical beauty and various sensory objects.
From within the realms, he gave rise to pride and began to despise others. He manifested a wondrous body, upright and exceptionally sublime, and proceeded to that city,
emitting a great radiance that illuminated everything universally, causing all the lights of that holy king, the various exquisite jewels, the sun, moon, and stars,
as well as the bodies of sentient beings, to become completely invisible— just as when the sun rises, it eclipses the multitude of stars.
The radiance was like a mass of ink set against Jāmbūnada gold; at that time, all sentient beings spoke thus: "Who is this?
Is it a deva or a Brahmā who now emits this light, causing all the radiance and colors of our own bodies to become unmanifest?
Though they reflected upon it in various ways, none were able to comprehend it. At that moment, Samantabhadra Bodhisattva was present there within the precious wheel-turning king’s [palace].

Abiding in the sky above the palace, he addressed him, saying: "Great King, you should know that now, within your kingdom, a Buddha has appeared in the world beneath the Bodhi tree named Universal Radiance Dharma-Cloud Sound Banner.

At that time, the daughter of the holy king, Lotus-Wondrous-Eye, beheld the sovereign mastery of the light of the physical body manifested by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, and she heard [the sound] upon her own body."
The exquisite sounds produced by all these ornaments brought joy to his heart, and he thought to himself:
"May all my roots of goodness result in such a body, such adornments, such marks and signs, such majestic deportment,
and such a self-presence as this Great Sage now possesses, who is able [to act] amidst the long night of darkness within the cycle of birth and death of sentient beings."
He emitted great rays of light to reveal that the Tathāgata has appeared in the world, and made this vow: "May I also attain such [a state] as this;
may I act as a light of wisdom for all sentient beings to shatter all the darkness of their ignorance.
May I never be separated from this spiritual friend, this noble son, in whatever place I am born. At that time, the Wheel-Turning King...
Surrounded by his thousand jewel-like daughters, his retinue, his ministers, his assistants, the fourfold army,
and the immeasurable populace within the city, he ascended into the air to a height of one yojana through the king’s supernatural power.
Emitting a great radiance that illuminated the four continents, he caused all beings to behold him, desiring to lead all sentient beings together.
He went to see the Buddha and praised him with these verses:
"The Tathāgata has appeared in the world, universally rescuing all living beings.
You all should quickly go to the presence of the Teacher; only after immeasurable and countless kalpas does a Buddha arise in the world."
He expounds the profound and wondrous Dharma, benefiting all sentient beings.
The Buddha observes that all worlds are constantly deluded by inversion, Suffering the pains of birth and death in saṃsāra;
Thus he gives rise to great compassion, and for countless billions of kalpas, He cultivates the practices of bodhi With the desire to deliver all living beings.
This arises from the power of great compassion; for the sake of seeking enlightenment, one is able to relinquish everything, including head, eyes, hands, and feet.
Throughout such immeasurable kalpas—even across countless billions of kalpas—a Guide is difficult to encounter. To see, hear, or serve him ensures that nothing passes in vain.
Now we shall go together with you all To behold the Honored One, the Tamer of Men, Who sat upon the seat of the Tathāgata,
Subdued the Māras, and attained Perfect Enlightenment. Beholding the body of the Tathāgata,
He emits immeasurable light of various subtle and wondrous colors, Extinguishing all darkness, From within each and every pore.
The inconceivable radiance of light universally illumines all living beings, causing them all to rejoice greatly.
You all should now give rise to a mind of vast and great diligence, go to where that Tathāgata dwells,
and pay him respectful homage and offerings.
At that time, having praised the Buddha with verses to awaken all sentient beings,
the Wheel-Turning Sage King produced ten thousand kinds of great clouds of offerings from his roots of goodness and proceeded to the site of enlightenment toward the place where the Tathāgata was,
namely: clouds of all kinds of precious canopies, clouds of all kinds of flower curtains, clouds of all kinds of precious garments, and clouds of all kinds of precious bell-nets.
Clouds of all fragrant oceans, clouds of all jewel thrones, clouds of all jewel banners, clouds of all palaces,
clouds of all exquisite flowers, and clouds of all various ornaments completely adorned the void;
having arrived, they prostrated at the feet of the Tathāgata Universal Wisdom Jewel Flame Wondrous Virtue Banner King and circumambulated him countless hundreds of times.
Having circumambulated the Buddha a thousand times, she sat before him upon a jewel lotus throne that universally illumines the ten directions.
At that time, the daughter of the Wheel-Turning King, Samantaprajñārci-vimalanetra, removed all the ornaments from her body and scattered them over the Buddha.
As she did so, the ornaments transformed into a precious canopy and jeweled nets suspended in mid-air, which the Dragon Kings then took up and held.
In the center of the palace, ten kinds of precious canopies were arranged in rows, surrounding it on all sides like a multi-storied pavilion.
Both inside and out, it was pure and adorned with clouds of various silk tassels, jewel trees, oceans of incense, and *maṇi* gems.
Within these canopies stood Bodhi trees with flourishing branches and leaves that universally covered the Dharma-realm, manifesting immeasurable forms in every thought-moment.
Adorned and seated beneath this tree was the Tathāgata Vairocana, surrounded before and behind by bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably many buddha-fields;
all had emerged from the practices and vows of Samantabhadra and dwelt in the non-differentiated abodes of bodhisattvas.
He also saw all the lords of the various worlds, and he beheld the sovereign spiritual powers of the Tathāgata.
Furthermore, they see the successive formation and destruction of all worlds throughout all kalpas;
they also see the successive appearance of all Buddhas in all those worlds;
they also see that in each and every world there is the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra making offerings to the Buddhas and taming sentient beings; and they also see all those bodhisattvas.
There was not one who did not find themselves within the body of Samantabhadra;
they also saw their own bodies within his body, and they saw that body before all Tathāgatas, before all Samantabhadras, before all Bodhisattvas, and before all sentient beings.
Furthermore, they saw that within each and every one of those worlds, there were worlds as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field.
Various boundaries, various supports, various shapes, various natures, various arrangements, various adornments, and various purities;

covered above by clouds of various adornments; with various names of kalpas, various appearances of Buddhas, various [divisions of] the three periods of time, various locations, and various ways of abiding within the Dharma-realm.
Entering the various abodes within the Dharma-realm; the various bodhimandas of the Tathāgatas in space;
the various supernormal powers of the Tathāgatas; the various lion thrones of the Tathāgatas; the various oceans of assemblies of the Tathāgatas;
the various distinctions among the assemblies of the Tathāgatas; the various skillful means of the Tathāgatas; and the various turnings of the wheel of Dharma by the Tathāgatas.
Having beheld the ocean of the various utterances of the Tathāgatas and the clouds of the various sūtras of the Tathāgatas,
which arrive with wondrous sounds, his mind became pure and he gave rise to great joy. Then,

the Tathāgata Samantabhadrajñānaratnajvālāguṇaketurāja preached for him a sūtra named *The Turning of the Wheel of Dharma by All Tathāgatas*, consisting of as many verses as there are atoms in ten Buddha-fields.
When Tārā was her attendant, that woman, having heard this sutra, attained ten thousand gateways of samādhi.
Her mind became supple and free from coarseness, like one newly conceived in the womb, like one just born, or like a śāla tree first sprouting its buds;
her mind of samādhi was likewise so, namely, the "Direct Vision of the One."
The Samādhi of Universally Illuminating All Lands of All Buddhas; the Samādhi of Entering the Gates of All Three Times;
the Samādhi of Expounding the Dharma-Wheel of All Buddhas; the Samādhi of Knowing the Ocean of Vows of All Buddhas;

the Samādhi of Awakening All Sentient Beings to Cause Them to Escape the Suffering of Birth and Death; and the Samādhi of Constantly Vowing to Shatter the Darkness of All Sentient Beings. Constantly Vowing...
Having attained ten thousand such samādhis as the Samādhi of Extinguishing the Suffering of All Sentient Beings, the Samādhi of Constantly Vowing to Produce Happiness for All Sentient Beings,
the Samādhi of Teaching and Transforming All Sentient Beings Without Weariness or Fatigue,
the Samādhi of the Unobstructed Banner of All Bodhisattvas, and the Samādhi of Universally Visiting All Pure Buddha-fields, he further...
Attaining a mind of wondrous concentration, a mind unmoving, a mind of joy, a mind of consolation, a vast mind,
a mind compliant with spiritual friends, a mind directed toward the profound omniscience, a mind abiding in the ocean of vast skillful means,
a mind relinquishing all attachments, a mind not dwelling in any worldly realms, a mind entering the realm of the Tathāgatas, universally illuminating all...
A mind that is free from affliction regarding the ocean of all forms; a mind free from arrogance; a mind free from weariness; a mind free from regression; a mind free from indolence;
a mind contemplating the intrinsic nature of all phenomena; a mind dwelling securely in the ocean of all dharma-gates; a mind observing the ocean of all dharma-gates;
a mind that thoroughly understands the ocean of all sentient beings; and a mind that protects and delivers all sentient beings.

The mind that gives birth to the ocean of resolve; the mind that universally illumines all oceans of worlds; the mind that universally generates the ocean of vows of all Buddhas; the mind that completely shatters all mountains of obstacles;
the mind that accumulates the merit and virtues that assist the path; the mind that directly perceives the ten powers of all Buddhas;
the mind that universally illumines the spheres of Bodhisattvas; the mind that increases the Bodhisattva’s aids to the path; and the mind that universally takes all directions as its object.

With a single-minded focus on the heart of the ocean, he contemplated the Great Vows of Samantabhadra: the vow to produce oceans of vows as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields of all Tathāgatas;
the vow to adorn and purify all buddha-lands; the vow to discipline all sentient beings; the vow to universally know the entire dharma-realm;
the vow to universally enter the oceans of all dharma-realms; and the vow to [remain] throughout the exhaustion of all buddha-fields.
Throughout all future kalpas, may I cultivate the practices and vows of a bodhisattva; throughout all future kalpas, may I never abandon any bodhisattva practice or vow;
may I obtain the vow to draw near to all Tathāgatas; may I obtain the vow to serve all spiritual friends; may I obtain the vow to make offerings to all Buddhas;
and in every thought-moment, may I cultivate bodhisattva practices, increasing all-encompassing wisdom without interruption.
When she had thus brought to fulfillment an ocean of vows as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields— the great vows of Samantabhadra—
that Tathāgata further revealed and expounded for her daughter the roots of goodness accumulated since first generating the aspiration for enlightenment,
the sublime practices cultivated, and the great fruits attained, causing her to awaken and accomplish all the vows of a Tathāgata.
"O son of good family who single-mindedly inclines toward the stage of omniscience, furthermore, ten great eons prior to this,
there was a world named Sūryamaṇḍalābha and a Buddha named Indraketudhvajaruciravyūha.
Within the legacy of that Tathāgata’s Dharma, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra exhorted this woman of beautiful eyes to repair a lotus seat."
Furthermore, when ancient Buddha images had been damaged, I repaired them; having repaired them, I painted them; having painted them, I adorned them with jewels.

Having thus generated the mind set on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, noble son, I recall that in the past, through the spiritual friend Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, I planted these roots of goodness. From that time onward, I have never fallen into the evil realms.

I have always been born into the lineages of all celestial kings and human kings, possessing a handsome and pleasing appearance with all marks perfectly complete, such that people delight in seeing me;

I have constantly seen the Buddha and always attained proximity to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, even until now, where he has shown me guidance, brought about awakening, and matured me, causing me to give rise to joy.

Son of good family, what do you think of this? You— (Note: The final "you" [爾] in the source text appears to be a scribal error for "I" [我], as the narrative voice is consistently first-person throughout.)
Was the Wheel-Turning Sage King Vairocanagarbha-suvicitra-ratna-padma-śekhara anyone else at that time?
He was none other than the present Maitreya Bodhisattva. Was the Queen Consort Pūrṇamukhī anyone else?
She was the Night Goddess Śāntasvaranirghoṣa, who dwells not far from here. And as for the young girl Sumatekṣaṇā at that time, she was myself.

At that time, as a young girl, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra exhorted me to repair an image of a lotus throne, making it a causal condition for unexcelled bodhi; he caused me to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
At that time, I first gave rise to that mind, and subsequently, he further guided me so that I might behold the Banner of Wondrous Virtue (*Guṇaketurāja*).
When the Buddha untied the necklaces from his body and scattered them as an offering to the Buddha, I beheld the Buddha’s spiritual power and heard the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma.
I immediately attained the Bodhisattva liberation door of "Universally Manifesting in All Worlds to Tame Sentient Beings.
In every thought-moment, I see Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, and I also see their sites of enlightenment, their assemblies, and their pure lands—all of which I fully perceive.
"O noble son, having honored, revered, made offerings to, heard the teaching of the Dharma from,
and practiced according to the instructions of those Buddhas in that world of Vairocana’s Great Majestic Virtue during the kalpa of Perfect Purity,
there followed a world named Jewel-Wheel Sublime Adornment and a kalpa named Great Radiance, in which five hundred Buddhas appeared; I served them all."
The first Buddha whom I reverently served and made offerings to was named Mahākaruṇādhvaja;
when he first left the household life, I was a night goddess and reverently made offerings to him. Next, there was a Buddha named Vajranārāyaṇadhvaja;
I was a universal monarch (cakravartin) and reverently made offerings to that Buddha, who preached for me a sūtra titled *Sarvabuddhavyūha-daśabuddha*.
With as many sūtras as there are atoms in a buddha-field serving as its retinue, there was next a Buddha named Vajra-Asaṅga-Guṇa.
At that time, I was a universal monarch (cakravartin) who reverently made offerings to that Buddha;
for my sake, he preached a sūtra titled "Universally Illuminating the Faculties of All Beings," which consisted of as many sūtras as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru.
I have fully received and upheld all these as my retinue. Next, there was a Buddha named Mountain of Wondrous Adornments of Blazing Fire Flames;

at that time, I was the daughter of an elder. That Buddha preached for me a sūtra titled *The Treasury of Universal Illumination of the Three Times*, with as many sūtras as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa serving as its retinue. I heard them all and received and upheld them according to the Dharma.
Next, there was a Buddha named Sarvadharma-sāgarodgata-vijaya-rāja.
I served and made offerings to that Buddha as the King of Asuras, and for my sake he preached a sūtra titled *Sarvadharma-dhātu-vibhaṅga*, with five hundred sūtras as its retinue;
I heard them all and received and upheld them according to the Dharma. Next, there was a Buddha named Sāgara.
At Mount Dharma-Prabhāsa, I was the daughter of a dragon king; I made offerings to that Buddha by raining down clouds of wish-fulfilling maṇi jewels.

That Buddha preached for me a sūtra named *Saṃvardhana-prīti-sāgara*, with hundreds of billions of sūtras as its retinue, all of which I heard and received and upheld according to the Dharma. Next, there was a Buddha named Ratna-jvālā-giri.
I, Lamp, was a sea deity who made offerings of clouds of rain-like precious lotuses to that Buddha with deep reverence;

for my sake, he preached a sūtra named *Dharmadhātu-upāya-sāgara-prabhāsa*, which had as its retinue as many sūtras as there are atoms in a buddha-field, all of which I heard and received according to the Dharma. Next, there appeared a Buddha named *Guṇasāgara-prabhāsa*.
At that time, I was a seer possessing the five supernatural powers (*pañcābhijña*), who manifested great miraculous feats while surrounded by sixty thousand seers.

They made offerings of clouds of fragrant flowers and incense to that Buddha, who then preached for me a *sūtra* titled "The Lamp of the Dharma Free from Attachment" (*Asaṅga-dharmapradīpa-sūtra*), with sixty thousand *sūtras* as its retinue; I heard them all and received and upheld them according to the Dharma. Next—
There was a Buddha named Vairocana-Guṇagarbha.

At that time, I was a presiding earth goddess named Samatā-nirhāra, and together with immeasurable earth goddesses, I rained down clouds of all kinds of jewel trees, all kinds of maṇi-treasures, and all kinds of precious necklaces as an offering to that Buddha. He then preached for me a sūtra called...
I have heard and upheld, without forgetting, all the immeasurable sūtras that constitute the retinue of the Treasury of Wisdom of all Tathāgatas.
Son of good family, in this sequence, the last Buddha was named Lamp of Wondrous Virtue Filling the Void of the Dharma Realm.
At that time, I was a courtesan named Beautiful Face, and I saw the Buddha entering the city and performed songs and dances for him.
Having made offerings and sustained by the Buddha’s spiritual power, they leaped up into the air and praised the Buddha with a thousand verses.
The Buddha then emitted from between his eyebrows a light called "The Great Radiance Adorning the Dharma Realm," which universally touched my body.
Having received this light, I immediately attained a gate of liberation called "The Non-retrogressive Treasury of Skillful Means in the Dharma Realm. Good son, in this world...
Within this realm, throughout as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field,
I have served, revered, and made offerings to all the Tathāgatas who appeared therein; I have recollected all the True Dharma taught by those Tathāgatas,
not forgetting even a single word or phrase, and I have praised and extolled each and every one of those Tathāgatas.
All Buddha-dharmas extensively perform benefit for immeasurable sentient beings;

from each and every one of those Tathāgatas, I have obtained the light of omniscience, which manifests the ocean of the dharma-realm of the three periods of time and enters all practices of Samantabhadra.
O son of good family, by relying on this light of omniscience, I see immeasurable Buddhas in every thought-moment, and having seen them—
The Buddha has already fully accomplished and perfected all the practices of Samantabhadra, which he had never before attained or seen.

Why is this? Because he has obtained the light of omniscience (*sarvajñā-jyotis*). At that time, the night goddess Sarvasattvatrāṇaśīlā, wishing to further clarify the meaning of this liberation, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, spoke these verses for the youth Sudhana:
"Good Wealth, listen as I speak of this profound and difficult-to-see Dharma, which universally illuminates all the diverse gateways throughout the three periods of time.
Just as I first resolved my mind upon enlightenment and single-mindedly sought the Buddha's virtues,
entering into various liberations— you should now listen attentively as I reflect upon the past."
Past as many eons as atoms in a buddha-field, there was once an eon named Perfectly Pure.
At that time, there was a world named Universal Illuminating Lamp, in which buddhas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru appeared in the world.
The first buddha was named Wisdom Flame; the next buddha was named Dharma Banner.
The third was Dharma-Sumeru; the fourth, Virtue-Lion; the fifth, King of Tranquility;
the sixth, Extinction of All Views; the seventh, High Renown; the eighth, Great Merit;
the ninth, named Supreme Sun; and the tenth, named Moon-Face—at the site of this one Buddha.
This is the first gateway to awakening; following this in succession, ten further Buddhas appeared.
The first was named Ākāśasthāna (Abiding in Space); the second was named Samantaprabha (Universal Radiance); the third was named Sarvadigsthita (Abiding in All Directions);
the fourth was named Smṛtisāgara (Ocean of Right Mindfulness); the fifth was named Uccagāminprabha (Exalted and Surpassing Light); and the sixth was named Merumegha (Sumeru Cloud).
Seventh is named Dharma-flame Buddha; Eighth is named Mountain-superior Buddha;
Ninth is named Great Compassion Flower; Tenth is named Dharma-realm Flower. When these ten appeared, The second awakening dharma-gate emerged.
Following this in succession, Ten more Buddhas appeared: The first was Light-banner Buddha.
The second was Wisdom Buddha; the third, Mind-Meaning Buddha; the fourth, Lord of Virtue Buddha;
the fifth, Celestial Wisdom Buddha; the sixth, King of Wisdom Buddha; the seventh, Supreme Knowledge Buddha;
the eighth, Light-King Buddha; the ninth, Valiant Buddha; and the tenth, Lotus Buddha.
Under these ten Buddhas, he realized the third Dharma-gate. Following this, there appeared in succession another ten Buddhas: first, Ratnajvālācala;
second, Guṇasāgara; third, Dharmaprabhāsa; fourth, Padmagarbha; fifth, Sattvacakṣus.
The sixth was Sugandhaprabha-ratna; the seventh, Sumeru-guṇa; the eighth, Gandharva-rāja;
the ninth, Maṇi-kośa; and the tenth, Śāntavarṇa. Following these, there appeared in succession ten more Buddhas:
the first Buddha was Viśāla-jñāna, and the next Buddha was Ratnaprabhāsa.
The third was Gaganamegha; the fourth, Viśeṣacārin; the fifth, Paripūrṇavrata;
the sixth, Nārāyaṇa; the seventh, Meruśrī; the eighth, Guṇacakravartin; the ninth, Aparājitadhvaja;
and the tenth, Mahādrumarāja. Following these, in successive order:
Furthermore, ten buddhas appeared: The first was Brahmagarbha; The second, Lokādhipateya-kāya;
The third, Uccagāmin-prabha; The fourth, Vajraprabhāsa; The fifth, Bhūmibalavega;
The sixth, Gambhīradharma; The seventh, Dharmamati-svara; The eighth, Merudhvaja.
The ninth was Supreme Radiance; the tenth was Wondrous Jewel Light.
Following these, ten more Buddhas appeared in succession: the first was Brahma Radiance; the second, Sound of Space;
the third, Body of the Dharma Realm; the fourth, Wheel of Radiance; and the fifth, Banner of Wisdom.
The sixth was Gaganapradīpa; the seventh, Sūkṣmaguṇa; the eighth, Samantāvabhāsaprabha;
the ninth, Varapuṇyaprabha; and the tenth, Mahākaruṇāmegha.
Following these, ten more Buddhas appeared in succession: the first was Balaprabhājñāna; the second, Samantamukhapratibhāsa.
Third, Lofty Radiance; fourth, Body of Light; fifth, Buddha Arising from Dharma; sixth, Buddha Jewel Mark;
seventh, Swift Wind; eighth, Valiant Banner; ninth, Exquisite Jewel Canopy;
tenth, Illuminating the Three Times. Following these, they appear in succession.
Furthermore, ten Buddhas appeared: First, Praṇidhānasāgaraprabha;
Second, Vajrakāya; Third, Meruguṇa; Fourth, Smṛtidhvajarāja;
Fifth, Guṇamati; Sixth, Jñānapradīpa; Seventh, Prabhādhvaja; Eighth, Viśālajñāna.
The ninth was the Wisdom of the Dharma Realm; the tenth was the Wisdom of the Ocean of Dharmas.
Following this, there appeared in succession ten further Buddhas: the first was named Bestowing the Dharma; the next was named Wheel of Merit;
the third was named Supreme and Wondrous Cloud; the fourth was named Lamp of Patience and Wisdom; and the fifth was named Silent Sound.
Sixth is named Śāntadhvaja; seventh is named Lokapradīpa; eighth is named Gambhīramahāpraṇidhāna;
ninth is named Anabhibhūtavijaya-dhvaja; tenth is named Jñānārci-samudra. Following this, ten more Buddhas appeared in succession:
the first Buddha was Dharmavaśavartin; the second Buddha was Asaṅgajñāna.
The third was named Ocean of Melodious Wisdom; the fourth, Multitude of Wondrous Voices; the fifth, Sovereign Bestower; the sixth, Universally Manifesting;
the seventh, Body According to Desire; the eighth, Abiding in Supreme Virtue; the ninth, Buddha of Original Nature;
and the tenth, Buddha of Worthy Virtue. [This occurred] throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru.

All the Buddhas who exist herein, universally acting as lamps for the world, I have all made offerings to throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field. Every Buddha who has appeared, I have made offerings to all;
having entered this door of liberation, I have practiced and attained this path over immeasurable kalpas.
If you can practice in this way, you too shall before long attain it, O son of good family.
I know only this liberation of a bodhisattva called "Universally Manifesting in All Worlds to Discipline Sentient Beings.
As for those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have accumulated boundless practices, giving rise to various understandings and manifesting various bodies—[I do not know their ways].
Possessing various faculties, fulfilling various aspirations, entering various samādhis, manifesting various supernatural transformations,
being able to observe phenomena in various ways, entering various gates of wisdom, and attaining the light of various dharmas—
how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct? Good son, not far from here there is a night goddess named...
Śāntasvarasāgaravatī sat upon a lotus throne adorned with mani-light banners, surrounded before and behind by a million asaṃkhyeya night goddesses.
Go to her and ask how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
At that time, Sudhana prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, gazed up at her with earnest devotion, and took his leave.
He withdrew and departed.
[Treatise] Within the first dharma-gate of the formal entry into the stage, the section beginning from "At that time, the youth Sudhana...
is divided into fourteen parts. First, from "At that time, the youth Sudhana... down to "acted as follows... [is the first part].

This vow is already explained in six and a half lines of scripture as the instruction of the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā on entering through contemplation, not contradicting the teaching of one's spiritual friend. This section is divided into two parts:
from "having gone to the place of the night goddess Viśvapadmasamantabhadravimalaprabhā" down to "emitting light that entered Sudhana’s crown and filled his body," which consists of five lines.
The Sūtra clarifies that the Universal Savior Night Goddess emits from between her eyebrows a light named "Wisdom Lamp Universally Illuminating Banner" which enters the body of Sudhana.
This section is divided into three parts: first, Sudhana’s descent [into the light] at that time; second, up until the point where he attains the pure light of all-knowledge;
and third, thirty-nine lines of sūtra text clarifying the wisdom-lamps seen by Sudhana as the light entered his body.

The boundless ocean of realms illuminated by the Gate of Universal Radiance and the ocean of realms for teaching and transforming sentient beings through the conduct of the Night Goddess Samantānugata are divided into four periods.
After the youth Sudhana had witnessed such supernatural powers of this goddess, he descended to praise her with verses. There are five lines of scripture clarifying Sudhana’s vision of her.
The section on the Night Goddess praising his virtues through the power of her spiritual faculties consists of five verses;

the section on Sudhana’s formal exposition consists of twenty and a half verses, which further clarify the phenomena previously seen, consisting of six parts; from the passage "At that time, the youth Sudhana, having spoken these verses...
down to "...by practicing what kind of conduct does one attain purity? there are three lines of scripture, which constitute Sudhana’s inquiry.
"What kind of practices must one cultivate to attain purity, and how long has it been since one attained this liberation?
The Night Goddess replied, "Noble son, from this point downward, I shall speak for you by virtue of the Buddha’s spiritual power.

There are nine and a half lines of scripture that clarify that the Night Goddess’s exposition of the Dharma is difficult to comprehend, and that it is not something accessible to gods, humans, or those of the two vehicles.
That which can be measured and known is explained for you through the Buddha’s spiritual power, divided into eight sections. Good son,

from "In a past age" down to "manifesting the inconceivable signs of a Tathāgata’s appearance," there are ninety-seven lines of scripture clarifying the lotus flower within the Jewel-Flower Radiance Pond before the Bodhi tree to the north of the Universal Monarch’s city.
"Good son, this section on 'The Ten Times Emitting Light from Flowers to Benefit Sentient Beings Differently and Universally Arising Clouds of Adornments throughout All Realms'—
beginning with the passage 'This Universal Illumination of All Tathāgatas of the Three Times' and extending down to the forty-eight and a half lines of verse—
clarifies the emergence of the first Buddha within a lotus flower to the north of the city of Ratnapuṣpadīpa."
The manifested Samantabhadra Bodhisattva informed the Wheel-Turning King and his retinue that they should all go together to see the Buddha;
he then recited the ten verses on the Ten Practices from the "Chapter on the Appearance of the Tathāgata" in praise of the Tathāgata’s virtues, as fully explained in the sutra.
At that time, the Wheel-Turning Sage King, down to those who had first resolved for Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, [all attained realization].

The *Cittotpāda-saptatriṃśat-pāda-sūtra* (The Sūtra on the Seventy-three and a Half Verses on the Arising of the Mind) clarifies how the Universal Monarch and his daughter made offerings, and how that daughter, Wondrous Eye (*Sunetra*), obtained benefit and gave rise to the bodhicitta. Section Eleven:
"Good son, I recall that in the past, through the spiritual friend Samantabhadra Bodhisattva—and continuing down to hearing the True Dharma and practicing according to the teachings—there was..."
The sixteen and a half lines of the sūtra clarify the conclusion above:

the causes and conditions of practice, the retinues, the names, and the section on the roots of goodness initiated by Samantabhadra. This first dharma-gate attained by the Buddha is named "The Bodhisattva’s Liberation Gate of Universally Manifesting in All Worlds to Tame Sentient Beings. Twelve sons passed beyond the... Following the kalpa of Perfect Purity in the world of Vairocana’s Great Majestic Virtue,
there was a world named Jewel-Wheel Sublime Adornment, during the kalpa named Great Radiance, in which five hundred Buddhas appeared;
it was among these [Buddhas] that this Night Goddess Samantānugata took birth under each of the ten Buddhas, her births differing in each case.
"Having made offerings to and heard all dharmas as they appear in the texts— thirteen good sons, in this world,
throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms within such Buddha-fields, all Tathāgatas have appeared therein;
I have served, revered, and made offerings to them all, and I have not forgotten a single word or a single phrase of any dharma-gate."

Below, down to the tenth and a half lines of the verse, there is a sutra passage that clarifies the section on the general conclusion regarding the various kalpas passed, the Buddhas honored, and the attainment of the dharma-gate.

This section elucidates how the practice for fulfilling wisdom is perfected: because one’s own Buddha-assembly and the assemblies of other Buddhas are unified as a single dharma-realm, the entire measure is taken as the number of atoms within a buddha-field. For the sake of a rough approximation, this is based on the Buddha of one's own practice.
Because the fruit is all-pervasive, the following verse summarizes the total number of Buddhas previously honored as presented above.
Dividing them into eleven sections with ten Buddhas each as the starting point, there are Buddhas in number equal to the atoms of Mount Sumeru whom he has previously honored.
This summary refers to the Buddha-fruit of his own practice on the eleventh stage; thus, his own practice corresponds to the self-nature of other Buddhas.
They shall become one body; one must not seek exclusively for self or others.
(14) "I only know this Bodhisattva’s liberation of universally manifesting in all worlds to discipline sentient beings.

From here below is the section on inferring virtues and ascending, which explains the meaning according to the text: It is said that in the past, beyond kalpas as numerous as the atoms of Buddha-lands, there was an eon...
It is named "Perfectly Pure," for it is the embodiment of the all-pervading illumination of omniscience.
There is a world named "Vairocana-Majesty," for it is the sovereign radiance of the various distinct and intermingled wisdoms.
This is the universal pervasiveness of the practice of diligence. [Therein lies] a Mount Sumeru... [microscopic].
The appearance of Buddhas as numerous as atoms within this stage is the fruit of the vast magnitude and lofty transcendence of the wisdom of progressive advancement in the stage of diligence.
In the preceding stage, thirty-two nayutas, another immeasurable, and five hundred more Buddhas were cited;
here, there are two further Buddhas to represent the vast magnitude of the wisdom of seeing Buddhas through progressive advancement. This must be understood.
The atoms of Mount Meru serve as the measure for the Buddhas. "Brilliantly Advancing and Rising High" refers to this world.
On the side of the Cakravāḍa Mountains at the eastern limit, there is a four-continent world-system named Ratnapradīpapuṣpadhvaja.
This clarifies that "the eastern limit" and "Ratnapradīpapuṣpadhvaja" together clarify the cultivation of differentiated wisdom, which consists of one hundred trillion nayutas.

"Various lands" clarifies that the realm of the sovereign wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*)—encompassing its primary and attendant dharma-gates, its retinue, its gathering of beings, and its retributive abodes—is being described.
Within this Jambudvīpa of the four continents, there is a land named Jewel Flower Lamp;
this clarifies the meaning of the sovereign illumination of differentiated wisdom. Within it, sentient beings fully practice the ten wholesome actions.
There appeared therein a wheel-turning monarch named Vairocana-Surabha-Keśara (Vairocana-Miraculous-Jewel-Flower-Crest).
That king’s sudden, miraculous birth within a lotus signifies that the various distinctions of omniscient wisdom arise from that which is unborn;
though they arise, they remain unstained. His possession of the thirty-two marks is the fruition born of wisdom.

The possession of the seven treasures symbolizes the seven factors of enlightenment (*saptabodhyaṅga*). The king’s sovereignty over the four continents signifies the universal pervasiveness of the four wisdoms (*caturjñāna*).
His constant exposition of the True Dharma to instruct all living beings represents the manifestation of right wisdom and the absence of deviant conduct.

That the king has a thousand sons signifies the fulfillment of the ten thousand practices (*daśasahasra-pratipatti*). The queen and the precious women together symbolize the joy of the Dharma, compassion, and loving-kindness.
Furthermore, she has a daughter named Samantaprajñārci-guṇalocanā; this is the assembly of the night goddess Samantaraśmi, who practices the conduct of wisdom and compassion.

In this world, where the pure and the defiled coexist and the foolish and the wise dwell together, this assembly integrates the defiled and the pure to accomplish the two practices of wisdom and compassion. To the north of that city, before the Bodhi tree, there is...
The name of the Fragrant Pond is "Radiance of Jewel Lotus Flowers. This symbolizes the fragrance of the essence of precepts and meditative concentration within the Dharma-body.

From within this Fragrant Pond emerges a great lotus flower named "Cloud of Adornments Manifesting the Realms of All Tathāgatas of the Three Times," which signifies the ability to give rise to the practices of the ten *pāramitās* within the Dharma-body and to manifest them all.

Because the realms of all Buddhas are like clouds, the appearance of as many Buddhas as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru within them collectively clarifies that all Buddhas arise from the pool of the Dharma-body—
characterized by the great compassion and great kindness of omniscient wisdom and the ten pāramitās—
and emerge through the practice of vigor. [This concludes the section] below the Fragrance Pool.
The Lotus is named Jewel Flower Radiance; it emits light in ten stages to benefit sentient beings.
Ten thousand years ago, this great lotus emitted pure radiance called "Manifesting All Spiritual Powers" to bring sentient beings to accomplishment.

Any sentient being who encountered this light would have their mind spontaneously awakened, such that there was none who did not attain full understanding. This corresponds to the Dāna-pāramitā (Perfection of Giving).
With *madhu* as the primary element and the other nine as its companions, after ten thousand years, a Buddha shall appear.

In each instance of a Buddha’s appearance, the *prajñāpāramitā* (perfection of wisdom) serves as the essential body (*mūlatattva*) for the ten [Buddhas], and by extension, for hundreds, thousands, and tens of millions—all of whom take wisdom as their ten Buddhas.
Furthermore, nine thousand years prior, he emits a pure light named "All Sentient Beings Free from..."
The Lamp of Purification takes the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīla-pāramitā*) as its primary focus, with the other nine perfections as its companions.
Regarding the Buddha who shall appear after nine thousand years: this refers to the perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*).

When the Buddha appears, eight thousand years prior to his manifestation, he will emit a great radiance called "The Sound of the Karmic Results of All Sentient Beings. If there are sentient beings who encounter this light, they shall attain self-... [realization].
Having understood the retributions of all karmas, they are next assigned to the ten *pāramitās* within the *kṣānti-pāramitā*. After eight thousand years, a Buddha shall appear;
from this point downward, [the stages] seven, six, five, four, three, two, and one are all assigned in sequence in this manner.
At the end, it says: "One makes offerings to Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field," which signifies that wisdom is perfected and practice is universal.
The mind is entirely like the conduct of a Buddha, and the view is entirely like that of a Buddha, for there is not a single world in the ten directions that is not a Buddha.
The following verses, which commemorate one hundred and ten Buddha names, correspond to the positions of the causal and resultant stages of the Buddhas of these ten stages and the eleventh stage.
Thus, the verse says: "The first initial Buddha is named Wisdom-Flame," which refers to the first [stage].

In the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*) is predominant; the remaining nine Buddhas represent the ten perfections within that perfection of giving in this first stage.

These names of the Buddhas all function as mutual leaders and companions according to each respective perfection, and one should carefully contemplate them to perceive their significance for one’s own mind.
Following this, there are again ten Buddhas in successive order, the first of whom is named... [end of fragment].

The Buddha of the Sphere of Empty Space corresponds to the second stage, the Stainless Ground (*vimalā-bhūmi*), because the nature of precepts is like empty space and the Dharma-body constitutes the essence of the precepts.
The names of the other nine Buddhas are the names of the primary and auxiliary *pāramitās* within the precepts of this stage. Following this, ten more Buddhas appear in succession.
The Buddha Eka-raśmi-dhvaja corresponds to the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*) within the third stage, the Luminous (*prabhākari-bhūmi*).

By cultivating the eight dhyānas, one purifies the afflictive obstacles of the three realms; this is termed "light. When delusion has perished and patience is established as immovable, it is termed a "banner" (*dhvaja*).
The nine Buddha names following this are the fruits of the primary and attendant *pāramitā* practices. Thus it is said.

In each subsequent stage (*bhūmi*), the ten *pāramitās* are integrated with all ten; the names of the Buddha-fruit are to be assigned as above, from which one will naturally perceive the intended meaning.

As for the total enumeration of Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field (*buddhakṣetra-rajas*), it is because when wisdom is perfected and conduct is universal, there is nothing that is not the Buddha.
"To serve them all" means that the holy and the ordinary share the same essence; there is not a single thing that is not the emptiness of the Buddha-dharma.
There is no interval [between them]. When one observes with the Universal Eye, penetrating both mind and境 (the objective realm), there is nothing that is not Buddha.
Because wisdom follows reverent practice, all things are Buddha; therefore, for one who sees thus, even when discussed in terms of phenomena, it is truly so.
Furthermore, when discussed in terms of the symbolic dharma, everything is collectively and truly Buddha. Thus, if there were even a single dharma or a single object that was not seen as Buddha—
One should know that such a person possesses false views rather than right views;
because they possess subject and object, and because these various views arise in competition, they cannot enter the realm of the wisdom-eye of Samantabhadra and Mañjuśrī.

Such is the vision of the initial mind and the perfection of wisdom, which does not shift from stage to stage. This is elucidated through the meaning of the six characteristics—both general and specific—as explained in the Sūtra.
If one asks, "Who was this Universal Monarch named Vairocanagarbha-suvimala-padma-śekhara? it is none other than the present-day Bodhisattva Maitreya.
This clarifies that the treasury of omniscient wisdom (*sarvajñājñānagarbha*) is perfected; thus, while his Buddha-fruition is complete, his bodhisattva practices are also exhaustive.
Furthermore, the perfection of the countenance of his queen signifies that she delights in the Dharma through the perfection of wisdom.
The "perfect face upon face" signifies that the dharmas of seeing, hearing, fragrance, and taste are fulfilled; it expresses the joy of the Dharma and represents the meaning of a wife.
Now, the Night Goddess Silent Ocean of Sound is assigned to the fifth dhyāna gateway to represent the bliss of meditative joy (*dhyāna-prīti*);
she does not merely take on a partial likeness of a worldly wife. She is the princess, the maiden Subhagadatta.
This indicates that through the practice of wisdom and compassion, one is free from the dual habits of defilement and purity. Furthermore, the Sūtra says:
"Good son, after the kalpa of Perfect Purity in the world-system of Vairocana’s Great Majestic Virtue, there follows a world-system named Jewel-Wheel Adornment;
the kalpa is named Great Radiance. Within it, five hundred Buddhas appear, all of whom I [have served]."
Regarding the "attendant" (sevaka): throughout these eleven stages, one practices each of the ten *pāramitās* within each of the five paths;
as they mutually serve as the essence for one another, there are one hundred [practices] per stage, totaling five hundred.

Among these, according to the appearance of the Buddha, the body that serves the Buddha may be that of a night goddess (*rātridevatā*), a universal monarch (*cakravartin*), or a lord of the *asuras*; this is the fruit of Buddhahood.
The final stage of the practices corresponding to the intermediate levels is represented by the courtesan, which symbolizes the joy of the Dharma;

this clarifies that within the eleventh bhūmi, the five hundred practices are fulfilled. Understanding it in this way, one realizes that those who seek the truth by exclusively focusing on external Buddhas outside of their own body—apart from the Dharma of self-practice and the fruit of Buddhahood itself—are fundamentally neither practitioners of the Path of Cultivation nor those of the Path of Seeing. If...
The fruit of the stage of self-cultivation is that which corresponds to the self-realization of all Buddhas;

because it corresponds to one's own Buddha-fruit, even if one were to seek it with great effort and succeed in seeing it, that would be a temporary manifestation and not something reachable through one's own practice.
This clarifies that within a single stage, the dharmas of the ten stages are complete, and within each stage, there are ten aspects—the essence of the ten stages.
Therefore, because the ten pāramitās interpenetrate one another, they are fully present both collectively and individually.

Thus, all are like the gateway of Indra’s net, wherein the one and the many mutually penetrate. This is the fourth stage, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom (*Arciṣmatī-bhūmi*), where the pāramitā of diligence (*vīrya-pāramitā*) is primary and the other nine are its companions.
Its sphere of cultivation is the world, and it consists of practicing compassion without weariness.

To counteract the obstacle of indolence—which causes one to take no pleasure in diligence and to abandon sentient beings—one must apply oneself with single-minded vigor to teach and transform sentient beings.

Thus, within these five stages and the ten stages (*bhūmi*), the name "Buddha" is designated for each fruit of Buddhahood in terms of the wisdom of practice, the scope of compassion, the conduct undertaken, and the destination reached.
One must not expect to see the Buddha merely by setting a goal according to one's own whims or through a momentary aspiration.
Each emanation body must establish its own wisdom, conduct, and locus to constitute a Buddha-name;
one must sequentially assign the meaning of each name to its corresponding reality and perceive its intent for oneself. One must not attempt to create a separate mold outside of one's own Dharma.
Good son, I know only this Bodhisattva practice of universally manifesting in all worlds to harmonize and transform beings.

Regarding the section on "The Liberation of Subduing Sentient Beings," which clarifies the advancement through the promotion of virtues, within this second advancement through the promotion of virtues, there are eight and a half lines of scripture—from "As for the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas... down to "...and withdrew"—which are established according to six gates:
first, the advancement through the promotion of virtues; second, the indication of where the spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) reside, stating "depart from here."
1. Not far away [is] the night goddess named *Śāntasvaranirghoṣasāgara* (Ocean of the Sound of Tranquility). 2. The number of the retinue and attendant deities of the night goddess.
3. Exhorting Sudhana to go and inquire [of her]. 4. Hearing where the spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) resides, he pays his respects and departs.
Commentary: Previously it was said "in the midst of the assembly," whereas here it says "not far away"; this indicates that the former refers to the stage of diligence (*vīrya*).
The *pāramitās* collectively bring all practices together to meet within the essence of bodhi, for they do not depart from the essence of bodhi;
thus it is said that they are "assembled therein. This clarifies that through the cultivation of meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), one ascends to this stage;

within this stage, one practices worldly techniques, crafts, and various other arts and skills, which are superior to those of the preceding stage. Because they do not depart from the essence of bodhi, they do not depart [from it].

Because of the practice of diligent progress, there arises skillful capability; the night goddess named Ocean of the Sound of Tranquility (Śāntasvaranirghoṣa) is near here, which clarifies that the function of tranquility is all-pervasive.
"Tranquility" is meditative concentration (*samādhi*), and "Ocean of Sound" is its function;
thus it clarifies that based on this fifth stage, the gate of dhyāna, wisdom arises from concentration, its function being as vast as the ocean, and therefore she sits upon a *mañca*.
The "Lotus Throne Adorned with the Banner of Nī" (Nī-dhvaja-vyūha) clarifies that the essence of meditative concentration (*samādhi*) is stainless and free from attachment.
That she is surrounded before and behind by ten million *asaṃkhyeya* night goddesses clarifies that the essence of meditative concentration pervades everywhere and acts universally;

furthermore, "ten million" (*koṭi*) is the highest among numbers, and raising the figure to "ten million *asaṃkhyeya*" is what is here termed "ten million. (In this context, it is said to be "ten million.")

As for these enumerations, since their source cannot be fully exhausted, they are merely summarized here by way of the conduct of traveling through the ten directions to gather and transform beings for their benefit;

thus, this Night Goddess Silent Sound Ocean is the mother of the Night Goddess Wondrous Virtue Who Universally Saves Sentient Beings, signifying that meditative concentration (*samādhi*) can bring about diligent practice (*vīrya*). For without concentration, all practices would [be ineffective].
There is fatigue.
