Fifth, not far from here, is the Night Goddess Silent Sound Ocean, who presides over the Ground Difficult to Conquer.

[Sūtra] At that time, the youth Sudhana, having heard from the night goddess Samantagambhīraśrīvimalaprabhā the bodhisattva liberation door of universally manifesting in all worlds to discipline sentient beings, attained thorough knowledge, faith, and understanding,
and dwelt therein with mastery. He then proceeded to the night goddess Praśāntarutasāgaravatī, prostrated at her feet, and circumambulated her countless times before her.
Joining his palms, he spoke these words: "Noble One, I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
I wish to rely upon a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) to learn the bodhisattva conduct, enter the bodhisattva conduct, cultivate the bodhisattva conduct, and abide in the bodhisattva conduct.
I pray that you, out of compassion, will explain for me how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct."
"How is it that when practicing the bodhisattva path, that night goddess said to Sudhana: 'Excellent, excellent, noble son!
You are able to seek the bodhisattva conduct by relying on spiritual friends.
Noble son, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door called "The Vast Array of Great Joy Arising in Every Thought-Moment. Sudhana said: 'O Great Sage, what is this liberation door?'"
"What activities do you perform? What spheres do you traverse? By what means do you act? What observations do you make?
The Night Goddess replied, "Noble son, I have initiated a mind of pure and equal aspiration;

I have initiated a mind of aspiration that is pure, firm, adorned with detachment from all worldly dust and grime, and indestructible; I have initiated an aspiration that does not retreat from its objective."
I resolve to generate a mind that never regresses throughout all stages of rebirth; I resolve to generate an immovable mind that adorns itself with the jewels of merit;
I resolve to generate a mind that dwells nowhere; I resolve to generate a mind that appears before all sentient beings to rescue and protect them;
I resolve to generate a mind that never tires of beholding the ocean of all Buddhas; I resolve to generate a mind that seeks the purity of all Bodhisattvas...
I resolve to arouse the mind of the power of pure vows; I resolve to arouse the mind that abides in the ocean of light of great wisdom;
I resolve to arouse the mind that causes all sentient beings to transcend the wilderness of sorrow and affliction;

I resolve to arouse the mind that causes all sentient beings to abandon grief, lamentation, suffering, and distress; I resolve to arouse the mind that causes all sentient beings to abandon unpleasant forms, sounds, smells, and tastes.

I resolve that my mind shall initiate [the practice of] flavors, tangibles, and mental objects so that all sentient beings may abandon the suffering of separation from the beloved and the suffering of encountering the hated;
I resolve that my mind shall initiate [the practice] so that all sentient beings may abandon the suffering of evil conditions, ignorance, and the like;
I resolve that my mind shall initiate [the practice] to act as a refuge for all sentient beings in perilous difficulties; I resolve that my mind shall initiate [the practice] so that all...
I resolve to cause all sentient beings to abandon the suffering of birth, old age, sickness, and death;
I resolve to cause all sentient beings to achieve the unsurpassed Dharma-joy of the Tathāgata;
I resolve to cause all sentient beings to experience joy and bliss. Having given rise to these thoughts, he further...
I preach the Dharma for them so that they may gradually reach the stage of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-bhūmi*).

That is to say, if I see sentient beings who are attached to the palaces, mansions, and dwellings where they reside, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may realize the self-nature (*svabhāva*) of all phenomena and become free from all attachments.
If I see sentient beings who are fondly attached to their parents, brothers, sisters, and siblings, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain...

I shall join the pure assemblies of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; if I see sentient beings who are attached to wives and children, I will preach the Dharma for them so that they may abandon the defilements of love within birth and death and give rise to great compassion, regarding all sentient beings with equanimity and non-duality.
If I see sentient beings dwelling in royal palaces attended by court ladies and maidservants, I will preach the Dharma for them so that they may...

I attain assembly with the multitude of sages and enter the teaching of the Tathāgata. If I see sentient beings who are stained by and attached to sensory realms, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may enter the realm of the Tathāgata.

If I see sentient beings who are full of anger and hatred, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may abide in the Tathāgata’s perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*). If I see sentient beings whose minds are indolent, I preach the Dharma for them...

I preach the Dharma so that they may attain the perfection of vigor through purification; if I see sentient beings whose minds are distracted, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the Tathāgata’s perfection of dhyāna;

if I see sentient beings who have entered the dense forest of views and are obscured by the darkness of ignorance, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may emerge from that thicket and the darkness; if I see sentient beings who lack...
For those who possess wisdom, I teach the Dharma so that they may attain the Prajñāpāramitā;
if I see sentient beings defiled by and attached to the triple world, I teach the Dharma so that they may transcend birth and death;

if I see sentient beings whose aspirations are inferior, I teach the Dharma so that they may fulfill their vows for the Bodhi of a Buddha; if I see sentient beings dwelling in practices for their own benefit, I teach them...
I preach the Dharma so that they may give rise to the vow to benefit all sentient beings;
if I see sentient beings whose will and strength are feeble, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the Bodhisattva’s perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*);

if I see sentient beings with minds shrouded in the darkness of ignorance, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the Bodhisattva’s perfection of wisdom (*jñāna-pāramitā*); if I see sentient beings [attached to] physical forms...
For those who lack [the conditions for] it, I preach the Dharma so that they may attain the pure physical body of a Tathāgata;
if I see sentient beings with ugly appearances, I preach the Dharma so that they may attain the supreme, pure Dharma-body;

if I see sentient beings with coarse and unrefined physical forms, I preach the Dharma so that they may attain the subtle and wondrous physical body of a Tathāgata; if I see sentient beings whose emotions are excessive...
When I see those afflicted by sorrow and distress, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the ultimate peace and happiness of a Tathāgata.
When I see sentient beings suffering from poverty, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may obtain the precious treasury of a Bodhisattva’s merits.

When I see sentient beings dwelling in gardens and groves, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may diligently seek the causes and conditions of the Buddha-dharma. When I see sentient beings walking along...
On the roads, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may proceed toward the path of omniscience.
If I see sentient beings within villages, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may emerge from the three realms.

If I see sentient beings dwelling among humans, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may transcend the paths of the two vehicles and abide in the stage of the Tathāgata. If I see sentient beings residing...
For those dwelling within the city walls, I preach the Dharma so that they may abide in the city of the Dharma King.
If I see sentient beings dwelling at the four corners, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the wisdom of the equality of the three periods of time.

If I see sentient beings dwelling in the various directions, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may attain the wisdom that perceives all phenomena. If I see sentient beings whose conduct is dominated by greed...
If I see those in whom lustful tendencies are predominant, I teach them the gate of the contemplation of impurity (*aśubha-bhāvanā*) to cause them to abandon their attachment to birth and death.

If I see sentient beings in whom tendencies toward anger are predominant, I teach them the gate of the contemplation of great loving-kindness (*maitrī-bhāvanā*) to cause them to enter it and practice it with diligent application.
If I see sentient beings in whom tendencies toward delusion are predominant, I teach them the Dharma so that they may attain clear wisdom and contemplate all things.
If Dharmasāgara sees sentient beings whose faculties are balanced, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may enter the ocean of vows of the various vehicles.
If I see sentient beings who delight in birth and death, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may cultivate weary detachment.
If I see sentient beings who weary of the suffering of birth and death and are fit to be transformed and delivered by a Tathāgata, I preach the Dharma for them so that they may [attain liberation].

If I see sentient beings who are attached to the five aggregates, I manifest through skillful means the taking of birth and preach the Dharma for them so that they may abide in the realm of non-reliance.
If I see sentient beings whose minds are inferior, I reveal to them the path of supreme adornment.
If I see sentient beings whose minds give rise to arrogance, I preach for them the patience of equality. If I see...
For those sentient beings whose minds are crooked and deceitful, I preach the bodhisattva’s straightforward mind.

Son of good family, by means of these immeasurable gifts of Dharma, I gather in all sentient beings through various skillful means, teaching and taming them so that they may leave the evil realms, enjoy the pleasures of humans and devas, escape the bonds of the triple world, and abide in omniscience. At that time, I immediately attained vast joy.
The ocean of the light of the Dharma gladdens his mind, making it serene, peaceful, and joyful. Furthermore, son of good family,
I have observed that within the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all Bodhisattvas, they cultivate various vows and practices, manifest various pure bodies,
possess various constant radiances, emit various rays of light, and enter the gates of omniscience through various skillful means.
Entering various samādhis, manifesting various supernatural transformations, emitting various oceans of sounds, possessing various adorned bodies,
entering various gates of the Tathāgatas, proceeding to various oceans of lands, beholding various oceans of Buddhas,
attaining various oceans of eloquence, illuminating various realms of liberation, obtaining various oceans of the light of wisdom, and entering various...
They sport in the ocean of various samādhis through various gates of liberation; they proceed toward omniscience by means of various gates;
they adorn the space of the dharma-realm with various ornaments; they pervade space with clouds of various adornments;
they observe the various assemblies at sites of enlightenment; they gather from various worlds; they enter various buddha-fields; and they travel to various directions.
Then, having received various commands from the Tathāgatas, accompanied by various bodhisattvas from the abodes of various Tathāgatas,
raining down clouds of various adornments, entering the various skillful means of the Tathāgatas, observing the various oceans of the Dharma of the Tathāgatas,
entering the various oceans of wisdom, and sitting upon various adorned seats— Good Son, I observe this path.
The assembly, knowing the Buddha’s immeasurable and boundless spiritual power, gave rise to great joy.
"Good son, I observe that in every thought-moment, the Tathāgata Vairocana manifests inconceivable and pure form-bodies;
having seen this, I give rise to great joy. Furthermore, I observe the Tathāgata emitting great radiance in every thought-moment, filling [all space]."
Having seen the Dharma-realm in this way, he gave rise to great joy; furthermore, he saw from each and every pore of the Tathāgata’s body,
in every thought-moment, emerge oceans of light rays as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable Buddha-lands,

each ray of light accompanied by a retinue of light rays as numerous as the atoms within immeasurable Buddha-lands, pervading the entirety of the entire Dharma-realm and extinguishing all [afflictions].
Having seen that all sentient beings are suffering, he gives rise to great joy.

Furthermore, good son, I observe that from the crown of the Tathāgata’s head and his two shoulders, clouds of jewel-flame mountains as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields appear moment by moment, filling all dharma-realms throughout the ten directions; having seen this, he gives rise to great joy. Furthermore, good son—

"Son, as I observe each and every pore of the Tathāgata, from moment to moment there emerge clouds of fragrant light as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, filling all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions; having seen this, I give rise to great joy.
Furthermore, son of good family, as I observe each and every mark of the Tathāgata, from moment to moment there emerge [lights] as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields..."
Having seen the clouds of Tathāgata-bodies adorned with marks as numerous as atoms of dust pervading all worlds throughout the ten directions,
they give rise to great joy. Furthermore, noble son, I observe that from every single pore of the Tathāgata, in every moment of thought,
there emerge clouds of Buddha-transformations as numerous as the atoms of unspeakable Buddha-fields, manifesting the Tathāgata’s emergence.
Having first resolved their minds on enlightenment, they cultivate the *pāramitās* and perfect the path of adornment to enter the stages of a bodhisattva.

Having seen this, they give rise to great joy. Furthermore, son of good family, I observe that from each and every pore of the Tathāgata, in every thought-moment, there emerge clouds of bodies of celestial kings, as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields, as well as the sovereign powers of those celestial kings.
The divine transformations pervade the entire dharma-realm of the ten directions;
to those who are to be liberated by appearing in the form of a celestial king (*devendra*), he manifests that very body and preaches the Dharma. Having seen this, they give rise to great joy.
Just as with the clouds of celestial kings, so too for the dragon kings (*nāgendra*), yakṣa kings, gandharva kings, asura kings, garuḍa kings, and kiṃnara kings...
The clouds of bodies of the kings of the asuras, the kings of the mahoragas, the kings of humans,
and the Brahma kings all emerge from every single pore and preach the Dharma in this manner; having seen this, in every thought-moment I give rise to great joy and great faith and delight,
equal in measure to the dharma-realm and to omniscience (*sarvajñā*), which I had never attained before but have now begun to realize.
That which was previously unattained is now attained; that which was previously unentered is now entered;
that which was previously unfilled is now filled; that which was previously unseen is now seen; that which was previously unheard is now heard. Why is this?
Because they are able to thoroughly understand the characteristics of the *dharmadhātu*, and because they know that all phenomena possess but a single characteristic.
Because they are able to enter the path of the three periods of time with equanimity, and because they are able to expound all infinite dharmas;
good son, I have entered this Bodhisattva liberation-light-ocean of the vast adornment of great joy that arises in every thought-moment.
Furthermore, good son, this liberation is boundless, universally entering the gates of the entire Dharma-realm; therefore, this liberation is inexhaustible.
Because it gives rise to the mind of omniscience, this liberation is boundless;
because it enters into the mental perceptions of all sentient beings throughout the limitless reaches of existence, this liberation is profoundly deep and tranquil, being the object known by wisdom;
because it is vast and pervasive throughout the domain of all Tathāgatas, this liberation is the indestructible eye of bodhisattva-wisdom.
Because it is that which is known by all, this liberation is bottomless; because it exhausts the very source and depths of the Dharma-realm, this liberation is the Universal Gate (*samantamukha*);
because within a single phenomenon one universally perceives all spiritual transformations, this liberation can never be grasped;
because all dharmas are equal and non-dual, this liberation ultimately has no [end].
Because he is able to understand all phenomena as being like illusions, this liberation is like a reflected image;
because it is produced by the light of the vows for omniscience, this liberation is like a magical transformation;
because it consists of the supreme practices of bodhisattvas born through transformation, this liberation is like the great earth, serving as the foundation for all sentient beings.
This liberation is like a great body of water, for it can moisten all things with great compassion;
this liberation is like a great fire, for it dries up the waters of sentient beings' craving and attachment;
this liberation is like a great wind, for it causes all sentient beings to swiftly advance toward omniscience; this liberation is like a great ocean, with its manifold...
Because it adorns all sentient beings with merit, this liberation is like Mount Sumeru;
because it brings forth the ocean of the Dharma-treasure of omniscience, this liberation is like a great city adorned with all sublime dharmas;
because it universally accommodates the spiritual powers of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, this liberation is like empty space.
This liberation is like a great cloud that universally rains down the rain of Dharma for all sentient beings;
this liberation is like the pure sun that can shatter the darkness of ignorance within sentient beings; this liberation is like the full moon that brings fulfillment to the vast ocean of merit;
this liberation is like true suchness (*tathatā*), which is able to pervade all things.
This liberation is like one's own shadow, manifested from one's own virtuous karma;
this liberation is like an echo, preaching the Dharma in accordance with what is appropriate for each;
this liberation is like a reflected image, appearing in accordance with the minds of sentient beings; this liberation is like the flowering of the king of great trees.
This liberation is like a flower of all supernormal powers; this liberation is like a vajra, for it has been indestructible from the very beginning;
this liberation is like a wish-fulfilling jewel, for it gives rise to immeasurable powers of mastery;
this liberation is like a sovereign maṇi-jewel of stainless treasury, for it manifests the divine manifestations of all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.
Because of this power, this liberation is like the *prītidhvaja-maṇi* jewel, which can equally produce the sounds of the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas.
"Good son, I shall now speak this parable for you; you should contemplate it and enter into realization accordingly.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the night goddess Śāntasvararutasāgaravatī, "O Noble One, what [is it]?"
"How does one practice to attain this liberation? The night goddess replied, "Noble son, by practicing ten great treasuries of Dharma, a bodhisattva attains this liberation.
What are these ten? First, they cultivate the great treasury of the vastness of giving, satisfying all sentient beings according to their hearts' desires.
Second, they cultivate the great treasury of the vastness of pure ethical discipline, universally entering into all the merits of the Buddhas."
1. Cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of patience, which is capable of universally contemplating the nature of all phenomena;
2. Cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of diligence, which proceeds toward omniscience and never regresses; 3.

Cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of meditative concentration, which can extinguish the feverish afflictions of all sentient beings; 4. Cultivating the vast Dharma-treasury of wisdom, which can universally comprehend [all things].
7) The vast Dharma-treasury of knowing the ocean of all phenomena, which can universally bring to maturity the ocean of all sentient beings;
8) The vast Dharma-treasury of cultivating various vows, which throughout all Buddha-lands and the ocean of all sentient beings, practices the bodhisattva path until the end of all future kalpas;
9) The vast Dharma-treasury of cultivating various powers, which manifests in every thought-moment within a single [atom].
To manifest perfect enlightenment in all oceans of the dharma-realm and in all buddha-fields without ever ceasing; to cultivate the ten great treasuries of pure wisdom;
and to attain the Tathāgata’s wisdom that universally knows all phenomena of the three periods of time without obstruction.
Noble son, if bodhisattvas abide in these ten great treasuries of dharma, they will be able to attain them.
Having thus explained this liberation— its purification, growth, accumulation, firmness, stability, and perfection— the youth Sudhana said, "Noble One,
how long has it been since you first resolved your mind toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?
The night goddess replied, "Son of good family, to the east of this Flower Bank Array World-Ocean, beyond ten world-oceans, there is..."
The ocean of worlds is named All-Pure Radiance Jewel. Within this ocean of worlds is a world-system named Light-Sound of the Vows of All Tathāgatas.

Within that system is a world named Pure Radiance Golden Adornment, which is composed of all-fragrant diamond-maṇi kings and is shaped like a multi-storied pavilion, with clouds of various exquisite jewels forming its boundaries.
Abiding upon a cloud of exquisite palaces formed from an ocean of all kinds of jewel garlands that overspread it,
within this world-system where the pure and the impure are intermingled, there was in a past age a kalpa named Universal Radiance Banner, a land named Universally Filled Exquisite Treasury,
and a site of enlightenment named All-Jewel Treasury Sublime Moonlight. Therein dwelt a Buddha named Non-Retrogression Sound of the Dharma Realm.
When he attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* here, at that time I was a bodhi-tree deity named Puṇyasaṃpatsamudgata-dhvaja-prabhā,
guarding the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*). Seeing that Buddha attain equal and perfect awakening and manifest his supernormal powers,
I conceived the aspiration for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, right here.
At that time, I attained a samādhi named "Universally Illuminating the Ocean of the Tathāgata’s Merits.
Within this very site of enlightenment, there subsequently appeared a Tathāgata in the world named Dharma-Tree Majestic Virtue Mountain (*Dharmadruma-tejo-giri*).

At that time, having passed away, I was reborn here as the Night Goddess of the site of enlightenment, named Exquisite Light of Merit and Wisdom (*Vicitra-puṇya-jñāna-prabhā*), and I beheld that Tathāgata turning the wheel of the sublime Dharma.
Immediately upon attaining great supernormal powers, I obtained a samādhi named "Universally Illuminating the Realm Free from Greed.
Subsequently, a Tathāgata named Sarvadharma-sāgarasvararāja appeared in the world. At that time, I was a night goddess;
because I was able to see the Buddha, serve him, and make offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi named "The Ground for Growing All Wholesome Dharmas."
Next, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Ratnaprabhā-dhvaja-rāja. At that time, I was a night goddess;
because I was able to see that Buddha and serve and make offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi called "Universal Manifestation of the Cloud of Radiance of Supernatural Powers.
Next, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Guṇa-sumeru-prabha. At that time, I...

At that time, as a night goddess, I was able to see the Buddha, serve him, and make offerings to him, whereby I immediately attained a samādhi named "Universally Illuminating the Ocean of All Buddhas.
Subsequently, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Dharmameghasvararāja;
at that time, as a night goddess, I was able to see that Buddha, serve him, and make offerings to him, whereby I immediately attained a samādhi named "All... [The text here is incomplete].
After the Buddha Dharmasāgarapradīpa, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Jñānapradīpāvabhāsarāja. At that time, I was a night goddess;

because I had the opportunity to see that Buddha, I served and made offerings to him, whereby I immediately attained a samādhi called "Pure Radiant Lamp that Extinguishes the Suffering of All Sentient Beings.
After that, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Dharmavīra.

O Samantaguṇavicitrābhāsa, at that time I was a night goddess; because I was able to see the Buddha and serve and make offerings to him, I immediately attained a samādhi called "The Radiant Treasury of the Tathāgatas of the Three Times. Subsequently, there appeared in the world a Tathāgata named Siṃhavikrāntadharmajñānapradīpa;
at that time I was again a night goddess, and because I was able to see the Buddha and serve...
By making material offerings, I immediately attained the samādhi named "The Wheel of Unobstructed Wisdom of All Worlds.
Subsequently, a Tathāgata named Jñānabalaśailendrarāja appeared in the world. At that time, I was a night goddess;

because I was able to see the Buddha, serve him, and make offerings to him, I immediately attained the samādhi named "Universally Illuminating the Faculties of Sentient Beings Throughout the Three Times."
In the world-system called Pure Radiance Adorned with Gold and the eon called Universal Radiant Banner,
within that realm as numerous as the atoms of a buddha-field, there appeared Tathāgatas such as these. At that time, I was sometimes a king of devas,
sometimes a king of nāgas, sometimes a king of yakṣas, sometimes a king of gandharvas, or sometimes an asura...
He may become a king of the nāgas, or a king of the garuḍas, or a king of the kiṃnaras,
or a king of the mahoragas; he may become a king of men, or a Brahmā king, or a celestial body, or a human body, or the body of a man, or the body of a woman,
or the body of a young boy, or the body of a young girl— manifesting in all these forms through his various seeds.
Having made offerings of all kinds of requisites to all those Tathāgatas and having heard the various dharmas taught by those Buddhas,
he passed away from that life and was immediately reborn in this very world-system. After practicing the bodhisattva conduct for as many eons as there are atoms in a Buddha-field,
he finally passed away and was reborn here in the Sahā world within the Flower Bank Array World-Ocean.
In the past, he encountered the Tathāgata Krakucchanda, whom he served and made offerings to, thereby attaining a samādhi named "Radiance Free from All Dust and Defilement.

Next, he encountered the Tathāgata Kanakamuni, whom he served and made offerings to, thereby attaining a samādhi named "Universally Manifesting the Ocean of All Buddha-lands. Next, he encountered the Tathāgata Kāśyapa, whom he served and made offerings to, thereby attaining... [the samādhi].
I am named "Proclaimer of the Ocean of Speech and Sounds of All Sentient Beings. Next, I encountered the Tathāgata Vairocana, who attained equal and perfect enlightenment at this site of the Way;

in every thought-moment, he manifested great supernormal powers. At that time, upon seeing him, I immediately attained this liberation called "The Constant Arising of Vast Joy and Adornment. Having attained this liberation, I am able to enter ten...

Within an ocean of the established structures of dharma-realms, as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, one beholds all those oceans of the established structures of dharma-realms;
within every single atom of all those Buddha-fields, there are ten times unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-lands, and in each of those Buddha-lands, there are... [Vairocana].
The Tathāgata Vairocana, seated at the site of enlightenment, attains perfect awakening in every moment of thought and manifests various spiritual transformations;
each of these manifested transformations pervades the entire ocean of all dharma-realms.
Furthermore, he perceives his own body in the presence of all those Tathāgatas, hears the sublime Dharma they proclaim, and beholds them all.
From each and every pore of all Buddhas, oceans of emanations emerge, manifesting supernatural powers throughout the ocean of all dharma realms,
the ocean of all world systems, all world-lineages, and within all worlds, turning the wheel of the true Dharma according to the minds of sentient beings;
by means of the power of swift dhāraṇīs, I receive, uphold, contemplate, and reflect upon all their words and meanings.
With the wisdom of clear comprehension, they universally enter the treasury of all pure dharmas; with the wisdom of mastery, they universally traverse the ocean of all profound dharmas;
with the wisdom of pervasiveness, they universally know the vast meanings of the three periods of time;
with the wisdom of equality, they universally penetrate the non-differentiated dharmas of all Buddhas—thus awakening to and understanding every dharma-gate within each and every dharma-gate.
He awakens to and understands every cloud of sūtras; within each cloud of sūtras, he awakens to and understands every ocean of dharmas;
within each ocean of dharmas, he awakens to and understands every category of dharmas; within each category of dharmas, he awakens to and understands every cloud of dharmas;
within each cloud of dharmas, he awakens to and understands every stream of dharmas; and from within each stream of dharmas, they emerge.
One gives birth to an ocean of all great joys; each and every ocean of great joy gives birth to an ocean of all stages;
each and every stage gives birth to an ocean of all samādhis; each and every ocean of samādhis attains an ocean of all visions of Buddhas;

each and every ocean of visions of Buddhas attains an ocean of all lights of wisdom; each and every ocean of lights of wisdom universally illumines the three periods of time and penetrates everywhere throughout the ten directions.
Only then did he come to know the ocean of all past practices of the infinite Tathāgatas; he came to know the ocean of all the former life-stories of the infinite Tathāgatas;
he came to know the ocean of the difficult renunciations and acts of giving of the infinite Tathāgatas; he came to know the ocean of the pure wheels of ethical discipline of the infinite Tathāgatas;
he came to know the ocean of the pure patience of the infinite Tathāgatas; and he came to know the vast ocean of the diligence of the infinite Tathāgatas.
Sāgara knows the immeasurable ocean of the Tathāgatas’ profound meditative concentration; he knows the immeasurable ocean of the Tathāgatas’ prajñāpāramitā;
he knows the immeasurable ocean of the Tathāgatas’ upāyakauśalyapāramitā; he knows the immeasurable ocean of the Tathāgatas’ praṇidhānapāramitā;
he knows the immeasurable ocean of the Tathāgatas’ balapāramitā; and he knows the immeasurable ocean of the Tathāgatas’ jñāna.
He knows the ocean of *pāramitās* of immeasurable Tathāgatas; he knows how immeasurable Tathāgatas in the past transcended the bodhisattva stages;
he knows how immeasurable Tathāgatas in the past dwelt in the bodhisattva stages for oceans of immeasurable eons, manifesting supernormal powers;

he knows how immeasurable Tathāgatas in the past entered the bodhisattva stages; he knows how immeasurable Tathāgatas in the past cultivated the bodhisattva stages; he knows immeasurable Tathāgatas...
In the past, while cultivating the bodhisattva stages, Infinite Tathāgata knew that in the past he had observed the bodhisattva stages;
Infinite Tathāgata knew that in the past, when he was a bodhisattva, he constantly beheld all Buddhas;

Infinite Tathāgata knew that in the past, when he was a bodhisattva, he fully beheld oceans of Buddhas and oceans of eons, dwelling together with them; Infinite Tathāgata [knew] that in the past, when he was a bodhisattva, by means of...
They know that the immeasurable bodies [of the Buddhas] are born pervading the ocean of lands;
they know that when the immeasurable Tathāgatas were formerly Bodhisattvas, they cultivated vast and great practices throughout the entire Dharma-realm;

they know that when the immeasurable Tathāgatas were formerly Bodhisattvas, they manifested various gates of skillful means to discipline and bring all sentient beings to maturity; and they know that the immeasurable Tathāgatas emit great rays of light.
Universally illuminating all oceans of lands in the ten directions, they know the immeasurable Tathāgatas manifesting great supernormal powers and appearing before all sentient beings;
they know the immeasurable Tathāgatas’ ground of vast wisdom; they know the immeasurable Tathāgatas turning the wheel of the true Dharma;
they know the immeasurable Tathāgatas manifesting oceans of marks; and they know the immeasurable Tathāgatas manifesting their bodies.
The Ocean-Knowledge One knows the ocean of the immeasurable great powers of the Tathāgatas;
from their first generation of the mind until the extinction of the Dharma, I have known and seen them all in every moment of thought.
Noble son, as to what you asked me, "How long has it been since you first generated the mind?"—Noble son, in the past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in two Buddha-fields...
As previously described, while in the world-system Adorned with Pure Radiant Gold,
she heard the Tathāgata Non-regressive Sound of the Dharma-realm preaching the Dharma as a bodhi-tree deity;

she then resolved her mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva for as many eons as there are atoms in two buddha-fields, after which she was born here in this Sahā world.

"In all realms and throughout all kalpas, all future Buddhas shall likewise be approached and served in this manner, O son of good family.
That world, Pure Light Adorned with Gold, still exists today, and the appearance of Buddhas therein continues without interruption.
You should single-mindedly cultivate this gate of the Bodhisattva’s great valor. At that time, [the World-Honored One] was silent.
The Night Goddess Śāntasvararājā, wishing to restate the meaning of this liberation for the sake of the youth Sudhana, spoke these verses:
"Sudhana, listen as I speak of this gate of pure liberation; having heard it, give rise to joy."
Diligently practice until reaching the ultimate goal. In the past, throughout oceans of eons, I gave rise to a heart of great faith and joy, pure as space;

I constantly contemplated all-knowledge. Toward the Buddhas of the three periods of time, I have given rise to a heart of faith and joy, as well as toward their assemblies; I vow to always draw near to them all.
In the past, I saw the Buddha making offerings for the sake of sentient beings; Having heard the pure Dharma, my heart was filled with great joy.
Always honoring and respecting my parents, I venerated and made offerings to them without ceasing.
Thus entering this gate of liberation, I [saw] those who were old, sick, and impoverished.
All those with impaired faculties, I compassionately deliver; may they attain peace and security.

From water, fire, kings, and thieves, and from all terrors within the sea—having practiced various deeds in the past to rescue those sentient beings—I now see them with afflictions constantly blazing and shrouded by the obstructions of karma.
Falling into various perilous paths, I shall rescue those sentient beings;
all the immeasurable pains of agony in every evil destiny, such as birth, old age, sickness, and death—I shall utterly extinguish them all.
May it continue through all future kalpas, universally for the sake of all living beings, to eliminate the suffering of saṃsāra.
"O son of good family, I have attained the ultimate bliss of Buddhahood; I know only this liberation called 'The Constant Arising of the Vast Adornment of Great Joy.
As for the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, they enter deeply into the ocean of all dharma-realms and fully know the number of all kalpas."
"O son of good family, as for seeing the formation and destruction of all lands, how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
Here in this assembly of the Tathāgata at the site of enlightenment, there is a night goddess named Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥprabhā.
Go to her and ask: 'How should a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?'"
Then the youth Sudhana, with single-minded attention, observed the body of the Night Goddess Śāntamati-svara-sāgara and spoke these verses:
"Following the instruction of my spiritual friend, I have come to the abode of the Night Goddess; I behold the Goddess seated upon her jewel throne."
The dimensions of the body are boundless; it is not something that can be grasped through physical characteristics.
How could those of inferior wisdom and shallow understanding, who reckon all phenomena to be finite, know the realm of the Honored One?
Even if gods and humans of the world were to observe for immeasurable eons, they would still be unable to fathom it, for its physical characteristics are without limit.
Distant from the five aggregates and not abiding in the sense bases, having forever severed worldly doubt, you manifest the power of mastery;
Without grasping at internal or external phenomena, with an unshakable and unobstructed eye of pure wisdom, you behold the Buddha’s supernormal powers; Your body is the treasury of the True Dharma.
The mind is unimpeded wisdom; having attained the illumination of this wisdom, it further illuminates the minds of all sentient beings.

Accumulating boundless karma, it adorns all worlds. Realizing that the world is entirely the manifestation of the mind appearing as sentient beings, one knows that the world is like a dream and that all Buddhas are like reflections.
All phenomena are like echoes, causing the multitude to have no attachments;
for the sake of sentient beings of the three periods of time, they manifest bodies in every thought-moment, yet their minds dwell nowhere.
Throughout the ten directions, they preach the Dharma everywhere across boundless oceans of lands, oceans of Buddhas, and oceans of sentient beings—all of which are contained within a single atom.
When the Honored One had thus explained the power of liberation,
Sudhana the youth prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, gazed upon him with earnest devotion,
and then took his leave and departed.

[is the second section].
From the passage "The night goddess Ghoṣasamudrā... down to "...how does one cultivate the bodhisattva path? there are five lines of sūtra clarifying Sudhana’s presentation of his own quest;
this section is divided into three parts. From the passage where that night goddess spoke to Sudhana...
down to the "Vast Joyous Adornment Liberation Gate," there are two and a half lines of sūtra clarifying how the night goddess [instructed] Sudhana.
The section on explaining the dharma-gate of one’s own practice is divided into four parts. First, Sudhana says:
"O Great Sage, what is the activity of this liberation gate? and so on, down to where it says, "I shall explain for you" (T. 310, p. 728a).

This includes sixty-five lines of scripture clarifying the activities and skillful means practiced by the Night Goddess as she instructs Sudhana in this dharma-gate. The section on the activities and skillful means is divided into five parts.
"Good man, having bestowed these immeasurable Dharma-gifts upon you, down to causing immeasurable and boundless beings to give rise to great joy—seventeen lines and a half of the sūtra clarify this.
Then the Night Goddess answered the previous question asked by Sudhana regarding 'the sphere of activity,' which is divided into six parts.
Good man, I observe the Tathāgata Vairocana... [down to] "...able to..."
Because it explains all infinite dharmas, there are thirty-two chapters of sutras that answer the previous inquiry regarding what is observed. [The Buddha said:

"Good sons, from the point where I entered this Bodhisattva liberation-light-ocean of the vast and great joy-adornment produced in every thought-moment, down to 'you should contemplate and accordingly awaken into it,' [this constitutes the seventh excellence]."
There are thirty-three and a half lines of scripture that answer the previous question asked by Sudhana regarding the "sphere of activity," divided into eight sections.
At that time, from the passage where the youth Sudhana addressed the night goddess Śāntamati-svara-sāgara up to the passage ending with "increasing,
accumulating, firm, securely established, and perfected," there are seventeen lines of scripture that answer Sudhana’s question as to how [one should practice].
Regarding the section on practicing this Dharma-gate through the ten pāramitās, Sudhana the youth said:
"O Noble One, how long has it been since you first resolved upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?
[The text continues] down to the fifty-four lines beginning with: "In every thought-moment, one gives birth to the liberation of the vast adornment of great joy."
The latter half of the sūtra answers Sudhana’s questions regarding how long it has been since he first resolved upon great bodhicitta;
it explains how, having attained this liberation in ten stages, he is able to enter ten unspeakable [kalpas],
and so on down to the fifty-eight lines of verse where the goddess Śāntamati-samudra herself describes her own practice— how this practice gives rise to vastness in every thought-moment.

Having attained the liberation "Adorned with Great Joy," she has entered this Dharma-door, made offerings to the Buddhas of the three periods of time, and resolved her mind [upon enlightenment] in worlds that still exist today. This section indicates that the essence of meditative concentration is immutable throughout time;
thus, at all times, it is universally so. Below this, there are ten verses in which the night goddess explains her own past conduct and exhorts [others].
The practice of Sudhana is self-evident from the text itself. "Good son, I only know this liberation of the 'Moment-to-Moment Arising of the Vast Adornment of Great Joy'";
the following passage, which involves deferring one's own virtues and progressing upward, explains the meaning according to the text:
"The liberation of the moment-to-moment arising of the vast adornment of great joy" clarifies that the delight of dhyāna is all-pervasive and benefits sentient beings.
She establishes her name by means of the vast practice of her original vows; the mutual adornment of principle and practice constitutes her "Adornment.
The Night Goddess is named *Śāntasvaranirghoṣasāgara* (Ocean of the Sound of Tranquility): she is called "Tranquil" because the nature of reality (*dharmatā*) is unconditioned (*asaṃskṛta*);

she is called "Ocean of Sound" because her vocal resonance benefits all sentient beings equally. This clarifies that sound itself is the essence and function of meditative concentration (*samādhi*), just as in the case of [the Bodhisattva] Śubhavyūha.
When the Night Goddess Dhana asked how long it had been since she first resolved her mind [on enlightenment], the Night Goddess replied:
"To the east of this Flower Treasury World-Ocean, passing through ten world-oceans, there is a world-ocean named Sarva-vimala-prabhā-ratna... (omitting intermediate text)...
thereafter, at the end of her life, she was born here in the Sahā world within this Flower Treasury Adorned World-Ocean. (Section 46)
The practice described in the latter half of the chapter concerns the offerings made by the Night Goddess Vidyutprabhā to ten Buddhas who appeared in succession;

for each Buddha, she served and made offerings with her own body, as well as receiving the Dharma from them. This constitutes the specific practice performed in response to Sudhana’s inquiry regarding the duration since his initial resolve.
If one were to represent this through the *dharmamukha* (gateways of the Dharma), it corresponds to the sequence of practicing the ten stages (*bhūmi*) within the context of a single stage.
Born in the Sahā world, having first beheld three Buddhas and subsequently beholding the Tathāgata Vairocana,
one attains this liberation of "the Great Joy-Adornment Arising Moment by Moment. This is the dharma-gate of entering the first stage through the tenth and eleventh stages,
wherein one receives the seal of the wisdom of the three periods of time and serves all Buddhas of the three periods of time.

All hear the Dharma as clearly elucidated in the sutras to manifest the essence of dhyāna, which universally encompasses the three periods of time and, in a single thought-moment, universally seals all dharmas without past, future, or present;
this is the answer to Sudhana’s question regarding the duration since he first resolved upon bodhicitta.

As for the passage concerning the ten Buddhas after whom he makes offerings to as many Buddhas as there are atoms in a buddha-field, this symbolizes the seal of wisdom (*jñānamudrā*) following the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*).

Pervading universally within a single atom, one encompasses many Buddha-fields; by dwelling within many Buddha-fields within a single atom, because of the non-obstruction of wisdom and the absence of interior or exterior, one is equal to the wisdom of all Buddhas and identical to the minds of all sentient beings.

This is discussed in terms of the essence and function of the dharma-realm meditative concentration (*dhyāna*). It is said that to the east of the Flower Treasury World (*Huazang Shijie*), one passes through ten worlds.
The "ocean" symbolizes the advancement through the ten stages (*bhūmi*); the "east" signifies the illumination of the initial beginning.
There is a world-ocean named *Sarva-vimala-prabhā-ratna* (All-Pure-Light-Jewel), which symbolizes that the essence of dhyāna in the fifth stage pervades all positions.
Within it, there is a world-lineage named *Sarva-tathāgata-praṇidhāna-raśmi-ghoṣa* (Light-Sound of the Vows of All Tathāgatas), which represents this very fifth stage.
Within the stages (*bhūmi*), on the first, the Stage of Joy (*pramuditā-bhūmi*), one gives rise to ten indestructible minds as the seeds of the world;

therefore, this clarifies that the great wisdom and compassion of the *dharmadhātu* serve as the seeds. Because the mind is generated on the first stage by relying upon the supreme vows of the Buddhas of the ten directions, it is called "The Radiant Sound of the Tathāgata’s Vows.
Furthermore, as the ancient masters have said, [it is so called] because of the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world...

When the number of realms reaches as many as the sands of the Ganges, it is called one world-ocean. When the number of these world-oceans reaches as many as the sands of the Ganges, it is called one world-nature (*dhātu*).
When the number of these world-natures reaches as many as the sands of the Ganges, it is called one world-lineage (*gotra*).

Within this, there is a world named Pure Light Golden Adornment; regarding the essence of dhyāna, it universally encompasses everything up to the adamantine wisdom (*vajrajñāna*), including all fragrant golds.

That which has the Vajra-maṇi King as its essence takes as its substance the nature of the vajra-wisdom of precepts, concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation—perfumed by incense and inherently stainless.
These constitute the essence for ascending through the five stages and ten grounds. The term "King" symbolizes the sovereignty of wisdom.
Its form being like a multi-storied pavilion signifies that the wisdom of the ten grounds is layered upon layer.
It is bounded by clouds of various wonderful jewels adorned with the infinite dharmas of knowledge, vision, compassion, joy,
and equanimity; it is formed by great clouds of compassionate vows and abides upon an ocean of all jewel-garlands,
having established the wondrous cloud-palaces of the ten stages in their proper sequence through an ocean of garlands of the ten thousand practices.
That which covers its summit is the Palace of Wisdom and the Vast Sanctuary of Compassion, which encompasses and shelters all sentient beings dwelling amidst the intermingling of purity and impurity.
It clarifies the gate of the Great Samādhi of the Dharma-realm, wherein wisdom and compassion advance in equal measure;

thus, the Buddha-land and the realm of sentient beings are not obstructed in their shared essence. This nature contains all within it without interior or exterior, viewing purity and impurity as equal within this world-system.
In ages long past, there was an eon named Universal Light Banner (*Samantābhāsa-dhvaja*), which symbolizes the fundamental wisdom of universal radiance (*samantābhāsa-jñāna*).
Its land was named Universal Fulfillment (*Samantapūrṇa*). "Wondrous Treasury" (*Miaozang*) symbolizes that the wisdom of universal radiance is equally shared by all sentient beings;

it is termed a "treasury. The name of the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) was "Treasury of All Jewels. "Wondrous Moon Radiance" (*Miaoyue Guangming*) symbolizes the fifth stage (*pañcamī-bhūmi*).
The meditation on intrinsic purity is the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), for it can manifest the treasury of wisdom from which all things emerge.

There is a Buddha named Non-retrogressive Sound of the Dharma-realm who, having attained this aforementioned dharma-gate of the site of enlightenment through skillful means to remedy delusions, immediately attains the non-retrogressive sound of turning the wheel of the Dharma within the Dharma-realm; therefore, [it is called] "therein."
One who attains *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* does so through the aforementioned dharma; when the delusions regarding dharmas vanish, that itself is bodhi.
There is no separate process of formation or destruction. At that time, I was a Bodhi-tree deity named *Puṇyasaṃpatsamudgata-prabhā-dhvaja*;
as a deity, I manifested the wondrous wisdom of bodhi, which expresses the principle of the absence of intrinsic nature (*niḥsvabhāva*).
Wisdom gives rise to immeasurable compassion; the myriad practices form its tree. Among these myriad practices, the retribution of virtue and merit is called the fulfillment of merit and virtue.
Through wisdom, one can constantly illuminate the faculties and gather them into transformation; this is named the "lamp-lighting wisdom.
This wisdom is eternally without substance and cannot be shaken; it can constantly destroy the afflictions of all sentient beings, serving as a banner to protect the Path.
The term "site" (*bodhimaṇḍa*) clarifies that the essential nature of this fifth stage is immovable; it carries the meaning of "guarding" and is also the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
Because meditative concentration (*samādhi*) can give rise to wisdom and eliminate delusions, the guarding of the site of enlightenment is entirely contained therein.
From this point onward, there is general worship of the ten Buddhas, as well as rebirth in the Sahā world to worship the four Buddhas and...
The General Table for Entering the Dharma: The Eleven Stages of Ascension. One should personally observe the sequential correspondence [of these stages] as their essential framework.
From here, the first Buddha is assigned to the first stage (*bhūmi*), the second to the second stage, and the third to the third stage.
The bodies produced therein are the practices according to each respective stage; the Buddhas to whom offerings are made are the fruits within those practices. May it be so established.

Even within the context of making vows, one does not deviate from this symbolic dharma. If one wishes to see other Buddhas, yet one's wisdom does not reach this Dharma-gate, then because one's practice is inconsistent with it, there is no way to attain correspondence and thus see those Buddhas.

For example, those who make offerings to ten Buddhas or to as many Buddhas as there are atoms in a Buddha-field are characterized by the culmination of the fruit of the tenth stage; this is what is perceived by the eye of wisdom.
Observing this clarifies that within the general characteristics of the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) contained in the meditative essence of the fifth stage,
the subsequent birth in the Sahā world to make offerings to the four Buddhas clarifies the fruits of the first, second, third, and fourth stages prior to the fifth;
whereas making offerings simultaneously to all Buddhas of all worlds throughout the three periods of time clarifies the tenth [stage] within this fifth stage.

The wisdom of the first stage is perfected and the conduct of Samantabhadra is fulfilled; the seal of wisdom shows that the three periods of time—past, present, and future—are all one and the same limit, for there is no distinction between times.

In reality, it is thus, being without falsehood. It also clarifies that within the essential nature of the meditative body and the principle-wisdom of this stage, the three periods of time are universally and entirely of one nature; the Buddhas of the three periods of time are, at once, non-existent.
From the perspective of the ultimate reality (*tattva*), based on the definitive essence of the Dharma-body and the realm of wisdom, it is indeed real;

however, from the standpoint of deluded sentiment, it cannot be seen. This is the stage of Difficult to Conquer (*Sudurjaya*), where the perfection of meditation (*dhyāna-pāramitā*) is primary and the other nine perfections are its companions.
Its purpose is to remedy the obstacle of the lack of mastery over quiescence and activity, thereby enabling the attainment of self-mastery; such is the nature of this stage.

It is named "Difficult to Conquer" because on this stage, one skillfully studies worldly knowledge, the five sciences (*pañcavidyāsthāna*), and all worldly arts within meditative concentration (*dhyāna*),
knowing them all through the application of effort and the power of samādhi. Just as the sixth stage enters the gate of great function and prajñā that is profound stillness,
so too is it like the sixth dwelling among the ten dwellings, namely the bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja.
This entry into the samādhi of cessation, wherein one is free from inhalation and exhalation, manifests transformation bodies like clouds and establishes teachings like the ocean.
Second, regarding the advancement through the promotion of virtues, from the passage "As for those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas...

down to "taking their leave and departing," including the verses, there are eighteen lines of scripture which are established according to five gates: first, the advancement through the promotion of virtues; second, the demonstration... [text truncated].
1. Wherever the spiritual friend may be, it is said to be here within this assembly of the Tathāgata at the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*);
for the third time, the name of the deity is mentioned as the protector of all cities who increases majestic power. 2. Sudhana speaks in verse to praise the virtues of Śāntamukhasāgaravatī.
3. He pays homage and departs; [the following] explains the meaning according to the text: within this site of enlightenment, the Tathāgata...

Those present in the assembly signify that they do not depart from the essence of *tathatā* (suchness), which is the bodhicitta; because they exist within this great ocean-like assembly, there are night goddesses (*rātridevatā*).

This clarifies that the nature of bodhi is the subtle principle within *tathatā*, and their wisdom serves as the "divine" (*devatā*) power capable of shattering the ignorance and attachments of all sentient beings.
As the presiding night goddesses, they constantly initiate [the practice] without departing from the great night of birth and death (*saṃsāra*).

Because the great illumination (*mahāvidyā*) of all sentient beings arises, "protecting all cities" and "increasing power" symbolize the constant protection of the city of the minds of all sentient beings;
it increases the wisdom-power within the sixth stage and for all sentient beings, causing the three emptinesses (*trīṇi śūnyatāni*) to manifest before one,
and [attaining] the power of the meditative concentration of tranquil extinction (*śamatha-samādhi*), both mundane and supramundane.
The power of wisdom fully manifesting before one forever transcends the ocean of birth and death; dwelling eternally in the world, one attains the power of the ocean of all supramundane wisdom.

As detailed below in the text, it is as when Sudhana praised the goddess Śāntamati-sāgaravatī with ten verses, stating that the infinite oceans of Buddhas with bodies of the Dharma-realm and the ocean of sentient beings are all contained within a single atom.
Regarding the power of liberation of this Honored One within the fifth ground:
because the nature of the *dharmakāya*—the essence of dhyāna—is boundless and lacks the dimensions of large or small, it is like water, a mirror, or the sky;

these dry substrates universally contain all forms, which appear therein without mutual obstruction. By sealing them with the power of meditative concentration (*samādhi*), they manifest spontaneously. The rest is self-evident from the verses.
