The Sūtra translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a Śramaṇa from Khotan during the Tang Dynasty;
the Commentary composed by Li Tongxuan, a Lay Elder of Fangshan in Taiyuan during the Tang Dynasty.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhining of Kaiyuan Temple in Fuzhou during the Tang Dynasty, combining the sutras and commentaries, Chapter Thirty-nine, Part Twenty-one: The Entry into the Dharma Realm.

[Commentary] The sixth assembly of the Tathāgata features the presiding deity of the "Growth of All Cities" (*Sarvanagararakṣāvivardhana*), who presides over the Stage of Presence (*Abhimukhī-bhūmi*).
[Sūtra] At that time, the youth Sudhana, following the instructions of the night goddess Silent Sound Ocean, contemplated and examined the dharma-gate she had taught;

he did not forget a single word or phrase. His immeasurable profound mind, his immeasurable nature of phenomena, all skillful means, spiritual powers, wisdom, mindfulness, and discernment continued in an uninterrupted succession, and his mind became vast.
She saw that night goddess, Great Entry into Peaceful Abiding Who Protects All Cities,
seated upon a lion throne of mani-jewel kings radiating all precious lights, surrounded by countless night goddesses;
she manifested a body appearing in the forms of all sentient beings, a body universally facing all sentient beings, and a body unsoiled by anything.

The manifestation of bodies equal in number to all sentient beings throughout all worlds; the manifestation of bodies that transcend all worldly bodies; the manifestation of bodies that bring all sentient beings to maturity;
the manifestation of bodies that swiftly travel to all ten directions; the manifestation of bodies that universally encompass all ten directions;
the manifestation of the ultimate body of the Tathāgata’s essence; and the manifestation of the ultimate body for the subduing of sentient beings.
Having seen him, Sudhana was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; he prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and standing before him with palms joined, spoke these words:

"O Noble One, I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva, while practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, benefits sentient beings, nor how [he does so] by means of..."
"By what means do you gather and sustain sentient beings? How do you accord with the teachings of all Buddhas? How do you draw near to the station of the Dharma King?
I pray that, out of compassion, you will explain this to me. Then, that night goddess addressed Sudhana, saying:
"Noble son, it is for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings; it is for the sake of adorning and purifying all Buddha-fields; it is for the sake of making offerings to one..."
Because you wish to serve all Tathāgatas; because you wish to abide for all eons to rescue sentient beings; because you wish to protect the lineage of all Buddhas;
because you wish to universally enter the ten directions and cultivate all practices; because you wish to universally enter the ocean of all dharma-gates;
because you wish to pervade all things with a mind of equanimity; because you wish to universally enter all [realms].

"Because you wish to universally accord with the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings by raining down the rain of Dharma for the sake of the Buddha's wheel of Dharma, you ask about the gates of practice cultivated by the bodhisattvas.
Good son, I have attained the Bodhisattva liberation of Profound and Sovereign Sublime Sound;
as a great Dharma teacher, I am without obstruction and am well able to reveal the Dharma-treasury of all Buddhas."
Possessing the power of great vows and great compassion, they cause all sentient beings to abide in the bodhicitta;

because they perform all manner of deeds for the benefit of sentient beings and accumulate roots of goodness without ceasing, they serve as teachers and guides for all sentient beings, leading them to abide in the path of *sarvajñā* (omniscience); thus, they are [the refuge] for all the world.
Because the sun of the pure Dharma shines universally upon the world to cause the roots of goodness to arise;
because his mind is impartial toward all worlds to cause all sentient beings to increase in wholesome dharmas;
because his mind is pure regarding all sensory objects to eliminate all unwholesome karma; he vows to benefit all sentient beings, his body constantly manifesting everywhere.
In all lands, they manifest all manner of past events and causal conditions so that all sentient beings may abide in virtuous conduct;
they constantly serve all spiritual friends so that sentient beings may abide in the Buddha’s teaching.
O Son of the Buddha, by means of these dharmas, I bestow them as gifts upon sentient beings, causing them to give rise to pure qualities (*śukladharma*) and seek omniscience with a firm mind.
I am indeed like the Vajra-Nārāyaṇa-treasury, well able to discern the powers of the Buddha and the powers of Māra;
I always remain in close proximity to spiritual friends, shatter the mountain-like obstructions of all karma and delusions, and gather the dharmas that assist the path to omniscience.
My mind never abandons the ground of omniscience. O son of noble family, by means of such pure dharma-light, I...
When gathering the roots of goodness and the factors conducive to the path for the benefit of all sentient beings, one performs ten kinds of observations regarding the dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*).
What are these ten? They are as follows: 1. I know that the dharma-realm is immeasurable, because I have attained the vast light of great wisdom; 2.
I know that the dharma-realm is boundless, because I see all that is known and seen by all Buddhas; 3. I know that the dharma-realm is limitless...
Because I universally enter all Buddha-lands to reverently make offerings to all Tathāgatas, I know that the Dharma-realm is without boundaries;
because I manifest the practice of bodhisattva conduct throughout the entire ocean of the Dharma-realm, I know that the Dharma-realm is uninterrupted;
because I enter the uninterrupted wisdom of the Tathāgata, I know that the Dharma-realm is of a single nature. Thus, [I know] the Tathāgata...
I know the nature of the dharma-realm because there is not a single sentient being who does not understand it through a single sound;
I know the nature of the dharma-realm because I have realized its purity and fulfilled the Tathāgata’s vow to universally deliver all sentient beings;

I know the nature of the dharma-realm because the sublime practices of Samantabhadra pervade all sentient beings everywhere; I know the nature of the dharma-realm because the sublime practices of Samantabhadra universally adorn it as a single ornament.
Because the indestructible realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) is filled with the roots of goodness of all-knowledge, and because it is indestructible, O son of good family,

I perform these ten kinds of observations of the realm of phenomena to gather all roots of goodness, to accomplish the factors conducive to the path, to understand the vast majesty and power of all Buddhas,
and to enter deeply into the inconceivable sphere of the Tathāgatas. Furthermore, O son of good family, I— like...
Through this right mindfulness and reflection, one attains the ten kinds of great majestic power *dhāraṇī*-wheels of the Tathāgata.
What are these ten? They are: the *dhāraṇī*-wheel of universal entry into all phenomena; the *dhāraṇī*-wheel of universal upholding of all phenomena;
the *dhāraṇī*-wheel of universal exposition of all phenomena; and the *dhāraṇī*-wheel of universally recollecting all Buddhas of the ten directions.
The Dharani-wheel that Universally Proclaims the Names of All Buddhas; the Dharani-wheel that Universally Enters the Ocean of Vows of All Buddhas of the Three Times;
the Dharani-wheel that Universally Enters the Ocean of All Vehicles; the Dharani-wheel that Universally Enters the Ocean of Karmic Actions of All Sentient Beings;
the Dharani-wheel that Swiftly Revolves All Karma; and the Dharani-wheel that Swiftly Produces All...
"O son of good family, this wheel of the *jñāna-dhāraṇī* has ten thousand wheels of *dhāraṇī* as its retinue,
and it constantly expounds the sublime Dharma for the sake of sentient beings. Son of good family, I may expound the Dharma of the wisdom of hearing for some sentient beings,
or the Dharma of the wisdom of reflection for others, or the Dharma of the wisdom of cultivation for others."
The Dharma may be taught to sentient beings as the existence of one thing, or it may be taught as the existence of all things;
it may be taught as the ocean of names of one Tathāgata, or as the ocean of names of all Tathāgatas;
it may be taught as the ocean of one world-system, or as the ocean of all world-systems; or it may be taught as the empowerment of one Buddha.
He may preach the Dharma of the ocean of prophecies; or he may preach the Dharma of the ocean of prophecies bestowed by all Buddhas;

or he may preach the Dharma of the ocean of the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of a single Tathāgata; or he may preach the Dharma of the ocean of the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Tathāgatas;
or he may preach the Dharma of the ocean of the wheel of Dharma of a single Tathāgata; or he may preach the Dharma of the ocean of the wheels of Dharma of all Tathāgatas; or...
For some he taught the Dharma of a single Tathāgata-sūtra, or for others he taught the Dharma of all Tathāgata-sūtras;
for some he taught the Dharma of a single Tathāgata-assembly, or for others he taught the Dharma of all Tathāgata-assemblies;
for some he taught the Dharma of the ocean of the mind of a single *sarvajñatā*, or for others he taught the Dharma of the ocean of the minds of all *sarvajñatās*.
To some I teach the Dharma of liberation through the Single Vehicle; to others I teach the Dharma of liberation through all vehicles.
Noble son, by means of such inconceivable Dharma-gates as these, I teach for the sake of sentient beings.

Noble son, I enter the ocean-like gateway of the Tathāgata’s non-differentiated Dharma-realm and preach the unsurpassed Dharma, universally gathering in all sentient beings throughout all future eons.

"O son of good family who abides in the conduct of Samantabhadra, I have attained this profound liberation of sovereign and wondrous sound, which in every thought-moment increases all gates of liberation and in every thought-moment fills the entire Dharma-realm.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the Night Goddess: "How marvelous, O goddess! This gate of liberation is so exceedingly rare."
The Night Goddess said, "Noble son, it has been a long time since the Noble One attained this realization.

In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a world-system, there was an eon named Stainless Radiance and a world named Dharma-realm Cloud of Merit, which had as its substance an ocean of mani-jewel kings manifesting the karma of all sentient beings; it was shaped like a lotus and rested upon it."
Within nets of fragrant maṇi Sumeru mountains as numerous as the atoms in the four continents,
there were lotus flowers emerging from the fundamental vows of all Tathāgatas to serve as adornments; these were accompanied by retinues of lotus flowers as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru,
interspersed with fragrant maṇis as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, and contained within [palaces] as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru.
In each of the four continents of the world-system, there are hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of unspeakably unspeakable cities.
Noble son, in that world-system, there is a set of four continents called *Sudarśanadhvaja*.
Within it is a royal capital named *Samantaratnakusumaprabhā*. Not far from here is a site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) called *Samantavyūhadharmanirbhāsa*.
Within that royal palace, as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru appeared;
the first of those Buddhas was named Dharma-Sea Thunder-Sound Radiance King.

When that Buddha appeared, there was a wheel-turning king named Pure Sun Radiance Face, who, under that Buddha, upheld the *Sūtra of the Whirlpool of the Entire Ocean of Dharmas*. After that Buddha entered parinirvāṇa...
When that king left the household life to protect and uphold the True Dharma at a time when the Dharma was about to perish, there were a thousand different sects and a thousand kinds of teachings.
Approaching the final kalpa, the karmic afflictions and obstacles became heavy; many wicked bhikṣus engaged in much strife and contention, delighting in sense objects rather than seeking merit.
They took pleasure in discoursing on kings, bandits, women, nations, and the ocean, as well as on [the self].
At that time, the Bhikṣu Kālarāja addressed those who were engaged in all manner of worldly discourse, saying: "How strange! How tragic!
The Buddha, throughout an ocean of immeasurable great kalpas, has gathered this torch of the Dharma; how can you all together seek to destroy it?
Having spoken these words, he ascended into the air to a height of seven *tāla* trees, and from his body issued forth immeasurable clouds of flames of various colors, emitting manifold...
A great net of light of various colors caused immeasurable sentient beings to eliminate the heat of their afflictions and caused immeasurable sentient beings to resolve upon bodhicitta;
by these causes and conditions, the teaching of that Tathāgata flourished once again for sixty-five thousand years.
At that time, there was a bhikṣuṇī named Dharmacakrapravartin-prabhā, who was this king’s daughter and had [served] hundreds of thousands [of teachers].
The bhikṣuṇī, who was her attendant, upon hearing the words of her father, the king, and witnessing his supernormal powers, gave rise to the bodhicitta and never again regressed.
She attained a samādhi named "Lamp of All Buddha Teachings" and also attained this profound liberation of "Majestic and Wondrous Sound.
Having attained it, her body and mind became supple and pliant, and she immediately beheld the Tathāgata Dharma-Ocean Thunder-Voice Radiance King.

"Good son, what do you think? As for that Universal Monarch who, following the Tathāgata, turned the wheel of the true Dharma and caused the Final Dharma to flourish after the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa—was he someone else?
He was none other than the present Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. That Bhikṣuṇī Dharmacakrapravartinī was myself."

At that time, he protected the Buddha-dharma, causing one hundred thousand bhikṣuṇīs to attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, to attain the samādhi of directly beholding all Buddhas,
to attain the *vajra-prabhā-dhāraṇī* of the wheel of the Dharma of all Buddhas, and to attain universal entry into all dharmas.
Following the Gate of the Ocean of Prajñāpāramitā, there arose a Buddha named Vimaladharmaprabha;
next, there arose a Buddha named Dharmacakraprabhakeśin; next, there arose a Buddha named Dharmasūryaguṇamegha;
next, there arose a Buddha named Dharmasāgarasusvararāja; next, there arose a Buddha named Dharmasūryajñānapradīpa; next, there arose a Buddha...
After the appearance of the Buddha named Lotus Banner Cloud, there appeared a Buddha named Dharma Flame Mountain Banner King;
after him, a Buddha named Profound Dharma Merit Moon; after him, a Buddha named Universal Radiance Treasury of Dharma Wisdom;
after him, a Buddha named Revealer of the Universal Wisdom Treasury; after him, a Buddha named Merit Treasury Mountain King; and after him, a Buddha appeared.
After the appearance of the Buddha named Universal Gate Sumeru Virtue, there appeared a Buddha named Banner of Diligence in All Dharmas;
after him, a Buddha named Cloud of Merit of Dharma-Jewel Flowers; after him, a Buddha named Tranquil Radiance Topknot;
after him, a Buddha named Compassionate Moon of Dharma-Radiance; and after him, a Buddha named Ocean of Merit-Flames.
There was a Buddha who appeared named Wisdom-Sun Universal Radiance; next, a Buddha appeared named Samantabhadra-Perfect Wisdom;
next, a Buddha appeared named King of Supernatural Power and Wisdom-Light; next, a Buddha appeared named Virtue-Flower Light-Lamp;
next, a Buddha appeared named Wisdom-Lion Banner King; next, a Buddha appeared named Sunlight Universal Illumination King.
There was a Buddha who appeared named Sumeru-ratna-vyūha-lakṣaṇa; next, a Buddha appeared named Sūryaprabhā-samanta-avabhāsa;
next, a Buddha appeared named Dharmarāja-guṇacandra; next, a Buddha appeared named Saṃkusumita-padma-svaramegha;
next, a Buddha appeared named Sūryaprabhā-lakṣaṇa; next, a Buddha appeared named Samantaprabhā-sudharma.
Following Ghoṣa, there arose a Buddha named Siṃhavajranārāyaṇābhaya; next there arose a Buddha named Samantajñānavikramadhvaja;
next there arose a Buddha named Samantadharmapadmaśarīra; next there arose a Buddha named Guṇasupuṣpasāgara;
next there arose a Buddha named Maṇḍalaguṇacandra; next there arose a Buddha...
After the Buddha named Dharma-Torch Blazing Moon, there arose a Buddha named Universal Radiance Topknot;
after him, a Buddha named Dharma-Banner Lamp; after him, a Buddha named Vajra-Ocean Banner Cloud;
after him, a Buddha named Fame-Mountain Merit-Cloud; after him, a Buddha named Sandalwood Wondrous Moon; and after him, a Buddha named Universal Wondrousness.
After the Buddha Prabhāsa-puṣpa, there arose a Buddha named Sarvasattvaprakāśa-prabharāja;
after him, a Buddha arose named Guṇapadmagarbha; after him, a Buddha arose named Gandhārci-prabharāja;
after him, a Buddha arose named Padmahetu; after him, a Buddha arose named Samantaprabha-sarvalakṣaṇaparvata. After that, there was a Buddha...
Next, there arose a Buddha named Universal Renown Banner; next, there arose a Buddha named Sumeru Universal Gate Light;
next, there arose a Buddha named Light of the City of Dharma Merit; next, there arose a Buddha named Light of the Great Tree Mountain;
next, there arose a Buddha named Universal Virtue Radiance Banner; next, there arose a Buddha named Auspicious Mark of Merit; next, there arose a Buddha.
Next there arose a Buddha named Vīryabaladhvaja; next there arose a Buddha named Dharmacakraprabhasvara;
next there arose a Buddha named Guṇaparvataprajñāprabha; next there arose a Buddha named Anuttarasaddharmacandra;
next there arose a Buddha named Dharmapuṇḍarīkaviśuddhaprabhādhvaja; next there arose a Buddha named Ratnapadmaprabhāgarbha.
There was a Buddha who appeared named Flame-Cloud Mountain Lamp; next there was a Buddha who appeared named Universal Awakening Flower;
next there was a Buddha who appeared named Various Merit-Flames Sumeru Treasury; next there was a Buddha who appeared named Perfect Mountain Light King;
next there was a Buddha who appeared named Virtue-Cloud Adornment; next there was a Buddha who appeared named Dharma-Mountain Cloud Banner.
There was a Buddha who appeared named Guṇaparvatejaprabha; next, a Buddha appeared named Dharmasūryameghapradīparāja;
next, a Buddha appeared named Dharmameghanāmarāja; next, a Buddha appeared named Dharmacakramegha;
next, a Buddha appeared named Bodhicittavibodhanajñānaraśmidhvaja; next, a Buddha appeared named Samantāvabhāsadharmacakracandra.
There was a Buddha named Ratnagiri-tejas-sujāta; next there was a Buddha named Sujāta-viśāla-prabhā;
next there was a Buddha named Samantaprajñā-megha; next there was a Buddha named Dharmabala-guṇaparvata;
next there was a Buddha named Guṇagandhārcirāja; next there was a Buddha named Suvarṇamaṇiparvata-susvara.
Next, there arose a Buddha named Crest-Top Emitting Clouds of Light from All Dharmas;
next, there arose a Buddha named Blazing Radiance of the Dharma-Wheel; next, there arose a Buddha named Unsurpassed Mountain of Merit;
next, there arose a Buddha named Radiant Cloud of the Torch of Diligence; next, there arose a Buddha named Vast Radiant Crown of the Seal of Samādhi. And so forth.
After the Buddha named King of the Merit of Jewel Radiance arose, there appeared a Buddha named Sound of the Dharma-Torch Jewel Canopy;
after him, a Buddha named Fearless Dharma-Radiance Universally Illuminating the Realm of Space;
after him, a Buddha named Banner Adorned with Lunar Features; after him, a Buddha named Cloud of the Mountain of Radiant Flames; after him, a Buddha named Illumination... [arose].
After the Dharma of Non-obstruction, like space, there arose a Buddha named Opening and Manifesting the Light of Wisdom Body;
next, a Buddha arose named World-Ruler Virtue Radiant Sound; next, a Buddha arose named Light-Sound of Samādhi of All Dharmas;
next, a Buddha arose named Treasury of Merit of the Dharma-Sound; next, a Buddha arose named Blazing Flame Ocean of Dharmas.
In the Cloud [Assembly], there arose a Buddha named Universal Illumination of the Marks of the Three Times’ Great Radiance;
next, there arose a Buddha named Universal Illumination of the Dharma-Wheel Mountain; next, there arose a Buddha named Dharma-Domain Lion Light;
next, there arose a Buddha named Sumeru Flower Radiance; next, there arose a Buddha named Lion-Flame of the Ocean of All Samādhis; next, there arose a Buddha...

"Son of good family, Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru arose in the world, their final names being Universal Wisdom Radiant Lamp and Dharma-realm City Wisdom Lamp; all appeared during the eon called Stainless Radiance.
I have in every case honored, approached, and made offerings to them, and have heard, received, and upheld the sublime Dharma they taught."
Furthermore, under all those Tathāgatas, he went forth to study the Path, upheld the teachings of the Dharma, and entered this Bodhisattva liberation of profound, sovereign, and wondrous sound.
Through various skillful means, he taught and matured immeasurable sentient beings.
From that time until now, throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, he has encountered all the Buddhas who have appeared in the world.

I have made offerings to all those who practice this Dharma, O son of good family. Since that time, amidst all sentient beings who sleep in the darkness of ignorance during the night of saṃsāra, I alone have awakened;

I have caused sentient beings to guard the city of their minds, to abandon the cities of the three realms, and to dwell in the unsurpassed city of the Dharma of omniscience. Son of good family, I know only this profound [Dharma].
The liberation of Sovereign Wondrous Sound causes all worlds to abandon discursive speech, to refrain from dualistic speech, to speak always with truth,
and to speak ever with purity; it enables one to know the intrinsic nature of all language as do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas,
so that in every thought-moment they freely awaken all sentient beings and enter into the vocal sounds of all sentient beings.
The Ocean [of Wisdom] has attained complete mastery over all verbal expressions and clearly perceives the ocean of all dharma-gates;
having attained sovereignty over the *dhāraṇī* that universally encompasses all dharmas, he expounds the Dharma according to the doubts in the minds of sentient beings,
ultimately taming all sentient beings and skillfully and universally gathering them in.

They cultivate all the unsurpassed deeds of bodhisattvas, penetrate deeply into the subtle wisdom of bodhisattvas, are able to skillfully examine the various bodhisattva-piṭakas, and can freely expound the teachings of bodhisattvas. Why is this?
Because they have already attained and perfected the *dhāraṇī* of all wheels of Dharma. How could I, O son of good family, know or speak of their meritorious conduct?
"Son, in this assembly of the Buddha there is a night goddess named Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasamantāloka. Go to her and ask:
'How does a bodhisattva train in all-knowledge? How does one establish all sentient beings so that they dwell in all-knowledge?
At that time, the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥ, wishing to reiterate the meaning of this liberation for the sake of Sudhana," [spoke these verses].
The youth spoke in verse:
“The liberation of the Bodhisattvas is profound and difficult to see; It is the mark of equality, like space and suchness.
Throughout the entirety of the boundless Dharma-realm, One universally beholds all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.”
Born with immeasurable, supreme merit, He realized the inconceivable true nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*).
Increasing all sovereign wisdoms, he opened the path of liberation throughout the three periods of time.
More than as many eons as there are motes of dust in a world-system, there was at that time an eon named Pure Light (*Vimalaprabhā*).
The world was named Dharma-Flame Cloud, and its city was called Jewel Flower Radiance.
Within it, various Buddhas appeared in the world, as numerous as the atoms in immeasurable Mount Sumerus.
Among them, a Buddha named Dharma-Ocean Sound first appeared during this eon.
Even unto the very last Buddha among them, named Dharmadhātu-jvālā-pradīpa-rāja—
To all such Tathāgatas as these, I have made offerings and listened to their Dharma.
I beheld the Buddha Dharmasāgara-nirghoṣa, whose body was entirely of a true golden color.
Adorned with all marks like a mountain of jewels, I resolve to attain the state of a Tathāgata.
Upon merely beholding the body of that Tathāgata, I immediately give rise to the vast mind of Bodhi,
Vowing to diligently seek all-encompassing wisdom, Whose nature is equal to the Dharma-realm and empty space.
By this, one universally beholds the Buddhas of the three periods of time, as well as the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas;
one also beholds the oceans of lands and sentient beings, and by universally taking them as objects of focus, gives rise to great compassion.
Following the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings, one manifests various and infinite bodies.
Pervading all lands throughout the ten directions, They shake the earth and radiate light to awaken all sentient beings.
Beholding the second Buddha and drawing near to him, They likewise see the Buddhas of the ocean-like lands of the ten directions,
Even unto the appearance of the very last Buddha— As numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru.
Throughout all lands, for as many eons as there are atoms, I have personally approached and venerated all the Tathāgatas,
The lamps that illuminate the world, Causing this liberation to become pure. At that time,
the youth Sudhana had attained entry into this profound and sovereign "Wondrous Sound" liberation of the Bodhisattvas.
Having entered the ocean of boundless samādhis, having entered the ocean of vast dhāraṇīs, having attained the great supernormal powers of a bodhisattva,
and having acquired the great eloquence of a bodhisattva, his heart was filled with great joy as he observed and paid homage to the night goddess Sarvanagararakṣāsaṃbhavatejaḥprabhā,
praising her with these verses:

Having traversed the vast ocean of sublime wisdom, And having crossed the boundless ocean of all existences, You possess a body that is a treasury of longevity, freedom from affliction, and knowledge;
With majestic power and radiant light, you abide among this assembly.
Thoroughly realizing the nature of phenomena as being like space, You enter universally throughout the three times without any obstruction.
Moment by moment, they grasp at all objects; Mind after mind, they forever sever all conceptual discrimination.
Thoroughly realizing that sentient beings have no inherent nature, They give rise to great compassion for all beings.
Deeply entering the gate of the Tathāgata’s liberation, They extensively deliver the immeasurable multitudes of deluded ones.
Contemplating and reflecting upon all phenomena, He thoroughly understands and realizes the nature of all dharmas;
Practicing the wisdom of the Buddha in this way, He universally transforms sentient beings, causing them to attain liberation.
The Deva is the charioteer of sentient beings, Revealing the path of the Tathāgata’s wisdom.
Universally for all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm, you have explained the practice of departing from all worldly fears;
you abide in the path of the Tathāgata’s vows, have received the vast teaching of Bodhi,
have cultivated the power of all-pervasive conduct, and have beheld the sovereign mastery of the Buddhas of the ten directions.
The celestial deity’s mind is pure as space, Universally free from all afflictions.
Knowing the infinite lands of the three times, The Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, sentient beings, and deities—
In a single thought-moment, they fully comprehend them, As well as days, nights, months, years, and oceans of eons.
They also know all classes of sentient beings, with their various names and characteristics each distinct;
they fully understand the places of birth and death for beings in the ten directions— whether possessing form, formless, with perception, or without perception—
and in accordance with worldly conventions, they guide them all onto the path to Bodhi.
"Born into the family of the Tathāgata’s vows, Having entered the ocean of the Buddhas' merits, The Dharma-body is pure and the mind is unimpeded;
Appearing in manifold forms according to the inclinations of sentient beings.
When the youth Sudhana had spoken these verses, he prostrated at the feet of the night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, and gazed upon her with profound reverence.
He bowed, took his leave, and departed.
[Treatise] Regarding the first section, the Dharma-gate of entering the specific stage (*dharmaparyāya*), from the passage beginning "At that time, Sudhana...
down to "I only know this profound and wondrous liberation-door of mastery over sound," this section is divided into ten parts.

Section One: At that time, the passage of four and a half lines of scripture, beginning from "Then the youth Sudhana descended to the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā," clarifies the stage of reflecting upon and ascending through the preceding dharma of right mindfulness. Section Two:
The passage of six lines of scripture, beginning from "Having seen that night goddess," down to "manifesting a body that ultimately tames all sentient beings," clarifies the night goddess herself.
The section on the manifestation of various bodies to teach and transform all sentient beings is divided into three parts:

from "After Sudhana saw this, he was filled with joy and leaped for gladness" down to "I only pray that you will compassionately pity me and explain it to me," which constitutes five lines of verse clarifying Sudhana’s formal request for what he seeks;
the fourth part is from "It clarifies how that night goddess spoke to Sudhana" down to the question.
Regarding the gates of practice cultivated by the various Bodhisattvas, there are seven sections of sūtra. First,
the passage from "O Son of Good Family, I have attained the liberation of profound, sovereign,
and wondrous sound" down to "with a mind that never abandons the ground of omniscience" consists of fifteen and a half lines of sūtra, which clarifies the night goddess.
The Section on the Gate of Practice for Benefiting Sentient Beings through One’s Own Spontaneous Conduct is divided into six parts.

First, "Good son, by means of such light of the pure Dharma," down to "entering the inconceivable realm of the Tathāgata," there are fourteen lines of scripture clarifying the Night Goddess’s exposition of the ten kinds of contemplations for entering the realm of the Tathāgata. Seventh: Furthermore, good son... [text continues].
As I thus reflect with right mindfulness, it has been a long time since the Noble One realized this;

as clarified by twenty-nine lines of scripture, he attained this liberation of Wondrous Sound (*Ghoṣavatī-vimokṣa*) and the Buddha-dhāraṇī, attaining mastery in preaching the Dharma for the sake of all sentient beings.
Furthermore, regarding the portion concerning Sudhana’s inquiry into the length of time since he attained this Dharma, the Night Goddess said: "O noble son..."
The passage from "Then, in ages past" down to "The Prajñāpāramitā that Universally Enters the Ocean of All Dharma-Gates" consists of thirty-five lines of scripture,
which clearly answer how long it has been since Sudhana attained this Dharma and detail the sequence of Buddhas he encountered.
First, there is the appearance of a Buddha named Vimaladharmaprabha, and so on, down to "abiding in all..."

In the "Section on the Duration of Attaining the Dharma and the Number of Buddhas Honored," which consists of sixty-nine and a half lines of scripture within the *Jñānottaradharmanagarasūtra*, it is clearly answered [how long it took] for Sudhana to attain the Dharma. This constitutes the tenth [section].

Having said, "I know only this profound liberation of Sovereign Wondrous Sound, which causes all worlds to be eternally pure," the following clarifies the progression through the stages by deferring to the virtues of others.
The wheel of wisdom of the Bodhisattva is far removed from all realms of conceptual discrimination;
it cannot be displayed through the distinctions of such eons as long or short, defiled or pure, broad or narrow, many or few within the cycle of birth and death.
As in the preceding ten sections, all the Dharma-gates therein are fully contained within the text itself. From the point where Sudhana asks about the realization of this Dharma...
Since long ago, as explained below, within the exposition of the Dharma through the mutual manifestation of principle and phenomena, the meanings are obscured and difficult to understand;

therefore, I shall briefly explain a small portion to provide a general outline. The intent is to clarify that because the retribution and the object are themselves the Dharma, one clarifies the Dharma by means of the retribution received, for it is accomplished through the Dharma practiced.
Thus, cause and effect resemble one another to manifest the practice; by seeing the retribution, one knows the Dharma. As the Sūtra says:
In the distant past, beyond world-rotations as numerous as the atoms of worlds— wherein "world-rotation" (*lokadhātu-parivarta*) is a number within the great numerical systems of the West,
such as those found in the *Śakraputra-bodhisattva-saṃkhyā-dharma*, which fully elucidates this—
the names and conventions of all sentient beings throughout world-rotations as numerous as atoms were transformed into the words of Great Wisdom.
The Ocean of Sound causes the world to be free from harsh speech and from defiled speech; as the subsequent text states:

"I have attained this profound liberation of sovereign wondrous sound, which causes all worlds to abandon discursive speech, dualistic speech, and to always speak words that are true and eternally pure. This means that it transforms all speech in the world.

This explains the general establishment of the gateways to the *prajñāpāramitā*: by taking the number of atoms produced by the transformation of the world as the measure, and by naming the eon "Stainless Radiance," it manifests that the fundamental principle of the threefold emptiness and quiescence within *prajñā* is its essential nature;
thus, naming the world "Dharmadhātu-Guṇa" clarifies that wisdom is the merit of teaching expounded within the *dharmadhātu*.

The reason the clouds take as their essence the ocean of mani-jewel kings that manifests the karma of all sentient beings is to symbolize the wondrous wisdom of the three emptinesses—which is devoid of intrinsic nature and quiescent—and which skillfully knows the ocean of differences in the karma of all sentient beings; thus they are called "mani-kings.
Their shape being like a lotus flower symbolizes the wondrous function of wisdom, which discerns the essence and characteristics while remaining centered within.

"Unstained by emptiness, this world abides within a net of fragrant maṇi-mountain-Sumerus as numerous as the atoms of the four continents" clarifies that these three kinds of empty, wondrous wisdom abide within the fragrance of the Tathāgata’s four unhindered analytical knowledges;
therefore, they possess a network of teachings as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru. This is because they bring forth the essence of all Tathāgatas.

The "Voice of Vows" refers to the sixth stage; because at the time of first generating the mind of enlightenment, one makes great vows based upon all Buddhas, and the sound of their turning the wheel of Dharma pervades the ten directions to awaken all sentient beings, it arises from these vows.
That it is adorned with lotus flowers clarifies that this Dharma-sound causes all beings—
Born with unimpeded wisdom, those who have as their retinue lotuses as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru:
"Sumeru" signifies that the light of wisdom rises loftily above the world; "atom" signifies that the light of wisdom is vast and manifold;
"lotus" signifies that the light of wisdom is free from attachment; and "retinue" signifies the skillful discernment of differentiated activities and all [phenomena].
The meaning of the total and specific, the same and different, and the formation and disintegration of dependent origination within the objective sphere—
wherein *sugandha-maṇi* jewels as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru are interspersed— clarifies that through the wisdom of differentiation,

one skillfully explains the stainless and pure fragrance of immeasurable morality, concentration, wisdom, and liberation; for these *maṇi* jewels signify freedom from defilement (*vimala*), they exist.
Regarding the four world-systems as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, they are merely formed of the four precious substances and stand high and preeminent within the great ocean;
however, if one were to discuss the measure of the four unhindered eloquences, the vocalizations, mental activities,
and karmic discriminations of all sentient beings within this Prajñā-wisdom, each individual four world-system would possess such a quantity.
In those hundred nayutas of unspeakably unspeakable cities, there are nayutas of dharma-gates for the accomplishment of nayutas of unspeakably unspeakable sentient beings.

At this time, when the number of such gatis is reached, the noble son—who is called Sudhana because of his virtues—was addressed by him as he proclaimed that Dharma. Within that world-system, there were four...
In this world, that which is called "Exquisite Banner" is the general name for a single set of four kinds of unimpeded eloquence (*catur-pratisaṃvid*).

Within this "Exquisite Banner," there is a royal capital; this capital, named "Universal Jewel Flower Light," is the manifestation of discriminative wisdom (*viveka-jñāna*) arising from fundamental wisdom (*mūla-jñāna*). Not far from here lies the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*).
The name "Palace of the Dharma King Universally Manifested" clarifies that, by means of fundamental wisdom (*mūla-jñāna*),

one gives rise to the mind of unsurpassed perfect enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi-citta*) and establishes the palace of great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) as a hall of differentiated wisdom; because one governs sentient beings through the True Dharma (*saddharma*),
Tathāgatas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru appear therein— namely, [Tathāgatas] as numerous as the atoms of all sentient beings.
The afflictions become the ocean of prajñā, and the manifestation of Buddhas all relies upon fundamental wisdom as the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa).

By giving rise to differentiated wisdom, one is able to treat the habitual tendencies of delusion; therefore, the first Buddha was named King of the Radiance of the Thunder-Sound of the Dharma-Ocean, signifying that from fundamental wisdom, differentiated wisdom arises, and through contemplation and observation, one transcends the realm of emotional consciousness.
He was named the First Buddha, skillfully able to preach the Dharma; his title was Thunderous Sound Teaching Light, who shattered the delusions of all sentient beings.
He was named Radiant Light, Sovereign in Establishing the Dharma, who could destroy all heterodoxies; amidst the heterodox, the heterodox could not harm him, and thus he was called a King.
When that Buddha appeared in the world, there was a Wheel-Turning King named Pure Sunlight.
"Clear-faced" means that the light of the wheel-turning king of wisdom shines forth brilliantly, like a mani-jewel mirror clearly reflecting all phenomena;

thus, "receiving and upholding the ocean-whirlpools of all dharmas under that Buddha" clarifies the wisdom of differentiation, for receiving and upholding the multitude of dharmas within fundamental wisdom—profound and boundless—is termed the "ocean-whirlpool. This refers to cultivation.
*Tara* refers to the prose sūtras. After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, those kings who renounced the world represent this sixth stage (*bhūmi*).

Within the ten stages, the wisdom of perfect enlightenment reaches its culmination; having emerged from entanglements, wisdom is fully perfected, and having transcended discursive thought (*vitarka-vicāra*), it is extinguished—this is called the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa.
World-transcending wisdom is thus accomplished in the eleventh stage, wherein only Samantabhadra remains.

The gate of entering the entanglements (*saṃyojana*) is not something that can be reached by the three types of wisdom regarding emptiness (*śūnyatā*) that transcend entanglement— such as the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) and so forth—

as found in this sixth stage. This is because, as described in the "Chapter on the Ten Samādhis," the thirty bodhisattvas who have attained liberation through the three types of wisdom regarding emptiness have all already entered the stage of consecration (*abhiṣeka*) in the tenth stage, wherein they universally seek [the goal] through immeasurable supramundane gates of samādhi.
The Worthy One ultimately cannot be found; one must see the Tathāgata and direct one’s thoughts toward seeking him.
Only when Samantabhadra appears does the mind clarify the wisdom of the three emptinesses. This reaches only as far as the tenth stage (*bhūmi*) and the gate of emerging from the entanglements.
From this point downward, the list proceeds from beginning to end, enumerating one hundred Buddha-fruit states, without including the final eleven stages or the Dharma-gate of Samantabhadra.
In the sixth stage (*ṣaṣṭhī bhūmi*), there is liberation through the wisdom of the three emptinesses of quiescent extinction;
because one reaches the state of the tenth stage and the Buddha-stage where discursive thought (*vitarka-vicāra*) has already ceased, it is called the "Buddha-nirvāṇa.

Therefore, for one who leaves the household life as a king, this gate of the wisdom of the three emptinesses of quiescent extinction in the sixth stage constitutes the meaning of "leaving the household life," just as in the *Daśabhūmika-sūtra*, the Bhikṣu Sāgaradhvaja enters [the path].
The King who renounced the world to protect the True Dharma manifested this through the meditative absorption of cessation (*nirodha-samāpatti*).

By means of the wisdom of the three gates of liberation (*trivimokṣa*), he protected the supramundane True Dharma. When the Dharma was on the verge of extinction, there arose a thousand distinct sects and a thousand varieties of teachings as the final age approached;
the karmic afflictions and obstacles became heavy, and many wicked bhikṣus engaged in strife and contention, even failing to seek spiritual merit.
"Virtue" refers to the fact that within this stage there are only three gates of emptiness and the wisdom of cessation;

because there is no teaching through compassion, the King manifests supernatural powers, radiance, and various other deeds so that his True Dharma may flourish for sixty-five thousand years. "Sixty thousand" refers to the advancement through the six stages.
The five thousand years of a single stage encompass all five stages; cause and effect advance together. This clarifies the gate of liberation through emptiness:
by means of wisdom, one gives rise to supramundane compassion, just as the royal daughter also left the household life.
One clarifies this gate of wisdom regarding emptiness, cultivating supramundane compassion until it includes both what precedes and what follows—totaling one hundred [years].
These Buddhas appear in succession to represent this sixth *prajñā* gate;
it extends only to the stage of the world-transcending Buddha-fruit at the tenth ground (*bhūmi*), wherein each single ground already encompasses all ten.

Below this, the offering to Buddhas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru is mentioned solely to represent that *prajñā*, emerging from the entanglements with supreme loftiness, just like the aforementioned hundred Buddhas—these ten.
The fruit of ascending through the stages consists of serving and making offerings to the Buddha-body, corresponding to each of the ten stages.
Such practice within the ten stages is like making offerings to Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field.
This is because the general characteristic of the *dharmadhātu* is that there is not a single thing that is not the Buddha, for within every single atom there are infinite Buddhas.

The above all clarifies that by means of the Dharma and through practice, one achieves the fruits of kalpas, lands, and buddha-fields; it causes one to contemplate the fruit as corresponding to the cause.
This entire dharma-gate is such that phenomena themselves are principle, and principle itself is phenomena.

As for the king and his daughter both becoming bhikṣus and bhikṣuṇīs, this is because the Prajñāpāramitā is the gate of the three emptinesses and quiescent extinction; thus, they emerge [from saṃsāra].
The one who was the Wheel-Turning King at that time, presiding over the gate of wisdom and compassion within birth and death, is now the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra;
this is the clarity of wisdom. The bhikṣuṇī was my own self; this is the clarity of compassion.
As for "I know only this liberation of profound, sovereign, and wondrous sound," this clarifies that a single sound pervades the entire dharma-realm, yet remains without [obstruction].
The essence is without discrimination, yet it can turn all dharma-gates and transform all sentient beings;
this is called the liberation of the "Profound and Sovereign Sublime Sound. This is the sixth stage, the Stage of Presence (*Abhimukhī*), because all wisdoms manifest before one;
herein, the perfection of wisdom (*prajñā-pāramitā*) is primary, while the other nine are its companions. This is that stage.
This section treats the obstacle to the sovereign mastery of the quiescent and active functions of the wisdom of the three gates of liberation, thereby enabling the attainment of such mastery.
Within the second part, "Advancing by Inferring Virtue," from the passage beginning with "As for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas" down to "took their leave and departed," there are six sections:
first, advancing by inferring virtue; second, indicating the location of spiritual friends, stating that they are here with this Buddha.
1. Within the assembly, the name of the spiritual friend was proclaimed three times: there is a night goddess named Sarvavṛkṣapraphullanasamaya (She Who Causes All Tree Blossoms to Bloom). 2.
There are twenty-two verses of gāthā by the city-ruling goddess, which restate the aforementioned Dharma as clearly explained in the text.
3. Sudhana praises the virtues of the city-ruling goddess with twenty verses of gāthā, as clearly explained in the text. 4. [Section] Six.
Having paid homage and departed from this assembly of Buddhas, it clarifies that one does not depart from this principle of right awakening (*samyak-saṃbodhi*),
which is unconditioned (*anabhisaṃskṛta*), inconceivable (*acintya*), non-active (*akṛtaka*), and devoid of intrinsic nature (*niḥsvabhāva*).

This is called "blooming the flowers of all practices within this assembly of Buddhas" and accomplishing the perfection of skillful means (*upāya-pāramitā*) by entering into all realms of birth and death through shared activity (*samānārthatā*) amidst the absence of birth and death.

Regarding the practice of beneficial conduct through the four means of integration (*saṃgrahavastu*), this is identical to the eight thousand four hundred nayutas of gates of affliction practiced by the laywoman Śreṣṭhī;
having thus completed the sixth stage, which is liberation from the entanglements, one now enters the seventh stage.
By means of those gates for emerging from the entanglements, one enters the mundane world to benefit sentient beings without fear, as this is the proper place.
Because both the fetters and the emergence from fetters are equal; because it causes the mind of great compassion to grow and become vast;
because it is without limit or measure; because it desires to cause the practice of great compassion to pervade the evil realms; and because it gathers in sentient beings until their liberation.
