[Treatise] The Eighth Night Goddess of the Great Vow and the Power of Diligence Who Protects and Saves All Sentient Beings within the Great Bodhimanda.
The Lord of the Immovable Ground.

[Sūtra] At that time, the youth Sudhana went to the place of the night goddess Sarvajagadrakṣāpraṇidhānavīryaprabhā and saw her sitting among the great assembly upon a universal manifestation of all palaces made of mani-jewel kings.

Seated upon a lion throne of the treasury, he universally manifests throughout the lands of the Dharma-realm; a net of mani-jewels covers him from above. He manifests a body that displays the reflections of the sun, moon, and stars;
he manifests a body that appears according to the minds of sentient beings so that all may see it; he manifests a body that takes on forms equal to those of all sentient beings;
he manifests a body that is an ocean of infinite and vast physical characteristics; he manifests a body that universally appears to all.
He manifests a body of majestic deportment that appears universally throughout the ten directions; he manifests a body that universally tames all sentient beings;

he manifests a body of vast, swift, and rapid supernatural powers; he manifests a body that brings benefit to sentient beings without ceasing; he manifests a body that constantly travels through space to bring benefit;
he manifests a body that pays homage at the feet of all Buddhas; and he manifests a body that cultivates all roots of goodness.
Upholding the Buddha-dharma without forgetfulness; manifesting a body that fulfills the great vows of a bodhisattva; manifesting a body that radiates light filling the ten directions;
manifesting a body that appears as the lamp of Dharma to universally extinguish the darkness of the world; manifesting a body of pure wisdom that realizes all phenomena are like illusions;

manifesting a body of the nature of reality (dharmatā) far removed from the darkness of defilements; manifesting a body of universal wisdom that illuminates the Dharma with clarity; and manifesting a body that is ultimately free from affliction.
The Body Free from Heat appeared; the Indestructible and Firm Body appeared; the Non-abiding Buddha-Power Body appeared;
the Non-conceptual and Defilement-Free Body appeared; and the Primordially Pure Dharmatā Body appeared.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, beholding such bodies as these, numbering as many as the atoms within a buddha-field, prostrated himself with single-minded devotion, casting his entire body to the ground, and remained thus for a long while.
Rising with palms joined, one gazes up at the spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) and gives rise to ten kinds of mind. What are these ten? They are as follows:
one gives rise to the mind that regards the spiritual friend as oneself, thinking, "May I be diligent in accomplishing all the factors conducive to the path for omniscience.

One gives rise to the mind that views the spiritual friend as the pure fruit of one's own karma, thinking, "By approaching and making offerings to them, I shall produce roots of goodness. One gives rise to... [the text continues].
One should conceive toward spiritual friends the thought of "ornamentation," because they cause me to quickly adorn all bodhisattva practices;
one should conceive toward spiritual friends the thought of "accomplishment," because they instruct and guide me so that I may cultivate the path;
one should conceive toward spiritual friends the thought of "origination," because they are able to give birth to the unsurpassed Dharma within me. Regarding spiritual friends...
I shall generate a mind of renunciation toward the spiritual friend, so that by practicing all the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, I may attain liberation;
I shall generate a mind that perceives the spiritual friend as the ocean of all merit and wisdom, so that I may accumulate all pure dharmas;
I shall generate a mind of growth toward the spiritual friend, so that I may increase all-encompassing knowledge.
One should generate a mind that perceives the spiritual friend as one who possesses all roots of goodness, so that my aspirations may be fulfilled;

one should generate a mind that perceives the spiritual friend as one capable of accomplishing great benefit, so that I may dwell with mastery in all bodhisattva dharmas, achieve the path to omniscience, and attain all Buddha-dharmas. These are the ten [kinds of] minds; having generated these minds, one attains them.
That night goddess shared in the same practices as bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field;

that is to say, she shared the same mindfulness, constantly recollecting all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time; she shared the same wisdom, discerning and resolving the various gateways to the ocean of all dharmas;
she shared the same aspiration, being able to turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma of all Buddhas, Tathāgatas; and she shared the same awakening.
Because they universally enter all three worlds through wisdom equal to space; because they achieve the same faculties as the pure light-wisdom faculties of Bodhisattvas;
because they share the same resolve and are well able to cultivate the unimpeded merit that adorns all Bodhisattva paths;
because they share the same objective realm, universally illuminating the spheres of action of all Buddhas; and because they equally realize all-knowledge.
They are identical in their pure radiance that illuminates the ocean of the true mark; they are identical in their wisdom that comprehends the true nature of all phenomena;
they are identical in their valor that can shatter all mountains of obstacles; they are identical in their physical bodies that manifest in accordance with the minds of sentient beings;
they are identical in their diligent pursuit of omniscience without ever regressing; and they are identical in their fearlessness and purity of mind.
They are identical in purity, being as pure as space; they are identical in diligence, practicing the bodhisattva path for immeasurable eons without weariness;

they are identical in eloquence, having attained the light of wisdom that is unimpeded regarding all phenomena; they are identical in their peerless physical marks, which are pure and transcend the world;
they are identical in their kind speech, causing all sentient beings to rejoice; and they are identical in their sublime voice, universally proclaiming the One [Dharma].

Because they encompass the ocean of all dharma-gates, they are identical in their full resonance; because they enable all sentient beings to understand according to their respective types, they are identical in their pure virtues;

because they cultivate the pure merits of the Tathāgata, they are identical in the ground of wisdom; because they receive the wheel of Dharma from all Buddhas, they are identical in their holy life (*brahmacarya*);
because they abide in the realm of all Buddhas, they are identical in their great compassion that universally covers all lands in every thought-moment.

Because they are the ocean of sentient beings, they are identical in great compassion; because they universally rain down the rain of Dharma to moisten and nourish all sentient beings, they are identical in physical action (*kāyakarman*);
because they teach and transform all sentient beings through skillful means, they are identical in verbal action (*vākkarman*);

because they expound all Dharma-gates using sounds according to the various species [of beings], they are identical in mental action (*manaskarman*); and because they universally gather in sentient beings and establish them in omniscience (*sarvajñatā*).
They are identical because they abide within the same realm; identical because they adorn and purify all Buddha-fields;
identical because they draw near to all Buddhas appearing in the world, attending them all; identical because they make requests of all Buddhas to turn the wheel of Dharma;
identical because they offer worship, constantly delighting in making offerings to all Buddhas; and identical because they teach and discipline all sentient beings.
They are identical in that their radiance illuminates all dharma-gates; they are identical in that through samādhi they universally know the minds of all sentient beings;
they are identical in that by the power of mastery they pervade all oceans of Buddha-fields while cultivating various practices;

they are identical in that they dwell in the same abodes as all bodhisattvas who possess great supernormal powers; and they are identical in that their retinues consist of all bodhisattvas dwelling together with them.
They are identical in their abiding, as they universally enter the subtle realms of all worlds; they are identical in their mental resolve, as they universally know all Buddha-fields;
they are identical in their approach, as they universally enter the oceans of all Buddha-fields; they are identical in their skillful means, as they manifest within all Buddha-fields;
they are identical in their transcendence, for they are peerless among all Buddha-fields; and they are identical in their non-retrogression.
Because they universally enter the ten directions without obstruction, they are identical in destroying darkness and attaining the great light of the wisdom of all Buddhas’ attainment of Bodhi;
because they share in the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*), they enter the ocean-like assemblies of all Buddhas;

because they universally pervade the networks of all Buddha-fields, they reverently make offerings to the Tathāgatas of unspeakably many lands; and because they are identical in the realization and understanding of wisdom.
Because they share the ocean of various Dharma-gates; because they equally practice and accord with all Dharma-gates;
because they equally aspire to the pure Dharma through deep longing and desire; because they equally purify the accumulation of the Buddha’s merits to adorn body, speech, and mind;
because they equally possess wondrous intent regarding all phenomena through clear understanding of wisdom; and because they equally apply diligence to universally gather [all virtues].
They are identical because they sever all roots of goodness; they are identical because they bring all bodhisattva practices to fulfillment through pure conduct;

they are identical because they understand that all phenomena are signless through unimpeded comprehension; they are identical because they possess mastery of wisdom regarding all phenomena through skillfulness;

they are identical because they manifest realms according to their inclinations and the minds of sentient beings; and they are identical because they skillfully practice all that ought to be practiced through expedient means.
They are identical in being protected by mindfulness, for they are protected by all Buddhas; identical in entering the stages, for they enter all bodhisattva stages;
identical in their dwelling, for they abide securely in all bodhisattva positions; identical in their prediction, for all Buddhas bestow predictions upon them;
and identical in samādhi, for in a single instant they universally enter all doors of samādhi. Thus they are identical.

They are identical in manifesting and establishing the various deeds of all Buddhas; they are identical in right mindfulness, because they possess the gateway of right mindfulness toward all spheres of experience;
they are identical in practice, because they cultivate all bodhisattva practices throughout all kalpas until the end of the future;

they are identical in pure faith, because they take supreme delight in the immeasurable wisdom of all Tathāgatas; and they are identical in relinquishment, because they have eliminated and extinguished all obstacles.

They are identical in being unimpeded; identical in wisdom, as their non-retrogressive knowledge is equal to that of all Tathāgatas; identical in taking birth, as they manifest to bring sentient beings to maturity;
identical in their dwelling, as they abide in the gateway of skillful means for omniscience; identical in their sphere of activity, as they attain mastery over the realm of the *dharmadhātu*;
and identical in their lack of dependence, as they have forever severed all minds that rely on a basis, and thus they are identical in their teaching.

They are identical because they have entered the wisdom of the equality of all phenomena; they are identical because they diligently cultivate together and are constantly protected by the mindfulness of all Buddhas;

they are identical because they employ supernatural powers together to awaken sentient beings and cause them to practice all bodhisattva deeds; they are identical because they possess supernatural might together to enter the oceans of worlds in the ten directions;
they are identical because they possess dharanis together that universally illumine the ocean of all total retention; they are identical in their secrets...
The Secret Dharma is identical [to other dharmas] because it thoroughly understands the sublime gateways within all sūtras;
it is identical because it realizes that all phenomena are like space through its profound nature; it is identical because its light universally illumines all worlds;

it is identical because it joyfully reveals teachings according to the minds of sentient beings to bring them delight; and it is identical because it manifests as a great trembling for the sake of all sentient beings.

Because the power of their supernormal knowledges universally shakes all lands in the ten directions, they are identical; because they cause all who see, hear, or remember them to have their minds fully tamed, they are identical;
because they bring about the fulfillment of the ocean of all great vows of renunciation and the accomplishment of the Tathāgata’s wisdom of the ten powers, they are identical.
At that time, the youth Sudhana observed the power of great vows and diligence that protects and saves all.

The night goddess Sarvasattvonmādana-jagadvirocana gave rise to ten kinds of pure minds and attained as many qualities as there are atoms in a buddha-field, all identical to the practices of bodhisattvas.
Having attained these, her mind became even more purified; she bared her right shoulder, prostrated at her feet, joined her palms with single-minded devotion, and praised her with these verses:
I have resolved with a firm intention, Vowing to seek supreme enlightenment. Now, regarding the spiritual friend, I give rise to the thought of my own self;
By seeing the spiritual friend, I gather inexhaustible pure dharmas and eliminate all stains of sin, Accomplishing the fruit of bodhi. Thus I behold the spiritual friend.
With a mind adorned by merit, throughout all lands and kalpas until the end of the future, I diligently cultivate the path I have traveled.
I call to mind my spiritual friends who have gathered me in and benefited me;
for my sake, they have fully manifested the true Dharma of correct teaching, closing off all evil realms and revealing the path to humans and devas.
They also demonstrate to all Tathāgatas the path to the attainment of omniscience. I recall that spiritual friends are the treasury of the Buddha’s merits;
in every thought-moment they are able to give birth to an ocean of space-like virtues, bestow upon me the pāramitās, increase my inconceivable merit, and grow my pure qualities.
May I wear the Buddha’s silk turban; may I mindfully rely upon spiritual friends who can fulfill the path of Buddha-wisdom.
With constant vows of reliance, may I bring the pure, white dharmas to perfection.
Because of these causes and conditions, may I be fully endowed with all merit, and for the sake of all sentient beings everywhere, may I expound the path of omniscience.
"The Noble One is my teacher; he has bestowed upon me the unsurpassed Dharma. Even throughout immeasurable and incalculable eons, one could never repay his kindness.
At that time, after Sudhana had spoken this verse, he said: "O Great Sage, I pray that you will explain to me this gate of liberation."
"What is the name of this resolve? How long has it been since you first awakened the mind? After how much time will you attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
The night goddess replied, "Noble son, this door of liberation is named 'Teaching and Transforming Sentient Beings to Cause Them to Generate Roots of Goodness.
Because I have accomplished this liberation, I have realized that the self-nature of all phenomena is equal."
They enter equally into the true nature of all phenomena and realize the state of non-reliance; they abandon the world and fully know the distinctions between the characteristics of all phenomena.

Furthermore, they comprehend that the natures of blue, yellow, red, and white are all unreal and without distinction, yet they constantly manifest immeasurable physical bodies—namely, various kinds of physical bodies that are not a single physical body.
The color-body of the limits, the pure color-body, the color-body of all adornments, the universally seen color-body,
and all such color-bodies of all sentient beings; the color-body that appears before all sentient beings, the color-body whose light shines everywhere,
the color-body that one never tires of beholding, the color-body of pure marks and signs, and the color-body of light free from all evils— these he manifests.
The physical body of great valor, which is extremely difficult to obtain; the physical body that no one in any world can outshine;
the physical body universally praised by all worlds as inexhaustible; the physical body that constantly observes in every thought-moment;
the physical body that manifests various clouds; the physical body with various shapes and manifest colors; the physical body that displays immeasurable powers of mastery.
The body of wondrous radiant light; the body of all-pure and exquisite adornment; the body that brings all sentient beings to maturity in accordance with their needs;
the body that appears before them to subdue them according to their mental inclinations; the body of unobstructed universal radiance;
the body that is pure and free from turbidity or defilement; the indestructible body fully endowed with adornments; and the inconceivable body.
The body of radiant light through skillful means in the Dharma; the body that cannot be eclipsed by any other form;
the body that destroys all darkness; the body that gathers all pure and white dharmas; the body of the ocean of merit with great power;
the body born from causes of past veneration; and the body born from a mind as pure as space.
The most supreme and vast body; the inexhaustible and endless body; the body of an ocean of light;
the body of equality that has no dependence upon any world; the body that pervades the ten directions without obstruction;
the body that manifests oceans of various forms and marks in every thought-moment; the body that increases the hearts of joy in all sentient beings; the body of gathering-in.
The body of the ocean of colors of all sentient beings; from each and every pore of this body, it proclaims the ocean of merits of all Buddhas;
the body that purifies the ocean of desires and understandings of all sentient beings; the body that decisively realizes the meaning of all dharmas;
the body of unobstructed, universal radiance; the body of pure light equal to space; emitting vast and pure light.
The luminous form-body that manifests the stainless Dharma-form-body; the incomparable form-body; the form-body adorned with diverse ornaments;

the form-body that universally illumines the ten directions; the form-body that manifests according to the times in response to sentient beings; the tranquil form-body; the form-body that extinguishes all afflictions;
the form-body that is a field of merit for all sentient beings; and the form-body that all sentient beings behold without weariness.
The body of empty form and great wisdom; the body of courageous power free from obstruction and universally pervasive;
the body of wondrous clouds of forms that appear throughout the world so that all may receive benefit; the body endowed with the ocean of great compassion;
the body of the king of jewel mountains of great merit; the body that emits light illuminating all realms within the world; the body of great knowledge.
The body born from the purity of wisdom; the body that generates right mindfulness in sentient beings; the body of the radiance of all jewels; the body that is a treasury of universal light;
the body that manifests various pure signs within the world; the body that seeks the locus of omniscience;
the body that manifests a smile to inspire pure faith in sentient beings; and the body of radiant adornment with all jewels.
The form-body neither grasps nor abandons the form-bodies of all sentient beings; it is without fixed determination and without ultimate limit.
The form-body manifests through the power of sovereign empowerment; the form-body manifests all supernatural powers and transformations; the form-body is born into the family of the Tathāgatas;
the form-body is far removed from all evils and pervades the ocean of the Dharma-realm; the form-body universally appears upon the paths of all Tathāgatas.
The physical body present in all assemblies; the physical body possessing an ocean of various colors; the physical body flowing from virtuous conduct;
the physical body manifested according to those to be transformed; the physical body that all worlds never tire of beholding; the physical body of various pure radiances;
the physical body manifesting the oceans of all three periods of time; and the physical body emitting an ocean of all radiances.
A body manifesting an ocean of infinite varieties of radiant colors; a body surpassing all worlds with the color of fragrant light;
a body manifesting unspeakable clouds of solar discs; a body manifesting vast clouds of lunar discs;
a body emitting clouds of exquisite flowers from Mount Sumeru; a body producing clouds of various garlands; a body manifesting all things...
The body that arises from clouds of jewel-lotus colors; the body that pervades the Dharma-realm with clouds of all kinds of burning incense;
the body that scatters clouds from the treasury of all powdered incenses; the body that manifests the great vows of all Tathāgatas;
the body that manifests the ocean of Dharma through all languages and sounds; and the body that manifests the image of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva—these bodies appear in every moment of thought.

In this manner, bodies of such forms and marks fill the ten directions, causing all sentient beings—whether by seeing them, recollecting them, hearing their preaching of the Dharma, through proximity to them, or by attaining awakening—to likewise see spiritual powers or witness transformations;
thus, according to their inclinations, they are tamed at the appropriate time, abandon unwholesome karma, and abide in wholesome conduct. Good son, you should know this.
By the power of great vows, by the power of the knowledge of all modes, by the power of the bodhisattva’s liberation,
by the power of great compassion, and by the power of great loving-kindness, I perform such deeds. Son of good family, having entered this liberation,

I thoroughly understand that the nature of phenomena is without differentiation, yet I am able to manifest immeasurable physical bodies, and within each body, I manifest immeasurable forms and characteristics.
From each and every mark on the ocean-like body, immeasurable clouds of light are emitted; from each and every ray of light, immeasurable Buddha-lands appear;
in each and every land, immeasurable Buddhas appearing in the world are manifested;

and from each and every Buddha, immeasurable supernormal powers are displayed to awaken the roots of goodness from past lives of sentient beings—causing those not yet planted to be planted, those already planted to increase, and those already increased to further flourish.
In every thought-moment, he brings immeasurable sentient beings to maturity, causing them to attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

"Good son, regarding the meaning of your question—'From what time did you first resolve upon bodhicitta and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva?'—I shall explain it for you by virtue of the Buddha's spiritual power. Good son, as for bodhi..."
The wheel of the Bodhisattva’s wisdom is far removed from all realms of conceptual discrimination;
it cannot be displayed through the distinctions of birth and death—such as long and short, defiled and pure, broad and narrow, many and few, or the various kalpas. Why is this?

Because the nature of the Bodhisattva’s wheel of wisdom is inherently pure, free from the net of all conceptual discriminations, and transcends all mountains of obstacles, manifesting according to those who are to be transformed.
Because it shines universally, good son, it is like the solar orb, for which there is no day or night; yet when it rises, it is called "day," and when it sets, it is called "night.

The wheel of the Bodhisattva’s wisdom is also like this: it is without discrimination and without the three periods of time, yet it manifests according to the minds [of beings] to teach and transform sentient beings.
To speak of its abiding in past kalpas or future kalpas, good son, is like... [the analogy continues].

Just as when the solar disc dwells in the sky over Jambudvīpa, its reflection appears in all precious objects, rivers, oceans, and pure waters, such that no sentient being fails to see it with their own eyes, yet that pure sun does not come here;
so too is the wheel of wisdom of this Bodhisattva: it emerges from the ocean of existence and dwells in the tranquil sky of the Buddha’s true Dharma.
Having a basis, it is for the sake of transforming and delivering all sentient beings that they take birth according to their kind within the various realms of existence;
yet in reality, they do not undergo birth and death, are unstained by anything, and have no conceptual discriminations regarding kalpas of long or short duration. Why is this?
Because Bodhisattvas have ultimately abandoned the mind, thoughts, views, and all perversions, attaining true vision; they see the true nature of phenomena and know them as one.

All worlds are like dreams and like illusions; there are no sentient beings therein, yet by the power of great compassion and great vows, they appear before sentient beings to teach and subdue them, O Son of the Buddha.

They are like a boatman who, with a great ship upon a river, relies neither on this shore nor clings to the far shore, nor does he dwell in midstream, yet he ferries sentient beings across without ceasing.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Śāntamati is also like this: by means of the ship of the pāramitās, he crosses over sentient beings within the stream of birth and death—neither relying on this shore, nor clinging to the other shore, nor dwelling in the middle current—without ceasing.
Although he has cultivated the bodhisattva practices for immeasurable kalpas, he has never discriminated regarding the length or brevity of those kalpas. O Son of the Buddha, it is like the great...
Just as all worlds within space undergo formation and destruction while space itself remains without discrimination—
inherently pure, unstained, undisturbed, unobstructed, and untiring, neither long nor short— sustaining all lands throughout kalpas until the end of the future,
so too do the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas, with a vast and profound mind equal to the realm of space, give rise to the wind of great vows.
The wheel gathers all sentient beings, causing them to leave the evil realms and be born in the various good destinies;
it causes them all to dwell securely on the ground of omniscience, extinguishing the afflictions and the bonds of birth and death, yet without a mind of sorrow, joy, weariness, or fatigue.
Good son, it is like a person created by illusion: though their limbs are complete, they have neither inhalation nor exhalation, and are free from cold, heat, hunger, or thirst.
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is likewise regarding these ten matters of sorrow, joy, birth, and death.

By means of the wisdom of illusion, they manifest various physical forms within the equal Dharma-body; dwelling for immeasurable eons among the various realms of existence, they transform sentient beings.
Amidst all objects within the cycle of birth and death, they feel neither delight nor aversion, neither craving nor anger, and neither suffering nor [joy].
Rejoicing in neither grasping nor abandoning, neither finding peace nor fearing, O Son of the Buddha,
although the wisdom of the Bodhisattvas is thus profound and difficult to fathom, I shall now, by the power of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority,
explain it for you so that the Bodhisattvas of future ages may fulfill their great vows and achieve all powers. Son of the Buddha, in the distant past, beyond worlds...
In an eon as numerous as the atoms in the ocean, there was an eon named Good Light and a world named Jewel Light.

Within that eon, ten thousand Buddhas appeared in the world; the first of these Buddhas was named Dharma-Wheel Sound Space-Lamp King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, complete with the ten titles. In that Jambudvīpa, there was a royal capital named Jewel Adornment.
Not far to the east of that [city] was a great forest named Wondrous Light (*Prabhāsa*). Within it was a site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) called Jewel Flower (*Ratnapuṣpa*).
In that site of enlightenment was a lion throne made of the *sarvāvabhāsa-maṇi-lotus-treasury*.
At that time, the Tathāgata had attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* upon this throne for a full hundred years.

Seated at the site of enlightenment, he expounded the True Dharma for the sake of the bodhisattvas, devas, humans, and those in Jambudvīpa whose roots of merit had been planted in the past and were now fully matured.
At that time, the king was named Prasenajit, and the lifespan of the people of that world was ten thousand years;
among them, there were many who committed killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, false speech, frivolous chatter, double-tongued speech, and harsh words.
At that time, there were those who were greedy, hateful, and held wrong views; they were unfilial toward their parents and disrespectful toward śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and others.
Desiring to subdue them, the king constructed prisons and used shackles and fetters to confine immeasurable sentient beings within them, where they suffered.
The king had a crown prince named Śubhavasu (Good Subduer), who was handsome, extraordinary, and pleasing to all people, endowed with twenty-eight [marks].
The marks of a Great Man were such that while within his palace, he could hear from afar the sounds of prisoners undergoing torture and agony;
his heart was filled with compassion as he entered the prisons from the palace and beheld the various offenders bound together by shackles, manacles, and neck-yokes,
cast into dark places where they were either scorched with fire or smoked with fumes, or subjected to flogging and scourging, or meted out punishments of disfigurement and mutilation.
Naked, with disheveled hair, emaciated by hunger and thirst, their sinews severed and bones exposed, they wailed in intense agony.
Upon seeing them, the Prince gave rise to a heart of compassion and comforted them with a voice free from fear, saying, "Do not be distressed; do not grieve or be afraid.
I shall cause you all to attain liberation. He then went to the King's presence and addressed him, saying, "The prisoners in the jail..."

"May you grant us clemency for these difficult and bitter circumstances and bestow upon us fearlessness. At that time, the King immediately assembled five hundred ministers and asked them, "What do you say regarding this matter?
The ministers replied, "That criminal has privately stolen official property, conspired to usurp the royal throne, and illicitly entered the palace precincts;
his crime deserves execution, and anyone who pities him or seeks to rescue him shall likewise face the death penalty."
At that time, the Prince’s heart of compassion grew even more urgent, and he said to the great minister: "As you have said, let this man be released;
whatever punishment he deserves may be inflicted upon me instead. For his sake, I am able to endure all manner of suffering;
I would not begrudge even the crushing of my body or the end of my life. I must ensure that this sinner is freed from his suffering. Why is this?"
If one does not rescue these sentient beings, how can one rescue those in the prison of the triple world from all their sufferings?
All sentient beings within the triple world are bound by craving and obscured by ignorance; they are impoverished and devoid of merit, falling into the various evil destinies.
Their physical forms are base and ugly, their faculties are dissolute, and their minds are deluded; they do not seek the path out of suffering and have lost it.
Delighting in the light of wisdom yet attached to the three realms of existence, they have severed all roots of merit and extinguished all wisdom.
Their minds are turbid and disordered by various afflictions; they dwell in the prison of suffering and enter the snare of Māra.

Constantly oppressed by such sufferings as birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, despair, and harm—how shall I cause them to be liberated? For this purpose, I should even sacrifice my own body and life.
At the time of his rescue, all the ministers went together to the king’s presence and, raising their hands, cried out in a loud voice:
"Great King, you should know that according to the Prince's intent, he has subverted the royal law, and the calamity will reach ten thousand people.
If Your Majesty cherishes him and does not punish him, the King’s precious reign will likewise not endure for long. Upon hearing these words, the king was filled with a towering rage and commanded:

Accompanied by a thousand court ladies, she hurried to the King’s presence, threw herself prostrate upon the ground, and prostrated at the King’s feet, all speaking these words together:
"We only pray that Your Majesty will spare the life of the Crown Prince. The King immediately turned back and said to the Crown Prince: "Do not save the criminals! If...

At that time, because the Prince sought exclusively for all-knowledge, because he desired to benefit all sentient beings, and because he wished to universally rescue and gather them through great compassion, his mind was firm and free from any retreat or fear.
He spoke again to the King, saying, "I pray you forgive his offense; let my body receive the execution. The King said, "Do as you wish."
Then the queen said to the Great King, "I pray that you will grant the Prince permission to practice giving for half a month and cultivate merit as he desires;

thereafter, he may be punished. The King immediately granted his consent. At that time, to the north of the capital city, there was a great garden named Sūryaprabha (Sunlight), which had formerly been a site for almsgiving.
The Prince went there and established a great assembly of giving, providing food, drink, clothing, flowers, hair-ornaments, necklaces, and ointments.
Incense, powdered incense, banners, flags, precious canopies, and all manner of ornamental implements were provided in full abundance according to whatever was requested.
After half a month had passed, on the final day, the king, ministers, elders, householders, the people of the city and towns, and all the non-Buddhists gathered together.

The time for his birth and subduing has arrived; he is accompanied by the great assembly, surrounded by the Heavenly Kings,
honored by the Dragon Kings, protected by the Yakṣa Kings, praised by the Gandharva Kings, bowed to with prostrations by the Asura Kings,
who scatter various precious flowers with pure hearts, and entreated with joy by the Kiṃnara Kings and Mahoraga Kings.
The king gazed with single-minded devotion as [the Buddha] entered that assembly.

At that time, the crown prince and the great multitude saw from afar the Buddha approaching, his appearance sublime and extraordinary, his sense faculties tranquil and composed like a well-trained elephant; his mind free from defilement like a pure pond;
manifesting great supernormal powers, displaying great mastery, and revealing great majestic virtue, adorned with various marks and signs of excellence.
His body emitted a great radiance that universally illuminated the world; from all his pores issued clouds of fragrant flames that shook immeasurable Buddha-fields in the ten directions.

Wherever they reached, they rained down all manner of ornaments. Through the Buddha’s majestic deportment and the Buddha’s merits, sentient beings who beheld him felt their minds purified and filled with joy, and their afflictions were extinguished. At that time, the Great...

"Welcome, World-Honored One! Welcome, Sugata! We pray that you will compassionately accept us and take your place upon this seat.
Through the Buddha's supernatural power, the devas of the Pure Abodes immediately transformed this seat into a fragrant maṇi lotus.
The Buddha sat upon his seat, and the assembly of bodhisattvas likewise took their seats, surrounding him on all sides.
At that time, all sentient beings in the assembly, by virtue of seeing the Tathāgata, had their suffering extinguished and their obstacles removed, becoming capable of receiving the noble Dharma.

ten thousand sentient beings dwelt in the path of the Mahāyāna, entered the conduct of Samantabhadra, and fulfilled their great vows. At that very moment, in each of the ten directions...
Beings as numerous as the atoms within a hundred buddha-fields attained mental discipline regarding the Mahāyāna;

Son of the Buddha, you should know that at that time I constantly acted for the benefit of all sentient beings, without attachment to the three realms and without seeking any fruit."
He was retributively free from craving for fame or reputation, had no desire to praise himself or disparage others, and was unstained by attachment to any sensory objects.

He was without fear; he merely adorned the essential path of the Mahāyāna, constantly delighted in contemplating the gateway to all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*), and attained this liberation through the practice of asceticism. "Son of the Buddha, what do you think? At that time, those five..."

journeys to the site of enlightenment, turnings of the wheel of the True Dharma, preaching of the sūtras, languages, voices,
radiances, assemblies, lifespans, durations of the Dharma, and even the names of those sinful beings whom I regard as my own children are each distinct and different.
The "Saviors" are Krakucchanda and the other thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, as well as the millions of asaṃkhyeya great Bodhisattvas,

who have now set their minds upon anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in the presence of the Tathāgata Amitavīryabalakīrtiguṇajñāna and are currently practicing and cultivating the Bodhisattva path in the lands of the ten directions.
This Bodhisattva who teaches and transforms sentient beings, causing them to give rise to roots of goodness and liberation, was at that time King Prasenajit;
the great master of debate, Sañjayin the Nirgrantha, was at that time the king’s courtiers and their retinue;
and those sixty thousand disciples of the Nirgrantha, together with their teacher, came and erected a banner of great debate to discuss with the Buddha, only to be entirely subdued.
Regarding those who have been granted the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, all these people shall indeed become Buddhas;

their Buddha-lands, their eons, and their names will each be distinct. Son of the Buddha, at that time, after I had saved these beings from their offenses, my parents permitted me to renounce my kingdom, wife, children, and wealth for the sake of the Sound of the Wheel of Dharma.

Having left the household life to study the Way under the Buddha Ākāśapradīparāja, he purified his Brahma-conduct for five hundred years and immediately attained the accomplishment of one million dhāraṇīs,
one million supernormal powers, one million treasuries of Dharma, and one million forms of courageous and diligent effort for seeking all-knowledge;
he purified one million gates of endurance and increased one million minds of contemplation.
By means of the power of a million bodhisattvas, they enter a million gates of bodhisattva wisdom,
attain a million gates of *prajñāpāramitā*, behold a million Buddhas of the ten directions, and give rise to a million great vows of a bodhisattva; in every thought-moment,
they illuminate a million Buddha-fields in each of the ten directions, and in every thought-moment, they recollect the past and future kalpas of the worlds in the ten directions.
In every thought-moment, the millions of Buddhas know the oceans of transformations of the millions of Buddhas throughout the worlds of the ten directions;

and in every thought-moment, they behold all sentient beings within the millions of worlds of the ten directions— those in their various realms of existence, according to the karma they have received,
at the time of birth and the time of death, whether in good or evil destinies, with beautiful or ugly forms— and they perceive the various minds of those sentient beings.
I clearly understood all their various desires, various faculties, various karmic habits, and various accomplishments.
Son of the Buddha, after my life ended at that time, I was reborn once again in that royal family as a Wheel-Turning King.
Following the parinirvāṇa of the Tathāgata Dharmacakra-ghoṣa-gaganapradīpa-rāja, I immediately encountered [the next Buddha] here.

Having served and made offerings to the Tathāgata Dharmakūṭarāja, he next became Śakra; in this very place of enlightenment, he encountered the Tathāgata Devendragarbha, whom he approached and made offerings to.

Next, as the King of the Yāma Heaven, he encountered the Tathāgata Mahāpṛthivībalaparvata in this very world, whom he approached and made offerings to. Next, as the King of the Tuṣita Heaven, in this very world...
Next, as the King of the Heaven of Delighting in Emanations, he encountered and made offerings to the Tathāgata Dharmacakra-prabhāsvara-ghoṣarāja;
subsequently, as the King of the Heaven of Enjoyment of Others' Emanations, he encountered and made offerings to the Tathāgata Gaganajñānarāja in this very world;
and finally, as the King of the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Emanations, he encountered and made offerings to the Tathāgata Abhedyadhvaja in this very world.
Next, he became an asura king, where in this very world he encountered the Tathāgata Sarvadharmameghasvararāja, whom he approached and made offerings to.
Next, he became a Brahmā king, where in this very world he encountered the Tathāgata Samantavyūhābhāsadharmaghoṣa, whom he approached and made offerings to.
O Son of the Buddha, within this Good Light eon of the Jewel Radiance world, there were ten thousand...
When Buddhas appeared in the world, I approached, served, and made offerings to them all. Subsequently, there was an eon named Sunlight, in which sixty billion Buddhas appeared in the world;
the first Tathāgata was named Mountain of Wondrous Features (*Lakṣaṇaparvata*).
At that time, I was a king named Great Wisdom (*Mahāmati*), and I served and made offerings to that Buddha. Following him, there was a Buddha named Appearance of Perfection (*Pūrṇavyūha*).
When the Buddha Pūrṇaskandha appeared, I was a householder who attended upon and made offerings to him;
next, when the Buddha Vimalaketu appeared, I was a minister who attended upon and made offerings to him;

next, when the Buddha Vikramadhara appeared, I was a king of the asuras who attended upon and made offerings to him; next, when the Buddha Merudhvaja appeared, I was a tree deity who attended upon him.
Following Poṣa, there was a Buddha named Vimalabāhu; I served and made offerings to him as a merchant leader (*sārthavāha*).
Following him, there was a Buddha named Siṃhavikrāntagāmin; I served and made offerings to him as a city deity (*nagaradevatā*). Following him, there was a Buddha named Ratnaśikhin;
I served and made offerings to him as the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa. Following him, there was a Buddha named Anuttara.

Dharmakīrti, I was the Gandharva King and attended upon and made offerings to him. Subsequently, there appeared a Buddha named Light-Radiant Crown (Prabhāsa-mukuṭa), and I was the Kumbhāṇḍa King and attended upon and made offerings to him.
During that eon, sixty billion Tathāgatas appeared in the world in this successive order; at each of those Buddhas' abodes, I constantly assumed various bodies [to serve them].
Approaching, making offerings to, teaching, and bringing to fulfillment immeasurable sentient beings, they attain at each and every Buddha various gates of samādhi,
various gates of dhāraṇī, various gates of supernormal powers, various gates of eloquence, various gates of all-knowledge,
various gates of the light of Dharma, and various gates of wisdom, illuminating the various worlds of the ten directions.
Entering into oceans of various Buddha-fields, they behold oceans of various Buddhas, which are pure, accomplished, increased, and vast—
just as if they had personally approached and made offerings to that many Buddhas within this eon, or had personally approached, made offerings to,
and listened to all the Buddhas who appeared in the world throughout as many eons as there are atoms in all places and all oceans of worlds.
Hearing the Dharma being taught, receiving it with faith, and upholding it is likewise so;
in this way, at the abodes of all such Tathāgatas, one cultivates this gate of liberation and further attains immeasurable skillful means of liberation.
At that time, the Night Goddess Sarvasattvatrāṇaśaraṇadā, wishing to restate the meaning of this liberation, spoke these verses for Sudhana:
He said:
"With a heart of joy, faith, and delight, you ask about this inconceivable dharma of liberation.
Relying on the power of the Tathāgata’s protective mindfulness, I shall proclaim it for you; you should listen and receive it."
In the past, across boundless and vast eons, exceeding the number of atoms in an ocean of lands, there was a world named Jewel Light. Within it, there was an eon called Good Light;
during this Great Eon of Good Light, ten thousand Tathāgatas appeared in the world.
I have approached and made offerings to them all, and from them I studied this liberation. At that time,
there was a royal capital named Priyavyūha (Joyous Adornment), vast, level, and exceedingly beautiful,
inhabited by sentient beings of various karmic conditions— some with pure minds and some who committed evil.
At that time there was a king named Prabhāsa, who always governed all living beings with the True Dharma.
His crown prince was named Sudānta; his physical form was upright and he was endowed with all the marks of excellence.
At that time, there were immeasurable criminals whose bodies were bound in prison, destined for execution.
Upon seeing this, the Crown Prince gave rise to compassion and addressed the King, entreating him for clemency.
Then the ministers spoke together to the King: "Now this Crown Prince endangers the kingdom;
such a criminal ought to be executed. How can you seek to save them all and grant them exemption?"
At that time, King Prasenajit said to the crown prince: "You must save him; you shall receive his retribution yourself.

The prince’s compassionate concern grew even deeper, and he vowed to save all sentient beings without ever retreating or fearing. Then the king’s queen, court ladies, and others all came to the king's presence and addressed him, saying: [The king] said to the crown prince: "You must save him; you shall receive his retribution yourself. The prince’s compassionate concern grew even deeper, And he vowed to save all sentient beings without ever retreating or fearing. Then the king’s queen, court ladies, and others All came to the king's presence and addressed him, saying:
"I pray that you grant the Prince half a month to practice the merit of giving to sentient beings.
Having heard this, the King immediately granted his permission. He established a great assembly of almsgiving to relieve the poor and destitute;
there were no sentient beings who did not arrive, and whatever they requested was provided to them all.
Thus, as the half-month drew to a close and the time for the Prince’s execution was at hand,
hundreds of thousands of millions of people gazed upon him together, all wailing in lamentation.
Knowing that the faculties of the multitude were about to ripen, that Buddha came to this assembly to transform all living beings.
Manifesting the great adornment of miraculous transformations, there is none who does not approach and revere him;
with a single voice and skillful means, the Buddha preaches the sutras that universally illuminate the lamp of Dharma,
so that the minds of immeasurable beings become supple and they all receive the prediction of their enlightenment.
Prince Śubha-vinīta gave rise to joy and conceived the aspiration for unexcelled, perfect enlightenment;
he vowed to serve the Tathāgata and become a refuge for all sentient beings.
He then immediately left the household life to dwell under the Buddha’s guidance, practicing the path to omniscience in all its aspects.
At that time, one attains this liberation, With great compassion extensively saving all living beings;
Abiding therein for oceans of kalpas, One contemplates the true nature of all phenomena,
Constantly rescuing sentient beings from the sea of suffering, Thus practicing the path to enlightenment.
All the Buddhas who appear throughout the kalpas, I serve them all without exception;
With a mind of pure faith and resolve, I hear, uphold, and protect all the teachings they proclaim.
Furthermore, throughout oceans of immeasurable and boundless kalpas, As numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, I practice thus.
I shall make offerings to every single Buddha appearing in the world,
just as I have done; I recall that in the past, when I was a prince, seeing sentient beings in prison,
I vowed to sacrifice my body to rescue and protect them, and by means of that, I realized this gate of liberation.
Throughout oceans of vast eons, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field,
I have constantly practiced and cultivated them so that they increase with every thought-moment; furthermore, I have attained boundless skillful means,
through which I have beheld all the Tathāgatas therein and received their awakening.
May I increase and clarify this liberation, as well as its various powers of skillful means.
Throughout immeasurable billions of eons, I shall study this inconceivable gateway of liberation.
The ocean of all Buddhas' teachings is boundless; I am able to drink it all in at once.
The bodies of all the lands throughout the ten directions enter everywhere without obstruction;
The various names of the realms of the three periods of time are fully understood in every thought-moment, leaving nothing behind.
The oceans of all Buddhas existing throughout the three periods of time are clearly seen one by one, exhaustively and without remainder.
They are also able to manifest their physical forms and travel everywhere to the abodes of those Tathāgatas;
furthermore, throughout all lands in the ten directions, before all Buddhas, the Teachers,
they rain down clouds of every kind of adornment as an offering to all the Unsurpassed Enlightened Ones.
Furthermore, with an infinite great ocean of questions, they entreat all the World-Honored Ones;
they receive and uphold, without ever forgetting, the clouds of sublime Dharma rained down by those Buddhas.
Moreover, in immeasurable lands throughout the ten directions, before the assemblies of all Tathāgatas, they [perform these acts].
Seated upon a throne adorned with myriad wonders, you manifest various supernormal powers;
furthermore, throughout the infinite lands of the ten directions, you display all manner of miraculous transformations.
From a single body you manifest infinite bodies, and within those infinite bodies you manifest a single body.
Furthermore, from each and every pore, they emit countless great rays of light;
through various skillful means, they extinguish the fires of affliction within sentient beings.
Moreover, from each and every pore, they manifest clouds of immeasurable transformation bodies.
Pervading all worlds throughout the ten directions, They rain down the Dharma everywhere to deliver all beings.
All the children of the Buddhas in the ten directions Enter this inconceivable gate of liberation;
Throughout all future eons until the very end, They dwell securely, practicing the bodhisattva path.
According to their inclinations, he preaches the Dharma for them, causing them all to remove the net of false views;
he reveals the path of the gods and the two vehicles, as well as the Tathāgata’s omniscience and the places where all sentient beings take birth, manifesting infinite and diverse bodies.
Manifesting myriad forms identical to all classes of beings, They preach the Dharma universally according to their minds.
If one attains this gate of liberation, Then they abide in an ocean of boundless merit.
Like the number of atoms in an ocean of lands, It is inconceivable and immeasurable.
"Noble son, I know only this gate of liberation for teaching and transforming sentient beings to cause them to produce roots of goodness.

they thoroughly understand the self-nature of all phenomena, skillfully observe all phenomena, and attain the realization of non-self."
How can I now know or describe that ocean of merit— his wisdom that realizes selflessness, his teaching and taming of all sentient beings without ever ceasing,
his mind constantly dwelling in the non-dual Dharma-gate, his universal entry into the ocean of all speech and expression,

"O son of good family, in this Jambudvīpa there is a grove named Lumbinī. In that grove there is a deity named Guṇakāraṇḍavyūhā.

The section on the distinctions manifested by the night goddess whom the deity perceives is divided into two parts. First, from "At that time, Sudhana...
down to this point, fifteen lines and a half of scripture clarify how Sudhana beholds the night goddess, prostrates with his five limbs touching the ground, and gives rise to ten kinds of mind.
This part is further divided into three sections. From "Having given rise to these minds... down to the verse, there are six [lines].

(4) At that time, Sudhana [continued] down to attaining *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

The *Avivartya-ṣaṭṣaṣṭi-gāthā-sūtra* clarifies the names of the Dharma-gates answered by the Night Goddess to Sudhana, as well as the section on the inexhaustible manifestation of various physical bodies upon awakening to these gates. Part Five:
"O Sons of Good Family, as you have asked, from what time did [she] first resolve for Bodhicitta and cultivate the practices of a Bodhisattva, until finally fulfilling the Great..."
Regarding the "Vow to Accomplish All Powers," there are thirty-seven practices explained in the sutra. The Night Goddess told the Bodhisattva Sudhana:
"The wheel of wisdom is far removed from all realms of conceptual discrimination;

it cannot be categorized by birth and death, nor by long and short, defilement and purity, broad and narrow, much and little, or by objects of knowledge. O Son of the Buddha, in the distant past, beyond oceans of worlds..."

From this point down to the verse, there are five and a half pages of scripture. This section clarifies the Night Goddess’s response to Sudhana regarding how long it has been since he first resolved his mind on enlightenment.
The subsequent section consists of verses in which the Night Goddess reiterates the preceding teaching;
the following is an explanation of the meaning according to the text. When Sudhana saw that Night Goddess seated amidst the great assembly, she was universally manifesting all palaces.
The lion throne of the treasury of the maṇi king, which universally manifests throughout the lands of the dharma-realm and is covered above by a net of maṇi jewels,
represents the essence of effortless wisdom— pure and stainless— which serves as a throne constantly manifesting within the palaces of all humans,
devas, nāgas, and spirits; the maṇi jewel net covering it above represents this effortlessness.
This wisdom constantly extends the net of teachings; this clarifies that it is accomplished through the retribution of wisdom.

Thus, it manifests the reflected images of the sun, moon, and stars within its body, and manifests according to the minds of sentient beings so that all may universally behold it. The clarity of the body is attained through the retribution of wisdom;
its seat is likewise like the essence of wisdom, capable of manifesting all dharmas. The multitude of dharmas thus manifested is as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field.
As explained in detail in the text below, Sudhana’s prostration with his five limbs touching the ground demonstrates the profound depth of his reverence for the Dharma.
That Sudhana obtained benefits is also as explained in detail in the text below. At that time, Sudhana asked the night goddess, "What is the name of this liberation you have attained?
The night goddess replied, "It is named 'Teaching and Transforming Sentient Beings to Cause Them to Produce Roots of Goodness. This clarifies the first point.
All sentient beings arise from the wisdom of non-nature; those who attain this wisdom find that all roots of goodness are spontaneously produced and all sufferings are naturally extinguished.

Because the essence of wisdom has no agent, sentient beings are deluded by it and falsely create various karmas within a state that is fundamentally free of suffering. If one penetrates this, suffering perishes and goodness flourishes.
Because they are born from this, it is called "teaching and transforming sentient beings to cause them to produce roots of goodness and liberation.

Furthermore, regarding this liberation, within the formless body, by means of the wisdom of non-abiding, one universally manifests the bodies of all Buddhas and sentient beings, as will be clearly explained in the text below.
Moreover, Sudhana asked the night goddess how she had generated the unsurpassed mind of great bodhicitta.
The night goddess replied that it has been as long as the wheel of a bodhisattva’s wisdom remains far removed from all objects of conceptualization;
it cannot be displayed through such distinctions as the length or brevity, defilement or purity, breadth or narrowness, or much or little within the cycle of birth and death,
for the wheel of a bodhisattva’s wisdom is by nature pure, free from the net of all conceptualization, and transcends the one.
Because all mountains of obstruction are universally transformed according to the needs of those to be converted, from this point onward six similes are presented:
first, the simile of the sun traveling through the sky without distinction between day and night;

second, the simile of the solar disc abiding over Jambudvīpa while its reflection appears within all jewels as well as in the rivers, oceans, and pure waters, such that no sentient being fails to see the sun.
1. Like a boatman who, amidst the great river, never relies upon this shore, that shore, or the middle of the stream;
2. Like the vast empty sky, wherein all worlds undergo formation and destruction while remaining without discrimination and fundamentally pure;
3. Like a wind-wheel of great vows that sustains the myriad phenomena; 4. Like the limbs and body of a magically conjured person.
Although it is fully present, it is without inhalation or exhalation, cold or heat, hunger or thirst, sorrow or joy, nor birth and death;
these six metaphors illustrate that the nature of wisdom is like space— self-sustaining, devoid of intrinsic nature, independent, and without location—
yet it constantly manifests before the assemblies of all Buddhas to teach and transform beings without ceasing, due to its previously made great vows.

Because it is supported by the wind-circle, from the phrase "O Son of the Buddha, in ages past beyond as many world-oceans as there are atoms" onwards, this night goddess speaks according to worldly convention regarding the duration of her initial resolve and the causes and conditions thereof;
this is established within the midst of illusion. As the *Sūtra* says: "In ages past, beyond as many world-oceans as there are atoms."
This clarifies that the "innumerable" serves as a designation for the number, while the essence of the innumerable itself remains attainable; the same applies to eons (*kalpa*).
There is an eon named "Excellent Light," which clarifies that it is a name established for the essence of non-effortful wisdom (*anābhoga-jñāna*).
The world-system is named "Jewel Light," which refers to a world-system where phenomena appear according to objects through non-effortful wisdom. Within that eon, there were ten thousand Buddhas.
As for those who appear in the world, they manifest in accordance with the faculties [of beings] through wisdom that is effortless;
this is called the appearance of ten thousand Buddhas. "Ten thousand" signifies that a single wisdom responds to ten thousand practices.

The name of the first Buddha is Dharmacakra-ghoṣa-gaganapradīpa-rāja Tathāgata, whose ten titles are fully perfected because he spontaneously benefits sentient beings through effortless wisdom. Constantly...
The sound of turning the Wheel of Dharma is like an echo in the void; having no place of dependence, it illuminates all sentient beings, and is thus called "Lamp of Wisdom.

Because his sovereign power is autonomous, he is called a "King. One who is "Endowed with the Ten Epithets" is so named because the application of his wisdom is all-pervasive, following his conduct to establish his title.
In that Jambudvīpa, there was a royal capital named Ratnavyūha (Jewel Adornment). This is...
The realm transformed by the King of Wisdom is named Jewel Adornment (*Ratnavyūha*). Not far to its east is a great forest named Sublime Light (*Sudarśana*).
The East symbolizes the place where wisdom transforms sentient beings to give rise to illumination; it also represents the Dharma.
The character for "East" (*dōng*) is formed by a wooden pin piercing the sun. The forest is named "Sublime Light" because its practice provides shade like a grove.

In this world-system, which is vast and renowned for its illumination that benefits sentient beings and is named *Prabhāsa-rucira* (Wondrous Light), there is a site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) named *Ratnakusuma* (Jewel Flower).
It is so named because it symbolizes the blossoming of the flower of the mind that practices altruism to benefit living beings.
Within that site of enlightenment is a lion throne made of the *sarvāvabhāsa-maṇi-padmagarbha* (Universal Radiance Mani Lotus Treasury). At that time, the Tathāgata was upon this [throne].

Regarding those who attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* upon the seat: because the nature of effortless wisdom (*anābhoga-jñāna*) constantly and universally illumines the *dharmadhātu*, and its self-nature is stainless, this serves as the seat.
Since the essence of this wisdom is neither produced nor destroyed, it is called "attaining unsurpassed *bodhi*.
To sit at the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*) for a full hundred years—wherein "hundred" symbolizes the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) within a single stage—is the meaning.

The ten [sets of] ten pāramitās are fulfilled. Furthermore, regarding the progression from this stage to the subsequent stages, one passes through the nine bhūmis with each being the fulfillment of a hundred pāramitās;
because the tenth bhūmi is the fulfillment of the Buddha-stage itself, one hundred [pāramitās] are established as the successive steps.
Below this, King Prasenajit is the object governed by wisdom and the sphere of the practice of loving-kindness; the King and...
The Crown Prince’s raising of the signs of good and evil to manifest the skillful means of a compassionate mind: the King’s name was Jyotiṣprabha (勝光), and his wisdom was skilled in subduing;
the Crown Prince was one who practiced the conduct of compassion. Having already transcended all realms of suffering, this is the stage of compassion and mercy practiced by wisdom.
As follows: he gathered five hundred great ministers who wished to harm him, and now [he] brings them forth.

Devadatta and his five hundred followers—these individuals, having been transformed by the Buddha’s teaching, shall attain Buddhahood in the future world-system called *Sudarśana*, after an interval of kalpas as numerous as the atoms within Mount Sumeru; they shall become five hundred Buddhas, attaining enlightenment in succession.
Furthermore, those sinful persons whom I have saved shall become the Buddhas such as Krakucchanda and others of the *Bhadrakalpa*.

The Thousand Buddhas of the Kalpa are Krakucchanda—here translated as "One Who Has Already Cut Off What Should Be Cut Off"—along with one million asaṃkhyeya bodhisattvas, all of whom are currently practicing the bodhisattva path throughout the ten directions. King Prasenajit is now the great master of treatises, the Nirgrantha Saccaka.
As for this Nirgrantha Saccaka, he is a non-Buddhist (tīrthika) who goes naked, starving himself, and does not wear clothing.

The palace attendants and kinsmen bound by food, as well as those sixty thousand disciples of the Nirgranthas—these and others above are, in total, the persons who have achieved the realm transformed by the Wisdom-King.

O Son of the Buddha, at that time, when I had saved the sinners and my parents permitted my renunciation, this signified that the essence of the stage of wisdom is pure and untainted; thus it is called "Renunciation."
Those who leave the household life through effort leave home under the Buddha Lamp-King (Dīpaṃkara) in the void to study the Way;
for five hundred years they purely cultivate the Brahma-conduct and immediately achieve one million *dhāraṇīs*.

These "five hundred years" symbolize the essence of effortless wisdom (*anābhoga-jñāna*) which pervades the five stages; it is simply that their development differs in terms of ripening and maturation. This refers to the first Buddha.

Including this initial Buddha, there are nineteen Buddhas who appear in succession; this clarifies that upon reaching the eighth stage (*bhūmi*), one trains in the wisdom of effortlessness (*anābhoga-jñāna*) to learn the ten powers (*daśabala*) of a Buddha and become a Buddha oneself, thus totaling twenty Buddhas.

This is because ascending to the ninth and tenth stages constitutes the fruition of Buddhahood, and since the fruits of these latter two stages are subsumed within this eighth stage, they are included herein.
Within the stages, the wisdom of non-effort—that is, the fruit of Buddhahood of the ten stages—is non-dual;

therefore, nineteen Buddha-illuminations are established within these stages. Together with the wisdom of non-effort of the eighth stage, they constitute twenty, as they interpenetrate one another to symbolize that the practices of the ten stages are present within the eighth stage. The three periods of time are one within this.
Serving the Buddhas represents the body of practice; the initial emergence of ten thousand Buddhas represents the fulfillment of the ten thousand practices of the ninth stage (*navamī bhūmi*).

Next, the emergence of sixty billion Buddhas within the *Suprabha* eon represents the six positions within the tenth stage (*daśamī bhūmi*), wherein cause and fruit are simultaneous and of one essence, without before or after.
The above meaning clarifies that this is by means of the Wisdom of Universal Radiance (*samantaprabhā-jñāna*).

The manner of establishing the practice for benefiting sentient beings— characterized by the sovereign wisdom of great compassion that spontaneously advances the essence [of the path] to benefit others—
and the application of the methods for rescuing sentient beings through the initiation of altruistic conduct, are set forth so that later students may emulate them as previously described; or,
following the establishment of one hundred Buddhas within each stage (*bhūmi*), one, two, or three more may subsequently be established.
Regarding the four Buddhas, this generally clarifies that practice is established according to stages; thus, within practice there is fruition.

Even if one were to perceive a Buddha external to the fruition of one's own practice, it would not be separate from what is perceived through one's own practice. Therefore, when practice and its direction are seen, this is precisely the True Buddha (*tathāgata*).

As for those perceived only through formal aspiration, they appear temporarily as an emanation and then vanish; these are the Transformation Buddhas (*nirmāṇa-buddha*). This is because [the True Buddha] is suchness in the very midst of phenomena.
In principle, it is said that the twenty-eight marks are incomplete by four, failing to reach the thirty-two marks;

this indicates that the eighth stage lacks the fourfold causes and effects of the ninth and tenth stages, as each stage contains both the causal factors of its own proper position (*samyaktva-avasthā*) and those directed toward the subsequent fruit. Thus, all worldly...

Those who have approached and made offerings to all the Buddhas appearing in the world throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms within oceans of realms possess the wisdom of non-action, which pervades everywhere such that there is no dharma that is not Buddha; for the Buddha is itself the Dharma.
Throughout the void of the ten directions, there is no interval or gap, and even the tip of a needle or a hair is not anything other than all dharmas and all Buddhas; it is simply this.
Even a speck of dust that is neither defiled nor pure is not the mind; this is seeing the Buddha when sealed with the eye of wisdom.
The following section of verses reiterates the aforementioned Dharma as it is fully contained within the text itself.

"Good son, I only know this method of teaching and transforming sentient beings to cause them to give rise to roots of goodness and liberation," and so forth—this is the passage that extols his virtues and advances him [in the path].

In the eighth Immovable Ground (*acalā-bhūmi*), the spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*)— with the perfection of aspiration (*praṇidhāna-pāramitā*) as the primary factor and the other nine as its companions—
remedies the obstacle regarding the lack of mastery in teaching the Dharma within effortless wisdom (*anābhoga-jñāna*), thereby causing one to attain such mastery. Second,
in the section on "Examining Qualities and Advancing," from the passage beginning with "Thus, O Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas" down to the point of taking leave.
There are eleven lines and a half of scripture in this section, which is divided into four parts: first, an examination of the virtues of his advancement;
second, an indication of the location where the spiritual friend resides, stating, "In this Jambudvīpa, there is a grove named Lumbinī";
third, the mention of the spiritual friend’s name, "Wondrous Virtue Perfect Light" (Miaode Yuanman Guang); and fourth, the expression of reverence and departure.

The statement that there is a grove in Jambudvīpa refers to the fact that when one cultivates the dharma of the ninth stage, the Ground of Excellent Intelligence (*sādhumatī-bhūmi*), its light universally rescues and provides shade for all sentient beings throughout the ten directions;

because its practice and realization are vast, the cycle of birth and death is like a garden and the myriad practices are like a forest, it is thus named. "Lumbinī" is translated here as "Grove of Supreme Joy."
Because he brings joy to sentient beings through the Dharma of wisdom, this grove is also the garden where the Tathāgata manifested his descent and birth;
it clarifies that a Bodhisattva of the eighth stage descends from Tuṣita Heaven not for the purpose of dwelling in a womb, but for the purpose of taking birth.
Within the ninth stage, one cultivates the wisdom that benefits humans and devas.

Because it fulfills the wisdom of all sentient beings, it is called "receiving birth"; because it receives and studies the wisdom of all Buddhas to cause the fulfillment of all sentient beings, as clarified by the sutra itself, there is a spirit named "Perfected Wondrous Virtue" (*Guṇakāraṇḍavyūha*), which clarifies that on the Stage of Excellent Wisdom (*Sādhumatī-bhūmi*), wondrous wisdom is perfected.
A "spirit" (*deva*) is so called because, through compassion and wisdom, it is well able to expound the teachings.
The deity is the Night Goddess Wondrous Virtue Perfect Light of the Lumbinī Grove in Jambudvīpa, who presides over the Stage of Excellent Wisdom.
[Sūtra] At that time, after the youth Sudhana had attained the bodhisattva liberation of "Protecting All Sentient Beings through the Power of Great Vows and Diligence" from the night goddess,
he recollected it, practiced it, mastered it, and increased it. Proceeding gradually on his journey,
he arrived at the Lumbinī grove and searched everywhere until he saw the goddess Viśvāmitrā dwelling amidst the adornments of all the jewel trees.
Seated upon a lion throne of precious lotuses within a magnificent pavilion, surrounded by twenty billion nayutas of devas who paid him respectful homage,
he was preaching the *Sūtra on the Ocean of Bodhisattva Births*, causing them all to be born into the family of the Tathāgata and to increase the ocean of the bodhisattvas' great merit.
When Sudhana saw this, he prostrated at his feet and stood before him with palms joined.

He addressed [the Buddha], saying: "O Great Sage, I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva practices the bodhisattva conduct, how they are born into the family of the Tathāgata, and how they become a great light for the world.
That deity replied: "Good son, there are ten kinds of treasuries of birth for bodhisattvas; if a bodhisattva accomplishes these dharmas..."

Thus, one is born into the family of the Tathāgatas, and in every thought-moment, the roots of goodness of a bodhisattva increase—without weariness, without slackening, without aversion, without retreating, without interruption, and without loss;
free from all delusions, one gives rise to no mind of cowardice, inferiority, affliction, or regret;
one proceeds toward omniscience, enters the gateway of the Dharma-realm, develops the vast mind, increases the perfections, and accomplishes the unsurpassed enlightenment of all Buddhas.

Tiṣya, entering the stage of the Tathāgata in this world, attaining supreme supernormal powers, and having the teachings of all Buddhas constantly present before him, he accords with the realm of the true meaning of omniscience. What are these eleven?
First, the womb of birth through the vow to constantly make offerings to all Buddhas; second, the womb of birth through the arousal of the bodhicitta; third, the contemplation of all phenomena...
Fourth is the treasury of birth through diligent practice at the gates; fifth is the treasury of birth through universally illuminating the three periods of time with a profound and pure mind;
sixth is the treasury of birth through the light of equanimity; seventh is the treasury of birth through the light of the Buddha’s power;
eighth is the treasury of birth through contemplating the gateway of universal wisdom; ninth is the treasury of universal manifestation.
The tenth is the treasury of the adornment of taking birth. Entering the stage of the Tathāgata is the treasury of the adornment of taking birth.

Good son, what is called the treasury of taking birth through the vow to always make offerings to all Buddhas? Good son, when a bodhisattva first resolves upon the mind of enlightenment, they make this vow:
"I shall respect, revere, and make offerings to all Buddhas; I shall never tire of seeing the Buddhas."

Constantly giving rise to love and joy toward all Buddhas, always generating profound faith, and cultivating all manner of meritorious virtues without ever ceasing—this is called the Bodhisattva’s “Womb of Rebirth for the Initial Accumulation of Roots of Goodness for the Sake of All-Knowledge.
What is meant by the “Womb of Rebirth for Generating the Bodhicitta”? Son of good family, it is when this Bodhisattva generates the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

The mind conceives the thought of giving rise to great compassion for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings; it gives rise to the thought of making offerings to the Buddhas for the sake of ultimate service;

it gives rise to the thought of universally seeking the True Dharma because of having no stinginess toward anything; it gives rise to the thought of vast aspiration for the sake of seeking all-knowledge;
it gives rise to the thought of immeasurable loving-kindness for the sake of universally gathering in all sentient beings; and it gives rise to the thought of never abandoning a single being.
Because they have donned the firm armor of the vow to seek all-knowledge for the sake of all sentient beings, they give rise to a mind free from flattery and deceit;

because they attain knowledge as it truly is, they give rise to a mind that acts according to their words; because they cultivate the Bodhisattva path, they give rise to a mind that does not deceive the Buddhas;
because they protect the great vows of all Buddhas, they give rise to a mind of universal equal vows to transform sentient beings until the end of the future.

Because they do not rest, bodhisattvas, by means of such merits of the bodhicitta as are equal in number to the atoms within Buddha-fields, attain birth in the family of the Tathāgatas; this is called the second treasury of the bodhisattva’s taking birth.
What is called the treasury of taking birth through diligent cultivation of the gate of contemplating all dharmas? Good son, this bodhisattva-mahāsattva gives rise to the contemplation of one...
The mind that arises from the ocean of all dharma-gates; the mind that arises for the sake of the path to the perfection of omniscience through dedication;
the mind that arises with right mindfulness free from error; the mind that arises as the purity of the ocean of samādhis of all bodhisattvas;
the mind that arises to cultivate and accomplish all bodhisattva merits; the mind that arises to adorn all bodhisattva paths; and the mind that arises seeking the great vigor of omniscience.
To cultivate all meritorious virtues with a mind as tireless as a blazing kalpa-fire;
to give rise to the resolve to practice the conduct of Samantabhadra and to transform all sentient beings; to give rise to the resolve to skillfully train in all modes of dignified deportment;
to cultivate the merits of a bodhisattva while relinquishing all possessions and abiding in the true mind of non-possession—this is the third birth of a bodhisattva.
"Good son, what is meant by the 'Treasury of Birth Illuminating the Three Times with a Profound and Pure Mind'?
Good son, this bodhisattva possesses a pure and superior mind; they receive the light of the Tathāgata’s enlightenment and enter the ocean of a bodhisattva’s skillful means.
