Their mind is as firm and solid as a diamond; they renounce all rebirths within the realms of existence and accomplish all the qualities of a Buddha."
Possessing sovereign power to cultivate sublime practices, endowed with the faculties of a bodhisattva, their mind is luminous and pure;

their power of aspiration is unshakable, and they are constantly protected and remembered by all Buddhas. They destroy all mountains of obstacles and serve as a place of refuge for all sentient beings.
This is called the fourth treasury of birth of a bodhisattva. What is meant by "reception of equal radiance"?
"O noble son Jāti-kośa, this bodhisattva is endowed with all practices to universally transform sentient beings;
he is able to relinquish everything that exists, abides in the realm of the Buddha’s ultimate pure precepts, is fully possessed of the dharma of patience,
achieves the light of the dharmas of the Buddhas' patience, advances toward omniscience through great diligence, reaches the other shore, and cultivates all meditative concentrations."
Attaining the Samādhi of the Universal Door and perfecting pure wisdom, they illuminate all phenomena with the light of the sun of wisdom;
obtaining unimpeded vision, they behold the oceans of Buddhas and penetrate the true nature of all dharmas.
All those in the world who see them rejoice, for they are well able to cultivate the Dharma-gate of reality as it is. This is called the Bodhisattva’s fifth treasury of birth. What is its name?

"O son of good family, this is the treasury of birth for those born into the family of the Tathāgatas: these bodhisattvas are born into the family of the Tathāgatas and dwell together with all Buddhas;
they accomplish all profound dharma-gates, attain the pure great vows of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, and acquire the same roots of goodness as all Buddhas.
They share the same single essence with all Tathāgatas and possess the white, pure goodness of supramundane conduct."

The Dharma-door of Abiding in Vast Meritorious Qualities, entering all samādhis, beholding the spiritual power of the Buddhas, purifying all sentient beings according to their needs for transformation, responding to questions with inexhaustible eloquence—this is the sixth treasury of birth of a Bodhisattva.
What is called the Treasury of Birth of the Radiance of the Buddha’s Power? Good son, this Bodhisattva enters deeply...
By the power of the Buddha, they travel through all buddha-fields with minds free from regression; they serve and honor the assemblies of bodhisattvas without weariness;
they understand that all phenomena are like illusions; they know that all worlds are like things seen in a dream;
they perceive all forms and appearances as being like light and shadows; their supernormal powers are like magical transformations; and all their births are entirely...
Like shadows, the teachings of all Buddhas are like echoes from a valley; they reveal the Dharma-realm to bring all beings to ultimate fulfillment.
This is the seventh birth-treasury of Bodhisattvas. What is called the birth-treasury of contemplating the gateways of universal wisdom?
Noble son, this Bodhisattva, dwelling in the stage of youthful truth, contemplates each and every gateway of omniscience, exhausting immeasurable eons to open them.
They manifest all the practices of bodhisattvas; they attain mastery over their minds within the profound samādhis of all bodhisattvas;

in every thought-moment, they are born in the presence of all Tathāgatas throughout the worlds of the ten directions; they enter non-differentiated meditative concentration regarding differentiated objects;
they possess differentiated wisdom regarding non-differentiated phenomena; and regarding immeasurable objects, they know them to be objectless.

Entering from a limited sphere into immeasurable spheres, they penetrate the vast and boundless nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), knowing that all worlds are merely provisional designations and that everything arises from the consciousness-mind. This is the eighth birth-treasury of Bodhisattvas.
What is called the "Birth-treasury of Universal Manifestation Adornments"? Good son, this Bodhisattva is able to adorn [all things] in various ways.
Adorning immeasurable Buddha-fields, they are universally able to manifest the bodies of all sentient beings and all Buddhas;
having attained fearlessness, they expound the pure Dharma, circulating throughout the Dharma-realm without obstruction.

According to the inclinations of their minds, they cause all to know and see, manifesting various practices for the realization of Bodhi, causing them to give rise to the unobstructed path of omniscience. Such as these...
Acting without missing the proper time, they constantly abide in the treasury of Vairocana’s wisdom;
this is the ninth birth-treasury of a bodhisattva. What is called the birth-treasury of entering the stage of the Tathāgata?
Good son, this bodhisattva receives the dharma of consecration from all the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time and universally knows all objects of experience.
The sequence of realms refers to knowing the sequence of the deaths and rebirths of all sentient beings throughout the past and future;
the sequence of the practices of all bodhisattvas; the sequence of the mental thoughts of all sentient beings; the sequence of the Tathāgatas of the three times attaining Buddhahood;
the sequence of teaching the Dharma through skillful means; and furthermore, knowing all that exists throughout the beginning, middle, and end.
The names and sequences of all kalpas, whether in the process of formation or destruction, are manifested according to what is necessary to transform and deliver sentient beings;
through the adornment of merit from manifesting the path to enlightenment, and by means of supernatural powers and skillful methods of preaching the Dharma, they subdue them.
This is the tenth treasury of birth of a bodhisattva. O Son of the Buddha, if a bodhisattva-mahāsattva cultivates and increases these ten dharmas until they are perfected...
When fulfillment is achieved, one is able to manifest various adornments within a single adornment;
thus adorning all lands, one guides, instructs, and awakens all sentient beings without ceasing throughout all future kalpas.
One expounds the various realms and various modes of maturation of the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas, which have been transmitted down through successive generations.
Measuring all phenomena, they manifest the inconceivable sovereign power of the Buddhas, which fills all of space and the dharma-realm;
they turn the wheel of Dharma within the ocean of the mental activities of all sentient beings; they manifest the attainment of Buddhahood in all worlds without interruption;
and through unspeakably pure speech and sounds, they teach all dharmas while abiding in the infinite.
Abiding in unimpeded penetration, he adorns the site of enlightenment with all dharmas;

according to the diverse inclinations and understandings of sentient beings, he manifests the attainment of Buddhahood and reveals the immeasurable, profound treasury of Dharma, teaching and bringing to fulfillment all the worlds.
At that time, the forest deity of Lumbinī, wishing to clarify this meaning further, by the Buddha’s spiritual power, universally observed the ten [directions].
Then he spoke in verse:
"With a supreme, stainless, and pure mind, Beholding all Buddhas without weariness,
Vowing to constantly make offerings until the end of the future— This is the treasury of birth for those of clear wisdom."
In all lands throughout the three periods of time, may all sentient beings and all Buddhas be completely delivered;
may they always gaze upon and serve this inconceivable treasury of birth,
never wearying of hearing the Dharma and joyfully contemplating it, remaining unimpeded throughout the three periods of time.
With body and mind as pure as space, this one of renowned name is a treasury of rebirth;
With a mind that dwells eternally in the ocean of great compassion, as firm as a diamond or a mountain of jewels,
And having thoroughly mastered the gateway to all-knowledge— this most excellent one is a treasury of rebirth.
Great compassion universally covers all beings; Sublime conduct constantly increases the ocean of the perfections.

With the light of the Dharma, he illuminates the multitudes; This heroic and valiant one is a treasury of rebirth, Thoroughly penetrating the nature of phenomena with an unimpeded mind, Born into the family of the Buddhas of the three times.

Universally entering the ocean of the dharma-realm in the ten directions, this treasury of birth of the wise ones is the pure dharma-body with unimpeded mind; universally visiting all lands throughout the ten directions,
there is nothing that is not accomplished through the power of all Buddhas— this is the inconceivable treasury of birth.
Having entered deep wisdom, they attain mastery; they also reach the ultimate realization of all samādhis and contemplate the gateway to omniscience as it truly is.
This true body is the treasury of birth, purifying all Buddha-lands and diligently practicing the methods for universally transforming sentient beings.
Manifesting the sovereign power of the Tathāgatas, this one of great fame possesses the treasury of birth;
having long practiced for omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), he swiftly enters the stage of the Tathāgata.
Fully knowing that the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*) is entirely unimpeded—this is the treasury of birth of these sons of the Buddha.
"Noble son, when a bodhisattva is endowed with these ten dharmas, they are born into the family of the Tathāgata and become a pure light for all the world.
Noble son, since immeasurable kalpas past, I have attained this liberation-door of sovereign birth.
Sudhana said, "Noble one, what is the scope of this liberation-door? He replied, "Noble son, I..."
First, he made this vow: "May I draw near to all Bodhisattvas at the time they manifest their descent into birth;

may I enter the immeasurable ocean of births of the Tathāgata Vairocana. By the power of this former vow, he was born in this world within the Lumbinī Grove of Jambudvīpa, where he focused his mind on when the Bodhisattva would descend to be born. After a hundred years had passed, the World-Honored One indeed appeared.
Descending from the Tuṣita Heaven to be born at this time, ten signs appeared within this grove. What are these eleven?
First, the ground of this garden suddenly became level of its own accord; all pits, hollows, mounds, and hills vanished entirely.
Second, the ground became composed of vajra, adorned with various jewels, and was free of tiles, rubble, thorns, stumps, and brushwood. Third, [the ground became] precious...

First, *tāla* trees stand in rows all around, their roots firmly planted down to the water's edge; second, sprouts of various fragrances grow forth, manifesting treasuries of various scents, with precious incense trees spreading wide to provide dense shade, such that all their fragrances surpass those of the heavens;

third, various exquisite flower garlands and precious ornaments are arranged in rows and distributed everywhere, filling all places; fourth, [the trees] stand in rows all around, their roots firmly planted down to the water's edge; fifth, sprouts of various fragrances grow forth, manifesting treasuries of various scents, with precious incense trees spreading wide to provide dense shade, such that all their fragrances surpass those of the heavens;
sixth, various exquisite flower garlands and precious ornaments are arranged in rows and distributed everywhere, filling all places. Sixth.
Seventh, all the various trees within the grove spontaneously blossomed with *maṇi* jewel flowers;
eighth, within all the ponds and pools, flowers spontaneously grew, emerging from the earth and spreading across the surface of the water;
ninth, at that time, within this forest, the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, and others dwelling in the desire and form realms of the Sahā world [gathered].
All the kings of the *kinnaras*, *mahoragas*, and *gandharvas* gathered there without exception,
standing with palms joined; ninthly, all the celestial maidens in this world, down to the daughters of the *mahoragas*,
were filled with joy and each held various offering implements, standing reverently before the *piplakṣa* tree.
Tenth, from the navels of all Buddhas of the ten directions, there radiates light named "Lamp of Sovereignty over the Birth of Bodhisattvas," which universally illumines this grove.
Within each ray of light, there appear all the miraculous manifestations of the Buddhas' births and the meritorious virtues of all bodhisattvas' births;
furthermore, the various voices and sounds of all Buddhas issue forth from them. This is...
When these ten kinds of auspicious signs appear within the grove, the celestial kings and others immediately know that a Bodhisattva is about to descend to be born.

Seeing these omens, I am filled with immeasurable joy. Son of good family, when Lady Māyā departed from the city of Kapilavastu and entered this grove, ten further kinds of radiant auspicious signs appeared, enabling all sentient beings to attain [liberation].
What are the ten lights of the Dharma? They are: the light of the treasury of all jewel-flowers; the light of the treasury of precious incense;
the light that issues forth the true and wondrous sounds from the blossoming of precious lotuses; the light of the initial resolve of Bodhisattvas in the ten directions;
the light of the spiritual transformations manifested by Bodhisattvas as they enter the various stages (*bhūmi*); and the light of the perfection of the *pāramitās* cultivated by all Bodhisattvas.
The light of the wisdom of all bodhisattvas’ fulfillment of great vows; the light of the wisdom of all bodhisattvas’ skillful means for teaching and transforming sentient beings;
the light of the wisdom of all bodhisattvas’ realization of the true reality of the dharma-realm;

and the light of all bodhisattvas attaining the sovereign power of a Buddha—manifesting birth, renouncing the world, and attaining perfect enlightenment. These ten lights universally illumine immeasurable worlds.

O son of good family, when the mind of sentient beings was thus disposed, at the time when Māyādevī sat beneath the Pippala tree, ten kinds of divine transformations were manifested as the Bodhisattva was about to be born. What are these ten?
Son of good family, at the time when the Bodhisattva was about to be born, the sons and daughters of the gods of the desire realm, as well as all those of the form realm...
The devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas,
and their retinues all gathered like clouds for the sake of making offerings.
The majesty and virtue of Lady Māyā were so preeminent that light radiated from every pore of her body, universally illuminating the trichiliocosm without any obstruction.

Obstructing all lights so that none appear, yet extinguishing the afflictions of all sentient beings and the sufferings of the evil realms—this is the first supernatural manifestation of the Bodhisattva as he is about to be born.
Furthermore, son of good family, at that time, within the womb of Lady Māyā, there appeared all the forms of the three thousandfold world-system; its ten billion [suns and moons]...
Within each of the Jambudvīpas, there were respective capitals and gardens, each with different names, all of which contained the Lady Māyā dwelling therein, surrounded by hosts of devas;
all these were manifested as inconceivable signs of supernatural transformation as the Bodhisattva was about to be born.
This was the second supernatural transformation of the Bodhisattva as he was about to take birth. Furthermore, it was excellent.

O noble son, within every pore of Lady Māyā appeared the sounds of all the Buddhas preaching the Dharma when the Tathāgata was practicing the bodhisattva path in the past, as well as his reverent offerings to all those Buddhas;
it was like the images of the sun, moon, stars, clouds, and thunder appearing in a clear mirror or in water. Māyā [appeared thus].
The pores of Queen Māyā’s body were likewise able to manifest the Tathāgata’s past causes and conditions;
this was the third supernormal transformation as the Bodhisattva was about to be born.
Furthermore, noble son, within each and every pore of Queen Māyā’s body, there appeared the worlds, cities, and towns where the Tathāgata resided while practicing the bodhisattva path in the past.

In villages, mountains, forests, rivers, and oceans, throughout the kalpas of sentient beings, whenever a Buddha appears in the world, they enter pure lands and take birth according to their lot, with lifespans long or short; relying on spiritual friends, they practice wholesome dharmas;
in every land and in every place of birth, the Lady Māyā is always their mother—all such things as these are present within a single pore without exception.
All these were manifested as the fourth supernatural transformation of the Bodhisattva when he was about to be born. Furthermore, noble son, within every single pore of Lady Māyā,
there appeared clearly and universally all the events of the Tathāgata’s past cultivation of the bodhisattva path—
specifically, the places where he was born, his physical characteristics and appearance, his clothing and food, and his experiences of suffering and joy.
To discern this clearly is the fifth supernatural manifestation of the Bodhisattva as he is about to be born. Furthermore, noble son, within every single pore of Lady Māyā’s body,

there appeared all the heads, eyes, ears, noses, lips, tongues, teeth, bodies, hands, feet, blood, flesh, sinews, and bones that the World-Honored One had sacrificed when practicing the perfection of giving in his past lives, including those most difficult to give away— whether to men or women.
He also saw his wives, concubines, cities, palaces, garments, necklaces, gold, silver, precious goods, and all such internal and external objects;
he likewise saw the appearance, voices, and locations of those who were to receive them.
This was the sixth supernormal transformation of the Bodhisattva as he was about to be born. Furthermore, noble son, when Lady Māyā entered this grove, her body—
Universally manifesting all the past Buddhas at the time of their entry into the mother’s womb—
including the lands, groves, garments, flower garlands, unguents, powdered incense, silken banners, flags, canopies, and all manner of precious adornments,
as well as the exquisite sounds of music, song, and chant— causing all sentient beings to universally see and hear these things; this is the Bodhisattva, being about to...
Furthermore, son of good family, at the time of his birth, when Queen Māyā entered this grove,
there issued forth from her body a palace and pavilion made of the king of *maṇi* jewels where the Bodhisattva resided,
surpassing all those of the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.
The dwelling place of all kings of men was covered above by jeweled nets, permeated everywhere with exquisite fragrances, and adorned with various jewels;
it was pure both inside and out, distinct in its various features without any confusion, and completely filled throughout the Lumbinī Grove.
This was the eighth miraculous manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born. Furthermore, O son of good family, Lady Māyā entered...
From his body, there then emerged ten times the number of unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of bodhisattvas,
as numerous as the atoms in a buddha-field; the physical forms, features, marks, radiance, deportment, majestic bearing, supernatural powers,
and retinues of all these bodhisattvas were entirely equal to those of the Bodhisattva Vairocana, without any difference, and they all appeared simultaneously.
To praise the Tathāgata is the ninth miraculous manifestation occurring when a Bodhisattva is about to be born. Furthermore, noble son,
when Lady Māyā was about to give birth to the Bodhisattva, suddenly before her, from the adamantine foundation,
there emerged a great lotus called the "Treasury of All Jewel Adornments," with a stem of vajra and filaments of various jewels.
Its pedestal was made of the king of wish-fulfilling jewels, and it had petals as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields.
All were composed of mani-jewels, covered above by jeweled nets and canopies, held aloft by all the celestial kings,
with all the dragon kings showering down rain of incense, and surrounded respectfully by all the yakṣa kings who scattered divine flowers.
The Gandharva King Adorned with All Flowers produced subtle and wondrous sounds, singing praises of the Bodhisattva’s past merits in making offerings to all Buddhas;
all the Asura Kings abandoned their hearts of pride and prostrated themselves in reverent salutation;
all the Garuḍa Kings hung down precious silk banners that filled the entirety of space; and all the Kiṃnara Kings gazed upon him with joy.
As they looked up and sang praises in verse for the virtues of the Bodhisattva, all the mahoraga kings gave rise to joy and sang in praise;
a universal rain of clouds adorned with every kind of jewel fell down. This was the tenth supernatural manifestation when the Bodhisattva was about to be born.
Son of Good Family, having thus displayed these ten kinds of signs in the Lumbinī Grove,
Subsequently, when the Bodhisattva was born from his mother’s side, the radiance of his physical marks was likewise like a pure solar disc appearing in the midst of space,
like auspicious clouds emerging from the summit of a high mountain, like lightning flashing amidst dense clouds,
or like a great torch being lit in the darkness of night. Good son, such was the Bodhisattva at that time.
At that time, although he manifested his initial birth, he had already fully realized that all phenomena are like dreams,
illusions, shadows, and images— without coming or going, neither arising nor ceasing. Good son,
when I saw the Buddha manifest various miraculous transformations upon his initial birth in the Lumbinī Grove within Jambudvīpa, this four-continent world system...
He saw the Tathāgata manifesting various miraculous transformations at his initial birth within the Lumbinī Grove in Jambudvīpa, among the ten billion four-continent worlds of the trichiliocosm;
he also saw immeasurable Buddha-fields within every single atom of the trichiliocosm, as well as hundreds of Buddha-worlds, thousands of Buddha-worlds, and so forth.
Within every single atom of all worlds in the ten directions, there are immeasurable Buddha-fields;
within all such Buddha-fields, Tathāgatas manifest birth and various supernatural transformations. Thus, moment after moment, this continues without interruption.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to that goddess: "O Great Goddess, how long has it been since you attained this liberation?"

He replied: "Good son, in the distant past, beyond kalpas as numerous as the atoms in a billion buddha-fields, and even further than that number of kalpas, there was a world named Universal Jewel and an eon named Joyful Delight, in which eighty nayutas of buddhas appeared.
The first of those buddhas was named Sovereign Merit Banner, complete with the ten titles; such was that world."
Within this world-system, there is a set of four continents named Wondrous Light Adornment.
In Jambudvīpa among those four continents, there is a royal capital named Sumeru Adornment Banner.
Therein dwells a king named Jewel Flame Eye, and the king’s queen is named Joyful Light. Noble son, in this world, Queen Māyā served as the mother for Vairocana.
The mother of that Tathāgata, Lady Joyful Light (*Priyakara*), who was the mother of the first Buddha in that world, was likewise, O son of good family.
When Lady Joyful Light was about to give birth to the Bodhisattva, she went with twenty billion nayutas of female attendants to the Golden Flower Garden (*Suvarṇapuṣpa-udyāna*).
Within that garden was a pavilion named *Ratnakūṭa* (Jewel Peak), and at its side—
There was a tree named Sarvārthasiddha; Lady Priyadarśanā climbed its branches and gave birth to the Bodhisattva.
The assembly of deva kings each held fragrant water and together bathed him. At that time, a wet nurse named Vimalaprabhā stood by his side.
Once he had been bathed, the assembly of deva kings handed him over to the wet nurse, who received him with reverence and gave birth to great joy.

Upon rejoicing, he immediately attained the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Universal Eye (*sarvabuddhanetra*). Having attained this samādhi, he universally beheld the infinite Buddhas of the ten directions.
He further attained the Bodhisattva liberation of sovereign mastery in manifesting birth in all places;
like the initial consciousness at conception, it was swift and unimpeded. Because he had attained this liberation, he beheld all Buddhas according to his original vows.
The mastery over birth through power is likewise so. Good son, what do you think? Was that wet nurse anyone else?

It was I myself. Since that time, in every thought-moment, I have constantly seen Vairocana Buddha manifesting the ocean of births as a bodhisattva and his sovereign spiritual powers for taming sentient beings, just as I see him now.

The Buddha Vairocana, by the power of his original vow, in every thought-moment manifests within this trichiliocosm and even within every atom of all worlds throughout the ten directions the miraculous transformations of a Bodhisattva’s birth; seeing all Buddhas in this same manner,
I reverently serve and make offerings to them, listen to the Dharma they preach, and practice according to what has been taught.
At that time, the goddess of the Lumbinī grove, wishing to further proclaim the meaning of this liberation, received the Buddha’s spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions,
and spoke in verse: "O Son of the Buddha,
regarding the profound realm of all Buddhas which you have asked about, you should now listen and receive it."
I shall explain the causes and conditions for this: Beyond eons as numerous as the atoms in billions of lands, there was an eon named Joyous Eighty-Nayuta.
A Tathāgata appeared in the world; the first of these Tathāgatas was named Sovereign Banner of Virtue.
While I was in the Golden Flower Garden, I beheld him on the day of his birth.
At that time, I served as his nurse, my wisdom being exceedingly sharp and keen. The various devas bestowed upon me the Bodhisattva’s golden body;

I then quickly took him up in my hands. Gazing intently, I could not see the crown of his head, for every mark of his physical form was perfectly complete, each one infinite and boundless—a stainless and pure body.
Adorned with the marks and signs of excellence, like a statue of exquisite jewels, one rejoices upon seeing them and contemplates those merits;

thus the ocean of manifold blessings increases swiftly. Witnessing these miraculous feats, one gives rise to the great bodhicitta, single-mindedly seeking the qualities of a Buddha and further expanding all great vows.
Purifying all lands and eliminating the three evil realms, I universally made offerings to countless Buddhas throughout the soils of the ten directions.
Cultivating my original vows, I rescued and liberated sentient beings from suffering.
In the presence of those Buddhas, I heard the Dharma and attained liberation, as numerous as the atoms within billions of lands.
Through practice over immeasurable eons, I have made offerings to every Buddha who appeared within those eons;
I have upheld their true Dharma and purified this ocean of liberation.
Having fully received the wheels of Dharma from as many past Honored Ones of Ten Powers as there are atoms in billions of lands, I have further illuminated this liberation.
In a single instant, I see within the atoms of this world-system each and every ocean of lands purified by a Tathāgata;
within each land there is a Buddha, manifesting his birth amidst a garden,
each displaying inconceivable and vast supernormal powers, or appearing in ways that are beyond thought.
I see all the bodhisattvas from billions of lands dwelling atop celestial palaces;
In immeasurable oceans of lands where they are about to realize the Buddha-enlightenment, I see all the Buddhas manifesting their births, surrounded by assemblies preaching the Dharma.
In a single thought-moment, I see billions of lands and bodhisattvas as numerous as atoms.
Leaving home and proceeding to the site of enlightenment, they manifest the realm of the Buddhas.
Within the atoms of every land, I see immeasurable Buddhas attaining the Way, each manifesting various skillful means to deliver sentient beings from suffering.
Within every single atom, all Buddhas turn the wheel of Dharma, doing so entirely with inexhaustible voices.
Universally raining down the nectar of the Dharma, as numerous as the atoms within billions of lands—
within each atom of every land, I see the Tathāgata manifesting parinirvāṇa; likewise, in such infinite lands,
the Tathāgatas manifest their birth, and I, having divided my body in its entirety, appear before them to offer worship.

In inconceivable oceans of lands, with their infinite varieties of realms, I manifest within them all and rain down the great rain of Dharma. O Son of the Buddha, I know this inconceivable door of liberation;
even in the course of immeasurable billions of eons, it could not be fully extolled.
"Noble son, I only know this liberation of the Bodhisattva’s mastery in manifesting birth throughout all places for immeasurable eons.
As for those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas who are able to take a single thought-moment as the treasury of all eons,
who contemplate all dharmas, and who manifest births through skillful means to universally make offerings to all Buddhas— I do not know their conduct."
Having attained ultimate penetration into all Buddha-dharmas, manifesting birth in all realms of existence, sitting upon lotus thrones before all Buddhas,
knowing the time when sentient beings should be delivered, manifesting births through skillful means to subdue them,
and displaying various spiritual transformations in all lands like reflections appearing before them— how shall I [attain this]?
"O noble son, you who are able to know and speak of those meritorious deeds, there is a woman of the Śākya clan in this city of Kapilavastu named Gopā;
go to her and ask how a bodhisattva teaches and transforms sentient beings while amidst birth and death.
Then, the youth Sudhana prostrated at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, gazed upon her with deep reverence, and took his leave.
Go. *The Combined Commentary on the New Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha*, Fascicle 111. Phonetic Transcription.
Lán (lú hán qiè). Wù (wǔ gǔ qiè). Luò (láng guǒ qiè). Fēng (fēng yīn). Jīng (xíng yīn). Qí (jū nì qiè). Fǎng (fēn liǎng qiè).
Duī (dū huí qiè). Fǔ (fáng jiǔ qiè). *The Combined Commentary on the New Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Great Vaipulya Buddha*, Fascicle 112.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a Śramaṇa from the Kingdom of Khotan during the Tang Dynasty.
Composed by Li Tongxuan, Elder of Fangshan in Taiyuan, Tang Dynasty;
compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhi-ning of Kaiyuan Monastery in Fuzhou, Tang Dynasty.
This is the collation of the Sūtra and the Treatise, Chapter Thirty-nine, Part Twenty-five of the "Entering the Dharma Realm" (Gandavyūha).
[Treatise] Regarding the first section, the Dharma-gate of Entering Properly into the Stage, it is divided into ten parts: 1.

From "At that time, the youth Sudhana" down to "increasing the great ocean of the Bodhisattva’s merit," there are six and a half lines of scripture clarifying the section on Sudhana going to visit spiritual friends;
2. From "Sudhana having seen [him]" down to "for the sake of the world... [the second part].
The *Da Ming* [Sutra] contains three sections of text clarifying the portion where Sudhana visits spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) and requests what he seeks, divided into three parts;

from the passage where that deity replies downward to "tenth, entering the stage of the Tathāgata, the treasury of birth" (*tathāgatabhūmi-praveśa-janmakośa*), there are thirteen and a half lines of text clarifying the fourth part, which correctly bestows upon Sudhana the ten kinds of treasuries of birth. "Good son," it says:
What is called "the treasury of taking birth through the vow to constantly make offerings to all Buddhas"?
From here below, down to "this is the tenth kind of treasury of taking birth for a bodhisattva," there are ten sections of text that distinguish these ten kinds of treasuries of taking birth.
Fifth, from "O Son of the Buddha, when a bodhisattva mahāsattva has cultivated and increased these ten dharmas" down to...
The verse consists of twelve lines, which clarify the section on exhorting practice and attaining benefits.

Following this, there are twenty lines of verse that restate the preceding teachings and praise the Dharma-gate of taking birth. Next, the passage beginning with "Good sons, when Bodhisattvas are endowed with these ten dharmas and are born into the family of the Tathāgata," down to "the liberation gate of taking birth with mastery," consists of two and a half lines of scripture.
The section on the Tree Deity (Vṛkṣadevatā) personally declaring the long duration since he attained the Dharma, divided into seven parts;

the section where Sudhana says, "Noble One, what is the scope of this liberation-gate? and so forth, down to the verses—occupying five pages of scripture—which answers the previous questions of Sudhana regarding the scope of his births, divided into eight parts;
and twenty-three lines of verse which reiterate the aforementioned Dharma, divided into nine sections.
"O son of noble family, I know only this much regarding the liberation of mastery in manifesting birth throughout all places for immeasurable eons.
Below this, the text clarifies the progression of virtues through the ten stages; as for the explanation of the meaning according to the text:
the intent of this "gate of manifesting birth" is to clarify that a Bodhisattva of the eighth stage attains the patience of non-arising (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*) and achieves [mastery].

The gate of eloquence for advancing through the nine stages by manifesting the primordial wisdom of merit and knowledge, and for fulfilling the intentions of all beings—both gods and humans—is called the "Initial Entry into the Womb" and the "Receptacle of Birth.
As a verse in the sutra says: "One never tires of hearing the Dharma; one delights in contemplation throughout the three [realms]."
Unimpeded in the world, with body and mind as pure as space—this is the treasury of birth for those of such renown.
Their minds dwell constantly within the ocean of great compassion, as firm as diamond and a mountain of jewels.
They have thoroughly mastered the gateway to all-knowledge—this is the treasury of birth for these most excellent ones. As explained extensively in the sutra, one should study this ninth stage here.
The Buddha’s wisdom universally pervades the ten stages (*bhūmi*), and the joy of the Dharma of great knowledge manifests before him; this is symbolized by Gopā.
On the eleventh stage, compassion is fulfilled and wisdom is all-encompassing; this is symbolized by Māyā giving birth to the Buddha.

To summarize his activities for the benefit of beings while remaining in the world, he is represented by Śakra, Māyā, King Śuddhodana, and others, signifying the fulfillment of his practices of wisdom and compassion. As for the Buddha himself, he is one.
Because there is no place or time where birth does not occur, Sudhana’s questions regarding the Dharma and the realm have two meanings:
first, he asks about the realm of taking birth; second, he asks about the duration and proximity of attaining the dharma-gates.
As in the case of Mahādeva attaining this liberation—asking how long it has been since his birth—this refers to the realm of the Three Vehicles within the context of birth.
Just as the phenomena produced from the body of Lady Māyā were perceived differently by sentient beings of middling and inferior faculties—
whereas those of superior faculties saw her as a lotus-born transformation body or as appearing directly from space rather than from a mother’s womb—

and for those of the highest superior faculties who suddenly awaken to the Way through their own self-realized noble wisdom, which is in profound resonance with primordial gnosis, it does not matter whether a Tathāgata has appeared in the world.
In this world, as described by the spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) of Sudhana, there are various streams of origins regarding the initial arousal of the mind (cittotpāda).
Some see a Buddha preaching the Dharma in the sky while observing the stars and moon at night;
some see a Buddha descending from the sky to preach the Dharma; and some make offerings in the sky.
Nurturing the sandalwood stupa seat for the Buddha who preaches the Dharma is like the laywoman Bhadrottamā, who attained the bodhisattva’s field of practice that is free from dependence;

having realized it herself, she further explained it to others, and she attained the inexhaustible gates of the inexhaustible eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind—this is not learned from a teacher. This is the body of Lady Māyā.

Both compassion and wisdom are clearly shown to mutually assist one another in the work of benefiting sentient beings; according to what each perceives based on their faculties, these manifestations differ individually.

Samantabhadra Bodhisattva explains that for sentient beings of inferior understanding, the Tathāgata appears from a mother’s womb, whereas for those of superior faculties, he arises from a lotus flower.
If one considers the differences among the various faculties of the six realms of existence, the ways in which the Tathāgata’s birth is perceived are ten thousandfold.

The categories differ; furthermore, regarding what is perceived by the faculties of sentient beings within the human realm, as clearly explained in detail in the sutras, one universally perceives the Tathāgata’s sphere of taking birth even within the dust motes of the worlds of the ten directions.
Taking this sphere as a garden, one contemplates when the Bodhisattva will be born. The passage of a hundred years signifies ascending from this ninth stage.
The ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) constitute one hundred years; reaching the eleventh stage is the time of birth.
Regarding the phenomena and events such as the light of the karmic fruition of the objective realm within the body of Lady Māyā, each is set forth in detail below according to the ten dharmas.
Below this, the *ratnatāla* tree is explained extensively: it is like the *tāla* tree of this region, yet it is composed of superior jewels. Below this follows the inquiry.
Regarding the duration of time since he first resolved his mind [on enlightenment], it is said:

"O son of good family, in ages past, beyond as many kalpas as there are atoms in a billion buddha-fields, and even more than that number"—this does not refer to a number defined by specific limits or distinctions, but signifies simply an incalculable amount.
The world was named Universal Jewels (*Sarvaratna*), for its very substance was formed from the vows and practices of Samantabhadra.
Therefore, the name of the eon, "Delightful" (Kāma), signifies that from the ninth stage, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence (Sādhumatī), the wisdom of the Tathāgata family becomes delightful.
The appearance of eighty nayutas of Buddhas therein signifies that from the eighth stage, one is born into the Buddha-wisdom family of the ninth stage.
The name of the first Buddha, "Light of Sovereign Virtue" (Vaiśvarya-guṇa-prabhāsa), indicates that he has already ascended.
The worlds below the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) are the realm of those to be converted; the royal capital represents the person to be converted by wisdom;

the king and his consort represent the practices of wisdom and compassion; the twenty billion *nayuta* of court ladies represent the two practices of wisdom and compassion being filled with the joy of the Dharma;
and the gardens and pavilions represent the wise one’s wandering through birth and death as if in a garden.

To clarify that the Bodhisattva, while dwelling within the cycle of birth and death, gathers and transforms sentient beings to enable them to attain happiness because he sports in the joy of the Dharma—there is a tree at its edge named "Light of Universal Bestowal of Joy. Because the Bodhisattva’s bestowal of the joy of the Dharma arises from this tree, it is so named.
That the Lady grasped a branch of that tree to give birth to the Bodhisattva signifies Great Compassion.
By relying upon the myriad practices that benefit sentient beings, great wisdom is produced, which is then employed to benefit others. However, how could a Bodhisattva truly undergo birth?
That they manifest the phenomena of birth is merely done by means of images to symbolize the Dharma, in order to guide and lead sentient beings so that they may understand it easily.
Thus, when one perceives birth, this refers only to a portion of sentient beings who perceive such birth; it is not the case for all.
From this point on, know it by this: taking [the teaching] according to the place where sentient beings understand it is the dharma of a bodhisattva’s birth;
merely following what is appropriate for sentient beings so that they may receive benefit is the dharma of a bodhisattva’s birth.
Thus, it is intentionally clarified that superior wisdom arises, and preaching the Dharma with mastery according to the desires of sentient beings is the birth of a bodhisattva. *Piluo* (Vairocana).
The *Kṣānti-vṛkṣa* (translated here as "Highly Manifest") is so named because it relies upon the name of the Buddha, "Highly Manifest.

The tree itself is also called "Virtue Highly Manifest," for it covers the ten directions. The following section on the convergence of causes and conditions and the original practices is clearly explained in detail according to the sūtra.
The subsequent twenty-three verses of verse-repetition (*geya*) restate the preceding Dharma as fully explained in the text. This is the ninth excellence.
On the Stage of Wisdom (*prajñā-bhūmi*), the spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) takes the perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*) as primary, with the other nine perfections as its companions.
This stage treats the obstacle regarding the lack of mastery in teaching the Dharma throughout all realms of existence, thereby enabling the attainment of such mastery.

Second, the section on "Inference of Virtue and Advancement" consists of nine lines of scripture, from "As for the various bodhisattvas... down to "...took their leave and departed," which is divided into four gates.
1. To promote his own virtue; 2. To show that the city where his teacher resides is named Kapilavastu;
3. To state the name of his teacher, which is Gopa; 4. To pay respects and take leave. As for "Kapilavastu," this means the "Yellow City";
it is the place where the Sage with Yellow Hair cultivated the path of immortals. These matters correspond to the Ten Stages (*daśabhūmi*).
This truly accords with the color of the Central Palace; thus it symbolizes the Dharma of the Central Palace, which is yellow, circular, and without squareness.
The two virtues of wisdom and compassion pervade all things through their essence and function, sustaining and nourishing the myriad beings while remaining without form.

It corresponds to the two positions of Wu (戊) and Ji (巳): Wu represents wisdom and Ji represents compassion. However, only those who have realized the worldly and the ultimate truth [can fully understand this].
To thoroughly penetrate the root of the myriad dharmas and thereby attain the subtle and profound essence of wondrous function, wisdom and compassion are the foundation.
This Gopā is also called Gopī; it means "Guardian of the Ground. She guards the ground of great loving-kindness and great compassion within the bodhisattva practice.
Just as Vairocana Tathāgata is the Flower of Wisdom, [she is the Flower of Compassion].
Adorned with crowns and necklaces, and graced by manifold blessings, this is the Buddha born as the fruition of the two practices of wisdom and compassion.
Although there are two ranks, the two practices constitute a single person; although Gopā is titled Tathāgata, she was merely one of the three consorts during his time as a prince.
This is intended to signify the state of the Dharma-joy of compassion, which is ultimately not like the five worldly desires.
The Tathāgata’s appearance in the world is a gathering of true wisdom whose essence pervades the ten directions;
it cannot be discussed in terms of worldly material obstruction, nor can it be understood through the formation of worldly forms.

He manifests as a human being and displays human laws, and he manifests in the heavens and shares the ways of the gods. In the hells and among animals, he appears according to the distinctions of each class. Is this not so?
It can be understood as a single practice, yet it cannot be understood as a single body. Sentient beings are infinite, and the Buddhas are likewise so.
Yet, their lands of retribution and their bodies of retribution pervade all directions; they transcend the three realms and dwell together with Bodhisattvas, humans, and devas.
To those of obscured vision, these beings always dwell together with them in the same body, yet such people constantly remain unaware of this.
The wisdom-realm that perceives the Buddha-fields of the ten directions as being contained within a single minute atom is perfectly complete and inexhaustible; this is called Gopā.
In relation to this human world, she manifests the ways of human beings while remaining unattached to them, thereby manifesting the merit of Great Wisdom.
She is able to relinquish what is difficult to relinquish, giving rise to the path of guidance and birth. As stated in the subsequent passage of the sutra, she herself recounts her past lives.
Regarding the causal conditions for practicing the conduct of a bodhisattva, from the circumstances of being husband and wife up until the stage of Buddhahood:

furthermore, according to the explanations of former masters, when the Tathāgata was a crown prince, he had three consorts—first named Yaśodharā, second named Gopā, and third named Manojñā. It is not known from which scriptural tradition this account originates.
There is this principle: for example, Yaśodharā left the household life to become a bhikṣuṇī and relied upon the supramundane Dharma of the Three Vehicles;
likewise, Gopā served as a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) within the stages of the Ten Grounds for Sudhana, manifesting the practice of great compassion throughout those ten grounds.
Regarding this, the ancients have provided a fourfold analysis: first, attaining the truth but not yet realizing it; second, knowing the truth while practicing it.

The three mundane stations of entanglement are not defiled; through the four great compassions and acting in accordance with others, this concerns the conduct of Vairocana and the conduct of Samantabhadra—the manifestation of transformation bodies throughout the ten directions and the six realms to respond to the faculties of beings through the practice of great compassion.

Now, ten gates are established to praise these virtues: first, the gate of the essence of wisdom being without dependence yet manifesting signs according to the capacity of the vessel; second, that which is...

1. The gate of the nature of appearances being like shadows, devoid of mundane dust; 2. The gate of the original non-existence of the images of the three wisdoms, appearing according to the mind as its vessel;
3. The gate of wisdom having no "self" or "other," responding to conditions like an echo; 4. The gate of what sentient beings see in delusive dreams not being produced by wisdom;
5. The gate of wisdom having no activity, arising in accordance with dreams and illusions; 6. The gate of illusory people having form but lacking substance.

1. The gate of the non-existence of the substance of desire; 2. The gate of the purity of the mind that transcends all phenomena; 3. The gate of the non-arising of the body of the Dharma-realm; 4. The gate of the non-origination of the nature of all dharmas; 5.

The gate of the non-differentiation of the essence of all dharmas; 6. The gate of the non-dual nature of all dharmas; 7. The gate of the manifestation of the ten directions through the wisdom-body being like space, in accordance with the power of original vows;

8. The gate of benefiting sentient beings by penetrating the mundane world through unconditioned great compassion; 9. The gate of the mundane essence being eternally true and undefiled, as all conscious beings are universally pervaded by great wisdom; By means of these ten dharmas, the practice of Gopā is praised.

Regarding the conduct of Samantabhadra: if one were to fully embody the conduct of drawing forth sentient beings from their entanglements and leading them away from the mundane world through Samantabhadra’s practices, one must discern the right and reject the wrong according to what is appropriate for the faculties of those to be trained and how to remedy their afflictions.

If wisdom manifests such that it flows with the stream while its nature remains constant, this is the general intent taught for the sons of the Buddha; herein, Gopā reaches the end of the ten stages of the Path and transcends the world.

The Wisdom-fulfillment [Samantabhadra] wishes to lead those Bodhisattvas who have reached the tenth stage (*bhūmi*) into the gateway of the Universal Worthy Practice (*samantabhadracaryā*) of the eleventh stage.
Just as a lotus remains in water without being wetted, one dwells in the world through great compassion, destroying the two types of habitual obstructions— both defiled and pure—
and only then enters the Universal Worthy Practice of the eleventh stage, as described previously in the "Ten Samādhis" chapter regarding the stages.

Having received the middle empowerment and attained the rank of a Tathāgata, with the two practices of supramundane wisdom and compassion already perfected, he yet entered three times into hundreds of thousands of samādhi-doors throughout the eleven stages; though he sought Bodhisattva Samantabhadra to the end, he could not find him.
Only when the Tathāgata caused him to give rise to mental conceptions and aspire for him did he finally see Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, as if he were something that exists within the supramundane.
Based on this analogy, one should understand that the cultivation of pure wisdom requires the arousal of vast compassionate vows to vow to deliver all sentient beings.

One must deeply contemplate that the mundane world and the true essence are one, neither belonging to defilement nor purity, and enter the gateway of illusory arising. Entering the ocean of illusory abiding, one transforms illusory sentient beings;
knowing their nature to be like an illusion, one enters the gateway of non-reliant wisdom and, through wisdom, realizes the nature of the dharma-realm.
Manifesting illusory bodies and creating all manner of illusory offerings, one makes offerings to all illusorily manifested Tathāgatas;
through such wisdom, one makes offerings to the Buddhas and benefits sentient beings via the gateway of illusory manifestation without ceasing.
The tenth is the Lady Gopā of the city of Kapilavastu, whose stage is the Cloud of Dharma (*dharmameghā*).
[Sūtra] At that time, the youth Sudhana, reflecting upon and practicing the liberation of taking birth,
increasing and expanding his mindfulness without abandoning it, gradually traveled until he reached the Universal Manifestation of the Dharma Assembly of Bodhisattvas.

In the Hall of Radiant Realms, there was a deity named Vigataśoka-guṇa (Virtue of Freedom from Sorrow), who, together with ten thousand palace-lord deities, came forth to welcome Sudhana, saying: "Welcome, noble son! You possess great wisdom and great courage;
you are able to cultivate the inconceivable, sovereign liberation of a bodhisattva, and your mind never abandons the vast vow."

May they be well able to observe the spheres of all phenomena, dwell securely within the city of Dharma, enter the gates of immeasurable skillful means, and accomplish the great ocean of the Tathāgata’s merits.
May they attain wondrous eloquence, skillfully harmonize sentient beings, and obtain the body of noble wisdom.
May they constantly practice in accordance with the truth, discern the differences in the mental activities of all sentient beings, cause them to rejoice, and lead them toward the Buddha.
I observe that you, O Noble One, cultivate all sublime practices with a mind never for a moment lax; your deportment and conduct are entirely pure.
Before long, you shall attain the supreme three karmas of the Tathāgatas’ pure adornment:
adorning your body with the various marks and signs, and embellishing your mind with the wisdom of the ten powers. As you traverse the worlds, I observe you, O Noble One.
One who possesses such courageous diligence beyond compare shall, before long, behold all Buddhas of the three periods of time and receive their teachings;
before long, one shall attain the bliss of all bodhisattva dhyānas, liberations, and samādhis;
and before long, one shall enter the profound liberation of all Buddhas, Tathāgatas. Why is this? Because one has encountered a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra).

"By drawing near to and making offerings to [the spiritual teacher], listening to and receiving their instructions, and practicing them with mindfulness—without slackening, without retreating, without sorrow, without regret, and without obstacles—one will not long before accomplishing the unsurpassed fruit; for neither Māra nor his followers can create difficulties.
Thus, the youth Sudhana said: "Noble One, as you have just described, I pray that I may attain all these things. This is my single aspiration."
All sentient beings are stilled from their various fevers of affliction and freed from all evil karma, giving rise to various forms of peace and happiness as they cultivate various pure practices.

Noble One, when all sentient beings give rise to afflictions, create various evil karmas, and fall into the various evil destinies—suffering constant agony and torment in both body and mind—the Bodhisattva, having seen this, feels sorrow and distress in his heart. Noble One, it is, for example, as if there were a person who...

Suppose there is a son for whom one’s affection and love have reached the ultimate point; if he suddenly sees him having his limbs severed by another, his heart is so pierced with pain that he cannot find peace.

In the same way, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva likewise perceives all sentient beings who, due to the karma of afflictions, fall into the three evil realms and undergo various kinds of suffering, experiencing great anguish and distress. Furthermore, if he sees sentient beings giving rise to [unwholesome] actions of body, speech, and mind...
Through the three kinds of wholesome karma, one is born in the realms of gods and humans and experiences physical and mental bliss. At that time, the Bodhisattva gives rise to great joy.
Why is this? Because the Bodhisattva does not seek omniscience for his own sake; he does not crave the pleasures of the various desires within saṃsāra;

and he does not follow the power of the inversions of perception, the inversions of view, the inversions of mind, or the underlying tendencies (*anuśaya*) of the fetters (*saṃyojana*), such as craving and views, which cause [afflictions] to arise.

While giving rise to various perceptions of bliss, they do not relish the pleasures of the meditative absorptions (*dhyāna-samādhi*). Free from obstacles, weariness, or regression, they remain within *saṃsāra*.

Seeing sentient beings undergoing immeasurable and diverse sufferings throughout the various realms of existence, they give rise to great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) and universally embrace them through the power of their great vows. By the power of this compassionate vow, they cultivate the bodhisattva path.
This conduct severs the afflictions of all sentient beings; it seeks the omniscient wisdom of a Tathāgata;
it makes offerings to all Buddhas and Tathāgatas; it adorns and purifies all vast lands;
and it thoroughly purifies the inclinations and all physical and mental activities of all sentient beings, remaining without weariness throughout the cycle of birth and death.
Noble Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas act as ornaments for all sentient beings, causing them to be born among gods and humans in states of wealth and nobility;
they act as parents, establishing them in the bodhicitta; they act as nurturers, bringing them to fulfillment in the bodhisattva path;
they act as guardians, protecting them so that they may remain far removed from the three evil realms; and they act as mariners, leading them...
Because it enables one to cross the ocean of birth and death, it is the refuge; because it causes one to abandon all fears of demons and afflictions, it is the ultimate goal;
because it causes one to eternally attain the bliss of coolness, it is the ferry; because it causes one to enter the ocean of all Buddhas, it is the guide;
because it causes one to reach the island of the jewels of all dharmas, it is the exquisite flower that blooms with the merits of the Buddhas' minds.
Therefore, they are ornaments, for they constantly radiate the light of merit and wisdom; therefore, they are delightful, for whatever they do is entirely dignified and majestic;
therefore, they are venerable, for they have distanced themselves from all evil karma; therefore, they are Samantabhadra, for they possess a body endowed with every form of dignity;
therefore, they are great luminaries, for they constantly radiate the pure light of wisdom; therefore, they are great clouds, for they constantly...
Because they rain down the Dharma of all ambrosia, when the noble Bodhisattva thus cultivates these various practices,
he causes all sentient beings to give rise to love and joy, becoming fully endowed with the bliss of the Dharma. At that time, as the youth Sudhana was about to ascend the Dharma Hall,
the goddess Viśoka and her host of deities presented him with exquisite celestial flower garlands, ointments, and powdered incense that surpassed those of all the heavens.
Scattering perfumes and various precious ornaments over Sudhana, they spoke these verses:
"You have now appeared in the world as a great lamp of light for the world. For the sake of all sentient beings, you diligently seek unsurpassed enlightenment.
Throughout immeasurable billions of kalpas, it would be difficult even to behold you."
The Sun of Merit now rises, extinguishing the darkness of all worlds.
Seeing that sentient beings are shrouded by the delusions of perversion, you have given rise to a mind of great compassion.
Seeking to realize the teacherless path, you have, with a pure mind, sought the Bodhi of the Buddhas and served spiritual friends.
Not begrudging your own body or life, you are without dependence or attachment among all worlds;
your mind is universally unimpeded and pure as space. You have cultivated the practices of bodhi until all your merits are fully perfected;
emitting the great light of wisdom, you illuminate all worlds everywhere.
You do not depart from the world, nor do you cling to the world;
you move through the world without obstruction, like the wind wandering through space.
Just as when a great conflagration arises, nothing can extinguish it, so too is the fire of your diligence in practicing the path to enlightenment—your courageous and great perseverance.
Firm and immovable, a lion of adamantine wisdom, you traverse all realms of the dharma-dhātu without fear;
to every ocean of lands, you are able to go and draw near to spiritual friends.
At that time, after the goddess Aśokaśrī had spoken these verses, she followed Sudhana out of her love for the Dharma,

never leaving him. Then, the youth Sudhana entered the Lecture Hall of Universal Manifestation of the Dharmadhātu and searched everywhere until he saw the Śākya girl sitting upon a lion throne of precious lotuses within the hall, surrounded by eighty thousand [attendants].
He was surrounded by four thousand court ladies; none of these ladies were not born from royal lineages,
and all had cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva in the past, planted identical roots of goodness, universally gathered in sentient beings through generosity and kind speech,
clearly perceived the realm of omniscience, jointly practiced the conduct for the enlightenment of a Buddha, and constantly dwelt in right concentration.
Constantly roaming in great compassion, he universally gathers all sentient beings as if they were his only child; endowed with a heart of loving-kindness, his retinue is pure.

Having already accomplished the inconceivable skillful means of a bodhisattva in the past, he has attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and is fully possessed of the various *pāramitās* of a bodhisattva. Free from...
Free from all attachments and taking no delight in birth and death, although he traversed all realms of existence, his mind was ever pure.

He constantly and diligently observed the path to omniscience, transcended the net of hindrances and veils, and surpassed all points of attachment. From the Dharma-body, he manifested transformational forms to give rise to the practices of Samantabhadra;
his long-standing bodhisattva powers, wisdom, solar intelligence, and lamps of insight were all fully perfected. At that time, the youth Sudhana...
The son went to where the Śākya woman Gopā was, prostrated at her feet, and stood with palms joined, saying: "Noble Lady,
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva, while within birth and death,
remains unstained by the faults and afflictions of birth and death, and realizes the self-nature of phenomena."
Abiding by nature yet not dwelling in the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas, they fulfill the Buddha-dharmas while practicing the bodhisattva path;
dwelling in the bodhisattva stage, they enter the realm of the Buddhas; transcending the world, they take birth within the world;
accomplishing the dharma-body, they manifest infinite and diverse form-bodies; realizing the signless dharma, they manifest for the sake of sentient beings.
All those who know that dharmas are ineffable yet extensively expound all dharmas for the sake of sentient beings;

who know that sentient beings are empty yet never abandon the work of transforming sentient beings; who, though knowing that all Buddhas are neither born nor extinguished, diligently make offerings without ever turning back;
and who, though knowing that all dharmas are without karma or retribution, cultivate all virtuous deeds without ever ceasing.
Then the daughter Gopā said to Sudhana: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!

That you are now able to ask about such practices of the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas—those who cultivate the various vows and conducts of Samantabhadra—and that you can inquire in this way, listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect well upon it. I shall, by the spiritual power of the Buddha, proclaim it for you, noble son."
Sons of noble family, if bodhisattvas accomplish ten dharmas, they will be able to fulfill the bodhisattva practice of the universal light of wisdom of Indra’s net.
What are these ten? They are: relying upon spiritual friends; attaining vast and superior resolve;
attaining pure aspiration and delight; gathering all merit and wisdom; and listening to the teachings from all Buddhas.
Because they accord with the Dharma; because their minds never abandon the Buddhas of the three periods of time; because they are identical to the practices of all Bodhisattvas;
because they are protected and remembered by all Tathāgatas; because their great compassion and wondrous vows are all pure;

and because they are able to universally sever all birth and death through the power of wisdom—these are the ten. If Bodhisattvas accomplish these qualities, they will be able to bring them to perfection.
The Bodhisattva Practice of Universal Wisdom Light Filling the Indra’s Net:
O Son of the Buddha, if a bodhisattva draws near to spiritual friends, they will be able to practice with diligence and without regression, giving rise to inexhaustible Buddha-dharmas.
O Son of the Buddha, there are ten ways in which a bodhisattva serves spiritual friends. What are these ten? They are as follows: [regarding] one's own body and life...
Without regard or attachment for worldly objects of enjoyment, their minds are free from craving and seeking;

they know that the nature of all phenomena is equal and never abandon their vow for omniscience. Observing the true reality of the entire dharma-realm, their minds constantly relinquish the ocean of all existence;
knowing phenomena as they truly are, their minds have no dependence, and they fulfill all the great vows of bodhisattvas.
One should always be able to manifest the ocean of all lands and cultivate the unimpeded wheel of wisdom of a bodhisattva;
O sons of the Buddha, you should serve all spiritual friends by means of this Dharma, never opposing them.
At that time, the Śākya girl Gopā, wishing to clarify this meaning once more, observed the ten directions through the Buddha’s spiritual power and spoke in verse:

To benefit all living beings, the Bodhisattva maintains right mindfulness and personally attends upon spiritual friends, honoring them as Buddhas with a mind free from indolence. This practice in the world is like the Indra-net;
their resolute understanding is as vast as space, encompassing all that exists throughout the three periods of time.

The lands, the sentient beings, and the Buddhas are all thus; this is the practice of universal wisdom-light, whose aspiration is like space, without limit. Having forever severed afflictions and departed from all defilements, it is the merit cultivated by all Buddhas;
this practice moves through the world as a cloud of bodies.
The Bodhisattva cultivates the wisdom of omniscience, a sea of inconceivable merit, purifying the body of all virtues and wisdom. This practice is unstained by worldly conduct;
in the presence of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas, they listen to and receive their teachings without ever feeling satiated.
This is the lamp of wisdom that gives rise to the true mark; this practice shines universally throughout the world and reaches the ten directions.
All Buddhas are immeasurable, yet in a single thought-moment one can enter them all;
the mind never abandons the Tathāgatas—this is the great vow-practice directed toward Bodhi.
They are able to enter the great assemblies of all Buddhas— the ocean of samādhis of all bodhisattvas,
the ocean of vows, and the ocean of skillful means. This practice, like a celestial net,
is sustained by all Buddhas throughout boundless kalpas until the end of the future.
Practicing the path of Samantabhadra everywhere—this is the Bodhisattva’s practice of manifesting emanations.
Seeing all sentient beings undergoing great suffering, He gives rise to great compassion and appears in the world;
Proclaiming the light of the Dharma to dispel the darkness— This is the Bodhisattva’s practice of the sun of wisdom.

Seeing all sentient beings in the various realms of existence, he gathers the boundless, wondrous Wheel of Dharma to cause them forever to sever the stream of birth and death. This is the practice of the conduct of Samantabhadra;
practicing this skillful means, he manifests his body according to the minds of sentient beings.
Throughout all realms of existence, you transform and deliver immeasurable sentient beings;
by the power of great compassion and skillful means, you manifest throughout the world,
preaching the Dharma according to their understandings and inclinations, causing them all to advance toward the path of Bodhi.
Then Śākyaguptā, having spoken these verses, addressed the youth Sudhana, saying:
"Noble son, I have attained the liberation-door called 'Contemplating the Ocean of Samādhis of All Bodhisattvas. Sudhana said: 'Great Sage, what is the scope of this liberation-door?
She replied: 'Noble son, having entered this liberation, I know this Sahā world-system...'"
Throughout as many eons as there are atoms in a Buddha-field of the Sahā world, all sentient beings within the various realms of existence— those who die here and are born there,

those who perform good deeds and those who perform evil deeds, those who receive various karmic retributions, those who seek liberation and those who do not seek liberation, those with right determination, wrong determination, and no fixed determination,
those with afflictions and those without afflictions, those with roots of goodness and those without roots of goodness, and those who possess complete roots of goodness— [all such beings...]
I fully know and see all the roots of goodness and roots of non-goodness that are comprised within them, as well as the roots of goodness comprised within the roots of non-goodness;

likewise, I know and see all the wholesome and unwholesome dharmas thus accumulated. Furthermore, I thoroughly understand the names and the sequential order of all the Buddhas who appeared during those kalpas;
I know the initial generation of the mind of enlightenment and the skillful means by which those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, sought [the path].
I fully understand how all-knowledge gives birth to the ocean of all great vows, making offerings to all Buddhas, practicing the bodhisattva path, attaining equal and perfect enlightenment,
turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma, manifesting great supernormal powers, and transforming and delivering sentient beings;
I also know the distinctions among the assemblies of those Buddhas, and within those assemblies, I know those sentient beings who attain [liberation] by relying on the Śrāvaka vehicle.
I fully know the various roots of goodness cultivated in the past by those śrāvakas who have attained liberation, as well as the diverse wisdoms they have acquired;

I also know all the roots of goodness, the bodhi, the cessation, the liberation, the supernormal powers, the transformations, and the maturation belonging to those sentient beings who have attained liberation by relying on the vehicle of the pratyekabuddhas.
I fully know all sentient beings who enter nirvana, and I also know those Buddhas and their assemblies of bodhisattvas—
how those bodhisattvas, from their first resolve, cultivated roots of goodness, gave rise to immeasurable great vows and practices,
fulfilled and perfected the various *pāramitās*, and through the power of mastery entered the path of the Bodhi adorned with manifold ornaments.
The Bodhisattva Grounds: abiding in the Bodhisattva Grounds, contemplating the Bodhisattva Grounds, purifying the Bodhisattva Grounds;

the characteristics of the Bodhisattva Grounds, the wisdom of the Bodhisattva Grounds, the wisdom by which Bodhisattvas are gathered, the wisdom by which Bodhisattvas teach and transform sentient beings, the wisdom by which Bodhisattvas establish themselves, the sphere of the vast practices of Bodhisattvas, the supernormal powers of Bodhisattvas, the ocean of samādhis of Bodhisattvas, and the skillful means of Bodhisattvas.
In every thought-moment, [the Bodhisattva] enters oceans of samādhis, attains the light of omniscience, acquires clouds of lightning from omniscience,
realizes the patience of the true nature of phenomena, penetrates the ocean of omniscience,
dwells in oceans of lands, knows the ocean of sentient beings, abides in skillful means, issues forth vows, and manifests spiritual powers.

"O son of good family, I thoroughly understand and know all this: throughout the ocean of kalpas extending to the end of the future in this Sahā world, which continue in uninterrupted succession, I know them all.
Just as I know the Sahā world, so too do I know the worlds within the Sahā world as numerous as its atoms, and I also know all the worlds within the Sahā world."

He also knows all the worlds within the atoms of the Sahā world; he also knows all the worlds dwelling in the uninterrupted succession of the ten directions outside the Sahā world; he also knows all the worlds comprised within the world-systems of the Sahā world;
and he also knows the infinite worlds of the ten directions within this Flower Treasury World-Ocean of the World-Honored One Vairocana.
The worlds comprised within the categories of realms— namely, the worlds of vast extent, the worlds of established order,
the worlds of wheels, the worlds of fields, the worlds of distinctions, the worlds of revolutions, the worlds of lotuses, and the worlds of Mount Sumeru—
all these worlds throughout this ocean of worlds, by the power of the original vows of the Bhagavān Vairocana.
Therefore, I am able to know them all, and I can also recollect and remember all the oceans of causal conditions of the Tathāgata in the past—
namely, his cultivation of the skillful means of all vehicles, his dwelling in the bodhisattva practices throughout immeasurable eons,

his purification of buddha-lands, his teaching and transforming of sentient beings, his serving of all Buddhas, his establishing of dwellings, and his receiving and hearing of the Dharma being preached.
Having attained all samādhis and all masteries, they cultivate the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*) and enter the ocean of the Buddha’s merits;

they maintain the precepts and undergo ascetic practices, are fully endowed with patience, and possess courageous diligence; they achieve all meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) and perfect pure wisdom.
In all places, they manifest birth; their *Samantabhadra* vows and practices are entirely purified; they universally enter all lands and universally purify the Buddhas.
The earth universally enters the ocean of wisdom of all Tathāgatas and universally encompasses the bodhi of all Buddhas; it attains the light of the great wisdom of the Tathāgatas,
realizes the nature of the all-knowledge of all Buddhas, achieves equal and perfect enlightenment, and turns the sublime wheel of Dharma—
along with all their sites of enlightenment and assemblies, and all sentient beings within those assemblies from past lives.

I fully understand all the roots of goodness planted by those who come here—how they mature sentient beings from their first aspiration through the practice of skillful means, increasing moment by moment, and attaining various samādhis, supernormal powers, and liberations. Why is this?
Because this liberation of mine enables me to know the mental activities of all sentient beings and the roots of goodness cultivated in the practices of all sentient beings.
Because he fully understands the defilement and purification of all sentient beings, the various distinctions among all sentient beings,
all the gateways of samādhi of all śrāvakas, the tranquil samādhis, supernormal powers, and liberations of all pratyekabuddhas, all bodhisattvas,
and the light of liberation of all Tathāgatas, at that time, the youth Sudhana addressed Gopa:
Pāyāsi said, "Noble One, how long has it been since you attained this liberation?
He replied, "Good son, in a past age, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, there was an eon named Victorious Conduct (*Vijayacaryā*) and a world named Fearless (*Abhaya*).
In that world, there were four continents called Tranquil (*Kṣema*), and within Jambudvīpa among those four continents, there was one..."
There was a royal city named Uccairnāga-vṛkṣa, which was the most preeminent among eighty royal cities. At that time, there was a king named Dhanapati;

that king possessed sixty thousand court ladies, five hundred ministers, and five hundred princes, all of whom were valiant and capable of subduing enemies. The king’s crown prince was named Tejodhipati.
He is upright and extraordinary, a sight that all people delight to behold. The soles of his feet are flat and full, complete with the mark of the wheel (*cakra*).
His heels are prominent; the spaces between his fingers and toes are joined by webs (*jālāvanaddha*). His heels are symmetrical and well-proportioned; his hands and feet are soft and supple.

His calves are like those of the king of *eṇeya* deer. His seven parts are perfectly rounded; his male organ is concealed within a sheath (*kośagata-vasti-guhya*). The upper part of his body is like that of a lion king, and his two shoulders are broad and well-fleshed.

His two arms are level and full; his body is tall and his posture is upright. His neck bears three lines, and his cheeks are like those of a lion. He possesses forty teeth, all of which are even and closely set;
his four canine teeth are brilliant white. His tongue is long and broad, and he utters the Brahma-voice.

His eyes are deep blue with eyelashes like those of a bull king. Between his eyebrows is the mark of the *ūrṇā*, and atop his head is the *uṣṇīṣa*. His skin is fine and soft, as if made of the finest cloth.
The golden hairs on his body curled upward, and his hair was the color of indigo; his body was full and robust like a nyagrodha tree.
At that time, having received the instructions of his father the king, the prince went with ten thousand court ladies to the Gandhahasti Garden to sightsee and enjoy themselves.
At that moment, the prince mounted a magnificent jeweled chariot, which was adorned with all manner of ornaments and contained a great maṇi jewel.
He sat upon a lion throne, while five hundred court ladies each holding a precious cord led him along;

his progress was measured, neither slow nor fast. A hundred thousand million people held various precious parasols, a hundred thousand million people held various precious banners, a hundred thousand million people held various precious pennants, and a hundred thousand million people performed various musical performances.

Hundreds of thousands of millions of people burned various famous incenses, and hundreds of thousands of millions of people scattered various exquisite flowers, surrounding and escorting him from before and behind.
The road was level and smooth, without elevations or depressions;

various precious flowers were strewn upon it, rows of jewel trees lined its sides, and jeweled nets covered it entirely. Various multi-storied pavilions extended throughout the space, and within those pavilions—
Some had accumulated various kinds of rare treasures; some had displayed all manner of ornaments;
some had prepared and set out various foods and drinks; some had hung and spread various garments; some had made ready all sorts of necessary provisions;
and others had stationed beautiful women along with countless servants and attendants to provide whatever was required.
While all these were being given away as gifts, there was a woman named Sujātā who brought a young girl named Guṇavatī.
She was upright in countenance, her features pure and refined, her proportions perfectly balanced—neither too stout nor too slender, neither too tall nor too short.
