Her eyes and hair were deep blue, her voice like that of Brahmā, and she was highly proficient in the arts and skilled in debate. She was respectful, diligent, untiring, and compassionate.

Endowed with harmlessness, shame, and modesty, gentle and upright, free from delusion, possessing few desires, and devoid of flattery or deceit, he rode in a magnificent jeweled chariot surrounded by court ladies.
Accompanied by his mother, he departed from the royal city and proceeded ahead of the crown prince.
Seeing the crown prince’s manner of speech and his chanting, she conceived a sense of affectionate attachment and said to her mother: "It is my heart's wish that I may serve and attend upon him."
"If a person does not fulfill their desires, they should bring about their own destruction. The mother said to her daughter, "Do not harbor such a thought.
Why? Because this man is extremely difficult to find; he is fully endowed with the marks of a Wheel-Turning King (cakravartin) and shall later succeed to the throne as a Wheel-Turning Monarch.
A precious woman shall appear who can soar through the air and possess self-mastery. We are lowly and base, and thus are no match for him; such a place is difficult to attain."
"Do not give rise to this thought: beside that Gandhakuṭī garden, there is a site of enlightenment named Dharma-Cloud Radiance.
At that time, a Tathāgata named Victorious Sun’s Body, complete with the ten titles, appeared therein. Seven days have already passed since his appearance.
Now, while that young girl was resting for a brief moment, she saw that Buddha in a dream; having awakened from the dream, a deva in the sky addressed her."
The Tathāgata Jina-divasakāya attained equal and perfect enlightenment at the Dharma-Cloud Radiance Bodhimanda seven days ago;
he is now surrounded by a multitude of bodhisattvas, as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas,
kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and brahmās, up to the Akaniṣṭha heaven, and all the various stages.
When the gods of wind, fire, water, rivers, oceans, mountains, trees, gardens, medicinal herbs,
and the city guardians had all assembled to behold the Buddha, the maiden Sudarśanā, having seen the Tathāgata in a dream and heard of the Buddha’s virtues,
felt her mind become peaceful and free from fear; she then spoke before the prince.
The verse says:
My body is most upright and handsome, My fame pervades the ten directions.
My wisdom is peerless, And I am well-versed in all arts and crafts. Countless hundreds of thousands of beings, Upon seeing me, are all filled with desire.
In my heart, I do not give rise to even a slight desire for him; I am without anger, without resentment, without aversion, and without joy.
I have merely resolved upon the vast mind To benefit all sentient beings.
Now that I behold the Prince, Who is endowed with all the marks of merit, My heart is filled with great joy and celebration.
All your faculties are full of joy; your complexion is like a luminous jewel. Your hair is beautiful and curls to the right;
your brow is broad and your eyebrows are fine and arched. My heart desires to serve you.
As I behold the Prince’s body, it is like an image of pure gold, or like a great mountain of precious gems, radiant with the marks and signs of excellence.
Your eyes are wide and deep blue; your face is like the moon and your cheeks are like those of a lion.
With a joyful countenance and exquisite voice, I pray that you will compassionately accept me. Your tongue is broad and long and wondrous, like the color of refined copper;
with a Brahma-voice like the song of the *kiṃnara*, all who hear it rejoice. Your mouth is square and not drawn back or shrunken.
With teeth white, even, and closely set, When speaking and manifesting a smile, Those who see him rejoice in their hearts.
Possessing a stainless, pure body Endowed with the thirty-two marks, He shall surely attain the rank of a Wheel-Turning King in this world.
At that time, the Prince said to the girl: "Whose daughter are you? By whom are you protected?
If you already belong to another, I ought not to give rise to a mind of passionate attachment. Then the Prince questioned her with a verse:
Your body is exceedingly pure, Endowed with the marks of merit.
I now ask you: In whose care do you dwell? Who are your parents? To whom do you belong now?
If you already belong to someone, That person must have taken you in; You do not steal the property of others.
You harbor no harmful intent; you do not engage in sexual misconduct. Upon what speech do you abide?
You do not speak ill of others, nor do you destroy the friendships of others. You do not encroach upon the domains of others, nor do you give way to anger toward them.
You do not give rise to perverse or dangerous views, nor do you perform contradictory actions.
One does not use the power of flattery and crookedness to deceive the world through expedient means.
One respects one’s parents and reveres spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). Upon seeing those who are poor and destitute, one is able to give rise to a mind of gathering-in.
If there is a spiritual friend who instructs you in the Dharma, one is able to give rise to a firm and steadfast mind.
Do you ultimately respect [the Buddha]? Do you delight in the Buddha?
Do you understand the ocean of merits of the Bodhisattvas and the Sangha? Are you able to pay them homage?
Are you able to know the Dharma, yet unable to purify sentient beings? Do you abide within the Dharma, or do you abide in what is not the Dharma?
When you see those who are solitary and friendless, are you able to give rise to a mind of loving-kindness?
When you see sentient beings in the evil realms, are you able to give rise to great compassion? When you see others obtain honor and joy, are you able to give rise to sympathetic joy?
When others come to oppress you, do you remain free from anger and resentment? Have you resolved upon the aspiration for enlightenment?
To awaken sentient beings, one practices for boundless eons; can one do so without weariness?
At that time, the mother of the girl spoke these verses to the crown prince:
"O Prince, you should listen as I now describe this girl’s birth and her growth, along with all their causal conditions.
On the very day the Prince was born, she likewise emerged from a lotus flower;
her eyes were pure, long, and wide, and her limbs and joints were fully formed. Once, during the spring month..."
Wandering through the Śāla Grove, he beheld everywhere various medicinal herbs, all flourishing and lush;
wondrous trees burst forth with exquisite flowers that looked like auspicious clouds. Beautiful birds sang in harmony, and they took delight together amidst the groves.
Accompanied by eight hundred women who were so beautiful they captivated the hearts of men, he wandered there.
Their garments were all magnificent and beautiful, and their songs were entirely exquisite.
In that garden there was a bathing pool named Lotus Banner; I sat upon its bank, surrounded by a multitude of court ladies.
Within that lotus pond, a thousand-petaled flower suddenly sprang up, with precious petals and stalks of lapis lazuli.
With a pedestal of Jambū-river gold, at that time when the night had ended, as the sun first appeared, that lotus flower fully blossomed.
It emitted a great, pure light; that radiance was exceedingly intense, like the sun when it first rises, universally illuminating Jambudvīpa. The multitude marveled at this unprecedented wonder.
At that time, I saw this jade maiden born from that lotus; her body was exceedingly pure, and all her limbs were perfectly formed. She is a treasure of the human world, born of pure karma;
her past causes have not been lost, and now she experiences this retribution—her hair is deep blue-black and her eyes are like blue lotuses.
With a Brahma-voice and golden light, adorned with flower garlands and a crest of various jewels,
pure and free from all defilements, his limbs are perfectly complete and his body is without deficiency.
Like a statue of pure gold set amidst precious flowers, the sandalwood fragrance from his pores universally perfumes all things.
Her mouth emits the fragrance of blue lotuses, and she constantly utters the sounds of Brahma-voice.
Wherever this woman dwells, there is always the music of the devas. She should not be joined with an inferior person;
there is no one in the world worthy to be her husband, save for you, whose body is adorned with the marks of excellence.
May you graciously accept me; neither tall nor short, neither coarse nor fine, in every way perfectly adorned—may you graciously accept me.
In the methods of writing and calculation, and in all crafts and arts, I have attained complete mastery—may you graciously accept me.
Well-versed in all military strategies, Skillful in resolving all disputes and litigation, Able to tame those who are difficult to tame— I pray that you will deign to accept me.
Your body is exceedingly pure; Those who behold it never tire of looking, Adorned by its own merits— You should deign to accept me. Regarding all the afflictions of sentient beings...
She thoroughly understands that dependent origination and administers medicine according to the ailment;

she is able to eliminate all the various and immeasurable kinds of linguistic conventions of Jambudvīpa, even down to the sounds of music—there is nothing she does not master, including all that women are capable of. This girl knows it all.
And being free from the faults of women, I pray that you will swiftly accept me; Without envy, nor stinginess, without greed, nor anger;
Of upright nature and gentle disposition, Free from all coarseness and evil, I pay respect to the Venerable One;
Serving you without opposition, I delight in cultivating all virtuous deeds.

This will accord with you: whenever you see those who are old or sick, impoverished, or beset by suffering—without rescue or refuge—always give rise to great compassion. Constantly contemplate the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*), seeking neither self-interest nor personal pleasure;
may you only wish to benefit sentient beings, adorning your mind with this resolve.
Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, they are at all times free from negligence.

Whether speaking or remaining silent, those who behold them find joy. Though in every situation their minds are entirely free from attachment, when they see one of virtuous qualities, they look upon them with tireless delight and revere that spiritual friend.
Delighting in seeing those who have left evil behind, her mind is not restless; she acts after first reflecting,
adorned with merit and wisdom, entirely free from resentment— she is the most excellent among women and should serve the Prince.
Combined Commentary on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, Fascicle 112. Phonetic Transcriptions: Shǎn (shuān, pronounced as shuān and ruǎn).

Chōng (chōng, pronounced as chǒu and gōng). Xié (xié, pronounced as zǐ and yè). Yì (yì, also pronounced as yī). Yǔn (yǔn, pronounced as yú and mǐn). Ǒu (ǒu, pronounced as wú and gǒu). Qiān (qiān, pronounced as qù and qián).
Qiè (pronounced as in *qiè*). Huò (pronounced as in *huō*). Màn (pronounced as in *màn*). Sì (pronounced as *sì*). Kuǎng (pronounced as in *kuǎng*).
The Combined Commentary on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya, Scroll 113.
The Sūtra translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a Śramaṇa from the Kingdom of Khotan during the Tang Dynasty;
the Commentary composed by Li Tongxuan, a Lay Elder of Fangshan in Taiyuan during the Tang Dynasty.
Compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhining of Kaiyuan Temple in Fuzhou during the Tang Dynasty, combining the various editions of the sutra for the *Entry into the Dharma Realm* Chapter, Part 39-26.
[Sutra] At that time, having entered the Garden of Fragrant Sprouts, the Prince addressed Māyādevī and Subhūti, saying: "O virtuous daughters..."
I shall seek Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi; throughout all future kalpas to the end of time,
I shall gather all factors conducive to omniscience, cultivate boundless bodhisattva practices,
purify all pāramitās, make offerings to all Tathāgatas, uphold all the teachings of the Buddhas, and adorn and purify all Buddha-fields.
One should cause the lineage of all Tathāgatas to remain uninterrupted throughout all lands; one should bring all sentient beings to universal maturity according to their respective dispositions;
one should extinguish the suffering of birth and death for all sentient beings and establish them in the state of ultimate peace and happiness;
one should purify the eye of wisdom of all sentient beings; and one should cultivate and practice all that is practiced by all Bodhisattvas.
One should abide in the impartial mind of all bodhisattvas; one should accomplish all the stages of the bodhisattva path;

one should cause all sentient beings to rejoice universally; and throughout the bounds of the future, one should practice the perfection of giving by relinquishing all things—clothing, food and drink, wives, concubines, sons, and daughters—to bring universal satisfaction to all sentient beings.
One should give away everything—head, eyes, hands, feet, and all else, whether internal or external—without any stinginess or regret.
At that time, you may create obstacles for me; when I give away wealth and goods, your mind may be stingy;
when I give away my sons and daughters, your heart may be pained; and when I cut off my limbs, your mind may be distressed. You must leave me and go forth into homelessness.
Out of compassion for sentient beings, I have resolved to attain bodhicitta; throughout immeasurable kalpas, I shall practice all-knowledge.
Within those immeasurable great kalpas, I shall purely cultivate the ocean of all vows.
Entering the stages and subduing hindrances, I shall pass through immeasurable kalpas. The six pāramitās studied by all Buddhas of the three times,
And the complete practice of skillful means— Having accomplished the path to Bodhi,
I shall purify all the defiled lands of the ten directions And all the hardships of the evil realms.

I shall cause them to emerge forever; I shall, through skillful means, extensively deliver all sentient beings, causing them to extinguish the darkness of ignorance and abide in the path of Buddha-wisdom. I shall make offerings to all Buddhas and purify all stages;
giving rise to a heart of great compassion, I shall relinquish all things, both internal and external.
When you see a beggar coming, Do not give rise to a mind of stinginess or envy. My heart always delights in giving;
do not oppose me. If you see me give away my head, Be careful not to feel sorrow or distress.
I speak these words to you first now, To make your mind firm and steadfast, Even when my hands and feet are cut off.
Do not disdain the beggar; having now heard my words, you should reflect upon them with care:
"I shall relinquish all things that men and women hold dear. If you can comply with my heart, I shall fulfill your wish.
At that time, the young girl addressed the Prince, respectfully accepting his instruction, and spoke in verse:
"Throughout oceans of immeasurable kalpas, May my body be consumed by the fires of hell;
If you would graciously accept me, I would willingly endure such suffering. Through immeasurable births, May my body be shattered like fine dust."
If you would graciously accept me, I am willing to endure this suffering: For immeasurable eons, I shall carry upon my head the vast adamantine mountain;
If you would graciously accept me, I am willing to endure this suffering:
Through the ocean of immeasurable births and deaths, I shall offer my own flesh and body, So that you may attain the state of the Dharma King.
May it be so for me as well; if you would graciously accept me as your servant, wherever you practice giving throughout all your lives, may you always include me in your gifts.
Out of compassion for the suffering of sentient beings, you have resolved upon bodhicitta;
having already gathered in sentient beings, you should likewise take me under your care.
I do not seek noble wealth, nor do I crave the pleasures of the five desires; I only wish to practice the Dharma together, taking benevolence as my guide.
With eyes deep blue, long and wide, you look upon the world with compassion, never giving rise to a mind of attachment.
You shall surely accomplish the path of a Bodhisattva—this is the place where the Prince has traveled.
From the earth emerge various jewel flowers; he shall surely become a Wheel-Turning King. May you graciously accept me!
I once dreamed of this wondrous Dharma site of enlightenment, where the Tathāgata sat beneath a tree surrounded by an immeasurable multitude.
In my dream, that Tathāgata’s body was like a mountain of pure gold.
He stroked the crown of my head with his hand, and upon waking, my heart was filled with joy.
A celestial being from a former life, named Joyous Radiance, spoke to me: "When the Buddha appeared in the world at the site of enlightenment, I once had this thought:
'I wish to see the body of the Prince. That celestial being then replied to me:"
"You shall now behold the ancient aspirations I once held; they are all fulfilled this very day.
I pray that you will go together with me to pay homage to that Tathāgata.
At that time, having heard the name of the Tathāgata Sūryavarcas, the Prince was filled with great joy and wished to see that Buddha.
She scattered five hundred mani jewels over the girl and crowned her with a wondrous treasury of radiant light jewel-crest;
she clothed her in robes of flaming mani jewels. At that time, the girl’s mind did not waver, nor did she show any sign of joy;
she merely joined her palms in reverence and gazed up at the prince, never for a moment averting her eyes. Her mother, Bhadra, then spoke before the prince:
The verse says:
"This woman is most upright and beautiful, Her body adorned with meritorious virtues.
Her former vow to serve the Prince is now fulfilled; She maintains the precepts and possesses wisdom, Endowed with every excellence."
Universally supreme and peerless throughout all worlds, this girl is born of the Lotus family and is free from any blemish or ugliness.
She shares the same conduct as the Prince; she is far removed from all faults.
Her body is soft and supple, like celestial silk or cotton wool; wherever her hands touch and stroke, [all things become so].
All afflictions are entirely extinguished, And from every pore issues a wondrous fragrance. Its sweet scent is peerless;
if sentient beings smell it, They all abide in pure precepts. Their physical form is like pure gold as they sit upright upon lotus pedestals.
If sentient beings behold them, They abandon harm and possess a mind of loving-kindness.
Their speech and voice are exceedingly gentle and soft; there is none who does not rejoice upon hearing them. If sentient beings should hear it, they will all be freed from every evil karma.
Their minds will be pure and free from blemish or stain; far removed from all flattery and crookedness, they will speak words that accord with the heart.
Those who hear them will all be filled with joy; they are harmonious and supple, endowed with a sense of shame and remorse.
She reveres the elders and seniors, is free from greed and free from deceit, and feels compassion for all sentient beings.
This woman does not rely on her physical beauty or her retinue; she honors all Buddhas solely with a pure mind.
At that time, the Prince, together with the maiden Sudarśanā, ten thousand court ladies, and their retinues, departed from the Gandhakuṭi Garden and proceeded to the Dharmameghaprabhāsa Bodhimaṇḍa.
Having arrived, he descended from his carriage and advanced on foot to where the Tathāgata was. There he beheld the Buddha’s physical marks, which were majestic and serene;
his faculties were perfectly disciplined and harmonious, and he was inwardly and outwardly pure, like a great dragon pool free from all [impurities].
With all their defilements purified, they gave rise to pure faith; leaping for joy and filled with rapture, they prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and circumambulated him countless times.
At that time, the Prince and the maiden Sudarśanā each took five hundred exquisite jewel lotuses and scattered them as offerings before the Buddha.
The Prince constructed five hundred vihāras for the Buddha, each fashioned from fragrant wood and adorned with various precious gems.
With hundreds of maṇi jewels interspersed as ornaments, the Buddha then preached for them the *Sūtra of the Universal Eye Lamp Gate*.
Having heard this sūtra, they attained oceans of samādhis regarding all dharmas, namely:

the samādhi of universally illuminating the ocean of vows of all Buddhas, the samādhi of universally illuminating the treasury of the three periods of time, and the samādhi of directly beholding the sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas. Universal...
The Samādhi of Illuminating All Sentient Beings; the Samādhi of the Universal Illumination of the Lamp of Wisdom for All Worlds;
the Samādhi of the Universal Illumination of the Lamp of Wisdom Regarding the Faculties of All Sentient Beings; the Samādhi of the Cloud of Radiance that Protects and Saves All Sentient Beings;
the Samādhi of the Great Bright Lamp Universally Illuminating All Sentient Beings; and the Samādhi of Proclaiming the Dharma Wheel of All Buddhas—these he fully possessed.

When Samantabhadra attained the Samādhi of Pure Conduct, the girl Viśeṣamati attained a samādhi named "Inconquerable Ocean-Treasury," whereby she became forever non-retrogressive from Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. At that time, the prince, together with the girl Viśeṣamati and their retinue,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him countless times, took their leave, and returned to the palace to see the father king.
Having completed his prostrations and obeisances, he addressed the King, saying: "Great King, you should know that the Tathāgata Sūryavarcas has appeared in the world;
not long ago, in this very kingdom at the Bodhimaṇḍa of Dharma-cloud Radiance, he attained perfect enlightenment.
At that time, the Great King said to the Prince: "Who told you such a thing? Was it a deva?"

"Is it a human? The Crown Prince replied, "It is this girl, Samantabhadra. When the King heard these words, he was filled with immeasurable joy, like a poor man who has discovered a great hidden treasure.
He thought thus: "The Buddha, the unsurpassed jewel, is difficult to encounter.
If one obtains the sight of the Buddha, all fear of the evil realms is forever severed. The Buddha is like a king of physicians, able to cure [all ailments]."
He who can save all from the diseases of every affliction and from the great suffering of birth and death— the Buddha, like a guide,
can lead sentient beings to the place of ultimate peace and security— having formed this thought, he assembled the minor kings, ministers, retinues,
as well as the kṣatriyas, brāhmaṇas, and the entire great assembly, and then relinquished his royal throne to bestow it upon them.
After the Prince had completed the consecration ceremony (*abhiṣeka*), he went together with ten thousand people to the place where the Buddha was.
Upon arrival, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and circumambulated him countless times; he and his retinue then all withdrew to sit.

At that time, the Tathāgata observed the King and the great assembly, and from the mark of the white tuft between his brows (*ūrṇā-kośa*), he emitted a great light named "Lamp of the Hearts of All Worlds," which universally illuminated the ten directions.
Abiding before all the lords of the worlds throughout immeasurable realms, he manifested the inconceivable great supernormal powers of a Tathāgata,
causing the minds of all those ready for transformation to attain purity. At that time, by means of his inconceivable and sovereign supernormal power,
the Tathāgata manifested a body that transcended all worlds, being perfectly complete.

The Voice universally preached for the great assembly *dhāraṇīs* named "Lamp Dispelling Darkness Regarding the Meaning of All Dharmas," with *dhāraṇīs* as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field serving as their retinue.
Upon hearing this, the King immediately attained the light of great wisdom;
within that assembly, Bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in Jambudvīpa simultaneously realized these *dhāraṇīs*.
Six hundred thousand nayutas of people, through this dharani, exhausted all outflows and attained liberation of mind;
ten thousand sentient beings were distanced from dust and freed from defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye; and immeasurable sentient beings resolved their minds upon Bodhi.
At that time, the Buddha, again by means of inconceivable power, extensively manifested spiritual transformations, expounding the Three Vehicles throughout immeasurable worlds in the ten directions.
When the Dharma was transforming and delivering sentient beings, his father, the King, thought to himself: "If I remain at home, I shall not be able to realize such a sublime Dharma;
if I instead leave the household life under the Buddha to study the Way, I shall surely achieve success. Having had this thought, he went before the Buddha and said:
"I pray that I may leave the household life under the Buddha to practice and study. The Buddha said: "As you wish; you should know this for yourself."
From time to time, King Dhanapati and ten thousand others all simultaneously went forth into homelessness in the presence of the Buddha;
before long, they all attained the accomplishment of the meaning of all dharmas, the *Vimalapradīpa-dhāraṇī*, as well as the aforementioned gateways of samādhi,
the gateways of the ten supernormal powers of a bodhisattva, and the boundless eloquence of a bodhisattva.
Having attained the unimpeded, pure body of a bodhisattva, they go to the abodes of all Tathāgatas throughout the ten directions to listen to and receive their teachings;

acting as great Dharma masters, they expound the sublime Dharma. Furthermore, by means of their supernormal powers, they manifest bodies in accordance with the minds of sentient beings throughout the lands of the ten directions, praising the appearance of Buddhas, recounting the original practices of Buddhas, revealing the original conditions of Buddhas, and extolling the virtues of the Tathāgatas themselves.

While the Buddha’s taught Dharma was being sustained by his supernormal power, at that time, on the fifteenth day, the Prince was in the main hall surrounded by court ladies when the seven treasures spontaneously appeared: first, the wheel treasure named Unobstructed Movement;
second, the elephant treasure named Vajra Body; third, the horse treasure named Swift Wind; fourth, the jewel treasure named...
The fifth was Sūryagarbha; the sixth, his jewel of a woman, was named Sumatī; the seventh, his jewel of a minister, was named Mahādhana;

and the eighth, his jewel of a military commander, was named Vimalanetra. Possessing these seven jewels, he became a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin) who ruled over Jambudvīpa with the True Dharma, bringing happiness to the people.
He had a thousand sons, all handsome, brave, and capable of subduing enemies.

Within Jambudvīpa, there were eighty royal cities; in each city there were five hundred monasteries, and in each monastery a stūpa for the Buddha was erected, all of which were lofty and vast and adorned with various exquisite jewels.
In every royal city, they invited the Tathāgata and made offerings with inconceivable and wondrous ritual implements as the Buddha entered.
At that time, he manifested great supernormal powers, causing immeasurable sentient beings to plant various roots of goodness;

immeasurable sentient beings attained purity of mind, seeing the Buddha with joy, generating the aspiration for enlightenment (*bodhicitta*), giving rise to great compassion, benefiting sentient beings,

diligently practicing the Buddha-dharma, entering into the true meaning, abiding in the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), realizing the equality of all dharmas, and attaining the wisdom of the three periods of time, and so forth.
Contemplating the three periods of time, they know the sequential emergence of all Buddhas and their preaching of various dharmas to gather in sentient beings;

they resolve the vows of Bodhisattvas and enter the Bodhisattva path; they know the Dharma of the Tathāgatas and achieve the ocean of Dharma; they are able to universally manifest their bodies throughout all lands;
they know the faculties, dispositions, and inclinations of sentient beings, causing them to give rise to the vow for omniscience—this is the Buddha.
"What do you think, son? Was that prince who attained the rank of a Wheel-Turning King and made offerings to the Buddha anyone else?
It was none other than the present Śākyamuni Buddha. As for King Dhanapati, he was the Buddha Ratnapuṣpa.
That Buddha Ratnapuṣpa currently resides in the eastern direction, beyond as many Buddha-fields as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds; there is an ocean of worlds named..."
Within the cloud of images of the space of the manifested dharma-realm, there is a world-system named Universal Manifestation of the Shadows of the Three Times Maṇi King.

Within that world-system, there is a world named Perfect Light, and within it is a site of enlightenment named Jewel Flower Manifesting the Bodies of All World Rulers. It is here that the Tathāgata has attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Surrounded before and behind by an assembly of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably many buddha-fields, he preached the Dharma.
When the Tathāgata Ratnakusuma was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, he purified this ocean of worlds;

all the Buddhas who have appeared, do appear, or will appear in the world throughout the past, future, and present within that ocean of worlds were all, while bodhisattvas, under the guidance of the Tathāgata Ratnakusuma.
At that time, she was taught and inspired to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The woman’s mother, Sunirmala, is now my mother, Sunetra; those who were the king’s retinue are this present assembly of the Tathāgata.

All have fully practiced the various deeds of Samantabhadra and perfected their great vows, and though they constantly remain within this assembly at the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), [they manifest in various forms].
They are able to universally manifest throughout all worlds, dwelling in the samādhi of equality of all bodhisattvas;
they constantly behold all Buddhas and all Tathāgatas as they turn the wheel of the true Dharma with clouds of wondrous voices equal to space, and they are able to hear and receive it all.
They have attained mastery over all dharmas, and their fame is heard throughout all Buddha-lands.
They go everywhere to all sites of enlightenment and appear before all sentient beings, teaching and taming them according to their needs;
throughout kalpas as numerous as those yet to come, they cultivate the bodhisattva path without interruption, fulfilling the vast vows of Samantabhadra.
O Son of the Buddha, that daughter of noble virtue, along with the Wheel-Turning Sage King Sovereign of Majestic Virtue, with four...
I myself am the one who performed the supreme service and offerings to the Tathāgata Sun-Body (Sūryakāya).
After that Buddha passed into extinction, sixty billion hundred thousand nayutas of Buddhas appeared in that world; I served and made offerings to them all along with the King.
The first of those Buddhas was named Pure Body (Vimalakāya); the next was named All-Knowledge Moon-Light Body (Sarvajñajyotirviśuddhakāya); the next...
The first was named Jambūnada-gold Radiance King; the second was named Body Adorned with All Marks; the third was named Wondrous Moonlight;
the fourth was named Banner of Wisdom Observation; the fifth was named Great Wisdom Light; the sixth was named Vajra Nārāyaṇa Diligence;
the seventh was named Invincible Power of Wisdom; the eighth was named Universal Tranquil Wisdom; and the ninth was named Cloud of Stainless Supreme Wisdom.
The first is named Lion Wisdom Radiance; the next is named Radiant Topknot; the next is named Banner of Merit Radiance; the next is named Banner of the Sun of Wisdom;
the next is named Body of Blossoming Jewel Lotuses; the next is named Adorned Pure Light of Merit; the next is named Cloud of Wisdom Flames;
the next is named Universally Illuminating Moon; the next is named Wondrous Sound of the Ornamented Canopy; and the next is named Lion.
The light of courageous wisdom is followed by the name Moon of the Dharma Realm; next is the name Manifesting the Reflections of Space to Awaken the Minds of Sentient Beings;
next is the name Constantly Inhaling the Fragrance of Quiescence; next is the name Universally Resounding Silent Sound;
next is the name Mountain of Ambrosia; next is the name Sound of the Ocean of Dharma; next is the name Firm Net; next is the name Buddha-Image Topknot; and next is the name Moonlight.
The next is named Tuft; the next is named Eloquence of the Mouth; the next is named Wisdom of the Awakened Flower; the next is named Mountain of Jewel Flames;
the next is named Star of Merit; the next is named Jewel Moon Banner; the next is named Body of Samādhi; the next is named King of Jewel Light;

the next is named Universal Course of Wisdom; the next is named Lamp of the Ocean of Flames; the next is named King of the Stainless Sound of Dharma; and the next is named Incomparable Virtue and Renown.

The names of the successive Buddhas were: Dhvaja (Banner), then Dīrghabāhu (Long Arm), then Praṇidhānaviśuddhicandra (Moon of Pure Vows), then Arthapradīpa (Lamp of Meaning), then Gambhīranirghoṣa (Deep and Far-Reaching Sound), then Vairocanavijayagarbharāja (King of the Victorious Treasury of Vairocana), then Sarvayānadhvaja (Banner of All Vehicles), and then Dharmasāgarasumeghapadma (Lotus of the Wondrous Clouds of the Ocean of Dharma).
Son of the Buddha, in that eon there were sixty billion hundred thousand nayutas of such [Buddhas].
Whenever a Buddha appeared in the world, I drew near to him, attended upon him, and made offerings to him. The last of those Buddhas was named Vistīrṇamatī.
Under that Buddha, I attained the pure eye of wisdom. At that time, when that Buddha entered the city to teach and transform beings, I was the king’s queen;
together with the king, I went to pay my respects and honored him with various exquisite objects. In the presence of that Buddha, I heard the teaching of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka*.
I immediately attained this Dharma-door of the Lamp that Gives Birth to All Tathāgatas, which is the liberation of observing the ocean-like realm of all Bodhisattva samādhis.
O Son of the Buddha, having attained this liberation, I have diligently practiced it for as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field,
and throughout those eons as numerous as atoms in a buddha-field, I have served and made offerings to [the Buddhas].
Suppose one were to serve a single Buddha for an eon, or two, or three, or an unspeakable number, or even as many Buddhas as there are atoms in a Buddha-field,
attending upon, serving, and making offerings to them all; yet one would still be unable to know the dimensions of the Bodhisattva’s body,
its physical appearance, nor the scope of his bodily actions, mental activities, wisdom, samādhis, and the realms of the Buddhas.
"Son, if there are sentient beings who, upon seeing a bodhisattva practicing the conduct of awakening, feel either doubt or faith,
the bodhisattva employs various mundane and supramundane skillful means to gather them in as followers,
causing them to attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. Son of the Buddha, I have seen that Buddha obtain this."
Having attained this liberation, I have practiced it together with bodhisattvas for as many eons as there are atoms in a hundred buddha-fields;
during those eons, I have personally approached, served, and made offerings to all the Buddhas who appeared in the world,
listening to the Dharma they taught, reading, reciting, receiving, and upholding it, thereby attaining these various aspects of this liberation from all those Tathāgatas.
They know various Dharma gates; they enter various oceans of lands throughout the three periods of time; they behold various Buddhas attaining perfect enlightenment;
they enter various assemblies of Buddha-disciples; they give rise to various great vows of Bodhisattvas; they cultivate various sublime practices of Bodhisattvas;
and they attain various liberations of Bodhisattvas. Yet, they are still unable to know the Samantabhadra liberation gate attained by Bodhisattvas.

For this reason, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra’s door of liberation is like the great void, like the names of sentient beings, like the ocean of the three periods of time, like the ocean of the ten directions, and like the ocean of the Dharma-realm; it is immeasurable and boundless.

O Son of the Buddha, the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra’s door of liberation is equal to the realm of the Tathāgata. O Son of the Buddha, for as many eons as there are atoms in a Buddha-field, I have contemplated the Bodhisattva...
My body never experiences satiety, like a person of great desire; when men and women gather together, they become mutually enamored, giving rise to immeasurable delusive thoughts and perceptions.

I, too, am thus: as I contemplate the body of a Bodhisattva, in every single pore and in every moment of thought, I see immeasurable and boundless vast worlds, each with its various modes of abiding, various adornments, and various forms.
Their manifestations include various mountains, various lands, various clouds, various names, the arising of various Buddhas,
various sites of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*), various assemblies, the preaching of various *sūtras*, various consecrations, various vehicles (*yāna*),
various skillful means (*upāya*), and various purities; furthermore, within every single pore of the Bodhisattvas, in every thought-moment, there is always...
I see boundless oceans of Buddhas seated upon various bodhimandas, manifesting various supernatural transformations,
turning various wheels of Dharma, and preaching various sūtras in a constant, uninterrupted stream; furthermore, within each and every pore of these Bodhisattvas,
I see boundless oceans of sentient beings with their various dwellings, various physical forms, various activities, and various faculties.
Furthermore, within each and every pore of the Bodhisattva, one sees the boundless gateways of practice of all Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time—
namely, their boundless and vast vows, their boundless distinctions of stages, their boundless perfections (*pāramitās*), their boundless past deeds, their boundless gates of great loving-kindness,
their boundless clouds of great compassion, their boundless mind of great joy, and their boundless gathering of sentient beings.
O Son of the Buddha, Master of Expedient Means, throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, I have thus contemplated, moment by moment, each and every pore of the Bodhisattva.
Wherever he has gone, I have not gone again; wherever I have seen him, I have not seen him again.
Yet, though I sought his limits, they could never be found—even until I beheld Prince Siddhārtha dwelling within the palace.

Surrounded by the inner court ladies, I use the power of liberation to contemplate each and every pore of the Bodhisattva, wherein I see all matters within the Dharma-realm of the three periods of time.
O Son of the Buddha, I have only attained this liberation of the ocean of samādhis for observing Bodhisattvas;
how could I know the ultimate, immeasurable oceans of skillful means of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas for the sake of all sentient beings?

He manifests bodies according to the various classes of beings to teach all sentient beings practices that accord with their inclinations; within each and every pore, he manifests an ocean of infinite forms and marks.
He knows that the nature of all phenomena is to have no-nature as its nature; he knows that the nature of sentient beings is identical to space and devoid of differentiation;
and he knows that the spiritual power of the Buddhas is identical to *tathatā* (suchness), manifesting everywhere throughout all places.

As for the dharma-gate of entering the realm of liberation from extremes with mastery in a single thought-moment, sporting within the vast dharma-realm and all the stages (*bhūmi*), how could I possibly know or speak of those meritorious practices?
Good son, in this world there is Māyā, the Mother of Buddhas; go to her and ask how a bodhisattva should cultivate the bodhisattva path.
Moving through all worlds without attachment, making offerings to all Buddhas without ever ceasing,
performing the deeds of a bodhisattva never to regress, free from all obstacles, entering the liberation of a bodhisattva without depending on others,
abiding in all bodhisattva paths, and proceeding to the presence of all Tathāgatas to encompass the realms of all sentient beings until the end of the future.
Having cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva for eons and made the vows of the Mahāyāna, they constantly increase the roots of goodness in all sentient beings without ever resting.
At that time, Śākyamuni’s daughter Gopā, wishing to clarify further the meaning of this liberation, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority,
spoke these verses:
If there are those who see a bodhisattva practicing various deeds, whether they give rise to wholesome or unwholesome thoughts, the bodhisattva gathers them all in.
In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in a hundred buddha-fields, there was an eon named Pure and a world named Radiant; in this eon, a Buddha appeared in the world.
Sixty quadrillion were the final lords of gods and men, Known by the name Dharma-dhvaja-pradīpa.
After that Buddha entered nirvana, There was a king named Jñāna-giri who ruled over Jambudvīpa;
He had no enemies whatsoever. The king had five hundred sons, Who were handsome, capable, and courageous.
His body was entirely pure, and all who saw him were filled with joy.

That king and his princes, with hearts of faith, made offerings to the Buddha and protected the treasury of his Dharma. Furthermore, the Prince named Sunlight delighted in diligently practicing the Dharma;
free from defilement and possessing many skillful means, he was perfected in all the primary marks.

Those who behold him never tire of doing so; five billion people together have left the household life to practice the Way with courageous and steadfast diligence, protecting and upholding his Buddha-dharma.
The royal capital is named Jñānavṛkṣa (Tree of Wisdom), surrounded by a thousand billion cities; there is a grove named Śāntaguṇa (Peaceful Virtue), adorned with all kinds of jewels.
The One of Excellent Radiance dwelt in that forest, widely proclaiming the Buddha’s True Dharma.
By the power of his eloquence and wisdom, he caused all beings to become pure. At one time, for the sake of alms, he entered the king’s capital city;
his every movement was exceedingly composed and serene. With right mindfulness, his mind was undisturbed. Within the city, there was a householder.
Known by the name Shanmingcheng (Good Renown), at that time I was that woman named Jingri guang (Pure Sunlight).
Then, within the city, I encountered Shan guangming (Good Radiance), whose various marks were exceedingly sublime and majestic;
my heart gave rise to defiled attachment. Subsequently, when he came to beg at my door, my mind’s passion and defilement increased.
He immediately untied his body’s necklace, And placed the pearls within the bowl.
Although he made this offering with a mind of attachment, For two hundred and fifty kalpas, He did not fall into the three evil realms.
Instead, he was born into the family of a celestial king, Or became the daughter of a human king, Constantly beholding the light of goodness.

With a body adorned with wondrous marks, throughout the kalpas that followed, for two hundred and fifty births, he was born into the family of Sunirmita, named Sumatideva. At that time, upon seeing the Prince, I conceived a heart of deep reverence;
I vowed to behold him fully and was fortunate enough to receive his compassionate acceptance.
At that time, I went with the crown prince to visit the Buddha Jayasūryakāya; having completed our respectful offerings, we immediately resolved upon bodhicitta.
During that single kalpa, there were sixty billion Tathāgatas, the last of whom was the World-Honored One named Vipulaprajña; it was from him that I attained the pure eye.
Having thoroughly understood the characteristics of all phenomena, I universally behold the places where beings take birth;
Forever eliminating the mind of perversion, I have attained the Bodhisattva’s Samādhi of the Realm of Liberation.
In a single thought-moment, I enter the inconceivable ocean of lands throughout the ten directions; I see all worlds, With their various distinctions of purity and defilement.
Neither craving for the pure nor increasing aversion toward the defiled,
they see throughout all worlds the Tathāgatas seated at the site of enlightenment. Within a single thought-moment,
they emit immeasurable light and are able to enter universally into unspeakably many assemblies, knowing them all as well.
The gates of samādhi attained, which they can fully know in a single thought; those vast practices,
the immeasurable skillful means of the stages, and the oceans of their vows—
I observe the bodies of these Bodhisattvas as they practice through boundless eons, yet even the measure of a single pore cannot be found when sought.
Within each and every pore are lands, Innumerable and beyond description. The wheels of earth, water, fire, and wind are all contained therein;
With various foundations, Various forms, various substances, and various names, Adorned with boundless varieties— I behold these oceans of lands.
One cannot describe the worlds, nor can one see the Buddhas therein who teach the Dharma to transform sentient beings;
one does not understand the bodies of the Bodhisattvas, nor their various physical actions, nor the wisdom of their minds,
nor the paths they traverse throughout the kalpas.
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet, circumambulated him countless times, and took his leave to depart.
[Commentary] Within the first section, the Dharma-gate of correctly entering the stage, the passage from "At that time, the youth Sudhana" onwards is divided into six sections:
(1) from "At that time, the youth Sudhana" down to "will before long attain realization."

Because it concerns the unsurpassed fruit, there are nineteen lines of sūtra clarifying that when Sudhana arrives at the Hall of Dharma-realm Radiance, the goddess Aśokaśrī and ten thousand palace-lord goddesses come to welcome him, praising Sudhana’s resolve, virtue, and his courageous diligence in generating the bodhicitta.
This section is divided into two parts: from "Sudhana the youth" down to the verse.
A section of the sutra clarifies Sudhana’s own account of his bodhisattva vows and his practice of benefiting sentient beings.
As he was about to ascend the Dharma hall, various deities scattered flowers as an offering to Sudhana.

Following this section, there are ten verses of praise by the deity Viśeṣamati (The God of Unrivalled Virtue) extolling the youth Sudhana, as clearly detailed in the text. At that time, the deity Viśeṣamati...

From "Having thus [attained]... down to "constantly practicing all virtuous deeds without ceasing," there are twenty-five lines of scripture clarifying how Sudhana went to the abode of Gopā and requested what he sought; this is divided into four periods. From "Gopā said to Sudhana...
down to the verse, this section clarifies how the maiden Gopā expounded for Sudhana the *Indra-dharmamukha-samādhi*, which is the cause of the bodhisattva practice.
The *Jālinīprabha-jñāna* and the ten kinds of practices of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*),
along with twenty-four verses that restate the preceding dharmas, are explained in five stages by Śākyaghoṣa.
From this point down to "because all Tathāgatas fully know the light of liberation," there are fifty-six lines of scripture that clarify [the teaching].
The sixth section, "Gopā’s Answer to Sudhana’s Inquiry Regarding the Scope of the Dharma-Gate," begins with Sudhana the youth addressing Gopā and continues to the end of the fascicle.
This section generally clarifies the answer to Sudhana’s inquiry concerning the duration for which he has attained the Dharma.
Following the literal explanation of the text, it states that by traveling in successive stages, one clarifies the ascent to the preceding levels and reaches the stage of a Bodhisattva.
The "Assembly Hall of the Universal Manifestation of the Dharma-realm Radiance" clarifies that the two wisdoms—mundane and supramundane—of the ten stages are pure, equal, and all-pervasive;
that wisdom and compassion are purely refined, and that all consecrated Bodhisattvas assemble in this hall.
Because these two wisdoms are identical with reality, they are called the "Universal Manifestation of the Dharma-realm Wisdom-Light," which destroys darkness.
The Radiance, which universally encompasses manifold dharmas through a single right gnosis, is called the Lecture Hall.
Within it dwells a deity named Sorrowless Virtue (*Aśoka-guṇa*), who is accompanied by ten thousand palace-deity lords to welcome Sudhana.

These are known as the Palace Deity Lords of Great Loving-kindness and Great Compassion, whose minds protect all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm; there are ten thousand such deities.

This is called the "Ten Thousand Practices" (myriad practices). Regarding the "welcoming," it is because at this stage, Sudhana’s world-transcending wisdom and compassion, as well as his spiritual rank, are in accord;
thus, it clarifies the advancement where wisdom and compassion meet at this stage. This is precisely why Gopā is made the mistress of the perfection of wisdom and compassion;
since she was born into a royal lineage, the king represents wisdom and the woman represents [compassion].

The expression "the ten thousand lords of the palace deities manifesting compassion" signifies that the primary lord and his retinue of ten thousand have perfected the meaning of the myriad practices.
Below this, the praise of Sudhana’s resolve and virtue is self-evident according to the text. When Sudhana ascends to the Hall of Dharma, he enters the stage [of realization].

Entering the Lecture Hall of Universal Manifestation of the Dharmadhātu Radiance means he has entered into the universal embodiment of the Tathāgata’s wisdom, principle, great compassion, and essential nature.
"Because he thoroughly sought [the truth] throughout the Zhou, he entered the stage of contemplative wisdom; his realization of the initial entry into this stage represents his spiritual advancement.
'The daughter of the Śākya clan' refers to her family name. 'Sitting upon a precious lotus lion-throne within the lecture hall' signifies conduct free from defilement.
'The eighty-four thousand court ladies' represent the eighty-four thousand afflictions, all of which are [subdued] through compassion."
All his companions were those born from the royal lineage who had given rise to clear compassion;
having been born from King Jñāna, these four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*) ensured that all his companions never departed from the realm of wisdom.

Below this, it describes the aspirations and virtues of Gopā and her attendants as clearly explained in the text. Next, Sudhana arrives at Gopā and requests what he seeks; Gopā then explains for him what [he should practice].
The method for seeking this is clearly explained in the text below, within the section on the realm of the Dharma-gate entered by Sudhana.
It states that roots of goodness subsumed under roots of non-goodness are like performing coarse actions while possessing subtle principles;

or like those in the world who, though practicing what is improper, are still able to perform a portion of wholesome deeds; or like the practitioners of external paths whose conduct is wrong and whose views are likewise erroneous.
That which is generally unwholesome yet seeks the wholesome is subsumed under the roots of goodness.

Unwholesome roots—such as those of humans, devas, and non-Buddhist worldlings—which are not subsumed under the roots of goodness and cannot eliminate the karma of suffering within the three realms, are unwholesome roots.
Furthermore, the roots of goodness of the two vehicles and the bodhisattvas of the Pure Land, who suppress the karma of the three realms so that it does not manifest, are roots of goodness.

That which is subsumed [by these roots] has not yet attained realization of the Tathāgata’s wisdom and compassion; it is an unwholesome root because it is subsumed by unwholesome roots that are themselves wholesome roots.

Furthermore, as in the case of the daughter of Gopa, who in a former life was the daughter of a householder and gave a jeweled necklace with a mind of passionate attachment—this was subsumed by an unwholesome root. Because of this, [she underwent] two hundred and five...
For ten kalpas, they do not enter the three evil realms, but are born among humans and devas, and within royal lineages, even reaching the stages up to the tenth bhūmi;
these are roots of goodness encompassed by [the transformation of] roots of non-virtue. The rest is self-evident in the text.

For example, it is like those who rely on non-Buddhists and followers of false views, lacking correct knowledge and vision, yet falsely claiming their path to be the true path and consequently generating the aspiration for enlightenment. Ultimately...
Those who cannot attain liberation, who give rise to false views, and enter the realms of suffering— these are subsumed within the roots of goodness,

while the roots of unwholesomeness are like the seeds of a world-system. As for what is subsumed by the "seeds of a world-system," as already explained regarding the Flower Treasury World (*Puṣpasaṃbhava-lokadhātu*),
it refers to a single great world-system surrounded on all four sides by attendant lands as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields.

Regarding the establishment of the world-systems (*dhātu-cakra*): it is like the wind-wheel at the very bottom which supports the water, the water supports the vajra, and the vajra supports the great earth;
this is because they mutually assist one another through the element of fire. "Succession" (*krama*) refers to the sequence, for they are established in successive order.
As for the "world-field" (*dharmadhātu-kṣetra*), it may be taken as the field of practice (*maṇḍala*) based on the dharma-gates one practices, and it is also called a "field" (*kṣetra*).
That which is level can treat the high and low as a field; "worlds" refers to a great number in the western tradition.
The rest is as stated in the text. Regarding Sudhana’s inquiry into the duration since he attained the Dharma, ten sections are established:
first, citing the vast number of kalpas, it says "passing through kalpas as numerous as the atoms of Buddha-fields"; second, citing a kalpa named "Victorious Practice" (*Vijayacaryā*).
1. He raised up the world-system named Abhayā. 2. Within that world-system, he raised up the four continents named Kṣema.
3. Within those four continents, he raised up Jambudvīpa. 4. Within Jambudvīpa, he raised up the city named Udgatavijaya.
5. Among the eighty cities, this city was the foremost. 6. He raised up the king, whose name was...
[Section 9] The Lord of Wealth, King Daśagrīva, had sixty thousand court ladies; [Section 10] the ministers and princes each possessed five hundred [attendants].
These ten preceding sections clarify the general causes for the initial generation of the resolve [for enlightenment].
The following sections clarify the Prince’s name, Vīryaprabha; his excursion; his marriage to Gopā; and the causes for his meeting with the Buddha.
Based on this section, ten topical gateways are established: first, the Prince goes out for a tour of observation;
second, the mother and daughter of Sujātā see the Prince and their hearts become stained with desire; third, the mother reflects that she is of lowly station and thus not a suitable match for him;
fourth, while the young woman is asleep, she sees a dream of the Victorious Sun-Light Buddha, and upon waking, a deity further addresses her.

When the Buddha Sunlight of Supreme Radiance appeared in the world, five young maidens personally proclaimed their own virtuous qualities and offered themselves to be accepted as his consorts, vowing, "May you graciously accept us. He accepted them and they gave birth to six princes.

When asked which of the maidens was the guardian and to whom they had previously belonged, the seven maidens' mother spoke verses to proclaim the virtues of the daughters and the causes for their births from within lotuses.

The magically born daughter was born on the same day as the Prince. When the nine princes entered the Garden of Fragrant Sprouts, they asked the girl and her mother, "We are practicing the bodhisattva path;
will you not hinder us? The nine girls replied to the Prince, "We respectfully accept your instructions.
The Prince took the girls as his consorts and scattered five hundred mani jewels over their bodies.
The above ten sections clarify the Prince’s taking of a wife and the young maiden’s receiving of her station.
From here below, regarding the female mother, Bhadraśrī, praising the daughter’s wisdom and virtue, there are further ten sections: first, the female mother praising the daughter’s virtues;
second, the Prince, together with Bhadraśrī and ten thousand court ladies, proceeding to the Gandhahasti Garden on the Path of Dharma-Cloud Radiance.
In that place, the three princes and their sister saw the Buddha and made offerings to him; the Buddha then preached for them the *Puyan dengmen jing* (Sūtra of the Universal Eye Lamp Gate).
Having heard this Dharma, the five princes and their sister attained oceans of samādhis within all dharmas.
The daughter of Wondrous Virtue attained a samādhi named "Ocean-Treasury of Difficult-to-Vanquish," whereby she became forever non-retrogressive from the great bodhicitta.

The seven princes took their leave of the Buddha and returned to the palace, where they informed their parents that the Tathāgata had appeared in the world. Upon hearing this, the eight kings were filled with joy;

These are bodies born at will, bodies without arising or ceasing, bodies without coming or going, and bodies that are neither unreal nor real, remaining immutable and indestructible.

The body is without arising or ceasing; all characteristics of the body are but a single characteristic; the body is free from the two extremes; the body has no place of dependence; the body is inexhaustible;

"Noble son, you should guard the city of the mind; that is to say, you must be free from greed."
One should adorn the city of the mind regarding all realms of birth and death, which means focusing one's intent on seeking the ten powers of the Tathāgata.
One should purify the city of the mind, which means ultimately severing stinginess, malice, flattery, and deception.
One should cool the city of the mind, which means contemplating the true nature of all phenomena. One should expand the city of the mind, which means accomplishing all factors conducive to the path.
The Dharma of this [practice] should adorn the city of the mind, meaning one should construct the palaces of various meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*) and liberations (*vimokṣa*).
It should illuminate the city of the mind, meaning one should universally enter all the *bodhimaṇḍas* of the Buddhas to hear and receive the *prajñāpāramitā* teachings.

It should augment the city of the mind, meaning one should universally gather all the skillful means (*upāya*) of the Buddhas. It should fortify the city of the mind, meaning one should be constantly diligent.
In practicing the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra, one should guard the city of the mind; that is, one should constantly and single-mindedly ward off evil friends and the armies of Māra.
One should clear and expand the city of the mind; that is, one should open it to and draw in the light of the wisdom of all Buddhas. One should skillfully repair the city of the mind;
that is, one should listen to and receive all the teachings spoken by all Buddhas. One should support the city of the mind; that is, one should have deep faith in the merits of all Buddhas.
One should make the city of the mind vast and expansive like an ocean of virtue, meaning that great loving-kindness should be extended universally to all worlds.

One should well-shelter the city of the mind, meaning that one should gather all wholesome dharmas to cover it from above. One should make the city of the mind broad and spacious, meaning that one should feel great compassion and pity for all sentient beings.
One should open the gates of the city of the mind, meaning that one should relinquish all that one possesses and bestow them as gifts according to need. One should keep [the city] secret...

One should guard the city of the mind, meaning one must prevent all evil desires from entering; one should fortify the city of the mind, meaning one must expel all unwholesome dharmas so they do not remain;
one should stabilize the city of the mind, meaning one must gather all the factors conducive to the path toward omniscience without ever regressing;
and one should establish the city of the mind, meaning one must maintain right mindfulness of all that pertains to the Tathāgatas of the three periods of time.

One should polish the citadel of the mind so that its boundaries are translucent; this means clearly penetrating all the Dharma-gates and various dependent originations within the sūtras of the True Dharma Wheel of all Buddhas.
One should partition the citadel of the mind; this means universally illuminating and showing all sentient beings so that they may all perceive the path to *sarvajñā* (omniscience).
One should maintain the citadel of the mind; this means generating [the resolve for] all three periods of time.
The Tathāgata’s ocean of great vows should enrich and fulfill the city of the mind, meaning that one should gather a vast accumulation of all-pervading merit throughout the entire Dharma-realm;
it should cause the city of the mind to be clear and lucid, meaning that one should universally know the faculties, desires, and other dharmas of sentient beings;

Son of the Buddha, if a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva can thus purify the city of the mind, they will be able to accumulate all virtues.

Now, that person, seated upon that throne before the assembly of all beings, manifests a pure form-body—namely, a form-body that transcends the three realms because it has emerged from all states of existence;

The body of comparison, because it causes all sentient beings to extinguish inverted views;
the body of immeasurable kinds, because it manifests in various ways according to the minds of sentient beings; the body of boundless marks, because it universally manifests all manner of forms;

Because it manifests before one's eyes, it is the inexhaustible color-body that appears throughout the entire realm of sentient beings without ever ending;
it is the non-departing color-body because it does not perish in any state of existence; it is the non-coming color-body because it does not emerge from any world;
it is the unborn color-body because it has no origination; it is the non-ceasing color-body because it is beyond the reach of language; and it is the non-substantial color-body.

Because it attains reality as it is, it is the non-illusory body; because it manifests in accordance with the world, it is the immovable body; because it is forever free from arising and ceasing, it is the indestructible body;
because the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) is indestructible, it is the signless body; because it transcends the path of speech, it is the single-characteristic body;
because it takes signlessness as its characteristic, it is the body like a reflection; because it appears in response to the mind, it is the body like an illusion.
The form-body is born from illusory wisdom, and is thus like a mirage; the form-body is sustained by mere mental conception, and is thus like a shadow;
the form-body manifests according to vows, and is thus like a dream; the form-body appears in accordance with the mind, and is thus like a reflection;

the dharma-realm form-body is pure in nature like space; the form-body of great compassion constantly protects sentient beings; and the unimpeded form-body pervades everywhere in every thought-moment.
Because it is the dharma-realm, it is the boundless body of form; because it universally purifies all sentient beings, it is the immeasurable body of form;
because it transcends all speech, it is the non-abiding body of form; because it vows to deliver all worlds, it is the placeless body of form;
because it constantly transforms sentient beings without interruption, it is the birthless body of form; because it is accomplished through illusory vows, it is the unsurpassed body of form.
The form-body that transcends all worlds; the form-body manifested by the concentrated mind according to reality;

the form-body that does not arise [inherently] yet appears in accordance with the karma of sentient beings; the form-body like a wish-fulfilling jewel that universally fulfills the aspirations of all sentient beings;
the form-body free from discrimination, arising merely in accordance with the discrimination of sentient beings; and the form-body detached from discrimination for all sentient beings.
Because it cannot be known by ordinary beings, it is the inexhaustible body; because it reaches the limit of birth and death for all sentient beings, it is the pure body;
because it is non-discriminative like the Tathāgata, such a body is not that which belongs to form, for its form-appearance is like a reflection;
it is not sensation, for worldly suffering-sensation is ultimately extinguished; it is not perception, for it merely accords with the perceptions of sentient beings.
Because it is manifested [only] as an appearance, it is not the basis for conditioned activity; because it is accomplished through karma that is like an illusion;
because it is devoid of the nature of consciousness, being the empty wisdom of the Bodhisattva’s vows; because all the speech of sentient beings has been severed;

and because he has already attained the body of perfect quiescence—at that time, the youth Sudhana again saw Lady Māyā manifesting herself according to the inclinations of the minds of all sentient beings.
Surpassing all worldly form-bodies— whether manifesting as bodies surpassing those of the goddesses of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Heaven up to those of the goddesses of the Cāturmahārājika Heaven;
or manifesting as bodies surpassing those of nāga maidens up to those of human women— he manifests such immeasurable form-bodies to benefit sentient beings, gathering them into one.
Practicing the methods that assist all-knowledge on the path of equality, they perform the perfection of giving (*dāna-pāramitā*) with great compassion universally covering all worlds;
they give birth to the immeasurable merits of a Tathāgata, cultivate and increase the mind of omniscience,
observe and contemplate the true nature of all phenomena, attain the ocean of profound patience, and dwell in the gateways of manifold concentrations within the samādhi of equality.
Having attained the Tathāgata’s concentration of the perfection of light within their sphere of experience, they exhaust the great ocean of sentient beings’ afflictions;
their minds are always in right concentration, never wavering or disturbed, as they constantly turn the pure, non-retrogressive wheel of Dharma.

They are well able to comprehend all Buddha-dharmas, and by constantly observing the true reality of phenomena with wisdom, they behold all Tathāgatas without ever feeling weary or satiated, knowing the three... [knowing the three].
The Buddhas appearing in succession throughout the world, the Samādhi of Constantly Manifesting the Vision of the Buddhas, are ever present before them.
They thoroughly comprehend the appearance of the Tathāgatas in the world and practice immeasurable and innumerable paths of purity.

Within the space-like realm of all Buddhas, they universally gather in sentient beings, teaching and transforming them according to their respective inclinations, leading them to accomplishment and entry into the immeasurable, pure Dharma-body of the Buddha. They achieve this perfection.
With great vows, they purify all Buddha-fields and ultimately subdue the minds of all sentient beings;
they constantly and universally enter the realms of all Buddhas and give rise to the sovereign spiritual powers of Bodhisattvas.

Having attained the pure and undefiled Dharma-body, they constantly manifest immeasurable form-bodies, crush all demonic forces, accomplish the power of great roots of goodness, and bring forth the True Dharma.
Endowed with power, they attain the powers of all Buddhas and the sovereign power of all Bodhisattvas;

they swiftly increase the power of all-knowledge and attain the light of Buddha-wisdom that universally illumines all, fully knowing the ocean of minds, faculties, natures, desires, and inclinations of immeasurable sentient beings in their various differences.
Their bodies pervade the oceans of lands throughout the ten directions, fully knowing the formation and destruction of all those lands.
With marks of such vastness, they see the oceans of the ten directions with their eyes; with all-pervasive wisdom, they know the oceans of the three periods of time;
their bodies universally serve the oceans of all Buddhas; their minds constantly receive and uphold the oceans of all dharmas;
they cultivate the merits of all Tathāgatas and give birth to the wisdom of all Bodhisattvas; and they always delight in observing all Bodhisattvas from their very beginning.

From the initial generation of the mind of enlightenment until the accomplishment of the path of practice, she constantly and diligently protected all sentient beings and always delighted in praising the merits of all Buddhas; may she become the mother of all Bodhisattvas.
At that time, the youth Sudhana saw Lady Māyā manifest such gates of skillful means as numerous as the atoms of Jambudvīpa. Having seen this...
Having seen this, Sudhana manifested as many bodies as were manifested by Lady Māyā;

in every place, before Lady Māyā, he paid respectful homage. Immediately, he realized countless and innumerable gates of samādhi, examining, practicing, and entering them through discernment. Rising from samādhi, he circumambulated Lady Māyā to the right.

Together with their retinues, they stood with palms joined and said: "O Great Sage Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, you have instructed us to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and to seek out spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) to attend and make offerings to.
We have gone to serve each and every spiritual friend without failing in our duties, and have gradually arrived here. We pray that...
"For me, tell how a bodhisattva studies the bodhisattva practice and attains its fulfillment.
She replied, "Son of the Buddha, I have attained the bodhisattva liberation door of the illusory wisdom of great vows; therefore, I am constantly the mother of all bodhisattvas.
Son of the Buddha, as I was born from the right side of Queen Māyā in the house of King Śuddhodana in the city of Kapilavastu within this Jambudvīpa..."
And so was born Prince Siddhārtha, manifesting inconceivable and sovereign miraculous transformations;
and in this manner, even all the Vairocana Tathāgatas throughout this entire ocean of worlds entered my body, manifesting the sovereign miraculous transformations of their birth.
Furthermore, noble son, when the Bodhisattva was about to descend into the palace of King Śuddhodana...
At the time of birth, one sees that from every single pore of the Bodhisattva’s body, light is emitted called the "Wheel of Merit for the Birth of All Tathāgatas.

Within each and every pore, there appear as many manifestations of the adornments of the births of bodhisattvas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields. All of those lights universally illuminate all worlds.
Having illuminated the world, the light entered my crown and even into all my pores;

furthermore, within that light, there were universally manifested the names of all bodhisattvas, their miraculous births, their transformations, their palaces, and their retinues, as they enjoyed themselves amidst the five desires.
Moreover, I saw them renounce the household life, proceed to the site of enlightenment, attain equal and perfect awakening, and sit upon the lion throne, surrounded by bodhisattvas.
He saw the various kings making offerings as [the Buddha] turned the wheel of the true Dharma for the great assembly;

he also saw that when the Tathāgata was practicing the bodhisattva path in the past, he respectfully made offerings at the abodes of various Buddhas, resolved his mind on bodhi, purified buddha-fields,
and manifested immeasurable transformation bodies in every thought-moment, pervading all worlds throughout the ten directions, even until the very end.

I saw all such matters as his entry into parinirvāṇa. Furthermore, son of good family, when that wondrous light entered my body, although the dimensions of my physical form did not exceed its original state, it had in fact already transcended all worlds. Why is this?
At that time, my body was equal in measure to empty space, capable of fully containing the bodhisattvas of the ten directions.

Because they adorn the various palaces for the sake of taking birth, at that time when the Bodhisattva was about to descend from the Tuṣita Heaven, there were bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within the Buddha-fields of the ten directions;

all of them shared the same vows, the same practices, the same roots of goodness, the same adornments, the same liberations, and the same wisdom. They possessed the same stages, the same powers, and the same dharma-bodies and form-bodies.
Surrounded by bodhisattvas whose spiritual powers, conduct, and vows were all equal to those of Samantabhadra,
and further accompanied by eighty thousand dragon kings and all the lords of the world who arrived riding upon their palaces to make offerings to the Bodhisattva,
he then, through his supernormal power, manifested himself universally in all the Tuṣita heavens together with the bodhisattvas.
Within a single palace, there appeared the reflections of all births within Jambudvīpa in every world throughout the ten directions;
through these skillful means of teaching and transforming, he led immeasurable sentient beings and caused all bodhisattvas to abandon all indolence and remain free from attachment.
Furthermore, by his supernormal power, he emitted great light that universally illuminated the world, destroying all darkness and extinguishing all suffering and affliction.
All sentient beings recognize their own past karmic actions and are forever delivered from the evil realms;
furthermore, for the sake of rescuing and protecting all sentient beings, they appear before them and manifest various divine transformations, displaying such extraordinary and marvelous deeds.
Together with their retinues, they enter my body, and those bodhisattvas move about freely within my belly, or...
Taking a trichiliocosm as a single step, or taking worlds as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields as a single step; furthermore, within every thought-moment,
[he beholds] all the Tathāgatas, their assemblies of Bodhisattvas, and the Four Heavenly Kings throughout unspeakably unspeakable numbers of all worlds in the ten directions.

The gods of the thirteen heavens, up to the Brahma kings of the form realm, desiring to behold the miraculous transformation of the Bodhisattva dwelling in the womb, to pay respectful homage and offerings, and to listen to and receive the True Dharma, all enter my body.

Although my belly can fully accommodate such a vast assembly, my body neither becomes enlarged nor does it become cramped; each of those bodhisattvas perceives themselves as remaining in their own respective places.

The assembly and the site of enlightenment are pure and magnificently adorned. Good son, just as I am the mother of the Bodhisattvas who take birth within the Jambudvīpa of this four-continent world system, it is likewise so for all the billions of four-continent world systems within the trichiliocosm.
Yet, this body of mine is fundamentally non-dual; it does not abide in one place alone, nor is it manifold.
Why do they dwell in many places? It is because they have cultivated the liberation door of the adornment of the illusory wisdom of the great vows of Bodhisattvas.
Good son, just as I am the mother of the present World-Honored One, so too was I the mother of all the immeasurable Buddhas of the past.
Good son, in the past, when I was a deity of a lotus pond, there was...
When a Bodhisattva was suddenly born by transformation within a lotus treasury, I immediately cradled, attended, and nurtured him;

all the world together called me the "Mother of the Bodhisattva. Furthermore, when I was formerly the deity of the Bodhimaṇḍa, a Bodhisattva was suddenly born by transformation within my womb, and the world likewise called me the "Mother of the Bodhisattva," O son of good family.
"Noble son, for all the immeasurable bodhisattvas in their final birth who manifest taking birth in this world through various skillful means,
I have been their mother. Noble son, likewise, during the past ages within this Bhadrakalpa of this world,
for Krakucchanda Buddha, Kanakamuni Buddha, Kāśyapa Buddha, and the present World-Honored One Śākyamuni..."

When the Buddha was manifesting his descent into birth, I was his mother. In a future age, when Maitreya Bodhisattva is about to descend from Tuṣita Heaven, he will emit a great light that universally illumines the Dharma-realm, manifesting the supernatural transformations of all bodhisattvas as they take birth.
He will then be born into a great clan among human beings to subdue sentient beings; at that time, I— [will likewise serve him].
