Chapter Thirty-nine, Part Twenty-nine: Entering the Dharma Realm.
[Treatise] Following these eleven stages, the gateway to attaining the fruit of Buddhahood in a single lifetime from Maitreya is presented;
within this gateway, it is extensively divided into ten sections.
[Sūtra] "Good son, to the south of here there is a land named Sāgara-tīra (Seashore).

There is a garden named Mahā-vyūha (Great Adornment), and within it is a vast, lofty pavilion named Vairocana-vyūha-garbha (Vairocana Adornment Treasury). It is born from the karmic fruition of the bodhisattvas' roots of goodness;
it is born from the power of the bodhisattvas' mindfulness, the power of their vows, the power of their mastery, and the power of their supernormal knowledges; it is born from the bodhisattvas..."
Born from skillful means, arising from the merit and wisdom of bodhisattvas— good sons who dwell in the inconceivable liberation—
these bodhisattvas manifest such realms for the sake of all sentient beings through their great compassion and assemble such adornments.
Maitreya Bodhisattva Mahāsattva dwells therein, desiring to embrace those by whom he was originally born.
It is for the sake of bringing to maturity those dwelling among parents, kinsmen, and all the people;
furthermore, it is because he wishes to cause those beings who share the same birth and the same practice to attain firmness within the Mahāyāna;

furthermore, it is because he wishes to cause all those sentient beings to achieve accomplishment according to their respective stages and roots of goodness; and furthermore, it is because he wishes to reveal to you the liberation of a bodhisattva.
By means of the doors of liberation, it demonstrates the Bodhisattva’s mastery over taking birth in all places;
it demonstrates the Bodhisattva’s constant teaching of all sentient beings by universally manifesting before them in various bodies;
it demonstrates the Bodhisattva’s tireless universal gathering of all worldly resources through the power of great compassion; and it demonstrates the Bodhisattva.
Having fully cultivated all practices, he knows that all practices are free from signs; he manifests birth in various places for Bodhisattvas, understanding that all births are signless.
Go to him and ask: how does a Bodhisattva practice the Bodhisattva conduct?
How does he cultivate the Bodhisattva path? How does he study the Bodhisattva precepts? How does he purify the Bodhisattva mind? How...
How does one arouse the bodhisattva vow? How does one practice the bodhisattva’s aids to enlightenment? How does one enter the bodhisattva stages? How does one fulfill the bodhisattva perfections?
How does one attain the bodhisattva’s patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena? How does one become endowed with the qualities of a bodhisattva?
How does one serve the spiritual friends of a bodhisattva? For what reason, noble son, is that bodhi... [text ends]
That Bodhisattva Mahāsattva has mastered all bodhisattva practices, knows the minds of all sentient beings,
and constantly manifests before them to teach and subdue them; he has fulfilled all pāramitās, dwells in all bodhisattva stages,
realized all bodhisattva patiences, entered all bodhisattva positions, and has received [the prediction].
Having been granted the full prediction, having traversed all the realms of the bodhisattvas, having attained the spiritual power of all Buddhas,
and having received the empowerment upon the crown of his head by all Tathāgatas with the nectar-water of the Dharma of omniscience—
O son of good family, that spiritual friend can moisten all your roots of goodness, can increase your bodhicitta, and can strengthen you.
Your resolve can benefit you; it can well cause your bodhisattva faculties to grow. It can show you the unimpeded Dharma; it can cause you to enter the stage of Samantabhadra.
It can explain the vows of a bodhisattva for you; it can explain the conduct of Samantabhadra for you;
it can explain the merits accomplished through all the practices and vows of a bodhisattva. Good son, you should not practice only one.

One should skillfully illuminate the practice of a single dharma, undertake a single practice, give rise to a single vow, attain a single mindfulness, and realize a single patience, conceiving the thought of ultimate perfection.
One should not practice the six perfections with a limited mind, nor dwell upon the ten stages, purifying buddha-fields, or serving spiritual friends.
Why is this? Good son, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should plant immeasurable roots of goodness.

One should gather immeasurable requisites for enlightenment; one should cultivate immeasurable causal conditions for enlightenment; one should train in immeasurable skillful dedications; one should transform immeasurable realms of sentient beings;
one should know the immeasurable minds of sentient beings; one should know the immeasurable faculties of sentient beings;
one should recognize the immeasurable inclinations of sentient beings; one should observe the immeasurable conduct of sentient beings; one should subdue [immeasurable sentient beings];...
One should measure the sentient beings who must sever immeasurable afflictions, purify immeasurable karmic habits, extinguish immeasurable false views,
eliminate immeasurable defiled minds, generate immeasurable pure minds, extract immeasurable poisonous arrows of suffering,
dry up immeasurable oceans of craving and desire, shatter immeasurable darkness of ignorance, and destroy immeasurable...

The mountain of self-conceit should be severed; the bonds of immeasurable birth and death should be cut; the torrents of immeasurable existence should be crossed; the ocean of immeasurable rebirth should be dried up;
immeasurable sentient beings should be led out from the mire of the five desires; immeasurable sentient beings should be made to leave the prison of the triple world;
immeasurable sentient beings should be established upon the Noble Path; and [all afflictions] should be extinguished.
One should purify immeasurable conduct of desire, destroy immeasurable conduct of hatred, transcend immeasurable conduct of delusion,
leave behind immeasurable nets of Māra, purify immeasurable deeds of Māra, increase immeasurable aspirations of a bodhisattva,
augment immeasurable skillful means of a bodhisattva, and bring forth immeasurable superior faculties of a bodhisattva.
One should clarify the bodhisattva’s immeasurable resolute understanding; one should enter into the bodhisattva’s immeasurable equanimity;
one should purify the bodhisattva’s immeasurable merits; one should cultivate and refine the bodhisattva’s immeasurable practices;
one should manifest the bodhisattva’s immeasurable conduct that accords with the world; one should generate immeasurable power of pure faith; and one should abide in the immeasurable.
The power of diligence should purify the immeasurable; the power of right mindfulness should fulfill the immeasurable; the power of samādhi should give rise to the immeasurable;
the power of pure wisdom should strengthen the immeasurable; the power of resolute conviction should gather the immeasurable;
the power of merit should extend the immeasurable; the power of wisdom should initiate the immeasurable; and the power of the bodhisattvas should perfect the immeasurable qualities of the Tathāgatas.
One should distinguish the immeasurable dharma-gates; one should understand the immeasurable dharma-gates; one should purify the immeasurable dharma-gates;
one should give rise to the light of immeasurable dharmas; one should perform the illumination of immeasurable dharmas; one should illuminate the faculties of immeasurable categories of beings;
one should know the diseases of immeasurable afflictions; one should collect the medicines of immeasurable sublime dharmas; and one should treat them.
One should, according to the measure of sentient beings, swiftly and diligently prepare immeasurable ambrosia;

one should proceed to immeasurable Buddha-lands to make offerings to immeasurable Tathāgatas; one should enter immeasurable assemblies of Bodhisattvas; one should receive the teachings of immeasurable Buddhas;
one should endure the offenses of immeasurable sentient beings; one should extinguish the hardships of immeasurable evil realms; and one should cause immeasurable... [to be fulfilled].
Sentient beings are born in the good realms; one should gather immeasurable sentient beings through the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*);
one should cultivate immeasurable doors of dhāraṇī; one should give rise to immeasurable doors of great vows; one should cultivate the power of immeasurable great compassion and great vows;

one should diligently seek immeasurable teachings without ever resting; one should give rise to immeasurable power of reflection; and one should give rise to immeasurable supernormal powers (*abhijñā*).
One should purify activities; one should manifest the light of immeasurable wisdom; one should proceed to the realms of immeasurable sentient beings;
one should undergo immeasurable births; one should manifest immeasurable distinct bodies; one should know immeasurable modes of speech and dharmas;
one should enter into immeasurable diverse minds; one should know the great domain of the bodhisattva; one should dwell in the great palace of the bodhisattva; one should contemplate the bodhi...

One should know the profound and wondrous Dharma of the Bodhisattvas; one should practice the difficult-to-know realms of the Bodhisattvas; one should perform the various difficult-to-practice deeds of the Bodhisattvas;
one should possess the honored majesty and virtue of the Bodhisattvas; one should tread upon the difficult-to-enter stage of correctness of the Bodhisattvas;

one should know the various types of practices of the Bodhisattvas; one should manifest the universal spiritual powers of the Bodhisattvas; and one should receive the impartial Dharma of the Bodhisattvas.
Clouds should fulfill the boundless web of practices of Bodhisattvas; clouds should fulfill the boundless perfections of Bodhisattvas;
clouds should receive the immeasurable predictions of enlightenment of Bodhisattvas; clouds should enter the immeasurable gates of patience of Bodhisattvas;

clouds should cultivate the immeasurable stages of Bodhisattvas; clouds should purify the immeasurable Dharma-gates of Bodhisattvas; and clouds should, together with all Bodhisattvas, dwell for boundless eons in making offerings.
They nurture immeasurable Buddhas and purify unspeakably many Buddha-lands; they give birth to unspeakably many bodhisattva vows.

Good sons, to state the essentials: one should universally cultivate all bodhisattva practices, universally transform all realms of sentient beings, universally enter all kalpas, universally be born in all places, and universally know all things.
The world should universally practice all dharmas; it should universally purify all buddha-lands; it should universally fulfill all vows;
it should universally make offerings to all buddhas; it should universally accord with the vows of all bodhisattvas; and it should universally serve all spiritual friends.
Son of good family, you should not grow weary in your quest for spiritual friends; upon seeing a spiritual friend, do not give rise to aversion.
One should respectfully inquire of spiritual friends; one should not shrink from toil or hardship in attending upon spiritual friends;
one should not harbor thoughts of regression; one should not cease making offerings to spiritual friends; one should not misinterpret the instructions received from spiritual friends;
one should not harbor doubts while learning the practices of spiritual friends; and one should not hesitate when seeing the spiritual friends expound the gateway to liberation.
One should follow the conduct of a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) even when it accords with the course of afflictions, and one should not give rise to aversion or suspicion.
One should develop a mind of deep faith and reverence toward the spiritual friend and must not allow it to change. Why is this?
Good son, it is because through a spiritual friend, a bodhisattva hears of all the practices of bodhisattvas, accomplishes all the merits of bodhisattvas, and gives birth to all bodhi.
The Great Vows of Samantabhadra: they give rise to all roots of goodness of Bodhisattvas; they accumulate all aids to the path of Bodhisattvas; they develop the light of all Bodhisattva dharmas;
they reveal all gates of transcendence for Bodhisattvas; they cause one to study and practice all pure precepts of Bodhisattvas;
they cause one to abide in all meritorious dharmas of Bodhisattvas; and they purify all Bodhisattvas... [text continues]... Bodhisattvas.
With vast resolve, he increases the steadfast mind of all bodhisattvas; he is fully endowed with all bodhisattva dhāraṇīs and doors of eloquence;
he attains the pure treasury of all bodhisattvas; he gives birth to the light of samādhi of all bodhisattvas;
he obtains the supreme vows of all bodhisattvas and shares a single vow with all bodhisattvas; he hears all...
The sublime dharma of bodhisattvas attains all secret stations of bodhisattvas; it reaches the island of the jewels of all bodhisattva dharmas;
it increases the sprouts of all bodhisattva roots of goodness; it causes the body of wisdom of all bodhisattvas to grow;
it protects the profound and secret treasury of all bodhisattvas; it sustains the mass of merit of all bodhisattvas; and it purifies the births of all bodhisattvas.
The path that receives the clouds of the true Dharma of all Bodhisattvas; enters the road of the great vows of all Bodhisattvas;
proceeds toward the fruit of the enlightenment of all Tathāgatas; gathers all the sublime practices of Bodhisattvas; reveals all the merits of Bodhisattvas;
travels to all directions to hear and receive the sublime Dharma; praises the vast majesty and virtue of all Bodhisattvas; and gives rise to a single...

By the power of the great compassion of all Bodhisattvas, they encompass the supreme sovereign power of all Bodhisattvas, give rise to all factors of enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*) of all Bodhisattvas, and perform all beneficial deeds for all Bodhisattvas.
Good son, by being sustained by spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), Bodhisattvas do not fall into the evil destinies;
by being taken into their care by spiritual friends, they do not regress from the Mahāyāna. By spiritual friends... [text continues].

One maintains mindfulness and does not violate the bodhisattva precepts through the protection of spiritual friends; one does not follow after evil associates through the protection of spiritual friends;

one nurtures the bodhisattva teachings without deficiency through the protection of spiritual friends; one is gathered and transcends the stage of ordinary beings through the protection of spiritual friends;
and one is taught and transcends the stages of the two vehicles through the instruction of spiritual friends. Thus do spiritual friends reveal [the path].
They lead one to transcendence from the world; they cause one to grow through spiritual friends so that one is not defiled by worldly dharmas;

they enable the cultivation of all bodhisattva practices through serving spiritual friends; they provide the possession of all factors conducive to enlightenment through making offerings to spiritual friends;
they ensure one is not overcome by karma and afflictions through intimacy with spiritual friends; and they provide reliance upon spiritual friends.
The power of consciousness is firm and steadfast, and one does not fear any māras.
This is because by relying on a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), one increases all factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*). Why is this?

Good son, a spiritual friend can purify all obscurations, can extinguish all sins, can eliminate all calamities, can cease all evils, can dispel the long night of darkness of ignorance, and can destroy all...
It is seen as a firm fortress capable of bringing forth escape from the city of birth and death; as a means to abandon the worldly home; as that which severs the nets of all Māras;

as that which extracts the arrows of manifold suffering; as that which leaves behind the perilous places of ignorance; as that which emerges from the great wilderness of false views; as that which crosses over the currents of existence;
as that which departs from all deviant paths; as that which shows the path to Bodhi; and as that which teaches the Dharma of the Bodhisattvas.
It causes one to dwell securely in the bodhisattva practices; it enables one to advance toward all-knowledge; it can purify the eye of wisdom; it can increase the bodhicitta;
it can give rise to great compassion; it can expound wondrous conduct; it can explain the pāramitās; it can banish evil associates;
it can cause one to abide in the various stages (bhūmis); it can cause one to attain the various patiences (kṣāntis); and it can cause one to cultivate and practice all roots of goodness.
It causes the accomplishment of all requisites; it enables the bestowal of all great merits;
it leads to the stage of omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*); it causes the joyful accumulation of merit; it inspires the enthusiastic cultivation of all practices;
it causes entry into the profound meaning; it causes the revelation of the gateway to liberation; and it causes the sealing off of all evil paths.
By means of the light of the Dharma, they can illuminate; by means of the rain of the Dharma, they can moisten and nourish;
they can cause all delusions to be extinguished, cause all views to be abandoned, cause all Buddha-wisdom to increase, and cause one to dwell securely in all Dharma-gates of the Buddhas.
Good son, a spiritual friend is like a compassionate mother, for they give birth to the seed of the Buddhas. Thus it is said.
He is like a compassionate father because he brings about vast benefit; like a nurse because he protects one from committing evil;
like a teacher because he demonstrates what a bodhisattva must study; like a skillful guide because he can show the path of the *pāramitās*;
like a skilled physician because he can cure the diseases of the afflictions (*kleśa*); like the Snowy Mountains because he increases the medicinal herbs of omniscience; and like a heroic general.
Because they utterly eliminate all fears, they are like those who rescue travelers; because they cause one to emerge from the torrential flood of birth and death, they are like boatmen;
because they cause one to reach the jewel-island of wisdom, they are like guides. Good son, you should always thus maintain right mindfulness and contemplate spiritual friends.
Furthermore, good son, in serving all spiritual friends, you should resolve to be like the great earth.
One should resolve upon a mind like a diamond, because it bears heavy burdens without weariness;
one should resolve upon a mind like Mount Cakravāḍa, because its vow is firm and indestructible;
one should resolve upon a mind like a servant, because it complies with all instructions; one should resolve upon a mind like a disciple... [all that is commanded].
Because one must not oppose instruction, one should develop a mind like that of a servant; because one must not grow weary of any task, one should develop a mind like that of a foster mother;
because one must not complain of hardship when undergoing toil, one should develop a mind like that of a hired laborer;

because one must not oppose whatever instructions are received, one should develop a mind like that of a man clearing away filth; because one must be free from arrogance... [one should develop such a mind].
One should generate a mind like ripened grain, for it is humble; one should generate a mind like a fine horse, for it is free from unruliness;
one should generate a mind like a great chariot, for it can carry heavy burdens; one should generate a mind like a well-trained elephant, for it is ever submissive;
one should generate a mind like Mount Sumeru, for it is unshakable; and one should generate a mind like a good dog, for it does no harm.
Because he is the Master, he should develop a mind like that of a caṇḍāla, being free from arrogance; because he is free from wrathful majesty, he should develop a mind like that of a castrated ox;
because he does not grow weary of coming and going, he should develop a mind like that of a boat; because he does not tire of ferrying others across, he should develop a mind like that of a bridge;
because he complies with and honors their countenance, he should develop a mind like that of a filial son; and he should develop a mind like that of a king.
Because you have followed and practiced these instructions with your heart, furthermore, son of good family, you should conceive the thought of yourself as being afflicted by illness,
the thought of the spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) as a king of physicians, the thought of the Dharma taught as excellent medicine,

and the thought of the practice undertaken as the removal of that illness. Furthermore, you should conceive the thought of yourself as one setting out on a long journey, and the thought of the spiritual friend as a guide.
The teacher should conceive of the Dharma being taught as the thought of the right path, and of the practice being cultivated as the thought of far-reaching attainment.
Furthermore, he should conceive of himself as one seeking deliverance; of the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) as a boatman; of the Dharma being taught as a vessel or oar;
and of the practice being cultivated as the thought of reaching the further shore. Moreover, he should conceive of himself as a crop.
One should conceive of the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) as a dragon king; of the Dharma taught as seasonal rain; and of one's own practice as the ripening [of crops].
Furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as being in poverty; of the spiritual friend as Vaiśravaṇa, the King of Wealth;
of the Dharma taught as wealth and treasure; and of one's own practice as abundant prosperity. Moreover—
One should conceive of oneself as a disciple, the spiritual friend as a skilled craftsman,
the Dharma taught as a craft, and the practice undertaken as its mastery. Furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as fearful,
the spiritual friend as a courageous warrior, the Dharma taught as a weapon, and the practice undertaken as...

While practicing, one should conceive the thought of destroying enmity; furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as a merchant, of the spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) as a guide, of the Dharma taught as precious treasure, and of the practice undertaken as the gathering of goods.
Furthermore, one should conceive of oneself as a son, of the spiritual friend as parents, and of the Dharma taught as...
One should conceive of one’s family business as the practice of the path; one should conceive of oneself as a prince;
one should conceive of the spiritual friend as a minister; one should conceive of the Dharma being taught as the king’s decree;
and one should conceive of the practice itself as donning the royal crown, wearing the royal robes, binding the royal fillet, and sitting upon the royal throne. Good son!
You should give rise to such a mind and form such an intention as to draw near to spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). Why is this?

Because by drawing near to spiritual friends with such a mind, one’s aspirations will attain eternal purity. Furthermore, son of good family, spiritual friends cause all roots of goodness (*kuśalamūla*) to grow;
they are like the Snowy Mountains (*Himavat*), which cause all medicinal herbs to grow. Spiritual friends are the Buddha.
A vessel for the Dharma is like the great ocean that swallows up all flowing streams;
a spiritual friend is a locus of merit, like the great ocean that produces all manner of jewels. A spiritual friend purifies the bodhicitta, like a fierce fire that can refine true gold.
A spiritual friend transcends worldly phenomena, like Mount Sumeru rising out from the great ocean. A spiritual friend...
The wise are unstained by worldly dharmas, just as the lotus flower is not defiled by water.

A spiritual friend does not accept any evils, just as the great ocean does not harbor a corpse. A spiritual friend increases pure dharmas (*śukla-dharma*), just as the white moon’s light and color reach fullness.
A spiritual friend illuminates the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), just as the blazing sun shines upon the four quarters.
The spiritual benefactors of the world cause the body of a bodhisattva to grow, just as parents nurture their children.

Good son, to speak of it in brief: if a bodhisattva mahāsattva can comply with the instructions of spiritual benefactors, they will attain ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of merits and purify ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of [qualities].
Through the profound resolve of others, they purify ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of bodhisattva faculties,
sever ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of bodhisattva powers, eliminate ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of asaṃkhyeyas of hindrances,
transcend ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of asaṃkhyeyas of demonic realms, and enter ten [unspeakable...]
One may speak of hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* Dharma-gates; one fulfills ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* aids to the Path;
one cultivates ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* sublime practices; and one brings forth ten unspeakable hundreds of thousands of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* great vows.
Good son, I have further briefly explained all these for the sake of the Bodhisattvas.
The practice of all bodhisattva pāramitās, all bodhisattva stages, all bodhisattva patiences,
all bodhisattva dhāraṇī-doors, all bodhisattva samādhi-doors, all bodhisattva supernormal knowledges and wisdoms,
all bodhisattva dedications, all bodhisattva vows, and the accomplishment of all Buddha-dharmas— all these arise from:
The power of spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) takes the spiritual friend as its root;

it is born from the spiritual friend, emerges from the spiritual friend, grows through the spiritual friend, and abides by the spiritual friend. The spiritual friend serves as the causal condition (pratyaya);
when the spiritual friend is able to inspire [one], the youth Sudhana heard of such merits of the spiritual friends that they are capable of revealing [the truth].
Having accomplished immeasurable sublime practices as bodhisattvas, they were able to achieve immeasurable and vast Buddha-dharmas;
leaping with joy, they prostrated at the feet of Śrīsaṃbhava and Guṇākara, circumambulated them countless times, gazed upon them with earnest devotion, and then took their leave and departed.
[Treatise] First, from the passage "O son of good family, to the south of here there is a land called Sāgara-garbha" down to "having paid his respects,
he departed," comprising approximately half a fascicle of the sutra, it describes how the youth Sudhana, through the virtuous girl Guṇavatī,
was led to contemplate the virtues of the Bodhisattva Maitreya, thereby enabling him to draw near to and advance toward [the goal]. This section follows the [preceding] excellence.
To the south of this land, there is a country named "Seashore" (*Sāgara-paryanta*). This signifies that one has advanced upward to reach the fruit of Buddhahood in a single lifetime under Maitreya;
thus it is called "Seashore," as one enters the ocean of Buddha-wisdom while standing on the brink of the ocean of birth-and-death (*saṃsāra*).
Furthermore, because this country is situated by the sea, there is a grove there named "Great Adornment" (*Mahā-vyūha*), which is established in relation to Maitreya.
Dwelling with birth and death as its garden and the myriad practices as its forest, one’s own Buddha-fruit of wisdom and compassion is already fully perfected;

this is called the "Great Ornament" (*mahāvyūha*). Within it stands a vast multi-storied pavilion named the "Vairocana-Ornament-Treasury" (*vairocanavyūhakośa*), so named because it manifests the essential nature of both fundamental wisdom and its differentiated wisdoms, arising as a result of maturation.

Therefore, Vairocana is called "Various Radiances" and Samantaprabha is called "Universal Illumination. Various radiances refer to the wisdom of differentiation (*pravicaya-jñāna*), while universal illumination refers to the fundamental wisdom (*mūla-jñāna*).
These two wisdoms are designated as names based on their functions, yet their essence and function are one. In total, there is no creator;
it is by means of this Dharmadhātu—its essence and function—the Wisdom of Universal Radiance, that all myriad phenomena are accomplished.
Because it performs vast benefit for all living beings as a recompense for their births, this Great Adorned Pavilion is vast in measure,
equal to empty space; all worlds and sentient beings dwell within it, cohabiting and moving about therein without being aware of it or knowing it,
just as when the youth Sudhana entered this pavilion and saw both pure and impure worlds.
The great trichiliocosm, the intermediate thousandfold world-system, and even the abodes of hell-beings, animals, and hungry ghosts,
as well as all the various matters throughout the worlds of the ten directions— whether they contain Buddhas or not, including the assemblies of bodhisattvas—
are all contained therein, as extensively described in the sutras; for the ocean of the Buddha’s wisdom, through its great compassion, embraces all beings.
Sustained by the great vows to benefit sentient beings through myriad practices, they together form the substance of this pavilion.

Abiding within the garden of birth and death for all sentient beings, the forest of myriad practices provides shade and shelter for all conscious beings, causing them all to eternally attain the bliss of the pure, stainless, and clear wisdom of the white Dharma-body. As the Sūtra says: "From the fruit and retribution of the Bodhisattva’s roots of goodness..."
Birth arises from skillful means; birth arises from merit and wisdom. Birth has no place of origin, and cessation has no place of departure;
all are like illusory wisdom abiding in the marks of arising and ceasing.

This is just as sentient beings are born and cease through karma, having no coming or going, and no substantial nature or characteristics that can be grasped or discarded, nor any joy or aversion. As the Sūtra says: "Good son..."

The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Subhavyūha, dwelling in the inconceivable liberation, out of great compassion manifested such a realm for the sake of all sentient beings and assembled such adornments; having established Maitreya Bodhisattva therein, it is explained at length as in the sutra.
From this first section, it is further divided into five parts: First, "O son of good family... [and so forth].
To the south of here, there is a land called Sāgaratīra... [down to] "For what reason? Son of good family, that bodhisattva mahāsattva...

This section, which clearly indicates the location of the spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) and exhorts one to go to him to inquire about the Dharma-gate, consists of twenty and a half lines of scripture and is divided into two parts. Why is this? Son of good family, that bodhisattva mahāsattva...

From the section below, which begins with "Furthermore, O son of good family, a bodhisattva should plant immeasurable roots of goodness" and continues down to "should [serve spiritual friends]," there are fourteen lines of scripture that clarify the deeds of the Bodhisattva dwelling on the tenth stage in purifying buddha-fields and serving spiritual friends;
this is the section titled "The Bright Virtue of the Youth Mingde (Vimalakīrti) Praising the Virtues of Maitreya and Urging Sudhana to Approach and Serve Him," which is divided into three parts.
Why is this? [Because... O son of good family, a bodhisattva should plant immeasurable roots of goodness... and so forth.

Regarding the "Universal Service to All Spiritual Friends," there are forty-nine and a half lines of scripture that clarify the vast dharmas that the youth Sudhana should learn and practice as taught by the youth Meghaśrī. This section is divided into four parts:
(1) "O son of good family, you should not grow weary in your quest for spiritual friends," and so on, down to (4) "increasing all bodhi-dharmas."

This section consists of thirty-four lines of sūtra that clarify the manner in which the youth Mingde (Vimalakīrti) instructed Sudhana in the matter of serving spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), not observing their faults, and not becoming weary; it shows how one obtains immeasurable benefits through spiritual friends.
It is divided into five parts. Why is this? "Good son, spiritual friends are those who can purify all obstacles," and so on, down to...

Having taken his leave and departed, there are eighty-nine lines of sūtra explaining the Bodhisattva Mingde (Vimalatejas) teaching the method for honoring spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), as well as the section on how one achieves the vast Buddha-dharma through a spiritual friend. As the sūtra says:
"One should not practice the six perfections with a limited mind, nor dwell in the ten stages or purify Buddha-fields while serving a spiritual friend."
Those who possess knowledge clarify that the six perfections and ten stages are all but a single portion of the supramundane;
because their pure vision has not yet been extinguished, they are obstructed by this and have not yet fulfilled the practices of Samantabhadra.

Thus, they differ from the causal and resultant realm of the *saṃbhogakāya* of Vairocana Tathāgata, and instead attain only what is identical to the supramundane *nirmāṇakāya* and *nairmāṇikabuddha*. [This is] through the *saṃbhogakāya* of Vairocana.
The body of merit, which is the ocean of the fruits of marks, is adorned with a flower crown, necklaces, bracelets, and various ornaments—an ocean of blessings that embellishes the body.

This is not a body that has emerged from bondage by discarding all finery out of weariness with birth and death; rather, it is the realm of the great wisdom of the *dharmadhātu*, having reached the fundamental source of ignorance.
It is the *saṃbhogakāya* naturally endowed with boundless merit, further augmented by the practices of Samantabhadra.

Because the body of retribution for merit is adorned by the mutual interplay of infinite merits accomplished through the wisdom that discerns the distinctions within the ocean of vows, the virtues of the fulfillment of the eleventh stage arise.

Thus, the fundamental essence of the fruit—the teaching of the youth Sudhana to enter the gateway of the Dharma-realm—does not follow after or lead toward conventional spheres of transformation; it abides in pure vision, free from the limitations of conditioned practice.
The other sections of the chapter are explained in detail as in the sutra. Since this is the realm of the *nirmāṇakāya* Buddha, it is the gateway to the supramundane.

It is said that there are distinct pure lands in other directions; however, from the perspective of the *saṃbhogakāya* Buddha, the ten directions are taken as a single pure land, without distinguishing between the pure and the impure.
[Sūtra] At that time, the youth Sudhana, his mind moistened by the instructions of the spiritual friend, reflected with right mindfulness upon the practices of all bodhisattvas.
As he headed toward the country of Sāgaratīra, he recalled how in past lives he had failed to cultivate respectful salutation; immediately, he resolved to practice with diligent effort.
He further recalled how in past lives his body and mind had been impure; immediately, he resolved to focus exclusively on purifying himself.
Furthermore, recollecting the various evil karmas committed in past lives, he immediately resolved to vigilantly guard against and sever them;
recollecting the various deluded thoughts arising in past lives, he immediately resolved to always maintain right reflection;

recollecting that the various practices cultivated in past lives were solely for his own sake, he immediately resolved to expand his mind so that it might reach all sentient beings; and recollecting past lives...

Pursuing the objects of desire, one constantly squanders and exhausts oneself without finding any true flavor; immediately, one resolves to practice the Buddha-dharma to nourish the faculties and achieve personal peace.
Furthermore, recollecting past lives of engaging in perverse thoughts associated with delusion, one immediately resolves to give rise to a mind of right view and form the vows of a bodhisattva.
Moreover, recollecting past lives of toiling day and night, [one resolves to cultivate diligence].
Upon committing various evil deeds, they immediately resolve their minds and arouse great vigor to accomplish the Buddha-dharma;

furthermore, recollecting how they have undergone births within the five destinies throughout past lives, they realize that these bodies—both their own and those of others—have brought no benefit at all.

Thereupon, they immediately resolve their minds, wishing to benefit sentient beings with these very bodies and accomplish the Buddha-dharma by serving all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra). Thus they reflect.
Experiencing great joy, he further contemplates this body as a dwelling place for the manifold sufferings of birth, old age, sickness, and death;

he vows to cultivate the Bodhisattva path throughout all future kalpas to transform sentient beings, to behold all Tathāgatas and bring their Buddha-dharma to fulfillment, to travel through all Buddha-fields,
to serve all Dharma masters, to uphold all Buddha-teachings, and to seek out all [truths].

When Dharma companions see all spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), practice all Buddha-dharmas, and perceive them as the causal conditions for the body of the vows and wisdom of all bodhisattvas, they form this thought:
"For an inconceivable and immeasurable length of time, these roots of goodness have been cultivated.
Thereupon, they conceive a sense of wonder toward all bodhisattvas, regarding them with deep faith and respect, perceiving them as great teachers, and their faculties become purified.
The increase of wholesome dharmas; the arising of all Bodhisattvas’ respectful offerings; the performing of all Bodhisattvas’ bowing with palms joined;
the birth of all Bodhisattvas’ universal eye that beholds the world; the arising of all Bodhisattvas’ thought of universally mindful regard for sentient beings;
the manifestation of all Bodhisattvas’ immeasurable vow-bodies; and the emergence of all Bodhisattvas’ pure praises.

In this discourse on sound and perception, one perceives all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the past and present manifesting the attainment of enlightenment and supernatural transformations in all places,
such that there is not even a single hair-tip’s breadth where they do not pervade.
Furthermore, having attained the eye of the light of pure wisdom, one sees the spheres of activity of all Bodhisattvas, and their mind universally enters the ten [directions].
The network of their buddha-fields pervades the entirety of space and the dharma-realm, equal throughout the three periods of time without ceasing;
all of this is brought about solely by their faithful acceptance of the instructions of spiritual friends.
[Treatise] Second: At that time, after the youth Sudhana had his mind moistened by the instruction of the spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*),
down to the point where it says "all this is brought about by the faithful acceptance of the spiritual friend's instruction," thirty lines of scripture clarify how Sudhana,
reflecting upon his own past causes, transgressions, and unwholesome deeds, gives rise to self-reproach, shame, and regret.
The section on reverently making offerings to and attending upon spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*) is clear from the text itself.
[Sūtra] Sudhana, with such reverence, such offerings, such praise, such observation,
such power of aspiration, such reflection, and such immeasurable sphere of wisdom, [approached] Vairocana...
Before the Great Pavilion of the Adorned Treasury of Vairocana, he prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground, briefly withdrawing his thoughts to contemplate and observe.
By virtue of his profound faith, understanding, and the power of his great vows, he entered the gate of the wisdom-body that is equal in all places;
he manifested his body everywhere before all Tathāgatas, before all Bodhisattvas, and before all virtuous ones.
Before all stūpas and shrines of the Tathāgatas; before all images of the Tathāgatas;
before all abodes of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; before all precious Dharmas; before all Śrāvakas, Pratyekabuddhas, and their stūpas and shrines;
before all fields of merit consisting of the assembly of noble ones; and before all parents and venerable elders.
Before the assemblies of beings in the ten directions, as previously described, they are honored, revered, and praised without ceasing until the end of the future;

because they are equal to space in their boundless measure; because they are equal to the *dharmadhātu* in their lack of obstruction; because they are equal to the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*) in their pervasiveness of all things;
because they are equal to the Tathāgata in their non-discrimination; because they appear according to wisdom like a shadow; and because they arise from [conditions] like a dream.
Because they arise from thought, they are like reflections; because they manifest to all, they are like echoes;
because they are produced by conditions, they have no birth; because they undergo successive arising and passing away, they have no intrinsic nature;
and because they revolve according to conditions, one definitively knows that all retributions arise from karma, all fruits arise from causes, and all karmas arise from habitual tendencies. One.
The arising of all Buddhas proceeds from faith; all manifested acts of offering proceed from resolute understanding;
all manifested Buddhas arise from a heart of reverence; all Buddha-dharmas arise from roots of goodness;
all transformation bodies arise from skillful means; all Buddha-activities arise from great vows; [and so it is for] all Bodhisattvas...
Cultivating all practices arises from dedication; the vast adornment of the entire dharma-realm arises from the sphere of omniscience.
Because one knows dedication, one is free from the view of nihilism; because one knows non-arising, one is free from the view of eternalism;

because one knows the correct cause, one is free from the view of causelessness; because one knows reality as it is, one is free from the view of inversion; and one is free from the view of a creator lord.
One knows that [knowledge] does not arise from another, and thus abandons the view of self and other; one knows that it arises from conditions, and thus abandons the view of extreme positions;
one knows that the dharma-realm is boundless, and thus abandons the view of coming and going; one knows that it is like a reflection, and thus abandons the view of existence and non-existence;
one knows that it is without arising or ceasing, and thus abandons the view of all phenomena; one knows that it is not autonomous, and thus knows the power of vows.
Because of birth, one is free from all marks and enters the limit of the signless;

because one knows that all phenomena arise like seeds producing sprouts, like seals producing impressions, one knows that substance is like an image, sound is like an echo, objects are like dreams, and karma is like an illusion;
one realizes that the world is a manifestation of the mind, that results arise from causes, and understands the nature of retributive karma.
Because of his practice, he thoroughly understands that all dharmas of merit flow forth from the skillful means (*upāyakauśalya*) of the bodhisattva.
[Treatise: Third, after Sudhana had paid such respect and made such offerings, down to...
Since all these arise from the skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) of the Bodhisattva, there are thirty-two lines of verse clarifying how Sudhana,
before the pavilion, prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground, briefly concentrated his mind in contemplation,
and thereby obtained immeasurable benefit, as clearly detailed in the text.
[Sūtra] The youth Sudhana entered into such wisdom; with an upright mind and pure mindfulness, he prostrated himself before the pavilion, bowing his entire body in earnest veneration.
An inconceivable flow of roots of goodness permeated his body and mind, which became cool, refreshed, and radiant.

Rising from the ground, he gazed up at [the pavilion] with single-minded devotion, not for a moment averting his eyes. Joining his palms, he circumambulated it for immeasurable circuits, and while doing so, he spoke thus:
He thought to himself: "This great celestial palace is the dwelling place of those who have realized emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
it is the dwelling place of those who are non-discriminative regarding all phenomena; it is the dwelling place of those who understand that the dharma-realm is without differentiation;
it is the dwelling place of those who know that all sentient beings are ungraspable; it is the dwelling place of those who know the One..."
The dwelling place of those for whom all phenomena are unarisen; the dwelling place of those who do not cling to any world;
the dwelling place of those who do not cling to any cave-dwelling; the dwelling place of those who do not delight in any village;
the dwelling place of those who do not rely on any objective sphere; it is the state of being free from [duality].
It is the dwelling place of those who have eliminated all conceptualization; it is the dwelling place of those who know that all phenomena lack intrinsic nature;
it is the dwelling place of those who have severed all karmic activities of discrimination;
it is the dwelling place of those who are free from all notions of mind, thought, and consciousness; it is the dwelling place of those who neither enter nor exit any path; it is the entrance.
The dwelling place of all those who possess the profound *prajñāpāramitā*;
the dwelling place of those who are able to abide in the universal gate of the *dharmadhātu* through skillful means; the dwelling place of those who extinguish the fires of all afflictions;
and the dwelling place of those who, by means of superior wisdom, sever all views, cravings, and pride.
This is the dwelling place of those who sport in all meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), samādhis, supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), and clarities (*vidyā*).
It is the dwelling place of those who observe the spheres of all bodhisattva samādhis.
It is the dwelling place of those who abide in the presence of all Tathāgatas. It is that which enters a single eon into all eons, and by means of all...
The dwelling place of those who enter one eon into another eon without destroying its characteristics;
the dwelling place of those who enter all lands into one land and one land into all lands without destroying their characteristics;
and the dwelling place of those who enter all phenomena into one phenomenon and one phenomenon into all phenomena without destroying their characteristics.

This is the dwelling place of those who, by means of a single sentient being, enter into all sentient beings, and by means of all sentient beings, enter into a single sentient being, without destroying their respective characteristics;

this is the dwelling place of those who, by means of a single Buddha, enter into all Buddhas, and by means of all Buddhas, enter into a single Buddha, without destroying their respective characteristics; this is, at [this]...
The dwelling place of those who, in a single thought-moment, know all that exists throughout the three periods of time;
the dwelling place of those who, in a single thought-moment, travel to all lands; the dwelling place of those who manifest their bodies before all sentient beings;
the dwelling place of those whose minds constantly benefit all worlds.

This is the dwelling place of those who are able to reach all places; it is the dwelling place of those who, though they have already transcended all worlds, constantly manifest their bodies therein for the sake of transforming sentient beings;
it is the dwelling place of those who do not cling to any land, yet travel through all lands in order to make offerings to all Buddhas. It is not...
This is the dwelling place of those who, from their own fundamental station, are able to travel universally to all Buddha-fields to adorn them;
it is the dwelling place of those who draw near to all Buddhas yet do not give rise to the notion of "Buddha";

it is the dwelling place of those who rely upon all spiritual friends yet do not give rise to the notion of "spiritual friend"; it is the dwelling place of those who abide within all the palaces of Māra.
It is the dwelling place of those who do not cling to the realms of desire; it is the dwelling place of those who have forever abandoned all mental conceptions;
it is the dwelling place of those who, though manifesting their bodies among all sentient beings, give rise to no dualistic notions of self and other;
and it is the dwelling place of those who are able to universally enter all worlds while remaining [unmoved] regarding phenomena.

This is the dwelling place of those who possess the perception of no distinction between realms; this is the dwelling place of those who vow to abide through all future kalpas yet maintain no perception of length or brevity regarding those kalpas;
this is the dwelling place of those who, without departing from the tip of a single hair, manifest their bodies throughout all worlds;
this is the dwelling place of those who are able to expound the Dharma that is difficult to encounter.

This is the dwelling place of those who abide in the dharma that is difficult to know, the profoundly deep dharma, the non-dual dharma, the signless dharma, the dharma without antidote, the dharma of non-apprehension, and the dharma free from conceptual proliferation; it is the dwelling place of those who abide in great loving-kindness and great compassion;
it is the dwelling place of those who have already transcended the wisdom of all followers of the two vehicles and have surpassed all Māras.
This is the dwelling place of those who have already transcended worldly dharmas without being stained by them, who have reached the shore attained by Bodhisattvas,
and who abide in the station of the Tathāgatas; it is the abode of those who, though detached from all marks, do not enter the fixed stage of the Śrāvakas, and who,
though they understand that all phenomena are unarisen, do not dwell in the nature of non-arising.
This is the dwelling place of one who, although contemplating impurity, does not realize the dharma of freedom from greed and yet is not accompanied by desire;
who, although cultivating loving-kindness, does not realize the dharma of freedom from hatred and yet is not accompanied by the defilement of anger;

and who, although contemplating dependent origination, does not realize the dharma of freedom from delusion and yet is not accompanied by the confusion of ignorance—this is the dwelling place of such a person. Although they dwell [therein]...

One who dwells in the four dhyānas yet is not reborn according to those dhyānas; who practices the four immeasurables for the sake of transforming sentient beings yet is not reborn in the realm of form;
who cultivates the four formless absorptions yet, out of great compassion, does not abide in the formless realm—this is the dwelling place of such a person.
Although they diligently cultivate śamatha and vipaśyanā for the sake of transforming sentient beings, they do not realize final liberation.
The dwelling place of one who practices equanimity yet does not abandon the work of transforming sentient beings;

the dwelling place of one who contemplates emptiness yet does not give rise to views of emptiness, who practices signlessness yet constantly transforms sentient beings attached to signs, and who practices wishlessness yet does not abandon the vows and practices for enlightenment; the dwelling place of one who, regarding all karma and afflictions...
Having attained mastery within the middle way, they manifest in accordance with various karmas and afflictions for the sake of transforming sentient beings;
though they are free from birth and death, they manifest the experience of birth and death for the sake of transforming sentient beings;

though they have already departed from all realms of existence, they manifest entry into those realms for the sake of transforming sentient beings—this is the dwelling place of such a one. Although they practice loving-kindness toward all beings...
This is the dwelling place of one who, though born without objects of attachment, practices compassion yet remains without grasping toward sentient beings;
who, though practicing sympathetic joy, constantly regards suffering beings with a heart of pity; who, though practicing equanimity, does not abandon the work of benefiting others;
and who, though practicing the nine successive meditative attainments, never grows weary of or turns away from desire.
Although they know that all phenomena are without arising or ceasing within the realms of rebirth, they do not realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).

Although they enter the three gates of liberation, they do not take up the liberation of the śrāvakas. Although they contemplate the four noble truths, they do not abide in the fruits of the Lesser Vehicle.
Although they contemplate profound dependent origination, they do not abide in ultimate quiescence. Although they cultivate the eight...

Though practicing the Noble Path, they do not seek permanent transcendence from the world; though they have transcended the stage of ordinary beings, they do not fall into the stages of Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas;

though they contemplate the five aggregates of clinging, they do not bring about the eternal extinction of the aggregates; though they have surpassed the four Māras, they do not discriminate among them;
though they do not cling to the six sense bases, they do not bring about the eternal extinction of the six sense bases; though they abide in the truth...
While remaining as such, he does not fall into the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); though he teaches all vehicles, he does not abandon the Great Vehicle.
This great celestial palace is the dwelling place of those who abide in all such merits.
At that time, the youth Sudhana spoke these verses:
[Treatise] The fourth section, from "The youth Sudhana entered such wisdom, his mind upright and his thoughts pure" down to the eighty stanzas spoken by Sudhana,
clarifies the portion on Sudhana’s praise of the pavilions where the spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) reside;
this is self-evident according to the text.
