Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a śramaṇa from the Kingdom of Khotan during the Tang Dynasty.
The Treatise composed by Li Tongxuan, Elder of Fangshan in Taiyuan, Tang Dynasty;
the Sūtra edited and the Treatise combined by the Śramaṇa Zhining of Kaiyuan Monastery in Fuzhou, Tang Dynasty;
Chapter Thirty-nine through Forty of the "Entering the Dharma Realm" (Gandavyūha).
[Sūtra] This is the Great Compassionate One of Pure Wisdom, the Honored Maitreya who benefits the world;
the eldest son of the Buddhas on the stage of consecration (*abhiṣeka*), who has entered the dwelling place of the Tathāgata’s realm.
All these sons of the Buddhas of universal renown have already entered the gate of liberation of the Mahāyāna.
Wandering through the dharma-realm with a mind free from attachment—this is the dwelling place of those who are peerless.
Giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditation, wisdom, skillful means, vows, power, and supernormal knowledges:
this is the dwelling place of those who are fully endowed with all such Mahāyāna perfections.
Your wisdom is as vast as space; you universally know all phenomena of the three times without obstruction, dependence, or grasping.
You thoroughly understand the abodes of those in existence and are skillfully able to comprehend all phenomena as being without intrinsic nature, unarisen, and without support.
Like a bird flying through the sky with mastery, this is the dwelling place of the great wise one.
Having realized the true nature of the three poisons, they discern that causes and conditions arise falsely;
yet they do not seek liberation out of aversion toward them—this is the dwelling place of the person of tranquility.

The three gates of liberation and the eightfold noble path, The aggregates, bases, elements, and dependent origination— They are able to observe all these without entering into quiescence. This is the dwelling place of those skilled in means;
They observe all lands and sentient beings in the ten directions With unimpeded wisdom.
Realizing that all natures are empty, they do not engage in discrimination; this is the dwelling place of those who abide in tranquility.
They practice throughout the entire dharma-realm without any obstruction, yet the nature of their practice cannot be apprehended.
Like the wind moving through space, there is nowhere it travels; this is the dwelling place of those who have no dependence.

Beholding everywhere the multitudes of beings in the evil realms, Who undergo all manner of agonizing torments with no place of refuge— He emits the great light of compassion to utterly extinguish them; This is the dwelling place of the one who feels such pity.
Seeing all sentient beings have lost the right path, They are like those born blind treading upon a perilous road.
He leads them into the city of liberation; this is the dwelling place of the Great Guide.

Seeing all sentient beings caught in the net of Māra, constantly oppressed by birth, old age, sickness, and death, he brings them liberation and provides them with consolation; this is the dwelling place of the Valiant Hero.
Seeing all sentient beings afflicted by the disease of delusion, he gives rise to a vast heart of compassion;
with the medicine of wisdom, he completely eradicates it—this is the dwelling place of the Great King of Physicians.
Seeing all living beings drowning in the ocean of existence, sinking and overwhelmed by distress as they endure manifold sufferings.
They rescue all by means of the Dharma-ship; this is the dwelling place of those who are skilled in crossing over.
Seeing all sentient beings within the ocean of delusion, they are able to give rise to the wondrous jewel-mind of bodhicitta and enter therein to deliver them;
this is the dwelling place of those who are skilled fishermen.
With eyes of great compassion and constant vows, He universally beholds all sentient beings And draws them forth from the ocean of existence.
This abode of the Golden-Winged King is like the sun and moon in the void; No demons of any world can obstruct it.
The radiance of wisdom is likewise so; this is the dwelling place of the Illuminator of the World.
To transform even a single sentient being, the Bodhisattva remains throughout all future eons as infinite as they may be;
as it is for one person, so it is for all—this is the dwelling place of the Savior of the World.
In a single land, they transform sentient beings, Without rest throughout all kalpas until the end of the future;
In every land it is thus. This is the dwelling place of the firm resolve.
The Dharma taught by the Buddhas of the ten directions, They receive in its entirety upon a single seat.
Thus it shall always be throughout all kalpas of the future; this is the dwelling place of those who possess the ocean of wisdom.

They travel everywhere through all oceans of worlds, universally enter all oceans of sites of enlightenment, and make offerings to all oceans of Tathāgatas; this is the dwelling place of these practitioners.
Practicing an ocean of all sublime conducts, Arousing an ocean of boundless great vows,
Thus passing through oceans of many eons— This is the dwelling place of those with such merit.
Within a single hair-tip are immeasurable lands, Where Buddhas, sentient beings, and eons are unspeakable.
Thus clearly seeing all things without exception—this is the dwelling place of the unimpeded eye.
In a single thought-moment, they universally encompass boundless eons;
Regarding the lands, the Buddhas, and sentient beings, their wisdom is unimpeded and knows them all correctly— this is the dwelling place of the person endowed with virtue.
The lands of the ten directions are ground into dust, and all the great oceans are measured by drops from a single hair;

such is the number of vows made by the Bodhisattva. This is the dwelling place of those who are unimpeded, where they achieve the gates of dhāraṇī and samādhi, as well as their great vows, meditative absorptions, and liberations.
Each one abides for boundless eons; this is the dwelling place of the true sons of the Buddha.

These immeasurable and boundless sons of the Buddha teach the Dharma in various ways to deliver sentient beings, and they also teach all the worldly arts and crafts; this is the dwelling place of those who practice.
Having accomplished the wisdom of skillful means regarding the supernormal powers, they practice the wondrous Dharma-gate that is like an illusion;
manifesting birth throughout the five destinies of the ten directions, this is the dwelling place of those who are unimpeded.
From the very first moment of generating the mind of enlightenment, these Bodhisattvas fully cultivate all practices.
Emanations are infinite, pervading the entire Dharma-realm; this is the dwelling place of one possessed of such supernormal power.

In a single thought-moment, the path to enlightenment is perfected; universally performing boundless deeds of wisdom, the conceptual thoughts of worldly beings go mad. This is the dwelling place of the One who is immeasurable.
Having accomplished unimpeded supernormal powers, they travel throughout the dharma-realm without exception;
their minds never grasp at anything attained—this is the dwelling place of those with pure wisdom.
Bodhisattvas cultivate unobstructed wisdom, entering all lands without attachment.
Illuminating all with non-dual wisdom, this is the dwelling place of those who are selfless;
Thoroughly knowing that all phenomena lack any basis of support, their original nature is quiescent like space.
Constantly practicing within such a sphere of experience—this is the dwelling place of those who are free from defilement.

Universally beholding all sentient beings undergoing various sufferings, They give rise to a mind of great compassion, benevolence, and wisdom, vowing to constantly benefit all worlds. This is the dwelling place of those who possess pity;
here the Sons of the Buddha reside, Appearing before all beings everywhere, Just like the orbs of the sun and the moon.
Universally dispelling the darkness of birth and death, the sons of the Buddha dwell here;
Manifesting infinite bodies in accordance with the minds of all sentient beings, they fill the lands of the ten directions.
The sons of the Buddha dwell here, traveling throughout all worlds To the presence of all Tathāgatas for immeasurable and innumerable eons.

The Buddha-sons dwelling here contemplate all the Buddha-dharmas; throughout immeasurable and incalculable eons, their minds never grow weary. The Buddha-sons dwelling here enter samādhi in every thought-moment;
through each and every gate of samādhi, they illuminate the realm of all Buddhas. The Buddha-sons dwelling here...
Fully knowing all lands and immeasurable, innumerable eons, the sons of the Buddha dwell here;

in a single thought-moment they encompass all kalpas. Following only the minds of sentient beings, they are free from discriminatory thoughts; the sons of the Buddha dwelling here cultivate all samādhis.
Within each and every thought-moment, they thoroughly know the phenomena of the three periods of time.
The sons of the Buddha dwell here, their bodies unmoving in the full lotus posture, yet they universally manifest in all lands.
The sons of the Buddha dwell here within all realms of existence, drinking from the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas and deeply entering the ocean of wisdom.

The sons of the Buddha dwell here, endowed with an ocean of merit; they fully know the number of all lands, the number of eons, and the number of sentient beings, as well as the number of Buddhas’ names.
Dwelling here, these sons of the Buddha can comprehend in a single thought all the formations and destructions of lands throughout the three periods of time.
The Buddha-sons dwelling here universally know the practices and vows of the Buddhas;

they know the practices cultivated by Bodhisattvas, as well as the faculties, natures, and desires of all sentient beings. The Buddha-sons dwelling here see within a single atom infinite lands and sites of enlightenment, as well as sentient beings and all kalpas, as if they were within a single atom.
All atoms are likewise so, Each endowed with every variety; Everywhere there is no obstruction.
The Son of the Buddha dwelling here Universally contemplates all phenomena: Sentient beings, lands, and worlds— Neither arising nor existing.
He observes that sentient beings are equal, That phenomena are equal, And that they are equal to the Tathāgata.
The buddha-fields, the various vows, and so forth— All are entirely equal throughout the three periods of time.
Buddha-sons dwelling herein teach and transform all living beings And make offerings to all Tathāgatas.
Contemplating the nature of all phenomena for immeasurable thousands of millions of eons, The practices of their cultivated vows and wisdom Are vast and beyond measure.
Their praises can never be fully told; those great heroes act without obstruction.
Abiding within this state, I join my palms in reverent salutation to the eldest son of all Buddhas, the noble and virtuous Maitreya.
I now pay homage with devotion; may you look upon me with compassion.
[Treatise] The above eighty-nine stanzas are a reiteration by the youth Sudhana of the preceding account of the pavilion dwelling where the Bodhisattva Maitreya resides,
as well as a praise of the Bodhisattva Maitreya’s virtues, all clearly explained according to the text.

[Sūtra] At that time, the youth Sudhana, having praised all the bodhisattvas within the Great Stūpa of Vairocana’s Adorned Treasury with such immeasurable dharmas of praise and eulogy for bodhisattvas,
bowed his body, joined his palms, and paid respectful homage; with a single-minded resolve, he wished to see Maitreya Bodhisattva and draw near to him to make offerings.
He saw the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya coming from another place, preceded by immeasurable devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas,
asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, kings of the Śakras, Brahmās, and World-Protectors,
along with immeasurable retinues from their places of birth, multitudes of brahmins, and other countless hundreds of thousands of beings.
Afterwards, they surrounded him and came together toward the Great Tower of the Treasury of Adornments.

Upon seeing it, Sudhana leaped for joy and prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground. At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva observed Sudhana, pointed him out to the great assembly, praised his meritorious virtues, and spoke these verses:
"Behold you, Sudhana, whose wisdom and mind are pure; Having come to my presence to seek the practice of enlightenment, Welcome, O one perfected in compassion! Welcome, O one of pure mercy!
Welcome, O one with eyes of tranquility! You who practice without weariness, Welcome, O one of pure intention!"
Welcome, you of vast and noble mind; welcome, you whose faculties never regress. Welcome, you who practice without weariness;

welcome, you of unwavering conduct. You who constantly seek out virtuous friends, who thoroughly understand all phenomena, and who subdue all living beings—welcome, you who walk the wondrous path; welcome, you who abide in merit.
Welcome, you who have set out for the fruit of Buddhahood; You have never known weariness. Welcome, you whose essence is virtue;
Welcome, nourished by the Dharma. Welcome, you of boundless conduct; Difficult to behold in this world. Welcome, free from delusion;
The worldly dharmas cannot stain you— Gain and loss, defamation and praise, and the like.
Completely free from conceptual discrimination, you come to bestow peace and happiness;
With minds made supple and ready for transformation, all deceit, flattery, anger, and pride are entirely extinguished. Welcome, true sons of the Buddha!
You travel everywhere throughout the ten directions, Increasing all merits, supple and free from weariness.
Welcome, you who possess the wisdom of the three times, who thoroughly know all phenomena,
and who universally give rise to a treasury of merit through tireless cultivation. Mañjuśrī, Guṇamegha, and all other sons of the Buddhas,
have brought you to my presence to show you the realm of non-obstruction, where you may fully practice the bodhisattva path.
Universally gathering all living beings— such a great person as you has now come to my presence to seek the pure realm of all Tathāgatas. You have come to me to inquire about the vast vows,
and regarding the various deeds and practices accomplished by the Buddhas of the past, future, and present.

Since you have come to me wishing to practice and study all things, and since you seek the subtle and wondrous Dharma from a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), desiring to receive the bodhisattva conduct, you have come to me.
You should keep in mind that spiritual friends are praised by all Buddhas; they shall cause you to attain awakening (*bodhi*).

And have come to my presence. You should remember your spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), who has given birth to me like a parent and nurtured me like a nurse; who increases my factors of enlightenment (bodhipakṣadharma);
who is like a physician for all ailments, like the heavens showering nectar, like the sun revealing the right path, and like the moon turning the pure wheel.
Unshakable like a mountain, Without increase or decrease like the ocean, Like a mariner who has come to ferry others across, you have arrived at my side. Behold this spiritual friend:
He is like a great and valiant general, Like a great caravan leader, And like a great guide, Able to raise the banner of the True Dharma.
It can manifest the virtues of the Buddhas; it can extinguish all evil realms; it can open the gates to the happy destinies;
it can reveal the bodies of all Buddhas; it can guard the treasuries of all Buddhas; it can uphold the teachings of all Buddhas.
Therefore, I pray that you will look upon me with favor. Desiring to fulfill pure wisdom, and desiring to possess a body of perfect form, [I seek this].
Desiring to be born into a noble family, you have come to my presence. You all should observe this person who has drawn near to a spiritual friend;
following what he practices and studies, you should all act in accordance with it.
By virtue of past causes and conditions of merit, Mañjuśrī has caused you to resolve upon the mind of enlightenment; follow him in harmony, without opposition.
Practicing without weariness, one renounces parents, relatives, palaces, and all wealth;
with humility, one seeks out wise teachers. Purifying the mind in this way and forever leaving behind the worldly body, one shall be born in a Buddha-land and receive all supreme rewards.
Seeing sentient beings suffering from birth, old age, sickness, and death, Sudhana gave rise to the mind of great compassion and diligently cultivated the unsurpassed path.
Seeing sentient beings constantly transmigrating through the five realms of existence, Sudhana sought adamantine wisdom to shatter the wheel of all those sufferings. Sudhana saw sentient beings...
The field of the mind is exceedingly wild and defiled; to remove the thorns of the three poisons, one must single-mindedly seek the plow of sharp wisdom.
Sentient beings dwell in the darkness of delusion, blind and lost on the right path; Sudhana acts as their guide, showing them the place of peace and security.
With the armor of patience and the vehicle of liberation, he takes wisdom as his sharp sword.
Within the three realms of existence, he is able to destroy the thieves of all afflictions;
Sudhana, the master of the Dharma-ship, universally rescues all sentient beings, Causing them to cross the ocean of saṃsāra and swiftly reach the pure jewel-island.
Sudhana, the sun of perfect enlightenment, with the wheel of great vows and the light of wisdom, Traverses everywhere through the void of the Dharma-realm.

Universally illuminating the abode of the deluded masses, The moon of the Perfectly Awakened One, Sudhana, With all white dharmas fully perfected, The cool light of compassionate concentration Shines equally upon the minds of sentient beings.
Sudhana’s ocean of supreme wisdom Abides in a mind of straightforwardness; His bodhisattva practices gradually deepen, Giving rise to the myriad treasures of the Dharma.
The Great-Minded Dragon Sudhana ascends into the void of the Dharma-realm; He raises clouds and pours down sweet rain, bringing all fruits to fruition.
Sudhana kindles the lamp of Dharma: Faith is the wick, compassion the oil, mindfulness the vessel, and merit the light.
It extinguishes the darkness of the three poisons, Awakening the mind from its embryonic stage of kalala.
Compassion is its womb, loving-kindness its flesh, The factors of enlightenment its limbs and joints. It grows from the Tathāgatagarbha;
it increases the treasury of merit, The treasury of pure wisdom, And reveals the treasury of skillful means.
It gives birth to the treasury of great vows— Such is this magnificent adornment that protects and delivers all living beings.
Among all devas and humans, it is difficult to hear and difficult to see.
Such a tree of wisdom has roots so deep they cannot be moved; its manifold practices gradually increase, universally shading all living beings.
If you wish to give rise to all virtues, if you wish to inquire about all dharmas, and if you wish to sever all doubts— [then approach this tree].
Seeking exclusively for spiritual friends, Desiring to shatter the demons of delusion, Desiring to remove the stains of all views,
And desiring to untie the bonds of sentient beings— Seeking exclusively for spiritual friends, One should extinguish all evil realms, Reveal the path to humans and devas,
Cause them to cultivate meritorious deeds, And swiftly enter the city of Nirvana.
I shall ferry across those in the perils of various views; I shall cut through the net of various views; I shall dry up the waters of craving and desire;
I shall show the path of the threefold way. I shall become the refuge for the world; I shall become the light of the world;
I shall become the teacher of the triple realm, showing them the place of liberation, and likewise cause the world to [attain it].

Universally free from all conceptual attachments, Universally awakened from the sleep of afflictions, Universally emerged from the mire of craving and desire— You shall realize all various dharmas, And you shall purify all various buddha-fields. All shall reach ultimate perfection;
Your mind is filled with great joy. Your conduct is exceedingly gentle and compliant, And your mind is most pure.
All the merits one wishes to cultivate shall be fully perfected; before long, one shall behold all Buddhas and thoroughly comprehend all dharmas.
One shall adorn and purify oceans of Buddha-lands and achieve great Bodhi, fulfilling the ocean of all practices.
One should know the ocean of all dharmas and cross over the ocean of sentient beings.
By practicing all such deeds in this way, one shall reach the shore of merit;
one shall give birth to all categories of goodness and become equal to the sons of the Buddha.
With such a resolute mind, one shall sever all delusions, purify all karma, subdue all Māras, and fulfill such vows as these.
You shall give birth to the path of wondrous wisdom; You shall open the path of the True Dharma. Before long, you shall abandon the paths of delusion, karma, and all suffering.

The wheel of all sentient beings, Sunk and lost within the wheel of existence— You shall turn the Wheel of Dharma, Causing them to sever the wheel of suffering. You shall uphold the lineage of the Buddhas.
You shall purify the seed of the Dharma; you shall gather the seed of the Saṃgha. You shall pervade all three times;
you shall sever the net of all cravings; you shall tear asunder the net of all views;
you shall rescue the net of all sufferings; you shall fulfill this net of vows; you shall deliver the realm of sentient beings; and you shall purify the realm of the buddha-fields.
One should cultivate the realm of wisdom; one should perfect this realm of mind.
One should cause sentient beings to rejoice, one should cause bodhisattvas to rejoice, and one should cause all Buddhas to rejoice. One should perfect this state of joy;
one should perceive all realms of existence, one should perceive all buddha-fields, and one should perceive all Buddhas.
When you attain Buddhahood, you shall emit light that shatters darkness; you shall emit light that soothes heat; you shall emit light that extinguishes evil.
You shall wash away the sufferings of the three realms of existence; you shall open the gates to the celestial realms;
you shall open the gates to the Buddha-way. You shall show the gate of liberation, causing all sentient beings to enter therein.
One should show the way of the right path; one should sever the way of the heterodox paths. Thus, through diligent practice, one accomplishes the path to Bodhi.

One should cultivate an ocean of merit; one should cross the ocean of the three realms of existence and cause the ocean of all living beings to emerge from the ocean of manifold sufferings. One should [act] toward the ocean of sentient beings.
Exhaust the ocean of afflictions, Cause the ocean of all practices to be cultivated, And swiftly enter the ocean of great wisdom.
You should increase the ocean of knowledge; You should cultivate the ocean of practice; The ocean of the great vows of all Buddhas— You should fulfill them all.
You should enter the ocean of lands; You should contemplate the ocean of sentient beings.
You should, by the power of wisdom, drink universally from the oceans of all dharmas;
you should behold the clouds of all Buddhas, raise clouds of offerings, and listen to the clouds of the sublime Dharma.

You should give rise to these clouds of vows, travel everywhere through the chambers of the three realms of existence, utterly destroy the chambers of all delusions, and enter universally into the chamber of the Tathāgata.
One should practice this path: universally entering the gates of samādhi, universally roaming through the gates of liberation, and universally abiding in the gates of supernormal powers;
traversing the entire dharma-realm, appearing before all sentient beings, and appearing before all Buddhas, just like the light of the sun and moon— one shall thus accomplish such power.
Your conduct shall be free from agitation; Your conduct shall be free from attachment. Like a bird moving through the sky, you shall achieve such wondrous mastery;
Like Indra’s net, the network of realms abides thus— You shall go to them all, Unimpeded like the wind, And enter the Dharma-realm.
You travel to all worlds and universally behold the Buddhas of the three times; your heart gives rise to great joy and celebration.
Regarding all dharma-gates, you have already attained some and shall attain others; you should give rise to great exultation.
Without greed and without weariness, you are a vessel of merit, able to follow the teachings of all Buddhas.
Those who are able to cultivate the bodhisattva practices can behold this marvel.
Such sons of the Buddhas are difficult to encounter even in hundreds of millions of eons, let alone behold their merits.
You who have cultivated these sublime paths and been born among human beings have gained great benefit from all virtues; you have been able to see Mañjuśrī and the others.
Possessing immeasurable virtues, you have already departed from all evil realms, emerged from all places of difficulty, and transcended all suffering and affliction.
Excellent! Do not be indolent; having left the stage of ordinary beings, you now dwell upon the stage of a bodhisattva.
You shall fulfill the stage of wisdom and swiftly enter the stage of the Tathāgata.
The Bodhisattva’s practice is like the ocean, And the Buddha’s wisdom is equal to space;

Your aspiration is likewise so— You should give rise to great joy. With the faculties free from weariness, And the vow ever resolute, By attending upon spiritual friends, All shall soon be fully perfected— Such are the various practices of the Bodhisattvas.
All act to harmonize sentient beings, universally practicing all dharma-gates. Be careful not to give rise to doubt;
you possess inconceivable merit as well as true faith. Therefore, on this very day, you are able to see these sons of the Buddha.
Having seen these sons of the Buddha, you shall all obtain vast and great benefit.
Each and every one of these great vows is accepted with faith by all.
You are able to cultivate the bodhisattva practice within the three realms of existence; therefore, O Son of the Buddha, I show you this gate of liberation.
It is not for those who are not vessels of the Dharma to dwell together with the Sons of the Buddha, even if they were to do so for immeasurable eons.

Its realm is unknown to others; seeing all these bodhisattvas and hearing such a Dharma as this, which is extremely rare in the world, you should give rise to great joy and celebration. The Buddhas protect and mind you, and the bodhisattvas take you into their care.
Since you are able to practice in accordance with their teachings, it is well that you dwell in this long life.

Having been born into the family of Bodhisattvas, having already perfected the virtues of a Bodhisattva, and having grown within the lineage of the Tathāgatas, you shall soon ascend to the stage of consecration. Before long, you shall attain equality with all the sons of the Buddhas;
seeing sentient beings suffering in affliction, you shall place them all in a state of peace and security, just as one plants seeds according to their kind.
You shall surely obtain such a fruit; I now congratulate and comfort you.

You ought to feel great joy, for while immeasurable bodhisattvas have practiced the Way for immeasurable eons and were yet unable to accomplish this conduct, you have now attained it all through the power of firm progress in faith and delight. Thus has Sudhana accomplished this practice.
If one possesses a heart of reverence and admiration, one should likewise train in this way:
All meritorious deeds arise from aspiration and desire; Sudhana has already understood this.
Always delighting in diligent cultivation, like a dragon spreading dense clouds, He will surely pour down a great rain; Thus does the Bodhisattva give rise to the wisdom of aspiration.
If you have a spiritual friend who decisively cultivates all practices and shows you the conduct of Samantabhadra, you should serve them well;
be careful not to give rise to doubt. Throughout immeasurable eons, you have recklessly sacrificed your body out of desire;
now, for the sake of seeking enlightenment, this sacrifice is truly virtuous.
Throughout immeasurable kalpas, you have undergone the sufferings of birth and death; you have never served the Buddhas nor heard of such a practice as this.
Now that you have obtained a human body, encountered the Buddha and spiritual friends, and are able to hear and receive these practices for awakening—why do you not rejoice?
Though you have met with the appearance of a Buddha in the world, [you remain indifferent].
Even if one encounters a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*), if their mind is not pure, they will not hear such a Dharma.
However, if one has faith, joy, and respect for a spiritual friend, and is free from doubt and weariness, then one hears such a Dharma.
If there are those who hear this Dharma and give rise to a heart of aspirational vows (*praṇidhāna-citta*), [they shall attain it].
One should know that such a person has already attained vast benefit;
with such purity of mind, they shall draw near to all Buddhas and also draw near to all Bodhisattvas, destined to achieve perfect enlightenment.
If one enters this Dharma-gate, they will possess all merits and be forever freed from the various evil realms.
Not experiencing any suffering, before long they shall cast off this body and be reborn in a Buddha-land,
where they constantly behold the Buddhas of the ten directions as well as all the Bodhisattvas. Through the power of past causes,
present pure understanding, and service to virtuous friends, their various merits increase like lotuses growing from the water.
Delight in spiritual friends; Diligently make offerings to all Buddhas;
Listen to the Dharma with single-minded focus, And practice it without weariness. You are a true vessel for the Dharma;
You shall possess all dharmas, You shall cultivate all paths, And you shall fulfill all vows. By means of your mind of faith and understanding,
And having come to pay homage to me, you shall before long enter universally into the assemblies of all Buddhas.
Excellent, true son of the Buddha! You who revere all Buddhas, before long you shall be endowed with all practices and reach the shore of a Buddha’s merit.
You should go now to the presence of Mañjuśrī, the one of great wisdom.
"He shall cause you to attain the profound and wondrous conduct of Samantabhadra.
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, standing before the assembly, praised the treasury of great merit of Sudhana.
Having heard this, Sudhana was filled with joy and leaped for gladness; the hairs on his body stood on end, and he wept with choked sobs. Rising from his seat, he joined his palms...
With palms joined in reverence, he gazed up at him and circumambulated him countless times.
By the power of Mañjuśrī’s mental recollection, various flower garlands and diverse exquisite jewels suddenly filled his hands without his even realizing it.
Sudhana, filled with joy, immediately scattered them over the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya. At that time, the Bodhisattva Maitreya placed his hand upon Sudhana’s head.
He spoke in verse:
“Excellent, excellent, true son of the Buddha! Universally exerting all faculties without weariness, Before long you shall be endowed with all virtues, Just like Mañjuśrī and myself.”
Then the youth Sudhana replied in verse:
"I reflect that spiritual friends are difficult to encounter even in hundreds of millions of eons;
now that I have been able to draw near them all and come into the presence of the Honored One, it is because of Mañjuśrī that I behold those who are so difficult to see."
That Honored One of Great Merit, I pray that you will quickly return so that I may behold you.

[Commentary] Fifth: At that time, after Sudhana had thus completed all these immeasurable dharmas of praising and extolling the Bodhisattvas, the following section concerns Sudhana’s desire to see Maitreya Bodhisattva, from which Maitreya emerges.

Coming from without to praise Sudhana’s merits for the great assembly—this section clarifies that Bodhisattvas constantly do not dwell in their own karmic retribution, but rather gather and transform sentient beings in accordance with worldly conventions; all those who follow after them are the beings thus gathered, who have been transformed and brought to the fruit.
The remainder is self-evident according to the text.
[Sūtra] At that time, the youth Sudhana joined his palms in reverent salutation and addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva again, saying:
"O Great Sage, I have already set my mind upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi;
yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practices, nor how one should cultivate the bodhisattva path. O Great Sage, [please explain] all such things..."
He came to bestow upon the Venerable One the prediction that in one lifetime he would attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
If in one lifetime he were to attain unsurpassed enlightenment, then he would have already transcended all the stages where Bodhisattvas dwell;
he would have already surpassed all the Bodhisattva positions of "leaving birth" (*avivartika*); and he would have already perfected all the *pāramitās*.
Having deeply entered all gateways of patience, they have already fulfilled all bodhisattva stages;
having sported within all gateways of liberation, they have already accomplished all dharmas of samādhi;
having thoroughly penetrated all bodhisattva practices, they have already realized all dhāraṇīs and eloquence; having [regarding] all bodhi...
Having attained mastery within sovereign power, having already accumulated all the bodhisattva factors conducive to enlightenment,
having already sported in wisdom and skillful means, having already brought forth the knowledge of great supernormal powers,
having already accomplished all the rules of training, having already perfected all sublime conduct, and having already fulfilled all great vows—
Having received the predictions of all Buddhas, they have fully understood the gateways of all vehicles;
they are worthy of being protected and remembered by all Tathāgatas; they are able to encompass the Bodhi of all Buddhas;
they are able to uphold the treasury of the Dharma of all Buddhas; and they are able to uphold the secret treasury of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Having already become a leader among the entire assembly of Bodhisattvas, one has thereby become a great heroic general capable of shattering the army of the Māra of afflictions;
one has thereby become a great guide capable of leading others out of the wilderness of birth and death;
one has thereby become a great King of Physicians capable of treating the grave illnesses of all delusions; and one has thereby become the most supreme among all sentient beings.
Thus, one has already attained mastery among all world-rulers; one has already become the foremost among all noble ones;
one has already become the most preeminent among all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
one has already become a helmsman within the ocean of birth and death; and one has already cast the net for the subduing of all sentient beings.
Thus, they have already been able to contemplate the faculties of all sentient beings; they have already been able to encompass the realms of all sentient beings;
they have already been able to protect the assembly of all bodhisattvas; they have already been able to discuss all matters concerning bodhisattvas;
they have already been able to go to the abodes of all Tathāgatas; and they have already been able to dwell within the assemblies of all Tathāgatas.
They have already been able to manifest their bodies before all sentient beings; they have already been able to remain unstained by all worldly dharmas;
they have already been able to transcend all realms of Māra; they have already been able to dwell securely in the realm of all Buddhas;
they have already been able to reach the unimpeded realm of all Bodhisattvas; and they have already been able to diligently make offerings to all Buddhas.

Having realized that one’s own nature is identical with the essence of all Buddha-dharmas, having bound the silken sash of the sublime Dharma, having received the Buddha-consecration, having abided in omniscience, and having been able to universally give birth to all Buddha-dharmas, one is able to swiftly tread upon the stage of omniscience.
Great Sage Bodhisattva, how should one learn the bodhisattva practice? How should one cultivate the bodhisattva path? According to what...
By practicing and studying, one swiftly attains the full perfection of all Buddha-dharmas; one is able to deliver all sentient beings as they are remembered;
one is universally able to fulfill all great vows that have been made; one is universally able to bring all initiated practices to ultimate completion;

one is universally able to comfort all devas and humans; one does not betray oneself; one does not sever the Three Jewels; one does not render the lineage of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas in vain; and one is able to uphold it.
"I pray that you will explain all such matters as these—the Dharma-eye of all Buddhas.
Then, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya surveyed the entire assembly at the site of enlightenment, pointed toward Sudhana, and spoke these words:
"O noble ones, do you see this son of a householder who is now inquiring of me regarding the various merits of the bodhisattva conduct?"
"O noble ones, this son of a householder is courageous and diligent; his aspirations are unadulterated, his profound mind is firm, and he never regresses.

Possessing superior hope, he is like one who seeks to extinguish a fire on his head—never satiated, delighting in spiritual friends, approaching and making offerings to them, seeking them out everywhere, serving them, and requesting the Dharma. O noble ones, this son of a householder in the past..."
Having received the instructions of Mañjuśrī in the City of Blessings (*Puṇyavatī*), he traveled southward in succession seeking spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
After passing through one hundred and ten spiritual friends, he finally came to where I am; not for a single moment did he give rise to a thought of weariness or indolence.
O noble ones, this son of a householder is exceedingly difficult to encounter; he is intent upon the Great Vehicle and has mounted the Great Wisdom (*mahāprajñā*).
One who has aroused great valor and donned the armor of great compassion; who rescues and protects sentient beings with a mind of great loving-kindness;

who initiates the practice of the perfection of great diligence; who acts as a great caravan leader to protect all sentient beings; who serves as a great Dharma-ship to ferry those across the ocean of existence;
who abides in the Great Path, gathers the great treasures of the Dharma, and cultivates all vast auxiliary dharmas of the path—such a person as this...
It is difficult to hear, difficult to see, and difficult to approach, dwell with, or practice alongside;

why is this? Because this son of a noble family has resolved to rescue and protect all sentient beings, causing them to be liberated from all sufferings, to transcend all evil realms, to leave behind all perilous difficulties, to shatter the darkness of ignorance, to emerge from the wilderness of birth and death, and to bring to rest the wheel of rebirth in the various destinies.

He has crossed beyond the realm of Māra, does not cling to worldly dharmas, has emerged from the mire of desire, severed the yoke of greed, untied the bonds of views, demolished the house of conceptualization, cut off the path of delusion, shattered the banner of pride, pulled out the arrows of confusion, removed the cover of sleep, rent the net of craving, extinguished ignorance, and crossed the stream of existence.
He is free from flattery and illusion, has purified the stains of the mind, severed the confusion of folly, and transcended birth and death. O virtuous ones, this is the Elder.
For those being swept away by the four torrents, you create a great Dharma-ship; for those submerged in the mud of views, you establish a great Dharma-bridge;
for those stupefied by the darkness of ignorance, you kindle the lamp of great wisdom; for those wandering in the wilderness of birth and death, you reveal the Noble Path;
for those afflicted by the grave illness of the afflictions, you compound the medicine of the Dharma; for those who have encountered [the suffering of] birth and old age...

To those suffering from death, he gives the nectar of immortality to bring them peace; to those entering the fires of greed, anger, and delusion, he pours the water of meditative concentration to make them cool;
to those with much sorrow and affliction, he consoles them to bring them comfort; to those bound in the prison of existence, he instructs them so they may enter and exit;
to those caught in the net of views, he opens it with the sword of wisdom; and to those dwelling in the city of the realms or in perilous places, he shows them the gates of liberation.
For those who encounter difficulties, he guides them to a place of peace; for those who fear the thieves of the fetters (*saṃyojana*), he bestows the Dharma of fearlessness;

for those fallen into evil destinies, he extends the hand of compassion; for those imprisoned by the aggregates (*skandha*), he shows the city of Nirvāṇa; for those entwined by the snakes of the elements (*dhātu*), he releases them by means of the Noble Path;

for those clinging to the empty village of the six sense-bases (*āyatana*), he draws them out with the light of wisdom; and for those dwelling in false salvation, he causes them to enter [the true path].
To those on the right path who associate with evil friends, he shows them virtuous friends; to those who delight in mundane dharmas, he instructs them in the noble Dharma;
to those attached to birth and death, he causes them to enter the city of omniscience.

O worthy ones, this son of a householder constantly protects sentient beings through such practices, never ceasing to resolve upon bodhicitta, and has never grown weary in his quest for the Mahāyāna path.
They never grow weary of drinking the waters of all dharmas, nor do they ever feel satiety; they constantly and diligently accumulate the practices that assist the path.

They always delight in purifying all dharma-gates and cultivate the conduct of a bodhisattva without abandoning diligence. They bring all vows to fulfillment through skillful means and, upon seeing spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), their hearts never tire of them.
In serving spiritual friends, their bodies never grow fatigued, and they never weary of hearing from them... [the teachings of] spiritual friends.
"O virtuous ones, you should always joyfully practice all instructions you receive and never act in opposition to them.
If there are sentient beings who can resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, that is rare;
if, having resolved their minds, they can furthermore apply themselves with such diligence and skillful means to study the Buddha-dharmas, it is doubly rare; and to be able to do so in this way..."
Seeking the bodhisattva path, one can likewise purify the bodhisattva conduct; likewise serve spiritual friends;
likewise act as if putting out a fire on one’s head; likewise comply with the instructions of spiritual friends;
likewise practice with firm resolve; likewise gather the factors of enlightenment; and likewise remain free from seeking anything at all.
Furthermore, they are able to thus not abandon the bodhisattva’s single-minded resolve;

they are able to thus take no pleasure in the household life, have no attachment to sensual delights, and feel no longing for parents, relatives, or acquaintances, but instead delight only in seeking out companions for the bodhisattva path;
and they are able to thus disregard their own bodies and lives, wishing only to diligently cultivate the path to all-knowledge.
Virtuous ones, you should know that it is progressively more difficult to attain:

other bodhisattvas must pass through immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of kalpas before they can fulfill their bodhisattva vows and practices, and before they can draw near to the enlightenment of the Buddhas;
yet this son of a householder is able, within a single lifetime, to purify Buddha-fields and to transform sentient beings.
Upon birth, one is able to penetrate the dharma-realm through wisdom; one is able to accomplish all the pāramitās;
one is able to expand all practices; one is able to fulfill all great vows; one is able to transcend all demonic activities;
one is able to serve all virtuous friends; one is able to purify the bodhisattva path; and one is able to...

Having thus praised the various merits of the youth Sudhana and inspired immeasurable hundreds of thousands of sentient beings to resolve upon Bodhicitta, Maitreya Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, who is fully endowed with all the practices of Samantabhadra, addressed Sudhana, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, noble son! For the benefit of the entire world, you have..."
"You protect and deliver all sentient beings; you have resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* for the sake of diligently seeking all Buddha-dharmas.
Good son, you have obtained a great benefit; you have well attained a human body; you have well established your lifespan;
you have well encountered the appearance of a Tathāgata in the world; and you have well beheld Mañjuśrī, the Great Knower of Virtue."
I recognize that your body is a vessel of goodness, moistened by all roots of virtue; you are sustained by the support of pure dharmas;
your understanding and aspirations are entirely purified; you are protected and remembered by all Buddhas;
and you are embraced by all spiritual friends. Why is this so? Son of good family, the bodhicitta is like a seed.
Because it can give birth to all the qualities of a Buddha, the bodhicitta is like a fertile field;
because it can cause the pure and white dharmas of sentient beings to grow, the bodhicitta is like the great earth;
because it can support all the worlds, the bodhicitta is like pure water; because it can wash away the stains of all afflictions, the bodhicitta is...
Just as a great wind is unimpeded throughout the entire world, so too is the bodhicitta;
it is like a blazing fire, for it can burn away the fuel of all views; it is like the pure sun, for it universally illuminates all worlds;
it is like the full moon, for all pure and white dharmas are therein brought to perfection.
The bodhicitta is like a bright lamp, for it can radiate the manifold light of the Dharma;
the bodhicitta is like pure eyes, for it universally perceives all places of safety and peril;
the bodhicitta is like a great highway, for it enables all to enter the city of great wisdom; the bodhicitta is like a correct ferry, for it causes one to attain liberation.
Because it counters all false dharmas, the bodhicitta is like a great vehicle, for it can universally transport all bodhisattvas;
because it reveals all bodhisattva practices, the bodhicitta is like a gateway;
because it provides a dwelling place for the cultivation of samādhi dharmas, the bodhicitta is like a palace; and the bodhicitta is like a garden grove.
Because one sports therein and experiences the joy of the Dharma, the bodhicitta is like a dwelling;
because it brings peace and security to all sentient beings, the bodhicitta is a place of refuge; because it benefits all worlds, the bodhicitta is a support;
because it is the locus upon which the practices of all bodhisattvas depend, the bodhicitta is...
Just as a compassionate father instructs and guides all bodhisattvas, so is the bodhicitta;
just as a compassionate mother gives birth to and raises all bodhisattvas, so is the bodhicitta; just as a wet nurse nurtures and nourishes all bodhisattvas, so is the bodhicitta;
and just as a virtuous friend brings about benefit for all bodhisattvas, so is the bodhicitta.
The bodhicitta is like a sovereign, for it excels all followers of the two vehicles;
the bodhicitta is like a universal monarch, for it attains mastery over all aspirations;
the bodhicitta is like the great ocean, for all virtues enter into it; the bodhicitta is like Mount Sumeru among all sentient beings...
Because the mind is impartial, the bodhicitta is like the Cakravāḍa mountains, which sustain all worlds;
because it nurtures all medicinal herbs of wisdom, the bodhicitta is like the Snowy Mountains;
because it gives birth to the fragrance of all virtues, the bodhicitta is like the Fragrant Mountain; and the bodhicitta is like space.
Because its various sublime virtues are vast and boundless, the bodhicitta is like a lotus flower, for it is unstained by any worldly phenomena;
the bodhicitta is like a well-trained wise elephant, for its mind is docile and free from wildness or perversity;
the bodhicitta is like a noble and good horse, for it is far removed from all evil natures. Thus is the bodhicitta.
Just as a charioteer protects all the dharmas of the Mahāyāna, so too is the bodhicitta like a potent medicine, for it can cure the disease of all afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like a pit or trap, for it causes all evil dharmas to fall into ruin;
the bodhicitta is like a vajra, for it is able to pierce through all phenomena.
The bodhicitta is like a casket of incense, for it can store all the fragrances of merit;
the bodhicitta is like a wondrous flower, for it is joyfully beheld by all the world;
the bodhicitta is like white sandalwood, for it removes the heat of the various desires and brings about coolness; the bodhicitta is like black agarwood, for it can permeate the entire dharma-realm.
Because it is all-pervasive, the bodhicitta is like the king of medicines, Sudarśana, for it can destroy all diseases of the afflictions (*kleśa*);
the bodhicitta is like the medicine Vigama, for it can extract all arrows of delusion;
the bodhicitta is like Śakra, for it is the most honored among all lords; the bodhicitta is like Vi... [text truncated]
Because the śramaṇa can sever all suffering of poverty, the bodhicitta is like the goddess Lakṣmī, adorned with all merits;
because it adorns all bodhisattvas, the bodhicitta is like an ornament;
because it can burn away all conditioned phenomena, the bodhicitta is like the fire at the end of an eon.
The mind is like the rootless medicinal herb that nurtures all the qualities of a Buddha;
the bodhicitta is like the dragon’s jewel that can dissolve all the poison of afflictions; the bodhicitta is like the water-purifying jewel that can clarify all the turbidity of afflictions;
the bodhicitta is like the wish-fulfilling jewel that provides for all beings everywhere.
Because it eliminates poverty, the bodhicitta is like a vessel of merit;
because it fulfills the minds of all sentient beings, the bodhicitta is like a wish-fulfilling tree that can rain down all manner of ornaments;
because it does not receive the stains of birth and death, the bodhicitta is like a garment of swan feathers; [it is] like white cotton thread from...
Because its nature has been pure from the very beginning, the bodhicitta is like a sharp plow that can cultivate the fields of all sentient beings;
the bodhicitta is like Nārāyaṇa, able to destroy the enemy of all views of self;
the bodhicitta is like a swift arrow, able to pierce through all sufferings; the bodhicitta is like...
Just as a sharp spear can pierce all armor of afflictions, so too is the bodhicitta like sturdy armor that can protect all minds that accord with reality;
just as a sharp blade can sever the heads of all afflictions, so too is the bodhicitta like a keen sword that can cut through the armor of all pride.
The bodhicitta is like the banner of a valiant general, for it can subdue all the armies of Māra;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp saw, for it can cut down all the trees of ignorance;
the bodhicitta is like a sharp axe, for it can fell all the trees of suffering; the bodhicitta is like weaponry, for it can defend against all...
The bodhicitta is like a hand in times of hardship, for it protects the body of all the perfections;
the bodhicitta is like a fine foot, for it firmly establishes all meritorious qualities;
the bodhicitta is like an eye-salve, for it eliminates the cataracts of all ignorance; the bodhicitta is like a pair of tongs.
Because it can extract the thorn of all views of a self, the bodhicitta is like a bed;
because it pacifies and eliminates the various toils and sufferings of birth and death, the bodhicitta is like a spiritual friend;
because it can untie all the bonds of birth and death, the bodhicitta is like excellent treasure; because it can eliminate all matters of poverty, the bodhicitta is like... [excellent treasure].
Because it well knows the essential path for bodhisattvas to emerge [from saṃsāra], the bodhicitta is like a great guide;

because it produces the wealth of merit without exhaustion, the bodhicitta is like a hidden treasure; because it gives rise to the water of wisdom without end, the bodhicitta is like a gushing spring;
and because it universally manifests the images of all dharma-gates, the bodhicitta is like a clear mirror.
The bodhicitta is like a lotus flower, for it is unstained by any defilement of sin;
the bodhicitta is like a great river, for it draws forth and gathers all dharmas of deliverance;
the bodhicitta is like a great nāga king, for it can rain down the rain of all sublime dharmas; the bodhicitta is like the life-faculty, for it sustains the bodhisattva.
Because it is the body of great compassion, the bodhicitta is like nectar, for it enables one to abide in the realm of immortality;
because it universally gathers all sentient beings, the bodhicitta is like a great net;
because it gathers all those who are to be converted, the bodhicitta is like a snare; and because it hooks [beings], the bodhicitta is like a baited hook.
Because that which dwells within the abyss of existence has emerged from it; because bodhicitta is like the agada medicine, capable of bringing about illness-free, eternal peace and security;
because bodhicitta is like an antidote for poison, capable of completely neutralizing the poison of craving and attachment;
because bodhicitta is like a well-held mantra, capable of removing all poisons of perversion.
The bodhicitta is like a swift wind, for it can sweep away all veils and mists;

the bodhicitta is like a great island of jewels, for it gives rise to all the jewels of the factors of enlightenment; the bodhicitta is like a noble lineage, for it gives rise to all pure and wholesome dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like a dwelling, for it is the locus upon which all meritorious qualities depend.
Therefore, the bodhicitta is like a marketplace, for it is the place where Bodhisattva-merchants trade;
the bodhicitta is like an alchemical elixir, for it can purify all stains of affliction;
the bodhicitta is like fine honey, for it perfects the flavor of all meritorious qualities; the bodhicitta is like the true path, for it leads all Bodhisattvas...
Because the Bodhisattva enters the city of wisdom, the bodhicitta is like an excellent vessel, for it can hold all pure and white dharmas;
the bodhicitta is like seasonal rain, for it can extinguish the dust of all afflictions;
the bodhicitta is a dwelling place, for it is the abode where all Bodhisattvas reside; the bodhicitta is life itself.
Because it does not take up the fruit of liberation of the śrāvakas, the bodhicitta is like pure lapis lazuli, being naturally clear and bright and free from all defilements;
because it surpasses the wisdom of the two vehicles of the world, the bodhicitta is like a sapphire;
because it awakens all sentient beings from the sleep of afflictions, the bodhicitta is like a watch-drum.
The bodhicitta is like the nature of pure water, for it is fundamentally clear, limpid, and free from defilement;
the bodhicitta is like Jāmbūnada gold, for its brilliance outshines all conditioned virtues;
the bodhicitta is like the king of great mountains, for it rises above all worlds; the bodhicitta is that which provides refuge, never rejecting any who come to it.
Therefore, the bodhicitta is that which brings benefit, for it can eliminate all causes of decline and affliction;
the bodhicitta is that which is a sublime jewel, for it causes all minds to rejoice;
the bodhicitta is like a great assembly of giving, for it fills the hearts of all sentient beings; the bodhicitta is that which is most honored and supreme among all sentient beings.
Because the mind has no equal, the bodhicitta is like a hidden treasure; because it can encompass all the qualities of a Buddha, the bodhicitta is like Indra’s net;
because it can subdue the asuras of the afflictions, the bodhicitta is like the wind of Varuṇa; because it can move all those who are to be transformed, the bodhicitta is like...
Because Indra-fire can burn away all habitual tendencies of the afflictions, the bodhicitta is like a stūpa of the Buddha,
which all the world should venerate.
*The Great Vaipulya Buddhāvataṃsaka Sūtra Combined Commentary*, Fascicle 117.
