[Sūtra] At that time, Sudhana saw his own body before all those Tathāgatas, and he also saw...
He remembered and did not forget all the Buddha-activities of that entire assembly, attaining unimpeded penetration; furthermore,
he heard from within all the pavilions the sounds of jewel nets, bells, and various musical instruments,
all of which clearly proclaimed the inconceivable and subtle Dharma-sounds, expounding various teachings— namely, some explaining how Bodhisattvas resolve upon Bodhicitta, or...
He hears the sounds of all the Buddha-dharmas as previously described— whether they speak of the practice of the pāramitās, or of various vows, or of the stages (bhūmis),
or of reverently making offerings to the Tathāgatas, or of adorning the buddha-fields, or of the distinctions in the Buddhas’ preaching of the Dharma—
all of which he hears clearly and understands with eloquent discernment. Furthermore, he hears that in such-and-such a place there is...
A certain bodhisattva, having heard a certain Dharma-gate and being exhorted by a certain spiritual friend, resolved upon the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*) in a certain eon,
at a certain buddha-field, in the presence of a certain Tathāgata, amidst a great assembly.
Having heard of such merits from a certain Buddha, they gave rise to such a mind, formulated such vows, and planted such vast roots of goodness over the course of several eons.
Practicing the bodhisattva path for such a length of time, one shall attain perfect enlightenment with such a name, such a lifespan, and such a land fully adorned;
fulfilling such vows, one shall transform such assemblies of sentient beings and such congregations of śrāvakas and bodhisattvas;
and after entering parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain in the world for so many kalpas, benefiting beings in such a manner.
Immeasurable sentient beings may hear that in a certain place a certain bodhisattva practices such perfections as generosity,
ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom; or they may hear that in a certain place a certain bodhisattva,
for the sake of seeking the Dharma, has renounced his royal throne, various treasures, wife, children, retinue, hands, feet, head, and eyes.
They have no attachment whatsoever to any part of their bodies; or they hear that in a certain place there is a certain bodhisattva who protects the True Dharma spoken by the Tathāgata,
acting as a great Dharma teacher, extensively practicing the gift of Dharma, erecting the banner of Dharma, blowing the conch of Dharma, beating the drum of Dharma,
raining down the rain of Dharma, constructing Buddha-stūpas and temples, and fashioning images of the Buddha, bestowing upon all sentient beings every kind of article of pleasure.
Or he might hear that in a certain place, a certain Tathāgata attained perfect enlightenment during a certain eon,
in such a land, amidst such an assembly, with such a lifespan, preaching such a Dharma, fulfilling such vows,
and transforming such immeasurable sentient beings. When the youth Sudhana heard such inconceivable and subtle sounds of the Dharma,

With body and mind filled with joy, pliancy, and delight, they immediately attained immeasurable gateways of *dhāraṇī*, gateways of eloquence (*pratibhāna*), various meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*),
various patiences (*kṣānti*), various vows (*praṇidhāna*), various perfections (*pāramitā*), various supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), various clarities (*vidyā*),

as well as various liberations (*vimokṣa*) and gateways of *samādhi*. Furthermore, within all the precious mirrors, they beheld various forms and images, namely, they saw the assemblies of various Buddhas.
In the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), one may see an assembly of bodhisattvas; or see an assembly of śrāvakas; or see an assembly of pratyekabuddhas;
or see a pure world; or see an impure world; or see a world that is both pure and impure;
or see a world that is both impure and pure; or see a world where a Buddha resides; or see a world where there is no [Buddha].
In the Buddha-worlds, some see small worlds, some see medium worlds, some see great worlds,
some see Indra-net worlds, some see inverted worlds, some see upright worlds, some see level worlds,
some see worlds inhabited by hell-beings, animals, and hungry ghosts, and some see worlds filled with devas and humans.
In such worlds as these, one sees within them countless great bodhisattvas, whether walking or sitting, engaged in various activities;
some give rise to great compassion out of pity for sentient beings, while others compose treatises to benefit the world;
some receive, uphold, write down, recite, inquire about, or answer [the teachings], performing repentance and dedicating their merit during the three periods of the day.
He made a vow and further beheld great nets of light from the mani-kings emanating from all the jewel pillars—
light that was blue, yellow, red, white, crystal-colored, indranila-blue, rainbow-colored, or the color of Jambūnada gold,
or appearing in the colors of every kind of radiance; he also beheld that Jambū...
There were youths and maidens of floating-tanḍana gold and various precious images; some held clouds of flowers with their hands,
or held clouds of robes, or held banners and streamers, or held garlands and canopies, or held various kinds of ointments and powdered incense,
or held exquisite nets of maṇi jewels, or hung golden chains, or draped necklaces, or raised their arms to offer up ornaments.
Some lowered their heads, their maṇi crowns hanging down as they bowed deeply to gaze up at him without ever averting their eyes;

others were seen wearing pearl necklaces that constantly emitted fragrant water possessing the eight virtues, and lapis lazuli necklaces with hundreds of thousands of rays of light shining simultaneously.
Banners, streamers, nets, and canopies—all such objects were adorned with every kind of precious jewel.
Furthermore, he saw those *utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* lotuses each producing immeasurable flowers— some as large as a hand, some a cubit in length,
and others as wide and broad as a chariot wheel— with every single flower manifesting various forms and images as its adornments.
That is to say, the forms of males, the forms of females, the forms of boys, the forms of girls,
and the forms of Śakra, Brahmā, the World-Protectors, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas,
śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and all bodhisattvas— all such sentient beings joined their palms together.
Bowing with reverence, he also beheld the Tathāgata seated in the full lotus posture, his body adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man.
Furthermore, he saw upon that ground of pure lapis lazuli, at every single step, the manifestation of inconceivable and diverse forms and images— namely, the forms and images of worlds,
the forms and images of bodhisattvas, the forms and images of Tathāgatas, as well as various pavilions and ornaments.
Furthermore, within each and every thing— the branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits of the jewel trees—
they saw various kinds of half-body forms, namely: half-bodies of Buddhas, half-bodies of Bodhisattvas, and even half-bodies of devas,
nāgas, yakṣas, up to the world-protectors, wheel-turning kings, minor kings, princes, ministers, high officials, and the fourfold assembly.
Their bodily forms and appearances were like those of all other beings; some held flower garlands, some held necklaces, and some carried all manner of ornaments.
Some bowed their bodies with palms joined in reverence, gazing up at them with single-minded devotion, their eyes never wavering for a moment.
Some offered praises, while others entered into samādhi; their bodies were all adorned with the primary and secondary marks, universally radiating various kinds of light.
As for the colors and radiances— namely, the radiance of gold, the radiance of silver, the radiance of coral,
the radiance of *duṣara*, the radiance of *indranīla* (sapphire), the radiance of *vairocana* jewels, the radiance of all manner of precious gems,
and the radiance of *campaka* flowers— he also beheld within the crescent-moon images of the various pavilions.
Emanating countless suns, moons, stars, and various radiances that universally illuminate the ten directions,
he further beheld the surrounding walls of the various pavilions, wherein every single step was adorned with all manner of precious jewels.
Within each and every jewel, there appeared Maitreya practicing the bodhisattva path in past kalpas— sometimes giving away his head and eyes, sometimes giving away his hands.
He is able to relinquish everything—his feet, lips, tongue, teeth, ears, nose, blood, flesh, skin, marrow, and even his nails and hair.
Furthermore, he gives away his wives, concubines, sons, daughters, cities, towns, villages, kingdoms, and royal thrones, providing whatever is required.
He causes those in prison to be released and those who are bound to be set free.
For those afflicted by illness, he acts as their healer; for those who have entered onto deviant paths, he shows them the right way.
He may become a mariner to ferry others across the great ocean, or a horse-king to protect them from calamities and hardships.

He may become a great seer to skillfully expound various treatises, or a wheel-turning monarch to encourage the cultivation of the ten wholesome deeds. He may become a king of physicians to skillfully treat all manner of diseases, or he may manifest as one who is filial and obedient.
Parents may either associate with virtuous friends, or become śrāvakas, or become pratyekabuddhas, or become bodhisattvas,
or become Tathāgatas to teach and discipline all sentient beings; or they may act as Dharma masters, practicing the Buddha’s teachings, upholding, reciting,
and contemplating them according to principle, establishing stūpas for the Buddha, or creating images of the Buddha, whether making offerings to them themselves or...
He exhorts others to perform such acts as applying fragrant ointments, scattering flowers, and paying respectful homage in an uninterrupted succession; or,
seeing him seated upon a lion throne extensively expounding the Dharma, he exhorts all sentient beings to abide securely in the ten wholesome paths of action,

to single-mindedly take refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, and to receive and uphold the five precepts, the eight fast-day precepts, and to go forth from the household life to hear the Dharma.

Holding, reading, reciting, and practicing according to the principle, they even behold the various forms of Maitreya Bodhisattva’s cultivation of all the perfections throughout hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asamkhyeya kalpas;
they also see all the spiritual friends whom Maitreya formerly served, adorned with every merit, and they see Maitreya in that single [assembly].

When he had approached, made offerings to, and practiced the teachings of a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), even until he reached the stage of consecration (abhiṣeka), those spiritual friends said to Sudhana:
"Welcome, young man! Behold these inconceivable deeds of the bodhisattvas;
do not give rise to weariness. At that time, because Sudhana the youth possessed the power of mindfulness that never forgets, [he beheld them].
Because they have attained the pure eyes that behold the ten directions; because they have attained the unimpeded wisdom of skillful observation;

because they have attained the sovereign wisdom of all bodhisattvas; and because they have attained the vast understanding of all bodhisattvas who have already entered the stages of wisdom—they see all such things, as well as other immeasurable and inconceivable realms of sovereignty, within every single object in each of the towers.

The various adornments of the realms are like a person who, within a dream, sees all manner of things—namely, cities, villages, palaces, gardens, mountain forests, rivers, ponds, clothing, food, drink, and even all the requisites for life;
or they see themselves, their parents, brothers, and internal or external relatives; or they see the great ocean, the *śūrasena* [mountain], and so forth.
From Mount Sumeru down to all the celestial palaces of the gods, and throughout the four continents including Jambudvīpa,
he may see his own physical form as vast as hundreds of thousands of yojanas, with dwellings and garments all proportionate to its size;
he remains thus for immeasurable periods during the day without sleeping or reclining, experiencing various states of bliss, and only upon awakening from that sleep...
Just as one who knows it is a dream can clearly remember the events seen therein, so too was the youth Sudhana; for he was sustained by the power of Maitreya Bodhisattva,
knew that all phenomena of the triple world are like dreams, extinguished the narrow and inferior conceptions of sentient beings,
attained unobstructed and vast understanding, and dwelt in the supreme realm of the bodhisattvas.
Because they have entered the inconceivable wisdom of skillful means, they are able to perceive such sovereign realms.
For example, it is like a person who, when about to die, sees the signs of the retribution they will receive according to their karma:
those who have committed evil deeds see all the various states of suffering belonging to the hells, animals, and hungry ghosts, or they see hell-wardens holding weapons in their hands.
Some were met with anger or verbal abuse, seized and led away, while others heard cries of lamentation and wailing;
some saw the River of Ashes, the Cauldron of Boiling Water, the Mountain of Knives, or the Forest of Swords, being oppressed by various forms of suffering.
Those who had performed virtuous deeds, however, immediately beheld all the celestial palaces, the immeasurable hosts of devas, and the celestial maidens.
Various garments completely adorned the palaces and gardens, all of which were exquisitely beautiful;
though his body was not yet dead, he saw such things through the power of karma. Sudhana the youth was likewise so:
by the inconceivable power of a bodhisattva’s karma, he was able to see all these adorned realms, just as if a person were possessed by a spirit.
He saw various things and was able to answer every question put to him; Sudhana the youth was likewise so, for he was sustained by the wisdom of the Bodhisattvas.
Thus, seeing all those various adornments, there was no questioner whom he could not satisfy with an answer.
It was as if a person possessed by a nāga were to consider himself a nāga and enter the nāga palace.
In a short time, he thought that days, months, years, and ages had already passed; the youth Sudhana was likewise so,
for by dwelling in the perception of the bodhisattva’s wisdom and through the empowerment of Maitreya Bodhisattva, he perceived immeasurable eons in a short time—
just as within a Brahma palace named Adorned Treasury (*Vyūha-kośa*), one sees all two thousand worlds therein.
Just as all things do not become confused or intermingled, so too it was with Sudhana;
within that pavilion, he universally beheld all the various distinct arrays of the adorned realms without any confusion.

It was like a bhikṣu who has entered the meditative concentration of the universal bases (*kṛtsnāyatana*): whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, the objects of the concentration he has entered appear before him.
The youth Sudhana was likewise; he entered the pavilion and beheld all realms with complete clarity and understanding.
It was as if a person were to see a city of Gandharvas in the midst of space, fully adorned, perceiving every detail without any obstruction.
It was also like a yakṣa palace and a human palace existing together in the same place.

Yet they do not intermingle, each according to its own karma, perceiving things differently. It is like the great ocean, within which all the forms and images of the three thousandfold world-system are seen;
or like a master illusionist who, through the power of illusion, manifests various illusory phenomena and diverse activities.
So too is it with the youth Sudhana, through the majestic spiritual power of Maitreya Bodhisattva.
Therefore, by means of the inconceivable power of illusory wisdom and because he is able to know all phenomena through that illusory wisdom,
and having attained the sovereign powers of all bodhisattvas, he beheld within the pavilion the sovereign realm of all its adornments.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya withdrew his supernatural power, entered the pavilion, snapped his fingers to make a sound, and addressed Sudhana:
Vasumitra said, "Good son, the arising of the dharma-nature is thus. This is the mark manifested by the gathering of causes and conditions through the bodhisattva’s wisdom that knows all dharmas.
Such an intrinsic nature is like an illusion, like a dream, like a shadow, and like a reflection; it is entirely unestablished.
At that time, having heard the sound of the snapping fingers, Sudhana arose from his samādhi. Maitreya addressed him, saying, "Good son..."
Child, you abide in the inconceivable sovereign liberation of a bodhisattva; you experience the joy and bliss of the various bodhisattva samādhis;
you behold the various sublime and wondrously adorned palaces sustained by the spiritual power of bodhisattvas and manifested through the vows and wisdom that flow from the factors of enlightenment;
you see the conduct of bodhisattvas, hear the Dharma of bodhisattvas, know the virtues of bodhisattvas, and understand the Tathāgatas.
Sudhana said, "Indeed, O Noble One! This is due to the power of the spiritual friend’s empowerment, mindfulness, and majestic authority.

Noble One, what is the name of this gate of liberation? Maitreya replied, "Son of good family, this gate of liberation is named 'The Treasury Adorned with the Wisdom of Unforgetting Mindfulness that Enters All Realms of the Three Times. Son of good family...
Within this gate of liberation, there are unspeakably unspeakable gates of liberation that can be attained by a bodhisattva in a single lifetime.
Sudhana asked, "Where has this arrayed phenomenon gone? Maitreya replied, "It has gone to the place from which it came.
[Sudhana] asked, "From where did it come? [Maitreya] replied, "It came from within the wisdom and spiritual power of the bodhisattvas; it relies upon the Bodhi..."
By the power of his wisdom and spiritual penetrations, he abides without a place of departure and without a place of dwelling;
he is neither accumulated nor permanent, being far removed from all things. Good son, it is like a dragon king sending down rain: it does not issue from his body, nor does it issue from his mind;
there is no accumulation, yet it is not unseen, for by the power of the dragon king’s mental intention, it pours down in vast torrents everywhere.
Such inconceivable realms pervading the world, O son of good family, are likewise with that matter of adornment;

it dwells neither within nor without, yet it is not unseen. It is solely through the power of the Bodhisattva’s majestic spiritual authority and the power of your own roots of goodness that you see such things.
Son of good family, it is like a master of illusions who creates various illusions.
Phenomena come from nowhere and go nowhere; although there is no coming or going, they are clearly visible due to the power of illusion.
Those adorned phenomena are likewise: they come from nowhere and go nowhere;
yet, although there is no coming or going, they appear through the power of inconceivable illusory wisdom resulting from habitual practice, as well as by the power of former great vows.
Thus, when it was manifested in this way, the youth Sudhana said, "Great Sage, from where have you come?
Maitreya replied, "Noble son, for all bodhisattvas there is no coming and no going; they come in such a manner. They come without movement and without abiding.

They come without location and without attachment. They do not perish, they are not born; they do not abide, they do not shift; they do not move, they do not arise; they are without longing and without..."
“Son of good family, they come thus—clinging to neither karma nor retribution, neither arising nor ceasing, neither annihilation nor permanence.
Bodhisattvas come from the state of great compassion because they wish to discipline all sentient beings;

they come from the state of great loving-kindness because they wish to rescue and protect all sentient beings; they come from the state of pure precepts, taking birth according to the inclinations of others.”
Thus, they come from the realm of great vows, being sustained by the power of their past aspirations; they come from the realm of supernormal powers, manifesting at will in all places;
they come from the realm of immovability, never abandoning or departing from any Buddha;
they come from the realm of neither grasping nor rejecting, for they do not exert body or mind to come and go; they come from the realm of wisdom and skillful means...
I come from the place that accords with all sentient beings; I come from the place where manifestations are displayed, appearing through transformation like reflections.
Yet, son of good family, as for your question, "From where do you come?"—son of good family, I come from my birthplace, the country of Mālava. There, son of good family, there is a village.
In a place known as a dwelling, there was a son of a householder named Gopāla; in order to transform him and lead him into the Buddha-dharma, [the Bodhisattva] resided there.
Furthermore, for all the people of that birthplace, he preached the Dharma according to their individual capacities for transformation.
He also expounded the Mahāyāna to his parents, his kinsmen, and the Brahmins, leading them to enter the path.
Therefore, while dwelling there and having come from there, the youth Sudhana said, "Noble One, what is the birthplace of a bodhisattva?
He replied, "Good son, there are ten kinds of birthplaces for a bodhisattva. What are the ten?

Good son, the mind of enlightenment (*bodhicitta*) is the birthplace of a bodhisattva, for it gives birth to the family of bodhisattvas. The profound resolve (*adhyāśaya*) is the birthplace of a bodhisattva..."

Because they are born into the family of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), the stages (*bhūmi*) are the birthplace of bodhisattvas; because they are born into the family of the perfections (*pāramitā*), great vows are the birthplace of bodhisattvas;
because they are born into the family of sublime conduct, great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*) is the birthplace of bodhisattvas;

because they are born into the family of the four means of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), thorough investigation according to reality is the birthplace of bodhisattvas; and because they are born into the family of the perfection of wisdom (*prajñāpāramitā*).

Therefore, the Mahāyāna is the birthplace of Bodhisattvas because it gives birth to them in the family of skillful means; it is the birthplace of Bodhisattvas because it gives birth to them in the family of teaching and transforming sentient beings;
it is the birthplace of Bodhisattvas because it gives birth to them in the family of the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena through wisdom and skillful means;
and it is the birthplace of Bodhisattvas because it gives birth to them in the family of practicing all dharmas throughout the past, present, and future.
Because they belong to the family of all Tathāgatas, noble son, the bodhisattva mahāsattva takes the perfection of wisdom as mother,
skillful means as father, the perfection of giving as wet-nurse, the perfection of ethical discipline as foster-mother,
the perfection of patience as ornaments, the perfection of diligence as nurturer, and the perfection of meditative concentration...
Honey is its cleansing agent; spiritual friends are its instructors; all factors of enlightenment are its companions; all wholesome dharmas are its retinue;
all bodhisattvas are its brothers; the bodhicitta is its home; practice in accordance with reality is its family law;
the stages (bhūmis) are its dwelling place; the patiences (kṣāntis) are its clan; and the great vows are its household.
Teaching the fulfillment of all practices is for the sake of conforming to the family dharma; exhorting [beings] toward the Mahāyāna is for the sake of inheriting the family legacy.
Being consecrated with the water of the Dharma, the bodhisattva bound to one more birth acts as the crown prince of the King; achieving awakening, he is able to purify the family.
O son of good family, in this way the bodhisattva transcends the stage of ordinary beings, enters the rank of bodhisattvas, and is born into the dwelling of the Tathāgata.
The Buddha-nature is able to cultivate all practices, ensuring that the Three Jewels are never interrupted;

it is well able to protect the lineage of Bodhisattvas, purifying the birthplace of the Bodhisattva lineage so that it is noble and supreme, free from all faults and evils, and is reverently praised by all the world—including devas, humans, Māras, Brahmās, śramaṇas, and brāhmaṇas. Noble son, the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva is born into such [a state].
The Noble Householder, having realized that all phenomena are like reflections, feels no contempt for any worldly realm;
having realized that all phenomena are like magical emanations, he is unstained by attachment to any state of existence;
and because he knows that all phenomena are devoid of self, his mind never tires of teaching and transforming sentient beings, for his very essence is great compassion.
They gather in sentient beings without perceiving weariness or hardship, for they thoroughly understand that birth and death are like a dream;
thus, they pass through all kalpas without fear. They know that all aggregates are like illusions, and thus they manifest taking birth without ever becoming weary.
They know that the elements and sense-bases are identical to the Dharma-realm, and thus they do not destroy or annihilate any objective realm. They know all perceptions...
Because it is like a mirage, I enter the various realms of existence without giving rise to deluded attachments;
because I realize that all phenomena are like illusions, I enter the realm of Māra without conceiving stained clinging; because I know the Dharma-body, all afflictions cannot deceive me;
and because I have attained mastery, I am unhindered in penetrating all realms of existence. Good son, my body is born everywhere as one.
The equality of all phenomena and the *dharmadhātu*; the various physical forms and marks of all sentient beings;
the diverse languages and sounds of all sentient beings; the various names and titles of all sentient beings;

the manifestations of conduct according to the inclinations of all sentient beings to teach, transform, and subdue them in accordance with the world; and the manifestations of taking birth shown by all pure sentient beings—[these are all equal].
Performing all manner of deeds and activities of ordinary beings, manifesting the perceptions of all sentient beings,
and appearing in forms that fulfill the vows of all bodhisattvas to pervade the Dharma-realm— O son of noble family,
I do this to transform and deliver those who formerly practiced the same conduct as I but have now fallen away from the bodhicitta, and likewise to instruct and transform my own parents and kinsmen.
Furthermore, in order to teach and transform the various brahmins so that they might abandon their pride regarding their lineage and be born into the Tathāgata-lineage,
I have been born here in this Jambudvīpa world, in the kingdom of Mālava, in the village of Koṭa,
into a brahmin family. O son of good family, I dwell here within this great pavilion, according to the inclinations of all sentient beings.
I employ various skillful means to teach, transform, and subdue those sons of good family whom I delight to see.
It is for the sake of conforming to the minds of sentient beings; it is for the sake of maturing those gods who share my practice in Tuṣita Heaven;
and it is so that by manifesting the transformations of a Bodhisattva’s merit and wisdom—adornments that surpass all realms of desire—I may cause them to abandon all sensual cravings.
Because he desires to cause them to know that all conditioned phenomena are impermanent; because he desires to cause them to know that the prosperity of the devas must inevitably decline;
because he desires to manifest, at the time of his imminent descent into birth, the dharma-gate of great wisdom through discourse with bodhisattvas in their final birth;
because he desires to gather and transform those who share the same practice; and because he desires to teach and transform those sent by Śākyamuni Tathāgata.
Because they awaken like lotuses in full bloom, when you pass away from this life, you will be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven.
Son of good family, my vows shall be fulfilled; when I attain omniscience and realize bodhi, both you and Mañjuśrī shall behold me.
Son of good family, you should go to the spiritual friend Mañjuśrī and ask him: "How does a bodhisattva..."
How does one study the bodhisattva conduct? How does one enter the gateway of Samantabhadra’s conduct?
How is it accomplished? How is it vast? How does one accord with it? How is it purified? How is it perfected?
Noble son, he shall explain these matters to you in detail for you. Why is this? Mañjuśrī, all his great vows are not like those of any other immeasurable hundreds [of bodhisattvas].
Good son, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, who possesses the virtues of a thousand koṭi-nayuta bodhisattvas, has vast conduct and boundless vows;
he gives rise to all the merits of a bodhisattva without ceasing.
Good son, Mañjuśrī is constantly the mother of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭi-nayuta Buddhas.
He constantly serves as the teacher for immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of bodhisattvas, teaching and bringing all sentient beings to maturity;
his fame is universally heard throughout the worlds of the ten directions. He always acts as a Dharma teacher within the assemblies of all Buddhas and is praised by all Tathāgatas.
Abiding in profound wisdom, he is able to see all things as they truly are.
"O son of good family, you who have attained mastery over all realms of liberation and have perfected the practices of Samantabhadra—Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta is your spiritual friend.

He shall cause you to be born into the family of the Tathāgata, nurture all roots of goodness, and initiate all factors conducive to enlightenment; he shall cause you to encounter true spiritual friends."
"You have cultivated all merits, entered the net of all vows, and abide in all great aspirations; for you,
I shall expound the secret teachings of all bodhisattvas, manifest the inconceivable practices of all bodhisattvas, and reveal those with whom you shared birth and practice in the past."
[Treatise] Seventh: At that time, after the youth Sudhana had respectfully circumambulated Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva to the right, he descended [to this section].
To the end of this fascicle, it clarifies how Sudhana entered the tower of Maitreya to contemplate the fruit and know the cause;
how the spheres of activity traversed throughout the three periods of time are identical yet distinct, general yet specific, and one yet many—unimpeded, sovereign, and perfectly simultaneous.

In this section, when Maitreya Bodhisattva snaps his fingers and the gate opens, it clarifies that "sound" signifies vibration and awakening, while "snapping the fingers" signifies the removal of dust;
the disappearance of dust and the departure of attachment cause the Dharma-gate to open spontaneously.
Once Sudhana has entered, the gate closes again because he has forgotten the wisdom through delusion.
What is currently called "opening the wisdom" is without interior, exterior, or middle; it has no exiting or entering, no delusion, and no realization—this is named "returning to closure.
That one perceives the pavilions as vast and immeasurable, identical to empty space, is the realm of wisdom.
Within them, all adornments are based upon wisdom and the various practices and vows performed by a compassionate heart, which constitute their retribution.
Each and every point is clearly elucidated therein according to the sūtras, regarding the realm of spiritual transformations.

Because the Dharma-realm and the realm of wisdom are inherently and naturally conjoined, there is nothing that is not spiritual. Realizing that all phenomena correspond to the truth, everything is itself divine, even extending to the vision of the realm of Maitreya Bodhisattva’s activities throughout the three periods of time, and the deeds performed by Maitreya Bodhisattva in the past.

The Buddhas and spiritual friends who also preached the Dharma for Sudhana did so because the realm of the wisdom of the Dharmakāya is inherently such as it is, devoid of the nature of the three periods of time.
Throughout the three periods of past, present, and future, across kalpas to the end of time, it never shifts from a single thought-moment.
This is not due to supernatural power; it is simply that the Dharma is naturally thus. As for the color *duṣara*, it is like the color of frost and ice; the rest is as before.
As the *Sūtra of the Self-Contained Sūtras* states: "Good son, when my vows are fulfilled and I attain all-knowledge and realize Bodhi, may you and Mañjuśrī both behold me.

This means that when the causes of the three periods of time are perfected and wisdom is realized as being without past or present, the Buddhas of the three periods encounter one another simultaneously within a single, identical wisdom. Within this passage:

Divided into three sections: First, from "At that time, the youth Sudhana, having respectfully circumambulated Maitreya Bodhisattva" down to "beholding all the majestic adornments within the pavilion," spanning nine pages of scripture, clarifies the section on entering the realm of Buddha-wisdom, wherein one observes the fruit and knows the cause as being non-different. Second, "At that time, Maitreya... [and so forth].

From the passage beginning with "The Bodhisattva" down to "the power of the inspiration, mindfulness, and majestic spiritual authority (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of the spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*)," there are nine lines and a half of scripture that clarify how all the realms manifested through Maitreya Bodhisattva’s own gathered spiritual power were such that he did not use his hand to snap his fingers to command Sudhana to rise.
This section is divided into three parts: [1] the noble one [Maitreya]; [2] the name of this liberation door (*vimokṣamukha*).

From "What is it? downwards, there is a sūtra of approximately four pages clarifying the titles of the Dharma-gates that Sudhana asked, as well as the section concerning his inquiry regarding where Maitreya Bodhisattva came from and where he was born.
Within the titles of those Dharma-gates, he inquires about four dharmas; the first is his entry into the pavilion.
There is a dharma-gate named "Liberation through the Realm of Understanding All Phenomena. The second question concerns the matter of adornment:

"Where has he gone? The third question concerns Maitreya Bodhisattva: "From where does he come? The fourth question concerns the place of the bodhisattva's birth. Regarding the first question, the name of the dharma-gate:
this liberation gate is called "The Adornment of Entering the Realms of All Three Times Without Forgetting Mindfulness."

The second question in the *Ratnaguṇasaṃcayagāthā* asks: "Where does that which is adorned go? Maitreya replies: "It goes to the place from which it came. He asks again: "From where did it come? He replies:
"It comes from within the wisdom and spiritual power (*prabhāva*) of the Bodhisattva; it abides within the wisdom and spiritual power of the Bodhisattva.
Regarding its essential nature (*tattva*), there is no place of coming or going, as is fully detailed in the sūtra. This concludes the third question concerning Maitreya.
As for where the Venerable One has come from, first he answers by way of the Dharma, and then he answers by way of the facts. First, the answer by way of the Dharma says:
"All Bodhisattvas neither come nor go; they come in such a way that there is no movement and no abiding;
they come from within great loving-kindness, great compassion, and great vows," as explained at length in the sutras. Regarding the answer by way of the facts, he says: "I have come from..."

He who came from the country of Mālava—this country was given its name based on the virtues of the Noble One, signifying that the Noble One’s wisdom and virtue transcend the world and are unsurpassed.

The son of a householder named Gopāla—this means "guardian of the ground of the pure dharmas" (*śukladharma*)—was caused by Maitreya to enter the Buddha-dharma; thus, he asked four questions regarding his birth.

Regarding the "places" (*sthāna*), there are first the answers based on the Dharma and secondly the answers based on the facts. First, regarding the answers based on the Dharma, there are ten things that constitute the birthplace of a Bodhisattva.
The *Sūtra on the Birthplace* states: "The bodhicitta is the birthplace of a Bodhisattva; next, the profound mind (*adhyāśaya*); next, the spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*);

next, the stages (*bhūmi*) and perfections (*pāramitā*); next, the great vows (*mahāpraṇidhāna*); next, great compassion (*mahākaruṇā*); next, investigation according to reality (*yoniśaḥ-pravicaya*); next, the Mahāyāna; and next, the teaching and transforming of others."
For sentient beings, wisdom and skillful means are likewise their birthplace;
Prajñā is the mother who gives birth, skillful means is the father, the perfection of giving is the wet nurse, the precepts are the foster mother,
patience is the adornment, diligence is the nurturer, meditative concentration is the washerwoman, and virtuous friends are the teachers who provide instruction.

Taking [the Buddhas] as companions, all virtues as kinsmen, and Bodhisattvas as brothers—by means of such things, this is the birthplace of a Bodhisattva, as detailed at length in the Sūtra itself. To answer according to the facts:
his birthplace was in the land of Mālava within this Jambudvīpa, in the village of Kuṭi, in the household of a Brahmin; that is, the village of Kuṭi.
This place is called "Many Families" because it is a gathering where many households dwell together;
thus, "Brahmin families" refers to those born of pure lineage who possess wisdom and are free from defilement.
Good son, I abide within this great multi-storied pavilion, manifesting various skillful means to teach and transform sentient beings according to their inclinations.
The Tamer, possessing great wisdom in the fields of knowledge and great compassion pervading the Dharma-realm,

is born through the vast fruition of his vows as a phantom within a pavilion; he manifests bodies according to the inclinations of sentient beings, appearing in accordance with their karmic fruits to subdue them,
and displays the majestic adornments of the bodhisattva’s merit and wisdom, which transcend all realms of desire.
This is said in reference to those in the desire realm who calculate that by means of a single birth they will attain the fruit of Buddhahood;
for the bodhisattva’s retributive state of merit and wisdom completely transcends all realms of the three worlds, the three vehicles, and even all lower stages.
This is because their wisdom is identical to that employed by all Buddhas of the ten directions, and because they manifest the unobstructed wisdom and virtue of a Buddha.
Because he has been entrusted with the succession to the Buddha’s position in his next life, he is like an eldest son who manages the father’s household affairs and is no different from the father;
he is also like the crown prince born of the chief consort of a Wheel-Turning King, who possesses the thirty-two marks and shares his father’s merit,
wisdom, and karmic retribution, acting as the father’s regent when carrying out the king’s commands to govern the state.
There is no difference; it is simply because the transformative conditions for the beings gathered under his father, the King, have not yet ended that he does not occupy the royal throne.

Maitreya Tathāgata is likewise: it is only because the single momentum of the beings gathered under the manifested traces of Vairocana has not yet concluded that he does not occupy the position of manifesting birth and attaining Buddhahood. However, regarding this...

In reality, the virtues and wisdom-activity of all Buddhas are without distinction; however, the Tathāgatas establish teachings to guide ordinary beings by manifesting appearance and disappearance, so that sentient beings do not grow weary of the long path and may cultivate their own bodhicitta. It is not that the Buddhas are born here and pass away there;
rather, from the perspective of the wisdom-realm of the *dharmadhātu*, across all lands in the ten directions, there is no such thing as birth or death according to the sentiments of ordinary beings.
Within each and every atom of the earth, oceans of Buddhas are inexhaustible, mutually interpenetrating and transparently clear;
they neither arise nor cease, neither emerge nor submerge, but simply enter the realm of the Dharma-nature body and the sphere of wisdom.
Through the gate of illusory abiding, when one illuminates them, all sentient beings likewise neither arise nor submerge, being exactly as the realm of the Buddha.
[Sūtra] Therefore, son of good family, you should go to the place where Mañjuśrī is; do not give rise to weariness or fatigue.

Mañjuśrī shall explain all merits for your sake. Why is this? All those spiritual friends whom you previously encountered, all the bodhisattva practices you heard, all the doors of liberation you entered and understood, and all the great vows you fulfilled—these were entirely due to the majestic spiritual power of Mañjuśrī.
When the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī had attained ultimate perfection in all respects, the youth Sudhana prostrated at his feet,
circumambulated him countless times, gazed upon him with deep reverence, and then took his leave and departed.
[Treatise] Eighth: Therefore, son of good family, you should go to the place where Mañjuśrī is...
[The following five lines and a half of scripture clarify that Maitreya causes Sudhana to see Mañjuśrī again.
This clarifies that the ultimate fruit is identical to the cause, manifesting that the fruit within the cause is fundamentally non-dual; this section clarifies [the role of] Maitreya.
Having already transcended and entered the Buddha-fruit of the "One Life" (ekajātipratibaddha),

he causes Sudhana to enter the gate of the Tathāgata’s treasury of wisdom in the Hall of Universal Radiance— the Buddha-fruit where the great function of the dharma-realm’s quiescence is eternally manifest.
Because there is no essence of the three periods of time and all is gathered into a single moment, the essence of Bodhi is like space, devoid of beginning, middle, or end.
Throughout the ages, the ancients and the moderns have entered and emerged from this principle; thus, it causes Sudhana to see Mañjuśrī again.

This is because the fruit does not deviate from the cause, as will be clarified in the following passage of the Sūtra. [Sūtra] At that time, the youth Sudhana, following the instructions of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, proceeded by stages.
Having traveled through more than one hundred and ten cities, he arrived at the city of Sumanā in the country of Samantamukha and stayed there at its gate.
There, he contemplated Mañjuśrī, observing him with focused attention and searching everywhere in his desire to pay homage to him.
At that time, Mañjuśrī extended his right hand from afar across one hundred and ten yojanas and touched Sudhana’s crown.

He spoke these words: "Excellent, excellent, son of good family! If one is devoid of the root of faith, with a weak mind and regretful, lacking in meritorious practice and falling away from diligence; if one becomes attached to a single root of goodness and considers a small amount of merit sufficient;
and if one is unable to skillfully initiate vows and practices, nor is protected by spiritual friends."
Not being remembered by the Tathāgata, they are unable to fully comprehend such a nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*),
such a principle (*naya*), such a gateway to the Dharma (*dharmamukha*), such a practice (*caryā*), or such a sphere (*viṣaya*)— whether through universal knowledge,
various kinds of knowledge, exhaustive knowledge of the source, thorough understanding, entry, liberation, discrimination, or realization.
At that time, Mañjuśrī proclaimed this Dharma, instructing, exhorting, benefiting, and gladdening him,
so as to cause the youth Sudhana to accomplish incalculable dharma-gates, to be endowed with the light of immeasurable great wisdom,
and to attain the Bodhisattva’s boundless dhāraṇīs, boundless vows, and boundless samādhis. None were able to fully grasp all that he had attained.
Through the supernatural power of the limit and the wisdom of the limitless, he caused [the assembly] to enter the practice site of Samantabhadra and placed Sudhana in his own abode;

then Mañjuśrī withdrew and became invisible. Thereupon, Sudhana contemplated and observed with single-minded resolve, wishing to see Mañjuśrī and to see all the good friends (kalyāṇamitra) as numerous as the atoms in a trichiliocosm.
He draws near to all those with knowledge, honoring and serving them, receiving and practicing their instructions without opposition;
he increases his pursuit of all wisdom, the vast ocean of great compassion, and the even greater clouds of great kindness;

he observes the birth of sentient beings everywhere, giving rise to great joy, and dwells securely in the bodhisattva’s gate of the dharma of tranquility; he universally contemplates all vast realms, studying the One.
Entering the vast merits of all Buddhas, entering the definitive knowledge and vision of all Buddhas, increasing the dharmas that assist the path to omniscience,
skillfully cultivating the profound resolve of all Bodhisattvas, knowing the sequence of the appearance of the Buddhas of the three periods of time,
entering the ocean of all dharmas, turning all wheels of Dharma, giving birth to all worlds, and entering into the vows of all Bodhisattvas.
Abiding in the ocean [of existence] throughout all kalpas, they cultivate the bodhisattva practices, illuminating the realms of all Tathāgatas, nurturing the faculties of all bodhisattvas,
and attaining the pure radiance of omniscience that shines universally upon the ten directions, removing all veils of darkness. Their wisdom pervades the Dharma-realm,
and they manifest their bodies universally within all Buddha-fields and all states of existence, such that there is nowhere they do not appear.
Having universally crushed all obstacles and entered the unimpeded Dharma, he dwelt upon the ground of equality within the Dharmadhātu; observing the realm of Samantabhadra’s liberation,
he heard the names of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Samantabhadra, as well as his practices, vows, the paths of assistance,
the direct path, the various grounds, the skillful means of each ground, the entry into the grounds, the grounds of superior progress, the grounds of abiding, and the grounds of cultivation.
Possessing the power of the realms and stages and dwelling together in longing to behold Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
they arose right there before the lion throne of Vairocana Tathāgata at this Vajragarbha Bodhimaṇḍa, upon seats of all-jeweled lotus treasuries;
they gave rise to a mind as vast as the realm of empty space, relinquishing all lands, free from all attachments, and unimpeded.
A mind that universally practices all unimpeded dharmas; an unimpeded mind that enters everywhere into the oceans of the ten directions;
an unimpeded mind that universally enters the realm of all-knowledge; a pure mind; a clear and lucid mind that contemplates the adornments of the site of enlightenment;
a vast mind that enters the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas; a transformative mind for all realms of sentient beings; and a pervasive mind that purifies all things.
With a mind that encompasses immeasurable lands, a mind that abides through all kalpas without exhaustion, and a mind that proceeds toward the ultimate ten powers of the Tathāgata—
when the youth Sudhana gave rise to such a mind, by the power of his own roots of goodness, the power of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas,
and the power of the shared roots of goodness of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, he beheld ten kinds of auspicious signs. What are these ten?
That is to say: seeing all Buddha-fields as pure, seeing all Tathāgatas attaining perfect enlightenment;
seeing all Buddha-fields as pure and free from all evil realms; seeing all Buddha-fields as pure and adorned with various exquisite lotus flowers;
seeing all Buddha-fields as pure, wherein the bodies and minds of all sentient beings are pure; seeing one...
They see all Buddha-fields purified and adorned with various kinds of jewels;

they see all Buddha-fields purified, with all sentient beings adorning their bodies with various marks; they see all Buddha-fields purified, with clouds of various adornments covering them from above;
they see all Buddha-fields purified, with all sentient beings giving rise to mutual compassion toward one another.
To benefit others without causing them distress; to see all Buddha-fields as pure sites of enlightenment adorned with splendor;
to see all Buddha-fields as pure; to have a mind that constantly recollects the Buddhas among all sentient beings—these are the ten.
Furthermore, one sees ten kinds of signs of light. What are the ten? They are: seeing every single atom within all the worlds, and within each and every atom...
From within [each pore], there issued forth clouds of Buddha-light-nets as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, shining everywhere and illuminating all;
from within each atom, there issued forth clouds of Buddha-light-wheels as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, with various colors and forms pervading the entire Dharma-realm;
and from within each atom, there issued forth jewel-clouds of the physical forms of Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in all worlds.
From every single atom throughout the entire Dharma-realm, there emerge clouds of flaming wheels of light from all Buddhas,
as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, pervading the Dharma-realm; from every single atom, there emerge clouds of various exquisite fragrances, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds,
pervading the ten directions and praising the great ocean of merit of Samantabhadra’s universal vows and practices, within each and every atom.

From within each [atom], there emerge clouds of suns, moons, and stars, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, all emitting the light of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva that universally illumines the Dharma-realm;

from within each atom, there emerge clouds of the physical forms and images of all sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, all emitting the light of the Buddhas that universally illumines the Dharma-realm; from within each atom, there emerges one...
From within every single atom, clouds of mani-jewel images of all Buddhas, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, pervade the entire Dharma-realm.

From within each atom, clouds of the bodily images of Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in all worlds, emerge and fill the Dharma-realm, causing all sentient beings to attain liberation and fulfill their aspirations. From within each and every atom, [all things] emerge...
Clouds of the physical forms and colors of Tathāgatas, as numerous as the atoms in the world-system, proclaiming the vast vows of all Buddhas that pervade the entire Dharma-realm—
this is the tenth. *The Combined Commentary on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, Fascicle 119.

The Combined Commentary on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Expanded and Vast Teachings, Fascicle One Hundred and Twentieth.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda, a Śramaṇa from Khotan during the Tang Dynasty;
The Treatise composed by Li Tongxuan, a Lay Elder of Fangshan in Taiyuan during the Tang Dynasty.

Compiled by the Śramaṇa Zhining of Kaiyuan Temple in Fuzhou during the Tang Dynasty, combining the various editions of the sutra for the *Entry into the Dharma Realm* Chapter, Chapter Thirty-nine, Part Three of Three.
[Sutra] At that time, having seen these ten kinds of radiant signs, the youth Sudhana immediately formed this thought: "I now..."
He will surely behold Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, increase his roots of goodness, see all Buddhas, and give rise to resolute understanding regarding the vast realm of all bodhisattvas;

he shall attain all-knowledge. At that time, Sudhana, having fully gathered his faculties and seeking with single-minded devotion to see Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, gave rise to a mind of great diligence without regression, and observed with the Universal Eye.
May I behold all the realms perceived by the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, conceiving them as the realm of Samantabhadra;
observing the path of Samantabhadra with the eye of wisdom, may my mind become as vast as space and my great compassion as firm as a diamond,
vowing to follow and accompany the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra in every thought-moment until the end of the future.
As he practiced in accordance with the conduct of Samantabhadra, accomplished wisdom, entered the realm of the Tathāgata, and dwelt upon the stage of Samantabhadra,
the youth Sudhana then beheld the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra seated before the Tathāgata amidst the great assembly upon a lion throne of precious lotuses,
surrounded by a multitude of bodhisattvas; he was most exceptionally sublime, peerless in the world.

The realm of his equal wisdom is immeasurable, boundless, unfathomable, and inconceivable; it is equal to that of all Buddhas of the three periods of time and all Bodhisattvas, whom none can fully observe.

From every single pore of Samantabhadra’s body, clouds of light rays as numerous as the atoms within all worlds emerge, pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space throughout all worlds, extinguishing the sufferings of all sentient beings.
The afflictions cause great joy to arise in the Bodhisattvas as they see from each and every pore emerge clouds of various colored fragrant flames,
numbering as many as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space,
universally perfuming all the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas; and they see from each and every pore emerge [clouds] numbering as many as the atoms in all Buddha-fields.
I saw clouds of various flowers pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, raining down all manner of exquisite blossoms upon the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas;

and from every single pore, I saw clouds of incense trees as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, raining down all manner of exquisite fragrances upon the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas. From every single pore...
They emit clouds of exquisite garments, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands, pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space,
raining down various wonderful garments upon all the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas. They see that from every single pore there emerge clouds of jewel-trees,
as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-lands, pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, raining down [upon all the assemblies and sites of enlightenment of all Buddhas].

The Maṇi-jewel saw from each and every pore emerge clouds of bodies of gods of the form realm (*rūpadhātu*) as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, filling the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), and it praised the bodhicitta;

it saw from each and every pore emerge clouds of bodies of Brahmā gods as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, exhorting all Tathāgatas to turn the sublime wheel of Dharma; it saw from each and every pore emerge...
Clouds of bodies of the kings of the desire realm, as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, protect and uphold the Dharma-wheel of all Tathāgatas;
from every single pore, in every moment of thought, they emit clouds of Buddha-fields of the three periods of time,
as numerous as the atoms in all Buddha-fields, pervading the dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, acting as a refuge for all sentient beings who have no refuge.
I saw those who were without protection provided with protection, and those who were without refuge provided with refuge;
and I saw from every single pore, in every moment of thought, clouds of pure Buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields emerge,
pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, wherein all Buddhas appear in the world and assemblies of Bodhisattvas completely fill them.
From every single pore, in every moment of thought, there issue forth clouds of pure and impure Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands,
pervading the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space, causing all defiled sentient beings to attain purity. From every single pore, in every moment of thought,
there issue forth clouds of impure and pure Buddha-lands as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-lands, pervading the Dharma-realm...
Within the realm of empty space, they cause all defiled sentient beings to attain purity;

from every single pore, in every moment of thought, they emit clouds of impure buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields, pervading the realm of empty space throughout the entire dharma-realm, causing all purely defiled sentient beings to attain purity; from every single pore, in every moment of thought, they emit... all [pure buddha-fields].
Clouds of the bodies of sentient beings, as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field, pervade the Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space;
according to what is appropriate for them, they teach and transform sentient beings, causing them all to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
From every single pore, in every moment of thought, there emerge clouds of the bodies of Bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, pervading the Dharma-realm and empty space.
In the realm of space, he proclaimed the various names of all Buddhas, causing all sentient beings to increase their roots of goodness.

From every single pore, in every moment of thought, there issued forth clouds of Bodhisattva bodies, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, pervading the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space.
In all Buddha-fields, they proclaimed the deeds of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas from the time they first resolved to attain enlightenment.

From every single pore, within each and every thought-moment, there emerge clouds of bodhisattva bodies as numerous as the atoms in all buddha-fields, pervading the entire dharma-realm and the realm of empty space;
they proclaim throughout every single one of those buddha-fields the ocean of all bodhisattva vows and the pure, wondrous conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva. Thus he beholds every single pore.
In every moment of thought, he produces clouds of the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva that satisfy the minds of all sentient beings and cause them to fully cultivate the path to omniscience;
from each and every pore, he causes clouds of the bodies of perfectly awakened ones, as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields, to emerge,
manifesting perfect enlightenment in all Buddha-fields and causing all bodhisattvas to increase in their realization.
When the Great Dharma of omniscience was thus accomplished, at that time the youth Sudhana beheld such a realm of the sovereign spiritual powers of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
his body and mind were filled with immeasurable joy and exultation as he contemplated again and again each and every limb and each and every pore of Samantabhadra,
wherein there were all the wind-circles, water-circles, earth-circles, and fire-circles of the triple-thousand great thousandfold world-systems.
The great oceans, rivers, and various jewel mountains; Mount Sumeru, the Iron Ring Mountains, villages, camps, cities, towns, palaces, gardens, and groves;
all the hells, hungry ghosts, animals, and the realm of King Yama; the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings, humans and non-humans;
the abodes of the desire realm, form realm, and formless realm; the sun, moon, stars, constellations, wind, clouds, thunder, lightning, day, and night.

The times, years, and kalpas, the appearance of all Buddhas in the world, the assemblies of Bodhisattvas, the adornments of the sites of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa), and all such matters were clearly seen;
just as this world was seen, so too were all worlds throughout the ten directions seen in the same way.
Just as the present worlds in the ten directions were seen, so too were all worlds of the past and future in the ten directions seen in the same way.

These visions are distinct from one another and do not intermingle; just as these supernatural powers were manifested by this Tathāgata Vairocana, so too were the supernatural powers manifested at the abode of the Buddha Bhadraśrī in the world Padmaśrī in the eastern direction.
Just as it was at the abode of the Buddha Bhadraśrī, so it was in all worlds in the eastern direction.

One should know that the supernatural powers manifested by all Tathāgatas in all worlds of the east, south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, above, and below are exactly like this; as it is in all worlds throughout the ten directions,

so too within every single atom of every Buddha-land in the ten directions, there are the assemblies of Buddhas of the entire Dharma-realm, and in each and every Buddha’s presence, [they are] universally present.
The noble Bodhisattva likewise manifests such supernormal powers while seated upon a precious lotus lion throne;
within each and every body of Samantabhadra, there appear all realms of the three periods of time, all Buddha-fields, all sentient beings,
the appearances of all Buddhas, the assemblies of all Bodhisattvas, and the sounds of the voices of all sentient beings.

Seeing the immeasurable and inconceivable power of great spiritual transformations of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva— the speech and sounds of all Buddhas, the turning of the wheel of Dharma by all Tathāgatas,
and all the practices accomplished by all Bodhisattvas, as well as the playful supernatural powers of all Tathāgatas—
Sudhana immediately attained ten kinds of *jñānapāramitā*. What are they?
There are ten, namely: the perfection of wisdom that is able to pervade all Buddha-fields in every moment of thought;
the perfection of wisdom that is able to go before all Buddhas in every moment of thought;
the perfection of wisdom that is able to make offerings to all Tathāgatas in every moment of thought; and [the perfection of wisdom] that universally [perceives] all in every moment of thought.

The perfection of wisdom that receives and maintains all dharmas heard from all Tathāgatas; the perfection of wisdom that contemplates the wheel of the Dharma of all Tathāgatas in every thought-moment;
the perfection of wisdom that knows the inconceivable great supernormal powers of all Buddhas in every thought-moment;
and the perfection of wisdom that explains a single phrase of the Dharma until the end of the future.
The perfection of wisdom of inexhaustible eloquence, which in every thought-moment contemplates all phenomena through profound *prajñā*;
the perfection of wisdom that in every thought-moment enters the ocean of the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all dharma-realms;
the perfection of wisdom that in every thought-moment knows the minds of all sentient beings; the perfection of wisdom of Samantabhadra in every thought-moment.
When the wisdom-practice had all appeared before him and the youth Sudhana had attained this Perfection of Wisdom,
the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra extended his right hand and touched the crown of his head. Once he had touched his head,
Sudhana immediately attained as many gates of samādhi as there are atoms in all Buddha-fields, each gate being characterized by as many samādhis as there are atoms in all Buddha-fields.
For each member of the retinue, through every single samādhi, they saw oceans of Buddhas as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields—Buddhas never before seen—gathered together;
they saw the arising of the requisites for omniscience as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields;

they saw the emergence of the supreme and wondrous Dharma of omniscience as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields; and they saw [the manifestation of] one [aspect] as numerous as the atoms within all Buddha-fields.
Through the great vow of omniscience, they enter oceans of great vows as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields;
they abide in the essential paths of omniscience as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields; they cultivate the practices of all bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields;
they give rise to the great vigor of omniscience as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields; and they attain [the first stage].
As many as there are atoms in all Buddha-fields, the pure light of omniscience—
just as the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra touched the crown of the head of Sudhana in the presence of the Buddha Vairocana in this Sahā world,
so too did the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra [touch the crowns of the heads] of all Buddhas in all worlds throughout the ten directions, and within every single atom of those worlds.
All were likewise so; they touched the crown of Sudhana’s head, and the Dharma-gates he attained were all equally such.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samantabhadra addressed Sudhana, saying: "Son of good family, do you see this power of my supernormal transformations?
"Indeed, Great Sage, I have seen it. "This inconceivable matter of great supernormal power belongs solely to the Tathāgata."
Samantabhadra replied, "Noble son, in the past, for as many eons as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields,
I practiced the conduct of a bodhisattva seeking all-knowledge. In each and every eon, for the sake of purifying the bodhicitta,
I served as many Buddhas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields."
In order to gather the merit for the attainment of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*) throughout a single eon,
he established vast assemblies of giving as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, so that all the worlds might hear and know of them,
and to ensure that whatever was sought was entirely fulfilled. Furthermore, in each and every eon, for the sake of seeking the Dharma of all-knowledge, he [performed] with the unspeakably...
For the sake of seeking the Buddha-wisdom, one may practice the giving of wealth and goods as numerous as the atoms within a Buddha-field in each and every eon;
furthermore, one may practice the giving of unspeakably unspeakable numbers of cities, towns, villages, kingdoms, royal thrones,
wives, children, retinues, eyes, ears, noses, tongues, bodies, flesh, hands, feet, and even one’s own life.
In each and every eon, for the sake of seeking the head of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā-śīrṣa*),
he practiced giving away as many heads as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields; and in each and every eon, for the sake of seeking all-knowledge,
he reverently honored, respected, and served as many Tathāgatas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields.
I have offered all necessities—robes, bedding, food, drink, medicine, and everything required—as alms.
Within that Dharma, I have gone forth to study the Way and practice the Buddha-dharma, upholding the True Teaching.
Good son, throughout those oceans of kalpas, I recall that never for even a single thought-moment have I failed to comply with the Buddha’s teachings, nor for a single thought-moment...
Giving rise to thoughts of anger and malice, thoughts of "I" and "mine," and thoughts of distinction between self and others; being far removed from the bodhicitta;

conceiving weariness and exhaustion toward saṃsāra; having thoughts of laziness, hindrance, and delusion—[yet] abiding solely in the unsurpassed, indestructible bodhicitta that gathers all the auxiliary dharmas for the path to omniscience, O noble son, I adorn [myself with it].
To adorn Buddha-lands with a heart of great compassion; to rescue and protect sentient beings, teaching and transforming them until they achieve maturity;
to make offerings to all Buddhas and serve spiritual friends; to seek the True Dharma and propagate, uphold, and protect it;

to be able to relinquish everything internal and external, even one's own body and life, without any regret—were one to explain the causes and conditions for these throughout oceans of kalpas, those oceans of kalpas might come to an end, but this [merit] would not.

"O son of good family, within the ocean of my Dharma there is not a single word or a single phrase that was not sought by relinquishing the sovereignty of a universal monarch (cakravartin), nor was it sought by relinquishing all that one possesses.
Son of good family, the Dharma I have sought is solely for the purpose of protecting and rescuing all sentient beings with a single-minded resolve."
I only pray that all sentient beings may hear this Dharma; that they may universally illumine the world with the light of wisdom;
that they may be shown the supramundane wisdom; that they may cause all sentient beings to attain peace and happiness;
and that they may universally praise all the merits of all Buddhas. Such causes and conditions of mine from the past are unspeakably unspeakable.

Even in oceans of eons as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field, it could not be fully described. Therefore, noble son, by means of the power of these factors conducive to enlightenment, the power of all roots of goodness, the power of great aspiration and resolve, the power of cultivating merit, the power of reflecting upon all dharmas as they truly are, the power of the eye of wisdom, the power of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, the power of great compassion, and the power of pure supernormal knowledges— [The text continues: ...I have attained this ocean of liberation called "the manifestation of the light of the Tathāgata’s unimpeded knowledge. Noble son, such is the extent of my attainment of this ocean of liberation. Furthermore, noble son, there are oceans of eons as numerous as the atoms within a buddha-field that preceded this; during those times, I served as many Buddhas as there are atoms in a buddha-field, and through their empowerment, I attained this ocean of liberation. Noble son, even if one were to spend as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field describing the names of those Buddhas, the lands where they appeared, their lineages, their families, their lifespans, their assemblies, their teachings, and the various ways in which I served them, heard their teachings, and practiced according to them, one would still not reach the end of the description. Yet, noble son, I have not yet exhausted the succession of births in which I cultivated this ocean of liberation. Noble son, I remember that in the past, during an eon called *Vimalaprabhāsa*, there was a world-system called *Ratnavicitra*. In that world-system, there was a central world called *Padmavikrānta*; therein, in the center of a four-continent world, there was a land called *Sumeruprabhāsa*. In that land, there was a city called *Vairocanaraśmi*; therein, there was a king named *Mahāvyūha*. At that time, the Tathāgata *Samantāvabhāsajñānabuddhi* appeared in the world. I was then a queen of that king, named *Vimaladattā*. Having heard the name of that Tathāgata, I went with five hundred women to the place where he dwelt. Upon seeing the Tathāgata, I paid homage at his feet and sat to one side. Then, the Tathāgata, knowing my thoughts, expounded for me a teaching called "the treasury of the inexhaustible light of the Tathāgata’s knowledge," consisting of ten thousand verses. Having heard this teaching, I attained an ocean of liberation called "the manifestation of the light of the Tathāgata’s unimpeded knowledge. Noble son, from that time until now, I have passed through as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, and during that interval, I have never been separated from this ocean of liberation. Noble son, I remember that in the past, during an eon called *Vicitraratna*, there was a world-system called *Sarvaratnavyūha*. In that world-system, there was a central world called *Padmavikrānta*; therein, in the center of a four-continent world, there was a land called *Sumeruprabhāsa*. In that land, there was a city called *Vairocanaraśmi*; therein, there was a king named *Mahāvyūha*. At that time, the Tathāgata *Samantāvabhāsajñānabuddhi* appeared in the world. I was then a queen of that king, named *Vimaladattā*. Having heard the name of that Tathāgata, I went with five hundred women to the place where he dwelt. Upon seeing the Tathāgata, I paid homage at his feet and sat to one side. Then, the Tathāgata, knowing my thoughts, expounded for me a teaching called "the treasury of the inexhaustible light of the Tathāgata’s knowledge," consisting of ten thousand verses. Having heard this teaching, I attained an ocean of liberation called "the manifestation of the light of the Tathāgata’s unimpeded knowledge. Noble son, from that time until now, I have passed through as many eons as there are atoms in a buddha-field, and during that interval, I have never been separated from this ocean of liberation. Noble son, I remember that in the past, during an eon called *Vicitraratna*, there was a world-system called *Sarvaratnavyūha*. In that world-system, there was a central world called *Padmavikrānta*; therein, in the center of a four-continent world, there was a land called *Sumeruprabhāsa*. In that land, there was a city called *Vairocanaraśmi*; therein, there was a king named *Mahāvyūha*. At that time, the Tathāgata *Samantāvabhāsajñānabuddhi* appeared in the world. I was then a queen of that king, named *Vimaladattā*. Having heard the name of that Tathāgata, I went with five hundred women to the place where he dwelt. Upon seeing the Tathāgata, I paid homage at his feet and sat to one side. Then, the Tathāgata, knowing my thoughts, expounded for me a teaching called "the treasury of the inexhaustible light of the Tathāgata’s knowledge," consisting of ten thousand verses. Having heard this teaching, I attained an ocean of liberation called "the manifestation of the light of the Tathāgata’s unimpeded knowledge.
